##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, the purified, shining, exceedingly great, true by nature, the lord, crosses the firmament with his stream. Urged by the priests, exceedingly of the nature of truth, he flows forth for the support of Mitra and Varuṇa.

##### English translation
The divine royal (Soma) vast and true, undergoing purification traverses the firmament in a stream ; vast and true, being sent forth he flows for the support of Mitra and Varuna.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नृभि॑र्येमा॒नो ह॑र्य॒तो वि॑चक्ष॒णो राजा॑ दे॒वः स॑मु॒द्रियः॑ ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नृभिः । येमानः । हर्यतः । विचक्षणः । राजा । देवः । समुद्रियः ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिर्येमानो नियम्यमानो हर्यतः स्पृहणीयो
> विचक्षणो विद्रष्टा देवो दीप्यमानः समुद्रियोऽंतरिक्षे भवो राजा सोम
> इंद्रार्थं पवत इत्युत्तरेण संबंधः ॥ समुद्राभ्राद्धः इति भवार्थे घप्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Regulated by the नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*), the leaders of the rite; हर्यतः (*haryataḥ*), desirable; विचक्षणः (*vicakṣaṇaḥ*), the far-seeing; देवः (*devaḥ*), shining; समुद्रियः (*samudriyaḥ*), born in the firmament; the king Soma flows for Indra. The connection is with the following verse. The affix घ (*gha*) is in the sense of "born in" (भवार्थे (*bhavārthe*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests
- येमानः (*yemānaḥ*)—regulated
- हरतः (*harataḥ*)—of attractive form
- विचक्षणः (*vicakṣaṇaḥ*)—of subtle sight
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—shining
- समुद्रियः (*samudriyaḥ*)—born in the firmament
- राजा (*rājā*)—Soma, the lord, flows

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑य पवते॒ मदः॒ सोमो॑ म॒रुत्व॑ते सु॒तः ।  
> स॒हस्र॑धारो॒ अत्यव्य॑मर्षति॒ तमीं॑ मृजंत्या॒यवः॑ ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राय । शवते । मदः । सोमः । मरुत्वते । सुतः ।  
> सहस्रधारः । अति । अव्यं । अर्षति । तं । ईमिति । मृजंति । आयवः ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मदो मादकः सुतोऽभिषुतः सोमो मरुत्वते मरुद्धिस्तद्वत इंद्रायेंद्रार्थं पवते । क्षरति । ततः सहस्रधारो बहुधारोपेतः सोमोऽव्यमविमयं पवित्रमत्यर्षति । अतिगच्छति । तमिमं सोममायवो मनुष्या ऋत्विजो
> मृजंति , शोधयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, मदः (*madaḥ*) (intoxicating) and सुतः (*sutaḥ*) (pressed), flows, that is, streams, for Indra, who is मरुत्वते (*marutvate*), accompanied by the Maruts. Then Soma, सहस्रधारः (*sahasradhāraḥ*) (with many streams), passes over the अव्यं (*avyaṃ*), the pavitra made of wool. The आयवः (*āyavaḥ*), men, that is the priests, cleanse this Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदः (*madaḥ*)—gladdening
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- मरुत्वते (*marutvate*)—accompanied by the Maruts
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- पवते (*pavate*)—flows
- सहस्रधारः (*sahasradhāraḥ*)—Soma with many streams
- अव्यं (*avyaṃ*)—the ten-fold pavitra of wool
- अत्यर्षति (*atyarṣati*)—crosses
- तं (*taṃ*)—this Soma
- आयवः (*āyavaḥ*)—men
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—cleanse

### Printed p. 78

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, gladdening and pressed, flows for the drinking of Indra, who is accompanied by the Maruts. Soma, with streams of many kinds, crosses the ten-fold pavitra of wool. Men cleanse this Soma.

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पु॒ना॒नश्च॒मू ज॒नय॑न्म॒तिं क॒विः सोमो॑ दे॒वेषु॑ रण्यति ।  
> अ॒पो वसा॑नः॒ परि॒ गोभि॒रुत्त॑रः॒ सीद॒न्वने॑ष्टव्यत ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुनानः । चमू इति । जनयन् । मतिं । कविं । सोमः । देवेषु । रण्यति ।  
> अपः । वसानः । परि । गोभिः । उत्तरः । सीदन् । वनेषु । अव्यत ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चमू ॥ सप्तम्याः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ॥ चन्नोरधिषवणफलकयोः पुनानति
> पूयमानोऽभिषूयमाणो मतिं स्तुतिं जनयन्नुत्पादयन् कविः क्रांतप्रज्ञः
> एतादृशः सोमो देवेष्ट्विंद्रादिषु रण्यति । किंचापो वसतीवरीर्वसान आच्छादयन् वनेषु काष्ठेषु पात्रेषु सीदन् सोमो गोभिगोर्विकारैः क्षीरादिभिः
> पर्यव्यत । परिदीयते आच्छाद्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

चमू (*camū*) is the locative dual, with lengthening of the preceding vowel by the rule on the homogeneous vowel; it means the two pressing-boards. Being purified, being pressed on them, producing praise (मतिं (*matiṃ*)), a कविः (*kaviḥ*), one of surpassing wisdom, such a Soma delights among the gods, Indra and the others. Moreover, clothing the waters, the vasatīvarī, and settling in the वनेषु (*vaneṣu*), the wooden vessels, Soma is surrounded (पर्यव्यत (*paryavyata*)), that is, covered, with गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*), products of the cow, milk and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चमू (*camū*)—on the pressing-boards
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—being pressed
- मतिं (*matiṃ*)—praise
- जनयन् (*janayan*)—producing
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—of surpassing wisdom
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods, Indra and the others
- रण्यति (*raṇyati*)—delights
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the vasatīvarī waters
- वसानः (*vasānaḥ*)—clothing himself
- वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—in the vessels
- उत्तरः सीदन् (*uttaraḥ sīdan*)—Soma, who has taken his place as the supreme
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with milk and the like
- परि अव्यत (*pari avyata*)—joins

### Printed p. 79

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Purified in the pressing boards, and producing praise, the wise Soma rejoices with Indra and the other gods. Joined with the Vasatīvarī waters and having taken his excellent abode in the vessels, Soma unites with milk and the other admixtures.

##### English translation
Purified in the cups, exciting laudation, the sage Soma rejoices amongst the gods ; clothed with the waters sitting in the wooden bowls, he is surrounded with the curds and milk.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तवा॒हं सो॑म रारण स॒ख्य इं॑दो दि॒वेदि॑ने ।  
> पु॒रूणि॑ बभ्रो॒ नि च॑रंति॒ मामन॑ परि॒धीरिति॒ ता इ॑हि ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । अहं । सोम । ररण । सख्ये । इंदो इति । दिवेदिवे ।  
> पुरूणि । बभ्रो इति । नि । चरंति । मां । अव । परिधीन् । अति । तान् । इहि ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो हे सोम तव सख्ये सखिकर्मण्यहं दिनेदिनेऽन्वहं रारण ॥
> रणेर्लिट्युत्तमे णलि रूपं ॥ हे बभ्रो बभ्रुवर्ण सोम पुरूणि बहूनि रक्षांसि
> मां तव सख्ये स्थितं न्यव चरंति । नीचीनं चरंति । बाधंते । ये मां बाधंते
> तान्नरिधीन्राक्षसांस्त्वमतीहि । अतीत्य गच्छ । जहीति यावत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indu, O Soma, in your friendship (sakhya) I rejoice day after day." The form रारण (*rāraṇa*) is the first person perfect (liṭ) of the root रण (*raṇa*). "O Babhru, golden-hued Soma, many (puruṇi = bahūni) Rakṣas-demons move about me, who stand in your friendship, and press upon me": न्यव चरंति (*nyava caraṃti*) means they go about lowly, that is, they oppress. "Those encircling Rākṣasas who oppress me — overcome them, go past them", that is, destroy them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O flowing one
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- तव (*tava*)—your
- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—in friendship
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- दिवेदिवे (*divedive*)—every day
- रारण (*rāraṇa*)—I experience delight
- बभ्रो (*babhro*)—O golden-hued Soma
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—numerous Asuras
- नि अव चरंति (*ni ava caraṃti*)—surround and harm
- तान् परिधीन् (*tān paridhīn*)—all those Asuras
- अति इहि (*ati ihi*)—confront and destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O flowing Soma, I who stand in your friendship experience delight every day. O golden-hued Soma, numerous Asuras surround me and harm me.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒ताहं नक्त॑मु॒त सो॑म ते॒ दिवा॑ स॒ख्याय॑ बभ्र॒ ऊध॑नि ।  
> घृ॒णा तपं॑त॒मति॒ सूर्यं॑ प॒रः श॑कु॒ना इ॑व पस्तिम ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । अहं । नक्तं । उत । सोम । ते । दिवा । सख्याय । बभ्रो इति । ऊधनि ।  
> घृणा । तपंतं । अति । सूर्यं । परः । शकुनाःइव । पप्तिम । २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे बभ्रो बभ्रुवर्ण हे सोम उतापि च नक्तमुतापि च दिनाहोरात्रयोः
> सख्याय सख्यार्थं तवोधनि समीपेऽहं रम इति शेषः । ते वयं फृणा दीप्त्या
> तपंतं ज्वलंतं परः परमस्थानस्थितं सूर्यं तदात्मकं त्वामति पप्तिम । तत्र
> स्थितं त्वां प्राप्तमतिपेतिम । कथमिव । शकुना इव यथा सुपर्णादयः पक्षिणः
> सूर्यमतिगच्छंति तद्वत् ॥ पत्लृगतौ । अस्माच्चांदसे लिटि तनिपत्योश्चंदसीत्युपधालोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Babhru, golden-hued Soma, both by night and by day, for friendship, near you I delight" (रम (*rama*) is to be supplied). "We, by ghṛṇā (radiance), leap (पप्तिम (*paptima*)) beyond the blazing Sun who stands in the supreme station — you, who are of his nature; having reached you who are established there, may we go beyond." How? As birds such as eagles pass beyond the sun, so.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बभ्रो (*babhro*)—golden-hued
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- उत (*uta*)—and
- नक्तं (*naktaṃ*)—by night
- उत (*uta*)—and
- दिवा (*divā*)—by day
- ते सख्याय (*te sakhyāya*)—for friendship with you
- ऊधनि (*ūdhani*)—near you
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I delight
- शकुनाः इव (*śakunāḥ iva*)—as birds fly up to the sun-world
- सृणा (*sṛṇā*)—by your own radiance
- तपंतं (*tapaṃtaṃ*)—blazing
- परः (*paraḥ*)—standing in the supreme station
- सूर‍्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—and of the nature of the Sun, to your presence
- अति पप्तिम (*ati paptima*)—may we fly to you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O golden-hued Soma, night and day, for friendship with you, I delight in your very nearness. As birds fly up to the sun-world, may we fly to your presence, blazing with your own radiance, standing in the supreme station, and of the nature of the Sun.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ग्रावस्तोत्रेऽभिरूपकरणे सोमे मृज्यमान एकस्तृचः । तत्र मृज्यमान
> इत्येषा तृतीया । सूत्रितं च । मृज्यमानः सुहस्त्वा दशभिर्विवस्वतः । आ. ५-१२
> इति ॥
> हे सुहस्त्य । हस्ते भवा हस्ता अंगुलयः । शोभनांगुलिक सोम मृज्यमानः शोध्यमानस्त्वं समुद्रेऽन्तरिक्षे कलशे वा वाचं शब्दमिन्वसि । प्रेरयसि ।
> किंच हे पवमान पूयमान सोम पिशंगं हिरण्यैः पिशंगवर्णं बहुलं प्रभूतं
> पुरुस्पृहं बहुभिः स्पृहणीयं रयिं धनमभ्यर्षसि । स्तोत्कणामभिक्षरसि ।
> प्रयच्छसि ॥
> xxv 6

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Grāvastotra, at the abhiṣava (pressing) of Soma, "मृज्यमान (*mṛjyamāna*)" is one tṛca; of it this verse beginning मृज्यमान (*mṛjyamāna*) is the third. It is also prescribed in the sūtra: मृज्यमानः सुहस्त्वा दशभिर्विवस्वतः (*mṛjyamānaḥ suhastvā daśabhirvivasvataḥ*) (Ā. 5-12).
"O Suhastya" — हस्ता (*hastā*) are the fingers that are in the hand; so, O Soma of beautiful fingers, being purified, you utter a sound (इन्वसि (*invasi*) = you send forth) in the samudra, that is, in the atmosphere or in the vessel. Further, O Pavamāna, Soma who are being purified, you bring (*abhyarṣasi*) wealth that is golden-hued (पिशंगं (*piśaṃgaṃ*), tawny with gold), ample (बहुलं (*bahulaṃ*) = abundant), and desired by many (पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*)); you pour it out for the singers and give it.

### Printed p. 82

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुहस्त्य (*suhastya*)—O Soma with excellent fingers
- मृज्यमानः (*mṛjyamānaḥ*)—you who are being purified
- समुद्रे (*samudre*)—in the atmosphere
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—a sound
- इन्वसि (*invasi*)—you send forth
- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O Soma, the purifier
- पिशंगं (*piśaṃgaṃ*)—of golden form
- बहुलं (*bahulaṃ*)—abundant
- पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*)—desired by many
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- अभ्यर्षिसि (*abhyarṣisi*)—you give to the singers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, pressed by excellent fingers, you who are being purified send forth a sound in the atmosphere. O Soma, the purifier, you give to the singers wealth that is of golden form, abundant, and desired by many.

##### English translation
Fair-fingered (Soma) being cleansed you utter a sound in the pitcher ; you bring, Pavamana, ample golden-hued much-coveted wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the time of the praise of the Grāvas (the stones used for pressing Soma), while the Soma is being crushed and pressed, three Ṛks are to be recited. Of these, this Ṛk beginning मृज्यमानः (*mṛjyamānaḥ*) is the third. This matter is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, मृज्यमानः सुहस्त्या दशभिर्विवस्वतः (*mṛjyamānaḥ suhastyā daśabhirvivasvataḥ*) (Ā. 5-12).

### Printed p. 83

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम वृषा वर्षिता त्वं मृजानो वसतीवरीभिर्मृज्यमानोऽलंक्रिय.
> माणोऽव्ययेऽविमये वारे वाले पवित्रे पवमानः पूयमानः सन् वने वननीय उदके काष्ठे कलशे वाव चक्रदः । अवक्रंदसि । शब्दायसे । ततो हे सोम
> हे पवमान त्वं गोभिर्गवैः क्षीरादिभिरंजानोऽज्यमानः सन्निष्कृतं संस्कृतं
> देवानां स्थानमर्षसि । गच्छसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, you the showerer (वृषा (*vṛṣā*) = one who rains), being cleansed (मृजानः (*mṛjānaḥ*)) by the Vasatīvarī waters, that is, being adorned, being purified in the sheep's-wool strainer (वारे (*vāre*) = in the hair, the purifier; अव्यये (*avyaye*) = made of sheep's wool), you cry aloud (अव चक्रदः (*ava cakradaḥ*), you make sound) in the वने (*vane*), that is, in the water, the wood, or the vessel. Then, O Soma, O Pavamāna, anointed (अंजानः (*aṃjānaḥ*)) with the gavas (milk and the like), you go to the prepared, refined station of the gods."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (सोम (*soma*)—O Soma)
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—you, the showerer of desires
- मृजानः (*mṛjānaḥ*)—being well refined
- अव्यये (*avyaye*)—of wool
- वारे (*vāre*)—in the ten-fold strainer with its fibres
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—being purified
- वने (*vane*)—in the vessel
- अव चक्रदः (*ava cakradaḥ*)—you make a sound
- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—you who are called Pavamāna
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with milk and the like
- अंजानः (*aṃjānaḥ*)—joined
- निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*)—the prepared
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods, the station
- अर्षसि (*arṣasi*)—you approach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you the showerer of desires, being well refined, being purified in the ten-fold strainer of woollen fibres, make a sound in the vessel. O Soma called Pavamāna, joined with milk and the like, you approach the prepared station of the gods.

##### English translation
The showerer of benefits, cleansed and filtered in the woollen fleece. you cry aloud in the water ; Soma Pavamana, mixed with the curds and milk, you go to the prepared (station) of the gods.

> पव॑स्व॒ वाज॑सातये॒ऽभि विश्वा॑नि॒ काव्या॑ ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवस्व । वाजसातये । अभि । विश्वानि । काव्या ।  
> त्वं । समुद्रं । प्रथमः । वि । धारयः । देवेभ्यः । सोम । मत्सरः ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वं । समुद्रं । प्रथमः । वि । धारयः । देवेभ्यः । सोम । मत्सरः ॥ २३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The block repeats the Pada text of the verse (त्वं समुद्रं प्रथमो वि धारयो देवेभ्यः सोम मत्सरः ॥ २३ ॥ (*tvaṃ samudraṃ prathamo vi dhārayo devebhyaḥ soma matsaraḥ ‖ 23 ‖*)), so there is no commentary in it.**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम विश्वानि सर्वाणि काव्या कविकर्माणि स्तोत्राण्यभिलक्ष्य वाजसातयेऽन्नलाभाय पवस्व । क्षर । हे सोम देवेभ्यो देवानां मत्सरो मदकरः
> प्रथमः सर्वदेवानां मुख्यस्त्वं समुद्रमंतरिक्षं कलशं ना वि धारयः । विशेषेण धारयसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, looking to all the compositions of the poets (काव्या (*kāvyā*) = the praises, the works of sages), flow (पवस्व (*pavasva*) = stream) for the winning of food (वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)). O Soma, you who are the exhilarator (मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*) = intoxicator) of the gods, the first (प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)), the chief of all the gods, sustain (वि धारयः (*vi dhārayaḥ*) = you uphold specially) the samudra, the atmosphere or the vessel."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma)
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- काव्या अभि (*kāvyā abhi*)—having regard to the praises
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for the winning of food
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the gods
- मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)—the giver of joy
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—the most excellent
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*)—the atmosphere
- वि धारयः (*vi dhārayaḥ*)—you have supported exceedingly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, facing all the praises, flow for the winning of food. O Soma, you who are the giver of joy to the gods and the most excellent, support the atmosphere exceedingly.

##### English translation
Flow, Soma, to all praises to procure food (for us) ; you, the exhilarator of the gods, are the chief supporter of the firmament.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम तादृशस्त्वं पार्थिवं रजो लोकं प्रति दिव्यानि च रजांसि प्रतिः

> विप्रासो विप्रा मेधाविनो मतिभिः स्तुतिभिर्थीतिभिरंगुलीभिश्च शुभ्रं श्वेतवर्णं
> त्वां हिन्वंति । प्रेरयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Soma: "O Soma, being such, flow swiftly, together with your supports, towards the terrestrial world and the celestial regions." परि पवस्व (*pari pavasva*) is glossed "flow all around". "O far-seeing Soma, the wise ones, the sages, with praises and with धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*), that is, the fingers, urge you on (हिन्वंति (*hinvaṃti*) means "impel"), you who are of white colour."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, the well-known one
- पार्थिवं रजः (*pārthivaṃ rajaḥ*)—to the terrestrial world
- च (*ca*)—and
- दिव्या (*divyā*)—facing also the celestial world
- धर्मभिः (*dharmabhiḥ*)—together with your powers that sustain
- तु (*tu*)—swiftly
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow
- विचक्षण (*vicakṣaṇa*)—O Soma, who are of subtle vision
- विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)—the wise
- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—with praises
- धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)—with fingers
- शुभ्रं (*śubhraṃ*)—of bright colour
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- हिन्वंति (*hinvaṃti*)—urge on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you the well-known, flow swiftly, together with your sustaining powers, towards the terrestrial world and the celestial world. O Soma of subtle vision, the wise urge you on, bright in colour, with praises and with their fingers.

##### English translation
Flow quickly, Soma, with your supports, to the terrestrial and celestial worlds ; the sages express you radiant. O observer of all, with praises and with their fingers,

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 86

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पवमानाः पूयमानाः सोमा धारयात्मीयया पवित्रमतीत्यासृक्षत ।
> सृज्यंते । कीदृशाः । मरुत्वंतो मरुद्भिर्युक्ता मत्सरा मदकरा इंद्रिया
> इंद्रजुष्टाः । मेधां स्तुतिं प्रयांस्यन्नानि चाभिलक्ष्य स्तोतृभ्य उभयं कर्तुं
> वा हया गंतार एते सृज्यंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma juices, being purified (पवमानाः (*pavamānāḥ*)), are released through the filter in their own stream. What sort are they? मरुत्वंतः (*marutvaṃtaḥ*): joined with the Maruts; मत्सराः (*matsarāḥ*): intoxicating; इंद्रियाः (*iṃdriyāḥ*): dear to Indra. They are हयाः (*hayāḥ*), "goers". Having in view मेधां (*medhāṃ*), praise, and प्रयांसि (*prayāṃsi*), foods, or in order to provide both to the praisers, these are released.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुत्वंतः (*marutvaṃtaḥ*)—joined with the Maruts
- मत्सराः (*matsarāḥ*)—causing delight
- इंद्रियाः (*iṃdriyāḥ*)—pleasing to Indra
- हयाः (*hayāḥ*)—swift-moving
- मेधां अभि (*medhāṃ abhi*)—with a view to praise
- प्रयांसि च (*prayāṃsi ca*)—and providing foods
- पवमानाः (*pavamānāḥ*)—the Soma juices that are being purified
- पवित्रं अति (*pavitraṃ ati*)—crossing the ten-fold filter
- धारया (*dhārayā*)—in the form of a stream
- असृक्षत (*asṛkṣata*)—flow out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma juices, which are joined with the Maruts, delight-giving, dear to Indra, swift-moving, providing foods with a view to praise, and undergoing purification, cross the ten-fold filter and flow out in the form of a stream.

##### English translation
Your purified juices are let flow through the filter in a stream accompanied by the Maruts, exhilarating, pleasing Indra, swift-moving, bringing praise and food.

#### Ṛk 26

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒पो वसा॑नः॒ परि॒ कोश॑मर्ष॒तींदु॑र्हिया॒नः सो॒तृभिः॑ ।  
> ज॒नय॒ इज्ज्योति॑र्मं॒दना॑ अवीवश॒द्गाः कृ॑ण्वा॒नो न नि॒र्णिजं॑॥

> अपः । वसानः । परि । कोशं । अर्षति । इंदुः । हियानः । सोतृभिः ।  
> जनयन् । ज्योतिः ! मंदनाः । अवीवशत् । गाः । कृष्ण्वानः । न । निःनिजं ॥ २६ ॥

### Printed p. 87

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपो वसतीवरीर्वसान आच्छादयन् सोतृभिरभिषुण्वद्भिर्हियानः प्रेर्यमाणः इंदुः सोमः कोशं कलशं पर्यर्षति । प्रति गच्छति । किं च ज्योतिर्दिप्तिं
> जनयन्नुत्पादयन् गा गव्यानि क्षेरादीनि निर्णिजमात्मनो रूपं कृष्णानः कुर्वन्
> मिश्रयन् सोऽयं सोमः । नः संप्रत्यर्थे । इदानीं मंदनाः स्तुतीरवीवशत् ।
> कामयते ॥ वश कांत् । लुजु चजि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indu, that is Soma, clothing himself in the अपः (*apaḥ*) (the Vasatīvarī waters) and urged on by the pressers (सोतृभिः (*sotṛbhiḥ*)), goes to the receptacle (कोशं (*kośaṃ*)), the vessel. Moreover, generating light (ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*), radiance) and making गाः (*gāḥ*), the cow-products such as milk, into निर्णिजं (*nirṇijaṃ*), his own form, mixing with them, this Soma now (न (*na*) is used in the sense of "now") desires (अवीवशत् (*avīvaśat*)) the praises (मंदनाः (*maṃdanāḥ*)). He glosses अवीवशत् (*avīvaśat*) as "desires", from the root वश (*vaśa*) in the sense of wishing, with the luṅ/caṅ form.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the Vasatīvarī waters
- वसानः (*vasānaḥ*)—clothed in
- सोतृभिः (*sotṛbhiḥ*)—by the pressing priests
- हियानः (*hiyānaḥ*)—pressed
- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—Soma
- कोशं परि (*kośaṃ pari*)—towards the vessel
- अर्षति (*arṣati*)—flows
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—radiance
- जनयन् (*janayan*)—producing
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—milk and the like
- निर्णिजं (*nirṇijaṃ*)—having a form of his own
- कृष्ण्वानः (*kṛṣṇvānaḥ*)—making
- न (*na*)—now
- मंदनाः (*maṃdanāḥ*)—praises
- अवीवशत् (*avīvaśat*)—desires

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, mingled with the Vasatīvarī waters and pressed by the pressing priests, flows towards the vessel. Producing radiance, and making milk and the like take on his own form, he now desires praises.

##### English translation
Indu clothed with waters effused by the worshippers rushes to the receptacle, generating light, identifying its form with the (products of the) cows, he covets now (our) praises-

## Sūkta 108 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पहस्वेति षोडशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं । आद्यद्वृचस्य गौरिवीतिर्नाम शक्तिपुत्र
> ऋषिः । तृतीयायाः शक्तिर्नाम वासिष्ठः । ततः पंचानां द्वृचानामूरुर्नामांगिरस ऋजिश्वा नाम भारद्वाज ऊर्ध्वसद्मा नामांगिरसः कृतयशा नाम कश्चित्
> सोऽप्यांगिरस ऋणंचयो नाम राजर्षिरित्येते क्रमेणर्षयः । एवं त्रयोदश

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta पहस्वेति (*pahasveti*) has sixteen Ṛks and is the fifth sūkta. For the first two Ṛks the seer is Gauriviti, son of Śakti; for the third, Śakti Vāsiṣṭha. Then for five pairs of Ṛks the seers are, in order, Ūru Āṅgirasa; Ṛjiśvā Bhāradvāja; Ūrdhvasadmā Āṅgirasa; Kṛtayaśā, also an Āṅgirasa; and Ṛṇaṃcaya, a royal seer. Thus thirteen Ṛks go by.

### Printed p. 88

> गताः ततस्ति सृणां वासिष्ठः शक्तिः । प्रथमातृतीयाद्या आयुजः ककुभः । द्वितीया
> चतुर्थ्याद्या युजः सतोबृहत्यः । स सुन्वे यो वसूनामित्येषा तु यवमध्या
> गायत्री । पवमानः सोमो देवता। तथा चानुक्रम्यते । पवस्व षोळश गौरिवीतिर्द्वृचं शक्तिरेकामूरुर्यजिश्वोर्ध्वसद्मा कृतयशा ऋणंचय इत्यृषयो
> द्वृचास्तिस्रः शक्तिः काकुभाः प्रगाथाः स सुन्वे गायत्री यवमध्यॆति ॥ गतो
> विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

After the thirteen, for the following three Ṛks the seer is Śakti Vāsiṣṭha. The first, third and the other odd-numbered Ṛks are Ayuj Kakubh; the second, fourth and the other even-numbered Ṛks are Yuj Satobṛhatī. But the Ṛk स सुन्वे यो वसूनां (*sa sunve yo vasūnāṃ*) is a Gāyatrī of the Yavamadhyā kind. The deity is Pavamāna Soma. He cites the Anukramaṇī, which says the same (seers, metres and the Gāyatrī Yavamadhyā). The viniyoga has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "Pavasva" is the fifth sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. It contains sixteen Ṛks. For the first two Ṛks of this sūkta the seer is Gauriviti, son of the seer Śakti; for the third Ṛk the seer is Śakti, son of Vasiṣṭha. From there onward, for two Ṛks (4-5) the seer is Ūru Āṅgirasa; for the next two (6-7) Ṛjiśvā, son of Bharadvāja; for the next two (8-9) Ūrdhvasadmā Āṅgirasa; for the next two (10-11) Kṛtayaśā Āṅgirasa; and for the next two (12-13) the royal seer called Ṛṇaṃcaya. After thirteen Ṛks in this way, for the next three Ṛks (14-16) the seer is the Śakti, son of the seer Vasiṣṭha, mentioned earlier. The deity is Pavamāna Soma. The odd-numbered Ṛks of this sūkta, 1, 3 and so on, are in the Kakubh metre; but the thirteenth Ṛk only, "स सुन्वे यो वसूनां (*sa sunve yo vasūnāṃ*)", is in the metre called Gāyatrī Yavamadhyā. The even-numbered Ṛks, 2, 4 and so on, are in the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: "Pavasva, sixteen; Gauriviti, two Ṛks; Śakti, one; Ūru, Ṛjiśvā, Ūrdhvasadmā, Kṛtayaśā, Ṛṇaṃcaya are the seers, two Ṛks each; three: Śakti; Kākubha Pragāthas; 'Sa sunve' Gāyatrī Yavamadhyā." The viniyoga has been stated earlier.

Sūkta—108
Maṇḍala—9. Anuvāka—7. Sūkta—108.
Aṣṭaka—7. Adhyāya—5. Varga—13, 14, 19.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—16.
Seer: 1, 2: Gauriviti. 1-3, 14-16: Śakti. 4, 5: Ūru. 6, 7, 9: Ṛjiśvā **NOTE**. 8, 9: Ūrdhvasadmā. 10, 11: Kṛtayaśā. 12, 13: Ṛṇaṃcaya.
Deity: Pavamāna Soma.
Metre: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 15: Kakubh. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16: Satobṛhatī. 13: Gāyatrī Yavamadhyā.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑स्व॒ मधु॑मत्तम॒ इंद्रा॑य सोम क्रतु॒वित्त॑मो॒ मदः॑ ।  
> महि॑ द्यु॒क्षत॑मो॒ मदः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवस्व । मधुमत् ऽतमः । इंद्राय । सोम । क्रतुवित् ऽतमः । मदः ।  
> महि । द्युक्षतमः । मदः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम मधुमत्तमोऽतिशयेन माधुर्योपेतस्त्वमिंद्रायेंद्रार्थं
> मदो मदकरः सन् पवस्व । क्षर । कीद्रशः ! क्रतुवित्तमोऽत्यंतं प्रज्ञायाः
> कर्मणो ना लंभको महि महान् महानीयो वा द्युक्षतमोऽत्यंतं दीपो
> मदो मदहेतुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, being most sweet, abounding in sweetness, flow (पवस्व (*pavasva*), "stream") for Indra, as an intoxicating drink (मदः (*madaḥ*)). Of what sort? क्रतुवित्तमः (*kratuvittamaḥ*): one who greatly obtains the knowledge of the rite. महि (*mahi*): great, or worthy of honour. द्युक्षतमः (*dyukṣatamaḥ*): most brilliant. मदः (*madaḥ*): the cause of intoxication."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- मधुमत्तमः (*madhumattamaḥ*)—endowed with sweetness
- क्रतुवित्तमः (*kratuvittamaḥ*)—the best accomplisher of rites
- महि (*mahi*)—the great
- द्युक्षतमः (*dyukṣatamaḥ*)—most resplendent
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—the delight-giver; you
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—producing delight
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who are endowed with sweetness, the best accomplisher of rites, great, most resplendent and delight-giving, flow, producing delight, for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Soma, who are most sweet-flavoured, most intelligent, the exhilarator, flow for Indra, the great, the most brilliant, the exhilarating.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्य॑ ते पी॒ता वृ॑ष॒भो वृ॑षा॒यते॒ऽस्य पी॒ता स्व॒र्विदः॑ ।  
> स सु॒प्रके॑तो अ॒भ्य॑क्रमा॒दिषोच्चा॒ वाजं॒ नैत॑शः ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 90

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्य । ते । पीत्वा । वृषभः । वृषयते । अस्य । पीता । स्वःविदः ।  
> सः । सुप्रकेतः । अभि । अक्रमीत् । इषः । अच्छ । वाजं । न । एतशः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषभः कामानां वर्षक इंद्रो यस्य ते त्वां पीता वृषायते वृषभवदाचरति । किं च स्वर्दृशः सर्वस्य दर्शकस्यास्य ते तव पीता पाने सति सुप्रकेतः
> सुप्रज्ञः स इंद्र इपः शत्रूणामन्नान्यभ्यक्रमीत् । अभिक्रामति । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> वाजं नैतशः । एतश इत्यश्वनाम । यथाश्वो वाजं संग्राममभिगच्छति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*) is Indra, the showerer of desires. Having drunk you, he acts like a bull (वृषायते (*vṛṣāyate*)). Moreover, when there is the drinking of you, who are the beholder of all (स्वर्दृशः (*svardṛśaḥ*)), सुप्रकेतः (*supraketaḥ*), the well-minded Indra, advances upon (अभ्यक्रमीत् (*abhyakramīt*)) the इषः (*iṣaḥ*), the foods of the enemies. The illustration is वाजं नैतशः (*vājaṃ naitaśaḥ*): एतशः (*etaśaḥ*) is a name for a horse; as a horse goes to the वाजं (*vājaṃ*), the battle, so does he.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एतशः (*etaśaḥ*)—a horse
- वाजं न (*vājaṃ na*)—as it enters the battlefield
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—Indra, the showerer of desires
- यस्य ते (*yasya te*)—you, by drinking whom
- पीतात्वा (*pītātvā*)—having drunk
- वृषायते (*vṛṣāyate*)—he becomes powerful like a bull
- स्वर्द्वशः (*svardvaśaḥ*)—the beholder of all
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this same you
- पीता (*pītā*)—when there is drinking
- सुप्रकेतः (*supraketaḥ*)—of excellent understanding
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Indra
- इषः अच्छ (*iṣaḥ accha*)—confronting the enemies' food
- अभ्यक्रमीत् (*abhyakramīt*)—advances upon

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a horse enters the battlefield, Indra, the showerer of desires, by drinking you becomes powerful like a bull; when there is the drinking of you, the beholder of all, that same Indra, of excellent understanding, confronts the enemies' food and advances upon it.

##### English translation
By drinking whom the showerer Indra is invigorated, by drinking you who are the beholder of everything, the intelligent (Indra) reaches the viands (of the enemy) as a horse (reaches) the battle.

> त्वं ह्य१॒ं॑ग दैव्या॒ पव॑मान॒ जनि॑मानि द्यु॒मत्त॑मः ।  
> अ॒मृ॒त॒त्वा य॑ घो॒षयः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 91
#### Ṛk 3 (continued)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । हि । अंग । दैव्या । पवमान । जनिमानि । द्युमत् 5तमः ।  
> अमृतत्वाय । घोषयः ॥ ३ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान पूयमान सोम द्युमत्तमोऽतिशयेन दीप्तिमांस्त्वं
> त्वमेव दैव्या देवसंबंधीनि जनिमानि जन्मानि । देवानित्यर्थः । तानभिलक्षामृत
> त्वाय तेषाममरणायांग क्षिप्रं घोषयः । शब्दायसे ॥ घुषिर् विशब्दनॆ ।
> ण्यंतस्य लेटि रूपं । हियोगादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O purifying Soma, you who are the most radiant, you alone, for the immortality of the gods, quickly proclaim (घोषयः (*ghoṣayaḥ*), you cause to sound) the births pertaining to the gods, that is, the gods themselves. He explains घोषयः (*ghoṣayaḥ*) as "you cause to sound", from the root घुषिर् (*ghuṣir*) in the sense of sounding.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O Soma-deva, called Pavamāna
- द्युमत्तमः (*dyumattamaḥ*)—shining exceedingly
- त्वं हि (*tvaṃ hi*)—you alone
- दैव्या (*daivyā*)—pertaining to the gods
- जनिमानि (*janimāni*)—the births (of all the gods)
- अमृतत्वाय (*amṛtatvāya*)—so that freedom from death may come about
- अंग (*aṃga*)—quickly
- घोषयः (*ghoṣayaḥ*)—you have proclaimed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, called Pavamāna, you who shine exceedingly have proclaimed that all the gods may have freedom from death.

##### English translation
For you, Pavamana, who are most brilliant, quickly shout to the races of the gods for (the sake of their) immortality:—

### Printed p. 92

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नवगो नवनीयगतिः यद्वा नवभिर्मासैः सत्रस्यानुष्ठाता दध्यजीतन्नामकोऽंगिरा येन सोमेन पणिभिरपहृतानां गवां द्वारमपोर्णुते
> आपाच्छादयति विवृतमकार्षित् विप्रासस्तन्मुखाः सर्वे मेधाविनोऽंगिरसो येन
> च सोमेनापिरे एतैरपहृता गा आप्नुवन् किंच देवानामिंद्रादीनां सुम्मे
> सुखे यज्ञेन संजाते सति चारुणः कल्याणस्यामृतस्कोदकस्य संबंधीनि श्रवांस्यन्नानि येन च सोमेन यजमाना आनशुः आप्नुवन् अलभंत स त्वं देवानाममृतत्वाय शब्दायस इति पूर्वेण समन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

नवगो (*navago*) means one whose course is to be praised; or else, one who performs a sattra of nine months. Dadhyañc, an Aṅgiras, by which Soma opens the door of the cows carried off by the Paṇis, which had been covered; all the wise Aṅgirases, led by him, by which Soma obtained the cows carried off by these. Further, when the sacrifice that gives happiness to the gods, Indra and the rest, has come into being, the sacrificers by which Soma obtained the foods connected with the auspicious ambrosial water. The construction is with the preceding: "you proclaim for the immortality of the gods".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नवग्वः (*navagvaḥ*)—who performed the sattra sacrifice in nine months
- दध्यज् (*dadhyaj*)—the sage named Dadhyañc
- येन (*yena*)—by whose help of yours
- अपोर्णुते (*aporṇute*)—he is able to open the door that had shut in the cows
- विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)—the wise Aṅgirases
- येन (*yena*)—by whose help of yours
- आपिरे (*āpire*)—they obtained all the cows (and)
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—for the gods, Indra and others
- सुम्मे (*summe*)—when the happy sacrifice has begun
- चारुणः (*cāruṇaḥ*)—beneficial
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—connected with water
- श्रवांसि (*śravāṃsi*)—the foods
- येन (*yena*)—by whose help of yours
- आनशुः (*ānaśuḥ*)—the sacrificers obtained (you, such as you are, proclaimed freedom from death to the gods)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, by whose help the sage named Dadhyañc, who performed the sattra sacrifice in nine months, is able to open the door that had shut in the cows; by whose help the wise Aṅgirases obtained all the cows; by whose help the sacrificers obtained the beneficial foods connected with water when the sacrifice giving happiness to Indra and the other gods began: you proclaimed freedom from death to the gods.

##### English translation
(You) through whom Dadhyanch the offerer of the nine days' rite opened (the cave), through whom the rishis recovertd (the stolen cows), through whom under the protection of the gods the worshippers obtained the sustenance of the delicious (ambrosial) water—

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्य स एष सुतोऽभिषुतः सोमोऽव्योऽनेर्वारेभिर्वालैस्तेभ्यः पवित्रेभ्यो
> धारयात्मीयया पवते । कलशमभिलक्ष्य क्षरति । कीदृशः । मदिंतमो मादयितृतमोऽपामिवोदकानामूर्मिः संघात इव क्रीळन्नितस्ततः संक्रीडमानः पवते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, pressed, flows from those purifiers, the hairs of the sheep, in his own stream; he flows aiming at the vessel. Of what kind? Most exhilarating, sporting here and there like a wave of waters, a mass.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदिंतमः (*madiṃtamaḥ*)—the one who gives exceeding joy
- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—the well-known
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—the pressed
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—Soma-deva
- अव्यः (*avyaḥ*)—of wool
- वारेभिः (*vārebhiḥ*)—through the fibres of the ten-fold strainer
- धारया (*dhārayā*)—in the form of a stream
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—of waters
- ऊर्मिः इव (*ūrmiḥ iva*)—like waves
- क्रीळन् (*krīḷan*)—sporting
- पवते (*pavate*)—flows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva, who gives exceeding joy, the well-known, the pressed, flows through the fibres of the woollen ten-fold strainer in the form of a stream, sporting like waves of water.

##### English translation
This (Soma) when effused flows most exhilarating through the woolen fleece, sporting like a wave of water.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य उ॒स्रिया॒ अप्या॑ अं॒तरश्म॑नो॒ निर्गा अकृं॑त॒दोज॑सा ।  
> अ॒भि व्र॒जं त॑त्निषे॒ गव्य॒मश्वं॑ व॒र्मीव॑ धृष्ण॒वा रु॑ज ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 94

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । उस्त्रियाः । अप्याः । अंतः । अश्मनः । निः । गाः । अकृंतत् । ओजसा ।  
> अभि । व्रजं । तत्निषे । गव्यं । अश्वं । वर्मीऽइव । धृष्ट्णो इति । आ । रुज ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः सोम उस्रिया उत्सरणशीला अप्याः ॥ अप इत्यंतरिक्षनाम । तस्माद्भवे
> छंदसीति यत् ॥ अंतरिक्षस्था अहिप्रभृतिभिरसुरैरपहृत्य निहिता गा अपोऽश्मनः ।
> मेघनामैतत् । मेघादंतरोजसा बलेन निरकृंतत् निरच्चिनत् । अंतरिक्षादृष्टिमकार्षिदित्यर्थः । स त्वमसुरैरपहृतं गव्यं गोसंबंधिनमश्वमश्वेषु
> भवं व्रजं समूहमभि तत्निषे । अभितो व्याप्योषि ॥ तनु विस्तारे । छांदसे लिट
> तनिपत्योश्चंदसीत्युपधालोपः ॥ किं च हे धृष्णो शत्रुधर्षणशील सोम स त्वं
> वर्मीव कवचीव शूर आ रुज । असुरानाजहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma who with his might split from within the rock the quick-flowing waters of the atmosphere, carried off by Ahi and other Asuras and set down; *apaḥ* is a name of the atmosphere, and अश्मनः (*aśmanaḥ*) a name of the cloud. That is, he made rain fall from the atmosphere. You spread over, on all sides, the herd connected with cows and horses carried off by the Asuras. Further, O bold Soma, who are accustomed to overpower enemies, like a mailed hero, smite the Asuras.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—you who
- उस्रियाः (*usriyāḥ*)—flowing
- अप्याः (*apyāḥ*)—abiding in the atmosphere
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the waters
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by your own power
- अश्मनः अंतः (*aśmanaḥ aṃtaḥ*)—from within the cloud
- निः अकृंतत् (*niḥ akṛṃtat*)—split and poured down
- गव्यं (*gavyaṃ*)—connected with cows
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—consisting of horses
- व्रजं (*vrajaṃ*)—the herd
- अभि तत्निषे (*abhi tatniṣe*)—you stand pervading
- धृण्णो (*dhṛṇṇo*)—O Soma, overpowerer of enemies
- वर्मीव (*varmīva*)—like a hero wearing armour
- आ रुज (*ā ruja*)—conquer the enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you who by your own power split and poured down from within the cloud the flowing waters of the atmosphere, such as you are, you stand pervading the herd connected with cows and horses. O Soma, overpowerer of enemies, like a hero who wears armour, conquer the enemies.

##### English translation
You, who by your might extricated from the rock the quick-moving cows abiding in the waters, you have spread out a pasturage for cattle and horses ; like a mailed (warrior) slay (the Asuras), brave (Soma)-

### Printed p. 95
#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ सो॑ता॒ परि॑ षिंच॒ताश्वं॒ न स्तोम॑म॒पुरं॑ रज॒स्तुरं॑ ।  
> वनक्रक्षमुदपुतं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । सोत । परि । सिंचत . अश्वं । न । स्तोमं । अप्तुरं । रजतुरं ।  
> वसक्रक्ष्यं । उदपुप्रतं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋत्विजः आ सोत । सोममभिसुणुत ॥ षुञ् अभिषवे । लोटि
> च्छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तस्य तबादेशः ॥ किंच परि षिंचत ।
> परितस्तं वसतीवर्यादिभिः सिंचत । कीदृशं । अश्वं नाश्वमिव वेगिनं स्तोमं
> स्तोतव्यमपुरमंतरिक्षस्थितानामुदकानां प्रेरकं रजस्तुरं तेजसां च प्रेरकं ।
> वनऋक्षमुदकानामर्षकं । यद्वा । काष्ठेषु पात्रेषु विप्रकीर्णं । उदपुतमुदके गच्छंतं प्लवमानं सोममभिसुणुताभिषिंचत च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O priests, press Soma, and sprinkle him all around with the vasatīvarī waters. Of what kind? Swift like a horse, to be praised, the impeller of the waters standing in the atmosphere, the impeller of lights, the sender-forth of waters; or else, scattered about in wooden vessels; going in the water, floating. Press and sprinkle such Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्वं न (*aśvaṃ na*)—swift-going like a horse
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—praiseworthy
- अप्तुरं (*apturaṃ*)—impelling the waters
- रजस्तुरं (*rajasturaṃ*)—causing light to spread
- वनऋक्षं (*vanaṛkṣaṃ*)—that pours down rain
- उदपुत्रं (*udaputraṃ*)—that moves in the waters
- आ सोत (*ā sota*)—press
- परि षिंचित (*pari ṣiṃcita*)—sprinkle all around

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, press Soma, who is swift-going like a horse, praiseworthy, impelling the waters, causing light to spread, pouring down rain, moving in the waters. Sprinkle him all around.

##### English translation
Pour forth (the Soma), sprinkle it round like a horse, adorable, dispenser of rain, dispenser cf light, showerer of fluid, swimming in water—

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒हस्र॑धारं वृष॒भं प॑यो॒वृधं॑ प्रि॒यं दे॒वाय॒ जन्म॑ने ।  
> ऋ॒तेन॒ य ऋ॒तजा॑तो विवावृ॒धे राजा॑ दे॒व ऋ॒तं बृ॒हत् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सहस्रधारं । वृषभं । पयःवृधं । प्रियं । देवाय । जन्मने ।  
> ऋतेन । यः । ऋतजातः । विववृधे । राजा । देवः । ऋतं । बृहत् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहस्रधारं बहुधारोपेतं वृषभं कामानां वर्षकं पयोवृधमुदकानां वर्धकं प्रियं प्रीणयितारं तं सोमं देवाय देवसंबंधिने जन्मने
> देवेभ्यस्तदर्थमभिषुणुत । ऋतजात उदकाज्ञातो यो राजा सोम ऋतेन
> वसतीवर्याख्येनोदकेन विववृधे विशेषेण वर्धते। कीदृशः । देवो द्योतमानः स्तोतव्यो वा ऋतं सत्यभूतः सन् बृहन्महान् । तमासुनुतेति पूर्वेण
> समन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Press that Soma, who has a thousand streams, a showerer of desires, increaser of waters, dear, a pleaser, for the gods, for the divine race. The king Soma, born of water, grows exceedingly by the water called vasatīvarī. Of what kind? Divine, shining or to be praised, true in nature, great. The construction is with the preceding: "press him".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Soma who
- ऋतजातः (*ṛtajātaḥ*)—born of water
- राजा (*rājā*)—and lord
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—joined with water
- वि ववृधे (*vi vavṛdhe*)—grows, such a one
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—of divine nature
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—true in nature
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—great, such a one
- सहस्रधारं (*sahasradhāraṃ*)—having many streams
- वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*)—showerer of desires
- पयोवृधं (*payovṛdhaṃ*)—increaser of water
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—causing joy: such Soma
- देवाय जन्मने (*devāya janmane*)—for the satisfaction of the divine people
- press him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Press for the satisfaction of the divine people that Soma who, born of water and a lord, grows joined with the waters, and who is of divine nature, who has many streams, is a showerer of desires, an increaser of waters, causing joy.

##### English translation
Thousand-streamed, showerer of benefits, augmenter of water, affectionate ; (pour it forth) for the race of the gods which water-born is fostered by the water, the king, the god, the true, the great.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि द्यु॒म्नं बृ॒हद्यश॒ इष॑स्पते दिदी॒हि दे॑व देव॒युः ।  
> वि कोशं॑ मध्य॒मं यु॑व ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । द्युम्नं । बृहत् । यशः । इषः । पते । दिदीहि । देव ' देवयुः ।  
> वि : कोशं । मध्यमं । युव ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इषस्पतेऽन्नस्य पते हे देव स्तोतव्य सोम देवयुर्देवकामस्त्वं
> द्युम्नं द्योतमानं बृहत्प्रभूतं यशोऽन्नमस्मभ्यमभि दिदीहि । अभिमुख्येन
> प्रकाशय । प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥ आमंत्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्वेन पादादित्वादनिघातः ॥
> किंच मध्यममंतरिक्षस्थितं कोशं मेघं वि युव । वृष्ट्यर्थं विगमय ।
> विश्लेषय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O lord of food (इषस्पते (*iṣaspate*)), O divine Soma worthy of praise, desiring the gods (देवयुः (*devayuḥ*)), make shine forth for us (अभि दिदीहि (*abhi didīhi*)) brilliant and abundant food (द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*), बृहत् (*bṛhat*), यशः (*yaśaḥ*)). अभि दिदीहि (*abhi didīhi*) means "illumine in our direction", that is, "give". Further, split open (वि युव (*vi yuva*)), for the sake of rain, the middle receptacle (कोशं (*kośaṃ*)), the cloud standing in the atmosphere; separate it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इषस्पते (*iṣaspate*)—O protector of food
- देव (*deva*)—O shining Soma
- देवयुः (*devayuḥ*)—you who desire the gods
- द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*)—the shining
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—the abundant
- यशः (*yaśaḥ*)—food
- अभि दिदीहि (*abhi didīhi*)—make shine forth (give) to us
- मध्यमं (*madhyamaṃ*)—standing in the atmosphere
- कोशं (*kośaṃ*)—the cloud
- वि युव (*vi yuva*)—split open for the sake of rain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, protector of food and shining, you who desire the gods, make shine forth (give) to us food that is brilliant and abundant. Split open the cloud that stands in the atmosphere, for the sake of rain.

##### English translation
Divine (Soma) lord of viands, who are devoted to the gods, bestow upon us brilliant and abundant food ; separate the mid-aerial receptacle.

### Printed p. 98
#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ व॑च्यस्व सुदक्ष च॒म्वोः॑ सु॒तो वि॒शां वर्ह्नि॒र्न वि॒श्वतिः॑ ।  
> वृ॒ष्टिं दि॒वः प॑वस्व री॒तिम॒पां जिन्वा॒ गवि॑ष्टये॒ धिय॑ॆः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । वच्यस्व । सुदक्ष । चन्वोः । सुतः । विशां । वह्निः । न । विश्वतिः ।  
> वृष्टिं । दिवः । पवस्व । रीतिं । अपां । जिन्न । गोs इष्टये । धियः ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुदक्ष सुबल सोम चन्नोरधिषवणफलकयोः सुतोऽभिषुतस्त्वं विशां
> प्रजानां वह्निर्न वोढा विश्वती राजेव सर्वासां प्रजानां वोढा त्वमा वच्यस्व ।
> आगच्छ । कलशमापवस्व ॥ वचेर्गत्यर्थस्य व्यत्ययेन श्यनि रूपं ॥ किंच त्वं वृष्टिं
> वृष्यमाणामपामुदकानां रीतिं गतिं दिवो द्युलोकात्पवस्व । कुरु । ततो गविष्टये गामात्मन इच्चते यजमानाय धियः कर्माणि जिन्व । आपूरय ॥
> क्रिशवर् ।
> सुदक्ष—उत्तमवाद शक्तियुळ्ळ ऎलै सोमने ! चव्वोः—हिंडुव हलगॆगळल्लि । सुतः—
> हिंडल्पट्टवनू । विश्पतिः न—राजनंतॆ । विशां—प्रजॆगळिगॆल्ल । वह्निः—वाहकनू (पालकनू)
> आद नीनु । आ वच्यस्व—दयमाडु । वृष्टिं—वृष्टिरूपवाद । अपां रीतिं—उदकगळ
> प्रवाहवन्नु । दिवः—द्युलोकदिंद । पवस्व—सुरिसु । गविष्टये—गोवन्नु अपेक्षिसुव
> यजमाननिगॆ । धियः—कर्मगळन्नु । जिन्व—तुंबु (फलप्रदवागुवंतॆ माडु).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma of good strength (सुदक्ष (*sudakṣa*)), pressed in the two pressing boards (चन्वोः (*canvoḥ*)), you who, like a king (विश्पतिः न (*viśpatiḥ na*)), bear all the people (विशां वह्निः (*viśāṃ vahniḥ*)), come (आ वच्यस्व (*ā vacyasva*)): flow into the vessel. Further, from the heavenly world (दिवः (*divaḥ*)) cause to flow the course (रीतिं (*rītiṃ*)) of the waters (अपां (*apāṃ*)) that are to be rained, namely the rain (वृष्टिं (*vṛṣṭiṃ*)). Then, for the sacrificer who desires cattle (गविष्टये (*gaviṣṭaye*)), fill up (जिन्व (*jinva*)) the rites (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुदक्ष (*sudakṣa*)—O Soma of excellent strength
- चव्वोः (*cavvoḥ*)—in the pressing boards
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed
- विश्पतिः न (*viśpatiḥ na*)—like a king
- विशां (*viśāṃ*)—of all the people
- वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—the bearer (protector)
- आ वच्यस्व (*ā vacyasva*)—be gracious
- वृष्टिं (*vṛṣṭiṃ*)—in the form of rain
- अपां रीतिं (*apāṃ rītiṃ*)—the flow of the waters
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the heavenly world
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—pour down
- गविष्टये (*gaviṣṭaye*)—for the sacrificer who desires cattle
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—the rites
- जिन्व (*jinva*)—fill (make fruitful)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma of excellent strength, pressed in the pressing boards, protector of all the people like a king, be gracious. Pour down from the heavenly world the flow of waters in the form of rain. For the sacrificer who desires cattle, increase the rite; make it fruitful.

##### English translation
Divine (Soma) lord of viands, who are devoted to the gods, bestow upon us brilliant and abundant food ; separate the mid-aerial receptacle.

### Printed p. 99

##### English translation
Come, powerful (Soma) effused into the cups, like a prince the sustainer of the people; pour the course of the waters, the rain from heaven ; accomplish the rites for the worshipper who seeks cattle

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒तमु॒ त्यं म॑द॒च्युतं॑ स॒हस्र॑सधारं वृष॒भं दिवो॑ दुहुः ।  
> विश्वा॒ वसू॑नि॒ बिभ्र॑तं ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वितं । ऊं इति । त्यं । मदच्युतं । सहस्रधारं । वृषभं । दिवः । दुहुः ।  
> विश्वा । वसूनि । बिभ्रतं ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवः देवान्कामयमाना ऋत्विज एतं त्यं तमिमं सोममेव दुहुः ।
> दुदुहुः । दुहंति । ग्रावाणो वत्सा ऋत्विजो दुहंतीति तैत्तरीयकब्राह्मणं ।
> तै. सं. ६-२-११-४ । कीदृशं सोमं । मदच्युतं मदस्य प्रेरकं सहस्रधारं बहुधारं वृषभं कामानां वर्षकं विश्वा सर्वाणि वसूनि धनानि बिभ्रतं धारयंतं
> सोमं दुहंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The officiating priests, desiring the gods, milk this very Soma (एतं त्यं (*etaṃ tyaṃ*)). दुहुः (*duhuḥ*) is the same as दुदुहुः (*duduhuḥ*) and दुहंति (*duhaṃti*). He cites the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa: ग्रावाणो वत्सा ऋत्विजो दुहंतीति (*grāvāṇo vatsā ṛtvijo duhaṃtīti*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-11-4). What kind of Soma? The impeller of exhilaration (मदच्युतं (*madacyutaṃ*)), thousand-streamed, i.e. many-streamed, showerer of desires (वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*)), bearing all treasures (विश्वा वसूनि बिभ्रतं (*viśvā vasūni bibhrataṃ*)): this Soma they milk.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदच्यतं (*madacyataṃ*)—the cause of joy
- सहस्रधारं (*sahasradhāraṃ*)—the many-streamed
- वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*)—the showerer of desires
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—treasures
- बिभ्रतं (*bibhrataṃ*)—the bearer
- त्यं (*tyaṃ*)—the well-known
- एतु (*etu*)—this Soma
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—the priests
- दुहुः (*duhuḥ*)—call (milk)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The priests call this well-known Soma, the cause of joy, flowing in many streams, showerer of desires, bearer of all treasures.

##### English translation
Him have they milked from heaven, the shedder of exhilarating juice, the thousand-streamed, the showerer (of benefits), bearing all treasures.

### Printed p. 100
#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृषा॒ वि ज॑ज्ञे ज॒नय॒न्नम॑र्त्यः प्र॒तप॒ञ्ज्योति॑षा॒ तमः॑ ।  
> स सुष्टु॑तः क॒विभि॑र्नि॒र्णिजं॑ दधे त्रि॒धात्व॑स्य॒ दंस॑सा ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषा । वि । जज्ञॆः जनयन् । अमर्त्यः । प्रतपन् । ज्योतिषा । तमः ।  
> सः । सुस्तुतः । कविभिः , निःनिजं । दधे । त्रिधातु । अस्य । दंससा ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषा कामानां वर्षकोऽमर्तो मनुष्यधर्मरहितः सोमो वि जज्ञे ।
> विज्ञायते । किं कुर्वन् । जनयङ्ब्धं ज्योतिर्वोत्पादयन् ज्योतिषा स्वीयेन
> तमः प्रतपन् प्रज्वलयन् विनाशयन् प्रादुर्भवति । ततः कविभिर्मेधाविभिः
> स्तोतृभिः सुष्टुतः स सोमो निर्णिजं निर्णॆजनहेतुं मिश्रणं गव्यं दधे । धारयति । अथ त्रिधातु त्रिषु सवनेषु देवानां पोषकं । यद्वा । त्रयः सोमधारका
> द्रोणकलशादयो यस्मिन् । तद्यज्ञार्थं कर्मास्य सोमस्य दंससा कर्मणा
> ध्रियते खलु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, showerer of desires and immortal, i.e. free from the nature of mortals, is manifested (वि जज्ञे (*vi jajñe*), is made known). What is he doing? Begetting (जनयन् (*janayan*)) light, or sound; with his own light he blazes against and destroys the darkness. Then, well praised by the wise singers, that Soma bears (दधे (*dadhe*)) the निर्णिजं (*nirṇijaṃ*), the mixture of milk and the like that is the means of cleansing. Further, त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*) is what nourishes the gods at the three pressings. Or else: that in which there are three Soma-holding vessels, the Droṇakalaśa and the others; the rite for the sacrifice is indeed sustained by this Soma's act (दंससा (*daṃsasā*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—showerer of desires
- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—Soma, free from mortal nature
- जनयन् (*janayan*)—making sound
- ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)—with his own radiance
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—the thick darkness
- प्रतपन् (*pratapan*)—destroying
- वि जज्ञे (*vi jajñe*)—is known by all
- कविभिः (*kavibhiḥ*)—by the wise
- सुष्टुतः (*suṣṭutaḥ*)—exceedingly praised
- सः (*saḥ*)—Soma
- निर्णिजं (*nirṇijaṃ*)—the milk and the like that make him refined
- दधे (*dadhe*)—bears
- त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*)—the rite consisting of three pressings
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Soma
- दंससा (*daṃsasā*)—is sustained by the act

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, showerer of desires and free from mortal nature, is known by all, making sound and destroying the thick darkness with his own radiance. Exceedingly praised by the wise, Soma bears the milk and the like that make him refined (he is mixed with milk and the like). The rite consisting of three pressings is sustained by the act of this Soma.

### Printed p. 101

##### English translation
The showerer (of benefits) is manifested begetting (light), immortal, destroying the darkness with (his) radiance; glorified by the wise he has assumed his shining robe ; the triple (oblation is supported) by his act.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स सु॑न्वे॒ यो वसू॑नां॒ यो रा॒यामा॑ने॒ता य इळा॑नां ।  
> सोमो॒ यः सु॑क्षिती॒नां ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । सुन्वे । यः । वसूनां । यः रायां । आनेता । यः ' इळानां ।  
> सोमः । यः । सुक्षितीनां । १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स सोमः सुन्वे । अभिसुषुव ऋत्विग्भिः । यः सोमो वसूनां धनानामानेता यश्च रायां । रांति प्रयच्छंति क्षीरादिकमिति रायो गावः । तेषामानेता यश्चेळानामन्नानां च यश्च सोमः सुक्षितीनां सुनिवासानां शोभनमनुष्ययुक्तानां गृहाणामानेता विद्यते सोऽभिषुतोऽभूदिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Soma has been pressed by the priests: the Soma who is the bringer of treasures (वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)), and who is the bringer of रायां (*rāyāṃ*) (*rāyaḥ* are cattle, since they give milk and the like), and the bringer of इळानां (*iḷānāṃ*), foods, and the Soma who is the bringer of सुक्षितीनां (*sukṣitīnāṃ*), well-inhabited homes furnished with good people: he has been pressed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Soma
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—treasures
- आनेता (*ānetā*)—brings
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- रायां (*rāyāṃ*)—giver of wealth
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- इळानां (*iḷānāṃ*)—giver of food
- यः सोमः (*yaḥ somaḥ*)—which Soma
- सुक्षितीनां (*sukṣitīnāṃ*)—provides excellent homes
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Soma
- सुन्वे (*sunve*)—is pressed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma who brings treasures, who gives wealth, who gives food, who provides excellent homes: that Soma is pressed.

##### English translation
The Soma has been effused who is the bringer of treasures, the bringer of riches, the bringer of food, the bringer of fair homes:-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma of ours (नः (*naḥ*)) which Indra drinks (पिबात् (*pibāt*); from पा (*pā*) in the sense of drinking, with the augment aṭ in the leṭ), the Soma which the Maruts drink, and which Bhaga drinks together with the god named Aryaman; the Soma by which we bring Mitra and Varuṇa to face us (करामहे (*karāmahe*)), and likewise for great (महे (*mahe*)) protection (अवसे (*avase*)), and by which we bring Indra to face us: that Soma is pressed.

- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—the god Bhaga, which he drinks

- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- इंद्रं आ (*iṃdraṃ ā*)—by which Soma we shall satisfy Indra, that Soma is pressed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma of ours which Indra drinks, which the Maruts drink, and which Bhaga drinks together with the god Aśvama **NOTE**; the Soma with whose help we shall invite Mitra and Varuṇa, and by which we shall satisfy Indra for great protection: that Soma is pressed.

- पातवे (*pātave*)—for drinking
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you who are restrained by the priests, possess excellent weapons, are full of joy and exceedingly sweet, flow for Indra's drinking.

Soma, collected by the priests, well-armed, most exhilarating, most sweet-flavoured, flow for Indra to drink.

- विष्टंभः (*viṣṭaṃbhaḥ*)—the establisher
- उत्तमः (*uttamaḥ*)—the most excellent; you who are such
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- हार्दि (*hārdi*)—giving satisfaction to the mind
- सोमधानं (*somadhānaṃ*)—the vessel
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—rivers
- समुद्रं इव (*samudraṃ iva*)—as they enter the sea
- आ विश (*ā viśa*)—enter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you who satisfy Mitra, Varuna and Vayu, establish the heavenly world and are most excellent, enter the vessel that gives satisfaction to Indra's mind, as rivers enter the sea.

##### English translation
Soma, enter the Somadhana, Indra's heart, as the rivers (enter) the sea agreeable to mitra, Varuna and Vayu, the chief stay of heaven.

## Sūkta 109 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> परि प्रेति द्वाविंशत्युचं द्वैपदं षष्ठं सूक्तं । यज्ञे सदस्यवस्थितहोत्रीयादिधिष्टोपेता अग्नयो नामेश्वरपुत्रा ऋषयः । विंशतिका द्विपदा विराजः ।
> पवमानः सोमो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । परि प्र द्व्यधिकाग्नयो धिष्णा
> ऐश्वरा द्वैपदमिति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥
> अनुनादवु—परि प्र धन्व ऎंब ई सूक्तवु एळनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि आरनॆय सूक्तवु.
> इदरल्लि इप्पत्तॆरडु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. यज्ञदल्लि सदःस्थानदल्लिरुववरू होत्रने मॊदलाद
> धिष्णोपेतरू, ईश्वरपुत्ररू आद अग्नयः ऎंब ऋषिगळु ई सूक्तक्कॆ ऋषिगळु. पवमान
> सोमनु देवतॆयु ; ई सूक्तद ऋक्कुगळु इप्पत्तक्षरगळिरुव विराट् छंदस्कवु. अनुक्रमणिकॆ
> यल्लि—परि प्र द्व्यधिकाग्नयो धिष्णा ऐश्वरा द्वैपदं ऎंदु हेळिरुवुदु. विनियोगवन्नु
> हिंदॆये हेळलागिदॆ.
> सूक्त—१०९
> मंडल—९ ॥ अनुवाक—७ ॥ सूक्त—१०९ ॥
> अष्टक—७ ॥ अध्याय—५ ॥ वर्ग—२०, २ १॥
> सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—२२ ॥
> ऋषि—अग्नयो धिष्णा ऐश्वराः ॥
> देवता—पवमानः सोमः ॥
> छंदः—द्विपदा॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sixth sūkta, "pari pra", of twenty-two Ṛks, in dvipadā verses. The seers are the sons of Īśvara called Agnis, who in the sacrifice are stationed in the sadas, with the dhiṣṇya hearths beginning with that of the Hotṛ. The twenty-syllable viṛāj-type dvipadā is the metre; Pavamāna Soma is the deity. The Anukramaṇī is quoted: परि प्र द्व्यधिकाग्नयो धिष्णा ऐश्वरा द्वैपदमिति (*pari pra dvyadhikāgnayo dhiṣṇā aiśvarā dvaipadamiti*). The viniyoga has been stated.

Particulars: Sūkta 109; Maṇḍala 9; Anuvāka 7; Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 5, Varga 20, 21; number of Ṛks in the sūkta 22; seers: the Agnis, the dhiṣṇya hearths, sons of Īśvara; deity: Pavamāna Soma; metre: dvipadā.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॒ प्र ध॒न्वेंद्रा॑य सोम स्वा॒दुर्मि॒त्राय॑ पू॒ष्टे भगा॑य॥  
> ॥ दडतारक ॥  
> परि॒ प्र । ध॒न्व । इंद्रा॑य । सोम । स्वा॒दुः । मि॒त्राय॑ । पू॒ष्टे । भगा॑य ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम स्वादुः स्वादरसत्त्वमिंद्राय मित्राय पूष्टे भगाय्तेभ्यो
> देवेभ्यः परि प्र धन्व । हरितः पात्रेषु प्रक्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who are sweet, flow around for Indra, Mitra, Pūṣan and Bhaga, these gods; stream into the vessels.

### Printed p. 106

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- स्वादु (*svādu*)—you who are tasty
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- मित्राय (*mitrāya*)—for Mitra
- पूष्टे (*pūṣṭe*)—for Pūṣan
- भगाय (*bhagāya*)—for Bhaga
- परि प्र धन्व (*pari pra dhanva*)—flow all around

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you who are tasty, flow all around for the drinking of these gods: Indra, Mitra, Pūṣan and Bhaga.

##### English translation
Flow, Soma, who are sweet-flavoured, for Indra, Mitra, Pushan and Bhaga.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑स्ते सोम सु॒तस्य॑ पेयाः॒ क्रत्वे॒ दक्षा॑य॒ विश्वे॑ च दे॒वाः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । ते । सोम । सुतस्य । पेयाः । क्रत्वे । दक्षाय विश्वे च । देवाः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम सुतस्याभिषुतस्य ते तव स्वं भागमिंद्रः पेयाः । पेयात् । पिबतु॥
> पातेराशीर्लिजति रूपं । पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ किमर्थं । क्रत्वे क्रतवे प्रज्ञानाय
> दक्षाय बलाय च । किंचामि सर्वॆ विश्वे देवाश्च त्वदीयमंशं पिबंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, may Indra drink his own share of you, the pressed one; पेयाः (*peyāḥ*) stands for पेयात् (*peyāt*), "let him drink": the benedictive form of the root पा (*pā*), with a change of person. For what purpose? For क्रत्वे (*kratve*), understanding, and दक्षाय (*dakṣāya*), strength. And let all the Viśvedevas also drink your portion.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of the pressed
- ते (*te*)—your share
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- क्रत्वे (*kratve*)—for the gaining of excellent knowledge
- दक्षाय (*dakṣāya*)—for increase of strength
- पेयाः (*peyāḥ*)—let him drink
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all
- देवाः च (*devāḥ ca*)—the gods too, let them drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, let Indra drink your share, prepared by pressing, for the gaining of excellent knowledge and for increase of strength. Let all the gods drink too.

### Printed p. 107

##### English translation
Soma, let Indra and all the gods drink of you when effused for intelligence and strength.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वामृता॑य म॒हे क्षया॑य॒ स शु॒क्रो अ॑र्ष दि॒व्यः  ॒॑
> पीयूषः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । अमृताय । महे । क्षयाय । सः । शुक्रः । अर्ष । दिव्यः । पीयूषः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम शुक्रो दीप्तो दिव्यो दिवि भवः पीयूषो देवैः पातव्यः स
> त्वममृतायामरणाय महे महते क्षयाय निवासाय चैवार्ष । एवं पवस्व ।
> क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, bright, heavenly, the drink to be drunk by the gods: you, for immortality and for a great dwelling, flow thus; stream.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma) शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)—shining
- दिव्यः (*divyaḥ*)—born in the heavenly world
- पीयूषः (*pīyūṣaḥ*)—fit to be drunk by the gods
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- अमृताय (*amṛtāya*)—for freedom from death
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- क्षयाय (*kṣayāya*)—for a dwelling
- एव (*eva*)—thus
- अर्ष (*arṣa*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you who are shining, born in the heavenly world and fit to be drunk by the gods, flow thus for freedom from death and for a great dwelling.

##### English translation
So do you who are pure, divine, the beverage of all the gods, flow for immortality and a spacious abode.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑स्व सोम म॒हान्त्स॑मु॒द्रः पि॒ता दे॒वानां॒ विश्वा॒भि धाम॑॥

### Printed p. 108

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवस्व । सोम । महान् । समुद्रः । पिता । देवानां । विश्वा । अभि । धाम ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम महान् देवोभ्यो दीयमानत्वेन महत्त्वयुक्तः समुद्रः
> समुंदनः । यस्मात्समुद्रवंति रसास्तादृशः । पिता सर्वेषां पालयिता त्वं
> देवानां विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाणि धाम धामानि शरीराण्यभिलक्ष्य पवस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you are great, being given to the gods and so possessed of greatness; समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*), "the one who wets": from you the juices flow. You are the father, the protector of all. Flow, directing yourself to all the dwellings, that is, bodies, of the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- महान् (*mahān*)—of great nature
- समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*)—of the nature of a stream
- पिता (*pitā*)—protector of all; you who are such
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- धाम अभि (*dhāma abhi*)—towards the dwellings
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you who are of great nature, of the nature of a stream and protector of all, flow towards all the dwellings of the gods.

##### English translation
Flow, Soma, who are mighty, the shedder of juice, the parent of gods, towards all bodies.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शु॒क्रः प॑वस्व दे॒वेभ्यः॑ सोम दि॒वे पृ॑थि॒व्यै शं च॑ प्र॒जायै॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुक्रः । पवस्व । देवेभ्यः । सोम । दिवे । पृथिवै । शं । च । प्रजायै ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम शुक्रो दीप्तस्त्वं देवेभ्यो देवार्थं पवस्व । क्षर । किंच दिवे
> पृथिवै च द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां च ततः प्रजायै प्रजाभ्यश्च शं सुखं च कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, bright, flow for the gods, that is, for their sake. Further, bring well-being to heaven and earth, and then to the offspring.

### Printed p. 109
#### Ṛk 5 (continued)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)—you, who are radiant
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the gods
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow
- दिवे (*dive*)—for the protection of the heavenly world
- पृथिव्यै (*pṛthivyai*)—for the earth
- प्रजायै (*prajāyai*)—for the welfare of all creatures
- शं च (*śaṃ ca*)—produce happiness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who are radiant, flow for the gods. Produce happiness for heaven and earth and for all creatures.

##### English translation
Soma, who are brilliant, flow for the gods and (give) joy to heaven and earth and all creatures-
#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒वो ध॒र्तासि॑ शु॒क्रः पी॒यूषः॑ स॒त्ये विध॑र्मन्वा॒जी प॑वस्व ॥६॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिवः ! धर्ता । असि । शुक्रः : पीयूषः । सत्ये । विधधर्मन् । वाजी । पवस्व ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम शुक्रो दीप्तः पीयूषः पातव्यस्त्वं दिवो द्युलोकस्य धर्ता
> धारकोऽसि । वाजी बलवान् स त्वं सत्ये सत्यभूते विधर्मन् विधर्मणि । विविधकर्माण ऋत्विजो यस्मिन् । यद्वा । विविधसोमादिहविषां धारके । अस्मिन्यज्ञे
> पवस्व । क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you are radiant (शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*), shining) and fit to be drunk (पीयूषः (*pīyūṣaḥ*)); you are the upholder of the heavenly world. Being strong (वाजी (*vājī*)), flow in this sacrifice, which is true (सत्ये (*satye*)) and विधर्मन् (*vidharman*), that is, in which the priests perform various rites. Or else: in this sacrifice which is the holder of the various oblations such as Soma. Flow, that is, stream.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)—radiant
- पीयूषः (*pīyūṣaḥ*)—worthy of being drunk by the gods
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- धर्ता (*dhartā*)—the upholder
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- वाजी (*vājī*)—you who are strong
- सत्ये (*satye*)—in the sacrifice that is of the nature of truth
- विधर्मन् (*vidharman*)—and that upholds everything
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who are radiant and worthy of the gods' drinking, you are the upholder of the heavenly world. You who are strong, flow in the sacrifice that is of the nature of truth and upholds everything.

### Printed p. 110

##### English translation
You are the upholder of heaven, radiant and good to drink; flow you who are strong, at the truthful sacrifice.
#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑स्व सोम द्यु॒म्ना सु॑धा॒रो म॒हामवी॑ना॒मनु॑ पू॒र्व्यः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवस्व । सोम । द्युम्नो । सुधारः । महां । अवीनां । अनु । पूर्व्यः ॥ ७ :

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम द्युम्ना । द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वेति यास्कः । अन्नवान् यशस्वी ना सुधारः शोभनधारायुक्तः पूर्वः पुरातनस्त्वं महां मह
> तामवीनां रोम्मां रोमभ्यः सकाशादनुक्रमेण पवस्व । क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you are द्युम्नि (*dyumni*), possessed of food and fame (Yāska: द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वेति यास्कः (*dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vānnaṃ veti yāskaḥ*)). You have a fair stream and are ancient. Flow in due order through the hairs of the great sheep (the woollen filter).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- द्युम्नि (*dyumni*)—one who has food
- सुधारः (*sudhāraḥ*)—one who has an excellent stream
- पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*)—and ancient, you
- महां (*mahāṃ*)—great
- अवीनां (*avīnāṃ*)—through the woollen threads
- अनु (*anu*)—in due order
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who are possessed of food, who have an excellent stream, and are ancient, flow in due order through the great woollen threads.

##### English translation
Do you, Soma, who are possessed of food, who have a copious stream, flow through the great sheep's hairs in due succession.
#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नृभि॑र्येमा॒नो ज॑ज्ञा॒नः पू॒तः क्षर॒द्विश्वा॑नि मं॒द्रः स्व॒र्वित्॥

### Printed p. 111

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नृभिः । येमानः । जज्ञानः । पूतः । क्षरत् । विश्वानि । मंद्रः । स्वःवित् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिर्युत्विग्भीर्येमानो नियम्यमानो जज्ञानो जायमानः पूतः पवित्रेण शोधितो मंद्रो मोदमानः स्वर्वित्सर्वज्ञः एतादृशः
> सोमो विश्वानि सर्वाणि धनान्यस्मभ्यं क्षरत् । क्षरतु । ददातु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, held in check (येमानः (*yemānaḥ*)) by the priests who conduct the rite, being born, purified by the filter, exhilarating and all-knowing, may he stream, that is, give, all riches to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests
- येमानः (*yemānaḥ*)—one who is restrained
- जज्ञानः (*jajñānaḥ*)—produced for the sacrifice
- पूतः (*pūtaḥ*)—purified by the ten-strand filter
- मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*)—joyful
- स्वर्वित् (*svarvit*)—all-knowing; such Soma
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all riches
- क्षरत् (*kṣarat*)—may he provide for us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Soma, who is restrained by the priests, produced for the sacrifice, purified by the ten-strand filter, joyful and all-knowing, provide all riches for us.

##### English translation
May the Soma regulated by the priests, engendered, purified, exhilarating, all-knowing, bring us all (riches).
#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंदुः॑ पुना॒नः प्र॒जामु॑रा॒णः कर॒द्वश्वा॑नि॒ द्रवि॑णानि नः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंदुः । पुनानः । प्रजां । उराणः । करत् । विश्वानि । द्रविणानि । नः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुनानः पूयमान उराणः । उराण उरु कुर्वाणः । नि. ६-१७ इति यास्कः ॥
> देवान् बहु कुर्वाण इंदुः सोमो नोऽस्माकुं प्रजामपत्यादिकां विश्वानि
> व्याप्तानि द्रविणानि धनानि च करत् । करोतु ॥ करोतेर्लजि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

पुनानः (*punānaḥ*) is "being purified". उराणः (*urāṇaḥ*) is "making wide": उराण उरु कुर्वाणः । नि. ६-१७ इति यास्कः (*urāṇa uru kurvāṇaḥ | ni. 6-17 iti yāskaḥ*) (Ni. 6-17). Soma Indu, doing much for the gods, may he make for us progeny and the like, and all pervading riches. करत् (*karat*) means "may he make".

- उराणः (*urāṇaḥ*)—one who nourishes the gods

- करत् (*karat*)—may he provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Soma, who has attained purity and nourishes the gods, provide us with sons and the like and with pervading riches.

##### English translation

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑स्व सोम॒ क्रत्वे॒ दक्षा॒याश्वो॒ न नि॒क्तो वा॒जी धना॑य ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम अश्वो नाश्व इव निक्वो वसतीवरीभिरद्भिर्निक्वो वाजी वेगवांस्त्वं क्रत्वे क्रतवे प्रज्ञानाय दक्षाय बलाय धनाय धनार्थं च पवस्व । क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धनाय (*dhanāya*)—for wealth
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who are joined with the vasatīvarī waters, being strong and swift like a horse, flow for excellent knowledge, strength and wealth.

##### English translation
Flow, Soma, for intelligence, for strength, for wealth, strong and cleansed like a horse.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । ते । सोतारः । रसं । मदाय । पुनंति । सोमं । महे । द्युम्नाय ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोतारोऽभिषोतार ऋत्विजो हे सोम ते तव स्वभूतं रसं मदाय
> मदार्थं पुनंति । तदेवोच्यते । महे महते द्युम्नाय । द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो नान्नं वा । अन्नाय यशसे वा सोमं पुनंति । शोधयंति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The pressing priests (सोतारः (*sotāraḥ*)) purify your own juice, O Soma, for exhilaration. Or else, the sentence is to be construed as one: they purify that juice of the Soma being pressed.

- मदाय (*madāya*)—for exhilaration
- पुनंति (*punaṃti*)—purify
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- द्युम्नाय (*dyumnāya*)—for food
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma (they purify)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, the priests purify your well-known juice for exhilaration. They purify the Soma also for great food.

##### English translation

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बिभ॑र्ति॒ चार्विंद्र॑स्य॒ नाम॒ येन॒ विश्वा॑नि वृ॒त्रा ज॒घान॑ ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बभर्ति । चारु । इंद्रस्य । नाम । येन । विश्वानि । वृत्रा । जघान ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स सोमश्चारु कल्याणमिंद्रस्य नाम शरीरं बिभर्ति । धारयति । पोषयति ।
> येन शरीरेणेंद्रो विश्वानि सर्वाणि वृत्राणि पापरूपाणि रक्षांसि जघान हतवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Soma bears Indra's lovely (चारु (*cāru*), auspicious) इंद्रस्य नाम (*iṃdrasya nāma*), that is, his body; he holds and nourishes it. By this body Indra slew all (विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)) वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*), that is, the demons (रक्षांसि (*rakṣāṃsi*)) of the nature of sin.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the god Soma
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- चारु (*cāru*)—attractive
- नाम (*nāma*)—body
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—bears
- येन (*yena*)—by which Soma-filled body
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- वृत्रा (*vṛtrā*)—enemies
- जघान (*jaghāna*)—Indra destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Soma bears Indra's attractive body. By that very Soma-filled body Indra destroyed all enemies.

##### English translation
The auspicious (Soma) sustains Indra's body by which he has slain all Rakshasas.

> प्र । सोम । याहि । इंद्रस्य । कुक्षा । नृभिः । येमानः । अद्रिभिः । सुतः ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम नृभिर्ऋग्विघ्र्येमानो नियम्यमानोऽद्रिभिर्गावभिः सुतोऽभिसुतस्त्वमिंद्रस्य कुक्षा ॥ सप्तम्या डादेशः ॥ कुक्षावुदरभूते कलशे वा प्र याहि ।
> प्रकर्षण गच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, restrained (येमानः (*yemānaḥ*)) by the priests and pressed with the stones (अद्रिभिः (*adribhiḥ*), the pressing stones), go forth into Indra's belly (कुक्षा (*kukṣā*), with डा (*ḍā*) substituted for the locative) or into the vessel that is like a belly; go forward.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O god Soma
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests
- येमानः (*yemānaḥ*)—restrained
- अद्रिभिः (*adribhiḥ*)—by the pressing stones
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed; you
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- कुक्षा (*kukṣā*)—into the belly
- प्र याहि (*pra yāhi*)—enter and go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Soma, restrained by the priests and crushed and pressed with the pressing stones, enter and go into Indra's belly.

##### English translation
Guided by the priests and eflused with the stones go, Soma, to Indra's belly.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाजी बलवान्वेगवान्ना पवित्रं तिरस्कुर्वन् सहस्रधारो बहुधारः सोम
> इंद्रायेंद्रार्थमसर्जि । सृज्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, vigorous (strong or swift), passing the filter, with a thousand (many) streams, has been sent forth (असर्जि (*asarji*), is released) for Indra.

- वाजी (*vājī*)—endowed with strength
- पवित्रं तिरः (*pavitraṃ tiraḥ*)—crossing the ten-fringed filter
- सहस्रधारः (*sahasradhāraḥ*)—flowing in many streams
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the god Soma
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra (is released)
- अस्पृजि (*aspṛji*)—flows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Soma, endowed with strength, crossing the ten-fringed filter and flowing in many streams, flows for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अं॒जंत्ये॑नं॒ मध्वो॒ रसे॒नेंद्रा॑य॒ वृष्ण॒ इंदुं॒ मदा॑य ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अंजंति, एनं मध्व । रसेन । इंद्राय वृष्णे । इंदुं मदाय ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृष्टे कामानां वर्षित्र इंद्रायेंद्रस्य मदाय मदार्थं मध्यो
> मधुनो रसेन गव्येनैनमिंदं सोममृत्विजो०जंति । संयोजयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For the exhilaration of Indra, the showerer (वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)) of desires, the priests anoint (अंजंति (*aṃjaṃti*)), that is, join together, this Soma with the juice (रसेन (*rasena*)) of the sweet (मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)), the juice made from the cow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—the granter of desired things
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—of Indra
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for exhilaration
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—sweet
- रसेन (*rasena*)—with the juice
- एनं इंदुं (*enaṃ iṃduṃ*)—this Soma
- अंजंति (*aṃjaṃti*)—the priests mix

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the exhilaration of Indra, the granter of desired things, the priests mix this Soma with sweet juice.

They mix the Soma with the liquid of the sweet (milk) for Indra, the showerer (of benefits) for his exhilaration.

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वेभ्य॑स्ता॒ वृथा॒ पाज॑से॒ऽपो वसा॑नं॒ हरिं॑ मृजंति ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवेभ्यः । त्वा । वृथा । पाजसे । अपः । वसानं । हरिं । मृजंति ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम अप उदकानि वसानमाच्छादयंतं हरिं हरितवर्णं त्वा त्वां
> वृथानायासेनर्विजो मृजंति । शोधयंति । किमर्थं । देवेभ्यो देवानां
> पानार्थं पाजसे तेषां बलार्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who clothe (वसानं (*vasānaṃ*), cover) yourself with the waters, green (हरिं (*hariṃ*)) in colour: the priests cleanse (मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)) you readily (वृथा (*vṛthā*), without effort). For what purpose? For the gods, for their drinking (पाजसे (*pājase*)), for their strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- वसानं (*vasānaṃ*)—one who is clothed in
- हरिं (*hariṃ*)—one of green colour
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- वृथा (*vṛthā*)—without effort
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—of the gods
- पाजसे (*pājase*)—for strength
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—the priests cleanse

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Soma, you who are clothed in the waters (mixed with them) and are green in colour: the priests cleanse you without effort for the strengthening of the gods.

##### English translation
They cleanse you readily, clothed with water, green-tinted, for the invigoration of the gods.
