##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंदु॒रिंद्रा॑य तोषते॒ नि तो॑षते श्री॒णन्नु॒ग्रो रि॒णन्न॒पः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंदुः । इंद्राय । तोशते । नि । तोशते । त्रीणन् । उग्रः । रिणन् । आपः ॥ २२ ॥

### Printed p. 121

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंदुः सोम इंद्रायेंद्रार्थं तोशते । हस्यते । अभिषूयते । नि
> तोशते । नितरामभिषूयते । तोशतिर्वधकर्मा । कीदृशः । श्रीणन् प्रेरयन्
> सोमोऽभिषूयते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indu, that is Soma, is effused (तोशते (*tośate*)) for Indra, that is, for Indra's sake; the word is glossed हस्यते (*hasyate*), "is pressed out". नि तोशते (*ni tośate*) means that he is pressed out thoroughly. The root तोशति (*tośati*) has the sense of slaying. What kind of Soma? श्रीणन् (*śrīṇan*) is glossed as "impelling": the Soma is pressed out as one who impels.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्रीणन् (*śrīṇan*)—he who is mixed with milk and the like
- उग्र: (*ugra:*)—he who has exceedingly great strength
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the Vasatīvarī waters and others
- रिणन् (*riṇan*)—he who sets them in motion
- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—Soma
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- तोशते (*tośate*)—is pressed out
- नि तोशते (*ni tośate*)—is pressed out exceedingly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, who is mixed with milk and the like, who has exceedingly great strength, and who sets the Vasatīvarī waters and others in motion, is pressed out for Indra's drinking; he is pressed out exceedingly.

##### English translation
Indu is effused for Indra, is effused downwards—fierce, mixing (with the milk), flowing (into) the water.

## Sūkta 110 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पर्यू ष्टिति द्वादशर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं । त्रैरुणत्रसदस्य राजर्षि अस्य
> सूक्तस्य द्रष्टारौ । आदितस्तिस्तः पिपीलिकमध्या अनुष्टुभो द्वादशकाष्टकद्वादशकवत्यः ।
> ततः षडूर्ध्वबृहत्यो द्वादशकत्रयवत्यः । अथ दशम्याद्यास्तिस्रो विराजः । पवमानः सोमो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । पर्यू षु दादश त्रैरुणत्रसदस्य
> तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभः पिपीलिकमध्याः षळूर्ध्वबृहत्यस्तिस्त्रत्व विराज इति ॥ गतो विनियोगः #

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning पर्यू ष्टिति (*paryū ṣṭiti*) has twelve ṛks and is the seventh sūkta. Trairuṇa and Trasadasyu, royal sages, are the seers of this sūkta. The first three ṛks are pipīlikamadhyā anuṣṭubh, of twelve, eight and twelve syllables. Then come six ūrdhvabṛhatī verses, each of three twelve-syllable pādas. The three beginning with the tenth are virāj. The deity is Pavamāna Soma. He cites the Anukramaṇī to the same effect, and says that the viniyoga has been given already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, beginning पर्यूषु (*paryūṣu*), is the seventh sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. It has twelve ṛks. Trairuṇa and Trasadasyu, two royal sages, are the seers of the sūkta. The first three ṛks of this sūkta are in the metre called pipīlikamadhyā anuṣṭubh. In this metre there are three pādas: twelve syllables in the first pāda, eight in the second, and twelve in the third. This is the definition of the metre. The six ṛks following the fourth ṛk are in the metre called ūrdhvabṛhatī. In this metre there are three pādas of twelve syllables; this is its definition. The three ṛks following the tenth ṛk are in the virāj metre. Pavamāna Soma is the deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated: पर्यूषु द्वादश त्रुणत्रसदस्यो तिस्रो5नुष्टुभः पिपीलिकमध्याः षळूर्थ्वबृहत्यस्ति स्रश्च विराजः (*paryūṣu dvādaśa truṇatrasadasyo tisro5nuṣṭubhaḥ pipīlikamadhyāḥ ṣaḷūrthvabṛhatyasti sraśca virājaḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated earlier.

### Printed p. 122

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 9; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 110; Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 5; Varga 23. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 12. Ṛṣi: Trairuṇa-Trasadasyu. Devatā: Pavamāna Soma. Chandas: 1–3 anuṣṭubh pipīlikamadhyā; 4–9 ūrdhvabṛhatī; 10–12 virāj.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पर्यू॒षु प्र ध॑न्व॒ वाज॑सातये॒ परि॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ स॒क्षणिः॑।  
> द्वि॒षस्त॒रध्या॑ ऋण॒या न॑ ईयसे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । ऊं इति । सु प्र । धन्व वाजसातये । परि वृत्राणि । सक्षिणिः ।  
> द्विषः । तरध्यै । यणयाः । नः ईयसे । १ .

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ॥ श्रीरामचंद्राय नमः ॥
> हे सोम सु सुस्तु वाजसातयेऽस्मभ्यमन्नदानायैव परि प्र धन्व ! परितः
> प्रगच्छ । यद्वा । वाजसातयेऽन्नलाभाय संग्रामं प्रगच्छ । किं च सक्षणिः सहनशीलस्त्वं वृत्राणि शत्रुन्परि गच्छ । तदेवोच्च्यते नोऽस्माकमृणया ऋणानां
> यापयिता त्वं द्विषः शत्रुंस्तरध्यै शरीतुं हंतुमीयसे । परिगच्छसि :
> १, प्रबंधगळु.
> (ऎलै सोमदेवने) सु—अतिशयवागि । वाजसातॆये—नमगॆ अन्नलाभार्थवागि ।
> हरि प्र धन्व—सुत्तलू प्रवहिसु ! सक्षणि—शत्रुगळन्नु ऎदुरिसुव शक्तियुळ्ळ नीनु. । वृत्राणि—

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, सु (*su*), exceedingly, flow all round (परि प्र धन्व (*pari pra dhanva*)) for वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*), that is, for giving us food; go forth on every side." Or else: "for वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*), the gain of food, go to battle." Further: "you, सक्षणिः (*sakṣaṇiḥ*), of enduring nature, go round the वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*), the enemies." The same is said again: "you, ऋणया (*ṛṇayā*), the remover of our debts, go (ईयसे (*īyase*)) to destroy (तरध्यै (*taradhyai*)) the enemies (द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)); you go round them."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सु (*su*)—(O Soma) exceedingly
- वाजसातॆये (*vājasātèye*)—for our gain of food
- हरि प्र धन्व (*hari pra dhanva*)—flow all round
- सक्षणि (*sakṣaṇi*)—you who have the power to face enemies
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the enemies

### Printed p. 123
- परि (*pari*)—go, encompassing them
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ऋणयाः (*ṛṇayāḥ*)—you who repay our debts
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—our enemies
- तरध्यै (*taradhyai*)—destroy
- ईयसे (*īyase*)—go forward

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, flow all round for our gain of food. You who have the power to face enemies, go encompassing the enemies. You who repay our debts, go forward to destroy our enemies.

##### English translation
Hasten, Soma, to bring us sustenance; gifted with endurance (attack our) foes ; the acquitter of our debts, you approach to disperse our enemies.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अनु॒ हि त्वा॑ सु॒तं सो॑म॒ मदा॑मसि म॒हे स॑मर्य॒राज्ये॑ ।  
> वाजा॑ अ॒भि प॑वमान॒ प्र गा॑हसे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अनु । हि । त्वा । सुतं । सोम । मदामसि । महे । समर्यराज्ये :  
> वाजन् । अभि ; पवमान । प्र । गाहसे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम सुतमभिषुतं त्वा त्वां वयमनु मदामसि हि । अनुमदामः ।
> अनुक्रमेणाभिष्टुमः खलु । हे पवमान सोम स त्वं महे महति समर्यराज्ये महत्समनुष्यं त्वदीयं राज्यमनुपालयितं वाजाइत्युबलान्यभिलक्ष्य प्र
> गाहसे । प्रगच्छसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, we praise you (मदामसि (*madāmasi*)) who have been pressed (सुतं (*sutaṃ*)), in due order; we eulogise you indeed." "O Pavamāna Soma, you, to protect your own great sovereignty over men (महे समर्यराज्ये (*mahe samaryarājye*)), advance (प्र गाहसे (*pra gāhase*)), aiming at the वाजान् (*vājān*), the forces."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—who have been pressed
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अनुमदामसि हि. (*anumadāmasi hi.*)—we praise
- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O Soma, called Pavamāna
- महे (*mahe*)—great

### Printed p. 124
- समर‍्ये राज्ये (*samarye rājye*)—to protect your sovereignty among men
- वाजान् अभि (*vājān abhi*)—facing the forces of the enemy
- प्र गाहसे (*pra gāhase*)—you charge forward

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, we praise you who have been pressed. O Soma, called Pavamāna, you charge forward against the forces of the enemy in order to protect your great sovereignty among men.

##### English translation
In turn we glorify you, Soma, when effused; you attack the (hostile) forces, O Pavamana, to (defend) your great sovereignty over men.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अजी॑जनो॒ हि प॑वमान॒ सूर्यं॑ वि॒धारे॒ शक्म॑ना॒  ॑
> पयः ।  
> गोजी॑रया॒ रंह॑माण॒ पुरं॑ध्या ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अजीजनः । हि । पवमान । सूर्यं । विधारे । शक्मना । पयः ।  
> गोर्जीरया । रंहमाणः । पुरंध्या । ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान सोम त्वं पयः पयस उदकस्य विधारे विधारकेंतरिक्षे
> शक्कना समर्थेन बलेन सूर्यमजीजनो हि । उत्पादितवान्भवसि खलु । कीदृशः !
> गोजीरया स्तोतृभ्यो गवां प्रेरकेण । स्तोतृणां प्रेरितपशुकेनेत्यर्थः ।
> तादृशेन पुरंध्या बहुविधप्रज्ञानेन युक्तो रंहमाणो वेगं कुर्वाणस्त्वं
> सूर्यमजीजनः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Pavamāna Soma, you have generated the sun (सूर्यमजीजनो हि (*sūryamajījano hi*)) in the sky (विधारे (*vidhāre*)), the sustainer of पयः (*payaḥ*), water, by your capable strength (शक्कना (*śakkanā*))." What sort of one? गोजीरया (*gojīrayā*) is explained as "by the impeller of cattle to the worshippers", that is, one by whom cattle are sent to the worshippers. Endowed with such पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*), manifold wisdom, and speeding (रंहमाणः (*raṃhamāṇaḥ*)), you generated the sun.
**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O Soma, called Pavamāna
- गोजीरया (*gojīrayā*)—you who provide cattle for the enemies
- पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*)—you who are endowed with wisdom
- रंहमाणः (*raṃhamāṇaḥ*)—you who are swift

### Printed p. 125
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—for the water
- विधारे (*vidhāre*)—in the sky, the sustainer
- शक्कना (*śakkanā*)—by your capacity
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- अजीजनो हि (*ajījano hi*)—you have generated, have you not

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you who provide cattle for the enemies, who are endowed with wisdom and are swift, have generated the sun by your capacity in the sky that sustains the water.

##### English translation
Pavamana, by your might you have generated the sun in (the firmament), the support of the water, hastening on with abundant wisdom that procures cattle (for your worshippers),

> चारुणः ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सदा । असरः । वाजं । अच्छ । सनिस्यदत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अमृत : मरधर्मरहित सोम त्वमृतस्य सत्यभूतस्य चारुणः कल्याणस्यामृतस्योदकस्य धर्मन्दारकेंतरिक्षे सूर्यमजीजनः । किमर्थं । मर्त्येष्व
> मनुष्येष्टभिमुखीभवनाय । किंच सनिष्यदत् संभजन् स त्वं वाजमच्छ संग्राममभिलक्ष्य सदासरः । सरसि । गच्छसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O immortal (अमृत (*amṛta*)), Soma, free from the nature of death, you generated the sun in the sky (धर्मन् (*dharman*)), the sustainer of ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*), the true, चारुणः (*cāruṇaḥ*), the auspicious, अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*), ambrosial water." For what purpose? "मर्त्येषु (*martyeṣu*), in order to face mortals, men." Further: "you, सनिष्यदत् (*saniṣyadat*), bestowing, always (सदा (*sadā*)) go (असरः (*asaraḥ*)), aiming at वाजं (*vājaṃ*), battle."

- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—and everlasting
- धर्मन् (*dharman*)—in the sky, the sustainer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, free from the nature of death, you generated the sun, in the sky that sustains the water that is true, auspicious and everlasting, so as to appear before men. You who flow majestically always charge forward towards the battle.

##### English translation
Immortal Soma, you have generated (the sun) among mortals in (the firmament), the support of the truthful auspicious ambrosia ; streaming forth you go to battle continually.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हे सोम त्वं शवसान्नेन हेतुनाभ्यभि त्रतर्दिथ हि ! पवित्रमभितृण्णवानसि ।
> छिन्नवानसि । तत्र दृष्टांतद्वयं । उत्सं न यथा कश्चिज्जनपानं ! अस्मिञ्चना उदकं
> पिबंति । तमक्षितमक्षीणं कं चित् कंचनोत्समुत्सरणशीलं वाप्यादिकमभितृणत्ति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, by शवसा (*śavasā*), with food as the cause, you have pierced right through (*abhyabhi tratarditha*): you have cut through the filter." Here there are two illustrations. First, "like a spring (उत्सं न (*utsaṃ na*))", as some जनपानं (*janapānaṃ*), a place where people drink water: that unexhausted, imperishable (अक्षितं (*akṣitaṃ*)) one, any (कं चित् (*kaṃ cit*)) spring, a well or the like of welling nature, he pierces.
**NOTE**

### Printed p. 127

> अथवा कश्चिद्गभस्तोर्बाह्वोः शर्याभिरंगुलीभिर्भरमाण उदकं संभरन् कंचिदभितृणत्ति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa gives a second explanation: or else someone, carrying water with the fingers (शर्याः (*śaryāḥ*)) of his two arms (गभस्त्योः (*gabhastyoḥ*)), pours it forth and breaks open a spring-like source; the Soma is like him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जनपानं (*janapānaṃ*)—fit to be drunk by the people of the world
- अक्षितं (*akṣitaṃ*)—inexhaustible
- कं चित् उत्सं न (*kaṃ cit utsaṃ na*)—as one bursts open a spring of water
- भरमाण् (*bharamāṇ*)—one who is carrying water
- गभस्त्यो (*gabhastyo*)—of his arms
- शराभिः (*śarābhiḥ*)—with the fingers, as one sprinkles water
- श्रवसा (*śravasā*)—for the sake of food
- अभ्यभि (*abhyabhi*)—all around the filter
- ततर्दिथ हि (*tatarditha hi*)—you have split it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you have split the filter all around, for the sake of food, as one breaks open a spring of water that people of the world can drink and that cannot dry up, to make the water rise up; and as one who carries water sprinkles it with the fingers of his arms.

##### English translation
You have burst open (the filter) with (your) food as (one bursts open) an inexhaustible fountain giving drink to the nation, like one taking up (water) with the fingers of his two hands.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Śaryāḥ—explaining the meaning of this word, Yāska says in his Nirukta: शर्याः । शर्या अंगुलयो भवंति । सृजंति कर्माणि । शर्या इषवः शरमय्यः । शरः शृणातेः । शर्याभिर्न भरमाणो गभस्तो इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*śaryāḥ | śaryā aṃgulayo bhavaṃti | sṛjaṃti karmāṇi | śaryā iṣavaḥ śaramayyaḥ | śaraḥ śṛṇāteḥ | śaryābhirna bharamāṇo gabhasto ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 5-4). Śaryāḥ means aṅguli, fingers. Because work is done with the help of these fingers, the word śaryāḥ indicates fingers. And this word has another meaning too, arrows. The word śara is derived from the root śṛ (śṛṇāti), "to split", and gives the sense of a weapon that splits and injures. For the word śarya in the sense of "finger", the Vedic text of the present Ṛk itself, शर्याभिर्न भरमाणो गभस्त्योः (*śaryābhirna bharamāṇo gabhastyoḥ*), is the example.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Thereafter, seeing him, certain celestial beings (दिव्या (*divyā*)), born in heaven and named Vasuruc, praised this Soma as a kinsman (आप्यं (*āpyaṃ*)), a good friend. Why "thereafter"? ##### English translation

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, the "first" (प्रथमाः (*prathamāḥ*)) are the ancient ones; or else, being sacrificers, the foremost of all people. The व्यक्तबर्हिषः (*vyaktabarhiṣaḥ*) are the sacrificers who have cut the sacred grass for the sacrifice. They have placed their thought (धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)) in you for great strength (वाजाय (*vājāya*)) and food (श्रवसे (*śravase*)). Therefore, O capable hero Soma, such as you are, impel us too in battle toward heroic power. Or else: impel us toward well-being (भवाय (*bhavāya*)), in a heroic son.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- प्रथमाः (*prathamāḥ*)—the ancient
- वृक्तबर्हिष. (*vṛktabarhiṣa.*)—sacrificers with the sacred-grass seat spread for the sacrifice
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- वाजाय (*vājāya*)—for strength
- क्रवसे (*kravase*)—for food
- धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)—their meditative thought
- श्वे (*śve*)—in you
- दधुः (*dadhuḥ*)—have placed
- वीर (*vīra*)—O capable Soma
- सः (*saḥ*)—the famous
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- वीर्याय (*vīryāya*)—for the gaining of strength
- चोदय (*codaya*)—impel

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, the sacrificers, the ancient ones who have spread the sacred grass for the sacrifice, have placed their meditative thought in you for great strength and for food. O Soma, endowed with capability, you, the famous one, impel us too toward the gaining of strength.

### Printed p. 130

##### English translation
The chief (of men) having cut the sacred grass have fixed their minds, Soma, on you for abundant strength and food ; do you, O hero, excite us to heroism.

> इंद्रं । अभि । जायमानं । सं । अस्वरन् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवो द्युलोकात् तत्र स्थितैर्देवैः पीयूषं पातव्यं पूर्व्यं प्रत्नं
> यत्सोमरूपमन्नमुक्थं प्रशस्यमस्ति तं सोमं महो महतो गाहाद्गहनाद्दिवो द्युलोकान्निरधुक्षत । अभिमुख्येन निर्दुहंति । ततो दुग्धमिंद्रमभिलक्ष्य
> जायमानं तं सोमं समस्वरन् । स्तोतारः संस्तुवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

From heaven, from the great deep heavenly world, they milk out the ancient Soma, which is the food in Soma form, to be drunk by the gods who dwell there and worthy of praise (*ukthaṃ*). They draw it forth facing it. Then, when that Soma is milked out and is being born with Indra as its aim, the singers praise it together.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—for the gods of heaven
- पीयूषं (*pīyūṣaṃ*)—fit to be drunk
- पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*)—ancient
- यत् (*yat*)—which Soma
- उक्ष्यं (*ukṣyaṃ*)—is worthy of praise, that Soma
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- गाहात् (*gāhāt*)—deep
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the world of heaven
- आ निरधुक्षत (*ā niradhukṣata*)—have called forth
- इंद्रं अभि (*iṃdraṃ abhi*)—for Indra's drinking
- जायमानं (*jāyamānaṃ*)—that Soma, which has been produced
- समस्वरन् (*samasvaran*)—the singers praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

They have called forth, from the great and deep world of heaven, the Soma that is fit for the gods of heaven to drink, ancient and worthy of praise. The singers praise that Soma, produced for Indra's drinking.

### Printed p. 131

##### English translation
They have milked from heaven from the mighty deep the ancient Soma, the beverage (of the gods) of heaven, which is worthy of praise; they have praised it when gencrated for Indra.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध॒ यदि॒मे प॑वमान॒ रोद॑सी इ॒मा च॒ विश्वा॒ भुव॑ना॒भि  ॒॑
> मज्मना ।  
> यू॒थे न नि॒ष्ठा वृ॑ष॒भो वि ति॑ष्ठसे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । यत् , इमे इति । पवमान ! रोदसी इति . इमा च । विश्वा । भुवना ।  
> अभि । मज्जना ।  
> यूथे । न निःस्था वृषभः । वि । तिष्ठसे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान सोम अधानंतरं यद्यथेमे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्याविमेमानि विश्वा विश्वानि भुवना भूतजातानि च मज्मना बलेनाभि तिष्ठसि सत्वं तथा कुर्वन्
> भुवनेषु वि तिष्ठसे । तत्र दृष्टांतः यूथे न यथा कश्चिद्वृषभो गवां यूथे
> वृंदे निष्का निष्मितो वर्तते तद्वदूथस्थानीयेषु भूतजातेषु निष्मितो भवसि !

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O purifying Soma, thereafter, just as you stand over (*abhi tiṣṭhasi*) these two worlds, heaven and earth, and all these beings by your might (मज्मना (*majmanā*)), so, doing thus, you stand in different ways among the beings. The example: as a bull stands established in a herd of cows, so you are established among the classes of beings, which are like the herd.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O Soma
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—a powerful bull
- यूथे (*yūthe*)—in a herd of cows
- निष्ठाः न (*niṣṭhāḥ na*)—as it stands exercising mastery
- अध (*adha*)—as soon as you are born
- यत् (*yat*)—in the way that
- इमे रोदसी (*ime rodasī*)—these two, heaven and earth
- इमा च विश्वा भुवना (*imā ca viśvā bhuvanā*)—in all these worlds
- मज्मना (*majmanā*)—by their power
- अभि (*abhi*)—you make them stand pervading, in that way also
- वि तिष्ठसे (*vi tiṣṭhase*)—you stand exercising mastery

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, just as a powerful bull stands exercising mastery in a herd of cows, so, as soon as you are born, in the way you make these two, heaven and earth, and all these worlds stand pervaded by their own power, in that way too you stand exercising mastery.

### Printed p. 132

##### English translation
Since, Pavamana, you by your might are chief over these two worlds and all these living beings, as a bull is ruler in a herd of cows.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोमः॑ पुना॒नो अ॒व्यये॒ वारे॒ शिशु॒र्न क्रीळ॒न्नव॑मानो  
> अक्षाः ।  
> स॒हस्र॑धारः श॒तवा॑ज॒ इंदुः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोमः । पुनानः । अव्यये । वारे । शिशुः । न । क्रीळन् । पवमानः । अक्षारिति ।  
> सहस्रधारः । शतनाजः । इंदुः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुनानः पूयमानः पवमानः पूतः सोमोऽव्ययेऽविमये वारे वाले
> पवित्रे शिशुर्न शिशुरिव क्रीळन्नितस्ततः संक्रीडमानः सन्नक्षाः । क्षरति । कीदृशः । सहस्रधारो बहुधारायुक्तः शतवाजो बहुबल इंदुर्दिप्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, being purified and cleansed, flows (अक्षाः (*akṣāḥ*)) through the woollen (अव्यये (*avyaye*)) filter (वारे (*vāre*)), playing here and there like a child. What is he like? Having a thousand streams, having hundredfold strength (शतवाजः (*śatavājaḥ*)), and bright (इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—the purifier
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—one who has attained purity
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- सहस्रधारः (*sahasradhāraḥ*)—having many streams
- शतवाजः (*śatavājaḥ*)—having abundant strength
- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—shining and radiant
- शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*)—a young child
- क्रीळन् न (*krīḷan na*)—as it plays
- अव्यये (*avyaye*)—of wool
- वारे (*vāre*)—through the fibres
- अक्षाः (*akṣāḥ*)—flows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, the purifier, who has attained purity, having many streams, abundant strength and shining, flows through the fibres of wool as a young child plays.

### Printed p. 133

##### English translation
Pavamana Soma sporting like a child drops filtered through the woollen fleece, thousand-streamed, having the might of a hundred, radiant.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष पु॑ना॒नो मधु॑मा ऋ॒तावेंद्रा॒येंदुः॑ पवते स्वा॒दुरू॒र्मिः ।  
> वा॒ज॒सनि॑र्वरिवो॒विद्व॑यो॒धाः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । पुनानः । मधुमान् । ऋतवा । इंद्राय । इंदु: पवते : स्वादुः  
> ऊर्मिः ।  
> वाजसनिः वरिवः वित् । वयःधाः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुनानः पूयमानो मधुमान् माधुर्योपेत ऋतवर्तवान् यज्ञवानिंदुः क्षरणशीलः स्वादुः स्वादुकर ऊर्मिरेष रसधारासंघ इंद्रायेंद्रार्थं
> पवते । क्षरति । कीदृशः । वाजसनिरन्नस्य दाता वरिवोविद्वनस्य लंभको वयोधा
> आयुषो दाता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, being purified, is sweet, possessed of ṛta (the sacrifice), flowing and delicious; this wave, a stream of juice, flows for Indra's sake. He is described as the giver of food (वाजसनिः (*vājasaniḥ*)), the obtainer of wealth (वरिवोवित् (*varivovit*)) and the giver of life (वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—the purifier
- मधुमान् (*madhumān*)—endowed with sweetness
- ऋतवा (*ṛtavā*)—possessing the sacrifice
- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—of flowing nature
- स्वादुः (*svāduḥ*)—delicious
- ऊर्मिः (*ūrmiḥ*)—possessing waves
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this Soma
- वाजसनिः (*vājasaniḥ*)—the giver of food
- वरिवोवित् (*varivovit*)—the giver of wealth
- वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)—the giver of life
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- पवते (*pavate*)—flows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Soma, who is the purifier, sweet, possessed of the sacrifice, flowing, delicious and wave-bearing, flows, as giver of food, wealth and life, for Indra to drink.

### Printed p. 134

##### English translation
This Soma juice undergoing purification, sweet-flavoured, holy, dropping, flows for Indra a sweet stream, bestowing food, dispensing wealth and life.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स प॑वस्व॒ सह॑मानः पृत॒न्यून्तेध॒न्रक्षां॒स्यप॑ दु॒र्गहा॑णि ।  
> स्वा॒यु॒धः सा॑स॒हवान्त्सो॑म॒ शत्रु॑न् ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । पवस्व । सहमानः । पृतन्यून् । सेधन् । रक्षांसि । अप । दुःगहानि ।  
> सुआयुधः । ससहवान् । सोम । शत्रून् ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम स तादृशस्त्वं पवस्व । किं कुर्वन् । पृतन्यून् ॥ कव्यध्वरपृतनस्यर्चि
> लोप इति क्यचि परतोऽकारलोपः ॥ संग्रामकामाञ्त्यून् सहमानोऽभिभवन् तथा दुर्गहाणि कैश्चितपि दुर्गमाणि रक्षांस्यप सेधन्नपगमयन् हिंसन् ।
> किंच स्वायुधः शोभनायधः सञ्त्यून्सासह्वानभिभवन्नभितपन् पवस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, such as you are, flow." What doing? Overcoming (सहमानः (*sahamānaḥ*)) the पृतन्यून् (*pṛtanyūn*), those desiring battle (the elision of the a before kyac is by the rule he cites), and driving away (अप सेधन् (*apa sedhan*)) the demons hard for anyone to approach. Moreover, well-armed, mastering the enemies, flow, afflicting them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, the renowned
- पृतन्यून् (*pṛtanyūn*)—the enemies who desire battle
- सहमानः (*sahamānaḥ*)—defeating
- दुर्गहाणि (*durgahāṇi*)—unassailable
- रक्षांसि (*rakṣāṃsi*)—the demons
- अप सेधन् (*apa sedhan*)—destroying
- स्वायुधः (*svāyudhaḥ*)—having excellent weapons
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—all enemies
- सासहवान् (*sāsahavān*)—wholly defeating
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, renowned as you are, flow, defeating the enemies who desire battle, destroying the unassailable demons, well-armed, and wholly defeating all enemies.

##### English translation
Flow, Soma, overcoming (our) enemies, driving away the Rakshasas who are difficult to approach, well-armed, triumphing over foes.

### Printed p. 135
## Sūkta 111 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अया रुचेति तृचमष्टमं सूक्तं परुच्छेपपुत्रस्यानानताख्यस्यार्षमत्यष्टिच्छंदस्कं । पवमानसोमदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । अया रुचा तृचमनानतः पारुच्छेपिरात्यष्टमिति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The eighth sūkta, अया रुचा (*ayā rucā*), a tṛca, has as its seer Anānata, son of Parucchepa; its deity is Pavamāna Soma; its metre is Atyaṣṭi. The Anukramaṇī says: अया रुचा तृचमनानतः पारुच्छेपिरात्यष्टमिति (*ayā rucā tṛcamanānataḥ pārucchepirātyaṣṭamiti*). The application (viniyoga) has been stated before.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning अया रुचा (*ayā rucā*) is the eighth sūkta in the seventh anuvāka; it has three ṛks. Its seer is Anānata, son of the seer Parucchepa; the deity is Pavamāna Soma; the metre is Atyaṣṭi. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अया रुचा तृचमनानतः पारुच्छेपिरात्यष्टं (*ayā rucā tṛcamanānataḥ pārucchepirātyaṣṭaṃ*). The application of the sūkta has been stated earlier.

Sūkta 111. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 7; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 5, Varga 24. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 3. Seer: Anānata Pārucchepi. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Atyaṣṭi.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒या रु॒चा हरि॑णा पुना॒नो विश्वा॒ द्वेषां॑सि तरति स्व॒युग्व॑भिः॒ सूरो॒ न स्व॒युग्व॑भिः ।  
> धारा॑ सु॒तस्य॑ रोचते पुना॒नो अ॑रु॒षो हरिः॑ ।  
> विश्वा॒ यद्रू॒पा प॑रि॒यात्यृक्व॑भिः स॒प्तास्ये॑भि॒र्ऋक्व॑भिः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अया । रुचा । हरिण्या । पुनानः । विश्वा । द्वेषांसि । तरति । स्वयुग्वभिः । सूरः ।  
> न । स्वयुग्वभिः ।  
> धारा । सुतस्य । रोचते । पुनानः . अरुषः । हरिः ।  
> विश्वा । यत् । रूपा । परियाति । यक्वभिः । सप्तआस्येभिः । यक्वभिः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 136

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुनानः पूयमानः सोमो हरिण्या हरितवर्णयायानया रुचा रोचमानया धारया विश्वा सर्वाणि द्वेषांसि द्वेष्टृणि रक्षांसि तरति । विनाशयति । तत्र
> दृष्टांतः । सूरो न यथा सूर्यः स्वयुग्वभिः स्वयं युक्तै रश्मिभिस्तमांसि
> हिनस्ति तद्वत् । स्वयुग्वभिरिति द्विरुक्तिरादरार्था । यद्वा । धारया युक्तः सोमः
> स्वीय्यर्युक्तैस्तेजोभी रक्षांसि तरति । तस्य सुतस्याभिसुतस्य सोमस्य धारा
> रोचते । दीप्यते । पुनानः पूयमानो हरिर्हरितवर्णः सोमोऽरुष आरोचमानो भवति । यद्यः सोमः सप्तास्येभीरसहरणशीलास्यॆर्ऋक्वभिः स्तुतिमद्भिर्युक्वभिस्तेजोभिर्विश्वा विश्वानि व्याप्तानि रूपा रूपाणि नक्षत्राणि परियाति गच्छति
> व्याप्नोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, being purified, with this shining green-tinted stream overcomes (destroys) all hateful demons. The example: as the sun destroys darkness with its self-yoked rays, so he does; the repetition स्वयुग्वभिः (*svayugvabhiḥ*) is for emphasis. Or else: Soma, joined with the stream, overcomes the demons with his own yoked energies. The stream of the pressed Soma shines; being purified, the green Soma becomes radiant. Or: that Soma, with the seven-mouthed, juice-bearing, praise-accompanied ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*) (energies), goes about and pervades all forms, the constellations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—the sun
- स्वयुग्वभिः न (*svayugvabhiḥ na*)—as he destroys darkness with rays born of himself
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—Soma, who is being purified
- हरिण्या (*hariṇyā*)—green-hued
- अया रुचा (*ayā rucā*)—with this radiance
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*)—enemies
- स्वयुग्वभिः (*svayugvabhiḥ*)—with his own energies
- तरति (*tarati*)—destroys
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of the pressed Soma
- धारा (*dhārā*)—the stream
- रोचते (*rocate*)—shines
- यत् (*yat*)—which Soma
- सप्तास्येभिः (*saptāsyebhiḥ*)—with seven (juice-bearing) mouths
- ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*)—accompanied by praises
- ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*)—with energies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the sun destroys darkness with rays born of himself, so Soma, being purified, destroys all enemies with this green-hued radiance. The stream of the pressed Soma juice shines. That Soma which possesses, with its juice-bearing, seven-mouthed energies accompanied by praises, the all-pervading forms such as the constellations, being purified and green-hued, is radiant.

##### English translation
With this bright green-tinted stream Soma being filtered overcomes all enemies with the (juices) yoked to it, as the sun (overcomes the darkness) with the (rays) yoked to it ; the stream of the effused (Soma) shines, the filtered green-tinted (Soma is) resplendent, which pervades all constellations, with the Rikvans, with the seven-mouthed Rikvans.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you found the wealth of the Paṇis, the wealth of cattle carried off by them. And you are well purified in your own house, the sacrifice, by the mothers, the supporting waters (वसतीवरीभिः (*vasatīvarībhiḥ*)) of the sacrifice. As the sound of a sāman is heard from a distant place, so that sound of yours is heard by all; this is said with reference to the pressing of Soma, in which the supporters of the rite, the sacrificers, rejoice. Shining Soma, with the radiant waters that sustain the three worlds, bestows food (वयः (*vayaḥ*)) on the praisers; the repetition वयो दधे (*vayo dadhe*) is for emphasis. **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you take the famous wealth of cattle carried off by the Paṇis. You are purified in your house, the sacrifice, by the waters that support the sacrifice. As the sound of the sāman is heard from a very distant place, that sound of your pressing, in which the sacrificers rejoice, is heard by all. The shining Soma, together with the glittering waters that sustain the three worlds, gives food to the sacrificers.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, the wise (चेकितत् (*cekitat*)), goes toward the eastern, foremost quarter. The chariot, visible to all and renowned among the gods, joins the sun's rays; the repetition दर्शतो रथः (*darśato rathaḥ*) is for emphasis. Then the manly hymns go to Indra and gladden him for the sake of victory; and his vajra also goes to Indra. When, in battles, you, Soma, and Indra are together unconquered by enemies, then the coming of the hymns and the rest takes place; the repetition अनपच्युता (*anapacyutā*) is for emphasis. **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wise Soma goes and joins the excellent eastern quarter. The chariot of Soma, visible to all and renowned among the gods, joins the sun's rays. O Soma, when you and Indra are unconquered by enemies in battles, then the hymns endowed with manly power join Indra and gladden him for the sake of victory. The vajra also joins Indra.

## Sūkta 112 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नानानमिति चतुर्यचं नवमं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य शिशुनाम्न आर्षं । पंचपदा पंक्तिश्चंदः । पवमानः सोमो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । नानानं चतुष्कं
> शिशुः पांक्तं हीति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta, beginning with नानानं (*nānānaṃ*), has four Ṛks. Its seer is Śiśu Āṅgirasa; the metre is Pañcapadā Paṅktiḥ; the deity is Pavamāna Soma. Sāyaṇa cites the Anukramaṇī to the same effect. He adds that the viniyoga has been stated already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning नानानं (*nānānaṃ*) is the ninth sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. It has four Ṛks. Its seer is Śiśu Āṅgirasa, its deity is Pavamāna Soma, and its metre is Pañcapadā Paṅktiḥ. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated: नानानं चतुष्कं शिशुः पांक्तं हि (*nānānaṃ catuṣkaṃ śiśuḥ pāṃktaṃ hi*). The viniyoga has been stated only once.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta—112
- Maṇḍala—9; Anuvāka—7; Sūkta—112
- Aṣṭaka—7; Adhyāya—5; Varga—25 **NOTE**
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—4
- Seer—Śiraḥ **NOTE**
- Deity—Pavamāna Soma
- Metre—Pāktiḥ **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ना॒ना॒नं वा उ॑ नो॒ धियो॒ वि व्र॒तानि॒ जना॑नां ।  
> तक्का॑रि॒ष्टं रु॒तं भि॒षग्ब्र॒ह्मा सु॒न्वंत॑मिच्छ॒तींद्रा॑येंदोः॒ ॑ 
> परि स्रव ॥ १ ॥

> तक्षा । रिष्टं । रुतं । भिषक् । ब्रह्मा । सुन्वंतं । इच्छति । इंद्राय । इंदो इति ।  
> परि । स्रव . १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिरेतदादिभिस्त्रिभिः सूक्तैरपरिस्रवतः सोमस्याजामित्वाय मनसो
> विनोदनं कुर्वन्नाह । हे सोम नोऽस्माकं धियः कर्माणि नानानं नानाजातीयकानि बहूनि भवंति । वैशब्दः प्रसिद्धर्थद्योतनार्थः । उ इति पूरणः ।
> तथान्येषामपि जनानां व्रतानि कर्माणि विविधानि भवंति । तक्षा त्वष्टा रिष्टं दारुतक्षणमिच्छति । तथा भिषगैद्यश्चित्सि को रुतं रोगमिच्छति । ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मणः सुन्वंतं
> सोमाभिषवं कुर्वंतं यजमानमिच्छति । तथाहं त्वत्परिस्रवणमिच्छामि । तस्माद्दे
> इंदो सोमेंद्रायेंद्रार्थं परि स्रव । परितः क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this and the next two sūkta-verses the seer, to console his mind about Soma not flowing, speaks. O Soma, our acts (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)) are of many kinds; so too the acts of other men are varied. The carpenter (तक्षा (*takṣā*), the wood-cutter) desires timber-cutting; the physician desires illness (रुतं (*rutaṃ*)); the Brahmā priest desires the sacrificer who presses Soma. In the same way I desire your flowing. Therefore, O Indu, flow around for Indra, that is, stream on all sides. The particle वै (*vai*) marks a well-known fact; उ (*u*) is a filler.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma-deva) नः (*naḥ*)—our
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—acts
- नानानं (*nānānaṃ*)—are of many kinds
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—of men
- व्रतानि (*vratāni*)—acts
- वि (*vi*)—are of many kinds
- तक्षा (*takṣā*)—the wood-worker
- रिष्टं (*riṣṭaṃ*)—wood-work
- इच्छति (*icchati*)—desires
- भिषक् (*bhiṣak*)—the physician
- रुतं (*rutaṃ*)—desires disease
- ब्रह्मा (*brahmā*)—the Brahmin
- सुन्वंतं (*sunvaṃtaṃ*)—desires the sacrificer who presses Soma
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, our acts are of many kinds. The acts of men are of many kinds. The carpenter desires wood-work. The physician desires disease. The Brahmin desires the one who presses Soma. O Soma-deva, flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Various are our acts, (various) are the occupations of men; the carpenter desires timber, the physician disease, the Brahman a worshipper who effuse Soma : flow, Indu, for Indra.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> जर॑तीभि॒रोष॑धीभिः प॒र्णेभिः॑ शकु॒नानां॑ ।  
> का॒र्मा॒रो अश्म॑भि॒र्दुर्यभि॒र्हिर॑ण्यवंतमिच्छ॒तींद्रा॑येंदो॒ परि॑  
> स्रव ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जरतीभिः । ओषधीभिः! पर्णॆभिः । शकुनानां ।  
> कार्मारः । अश्वभिः । द्युभिः हिरण्यवंतं । इच्छति । इंद्राय । इंदो इति ।  
> परि । स्रव ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जरतीभिर्जीर्णाभिरोषधीभिरिषवः क्रियंते तथा शकुनानां पर्णॆभिरिषूणां
> पक्षभूतैः पर्णॆश्च क्रियंते तथा द्युभिर्दिप्ताभिरिषूणां तेजनार्थाभिरश्मिभिः
> शिलाभिश्च क्रियंते । एतैः कार्मारोऽयस्कारो हिरण्यवंतमाढ्यं पुरुषमिच्छति ।
> तथाहं त्वत्परिस्रवणमिच्छामि । तस्मादिंदो इंद्राय परि स्रव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Arrows are made with old dried plants (जरतीभिः ओषधीभिः (*jaratībhiḥ oṣadhībhiḥ*)); likewise the feathers of birds serve as the feathering of arrows; and with shining (द्युभिः (*dyubhiḥ*)) stones, that is, whetting stones or rays for sharpening the arrows, they are made. With these the smith (कार्मारः (*kārmāraḥ*), the iron-worker) desires a rich man (हिरण्यवंतं (*hiraṇyavaṃtaṃ*)). So I desire your flowing; therefore, O Indu, flow for Indra.

- इषवः (*iṣavaḥ*)—arrows are made
- शकुनानां (*śakunānāṃ*)—of birds
- पर्णेभिः (*parṇebhiḥ*)—with feathers the feathers of arrows are made
- द्युभिः (*dyubhiḥ*)—shining
- अश्वभीः (*aśvabhīḥ*)—with stones they are also made

- इच्छति (*icchati*)—desires
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Arrows are made with dried sticks. The feathers of arrows are made with the feathers of birds. They are also made with shining stones. The goldsmith and the carpenter desire a wealthy man. O Soma-deva, flow for Indra.

##### English translation
With dried plants (are arrows made), with the feathers of birds (and) with glistening stones; the smith seeks a man who has gold: flow, Indu, for Indra.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> का॒रुर॒हं त॒तो भि॒षगु॑पलप्र॒क्षिणी॑ न॒ना ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । स्रव ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिः प्रवृत्तसोमयागः सन् दशापवित्रात्सोमे क्षरति प्रतिबंधकपापापनुत्तये पुरश्चरितानुकीर्तनपुरःसरमध्येषणां चकार । तावदहं कारुः स्तोमानां
> कर्तास्मि । तत इति संताननाम । तन्यतेऽस्मादिति ततः पिता । तन्यतेसाविति वा ततः
> पुत्रः । भिषग्येषजकृत् । यज्ञस्य ब्रह्मेत्यर्थः । सर्वं त्रय्या विद्यया भिषज्यतीति
> श्रुतेः । ततोपलप्रक्षिणी । उपलेषु वालुकासु प्रक्षणोति यवान्हिनस्ति भृज्जतीति ।
> यद्वा । दृषदादिषूपलेषु बृष्टान्यवान्हिनस्ति चूर्णयतीति । अथवा धानासक्तुकरंभादीनां कारिका वा । असौ नना माता दुहिता वा । नमनक्रियायोग्यत्वात् ।
> माता खल्वपत्यं प्रति स्तनपानादिना नमनशीला भवति । दुहिता वा शुश्रूषार्थं ।
> एवं सर्वेषां परिचरणेन नानाधियो नानाकर्माणो वसूयवो धनकामा
> वयमनु तस्थिम । लोकमन्वास्थिताः स्मः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । गा इव ॥ छांदसो जसः
> शसादेशः ॥ गावो यथा गोष्ठमनुतिष्ठंति स्वपयःप्रदानेन परिचरंति वा एवं
> वयमपि परिचरामः । एतज्ञात्वा हे इंदो सोम इंद्राय परि स्रव । दशापवित्रात् क्षर । एवमेषाध्येषणा सत्कारपूर्विका व्यापारणा । अत्र निरुक्तं : उपलप्रक्षिणीत्युपलेषु प्रक्षिणात्युपलप्रक्षेपिणी वा । कारुरहमस्मि कर्ता स्तोमानां ततो
> भिषक् तत इति संताननाम पितुर्वा पुत्रस्य वा । उपलप्रक्षिणी सक्तुकारिका नना
> नमतेर्माता पा दुहिता वा ! नानाधियो नानाकर्माणो वसूयवो वसुकामा
> अन्वास्थिताः स्मो गाव इव लोकं । नि. ६.५ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer, having begun a Soma sacrifice, and Soma not flowing from the ten-fold filter, made a request, preceded by a recital of his own family's occupations, to remove the sin that obstructs. "I am a कारुः (*kāruḥ*), a maker of praises. ततः (*tataḥ*) is a name for offspring: one from whom (the family) is extended is father (ततः (*tataḥ*)), or one who is extended is son. भिषक् (*bhiṣak*) is the one who does the healing: the Brahmā of the sacrifice, since the Śruti says that everything is healed by the threefold knowledge. उपलप्रक्षिणी (*upalaprakṣiṇī*) is one who throws barley on the stones (grinding stones) and crushes or parches it; or, in another explanation, one who crushes the parched barley on mortar-stones; or she makes fried grain, flour, gruel and so on. नना (*nanā*) is mother or daughter, since she is fit for bowing: a mother bows to her child in nursing and so on; or a daughter for service. Thus by serving all, we, of various acts (नानाधियः (*nānādhiyaḥ*)) and desiring wealth (*vasūyavaḥ*), have taken our place in the world (अनु तस्थिम (*anu tasthima*)). Example: like cows (गा इव (*gā iva*); the plural accusative is Vedic): as cows keep to the stall or serve with the gift of their milk, so we serve. Knowing this, O Indu Soma, flow for Indra from the ten-fold filter. Such is this request, preceded by respect." Sāyaṇa then quotes the Nirukta (Ni. 6.5): उपलप्रक्षिणीत्युपलेषु प्रक्षिणात्युपलप्रक्षेपिणी वा । कारुरहमस्मि कर्ता स्तोमानां ततो भिषक् तत इति संताननाम पितुर्वा पुत्रस्य वा । उपलप्रक्षिणी सक्तुकारिका नना नमतेर्माता पा दुहिता वा ! नानाधियो नानाकर्माणो वसूयवो वसुकामा अन्वास्थिताः स्मो गाव इव लोकं । नि. ६.५ । इति ॥ (*upalaprakṣiṇītyupaleṣu prakṣiṇātyupalaprakṣepiṇī vā | kārurahamasmi kartā stomānāṃ tato bhiṣak tata iti saṃtānanāma piturvā putrasya vā | upalaprakṣiṇī saktukārikā nanā namatermātā pā duhitā vā ! nānādhiyo nānākarmāṇo vasūyavo vasukāmā anvāsthitāḥ smo gāva iva lokaṃ | ni. 6.5 | iti ‖*).

- नना (*nanā*)—our mother
- उपलप्रक्षिणी (*upalaprakṣiṇī*)—puts grain on the grinding stone and grinds

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I am a praiser. My father is a physician. Our mother puts grain on the grinding stone and grinds. Like cows resorting to the stall, we, having acts of many kinds and desiring wealth, have taken up various ways of life in this world. O Soma, flow for Indra.

##### English translation
I am the singer ; father is the physician, mother throws the corn upon the grinding stones; having various occupations, desiring riches we remain (in the world) like cattle (in the stalls): flow, Indu, for Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the beginning of this sūkta the commentator says: ऋषिरेतदादिभिस्त्रिभिः सूक्तैः अपरिस्रवतः सोमस्याजामित्वाय मनसो विनोदनं कुर्पन्नाह (*ṛṣiretadādibhistribhiḥ sūktaiḥ aparisravataḥ somasyājāmitvāya manaso vinodanaṃ kurpannāha*). The seer Śiśu, seer of this sūkta, was performing a sacrifice. At the time of pressing Soma, though he crushed and pressed the Soma plants, the Soma juice did not flow out properly. Noticing this, thinking स्वदुष्कृताशंकया किलापरिस्रवति सोमे पापसंकीर्तनादात्मशुद्धिर्भविष्यतीति मन्यमान आत्मानमेव निर्दिष्टन्नाह (*svaduṣkṛtāśaṃkayā kilāparisravati some pāpasaṃkīrtanādātmaśuddhirbhaviṣyatīti manyamāna ātmānameva nirdiṣṭannāha*) **NOTE**, he says: "Because of the sins I have committed, Soma does not come out of the plants in this way. Therefore if I proclaim my sins, and the acts done by me and by those connected with me, so that others hear them clearly, that sin will be pacified." So he has described in the Ṛks of this sūkta the activities of himself and of his father and the rest.

On these Ṛks Yāska has given the Nirukta:
कारुरहमस्मि कर्ता स्तोमानां । ततो भिषक् तत इति संताननाम पितुर्वा पुत्रस्य वा । उपलप्रक्षिणी सक्तुकारिका । नना नमतेर्माता ना दुहिता वा नानाधियो नानाकर्माणो वसूयवो वसुकामा अस्वास्थिताः स्मोगाव इव लोकं । इंद्रायेंदो परि स्रव इत्यध्येषणा ॥ (*kārurahamasmi kartā stomānāṃ | tato bhiṣak tata iti saṃtānanāma piturvā putrasya vā | upalaprakṣiṇī saktukārikā | nanā namatermātā nā duhitā vā nānādhiyo nānākarmāṇo vasūyavo vasukāmā asvāsthitāḥ smogāva iva lokaṃ | iṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ityadhyeṣaṇā ‖*) (Ni. 6-5)

### Printed p. 145
That is: I am a praiser, one who composes words of praise and offers them for the delight of the gods; my father is a physician who treats diseases. Here, since the word ततः (*tataḥ*) denotes offspring, the word may mean father or son. For the word भिषक् (*bhiṣak*) the Bhāṣyakāra and the commentators of the Nirukta have explained in another way, leaving aside the meaning "physician". Here "diseases" are the defects and omissions that occur in sacrifices and the like, and the priest called Brahmā, who corrects them by expiations and the like, is the physician. The word नना (*nanā*) also has two meanings, mother and daughter: since she is fit to be bowed to she is the mother; since she bows to oneself she is the daughter; so it can be explained in two ways. Therefore नना (*nanā*) means my mother or daughter, who grinds flour with the grinding stone. Therefore all of our household are engaged in various works for the sacrifice. And we, desiring wealth, are intent on our several duties as cows go to their stalls. Therefore, O Soma, flow quickly from the plants for Indra's drinking: such is the intent of the explanation (of the Nirukta) **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अश्वो॒ वोळ्हा॑ सु॒खं रथं॑ हस॒नामु॑पमं॒त्रिणः॑ ।  
> शेपो॒ रोम॑ण्वंत् भे॒दौ वारिन्मं॒डूक॑ इच्छ॒तींद्रा॑येंदो॒ परि॑ स्रव ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अश्वः । वोळ्हा । सुखं । रथं । हसनां । उपमंत्रिणः .  
> शेपः । रोमण् ऽवंतौ । भेदौ । वाः । इत् । मंडूकः । इच्छति । इंद्राय ।  
> इंदो इति । परि , स्रव ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वोळ्हा लक्ष्यं देशं प्रापयन्नश्वः सुखं कल्याणं रथमिच्छति । उपमंत्रिण
> उपमंत्रवंतो नर्मसचिवा हसनामुपहसनां वाचमिच्छंति । तथा शेषः । शेषो
> नैतस इति पुंसृजननस्येति यास्कः । नि. ३-२१ । यथा शेषो रोमण्वंतौ भेदाविच्छति । मंडूको वारित् ; इदवधारणे । उदकमेवेच्छति । तथाहं त्वत्परिस्रवणमिच्छामि । तस्मादिंद्रायेंदो परि स्रवेति ॥
> xxvii 10

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The horse (अश्वः (*aśvaḥ*)) that carries (वोळ्हा (*voḷhā*)) one to the intended place desires a good, comfortable chariot. The jesting companions (उपमंत्रिणः (*upamaṃtriṇaḥ*)), those who confer in jest, desire mocking speech (हसनां (*hasanāṃ*)). So also शेपः (*śepaḥ*): Yāska says शेषो नैतस इति पुंसृजननस्येति (*śeṣo naitasa iti puṃsṛjananasyeti*) (Ni. 3-21), i.e. the male organ of generation. As this desires the two hairy thighs (रोमण्वंत् भेदौ (*romaṇvaṃt bhedau*)), and the frog (मंडूकः (*maṃḍūkaḥ*)) desires only water (वारित् (*vārit*); इत् (*it*) is used in the sense of restriction), so I desire your flowing. Therefore, O Indu, flow for Indra.

## Sūkta 113 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शर्यणावतीत्येकादशर्चं दशमं सूक्तं मारीचस्य कश्यपस्यार्षं । पूर्वत्र
> हीत्युक्तत्वादिदमुत्तरं च पांक्तं । पवमानसोमदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रम्यते ।
> शर्यणावत्येकादश कश्यप इति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Śaryaṇāvatī…" is the tenth sūkta, of eleven ṛks; its seer is Kaśyapa, son of Marīci. This sūkta and the next are in the Pāṅkta metre (paṅkti). The deity is Pavamāna Soma. The Anukramaṇī says: शर्यणावत्येकादश कश्यप इति (*śaryaṇāvatyekādaśa kaśyapa iti*). The viniyoga has been stated already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "Śaryaṇāvatī" is the tenth sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. It has eleven ṛks. Kaśyapa, son of the sage Marīci, is its seer; this sūkta and the one after it are in the paṅkti metre. Pavamāna Soma is the deity. The statement in the Anukramaṇī, शर्यणावत्येकादश कश्यपः (*śaryaṇāvatyekādaśa kaśyapaḥ*), has been given; the viniyoga was stated earlier.

##### Particulars

Sūkta 113. Maṇḍala 9; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 113; Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 5; Vargas 26, 27. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 11. Seer: Kaśyapa. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Paṅkti.

### Printed p. 147
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒र्य॒णाव॑ति॒ सोम॒मिंद्रः॑ पिबतु वृत्र॒हा ।  
> बलं॒ दधा॑न आ॒त्मनि॑ करि॒ष्यन्वी॒र्यं॑ म॒हदिंद्रा॑येंदो॒ परि॑  
> स्रव ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बलं । दधानः । आत्मनि । करिष्यन् वीर्यं । महत् । इंद्राय । इंदो इति ।  
> परि । स्रव ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शर्यणावति । शर्यणावन्नाम कुरुक्षेत्रस्य जघनार्धे सरः । तत्र स्थितं
> सोमं वृत्रहेंद्रः पिबतु । कीदृशः । आत्मनि बलं दधानो बलं निदधानः अत एव
> महद्वीर्यं करिष्यञ्यत्रून्प्रति । तस्मादिंद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Śaryaṇāvat is the name of a lake in the rear half of Kurukṣetra. Let Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, drink the Soma that stands there. How is he? He holds strength within himself, and therefore will perform great valour against his enemies. Therefore, O Indu, flow for Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आत्मनि (*ātmani*)—in himself
- बलं (*balaṃ*)—strength
- दधानः (*dadhānaḥ*)—bearing
- महत् (*mahat*)—abundant
- वीर्यं (*vīryaṃ*)—valour

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Śaryaṇāvati—Śaryaṇāvat is the name of a lake near Kurukṣetra. It is traditionally said that Soma plants grew abundantly in the regions near this lake. An account has also been given earlier that the horse-shaped head of the sage Dadhyañc fell near this lake.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O lord of the directions, lord of the eastern and other directions as their illuminator; O showerer of desires; O Soma, from Ārjīka—Ārjīka is the country not far from Ṛjīkā—flow hither, come back to our sacrifice. Or else: flow from the Ārjīka, the straight, from the strainer. How is he? Pressed with the speech of ṛta and with satya (a slight difference between satya and ṛta is to be observed), by the initiated, endowed with faith and austerity. Flow thus pressed.

##### English translation
Soma, lord of the four regions, sprinkler ( of benefits ) flow from Arjika effused by a truthful man) with faith and devotion : flow, Indu, for Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Ārjikāt—यजीकानामदूरभव आर्जिको जनपदः । तस्मात् । (*yajīkānāmadūrabhava ārjiko janapadaḥ | tasmāt |*) Yajīkā is the name of a distant people; the region where they live is called Ārjika. So the commentator explains. Yāska, discussing rivers, says आर्जिकीयां विपाडित्याहुः (*ārjikīyāṃ vipāḍityāhuḥ*) (Ni. 9-26): Ārjikī is the name of a river, which has another name, Vipāṭ. Yajīka is a mountain, and the river that is born on it and flows is explained as named Ārjikā. It is well known that the Soma plants growing in the lands of the five peoples—Ārjīka, Pastāvat, Śaryaṇāvat, Suṣomā—are of the best kind and are obtained abundantly.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sūryasya duhitā is Śraddhā: श्रद्धा वै सूर्यस्य दुहितेति वाजसनेयकं (*śraddhā vai sūryasya duhiteti vājasaneyakaṃ*) (Śa. 12-7-3-11 **NOTE**). She brought that Soma, "grown by Parjanya", i.e. as capable as Parjanya; or else, grown by water, which is Parjanya's effect; *mahiṣa*, great and worthy of worship.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Gandharvāḥ pratyagṛbhan—this ṛk says that the goddess Śraddhā, daughter of Sūrya, brought Soma from the heavenly world and that the Gandharvas received it. The matter is told slightly differently in other śākhās. For example in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda: तं सोममाह्रियमाणं गंधर्वो विश्वावसुः पर्यमुष्णात्स तिस्रो रात्रिः परिमुषितोऽवसत्तस्मात्रिस्रो रात्रिः क्रीतः सोमो वसति ते देवा अब्रुवन्स्कीकामा वै गंधर्वास्त्रिया निष्क्रीणामेति ते वाचग्स् स्त्रीयमेकहायनीं कृत्वा तया निरक्रीणन्ता रोहिद्रूपं कृत्वाःगंधर्वेभ्योऽपक्रम्यातिष्ठत् ॥ (*taṃ somamāhriyamāṇaṃ gaṃdharvo viśvāvasuḥ paryamuṣṇātsa tisro rātriḥ parimuṣito 'vasattasmātrisro rātriḥ krītaḥ somo vasati te devā abruvanskīkāmā vai gaṃdharvāstriyā niṣkrīṇāmeti te vācags strīyamekahāyanīṃ kṛtvā tayā nirakrīṇantā rohidrūpaṃ kṛtvāḥgaṃdharvebhyo 'pakramyātiṣṭhat ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-6--5)
**NOTE**

Formerly Soma was in heaven. When no one could bring it to earth, Gāyatrī went to heaven in the form of a hawk, disregarded the resistance of the guardians of Soma who watched it there—Svān, Bhrāja, Aṅghāri, Bambhāri, Hasta, Sudasta, Kṛśānu—and

### Printed p. 151
brought it to earth. While she was bringing it, a Gandharva named Viśvāvasu seized that Soma on the way and kept it with himself for three days. The gods considered how to get it back from him; since the Gandharvas are greatly attached to women and full of desire, they resolved to show them the prospect of a woman and so recover the Soma. For this they went to Vāc, the goddess of speech, told her everything, and with her consent decided that she should become a beautiful woman, be sold to the Gandharvas, and that Soma be brought in exchange. Accordingly, when Vāc took the form of a beautiful woman, they gave her to the Gandharvas and brought back the Soma they had carried off. When Soma had become the gods' possession, Vāc, who was in the form of the beautiful woman, took the form of a red antelope, escaped from the Gandharvas, ran and joined the gods. Therefore from that time it became the custom to buy Soma plants for use in sacrifices. This ritual part of the sacrifice, the purchase of Soma, is still performed in sacrifices. Moreover, since the best Soma plants grow in high mountain regions (the mountain Mūjavat is famous for the Soma plant), bringing it requires great toil. So it seems it became the custom to pay a fitting price to those who took the trouble, out of desire for wealth, to go to the mountains and bring Soma, and to buy it. Because Soma, when the Gandharva carried it off, stayed with him three nights, there is a rule that Soma bought must be kept three nights. In the present ṛk this kind of praise of the Soma plant is stated.

- ऋतद्युम्न (*ṛtadyumna*)—you who shine with truth

- सोम (*soma*)—O divine Soma

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सत्यं उग्रस्य । बृहतः । सं । स्रवंति । संस्रवाः ।  
> सं । यंति । रसिनः । रसाः । पुनानः । ब्रह्मणा । हरे । इंद्राय । इंदो इति ।  
> परि । स्रव ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सत्यमुग्रस्य संग्रामे सत्येन शत्रूणामुद्गारयितुः । यद्वा । उद्धर्णसत्यस्य । यद्वा । यथार्थभूतमुद्दूर्णं बलं यस्य तस्य ॥ पृषोदरादित्वाद्रूपसिद्धिः ॥ बृहतो महतः सोमस्य तव संस्रवाः सम्यक्स्रवणशीला धाराः सं
> स्रवंति । सम्यग्गच्छंति । किंच रसिनो रसवतस्तव स्वभूता रसाः सं यंति। संगच्छंते।
> तस्माद्दे हरे हरितवर्ण सोम ब्रह्मणा ब्राह्मणेन मंत्रेण वा पुनानः पूयमानः स त्वमिंद्रार्थं परि स्रव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains सत्यमुग्रस्य (*satyamugrasya*) as "of him who by truth makes his enemies vomit up (their strength) in battle"; or "of him whose truth is lofty"; or "of him whose strength is real and lofty". The form is accounted for by the rule of पृषोदरादि (*pṛṣodarādi*). The streams (संस्रवाः (*saṃsravāḥ*)), whose nature is to flow together, of you, the great Soma, flow together, that is, go together properly. Further, your own juices, the juices of you the juicy one, meet together. Therefore, O green-hued Soma, being purified by the Brāhmaṇa or by a mantra, flow for Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सत्यमुग्रस्य (*satyamugrasya*)—of him who truly has a manifesting strength
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—of the great Soma
- संस्रवाः (*saṃsravāḥ*)—flowing streams
- सं स्रवंति (*saṃ sravaṃti*)—flow
- रसिनः (*rasinaḥ*)—of the juicy Soma
- रसाः (*rasāḥ*)—juices
- सं यंति (*saṃ yaṃti*)—flow together
- हरे (*hare*)—green-hued
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)—by the mantra
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—you who are purified
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The streams of Soma, who shines with true valour and is great, flow. The juices of the juicy Soma flow together. O green-hued Soma, purified by the mantra or by the Brāhmaṇa, flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
The united sereams of you who are vast and truly formidable flow united ; the juices of you the juicy one meet together ; green-tinted (Soma) purified by holy prayer, Indu, flow for Indra.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत्र । ब्रह्मा । प्रवमान । छंदस्यां । वाचं । वदन् ।  
> ग्रावा । सोमे । महीयते । सोमेन । आनंदं । जनयन् : इंद्राय ।  
> इंदो इति । परि । स्रव ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान पूयमान सोम त्वदर्थं छंदस्यां सप्तछंदोभिः कृतां तेषु
> भवां वाचं स्तुतिं वदन्नुच्चारयन् सोमे सोमाभिषवार्थं ग्राव्णाभिषवं
> कुर्वता युक्तस्तेनाभिषुतेन सोमेन देवानामानंदं संतोषं जनयन्नुत्पादयन्न ब्राह्मणो यत्र यस्मिन्देशे महीयते देवैः पूज्यते तत्र हे
> सोम त्वं परि स्रव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O purified Soma, for you the Brāhmaṇa (ब्रह्मा (*brahmā*)) utters a speech (वाचं (*vācaṃ*)), a praise, composed in the seven metres and consisting of them. He is engaged in pressing Soma with the pressing-stone, and by the pressed Soma he produces delight, contentment, for the gods. In whatever region he is honoured by the gods, there, O Soma, flow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O Soma, who are purified
- छंदस्यां (*chaṃdasyāṃ*)—composed of the seven metres
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—the praise-speech
- वदन् (*vadan*)—reciting
- सोमे (*some*)—for the obtaining of Soma
- ग्राव्णा (*grāvṇā*)—with the pressing-stones, pressed
- सोमेन (*somena*)—with the Soma juice
- आनंदं (*ānaṃdaṃ*)—delight to the gods
- जनयन् (*janayan*)—producing
- ब्रह्मा (*brahmā*)—the Brāhmaṇa
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in whatever region
- महीयते (*mahīyate*)—is honoured, in that place
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, who are purified: in whatever region the Brāhmaṇa is honoured who recites praise-speech composed in the seven metres and with Soma pressed by the pressing-stones for the obtaining of Soma produces delight for the gods, in that place flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Wherever the Brahman, O purified ( Soma ), reciting the holy rhythmical text, engendering the delight (of the gods) by the Soma (expressed) with the grinding-stone, is reverenced, flow, Indu, for Indra.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्र॒ ज्योति॒रज॑स्रं॒ यस्मि॑ल्लो॒के स्व॑र्हि॒तं ।  
> तस्मि॒न्मां धे॑हि पवमाना॒मृते॑ लो॒के अक्षि॑त॒ इंद्रा॑येंदो॒ ॑ 
> परि स्रव ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत्र । ज्योतिः । अजस्रं । यस्मिन् । लोके । स्वः । हितं ।  
> तस्मिन् । मां । धेहि । पवमान । अमृते । लोके । अक्षिते । इंद्राय । इंदोइति । हरि । स्तव ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान यत्र यस्मिल्लोके ज्योतिः सर्वं तेजोऽजस्रं सर्वदाविनश्वरं वर्तते । यस्मिंश्च लोके स्वरादित्याख्यं ज्योतिर्हितं निहितमस्ति । तस्मिन्न
> मृते मरणधर्मरहिते आत एवाक्षितेऽक्षीणे लोके मां सोमाभिषवं कुर्वंतं
> धेहि । निधेहि । तस्मान्मामुत्तमलोकं प्रापयितुं त्वमिंद्राय परि स्रव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pavamāna, in the world where all light is unceasing and imperishable, and in which the light called the sun is placed, in that immortal, hence undecaying world, place me who am pressing Soma. To bring me to that highest world, flow for Indra.

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O Soma-deva
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which world

- अजस्रं (*ajasraṃ*)—is eternal
- यस्मिन् लोके (*yasmin loke*)—in which world
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the radiance of the sun
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—is established
- तस्मिन् (*tasmin*)—in that
- अमृते (*amṛte*)—deathless
- अक्षिते (*akṣite*)—and undecaying
- लोके (*loke*)—world
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—place
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, in the world where all radiance is eternal, in which the sun's radiance is established, in that deathless and undecaying world place me. O Soma, flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Where light is perpetual, in the world in which the sun is placed, in that immortal imperishable world place me, Pavamana; flow, Indu, for Indra.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्रा॒मूर्य॒ह्वती॒राप॒स्तत्र॒ माम॒मृतं॑ कृ॒धींद्रा॑येंदो॒ ॑

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत्र । राजा । वैवस्वतः । यत्र । अव्यरोधनं । दिवः ।  
> यत्र । अमूः । यह्वतीः । अपः । तत्र । मां । अमृतं । कृधि । इंद्राय । इंदो  
> इति । परि । स्वव ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत्र यस्मिल्लोके वैवस्वतो विवस्वत्पुत्रो राजा भवति । यत्र च लोके
> दिव आदित्यस्यावरोधनं भूतानां प्रवेशनं । किंच यत्र लोके यह्वतीर्महत्योमूरिमा गंगाद्या अपस्तिष्ठंति । तत्र तादृशे लोके मामृतं मरणधर्मरहितं कृधि ! कुरु । मम देवत्वं प्रापयेत्यर्थः । ततः कारणात्परि स्रव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the world where Vaivasvata, the son of Vivasvat, is king; where there is the अवरोधनं (*avarodhanaṃ*) of the sun, the entering of beings; and where those great waters, the Gaṅgā and others, abide: in such a world make me immortal, free from the nature of death; that is, bring me to godhood. For that reason flow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which world

- राजा (*rājā*)—is lord
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which world
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the sun
- अवरोधनं (*avarodhanaṃ*)—there is inner entry
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which world
- यह्वतीः (*yahvatīḥ*)—of great nature
- अमूः आपः (*amūḥ āpaḥ*)—the purified waters of the Gaṅgā and other rivers are
- तत्र (*tatra*)—in such a world
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—as deathless
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make (establish)
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, in the world where the son of Vivasvat is lord, where the sun has inner entry, where the purified waters of the Gaṅgā and other rivers, of great nature, are, in such a world make me deathless. Flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Where Vivaswat's son is king, where the inner chamber of the sun (is), where these great waters (are). there make me immortal; flow, Indu, for Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यत्र राजा वैवस्वतः (*yatra rājā vaivasvataḥ*)—The king who is the son of the well-known deity named Vivasvān is called Vaivasvata. It is customary also to call him Yama. Explanations concerning him are given at length in the later sūktas of this same part (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-10 etc.).

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्रा॑नुका॒मं चर॑णं त्रिना॒के त्रि॑दि॒वे दि॒वः ।  
> लो॒का यत्र॒ ज्योति॑ष्मंत॒स्तत्र॒ माम॒मृतं॑ कृ॒धींद्रा॑येंदो॒ ॑ 
> परि स्रव ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत्र । अनुकामं । चरणं । त्रिनाके । त्रिदिने । दिवः ।  
> लोकाः । यत्र । ज्योतिष्मंतः । तत्र । मां । अमृतं । कृधि । इंद्राय ; इंदो  
> इति । परि । स्त्रव ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत्र त्रिदिवे तृतीयस्यां दिवि द्युलोके त्रिनाके । तत्राधरमध्यमोत्तमभावेन त्रीणि स्थानानि संति । तत्र तृतीये नाक उत्तमे स्थाने दिव आदित्यस्यानुकामं कामानुगुणं चरणमस्ति । किंच यत्र यस्मिल्लोके लोका ज्योतिष्मंतो
> ज्योतिर्युक्तास्तिष्ठंति । तत्र तादृरे लोके मामृतं कृधि । यथा ममोत्तमलोको भवति तथा त्वमिंद्राय परि स्रव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the third heaven (त्रिदिवे (*tridive*)), the heavenly world, the त्रिनाके (*trināke*), there are three places, lower, middle and highest. In the third, the highest place (नाके (*nāke*)), the sun has movement as he wishes (अनुकामं (*anukāmaṃ*)). Further, in whatever world the worlds stand endowed with light, in such a world make me immortal. That I may get the highest world, flow for Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma-deva) त्रिनाके (*trināke*)—which has three places, lower, middle and highest
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which
- त्रिदिवे (*tridive*)—in the third heavenly world
- दिनः (*dinaḥ*)—of the sun
- अनुकामं (*anukāmaṃ*)—independent **NOTE**

- चरणं (*caraṇaṃ*)—movement is
- यत्र (*yatra*)—where
- लोकाः (*lokāḥ*)—all worlds
- ज्योतिष्मंतः (*jyotiṣmaṃtaḥ*)—are full of radiance
- तत्र (*tatra*)—in such a highest world
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—deathless
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make and establish
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, in that third heavenly world having three divisions, lower, middle and highest, where the sun has independent movement, where all worlds are full of radiance, in such a highest world make me deathless and establish me. O Soma, flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Where in the third heaven, in the third sphere, the sun wanders at will, where the regions are filled with light, there make me immortal: flow, Indu, for Indra.

In the world where there are desires and excellent aims, in the world where the abode of the Āditya, the impeller of rites, is, where there are food and satisfaction, there make me free from death and establish me. O Soma, flow for Indra's drinking.

Where wishes and desires (are), where the region of the sun (is), where food and delight (are) found, there make me immortal ; flow, Indu, for Indra.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the world where bliss and the rest abide (a slight difference among them is to be noted), and where all the desires of the god who is desired are fulfilled, there make me immortal. This cannot happen without you; therefore, O Soma, flow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—where
- कामस्य (*kāmasya*)—of one who seeks happiness
- आप्ताः (*āptāḥ*)—desired
- कामाः (*kāmāḥ*)—wishes are fulfilled
- तत्र (*tatra*)—there
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—free from death
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make and establish
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the world where there are supreme bliss of Brahman, joys, means of happiness and experiences of happiness, where the wishes of one who seeks happiness are fulfilled so as to satisfy his desire, there make me free from death and establish me. O Soma, flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Where there is happiness, pleasures, joy and enjoyment, where the wishes of the wisher are obtained, there make me immortal; flow, Indu, for Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Ānandāḥ, modāḥ, mudaḥ, pramudaḥ: all these words denote one kind of meaning, bliss. Though there are slight differences, the use of these words denoting one meaning is seen in many Śruti sentences such as मोदः प्रमोद आनंदः (*modaḥ pramoda ānaṃdaḥ*) and the like.

## Sūkta 114 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: the sūkta य इंदोः (*ya iṃdoḥ*) is the eleventh sūkta; it has four Ṛks; its first (seer, deity, metre) are as in the previous sūkta. The Anukramaṇī says य इंदोश्च तुष्कमिति (*ya iṃdośca tuṣkamiti*). The use of the sūkta has been stated.**NOTE**

### Printed p. 161

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta य इंदोः (*ya iṃdoḥ*) is the eleventh sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. It has four Ṛks. This sūkta has the same seer, deity and metre as the preceding sūkta. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: य इंदोश्चतुष्कं (*ya iṃdoścatuṣkaṃ*). The use of the sūkta was stated earlier.

Sūkta—114
Maṇḍala—9; Anuvāka—7; Sūkta—114
Aṣṭaka—7; Adhyāya—5; Varga—28
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—4
Seer—Kaśyapa
Deity—Pavamāna Soma
Metre—Paṅkti

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पवमानस्य पूयमानस्येंदोः सोमस्येंदोः सोमस्य धामानि
> स्थानानि द्रोणकलशादीनि यद्वा धामानि तेजांसि यो ब्राह्मणोऽस्त्वक्रमीत् अनुक्रामति अनुगच्छति तं जनं सुप्रजाः शोभनप्रजननः कल्याणपुत्रादिप्रजायुक्त इत्याहुः ॥ नित्यमसिच् प्रजामेधयोरित्यसिच् समासांतः ॥ यः सोममभिषुणोति स पुत्रादियुक्तो भवतीत्यर्थः । किंच हे सोम यो मनुष्यस्ते
> त्वदर्थं मनोऽविधत् करोति । यद्वा ! ते त्वदीयं मनोऽविधत् परिचरति ।
> विधतिः परिचरणकर्मा ! तमपि कल्याण जननमित्याहुः । तस्मात्त्वं परि स्रव ॥
> xxv xxvii 11

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of the purifying Soma, whose abodes are the Droṇa-vessel and the like (or else "abodes" means splendours), the Brāhmaṇa who follows them is called सुप्रजाः (*suprajāḥ*), blessed with fine offspring, sons and the like; that is, whoever presses Soma becomes endowed with sons and the rest. Further, O Soma, the man who directs his mind to you (or else: attends upon your mind, विधतिः (*vidhatiḥ*) being a root of service) is also called blessed with fine offspring. Therefore flow.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सप्त दिशः । सोमो यस्यां दिशि वर्तते तद्व्यतिरिक्ताः सप्त भवंति । ता नानासूर्या नानाविधैः सूर्यैरधिष्ठिता ऋतवो भवंति । नागलिंगत्वादृतूनां नानासूर्यत्वमित्याम्नानात् । यद्वा । नानासूर्या इति दिग्विशेषणं । तथा होतारो
> वषट्कर्तारो होत्रादयः सप्तर्त्वजो भवंति । किंच सप्तादित्या अदितेः पुत्रा,
> धात्रादयो मार्तंडवर्जिता ये सप्त देवाः संति । एतत्त्वष्टौ पुत्रासो आदितेः ।
> ऋ. सं. १०-७२-८ । इत्यत्र प्रपंचयिष्यते । हे सोम तेभिस्तैर्दिगादिभिः सर्वैर्नोऽस्मानभि रक्ष । एतत्तु त्वया विना न घटत इति तस्मादिंद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seven quarters: those other than the quarter in which Soma stands are seven; they are the seasons, governed by various suns, since the seasons have various forms ("because of the many genders of the seasons they have many suns", so the tradition says); or else "of various suns" qualifies the quarters. The seven priests, hotṛ and the rest, are the utterers of vaṣaṭ. The seven Ādityas, sons of Aditi, Dhātṛ and others without Mārtaṇḍa, are the seven gods; this is to be elaborated at ऋ. सं. १०-७२-८ (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-72-8*) (एतत्त्वष्टौ पुत्रासो आदितेः (*etattvaṣṭau putrāso āditeḥ*)). O Soma, protect us with all these, the quarters and the rest. This cannot happen without you; therefore flow for Indra.
