##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सप्त दिशो नानासूर्याः (*sapta diśo nānāsūryāḥ*)—Here the four directions and the four intermediate directions together make eight quarters. सोमो यस्यां दिशि वर्तते दद्व्यतिरिक्ता सप्त भवंति (*somo yasyāṃ diśi vartate dadvyatiriktā sapta bhavaṃti*): apart from the quarter in which Soma or the deity Soma is, the remaining ones are seven quarters; therefore it is said here "seven quarters". In these quarters there are various seasons presided over by various kinds of suns. On this point the commentator has cited the Śruti sentence नानालिंगत्वावृतूनां नानासूर्यत्वं (*nānāliṃgatvāvṛtūnāṃ nānāsūryatvaṃ*). Though the sun is one, according to the nature of the seasons the sun

### Printed p. 165

Since they are present in those (directions), that is, since they are endowed with various qualities according to the seasons, the plural "various suns" is used here.

देवा आदित्या ये सप्त (*devā ādityā ye sapta*): further, if the word sūrya is taken in the sense of Āditya (son of Aditi), then Aditi has six, seven or eight sons. Who they are can be cited from the Ṛk अष्टौ पुत्रासो आदितेः (*aṣṭau putrāso āditeḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 18-72.-8) **NOTE** and from other Vedic passages. On this question, how many sons of Aditi, or Ādityas, there are, some explanation is necessary.

It is necessary to discuss closely here what the numerical limit of the deities called Ādityas is. In the Ṛk इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यः (*imā gira ādityebhyaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-26-1) which Yāska gives as an example, six deities are named: Mitra, Aryamā, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa and Aṃśa; these are said to be the Ādityas. But for the word tuvijāta the Nirukta-author explains बहुजातश्च धाता (*bahujātaśca dhātā*) (Ni. 12.-26), "धाता (*dhātā*)". How? तुवीति बहुनाम । सर्वविधातृत्वाद्वहुजन्मा धाता यावदधिकारं जन्मेति । (*tuvīti bahunāma | sarvavidhātṛtvādvahujanmā dhātā yāvadadhikāraṃ janmeti |*), the Nirukta-author has explained. The word tuvi means "many". Janman means "office"; tuvijāta means Dhātā, the maker of all, with many kinds of offices. Since the word tuvijāta is thus explained, one must say that in this Ṛk there are seven Ādityas, counting Dhātā. And in the mantra सप्त दिशो नाना सूराः (*sapta diśo nānā sūrāḥ*) the number of Ādityas is given as seven (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-114-3), but the names are not given; only देवा आदित्या ये सप्त (*devā ādityā ye sapta*) is stated. Earlier, when speaking of Aditi, the mantras 10.27-8, 9 were cited, and it was explained that Aditi had eight sons, that she offered seven of them to the gods, and that she kept the eighth, Mārtāṇḍa, for herself and nourished him. Here too, apart from Mārtāṇḍa, the others are not named. In the mantra (Ai. Ve. 8-9-21) **NOTE** it is said that Aditi has eight sons. In explaining the purport of the mantra 2-27-1, Sāyaṇa quoted a sentence of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka to state their number: अष्टौ पुत्रासो आदिते (*aṣṭau putrāso ādite*) ... and ताननुक्रमि स्वामः मित्रश्च वरुणश्च ! धाता चारमा च । अग्‌ंशश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्ंक्षेते (*tānanukrami svāmaḥ mitraśca varuṇaśca ! dhātā cāramā ca | agṃśaśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāgṃkṣete*) (Tai. Ā. 1-13.3); as is there, the eight sons of Aditi are named.

In places such as उदगादयमादित्यः (*udagādayamādityaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-12) and उदपप्तदसौ सूर्यः (*udapaptadasau sūryaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-191-1), the identity of Sūrya and Āditya is stated. It is also described that Agni, the son of Aditi, was established in the sky by the gods in the form of the sun: यदेदेनमदधुर्यज्ञि यासो दिवि देवाः सूर्यमादितेयं (*yadedenamadadhuryajñi yāso divi devāḥ sūryamāditeyaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 11-88-11) **NOTE**. आनर्वाणो हैषां पंथा आदित्यानां (*ānarvāṇo haiṣāṃ paṃthā ādityānāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-18-2): thus the nature of the path of the Ādityas is stated, and

### Printed p. 166

then, तत्सु नः सविता भगो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा (*tatsu naḥ savitā bhago varuṇo mitro aryamā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-18-3): here the name of Savitṛ is joined with the four Ādityas. In some places the deity Sūra or Savitṛ is assigned the seventh place among the Ādityas (Ath. Saṃ. 8-2-9 : 37) **NOTE**. In some places Indra, along with Varuṇa, is counted as an Āditya (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-85-4).

In places such as शत्रु त्वादित्या रक्ष्यतां सूर्याचंद्रमसावुभौ (*śatru tvādityā rakṣyatāṃ sūryācaṃdramasāvubhau*) (Ath. Saṃ. 8-2-15), both Sūrya and Candra are included in the group of Ādityas.

मात्यादित्यानां दुहिता वसूनां . . . हिरण्यवर्णा मधुकशा (*mātyādityānāṃ duhitā vasūnāṃ . . . hiraṇyavarṇā madhukaśā*) (Ath. Saṃ. 9-1-4): the golden-hued Madhukaśā is called the mother of the Ādityas and the daughter of the Vasus. Thus in each context the relation between Aditi and the Ādityas is stated in a different way. Their relation is explained in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa as follows.

अदितिः पुत्रकामा । साध्येभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्रह्मादनमपचत् । तस्या उच्छे षणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्मै धाता चार्यमा चा जायेतां । सा द्वितीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् ॥ सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्यै मित्रश्च वरुणश्चाजायेतां । सा तृतीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या अगंंशश्च भगश्चाजायेतां । सा चतुर्थमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्श्चाजायेतां ॥ (*aditiḥ putrakāmā | sādhyebhyo devebhyo brahmādanamapacat | tasyā ucche ṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasmai dhātā cāryamā cā jāyetāṃ | sā dvitīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt ‖ sā reto 'dhatta | tasyai mitraśca varuṇaścājāyetāṃ | sā tṛtīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā agaṃṃśaśca bhagaścājāyetāṃ | sā caturthamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā iṃdraśca vivasvāgścājāyetāṃ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1,2,3) **NOTE**.

Aditi, desiring sons, cooked for the gods and the Sādhyas a oblation of the form of brahmaudana. They themselves ate that oblation and gave her the remainder. When she ate it, by its power two sons were born, Dhātā and Aryamā. When the same procedure was performed a second time, Mitra and Varuṇa were produced; the third time, Aṃśa and Bhaga; the fourth time, Indra and Vivasvat. The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa describes these as the Ādityas.

Explaining the same matter, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa says as follows.

स मनसा एव वाचं मिथुनं समभवत्स द्वादशद्रप्सान्गर्भ्यभवत् । ते द्वादश आदित्या अस्यज्यंत तान् दिक्षूपादधत् ॥ (*sa manasā eva vācaṃ mithunaṃ samabhavatsa dvādaśadrapsāngarbhyabhavat | te dvādaśa ādityā asyajyaṃta tān dikṣūpādadhat ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 6:1-2-8)

### Printed p. 167

(Prajāpati) entered into a mental union with Vāk. Then he conceived a womb consisting of twelve drops. Its fruit was the appearance of the twelve Ādityas. Then he placed them as the guardians of the directions. So it is said. In the same way one may examine other Vedic passages that speak of the Ādityas.

कतम आदित्या इति । द्वादश वै मासाः । संवत्सरस्यैत आदित्या एते हीदं सर्वमाददाना यंति ते यदिदं सर्वमाददाना यंति तस्मादादित्या इति ॥ (*katama ādityā iti | dvādaśa vai māsāḥ | saṃvatsarasyaita ādityā ete hīdaṃ sarvamādadānā yaṃti te yadidaṃ sarvamādadānā yaṃti tasmādādityā iti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 11-6-3-8)

How many Ādityas are there? The Ādityas are twelve in number. In a year there are twelve months. These are the Ādityas. Because those months go on taking hold of everything, they are called Ādityas. So it is said. The story concerning these Ādityas is told in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa as follows:

आदित्याश्चांगिरसश्च सुवर्गे लोकेऽस्पर्धंतः तेऽंगिरस आदित्येभ्यः। अमुमादित्यमश्वग्न् श्वेतं भूतं दक्षिणामनयन् । तेऽब्रुवन् । यन्नोऽवेष्ट । स वरोऽभूदिति। तस्मादश्वग्न् सवर्येत्याह्वयंति। तस्माद्यज्ञे वरो दीयते॥ (*ādityāścāṃgirasaśca suvarge loke 'spardhaṃtaḥ te 'ṃgirasa ādityebhyaḥ| amumādityamaśvagn śvetaṃ bhūtaṃ dakṣiṇāmanayan | te 'bruvan | yanno 'veṣṭa | sa varo 'bhūditi| tasmādaśvagn savaryetyāhvayaṃti| tasmādyajñe varo dīyate‖*)

यत्प्रजापतिरालब्दोऽश्वोऽभवत् । तस्मादश्वो नाम । यच्छ्वयदरुरासीत् । तस्मादर्वानाम । यत्सद्यो वाजस्थमजयत् । तस्माद्वाजी नाम । यदसुसाराणां लोकानादत्त । तस्मादादित्यो नाम ॥ (*yatprajāpatirālabdo 'śvo 'bhavat | tasmādaśvo nāma | yacchvayadarurāsīt | tasmādarvānāma | yatsadyo vājasthamajayat | tasmādvājī nāma | yadasusārāṇāṃ lokānādatta | tasmādādityo nāma ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-9-21-1,2) **NOTE**

In heaven the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases competed with one another. The Aṅgirases offered to the Ādityas, as sacrificial fee, that Āditya who had the form of a white horse. Then the Ādityas said to the Aṅgirases: "This Āditya that you have brought is of a most excellent form." Because the Ādityas said of the horse-formed Āditya "स वरः (*sa varaḥ*)" (he is the best), the horse too came to be called savara in the world. Therefore a boon (vara) is given in the sacrifice. Prajāpati, offered in the sacrifice, is famous as *aśva* because he is all-pervading; as "arvan" because he experienced a pain of the eyes **NOTE**; as "वाजि (*vāji*)" because he brought all wealth under his control; and as "आदित्य (*āditya*)" because he seized (ādatta) all the worlds from the Asuras. In this way the derivation of the word Āditya is given. Explaining the same derivation, the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka says:

योऽसौ तपन्नुदेति । स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायोदेति । (*yo 'sau tapannudeti | sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇānādāyodeti |*) (Tai. Ā. 1.14-1) **NOTE**

This sun who rises, he rises after seizing (ā + dā) the vital breaths of all beings. Therefore he is Āditya. Thus two kinds of context are described: that they are Ādityas because they are sons of Aditi, or that they are Ādityas because they are characterised by the act of seizing (ādāna). The Nirukta-author has explained this word as follows.

### Printed p. 168

आदित्यः कस्मात् । आदत्ते रसान् । आदत्ते भासं ज्योतिषां । आदीपो भासेति वा अदितेः पुत्र इति वा । ...... ...... .....सूरमादितेयं । एवमन्यासामपि देवतानामादित्यप्रवादाः स्तुतयो भवंति । तद्यथैतत् । मित्रस्य वरुणस्यार्यन्नो दक्षस्य भगस्यांशस्येति ॥ (*ādityaḥ kasmāt | ādatte rasān | ādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāṃ | ādīpo bhāseti vā aditeḥ putra iti vā | ...... ...... .....sūramāditeyaṃ | evamanyāsāmapi devatānāmādityapravādāḥ stutayo bhavaṃti | tadyathaitat | mitrasya varuṇasyāryanno dakṣasya bhagasyāṃśasyeti ‖*) (Ni. 2.13)

As it is described in सहस्रगुणमुत्सृष्टमादत्ते हि रसं रविः (*sahasraguṇamutsṛṣṭamādatte hi rasaṃ raviḥ*) and so on, the name Āditya is famous because he seizes the sap. Not only the sap; he seizes all brilliance. The name is famous either because he blazes with light or because he is the son of Aditi. But in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā Sūra is called a son of Aditi only in a place or two. In places such as दिवि देवाः सूर आदितेयं (*divi devāḥ sūra āditeyaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-11) there is this explanatory description. Besides Sūra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Dakṣa, Bhaga and Aṃśa are also designated as Ādityas. Thus, if the purport of the word Āditya is the description of one's own quality, it applies only to Sūra. If it shows being a son of Aditi, it applies also to Mitra, Varuṇa and the rest. If the second meaning is given, then how many sons of Aditi there are becomes a matter to be determined exactly. Numbers are stated as six, eight, twelve and so on. Some Vedic passages showing this number have been cited above.

सप्त होतार ऋत्विजः (*sapta hotāra ṛtvijaḥ*): the seven hotṛs here are seven officiating priests: Hotṛ, Maitrāvaruṇa, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, Acchāvāka and Āgnīdhra. These priests, in all three savanas, the morning savana, the midday savana and the third savana (the rite of pressing out the Soma juice and offering it in the fire according to rule is called a savana), each offer Soma in the fire with one Ṛk, with the vaṣaṭ-call, that is, adding the word vauṣaṭ at the end of the mantra. The rule is that at the morning savana the offering is made with Ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre, at the midday savana with Ṛks in the Triṣṭubh metre, and at the third savana with mantras in the Jagatī metre. These mantras, recited by the respective priests at the respective savanas, are called prasthita-yājyā mantras or sapta-hotra mantras. They are set out here in detail:

**The morning savana**

At this savana all seven priests must recite Ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre.

1. The mantra to be recited by the Hotṛ:
इदं ते सोम्यं मध्वधक्षन्नद्रिभिर्नरः । जुषाण इंद्र तत्पिब ॥ (*idaṃ te somyaṃ madhvadhakṣannadribhirnaraḥ | juṣāṇa iṃdra tatpiba ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-65-8)

### Printed p. 169

2. The mantra to be recited by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin:
इंद्र त्वा वृषभं वयं सुते सोमे हवामहे । स पाहि मध्यो अंधसः ॥ (*iṃdra tvā vṛṣabhaṃ vayaṃ sute some havāmahe | sa pāhi madhyo aṃdhasaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-40-1)

3. The mantra to be recited by the priest called Mitrāvaruṇa:
मित्रं वयं हवामहे वरुणं सोमपीतये । जज्ञाना पूतदक्षसा ॥ (*mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe varuṇaṃ somapītaye | jajñānā pūtadakṣasā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-4)

4. The mantra to be recited by the priest called Potṛ:
नुरुतो यस्य हि क्षये पाथा दिवो विमहसः । स सुगोपातमो जनः ॥ (*nuruto yasya hi kṣaye pāthā divo vimahasaḥ | sa sugopātamo janaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-86-1)

5. The mantra to be recited by the priest called Neṣṭṛ:
अग्ने पत्निरिहा वह देवानामुशतीरुव । त्वष्टारं सोमपीतये ॥ (*agne patnirihā vaha devānāmuśatīruva | tvaṣṭāraṃ somapītaye ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-9)

6. The mantra to be recited by the priest called Āgnīdhra:
उक्षान्नाय वशान्नाय सोमपृष्टाय वेधसे । स्तोमैर्विधेमाग्नये ॥ (*ukṣānnāya vaśānnāya somapṛṣṭāya vedhase | stomairvidhemāgnaye ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-43-11)

7. The mantra to be recited by the priest called Ājñāvāka **NOTE**:
प्रातर्यावभिरा गतं देवेभिर्जेन्यावसू ! इंद्राग्नी सोमपीतये ॥ (*prātaryāvabhirā gataṃ devebhirjenyāvasū ! iṃdrāgnī somapītaye ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-38-7)

**The midday savana**

At this savana only mantras in the Triṣṭubh metre are to be recited. Among them:

8. The mantra to be recited by the Hotṛ:
पिबा सोममभि यमुग्र तर्द ऊर्वं गव्यं महि गृणान वि यो धृष्टो वधिषो वज्रहस्त विश्वा वृक्रममित्रिया शव (*pibā somamabhi yamugra tarda ūrvaṃ gavyaṃ mahi gṛṇāna vi yo dhṛṣṭo vadhiṣo vajrahasta viśvā vṛkramamitriyā śava*)

### Printed p. 170

2. Maitrāvaruṇa:
स ई पाहि य ऋजीषी तरुत्तो यः शिप्रवान् वृषभो यो मतीनां । यो गोत्रभिद्दज्रभिद्यो हरिष्ठाः स इंद्र चित्रा मभि त्वंधि वाजान् ॥ (*sa ī pāhi ya ṛjīṣī tarutto yaḥ śipravān vṛṣabho yo matīnāṃ | yo gotrabhiddajrabhidyo hariṣṭhāḥ sa iṃdra citrā mabhi tvaṃdhi vājān ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-17-2)

3. Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin:
एवा पाहि प्रत्नथा मंदतु त्वा श्रुधि ब्रह्म नावृधस्वत गीर्भिः । आविः सूर्यं कृणुहि पीपिहीषो जहि शत्रुरभि गा इंद्र तृंधि ॥ (*evā pāhi pratnathā maṃdatu tvā śrudhi brahma nāvṛdhasvata gīrbhiḥ | āviḥ sūryaṃ kṛṇuhi pīpihīṣo jahi śatrurabhi gā iṃdra tṛṃdhi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-17-2) **NOTE**

4. Potṛ:
अर्वाजीहि सोमकामं त्वाहुरयं सुतस्तस्य पिबा मदाय । उरुव्यचा जठर आ वृषस्व पितेव नः शृणुहि हूयमानः ॥ (*arvājīhi somakāmaṃ tvāhurayaṃ sutastasya pibā madāya | uruvyacā jaṭhara ā vṛṣasva piteva naḥ śṛṇuhi hūyamānaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-104-9)

5. Neṣṭṛ:
तवायं सोमस्त्वमेह्यर्वाज् शश्वत्तमं सुमना अस्य पाहि । अस्मिन् यज्ञॆ बर्हिष्या निषद्या दधिष्टेमं जठर इंदुमिंद्र ॥ (*tavāyaṃ somastvamehyarvāj śaśvattamaṃ sumanā asya pāhi | asmin yajñè barhiṣyā niṣadyā dadhiṣṭemaṃ jaṭhara iṃdumiṃdra ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-35-6)

6. Acchāvāka:
इंद्राय सोमाः प्रदिवो विदाना ऋभुर्येभिर्वषपर्वा विहायाः प्रयम्यमानान् प्रति षू गृथायेंद्र पिब वृषधूतस्य वृषः ॥ (*iṃdrāya somāḥ pradivo vidānā ṛbhuryebhirvaṣaparvā vihāyāḥ prayamyamānān prati ṣū gṛthāyeṃdra piba vṛṣadhūtasya vṛṣaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-36-2)

7. Āgnīdhra:
आपूर्णो अस्य कलशः स्वाहा सेक्तेव कोशं सिसिचे पिबध्यै । समु प्रिया आववृत्रन् मदाय प्रदक्षिणिदभि सोमास इंद्रं । (*āpūrṇo asya kalaśaḥ svāhā sekteva kośaṃ sisice pibadhyai | samu priyā āvavṛtran madāya pradakṣiṇidabhi somāsa iṃdraṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-36-15)

**The third savana**

All the mantras to be recited at this savana are in the Jagatī metre.

1. The Hotṛ:
इंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्भि: समुक्षितं सुतं सोममा वृषस्वा गभस्तोः । धियेषितो मघवन्माशुषो गृहे सौधन्वनेभिः सह मत्साव्नृभिः ॥ (*iṃdra ṛbhubhirvājavadbhi: samukṣitaṃ sutaṃ somamā vṛṣasvā gabhastoḥ | dhiyeṣito maghavanmāśuṣo gṛhe saudhanvanebhiḥ saha matsāvnṛbhiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-60-5)

### Printed p. 171
2. For the Maitrāvaruṇa priest: इंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं सोमं पिबतं मद्यं धृतव्रता । युवो रथो अध्वरं देवीतये प्रति स्वसरमुप याति तये ॥ (*iṃdrāvaruṇā sutapāvimaṃ sutaṃ somaṃ pibataṃ madyaṃ dhṛtavratā | yuvo ratho adhvaraṃ devītaye prati svasaramupa yāti taye ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-68-10)

3. For the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin: इंद्रश्च सोमं पिबतं बृहस्पतेऽस्मिन्यज्ञॆ मंदसाना वृषण्वसू । आ वां विशंत्विंदवः स्वाभुवोऽस्मे रयिं सर्ववीरं नि यच्चतं ॥ (*iṃdraśca somaṃ pibataṃ bṛhaspate 'sminyajñè maṃdasānā vṛṣaṇvasū | ā vāṃ viśaṃtviṃdavaḥ svābhuvo 'sme rayiṃ sarvavīraṃ ni yaccataṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-10-50)

4. For the Potṛ: आ वो वहंतु सप्तयो रघुष्यदो रघुपत्वानः प्रजिगात बाहुभिः । सीदता बर्हिरुरु वः सदस्यतं मादयध्वं मरुतो मध्यो अंधसः ॥ (*ā vo vahaṃtu saptayo raghuṣyado raghupatvānaḥ prajigāta bāhubhiḥ | sīdatā barhiruru vaḥ sadasyataṃ mādayadhvaṃ maruto madhyo aṃdhasaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-85-6)

5. For the Neṣṭṛ: अमेव नः सहवा आ हि गंतन नि बर्हिषि सदतना रणिष्टन । अथा मंदस्व जुजुषाणो अंधसस्त्वर्देवेर्भिर्जनिभिः सुमद्गणः ॥ (*ameva naḥ sahavā ā hi gaṃtana ni barhiṣi sadatanā raṇiṣṭana | athā maṃdasva jujuṣāṇo aṃdhasastvardeverbhirjanibhiḥ sumadgaṇaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-36-3)

6. For the Acchāvāka: इंद्राविष्णू पिबतं मध्यो अस्य सोमस्य दस्रा जठरं पृणेथां । आ वामंधांसि मदिराण्यग्मन्नुप ब्रह्माणि शृणुतं हवं मे ॥ (*iṃdrāviṣṇū pibataṃ madhyo asya somasya dasrā jaṭharaṃ pṛṇethāṃ | ā vāmaṃdhāṃsi madirāṇyagmannupa brahmāṇi śṛṇutaṃ havaṃ me ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-69-7)

7. For the Āgnīdhra: इमं स्तोममर्हते जातवेदसे रथमिव सं महेमा मनीषया । भद्रा हि नः प्रमतिरस्य संसद्यन्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ (*imaṃ stomamarhate jātavedase rathamiva saṃ mahemā manīṣayā | bhadrā hi naḥ pramatirasya saṃsadyanne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-44-1) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-94-1)

In this way, at every savana, each of these seven officiating priests recites one Ṛk apiece, seven Ṛks in all, and makes the offering. As said before, the offerings are made with mantras in the Gāyatrī metre at the morning savana, with mantras in the Triṣṭubh metre at the midday savana, and with mantras in the Jagatī metre at the third savana. This is the account of the mantras to be recited at the times of the savanas.

For the sūktas to be recited in the unnīyamāna rite connected with this subject, for the mantras to be recited by the respective priests at the morning savana, the midday savana and the third savana, and for further detailed explanations, see Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 15, pages 697-715, where they are set out according to the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.

> च । यत्ते राजञ्कृतं हविरिति द्वृचाः समानी व आकूतिरित्येका : आ. गृ- ३-५-७ ।

> हविषा नोऽस्मानभि रक्ष । अभिपालय तस्मात्त्वदभिरक्षितानस्मानरातीवारातिवाणि तु
> र्नोऽस्मान्मा तारीत् । मा वधीत् । किं च नोस्माकं किं चन किंचदपि धनादिकं
> शत्रुर्मो आनुमत् । मा हिंसीत् । यदेतदेत्यैः सूक्तैरुक्तं तद्यथास्माकं भवति

> करणीय इत्युक्तं भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The verse यत्ते राजन् (*yatte rājan*) is used in the concluding offering at the end of the maṇḍala, in the upākaraṇa and utsarjana rites. The sūtra says: यत्ते राजञ्कृतं हविरिति द्वृचाः समानी व आकूतिरित्येका (*yatte rājañkṛtaṃ haviriti dvṛcāḥ samānī va ākūtirityekā*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 3-5-7). Sāyaṇa explains: O king, i.e. lord of all, since you are the means of all rites; O Soma, whatever oblation is cooked for you, with that oblation protect us, guard us on every side. Therefore, protected by you, let the enemy not harm us, let no enemy destroy us; and let no enemy injure anything of ours, any wealth or the like. Just as what has been said in these sūktas may come to pass for us, so, O Indu, flow for Indra. Thus, in the sūktas ending with this one, beginning with स्वादिष्टयेत्यादिभि (*svādiṣṭayetyādibhi*), the greatness of Soma has been declared in many ways. Hence it is implied that the Soma sacrifice should be performed for the accomplishment of fruits in this world and the next.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजन् (*rājan*)—O lord of all
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- ते (*te*)—for you
- शृतं (*śṛtaṃ*)—cooked
- यत् हविः (*yat haviḥ*)—whatever oblation there is
- तेन (*tena*)—with that
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अभि रक्ष (*abhi rakṣa*)—protect fully
- अरातीना (*arātīnā*)—our enemies **NOTE**
- नः (*naḥ*)—us

### Printed p. 173
- मा तारीत् (*mā tārīt*)—let them not harm
- नः (*naḥ*)—our wealth also
- किं चन (*kiṃ cana*)—any enemy
- मो आममत् (*mo āmamat*)—let him not harm
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's drinking
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, lord of all, with whatever oblation has been cooked for you, protect us fully. Let our enemies not harm us. Let no enemy carry off our wealth. O Soma, flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Protect us, royal Soma, with the oblation which has been cooked for you; let no enemy assail us, or harm anything of ours; flow, Indu, for Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The use of this Ṛk यत्ते राजन् (*yatte rājan*) is for the concluding Ṛks of the maṇḍala, in the principal offering of the upākaraṇa and utsarjana rites; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra, यत्ते राजञ्चितं हविरिति द्वृचाः समानी व आकूतिरित्येका (*yatte rājañcitaṃ haviriti dvṛcāḥ samānī va ākūtirityekā*) (A. Gṛ. 3-5-7) **NOTE**.

इति सायणाचार्यविरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे दाशतय्या नवमे मंडले सप्तमोऽनुवाकः समाप्तं च नवमं मंडलं (*iti sāyaṇācāryaviracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe dāśatayyā navame maṃḍale saptamo 'nuvākaḥ samāptaṃ ca navamaṃ maṃḍalaṃ*)

Here the ninth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, with the Bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and with the Kannada translation, is concluded.

ओं तत्सत् (*oṃ tatsat*)

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ‖*)

शुभं भूयात् (*śubhaṃ bhūyāt*) हरिहर (*harihara*)

Supplementary mantras of the Ninth Maṇḍala. Mantras to be recited at the end of Sūkta 27—

Mantras to be recited at the end of the sūkta—

1. पावमानीः स्वस्त्ययनीः सुदुघा हि धृतश्चुतः । ऋषिभिः संभ्रतो रसो ब्राह्मणेष्टमृतं हितं ॥ (*pāvamānīḥ svastyayanīḥ sudughā hi dhṛtaścutaḥ | ṛṣibhiḥ saṃbhrato raso brāhmaṇeṣṭamṛtaṃ hitaṃ ‖*)
2. पावमानिर्दिशंतु न इमं लोकमथो अमुं । कामान्समर्थयंतु नो देवीर्देवैः समाहिताः ॥ (*pāvamānirdiśaṃtu na imaṃ lokamatho amuṃ | kāmānsamarthayaṃtu no devīrdevaiḥ samāhitāḥ ‖*)
3. येन देवाः पवित्रेणात्मानं पुनते सदा । तेन सहस्रधारेण पावमान्यः पुनंतु मां ॥ (*yena devāḥ pavitreṇātmānaṃ punate sadā | tena sahasradhāreṇa pāvamānyaḥ punaṃtu māṃ ‖*)
4. प्राजापत्यं पवित्रं शतोद्यामं हिरण्मयं । तेन ब्रह्मविदो वयं पूतं ब्रह्म पुनीमहे ॥ (*prājāpatyaṃ pavitraṃ śatodyāmaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ | tena brahmavido vayaṃ pūtaṃ brahma punīmahe ‖*)
5. इंद्रः पुनीति सह मा पुरातु सोमः स्वस्ता वरुणः समिच्या । यमो राजा प्रमृणाभिः पुनातु मा जातवेदा मूर्जयंत्या पुनातु ॥ (*iṃdraḥ punīti saha mā purātu somaḥ svastā varuṇaḥ samicyā | yamo rājā pramṛṇābhiḥ punātu mā jātavedā mūrjayaṃtyā punātu ‖*)
6. ऋषयस्तु तपस्तेपुः सर्वॆ स्वर्गजिगीषवः । तपंतस्तपसोग्रेण पावमानीर्यचोऽब्रुवन् ॥ (*ṛṣayastu tapastepuḥ sarvè svargajigīṣavaḥ | tapaṃtastapasogreṇa pāvamānīryaco 'bruvan ‖*)
7. यन्ने गर्भे वसतः पापमुग्रं यज्जायमानस्य च किंचिदन्यत् । जातस्य च यच्चापि च वर्धतो मे तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*yanne garbhe vasataḥ pāpamugraṃ yajjāyamānasya ca kiṃcidanyat | jātasya ca yaccāpi ca vardhato me tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*)
8. माता पित्रोर्यन्न कृतं वचो मे यत्सावरं जंगममाबभूव । विश्वस्य तत्प्रहृषितं वचो मे तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*mātā pitroryanna kṛtaṃ vaco me yatsāvaraṃ jaṃgamamābabhūva | viśvasya tatprahṛṣitaṃ vaco me tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*)
9. गोघ्नात्तस्वरत्वात् स्त्रीवधाद्यच्च किल्पिषं । पापकं च चरणेभ्यस्तापमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ ९ ॥ ब्रह्मवधात्सुरापानात्सर्णस्तेयाद्वृषलिगमनमैथुनसंगमात् । गुरोर्दाराधिगमनाच्च तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ १० ॥ बालघ्नान्मातृपितृवधाद्दूमितस्करात्सर्ववर्णगमनमैथुनसंगमात् । पापेभ्यश्च प्रतिग्रहात्सद्यः प्रहरति सर्वदुष्कृतं तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ! क्रयविक्रयाद्योनिदोषाद्दक्षाद्योज्यात्मतिग्रहात् असंभोजनाच्छापि नृशंसं तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि । १२ ॥ दुर्यष्टं दुरधीतं पापं यच्चाज्ञानतो कृतं । अयाजिताश्च संयाज्यास्तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ १३ ॥ अमंत्रमन्नं यत्किंचिद्दूयते च हुताशने । संवत्सरकृतं पापं तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*goghnāttasvaratvāt strīvadhādyacca kilpiṣaṃ | pāpakaṃ ca caraṇebhyastāpamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖ 9 ‖ brahmavadhātsurāpānātsarṇasteyādvṛṣaligamanamaithunasaṃgamāt | gurordārādhigamanācca tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖ 10 ‖ bālaghnānmātṛpitṛvadhāddūmitaskarātsarvavarṇagamanamaithunasaṃgamāt | pāpebhyaśca pratigrahātsadyaḥ praharati sarvaduṣkṛtaṃ tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ! krayavikrayādyonidoṣāddakṣādyojyātmatigrahāt asaṃbhojanācchāpi nṛśaṃsaṃ tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi | 12 ‖ duryaṣṭaṃ duradhītaṃ pāpaṃ yaccājñānato kṛtaṃ | ayājitāśca saṃyājyāstatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖ 13 ‖ amaṃtramannaṃ yatkiṃciddūyate ca hutāśane | saṃvatsarakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*)
10. ब्रह्मवधात्सुरापानात्सर्णस्तेयाद्वृषलिगमनमैथुनसंगमात् । गुरोर्दाराधिगमनाच्च तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*brahmavadhātsurāpānātsarṇasteyādvṛṣaligamanamaithunasaṃgamāt | gurordārādhigamanācca tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*)
11. बालघ्नान्मातृपितृवधाद्दूमितस्करात्सर्ववर्णगमनमैथुनसंगमात् । पापेभ्यश्च प्रतिग्रहात्सद्यः प्रहरति सर्वदुष्कृतं तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि (*bālaghnānmātṛpitṛvadhāddūmitaskarātsarvavarṇagamanamaithunasaṃgamāt | pāpebhyaśca pratigrahātsadyaḥ praharati sarvaduṣkṛtaṃ tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi*)
12. क्रयविक्रयाद्योनिदोषाद्दक्षाद्योज्यात्मतिग्रहात् असंभोजनाच्छापि नृशंसं तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि । (*krayavikrayādyonidoṣāddakṣādyojyātmatigrahāt asaṃbhojanācchāpi nṛśaṃsaṃ tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi |*)

13. दुर्यष्टं दुरधीतं पापं यच्चाज्ञानतो कृतं । अयाजिताश्च संयाज्यास्तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*duryaṣṭaṃ duradhītaṃ pāpaṃ yaccājñānato kṛtaṃ | ayājitāśca saṃyājyāstatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*)
14. अमंत्रमन्नं यत्किंचिद्दूयते च हुताशने । संवत्सरकृतं पापं तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*amaṃtramannaṃ yatkiṃciddūyate ca hutāśane | saṃvatsarakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*)
15. ऋतस्य योनयोऽमृतस्य धाम विश्वा देवेभ्यः पुण्यगंधाः । ता न आपः प्रवहंतु पापं शुद्धागच्छामि सुकृतामु लोकं तत्सावमानीभिरहं पुनामि । (*ṛtasya yonayo 'mṛtasya dhāma viśvā devebhyaḥ puṇyagaṃdhāḥ | tā na āpaḥ pravahaṃtu pāpaṃ śuddhāgacchāmi sukṛtāmu lokaṃ tatsāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi |*)
16. पावमानीः स्वस्त्ययनीयाभिर्गच्छति नांदनं । पुण्यांश्च भक्षान्भक्षयत्यमृतत्वं च गच्छति ॥ (*pāvamānīḥ svastyayanīyābhirgacchati nāṃdanaṃ | puṇyāṃśca bhakṣānbhakṣayatyamṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati ‖*)
17. पावमानीः पित्थान्देवानाध्यायेद्यश्च सरस्वतीं । पित्थांस्तस्योप वर्तेत क्षीरं सर्पिर्मधूदकं ॥ (*pāvamānīḥ pitthāndevānādhyāyedyaśca sarasvatīṃ | pitthāṃstasyopa varteta kṣīraṃ sarpirmadhūdakaṃ ‖*)
18. पावमानं परं ब्रह्म शुक्रं ज्योतिः सनातनं । ऋषींस्तस्योप तिष्ठेत क्षीरं सर्पिर्मधूदकं ॥ (*pāvamānaṃ paraṃ brahma śukraṃ jyotiḥ sanātanaṃ | ṛṣīṃstasyopa tiṣṭheta kṣīraṃ sarpirmadhūdakaṃ ‖*)
19. पावमानं परं ब्रह्म ये पठंति मनीषिणः । सप्त जन्म भवेद्विप्रो धनाढ्यो वेदपारगः ॥ (*pāvamānaṃ paraṃ brahma ye paṭhaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ | sapta janma bhavedvipro dhanāḍhyo vedapāragaḥ ‖*)
20. दशोत्तराण्यचांश्चैव पावमानीः शतानि षट् । एतज्जु ह्वन्जपेन्मंत्रं घोरमृत्युधयं हरेत् ॥ (*daśottarāṇyacāṃścaiva pāvamānīḥ śatāni ṣaṭ | etajju hvanjapenmaṃtraṃ ghoramṛtyudhayaṃ haret ‖*)
21. एतत्सुण्यं पापहरं रोगमृत्युभयापहं । पठतां शृण्वतां चैव ददाति परमां गतिं ॥ (*etatsuṇyaṃ pāpaharaṃ rogamṛtyubhayāpahaṃ | paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva dadāti paramāṃ gatiṃ ‖*)

Supplementary mantra to be recited at the end of the 5th Ṛk of the 3rd sūkta—

1. इळ्ळैव वामनु वस्तां धृतेन यस्याः पदे पुनते देवयंतः । धृतपदी शक्वरी सोमपृष्ठोप यज्ञमस्थित वैश्वदेवी ॥ (*iḷḷaiva vāmanu vastāṃ dhṛtena yasyāḥ pade punate devayaṃtaḥ | dhṛtapadī śakvarī somapṛṣṭhopa yajñamasthita vaiśvadevī ‖*)
2. वैश्वदेवी पुनती देव्यागाद्यस्यामिमा बह्वस्तन्वो वीतपृष्ठाः । तया मदंतः सधमादेषु वयं स्याम पतयो रयाणां ॥ (*vaiśvadevī punatī devyāgādyasyāmimā bahvastanvo vītapṛṣṭhāḥ | tayā madaṃtaḥ sadhamādeṣu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayāṇāṃ ‖*)

Supplementary mantras to be recited at the end of the ninth maṇḍala, that is, at the end of the 114th sūkta—

1. यत्र तत्सरमं पदं विष्णोर्लोके महीयते । देवैः सुकृतकर्मभिस्तत्र नाममृतं कृधींद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*yatra tatsaramaṃ padaṃ viṣṇorloke mahīyate | devaiḥ sukṛtakarmabhistatra nāmamṛtaṃ kṛdhīṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*)

### Printed p. 176
2. यत्र तत्परमाप्यं भूतानामधिपतिं । भावभावी च योगीश्च तत्र मामृतं कृधींद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*yatra tatparamāpyaṃ bhūtānāmadhipatiṃ | bhāvabhāvī ca yogīśca tatra māmṛtaṃ kṛdhīṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*)
3. यत्र लोकास्तनूत्यजः श्रद्धया तपसा जिताः । तेजश्च यत्र ब्रह्म च तत्र माममृतं कृधींद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*yatra lokāstanūtyajaḥ śraddhayā tapasā jitāḥ | tejaśca yatra brahma ca tatra māmamṛtaṃ kṛdhīṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*)
4. यत्र देवा महात्मानः सेंद्राश्च समरुद्धणाः । ब्रह्मा च यत्र विष्णुश्च तत्र माममृतं कृधींद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*yatra devā mahātmānaḥ seṃdrāśca samaruddhaṇāḥ | brahmā ca yatra viṣṇuśca tatra māmamṛtaṃ kṛdhīṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*)
5. यत्र गंगा च यमुना च यत्र प्राची सरस्वती । यत्र सोमेश्वरो देवस्तत्र माममृतं कृधींद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*yatra gaṃgā ca yamunā ca yatra prācī sarasvatī | yatra someśvaro devastatra māmamṛtaṃ kṛdhīṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*)
6. यत्र तद्विष्णुर्महीयते नराणामधिपतिं । यत्र शंखचक्रगदादरस्मरणं मुक्तिश्च तत्र माममृतं कृधींद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*yatra tadviṣṇurmahīyate narāṇāmadhipatiṃ | yatra śaṃkhacakragadādarasmaraṇaṃ muktiśca tatra māmamṛtaṃ kṛdhīṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*)

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)

Here the ninth book is concluded.

शुभं भूयात् (*śubhaṃ bhūyāt*) मंगळं (*maṃgaḷaṃ*) श्री (*śrī*) श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः (*śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ*)

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुकप्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्या स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmukaprame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyā syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*)

यस्य निश्यसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niśyasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*)

वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*)

Ṛgveda Saṃhitā with the Bhāṣya of Sāyaṇa. The Tenth Maṇḍala.

Introduction.

It has already been said that the Ṛgveda has ten maṇḍalas in all. The first maṇḍala and the last, the tenth, resemble each other in many respects. In both these maṇḍalas there are many different seers. Therefore, since the seers of the first maṇḍala are the seers of about a hundred or more Ṛks each, the seers of that maṇḍala are well known as śatarcins. In this tenth maṇḍala there are long sūktas at the beginning and after, and small sūktas at the end, so it is well known as the maṇḍala of great sūktas and small sūktas. In both maṇḍalas the number of sūktas is 191. In both, various deities are praised. In these and similar matters the two maṇḍalas resemble each other. But in this tenth maṇḍala, besides many sūktas useful for śrauta and smārta rites, there are also many sūktas that set forth profound philosophical reflection. Such sūktas

### Printed p. 178
In these hymns there are also many that discuss profound matters: how the universe, the world, came into being; what the state was before creation; the question of the self and the not-self; the question of the supreme Brahman; the question of heaven and hell. Besides this, many hymns of this same Maṇḍala, beginning with the Puruṣa-sūkta, which contain the principles of the Vedānta and have won the respect of the people, are found here. Hence the excellence and usefulness of this Maṇḍala are evident.

Because the objects of worship in some of the very small hymns of this Maṇḍala are seen here and there to be inanimate things, some Western scholars hold that the hymns of this Maṇḍala are not so ancient, and that the praise of inanimate things from the notion that they are deities, a custom come into use only lately, is the proof of this. This opinion is not sound, and it has no proper support. Since all the hymns of the Ṛgveda are arranged in a certain order, various subjects may be described in some of the last hymns. It is not reasonable to say on that ground alone that this Maṇḍala is not ancient.

## Maṇḍala 10

## Sūkta 1 (Maṇḍala 10)

**The first sūkta.**

**Introduction to the ṛṣi Trita Āptya**

The seer of the first seven sūktas of this tenth Maṇḍala is Trita Āptya. Although a few matters about this ṛṣi have been mentioned here and there earlier, it is now necessary to present his identity somewhat more fully.

The matter of Trita is a problem for critics. It is not possible to give a settled answer to the question whether this name is the name of the ṛṣi who saw a sūkta, or whether there is a deity called Trita. In some places the word Trita is used as an epithet of Indra and Agni. So if one is to learn as far as possible, from the Ṛksaṃhitā and other sources, what the nature of Trita is, the opinions of Vedic critics beginning with Yāska must first be noted.

The name Trita is used 40 times in all, in 29 sūktas. But there is no separate sūkta relating to Trita (that is, addressed to a deity called Trita). The name is also not mentioned in the Nighaṇṭu among the groups of deities. Only Yāska has given an explanation (nirvacana) of this word, in two places. First, while explaining the 8th ṛk of the 105th sūkta of the first Maṇḍala (Ni. 4-6): त्रितं कूपेऽवहितमेतत्तूक्तं प्रतिबभौ।तत्र ब्रह्मतिहासमिश्रमृज्मुश्रं गाथा मिश्रं भवति । त्रितस्तीर्णतमो मेधया बभूव अपि वा संख्यानामैवाभिप्रेतं स्यादेकतो द्वितस्त्रि त इति त्रयो बभोवुः । (*tritaṃ kūpe 'vahitametattūktaṃ pratibabhau|tatra brahmatihāsamiśramṛjmuśraṃ gāthā miśraṃ bhavati | tritastīrṇatamo medhayā babhūva api vā saṃkhyānāmaivābhipretaṃ syādekato dvitastri ta iti trayo babhovuḥ |*) "This sūkta shone forth to Trita, who had fallen into a well. It is mixed with Brāhmaṇa-history, mixed with ṛks, mixed with gāthās. Trita crossed over (tīrṇatama) by intelligence"; the sūkta was seen by Trita who had fallen into the well. It is a prayer with a story, partly in ṛks and partly in gāthās (वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी (*vittaṃ me asya rodasī*)). He got the name Trita from his proficiency in intelligence. Or else, among the three Ekata, Dvita and Trita, being the third he may have got the name Trita. So he explained it the first time; the second time, while explaining ṛk 1-187-1, he explained Trita as an epithet of Indra, "Indra who pervades the three regions" (Ni. 9-25).

**NOTE**

In the Ṛksaṃhitā this word is said to be used sixteen times together with Indra, once as the slayer of Vṛtra, once as Viyadaśva, in four places as an epithet of the Maruts, in seven places with Agni, in one place with Varuṇa, four times with Soma, and six times as a person hidden in a distant place.

### Printed p. 189

In these places Sāyaṇa's explanation follows Yāska's nirvacana. He has explained the word Trita, in 20 ṛks, as the name of the mantra-seeing ṛṣi, a proper name, and in the other places, according to the context, as an epithet indicating the nature of the deities Vāyu, Varuṇa, Indra and Agni.

The story of Trita, the third among the three ṛṣis Ekata, Dvita and Trita, is told in the special topics under the first ṛk of sūkta 1-105. In the 9th ṛk of the same sūkta Trita has the epithet Āptya. He also indicates that he has a relation with Agni. How did he get the epithet Āptya? How is his relation with Agni? To explain this there is a story in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa.

चतुर्धाविहितो ह वाग्रेऽग्निरास । स यमग्रेऽग्निं होत्राय प्रावृणत स प्राधन्वद्यं द्वितीयं प्रावृणत स प्रैवाधन्वद्यं तृतीयं प्रावृण तस प्रैधन्वदथ योऽयमेतर्ह्यग्निः सभीषा निलिल्ये सोऽपः प्रविवेश तं देवा अनुविद्य सहस्यॆनाद्भ्य आनिन्युः सोऽपोऽभितिष्ठेवानवष्टूता स्थ या अप्रपदनं स्थ याभ्यो वो मामकामं नयंतीति तत आप्त्याः संबभूवुस्त्रितो द्वित एकतः । (*caturdhāvihito ha vāgre 'gnirāsa | sa yamagre 'gniṃ hotrāya prāvṛṇata sa prādhanvadyaṃ dvitīyaṃ prāvṛṇata sa praivādhanvadyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ prāvṛṇa tasa praidhanvadatha yo 'yametarhyagniḥ sabhīṣā nililye so 'paḥ praviveśa taṃ devā anuvidya sahasyènādbhya āninyuḥ so 'po 'bhitiṣṭhevānavaṣṭūtā stha yā aprapadanaṃ stha yābhyo vo māmakāmaṃ nayaṃtīti tata āptyāḥ saṃbabhūvustrito dvita ekataḥ |*) (Śa. Brā. 1-2-3 1)

**NOTE**

Agni's three elder brothers became tired and emaciated in the work of carrying the oblation to the gods. Agni, fearing that the same state might come to him, ran away and hid in the water. Then the gods entered the water too and caught him and brought him; and Agni, in anger, spat on the water, saying that this water is an unfit substance for giving protection. Then three Āptya deities arose, called Ekata, Dvita and Trita. This is one reason for the epithet Āptya.

Second, to show that Trita and the others were produced from Agni, Sāyaṇa has given the nirvacana of the word Trita on the basis of a Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa passage (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-52-5, Sā. Bhā.): देवानां हविर्लेपनिघर्षणाय अग्नेःसकाशात् अप्सु एकतो द्वितस्त्रित इति त्रयः पुरुषा जज्जिरे । (*devānāṃ havirlepanigharṣaṇāya agneḥsakāśāt apsu ekato dvitastrita iti trayaḥ puruṣā jajjire |*) "For the rubbing off of the oblation smeared on the vessels of the gods, three persons, Ekata, Dvita and Trita, were born in the waters from Agni." And so it is recorded by the Taittirīyas: सोंगारेणापः अभ्यपातयत् । तत एकतोजायत । स द्वितीयमभ्यपातयत् । ततो द्वितोऽजायत । स तृतीयमभ्यपातयत् । ततस्त्रितोऽजायत । (*soṃgāreṇāpaḥ abhyapātayat | tata ekatojāyata | sa dvitīyamabhyapātayat | tato dvito 'jāyata | sa tṛtīyamabhyapātayat | tatastrito 'jāyata |*) (Tai. Brā. 3.-2.-8-10)

### Printed p. 190
The purport of this Brāhmaṇa passage is that, to wipe out the fault of the gods, Agni caused three persons, Ekata, Dvita and Trita, to come into being in the water. For this very reason, Trita is so called.

In the Ṛk अग्निं मन्ये पितरमग्निमापिमग्निं भ्रातरं सदमित्सखायं । (*agniṃ manye pitaramagnimāpimagniṃ bhrātaraṃ sadamitsakhāyaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-7-3) and similar Ṛks, Trita calls Agni his father, brother and friend. He says that he worships such an Agni, and he praises Agni as one who helps the venerable Sūrya, dweller of the heavenly world, to shine more brightly.

Since there is thus a text of Trita himself showing a direct relation between Trita and Agni, the opinions of scholars who assert his identity with other deities such as Indra and Vāyu may be said not to state Trita's true nature. On many grounds one must say that Trita is a portion of the lightning-fire (vaidyutāgni). Before stating definitively, with proper reasons, that the lightning-fire is itself called by the alternative name Trita, it would not be improper to cite here some views on Trita from among the English scholars who have pursued Vedic study with great interest and in a scientific manner and have expressed their opinions on such matters. Among them the scholar Benfey says: "Trita is a mythical personage, to whom, as to Indra and other deities, is ascribed the destruction of the demons withholding the fertilising rain from the earth. In some passages, special mention is made of the fact, that Trita owes his strength for this deed to the sacred Soma draught, and in one passage, Indra is described as drinking Soma with him." Bergaigne says: "In his warlike exploits he always preserves his part as a sacrificer. Trita, who was certainly a God, has none the less become a priest, favourite of Indra." The scholar Pischel says: "Trita was from the beginning a God of the sea and of the waters." The scholar Roth asserts the identity of Trita and Vāyu, and the scholar Ludwig has approved the same view. Muir has stated his view that Trita is another name of Indra.

Just as the Western scholars each hold a different opinion, the followers of the Vedic tradition too have shown differences of view, as stated earlier. But there are no sound grounds for positing Trita's identity with any deities other than Agni. Although Trita's name is mentioned with Indra

### Printed p. 191
sixteen times, in the Ṛks 2-11-20; 8-7-24; 8-52-1; 9-32-2; 9-38-2 and others, he is described everywhere as Indra's helper, as "the sage Trita, Indra's friend", that is, as a separate person who accompanies Indra. Hence Trita is not a synonym of Indra.

Likewise, in the Ṛk इमं त्रितो भूर्व्यविंददिच्छन्वैभूवसो मूर्धन्यघ्न्यायाः । (*imaṃ trito bhūrvyaviṃdadicchanvaibhūvaso mūrdhanyaghnyāyāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-46-3), what is said of a "house-friend" applies to Agni; Vāyu is not famed as a house-friend. Similarly the Ṛk 10-46-6 **NOTE** is also a praise addressed to Agni. Thus on many grounds one can say freely that Trita is not another name of other deities but a portion of Agni. Since the word Āptya is described in the Ṛks 8-47-13 to 17 as one who is distant and who moves within the clouds, he can also be said to be a form of the lightning-fire. If so, the association between deities such as Indra and the Maruts and the lightning-fire in the form of Trita becomes intelligible.

From the standpoint of the derivation of the form as well, it is possible to assert the identity of Trita and Agni, who exists in three forms.

अग्ने त्री ते वाजिना त्री षधस्था तिस्रस्ते जिह्वा ऋतजात पूर्विः । तिस्र उ ते तन्नो देवनातास्ताभिर्नः पाहि गिरो अप्रयुच्छन् ॥ (*agne trī te vājinā trī ṣadhasthā tisraste jihvā ṛtajāta pūrviḥ | tisra u te tanno devanātāstābhirnaḥ pāhi giro aprayucchan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-20-2).

Just as this Ṛk describes Agni as having three powers, three stations, three tongues and three bodies, three radiances (3-26-7) and three flamings (3-2-9) are also described. Moreover: त्रिरस्य ता परमा संति सत्या स्वाहर्हा देवस्य जनिमान्यग्नेः । (*trirasya tā paramā saṃti satyā svāharhā devasya janimānyagneḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-1-7): the places of origin of the divine Agni are also three. Which are they? As described in Ṛks such as स जायत प्रथम: पस्त्यासु महो बुद्धे रजसो अस्य योन्सौ । (*sa jāyata prathama: pastyāsu maho buddhe rajaso asya yonsau |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-1-11), they are the earth, the heavenly world and the atmosphere. In the same way the common property of the lightning-fire, situated in the atmosphere, and of Trita, who is far away and within the clouds, becomes clear. Trita himself has stated this point plainly:

अविमा यः सप्त रश्मयस्तत्र मे नाभिरातता । त्रितस्तद्वेदाप्तः स जामित्वाय रेभति वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥ (*avimā yaḥ sapta raśmayastatra me nābhirātatā | tritastadvedāptaḥ sa jāmitvāya rebhati vittaṃ me asya rodasī ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-9).

### Printed p. 192
"In these seven sun-rays, which are in the form of the seven vital breaths, my navel has grown out widely. Trita, who has crossed ignorance, the son of the waters, knows his former history. The sage who has this knowledge praises these rays, his kin, in order to come out of the well." From this, and also from यदीमह त्रितो दिव्युप ध्मातेव धमति शिशीते ध्मातरी यथा। (*yadīmaha trito divyupa dhmāteva dhamati śiśīte dhmātarī yathā|*) (5-9-5) ("Trita, dweller of the atmosphere, makes this Agni blaze") and प्र सक्षणो दिव्यः कण्वहोता त्रितो दिवः सजोषा वातो अग्निः । (*pra sakṣaṇo divyaḥ kaṇvahotā trito divaḥ sajoṣā vāto agniḥ |*) (5-14-4) ("Trita, dweller of the atmosphere, comes with Sūrya and the others") and similar passages, it can be said that the lightning-fire is known by the alternative name Trita.

Wherever such an epithet as Āptya (Āpta, "son of the waters", 1-105-9) occurs, it refers to Trita. Likewise the epithet "Apāṃ napāt" always refers to the lightning-fire. Therefore it can be said that Trita and the lightning-fire are originally one.

Sūkta 105 of the first Maṇḍala was seen by Trita when he had fallen into the well. In this sūkta the Viśvedevas are prayed to. There is a story behind this prayer. But the sequence of the story in the introduction of Sāyaṇa's commentary on this sūkta is one thing, and the sequence in Skandasvāmin's commentary is another. According to Sāyaṇa's commentary (which follows the Śākaṭāyana version):

एकतो द्वितस्त्रित इति पुरा त्रय ऋषयो बभूवुः । ते कदाचिन्मरुभूमावरण्ये वर्तमानाः पिजासया संतप्तगात्राः संत एकं कूपमहिंदन् । तत्र त्रिताख्य एको जलपानाय कूपं प्राविशत् । स्वयं पीत्वा इतरयोश्च कूपादुदकमुद्धृत्य प्रादात् । ता तदुदकं पीत्वा त्रितु कूपे पातयित्वा तदीयं धनं सर्वमपहृत्य कूपं च रथचक्रेण सिधाय प्रास्थिषातां । ततः कूपे पतितः स त्रितः कूपादुत्तरीतुमशक्कुवन् सर्वॆ देवा मामुद्धरंत्त्विति मनसा सस्मार । ततस्तेषां स्तावकमिदं सूक्तं ददर्श ' तत्र रात्रौ कूपस्यांतश्चंद्रमसो रश्मीन् पश्यन् परिदेवयते । (*ekato dvitastrita iti purā traya ṛṣayo babhūvuḥ | te kadācinmarubhūmāvaraṇye vartamānāḥ pijāsayā saṃtaptagātrāḥ saṃta ekaṃ kūpamahiṃdan | tatra tritākhya eko jalapānāya kūpaṃ prāviśat | svayaṃ pītvā itarayośca kūpādudakamuddhṛtya prādāt | tā tadudakaṃ pītvā tritu kūpe pātayitvā tadīyaṃ dhanaṃ sarvamapahṛtya kūpaṃ ca rathacakreṇa sidhāya prāsthiṣātāṃ | tataḥ kūpe patitaḥ sa tritaḥ kūpāduttarītumaśakkuvan sarvè devā māmuddharaṃttviti manasā sasmāra | tatasteṣāṃ stāvakamidaṃ sūktaṃ dadarśa ' tatra rātrau kūpasyāṃtaścaṃdramaso raśmīn paśyan paridevayate |*).

There were three sages, Ekata, Dvita and Trita. Once, caught in a desert in the middle of a forest and tormented by extreme thirst, they suddenly saw a well and came near it. Then Trita went down into the well to drink water. After drinking himself, he drew water from the well for the other two as well and came up. Ekata and Dvita, who were above, drank that water, and, wishing to seize all of Trita's wealth, pushed him into the well, covered the well with a chariot wheel and went away from there. Trita, fallen in the well, unable to come up, remembered in his mind, standing right there, the Viśvedevas, thinking "may they raise me up". Then he obtained the vision of this sūkta praising them. In that forest, seeing the moon's rays that had spread into the well, he lamented, expressing his anguish and praying. Such is the story of Sāyaṇa's commentary.

### Printed p. 193
In Skandasvāmin's commentary the sequence of the story is as follows:

अत्र सूक्ते इतिहासमाचक्षते । आप्त्यस्य ऋषेः त्रयः पुत्रा बभूवुः एकतो द्वितस्तित इति । ते यष्टुकामाः स्वान् याज्यान् गा ययाचिरे । ता आदाय सरस्वत्यास्तिरेण पथा गच्छतः तान् परस्मिन् कूले निषण्णो रात्रौ वृको ददर्श। दृष्ट्वा चोत्थाय अभिमुखः सारस्वतीरप उत्तरन् तांस्त्रासयामास । तेषां पश्यतां त्रितो निर्जले पांसुभिः वीरुद्भिः तृणैश्चावृते महत्यंधकूपे पपात । एकतद्वित्त्वा तु सह गोभिः गृहं जग्मतुः । अथ कूपस्थस्य इयं चिंता बभूव । अकृतसोमयागस्य मृत्युर्न श्रेयसे । तत् कः उपायः स्यात् येनाहमिहस्थः सोमं पिबेयमिति । चिंतयन्नेव यदृच्छया तत्र लंबमानां वीरुधं ददर्श । तां सोम इति संकल्प्य योगैश्वर्यात् मनसा शिष्टानि अग्न्यादीनि साधनानि परिसंकल्प्य शर्करा ग्राव्णः कृत्वा ताभिस्तां वीरुधमभिष्टुत्य यागार्थं देवान् आजुहाव । ता आह्वानकारणमनवबुध्यमाना आविग्ना बुभूवुः । अथ तदाह्वानं बृहस्पतिः शुश्राव । स देवानुवाच । त्रितस्य वर्तते यज्ञस्तत्र गच्छाम इति । अथ तत्र सर्वे देवा जग्मुः । तानागतान् कूपादुत्तारणार्थी त्रितः क्रमेण तुष्टाव चंद्रमा इत्यादिनेति । (*atra sūkte itihāsamācakṣate | āptyasya ṛṣeḥ trayaḥ putrā babhūvuḥ ekato dvitastita iti | te yaṣṭukāmāḥ svān yājyān gā yayācire | tā ādāya sarasvatyāstireṇa pathā gacchataḥ tān parasmin kūle niṣaṇṇo rātrau vṛko dadarśa| dṛṣṭvā cotthāya abhimukhaḥ sārasvatīrapa uttaran tāṃstrāsayāmāsa | teṣāṃ paśyatāṃ trito nirjale pāṃsubhiḥ vīrudbhiḥ tṛṇaiścāvṛte mahatyaṃdhakūpe papāta | ekatadvittvā tu saha gobhiḥ gṛhaṃ jagmatuḥ | atha kūpasthasya iyaṃ ciṃtā babhūva | akṛtasomayāgasya mṛtyurna śreyase | tat kaḥ upāyaḥ syāt yenāhamihasthaḥ somaṃ pibeyamiti | ciṃtayanneva yadṛcchayā tatra laṃbamānāṃ vīrudhaṃ dadarśa | tāṃ soma iti saṃkalpya yogaiśvaryāt manasā śiṣṭāni agnyādīni sādhanāni parisaṃkalpya śarkarā grāvṇaḥ kṛtvā tābhistāṃ vīrudhamabhiṣṭutya yāgārthaṃ devān ājuhāva | tā āhvānakāraṇamanavabudhyamānā āvignā bubhūvuḥ | atha tadāhvānaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ śuśrāva | sa devānuvāca | tritasya vartate yajñastatra gacchāma iti | atha tatra sarve devā jagmuḥ | tānāgatān kūpāduttāraṇārthī tritaḥ krameṇa tuṣṭāva caṃdramā ityādineti |*).

The sage Āpta had three sons, Ekata, Dvita and Trita. Desiring to perform a sacrifice, they begged sacrificial animals and were coming with them along the bank of the river Sarasvatī, when a wolf on the opposite bank saw them. At once it rose, crossed the river water, came and menaced them. When all were alarmed with fear for their lives, Trita fell into a great unfathomable well covered with dust, creepers and reeds. Ekata and Dvita somehow escaped and went home driving the cattle. Then Trita, fallen in the well covered with pitch darkness, began to think: "For a man who dies without having performed a Soma sacrifice there is no welfare. By what means could I perform a sacrifice and drink Soma juice?" While he was thinking thus, by chance he saw a creeper hanging there. Resolving that it was the Soma plant, by his inner yogic power he prepared the inner fire and the other requisites, pressed that creeper and called the gods for the sacrifice. Not understanding the reason for the invitation, they began to be troubled. Then Bṛhaspati heard that invitation and said to the gods, "Trita's sacrifice is going on. Let us all go there."

### Printed p. 194
Then all went there. Then Trita, wishing to come up out of the well, began to praise one by one the gods who had come there. Such is the sequence of the story in Skandasvāmin's commentary.

This story is told in the Bṛhaddevatā also. There too it is said that Trita fell into the well through fear of the wolf, and that afterwards he praised the gods.

त्रितं गास्त्वनुगच्छंतं क्रूराः सालावृकीसुताः । कूपे प्रक्षिप्य गाः सर्वास्तत एवापजह्रिरे ॥ स तत्र सुषुवे सोमं मंत्रविन्मंत्रवित्तमः । देवांश्चावाहयत्सर्वांस्तच्चुश्राव बृहस्पतिः ॥ आगच्छतोऽथ तान्दृष्ट्वा क्व वसत्यस्य तत्त्वतः । सर्वदृक्त्वं च वरुणस्यार्यम्म श्चित्युपालभत् ॥ कूपेष्टकाभिर्वणितान्यंगाव्येवाभवन्मम! दृष्ट्वा सर्वानहं सौमि यद्यष्टेको न पश्यति ॥ बृहस्पतिप्रचोदिता विश्वे देवगणास्त्रयः । जग्मुस्तितस्य तं यज्ञं भागांश्च जगृहुः सह ॥ बृहस्पतिस्तितस्यैतद् ज्ञानं विज्ञानमेव च । तृचेनांत्येन सूक्तस्य जगादर्षिरसाविति ॥ (*tritaṃ gāstvanugacchaṃtaṃ krūrāḥ sālāvṛkīsutāḥ | kūpe prakṣipya gāḥ sarvāstata evāpajahrire ‖ sa tatra suṣuve somaṃ maṃtravinmaṃtravittamaḥ | devāṃścāvāhayatsarvāṃstaccuśrāva bṛhaspatiḥ ‖ āgacchato 'tha tāndṛṣṭvā kva vasatyasya tattvataḥ | sarvadṛktvaṃ ca varuṇasyāryamma ścityupālabhat ‖ kūpeṣṭakābhirvaṇitānyaṃgāvyevābhavanmama! dṛṣṭvā sarvānahaṃ saumi yadyaṣṭeko na paśyati ‖ bṛhaspatipracoditā viśve devagaṇāstrayaḥ | jagmustitasya taṃ yajñaṃ bhāgāṃśca jagṛhuḥ saha ‖ bṛhaspatistitasyaitad jñānaṃ vijñānameva ca | tṛcenāṃtyena sūktasya jagādarṣirasāviti ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-132 to 137).

The cruel cubs of the she-wolf pushed Trita into the well and went away from there, seizing his cattle. Then Trita, the best of the knowers of mantras, pressed Soma juice and called the gods. Bṛhaspati heard this invitation and came together with all the gods. As soon as they arrived, with a kind of discontent he expressed it with the anguish: "Where has gone this omniscience (the power of seeing everything) of Varuṇa and Aryaman? All my limbs have been wounded by the bricks of this well. Although I look on all of them and praise them, not one of them sees me." Then all the gods, urged by Bṛhaspati, went to that sacrifice and received their respective shares of the offering. Afterwards Bṛhaspati praised Trita's knowledge and special knowledge. This is the story told in the Bṛhaddevatā.

"I am that Trita who formerly, whenever Soma juice was pressed for sacrifice, recited hymns pleasing to you": thus Trita reminds the gods that he formerly worshipped them and gave them joy

### Printed p. 195
. From many authorities it is known that Trita is very famous in pressing Soma juice and in reciting mantras in the form of praise.

स तत्र सुषुवे सोमं मंत्रविन्मंत्रपित्तमः (*sa tatra suṣuve somaṃ maṃtravinmaṃtrapittamaḥ*) (Bṛ. De. 3-133).

In the Bṛhaddevatā his greatness is described: Trita, the foremost of the knowers of mantras, pressed Soma juice and made himself ready for the sacrifice. Because he showed this worthiness full of greatness, Bṛhaspati, at the time of his lament:

बृहस्पतिस्त्रि तस्यैतद् ज्ञानं विज्ञानमेव च । तृचेनांत्येन सूक्तस्य जगादर्षिरसाविति । (*bṛhaspatistri tasyaitad jñānaṃ vijñānameva ca | tṛcenāṃtyena sūktasya jagādarṣirasāviti |*) (Bṛ. De. 2-137).**NOTE**

Immediately understanding his praise, filled with the power of knowledge and special knowledge, he told the other sages too about that sage's mental sacrifice, full of greatness and accompanied by praise; so it is said. In Skandasvāmin's commentary also the greatness of his yogic power is told. That Trita, of such excellent worthiness, in earlier times pressed Soma juice, performed sacrifice, and at that time recited excellent hymns, is described in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself. For example—

आदीं त्रितस्य योषणो हरिं हिस्वंत्यद्रिभिः । ( (*ādīṃ tritasya yoṣaṇo hariṃ hisvaṃtyadribhiḥ | (*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-32-2)

भुवनस्तस्य मर्ज्यो भुवदिंद्राय मत्सरः (*bhuvanastasya marjyo bhuvadiṃdrāya matsaraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-34-4)

In these and similar Ṛks it is said that the Soma juice pressed by Trita gave joy to Indra and increased his power; and in

स त्रितस्याधि सानवि पवमानो अरोचयत् (*sa tritasyādhi sānavi pavamāno arocayat*) जामिभिः सूर‍्यं सह (*jāmibhiḥ sūryaṃ saha*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-37-4)

and similar Ṛks, that the pure Somas pressed at the time of Trita's sacrifice made Sūrya shine exceedingly; and in

अस्य सुवानस्य मुंदिनस्त्रितस्य न्यर्बुदं वावृधानो आस्तः । आवर्तयत्सूर्यो न चक्रं भिनद्वलमिंद्रो अंगिरस्वान् ॥ (*asya suvānasya muṃdinastritasya nyarbudaṃ vāvṛdhāno āstaḥ | āvartayatsūryo na cakraṃ bhinadvalamiṃdro aṃgirasvān ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-20)

### Printed p. 196

…
अनु श्रितस्य युध्यतः शुष्मावन्नुत क्रतुं । अन्विंद्रं वृत्रतूरै ॥ (*anu śritasya yudhyataḥ śuṣmāvannuta kratuṃ | anviṃdraṃ vṛtratūrai ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-24)

In these and similar ṛks it is described at length that Indra, delighted by Trita's praise and by the Soma-juice offered by him, gained exceeding power and became able to destroy the Asuras. It is also said that the Maruts and Indra, too, became able to slay Vṛtra and others only with the help of Trita's strength. Thus Trita now reminds the gods of how he formerly satisfied them and helped them in many ways, and prays that they should help him now that he has fallen into distress.

The Nirukta-writers have commented as follows on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-8.

संतपंति मामभितः सपत्न्य इवेमाः पर्शवः कूपपर्शवो मूषिका इवास्नातानि सूत्राणि व्यदंति । स्वांगाभिधानं ना स्याच्छिश्नानि व्यदंतीति वा संतपंति माध्यःकामाः ' स्तोतारं ते शतक्रतो', ' वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ' जानीतं मेऽस्य द्यावापृथिव्याविति । त्रितं कूपेऽवहितमेत्सूक्तं प्रतिबभौ । तत्र ब्रह्मेतिहासमिश्रमृज्ङ्मिश्रं गाथामिश्रं भवति । त्रितस्तीर्णतमो मेधया बभूव अपि वा संख्यानामैवाभिप्रेतं स्यादेकतो द्वितिस्त्रित इति त्रयो बभूवुः । (*saṃtapaṃti māmabhitaḥ sapatnya ivemāḥ parśavaḥ kūpaparśavo mūṣikā ivāsnātāni sūtrāṇi vyadaṃti | svāṃgābhidhānaṃ nā syācchiśnāni vyadaṃtīti vā saṃtapaṃti mādhyaḥkāmāḥ ' stotāraṃ te śatakrato ', ' vittaṃ me asya rodasī ' jānītaṃ me 'sya dyāvāpṛthivyāviti | tritaṃ kūpe 'vahitametsūktaṃ pratibabhau | tatra brahmetihāsamiśramṛjṅmiśraṃ gāthāmiśraṃ bhavati | tritastīrṇatamo medhayā babhūva api vā saṃkhyānāmaivābhipretaṃ syādekato dvitistrita iti trayo babhūvuḥ |*) (Ni. 4-6).

"Like co-wives surrounding and pressing their husband, and like mice gnawing a thread soaked in oil, the bricks of the walls of this well surround me on every side and torment me. Or, as for the word 'śiśna': just as mice gnaw even their own limb, the śiśna, so my mental afflictions bite and eat me. O Indra, Śatakratu, such mental pains torment me, your praiser. O Heaven and Earth, know this suffering of mine." Having thus explained this ṛk, they then state further particulars. This sūkta was seen by Trita, who had fallen into the well. In connection with it there is a story mixed with verses (gāthā) and ṛks. Trita was the most excellent of the wise, one who had crossed over the darkness by his intelligence. Or else it may be a numeral, indicating the last of the three who were born in succession, Ekata, Dvita and Trita. So the Nirukta-writers explain. These ṛks indicate this very meaning:

सं मा तपंत्यभितः सपत्नीरिव पर्शवः । नि बाधते अमतिर्नग्नता जसुर्वेर्न वेवीयते मतिः ॥ मूषो न शिश्ना व्यदंति माध्यः स्तोतारं ते शतक्रतो । सकृत्सु नो मघवन्निंद्र मृळयाधा पितेव नो भव ॥ (*saṃ mā tapaṃtyabhitaḥ sapatnīriva parśavaḥ | ni bādhate amatirnagnatā jasurverna vevīyate matiḥ ‖ mūṣo na śiśnā vyadaṃti mādhyaḥ stotāraṃ te śatakrato | sakṛtsu no maghavanniṃdra mṛḷayādhā piteva no bhava ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-33-2-3)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the tenth maṇḍala there are twelve anuvākas; in the first anuvāka sixteen sūktas. Of these, the one beginning अग्रे बृहन् (*agre bṛhan*), of seven ṛks, is the first. Its seer is Trita Āptya. By the rule of "no specification" the metre is Triṣṭubh; by the rule for the beginning of a maṇḍala the deity is Agni. So the Anukramaṇī says: अग्रे सप्त त्रित इति (*agre sapta trita iti*).

Use: in the Prātaranuvāka-śastra, in the Āgneya kratu, for the Triṣṭubh metre, the first eight sūktas beginning with this one are employed, leaving out the last three ṛks of the eighth. For it is prescribed in the sūtra अग्ने नयाग्रे बृहन्नित्यष्टानामुत्तमवादुत्तमास्तिस्र उद्दरेदिति त्रैष्टुभं । (*agne nayāgre bṛhannityaṣṭānāmuttamavāduttamāstisra uddarediti traiṣṭubhaṃ |*) (Ā. 4-13); and प्रातरनुवाकन्यायेन तस्यॆव समाम्नायस्य सहस्रावममोदेतोः शंसेत् । (*prātaranuvākanyāyena tasyèva samāmnāyasya sahasrāvamamodetoḥ śaṃset |*) (Ā. 6-5). Further, when the Āhavanīya fire has been brought forward for the homa and, before the homa, has become quiet, there is an iṣṭi addressed to Agni with the quality *jyotiṣmat* (luminous). In it the first ṛk is the yājyā. It is stated in the sūtra इष्टिरग्निर्ज्योतिष्मान्वरुण उदग्ने शुचयस्तवाग्ने बृहन्नुषसामूर्ध्वो अस्थात् (*iṣṭiragnirjyotiṣmānvaruṇa udagne śucayastavāgne bṛhannuṣasāmūrdhvo asthāt*) (Ā. 3-12). This ṛk is also used in the principal homa at the beginning of a maṇḍala in the Upākaraṇa and Utsarjana rites; the sūtra has been cited.

##### Anuvāda

In the tenth maṇḍala there are twelve anuvākas. In the first anuvāka there are sixteen sūktas. Of them this sūkta beginning "अग्रे बृहन् (*agre bṛhan*)" is the first. It has seven ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Trita Āptya; the deity is Agni; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said "अग्रे सप्त त्रितः (*agre sapta tritaḥ*)". At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, the first eight sūktas of this maṇḍala, except the last three ṛks of the eighth sūkta, are used for the Triṣṭubh-metre mantras of Agni connected with the kratu; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra "agne nayāgre bṛhann ityaṣṭānām uttamād uttamās tisra uddhared iti traiṣṭubham" (Ā. 4-13). And on this matter there is also the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra "prātaranuvākanyāyena tasyaiva samāmnāyasya sahasrāvamamodetoḥ śaṃset" (Ā. 6-5). When the Āhavanīya fire has been brought and established for the homa, after the first homa an iṣṭi should be performed addressed to the deity called Agni Jyotiṣmat. In that iṣṭi the first ṛk of this sūkta is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra "iṣṭir agnir jyotiṣmān varuṇa udagne śucayas tavāgne bṛhann uṣasām ūrdhvo asmāt" (Ā. 3-12). **NOTE** And it has been stated earlier, by the citing of the sūtra, that in the principal homas of the Upākaraṇa and Utsarjana rites this first ṛk of the sūkta is used for the maṇḍala-beginning ṛks.

> हैष बृहन्नुषसामूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठति । निर्जगन्वानमसो ज्योतिषागादिति निर्जगन्वा-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This great (बृहन् (*bṛhan*) = महान् (*mahān*)) Agni stands upright, blazing in the form of flame, at the head of the dawns, that is, above the dawns, at the time of dawn. From स्तमसः (*stamasaḥ*), a name for night, he has gone out: निर्जगन्वान् (*nirjaganvān*) is "gone forth", the form from the root गम (*gama*) with kvasu and without the augment iṭ. That Agni, marked by his own light (ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)), comes: being carried from the Gārhapatya he arrives at the Āhavanīya. Then, स्वंगः (*svaṃgaḥ*) with fair flame-limbs, जातः (*jātaḥ*) born for the rite, this Agni with रुशता (*ruśatā*) (from the root रोच (*roca*) in the sense of burning; "shining"), or else, रुशति (*ruśati*) in the sense of harming, "destroying the darkness", with भानुना (*bhānunā*) (brilliance) fills (*āprāḥ*, from प्रा (*prā*) "to fill") विश्वा सद्मानि (*viśvā sadmāni*), all the worlds, or else the sacrificial houses. The Vājasaneyaka (Śatapatha) is cited here.

### Printed p. 199

> नात्रेस्तमसो ज्योतिष्यति । अग्निर्भानुना रुशता स्वंग इत्यग्निर्वा एष भानुना
> रुशता स्टंग आ जातो विश्वा सद्मान्यप्रा इतीमे वै लोका विश्वा सद्मानि तानेष
> जात आपूरयति । शत ६-७-३-१८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Brāhmaṇa explains the ṛk phrase by phrase: in the beginning this Agni stands upright, great, above the dawns; having gone forth from the darkness of night he shines forth; "Agni with bright light, fair-limbed": it is Agni indeed with bright light, fair-limbed; "born he fills all dwellings": these worlds are all the dwellings, and he, born, fills them. (Śa. 6-7-3-18) **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहन् (*bṛhan*)—the great Agni
- उषसां अग्रे (*uṣasāṃ agre*)—at the very time of the appearance of the dawns
- ऊर्ध्वः अस्थात् (*ūrdhvaḥ asthāt*)—stands risen up, blazing
- तमसः (*tamasaḥ*)—from the dark night
- निर्जगन्वान् (*nirjaganvān*)—having come out
- ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)—together with his own radiance
- आगात् (*āgāt*)—has come out
- स्वंगः (*svaṃgaḥ*)—he who has excellent limbs
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—he who is born for the sacrifice
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- रुशता (*ruśatā*)—with shining
- भानुना (*bhānunā*)—with brilliance
- विश्वा सद्मानि (*viśvā sadmāni*)—all the sacrificial houses
- अप्राः (*aprāḥ*)—fills

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The great Agni stands risen up, blazing, at the very time of the appearance of the dawns. Having gone out from the dark night, he has come out together with his radiance. Agni, who has excellent limbs and is born for the sacrifice, fills with his shining brilliance all the worlds, or the sacrificial houses.

##### English translation
The great fire at the beginning of the dawn has sprung aloft, and issuing forth from the darkness has come with radiance. Agni, the bright-bodied, as soon as born, fills all dwellings with shining light.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

बृहन् उषसां अग्रे ऊर्ध्वः अस्थात् (*bṛhan uṣasāṃ agre ūrdhvaḥ asthāt*)—Two meanings can be given for the word bṛhat. One: he who rises up with a huge form, joined with many flames, and shines. The other: बृहन् (*bṛhan*) means महान् (*mahān*), the great one, the worshipful, one distinguished by many qualities, one to be honoured on every side. उषसां अग्रे (*uṣasāṃ agre*) is उषसामुपर्युषःकाले (*uṣasāmuparyuṣaḥkāle*): immediately as the time of dawn manifests. The time of dawn is the time when the pitch darkness of night has ended and it is light before the sun rises. The beginning of this time is when the darkness is just going and a little light has come. The meaning is that at such a time Agni, risen up with his flames upward, that is, burning large, is shining. Because the sacrifice is begun in the early morning, and because Agni, the chief means of the sacrifice, is produced from the aranis in the early morning and made to blaze, the seer here describes Agni as shining at the beginning of the dawn.

### Printed p. 200

तमसः निर्जगन्वान् ज्योतिषा आ अगात् (*tamasaḥ nirjaganvān jyotiṣā ā agāt*)—With the manifestation of dawn the darkness too has gone. Therefore Agni, gone out from the darkness, growing bright with his own light, is carried by the priests from the Gārhapatya fire-pit to the Āhavanīya fire. That is what is described here: Agni, gone out from the darkness and shining with his own light, has come to the Āhavanīya fire.

स्वंगः अग्निः जातः रुशता भानुना विश्वा सद्मानि आ अप्राः (*svaṃgaḥ agniḥ jātaḥ ruśatā bhānunā viśvā sadmāni ā aprāḥ*)—Here स्वंगः (*svaṃgaḥ*) means शोभनज्वालावयवः (*śobhanajvālāvayavaḥ*): one who has excellent limbs. The flames of Agni are his limbs. Therefore Agni, whose limbs are excellent flames, is जातः (*jātaḥ*), born for the sacrifice, produced by being churned in the aranis by the priests. Such an Agni fills all the worlds, or all the sacrificial houses, with his light. By Agni's light the whole world shines well, and in it especially the sacrificial house, the place where Agni is, shines with Agni's great brilliance; thus the seer describes Agni's power of illumining.

The Bhāṣyakāra has cited a passage of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa that makes the meaning of this ṛk clear:

अग्रे बृहन्नुषसामूर्ध्वो अस्थादित्यग्रे हैष बृहन्नुषसामूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठति । निर्जगन्वास्तमसो ज्योतिरागादिति निर्जगन्वान् रात्रेस्तमसो ज्योतिष्यति। अग्निर्भानुना रुशता स्वंग इत्यग्निर्वा एष भानुना रुशता स्वंग आ जातो विश्वा सद्मान्यप्रा इतीमे वै लोका विश्वा सद्मानि तानेष जात आपूरयति ॥ (*agre bṛhannuṣasāmūrdhvo asthādityagre haiṣa bṛhannuṣasāmūrdhvastiṣṭhati | nirjaganvāstamaso jyotirāgāditi nirjaganvān rātrestamaso jyotiṣyati| agnirbhānunā ruśatā svaṃga ityagnirvā eṣa bhānunā ruśatā svaṃga ā jāto viśvā sadmānyaprā itīme vai lokā viśvā sadmāni tāneṣa jāta āpūrayati ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 6-7-3-10)

Since the explanation of the meaning of this Vedic passage accords with the meaning we have explained above, there is no need to explain it again.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने जात उत्पन्नश्चारुः कल्याणरूप ओषधीष्टोषधिविकारेष्वरणेषु
> विभृतो विशेषेण मथित आहवनीयाद्यात्मना विविधं ह्रियमाण ओषधीषु वर्तमानः
> स त्वं रोदस्योर्दावापृथिव्योर्गर्भोऽसि । गर्भो भवसि । अग्निरूप आदित्यरूपश्चेति । किं च चित्रश्चित्रवर्णः काली कराली च मनोजवेत्यादिसप्तजिह्वाभिर्नानारूपः
> यद्वा चित्रश्चायनीयः शिशुरोषधीनां शिशुरग्निस्तमांस्कक्कूनात्रिवत्कृष्णाञ्चत्रूंश्च परि भवसि । स्वतेजसाभिभवसि । स त्वं मातृभ्यो मातृभूताभ्य ओषधीभ्यः ।
> अधिः पंचम्यर्थद्योतकः । ताभ्यः कनिक्रदत्पुनःपुनः शब्दं कुर्वन्न, गाः । प्रगच्छसि ।
> प्रजायसे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, being born, beautiful in form, ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*), that is, in the aranis, which are modifications of plants, specially churned, or else variously carried as Āhavanīya and the rest while remaining in the plants: such as you are, you are the embryo of Heaven and Earth (रोदस्योः (*rodasyoḥ*)), in the form of fire and in the form of the sun. Further, you are चित्रः (*citraḥ*), of variegated colour, of manifold forms with the seven tongues beginning काली कराली च मनोजवेत्यादि (*kālī karālī ca manojavetyādi*); or else चित्रः (*citraḥ*) means "to be gathered (worshipped)". As the child of the plants, you overcome (परि भवसि (*pari bhavasi*)) the darkness and the black foes with your own splendour. **NOTE** Such as you are, you go forth (प्र गाः (*pra gāḥ*)), that is, are born, from the mothers, namely the plants as mothers, repeatedly making a sound; अधि (*adhi*) shows the sense of the ablative.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—when you are born
- चारुः (*cāruḥ*)—attractive
- ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*)—in the aranis, which are modifications of plants
- विभृतः (*vibhṛtaḥ*)—you are borne
- सः (*saḥ*)—such a you
- रोदस्योः (*rodasyoḥ*)—for Heaven and Earth
- गर्भः असि (*garbhaḥ asi*)—you are of the form of an embryo
- चित्रः (*citraḥ*)—having many kinds of colour
- शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*)—you who are of the form of a son to creepers and the like
- अक्तून् (*aktūn*)—the foes who are of the form of darkness
- तमांसि (*tamāṃsi*)—the pitch darkness of night
- परि (भवसि) (*pari (bhavasi)*)—you destroy
- मातृभ्यः अधि (*mātṛbhyaḥ adhi*)—from the plants, which are of the form of mothers
- कनिक्रदत् (*kanikradat*)—making a sound
- प्र गाः (*pra gāḥ*)—you come forth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, when you are born you are attractive and are borne in the aranis, which are modifications of plants. Such as you are, you are of the form of an embryo to Heaven and Earth. You, who have many kinds of colour and are of the form of a son to creepers and the like, destroy the foes who are of the form of darkness and the pitch darkness of night; you come forth making a sound from the plants that are of the form of mothers.

##### English translation
When born, you, O Agni, are the embryo of heaven and earth, beautiful, borne about in the plants; variegated, infantine, you disperse the nocturnal glooms ; you issue roaring loudly from the maternal (sources).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ओषधीषु ओषधिविकारेष्वर्णेषु विशेषेण मथितः । यद्वा आहवनीयाद्यात्मना विविधं ह्रियमाण ओषधीषु वर्तमानः । (*oṣadhīṣu oṣadhivikāreṣvarṇeṣu viśeṣeṇa mathitaḥ | yadvā āhavanīyādyātmanā vividhaṃ hriyamāṇa oṣadhīṣu vartamānaḥ |*). Oṣadhis here means the aranis made from large grown trees and the like. In these aranis, in a special manner, that is, in the manner prescribed by the rule (विध्युक्तरीति (*vidhyuktarīti*)

### Printed p. 202

churned in the prescribed manner, Agni is born. Or, established by the priests in the Āhavanīya and other fire-pits and fed by the herbs, that is, by wood and the like, he blazes up. Both meanings can be given.

गर्भः असि रोदस्योः (*garbhaḥ asi rodasyoḥ*)—O Agni, you are established as an embryo in heaven and earth. That is, on earth you shine in the form of terrestrial fire or sacrificial fire, and in heaven in the form of the sun. This is the intention.

चित्रः शिशुः (*citraḥ śiśuḥ*)—Of variegated colour, having many forms through the seven tongues चित्रवर्णः काली कराळी च मनोजवा इत्यादि सप्तजिह्वाभिः नानारूपः । (*citravarṇaḥ kālī karāḷī ca manojavā ityādi saptajihvābhiḥ nānārūpaḥ |*). Or चित्रश्चायनीयः ओषधीनां शिशुरग्निः (*citraścāyanīyaḥ oṣadhīnāṃ śiśuragniḥ*). That Agni has seven tongues is well known:

काली कराली च मनोजना च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा । स्पुलिंगिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः ॥ (*kālī karālī ca manojanā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā | spuliṃginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ ‖*) (Muṃ. U. 1-2-4) **NOTE**

So it is said in the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad. Agni is the one of variegated colour who shines with the seven tongues or flames, Kālī, Karālī, Manojavā, Sulohitā, Sudhūmravarṇā, Sphuliṅginī and Viśvaruchī. Or, because he is born in plants and the like (trees, forest trees), Agni may also be called the child of the herbs. Thus two kinds of meaning are explained.

तमांसि अक्तून् (*tamāṃsi aktūn*)—Black like night, and enemies too. Agni destroys the darkness; or he destroys the enemies, the Dasyus and others, who are black like night.

प्र मातृभ्यः अधि कनिक्रदत् गाः (*pra mātṛbhyaḥ adhi kanikradat gāḥ*)—Here मातृभ्यः (*mātṛbhyaḥ*) means from the herbs that are mothers to him, that is, from the pieces of wood. The intention is that as you burn them you blaze up, making a crackling sound.

> विष्णुः । इत्था । परमं । अस्य । विद्वान् । जातः । बृहन् । अभि । पाति । तृतीयं ।  
> आसा । यत् । अस्य । पयः । अक्रत । स्वं । सचेतसः । अभि । अर्चंति । अत्र ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विद्वाञ्ज्ञानानो जातः प्रादुर्भूतो बृहन्महान् विष्णुरिद्धेत्थमनेन प्रकारेण विष्णुर्व्यापनशीलो ज्ञानादिगुणयुक्तोऽग्निरस्य मे तृतीयं त्रयाणां
> पूरकं त्रितं मामभि पाति । अभिरक्षतु । इति त्रयो बभूवुः ।
> नि. ४.६ । इति यास्केनोक्तं । किंचास्याग्नेः स्वमात्मीयं पय उदकमासास्येन
> यद्यदाक्रत कुर्वंति यजमाना याचंते तदानीमतास्मिल्लोके स्थिताः स्तोतारः
> सचेतसः समानमनस्का भूत्वे नमभ्यर्चंति । अभिष्टु वंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viṣṇu is the knowing one, born, manifested, great. *itthaṃ*: in this manner. Viṣṇu is the pervading one, Agni endowed with knowledge and other qualities. Let him protect me, the third, that is, the completer of the three, Trita. Yāska has said, "so the three came to be" (Ni. 4.6). Further, when the sacrificers ask with the mouth for this Agni's own water, then the worshippers standing in this world, being of one mind, praise him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—the all-knowing one
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—born for the sacrifice
- बृहन् (*bṛhan*)—of great form
- इत्था परनुं (*itthā paranuṃ*)—thus, in a special way
- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—Agni, the pervader
- अस्य तृतीयं (*asya tṛtīyaṃ*)—me, who am called Trita
- अभि पाति (*abhi pāti*)—let him protect
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Agni's
- स्वं (*svaṃ*)—own
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—water
- आसा (*āsā*)—with the mouth (asking)
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अक्रत (*akrata*)—they ask; then
- अत्र (*atra*)—the worshippers of this world
- सचेतसः (*sacetasaḥ*)—being of one mind
- अभ्यर्चंति (*abhyarcaṃti*)—praise Agni

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Agni, the all-knowing, born for the sacrifice and pervading in a special way, protect me, who am called Trita. When the sacrificers open their mouths and ask for this Agni's own water, all the worshippers of this world praise Agni with one mind.

##### English translation
May he, who as soon as manifested is vast and wise, and thus (universally) pervading, defend (me), his third (manifestation); and when (the worshippers) ask with their mouths for his own water, animated by one purpose, they praise him in this world.

### Printed p. 204

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तृतीयं अभि पाति (*tṛtīyaṃ abhi pāti*)—तृतीयं त्रयाणां पूरकं मां अभिरक्षतु (*tṛtīyaṃ trayāṇāṃ pūrakaṃ māṃ abhirakṣatu*). It was said earlier that Ekata, Dvita and Trita are three brothers, that Trita is the last of them, and that he is the seer of this sūkta. Therefore the prayer is made here that Agni protect me, the third (the last) among the brothers.

आसा यत् अस्य पयः अक्रत स्वं (*āsā yat asya payaḥ akrata svaṃ*)—The intention is that the priests who chant praises beg this Agni for rain-water with their mouths, that is, with the hymns and the like that they recite with their mouths.

सचेतसः अभ्यर्चंति (*sacetasaḥ abhyarcaṃti*)—समानमनस्का भूत्त्वैनं अधिष्टुवंति (*samānamanaskā bhūttvainaṃ adhiṣṭuvaṃti*). These priests, being of one mind, that is, with one and the same desire that rain-water should come to them, praise Agni.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आत॑ उ त्वा सितु॒भृतो॒ जनि॑त्रीरन्ना॒वृधं॒ प्रति॑ चरं॒त्यन्नैः॑ ।  
> ता ईं॒ प्रत्ये॑षि॒ पुन॑र॒न्यरू॑पा॒ असि॒ त्वं वि॒क्षु मानु॑षीषु॒  ॑
> होता ॥ ४ ॥

> आतः । ऊं इति ; त्वा । पितुभृतः । जनित्रीः । अन्नवृधं । प्रति । चरंति । अन्नैः ।  
> ताः । ईं । प्रति । एषि । पुनः ! अन्यरूपाः । असि । त्वं । विक्षु । मानुषीषु  
> होता ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने अतः । उ इत्यवधारणे । अस्मादेव कारणात् पितुभृतः पितुनान्नेन
> सर्वस्य जतो धारयित्र्यः पोषयित्र्यो वा जनित्रीर्जनयित्र्य ओषधयोऽन्नावृधमन्नस्य वर्धकं त्वा त्वामन्नॆर्हेतुभिः प्रति चरंति । परिचरंति । अभिगच्छंति । ततस्तमीमेनास्ता ओषधीः प्रत्येषि । प्रतिगच्छसि । पुनरप्यन्यरूपा जीर्णा ओषधीर्दावभूतस्त्वं गच्छसि । किंच मानुषीषु मनुष्यजातिषु विक्षु प्रजासु । यद्वा । विश्वग्नि-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, अतः (*ataḥ*); उ (*u*) is in the sense of emphasis. For this very reason the herbs, which are पितुभृतः (*pitubhṛtaḥ*), that is, supporters or nourishers of all with food (पितु (*pitu*) being food), and जनित्रीः (*janitrīḥ*), producers, attend you who increase food, *annairhetubhiḥ*, by way of foods. Then you go back to those same herbs. Again you go, having other forms, as the fire that consumes the withered herbs. Further, among the human clans, the विक्षु (*vikṣu*) (peoples); or else among the human races that engage in actions such as Agnihotra, as

### Printed p. 205

> होत्रादिक्रियास्वभिनिविशंतीषु मानुषीषु मनुष्यजातिषु । होता देवानामाह्वाता होमनिष्पादको वासि । भवसि । मनुष्येषु स्थित इत्यर्थे ब्राह्मणं देवो
> ह्येष मर्त्येष्टिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

...you are the Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods, or the accomplisher of the oblation. The meaning is that he abides among men. For this the Brāhmaṇa is cited: देवो ह्येष मर्त्येष्टिति (*devo hyeṣa martyeṣṭiti*). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अतः (*ataḥ*)—therefore (O Agni)
- पितुभृतः (*pitubhṛtaḥ*)—those that nourish the whole world with food
- जनित्रीः (*janitrīḥ*)—and are the producers of fire, the herbs
- अन्नावृधं (*annāvṛdhaṃ*)—the increaser of food
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अन्नैः (*annaiḥ*)—for the sake of food
- प्रति चरंति (*prati caraṃti*)—serve
- अन्यरूपाः (*anyarūpāḥ*)—having taken other forms
- ईं ताः (*īṃ tāḥ*)—those same herbs
- प्रत्येषि (*pratyeṣi*)—you go again and join
- मानुषीषु (*mānuṣīṣu*)—among the human
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—peoples
- होता असि (*hotā asi*)—you are of the form of the Hotṛ

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the herbs, which nourish the whole world with food and are the producers of fire, serve you, the increaser of food, for the sake of food. You go again and join those same herbs after they have taken other forms. Among the peoples belonging to men you are of the form of the Hotṛ.

##### English translation
Therefore the genetrices (of all things, the herbs), the cherishers (of all) with food, wait on you who are the augmenter of food, with (sactificial) viands; you visit them again, when they have assumed other forms, you are amongst human beings the invoker (of the gods).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अन्यरूपाः (*anyarūpāḥ*)—There are two kinds of herbs. The growing forest trees serve Agni for the sake of food; that is, they attend upon Agni to obtain rain-water, which is of the nature of food for them. This is one meaning. The second meaning is that you, Agni, burn the dried wood and the like among the herbs and grow strong. Thus two kinds of meaning are suggested here.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> होता॑रं चि॒त्रर॑थमध्व॒रस्य॑ य॒ज्ञस्य॑यज्ञस्य के॒तुं रुशं॑तं ।  
> प्रत्य॑र्धि० दे॒वस्य॑देवस्य म॒हा श्रि॒या त्व१॒॑ग्निमति॑थिं॒ जना॑नां ॥
