#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भवा॑ नो अग्नेऽवि॒तोत गो॒पा भवा॑ वय॒स्कृदु॒त नो॑  ॒
> वयोधाः ।  
> रास्वा॑ च नः सुमहो ह॒व्यदा॑तिं॒ त्रास्वो॒त न॑स्त॒न्वो॒३॒॑ ३ अप्र॑युच्छन् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भव । नः । अग्ने । अविता । उत । गोपाः । भव । वयःकृत् । उत । नः । वयःधाः।  
> रास्व । च । नः । सुमहः । हव्यदातिं । त्रास्व । उत । नःतन्न्वः । अप्रयुच्छन् ॥ ७॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं नोऽस्माकमविता दृष्टभयेभ्यो रक्षको भव । भूयाः ।
> उतापि च गोपा अदृष्टभयेभ्यो गोप्ता रक्षको भव । उतापि च वयस्कदन्नस्य
> कर्ता भव । वयोधा अन्नस्य दाता भव हे सुमह: सुष्टु पूजनीयाग्ने त्वं
> स्वभूतां हव्यदातिं हविषो दातिं नोऽस्मभ्यं रास्व च । प्रयच्छ । उतापि च
> नोऽस्माकं स्वभूतास्तन्वः शरीराण्यप्रयुच्छन्न प्रमाद्यंस्रास्व । पालय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, be our protector (अविता (*avitā*)) from visible dangers. Also be our गोपाः (*gopāḥ*), our guardian from invisible dangers. Also be the maker of food (*vayaskṛt*) and the giver of food (वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)). O सुमहः (*sumahaḥ*), Agni who are well worthy of worship, grant (रास्व (*rāsva*)) to us your own हव्यदातिं (*havyadātiṃ*), the giving of the oblation. And protect (त्रास्व (*trāsva*)), watch over, our own bodies (तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*)), not being negligent (अप्रयुच्छन् (*aprayucchan*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अविता (*avitā*)—as protector
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- उत (*uta*)—and
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—be our guardian
- उत (*uta*)—and
- वयस्कत् (*vayaskat*)—be the producer of food for us **NOTE**
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)—be the giver of food
- सुमहः (*sumahaḥ*)—O Agni, worthy of excellent worship
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- हव्यदातिं (*havyadātiṃ*)—fitness for giving oblations
- रास्व (*rāsva*)—give
- उत (*uta*)—and
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*)—bodies
- अप्रयुच्छन् (*aprayucchan*)—carefully
- त्रास्व (*trāsva*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, be our protector. Remove all our calamities and protect us; produce food for us and give it. O Agni, worthy of excellent worship, give us fitness for giving oblations. Carefully protect our bodies.

### Printed p. 299

##### English translation
Be our protector, Agni, (in obvious peril) : be our presever (in un, seen danger), be the provider and giver of sustenance ; bestow upon us- mighty Agni, the donation of oblations, and ever attentive, protect our persons.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, which serves as the conclusion of the sūkta, Agni is prayed to grant protection and food and the like, to create in us the fitness to offer oblations and so forth to the gods, and to protect us at all times. Here the commentator explains two kinds of protection: protection from enemies and wild beasts that can be seen is one kind; protection from invisible things such as disease, and from sins, is the other.

## Sūkta 8 (Maṇḍala 10)
Introduction.
The seer of this sūkta and of the one after it is Triśirā, son of Tvaṣṭṛ. This Triśirā was formerly the family priest of the gods. He had a connection with the Asuras; that is, he was born of an Asura woman. Therefore he also had a fondness for the Asuras. Fearing that this partisan of the Asuras might somehow harm the gods, Indra wished to kill him. In this matter Trita (the seer Trita Āptya) became his helper. In some places it is said that Indra killed him for the sake of this Trita, that is, to please Trita.

In the Ṛk
अस्मभ्यं तत्वाष्टं विश्वरूपमरंधयः साख्यस्य त्रिताय ॥ (*asmabhyaṃ tatvāṣṭaṃ viśvarūpamaraṃdhayaḥ sākhyasya tritāya ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-19)
it is said that Indra killed Viśvarūpa out of friendship for Trita. In the Bṛhaddevatā (sixth chapter) this is said about him:
प्र केतुनेति त्वाष्ट्रस्तु त्रिशिराः सूक्तमुत्तरं ॥ १४७ ॥ (*pra ketuneti tvāṣṭrastu triśirāḥ sūktamuttaraṃ ‖ 147 ‖*)
ऋचस्त्वस्य षळाग्नेय्यं तृचस्त्वस्येति यः परः । (*ṛcastvasya ṣaḷāgneyyaṃ tṛcastvasyeti yaḥ paraḥ |*)
तेनेंद्रमभितुष्टाव स्वप्नांत इति नः श्रुतिः ॥ १४८ ॥ (*teneṃdramabhituṣṭāva svapnāṃta iti naḥ śrutiḥ ‖ 148 ‖*)

### Printed p. 300

The seer of this sūkta beginning प्रकेतुना (*praketunā*) is Triśirā, son of Tvaṣṭṛ. In the first six Ṛks of this sūkta this seer praises Agni, and in the next three, Indra.
अभवत्स हि देवानां पुरोधाः प्रियकाम्यया । (*abhavatsa hi devānāṃ purodhāḥ priyakāmyayā |*)
असुराणां स्वसुः पुत्रस्त्रिशिरा विश्वरूपधृक् ॥ १४९ ॥ (*asurāṇāṃ svasuḥ putrastriśirā viśvarūpadhṛk ‖ 149 ‖*)
तमृषिं प्रहितं त्विंद्रो देवेषु बुबुधेऽसुरैः । (*tamṛṣiṃ prahitaṃ tviṃdro deveṣu bubudhe 'suraiḥ |*)
सोऽस्य वज्रेण तान्याशु शिरांसि त्रीण्यथाच्छिदत् ॥ १५० ॥ (*so 'sya vajreṇa tānyāśu śirāṃsi trīṇyathācchidat ‖ 150 ‖*)
This seer Triśirā was formerly the family priest of the gods. Since he was the son of the Asuras' sister, he remained a partisan of the Asuras. The gods came to know of this and suspected that the Asuras themselves, for their own advantage, to learn the secrets of the gods, had installed him, under the name Viśvarūpa, as family priest among the gods, to act as a spy. Therefore Indra took his thunderbolt and cut off the three heads of this Triśiras.
तस्य यत्सोमपानं तु मुखं सोऽभूत्कपिंजलः । (*tasya yatsomapānaṃ tu mukhaṃ so 'bhūtkapiṃjalaḥ |*)
कलविंकः सुरापाणं अन्नादं तित्तिरिस्त्वभूत् ॥ १५१ ॥ (*kalaviṃkaḥ surāpāṇaṃ annādaṃ tittiristvabhūt ‖ 151 ‖*)
Of the three heads of that Triśiras, the mouth that drank Soma became the bird called kapiñjala. The mouth that drank surā became the bird called kalaviṅka. The mouth that ate food became the bird called tittiri.
तं वागभ्यवदद्ब्रह्मी ब्रह्महासि शतक्रतो । (*taṃ vāgabhyavadadbrahmī brahmahāsi śatakrato |*)
प्रपन्नं हतवान्यस्माद्विश्वरूपं पराङ्मुखं ॥ १५२ ॥ (*prapannaṃ hatavānyasmādviśvarūpaṃ parāṅmukhaṃ ‖ 152 ‖*)
At that time a bodiless voice was heard. Addressing Indra it said: "O Indra, you have gone behind Viśvarūpa, who was पराङ्मुखं (*parāṅmukhaṃ*), that is, not facing you but turned in another direction, and have killed him. Since he was a Brāhmaṇa, the guilt of brahmin-slaying has come upon you."
तमभ्यसिंचत्तूक्तेन ऋषिराप इति स्वयं । (*tamabhyasiṃcattūktena ṛṣirāpa iti svayaṃ |*)
सिंधुद्वीप्रोपनुत्त्यर्थं तस्याश्लीलस्य पाप्मन्य ॥ १५३ ॥ (*siṃdhudvīpropanuttyarthaṃ tasyāślīlasya pāpmanya ‖ 153 ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. chapter 6)
To remove this sin, Indra besought Sindhudvīpa, the seer of the next sūkta, and that seer, by reciting the sūkta of nine Ṛks beginning आपोहिष्ठा (*āpohiṣṭhā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-9th sūkta), water **NOTE**

### Printed p. 301

…took water, consecrated it with mantras and bathed Indra with it. By that Indra's sin was removed, as has been said. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā this matter is told somewhat differently; we shall explain that too further on.

In this sūkta the seer praises Indra, saying that he slew the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, Viśvarūpa, for the sake of the royal sage Trita. Who this Trita is, what his story is, and many other matters concerning him, we have already explained at length earlier, that is, in this same volume at p. 187, and in Vol. 8 at pp. 443 and 473, and elsewhere. Although the word Trita occurs in many Ṛks, nothing more about him can be learnt from them. Or rather, even in the Veda the word Trita is used in five or six places, but nothing is learnt there either. Only his association with Indra is found in many places. As said everywhere, all that is known is that Trita is a deity dwelling very far away, and that sin or bad dreams are sent to him. (Ath. Saṃ. 1-131-1, 3; 19-55-4) **NOTE** In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā he is said to be the giver of long life (Tai. Saṃ. 1-8-10-2). He is the preparer of the Soma juice that confers immortality. Trita is one of three brothers, Ekata, Dvita and Trita. All three are sons of Agni; that Trita arose from water is said in Brāhmaṇas such as Śa. Brā. 1-2-3-1, 2 and Tai. Brā. 3-2-8-10, 11.

As said in the Ṛgveda, in three or four contexts Indra and Trita have done the same deed (the slaying of a demon). Once Indra is the instigator of Trita; in another place it is said that Indra himself is encouraged by Trita. Twice Indra has worked for Trita. As said in the present sūkta, Indra slew for Trita one called Viśvarūpa. Trita seeks Agni; he kindles Agni in heaven; he dwells in the houses of men in place of Agni; his dwelling is hidden far away; Soma is there too. Indra drinks Soma, but Trita prepares Soma. This is the difference between Indra and Trita.

From the points stated above, Trita may be called a lightning deity, that is, the atmospheric form of Agni; like the deities Agni, Vāyu, Indra and Sūrya, he is a deity of the middle region. But since all this deity's deeds are done by Indra, he is a subordinate deity in the Ṛgveda. It may be that the connection of Trita with Soma is stated because, in the form of lightning, he brought Soma from heaven to the earth. Since the evidence is slight, each scholar has formed a different opinion about him.

### Printed p. 302

To mention only a few: the scholar Roth (Roth) says he is a deity of water and wind; Hillbratnd (Hillbratnd) a deity of the kindled sky; Perry (Perry) a deity of the storm. Another scholar, Pischel (Pischel), says that he was first a deity of the sea and water, then a physician among men, and afterwards attained godhood. Hardy (Hardy) says he is a moon deity. In the present sūkta, since Trita has the relation of friendship with Indra, it is said that for his sake Indra killed the son of Tvaṣṭṛ called Viśvarūpa.

The slaying of Viśvarūpa by Indra is told at the beginning of the fifth prapāṭhaka of the second kāṇḍa of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. In the Ṛgveda too, on this matter, in the Ṛk

> भूरीदिंद्र उदिनक्षंतमोजोऽवाभिनत्सत्पतिर्मन्यमानं ।
> त्वाष्टस्य चिद्विश्वरूपस्य गोनामाचक्राणस्त्रीणि शीर्षा परा वर्क् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-8-9)

it is said that Indra cut off the three heads of Viśvarūpa, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ. That Indra did this deed for Trita, and that Trita helped Indra in it, is said in the 7th Ṛk of the same sūkta—

> अस्य त्रितः क्रतुना वव्रे अंतरिच्छन् धीतिं पितुरेवैः परस्य ।
> सचस्यमानः पित्रोरुपस्थे जामि ब्रुवाण आयुधानि वेति ।
> स पित्राण्यायुधानि विद्वानिंद्रॆषित आप्त्यो अभ्ययुध्यत् ।
> त्रिशीर्षाणं सप्तरश्मिं जघन्वान् त्वाष्टस्य चिन्निः सस्यजे त्रितो गाः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-8-7, 8)

In the bhāṣya on these Ṛks Sāyaṇa has also told a narrative: Indra asked Trita's help in killing Viśvarūpa, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, who had three heads. To increase his own strength Trita asked as a boon that he be given a share of the offering in sacrifices. Indra agreed, and gave him water for washing the hands and a share in the sacrifice. Then Trita, equipped with the weapons that belonged to his father and impelled by Indra, fought with Viśvarūpa, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, struck him hard with his weapons and made him faint. Afterwards Indra cut off the three heads of that Viśvarūpa. This is what is said in the Ṛks above.

### Printed p. 303

This same matter is told at length in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-1-1); it is explained here with its meaning—

> विश्वरूपो वै त्वाष्ट्रः पुरोहितो देवनामासीत् स्वस्रियॊसुराणां तस
> त्रीणि शीर्षाण्यासन्तोमपानग्ं सुरापानमन्नादनग्ं स प्रत्यक्षं देवेभ्यो भागमवदत् परोक्षमसुरेभ्यः ॥

In former times Viśvarūpa, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, was the family priest of the gods. Since he was the son of the asuras' younger sister, he also had a fondness for the asuras. This Viśvarūpa had three heads (śiras). With one of the three heads he drank Soma, with another he drank surā (liquor), with the third he ate food and the like. Meanwhile this Viśvarūpa told everyone openly that he would obtain for the gods their share of the offering in the sacrifice. But inwardly, unknown to anyone, he was helping the asuras.

> सर्वस्मै वै प्रत्यक्षं भागं वदंति यस्मा एव परोक्षं वदंति तस्य भाग उदितस्तस्मादिंद्रोऽबिभेदीदृज्ञै राष्ट्रं विपर्यावर्तयतीति तस्य वज्रमादाय शीर्षाण्यच्छिनत् ॥

People promise a share to everyone openly, in front of all. But those who fulfil the promise so given are very rare. If they promise secretly (in private) that they will give the share, in a way that inspires trust, they surely keep that word. Therefore Indra, seeing Viśvarūpa's secret dealing, was afraid; fearing that he would betray him and bring the kingdom under the control of others (the asuras), he took his vajra weapon and cut off all three heads of that Viśvarūpa.

> यत्सोमपानमासीत्स कपिंजलोऽभवद्यत्सुरापानग्ं स कलविंको यदन्नादनग्ं स तित्तिरिस्तस्यांजलिना ब्रह्महत्यामुपागृह्णात्ताग्ं संवत्सरमबिभस्तं भूतान्यभ्यक्रोशन् ब्रह्महन्निति ॥

Then, of the three heads cut off by Indra, the head that used to drink Soma became a bird called kapiñjala (hazecock); the second head, that drank surā, became a kalaviṅka, that is, a sparrow; the third head, that ate food, became a bird called tittiri (partridge). Then, since Indra had killed the brahmin Viśvarūpa, the sin of brahmin-slaying fell upon him and he had to accept it with his own hand. So he bore the sin of brahmin-slaying for a full year.

### Printed p. 304

All the creatures, seeing him (Indra), cried out, "O Indra, you are a killer of a brahmin."

> स पृथिवीमुपासीददस्यै ब्रह्महत्यायै तृतीयं प्रतिगृहाणेति साब्रवीद्वरं
> वृणै खातात्पराभविष्यंती मन्ये ततो मा पराभूवमिति पुरा ते संवत्सरादसिरोहादित्यब्रवीत्तस्मात्पुरा संवत्सरात्पृथिव्यै खातामपिरोहति वारेवृतग्घ्नस्यै तृतीयं ब्रह्महत्यायै प्रत्यगृह्णात्तत्त्वकृतमिरिणमभवत्तस्मादाहिताग्निः शद्धादेवः स्वकृत इरिणे नावस्येद्ब्रह्महत्यायै हेष वर्णः ॥

Seeing this, Indra (ashamed), for the removal of the sin of brahmin-slaying, went to Pṛthivī (the Earth) and said, "O Earth, take one third of this brahmin-slaying that has come upon me." The Earth replied, "Then I shall ask a boon: people dig the earth and make pits, and by that I am dishonoured. Grant me a boon that this may not happen." Indra said, "So be it. Let a pit so dug close up of itself, without any effort, within a year, and let the earth become level as before," and gave the boon. Therefore pits and the like dug in the earth close up of themselves before a year has passed. This is the boon the Earth asked for. Having obtained such a boon, the Earth took one third of Indra's sin of brahmin-slaying. From then on it became natural to the Earth. Therefore a man who has kept the Agnihotra or performed sacrifices and the like, and has faith and devotion toward the gods, should not choose a part of the earth that has been dug into a pit as the sacrificial altar for performing a sacrifice. For such a dug pit-place is the sign (varṇa) of the brahmin-slaying which the Earth took upon herself.

> स वनस्पतीनुपासीददस्यॆ ब्रह्महत्यायै तृतीयं पतिगृह्चितेति तेऽब्रुवन्
> वरं वृणामहै वृक्षात्पराभविष्यंतो मन्यामहे ततो मा पराभूमेत्याव्रश्चनाद्यो भूयाग्‌ंस उत्तिष्टानित्यब्रवीत्तस्मादाव्रश्चनाद्वृक्षाणां
> भूयाग्ंस उत्तिष्यंति वारेवृतग् हैषां तृतीयं ब्रह्महत्यायै प्रत्यगृहन्स् निर्यासोऽभवत्तस्मान्निर्यासस्य नाश्यं ब्रह्महत्यायै ह्येष

Then Indra went near the trees and said, "O trees, take one third of my sin of brahmin-slaying." The trees said, "Then we shall wish for a boon—

### Printed p. 305

people cut the branches and the like of a tree; by that we are overcome. Grant a boon that it may not be so." Indra said, "Good; when it is cut, let more shoots sprout around the cut part," and gave the boon. Therefore, as the boon the trees asked for, when branches are cut, more shoots sprout in that place. Then the trees, as they had said, accepted one third of Indra's brahmin-slaying. The sap that comes out when a tree is cut is the sign of this brahmin-slaying. Therefore no one should drink the sap that flows out when the tree is cut, for it is the colour of brahmin-slaying. Or else: if the sap that flows from the cutting of a tree is red, it should not be drunk; if it is not so, one may drink it if one wishes.

> नाश्यं काममन्यस्य ।

Then Indra went to the company of women and said to them, "O women, take the remaining third of my sin of brahmin-slaying." The women said, "Then we shall wish for a boon: after our monthly course (after the ritual bath) we should bear children; and until childbirth we should be able, if we wish, to find satisfaction of desire through intercourse." Indra said, "So be it." Therefore women, after their monthly course, obtain offspring, and until childbirth they have intercourse whenever they wish. For this is the boon they asked for. Then those women took upon themselves the third part of Indra's sin of brahmin-slaying. The blood that flows when women have their course is the sign of this brahmin-slaying. At the time when the blood flows (during the course) women are impure (unclean).

> स स्त्रीषग्‌ंसादमुपासीददस्यै ब्रह्महत्यायै तृतीयं प्रतिगृह्णीतेति ता
> अब्रुवन्वरं वृणामहा ऋत्वियात् प्रजां निंदामहै काममाविजनितोः
> संभवामेति तस्मादृत्वियात् स्त्रियः प्रजां निंदंते काममा विजनितोः
> संभवंति वारेवृतग् ह्यासां तृतीयं ब्रह्महत्यायै प्रत्यगृह्णन्ता मलवद्वासा अभवत् ॥

Therefore one should not speak with a woman who has her course, should not sit with her, and should not eat food given by her or touched by her; for she is discharging the impure menstrual fluid, the sign of the sin of brahmin-slaying.

### Printed p. 306

During the time of the course she should not apply oil to the body and the like; or, at that time no one should accept food and the like from her (touched by her).

> तस्मान्मलवद्वाससा न संवदेत न सहासीत नास्या अन्नमद्याद्ब्रह्महत्यायै
> हैषा वर्णं प्रतिमुच्यास्तेऽथो खल्वाहुरध्यंजनं वाव स्त्रिया अन्नमभ्यंजनमेव न प्रतिगृह्यं काममन्यदिति ॥

**NOTE**

> यां मलवद्वाससग्‌रि संभवंति यस्ततो जायते सोऽभिशस्तो यामरण्ये
> तस्यै स्तेनो यां पराचीं तस्यै ह्रीतमुख्यपगॆल्लो या स्नाति तस्या
> अप्पु मारुको याभ्यंक्ते तस्यै दुश्चर्मा या प्रलिखते तस्यै खलतिरपमारी यांक्ते तस्यै काणो या दतो धावते तस्यै श्यावदन् या नखानि
> निकृतंते तस्यै कुनखी या कृणत्ति तस्यै क्लीबो या रज्जुग्ं सृजति
> तस्या उद्बंधुको या पर्णॆन पिबति तस्या उन्मादुको या खर्वॆण
> पिबति तस्यै खर्वस्तिस्रो रात्रीव्रतं चरेदंजलिना वा पिबेदखर्वेण
> वा पात्रेण प्रजाय्कॆ गोपीथाय ॥

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-1-1 to 7)

If one has intercourse during the time of the course, the son born of it becomes cursed. If a woman in her course has intercourse in the forest, the son born to her becomes a thief. If she has intercourse with the face covered or turned elsewhere, the son born becomes a timid fellow who from shame cannot speak properly with anyone. The son of a woman who bathes at the time of her course dies by drowning in water. The son of a woman who anoints herself with oil is afflicted with skin disease (leprosy, white patches). The son of a woman who combs her head becomes bald, with no hair on the head, and becomes without strength. The son of a woman who applies collyrium to the eyes becomes blind; the son of a woman who cleans her teeth at that time will have dirty teeth. The son of a woman who cuts her nails will have ugly, bad nails, repulsive to look at. The son of a woman who plaits (mats and the like) at that time becomes a eunuch. The son of a woman who twists a rope dies by suicide. The son of a woman who drinks water from leaves (lotus leaves and the like) becomes a drunkard. A woman who drinks water from a broken or cracked vessel will have a son deficient in limbs or deformed in limbs. Therefore women should observe the vrata (the rule) very strictly until three nights have passed during the course. For the attainment of good offspring, when women drink water at that time, they should drink only from the cupped hands or from a good, unbroken vessel.

Of the matters stated above, the slaying of Viśvarūpa by Indra, the sin of brahmin-slaying that came upon Indra from that slaying, and the deeds Indra performed for the removal of that sin…

### Printed p. 307

(The Kannada text continues:) As a consequence of this, the rule is also stated that women must observe restraint while they are in their courses. In the present context only the account of Viśvarūpa's slaying is to be taken. Yet other matters connected with it, and found in the same anuvāka, are also mentioned here. For in the Purāṇas and similar works it is said that Indra incurred the guilt of brahmin-slaying through the slaying of Vṛtra, and that he made the efforts described above to remove it. So this explanation became necessary in order to show how the Veda differs from the Purāṇas and similar works in these details.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र केतुनेति नवर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभं । त्वष्टपुत्रस्त्रिशिरा नामर्षिः ।
> आदितः षडाग्नेय्यस्ततस्ति स्र ऐंद्रः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्र केतुना नव त्रिशिरास्त्वाष्ट्रश्चोऽंत्य ऐंद्र इति ॥ आदितः षण्णां प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोराग्नेयक्रतावुक्तो विनियोगः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The eighth sūkta, प्र केतुना (*pra ketunā*), has nine Ṛks and is in the Triṣṭubh metre. Its seer is Triśiras, son of Tvaṣṭṛ. The first six verses are addressed to Agni, and the last three to Indra. Sāyaṇa quotes the Anukramaṇī to this effect: प्र केतुना नव त्रिशिरास्त्वाष्ट्रश्चोऽंत्य ऐंद्र इति (*pra ketunā nava triśirāstvāṣṭraśco 'ṃtya aiṃdra iti*). As to use, the first six verses have already had their application stated: they serve the Āgneya-kratu in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Āśvina-śastra.

The Kannada Anuvāda: This sūkta, प्र केतुना (*pra ketunā*), is the eighth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It is said to contain eight Ṛks. **NOTE** Its seer is Triśiras, son of Tvaṣṭṛ. Agni is the deity of the first six Ṛks and Indra of the last three. The Anukramaṇī says: प्र केतुना नव त्रिशिरास्ताष्टस्यचोऽन्त्य ऐंद्रः (*pra ketunā nava triśirāstāṣṭasyaco 'ntya aiṃdraḥ*). It was already stated earlier that the first six Ṛks of this sūkta are applied to the Triṣṭubh mantras connected with the Āgneya-kratu in the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra mantras.

Particulars: Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 8. Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 6; Varga 3, 4. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 9. Seer: Triśiras Tvāṣṭra. Deity: 1–6 Agni; 7–9 Indra. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र के॒तुना॑ बृह॒ता या॑त्य॒ग्निरा रोद॑सी वृष॒भो रो॑रवीति ।  
> दि॒वश्चि॒दंता॑ उप॒मा उदा॑नळ॒गामु॒पस्थे॑ महि॒षो न॑वर्ध ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । केतुना । बृहता । याति । अग्निः । आ । रोदसी इति । वृषभः । रोरवीति ।  
> दिवः । चित् । अंतान् । उप्यमान् । उत् । आनट् । अपां । उपस्थे । महिषः ।  
> ववर्ध ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निर्बृहता महता केतुना प्रज्ञानेन युक्तः सन्नेदानीं रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ प्र याति । प्रकर्षेण गच्छति । किंच देवानामाह्वानकाले वृषभ इव रोरवीति । अत्यर्थं शब्दं करोति । दिवश्चिद्भुलोकस्याप्यंतानवसानानुपमान् समिपांश्च प्रदेशान् ज्वलनात्मनादित्यात्मना वा स्थित उदानट् । ऊर्ध्वं व्याप्न्नोति ।
> अपां वृष्टिलक्षणानामुदकानामुपस्थ उपस्थाने०तरिक्षे वैद्युतात्मना महिषो
> महान्ववर्ध । वर्धते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, endowed with a great banner (केतुना (*ketunā*), meaning knowledge or insight), now goes forth through heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)), that is, moves on with force. When the gods are being invoked he bellows like a bull, that is, he makes a great sound. He pervades upward the farthest and the nearest regions even of the sky, abiding in the form of fire or of the sun. In the lap of the waters, that is, in the atmosphere, which is the abode of the waters in the form of rain, the mighty one grows in the form of lightning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- बृहता (*bṛhatā*)—great
- केतुना (*ketunā*)—with a sign that makes known
- आ (*ā*)—now
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—throughout heaven and earth
- प्र याति (*pra yāti*)—moves exceedingly
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—like a bull
- रोरवीति (*roravīti*)—roars
- दिवश्चित् (*divaścit*)—of the region of the sky
- अंतान् (*aṃtān*)—the farthest regions
- उपमान् (*upamān*)—the nearest regions
- उदानट् (*udānaṭ*)—overruns and pervades
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—of the waters in the form of rain
- उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—in the atmosphere, their place of resort
- महिषः (*mahiṣaḥ*)—Agni, the great one
- ववर्ध (*vavardha*)—grows in the form of lightning

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, endowed with a great sign that makes him known, now moves exceedingly throughout heaven and earth. He roars like a bull. He overruns and pervades the farthest parts of the sky-region and the regions near by. In the atmosphere, the place of resort of the waters in the form of rain, the mighty Agni grows in the form of lightning.

### Printed p. 309

##### English translation
Agni traverses heaven and earth with a vast banner ; he roars (like) a bull ; he spreads aloft over the remote and proximate (regions) of the sky ; mighty, he increases in the lap of the water.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मु॒मोद॒ गर्भो॑ वृष॒भः क॒कुद्मा॑नस्रे॒मा व॒त्सः शिमी॑ना  
> अरावीत् ।  
> स दे॒वता॒त्युद्य॑तानि कृ॒ण्वन्तैषु॒ क्षये॑षु प्रथ॒मो जि॑गाति ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मुमोद । गर्भः । वृषभः । ककुत्मान् । अस्त्रेमा । वत्सः । शिमीवान् । आरावीत् ।  
> सः । देवताति । उत्यतानि । कृण्वन् । स्वेषु । क्षयेषु । प्रथमः । जिगाति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गर्भो द्यावापृथिव्योरंतर्गतो वृषभः कामानां वर्षिताग्निः ककुद्मानुन्नततेजस्को मुमोद : मोदते । किंचास्रेमा । प्रशस्यनामैतत् ' प्रशस्तो वत्सो
> नक्तोषसोर्वत्सभूतः सायंप्रातराहुत्युपजीवनात् शिमीवान् हविर्वहनदेवाह्वानादिकर्मवानग्निररावीत् । देवाह्वानादिशब्दं करोति । सोऽग्निर्देवताति
> यज्ञ उद्यतान्युद्यमान्युत्साहकर्माणि कृण्वन् कुर्वन् स्वेषु क्षयेष्वात्मीयेष्णाहवनीयादिस्थानेषु स्थितः प्रथमो देवानां स्थानेषु मुख्यो जिगाति । गच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the embryo within heaven and earth, the showerer of desires, of lofty radiance, rejoices. अस्रेमा (*asremā*) is a word meaning "praiseworthy". He is the excellent calf, in the form of a child, of night and dawn, since he lives on the evening and morning oblations. शिमीवान् (*śimīvān*) is the Agni who is engaged in carrying the oblation, in calling the gods and the like, and he cries out, making the sound that calls the gods. That same Agni, performing zealous rites (उद्यतानि (*udyatāni*)) in the sacrifice (देवताति (*devatāti*)), and abiding in his own abodes (क्षयेषु (*kṣayeṣu*)), the Āhavanīya and the other places, goes first, that is, as chief among the places of the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गर्भ: (*garbha:*)—who is the embryo of heaven and earth
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the showerer of desires
- ककुद्मान् (*kakudmān*)—Agni, who has lofty radiance
- मुमोद (*mumoda*)—rejoices
- अस्रेमा (*asremā*)—worthy of praise

### Printed p. 310

- वत्सः (*vatsaḥ*)—in the form of a son of day and night
- शिमीवान् (*śimīvān*)—Agni, who has the work of taking up the oblation
- अरावीत् (*arāvīt*)—makes a sound
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- देवताति (*devatāti*)—in the sacrifice that worships the gods
- उद्यतानि (*udyatāni*)—zealous rites
- कृण्वन् (*kṛṇvan*)—performing
- स्वेषु (*sveṣu*)—in his very own
- क्षयेषु (*kṣayeṣu*)—being in the places such as the Āhavanīya
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—as chief among all the gods
- जिगाति (*jigāti*)—moves about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is the embryo of heaven and earth, the showerer of desires, one of lofty radiance, rejoices. He, worthy of praise, in the form of a son of day and night, engaged in taking up the oblation, makes a sound. That same Agni, performing zealous rites in the sacrifice that worships the gods, and abiding in his own places such as the Āhavanīya, moves about as chief among all the gods.

##### English translation
The embryo (of heaven and earth), the showerer (of benefits), the glorious, rejoices ; the excellent child (of morn and eve), the celebrator of holy rites calls aloud : assiduous in exertions at the worship of the gods, he moves chief in his own abodes.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽग्निः पित्रोर्मातापितृभूतयोर्दार्वानापृथिव्योर्मूर्धानमारु
> स्वतेजोभिरारभते । यद्वा । मातापितृभूतयोररण्योर्मूर्धानं शिरोनत्पु-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni who with his own radiance lays hold of (आरब्ध (*ārabdha*)) the head of his parents, that is, of heaven and earth, who stand as mother and father. Or else: he seizes the head, that is, the top, of the two aranis, which are as mother and father, the churning place.

### Printed p. 311

> धानभूतं मंथनप्रदेशं । आ जीषदर्थे । आरब्ध ईषद्धिनस्ति । निर्मथनकालेऽपि
> दाहेन दग्गुं समर्थः । सूरः सुवीर्यस्याग्नेरणो गमनशीलं तेजोऽध्वरे
> यज्ञे नि दधिरे । यष्टारो नियमेन धारयंति । अस्याग्नेः पत्मनतनेऽरुषीरारोचमाना ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य योन् स्थानेऽश्वबुध्ना व्याप्तमूला अशनबंधना वा ।
> हविराहारान्विता इत्यर्थः तन्नस्तदीयास्तनूर्जुषंत । कवयः सेवंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continuing) आ (*ā*) has the sense of "slightly". आरब्ध (*ārabdha*) means he slightly harms; even at the time of churning he is able to burn with his burning. Of the valiant Agni, the moving (अर्णः (*arṇaḥ*)) radiance the sacrificers set firmly in the sacrifice (अध्वरे (*adhvare*)). Of this Agni, the shining (अरुषीः (*aruṣīḥ*)) flames in his course, in the place (योन् (*yon*)) of the sacrifice, अश्वबुध्ना (*aśvabudhnā*), that is, with their roots pervading, or having food as their bond, meaning endowed with the carrying of the oblation: these bodies of his the sages serve. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Agni who
- पित्रोः (*pitroḥ*)—of his parents, heaven and earth
- मूर्धानं (*mūrdhānaṃ*)—the lofty region
- आ अरब्ध (*ā arabdha*)—has overrun with his radiance
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—of that same valiant Agni
- अर्णः (*arṇaḥ*)—the moving radiance
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- नि दधिरे (*ni dadhire*)—the priests have established
- अस्य (*asya*)—of Agni
- पत्मन् (*patman*)—in the time of moving
- अरुषीः (*aruṣīḥ*)—attractive
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- योन्सौ (*yonsau*)—in the place
- अश्वबुध्नाः (*aśvabudhnāḥ*)—and covering the whole root-region
- तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*)—the body of Agni, in the form of radiance
- जुषंत (*juṣaṃta*)—they serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni who has overrun with his radiance the lofty region of his parents, heaven and earth: of that same valiant Agni the moving radiance the priests have established in the sacrifice, binding it by rule. They serve the body in the form of radiance of that Agni, which is attractive in the time of his moving and covers the whole root-region in the place of sacrifice.

##### English translation
They have placed in the sacrifice the radiance of the powerful Agni, who seizes hold of the forehead of his parents, gratifying his cherished, radiant, and expanding limbs, in their course, in their chamber of sacrifice.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वसो स्वेन तेजसा सर्वस्याच्छादयितर्वसुमन्वा प्रशस्य वाग्ने त्वमुष
> उषः सर्वस्या एवोषसोऽग्रं पूर्वमेषि । प्राप्नोषि । अपि च यमयोर्युग्मयोः परस्परमवियुक्तयोरहोरात्रयोर्विभावा दीप्तिमानभवः । भवसि । तन्ने
> स्वाया आत्मीयाच्छरीरान्मित्रमादित्यं जनयन्नुत्पायन् सप्त पदानि सप्तसंख्याकानि
> धिष्ण्यादिस्थानान्यृताय यज्ञार्थं दधिषे । धारयसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, वसो (*vaso*): one who covers all with his own radiance, or one possessed of wealth, or one who is praiseworthy. You go first before every dawn, that is, you reach it. And you are the illuminator (विभावा (*vibhāvā*)) of the twins (यमयोः (*yamayoḥ*)), day and night, which are a pair never parted from each other. Producing Mitra, the sun, from your own body, you hold seven places, the dhiṣṇya hearths and the like, for the sacrifice (ऋताय (*ṛtāya*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यमयोः (*yamayoḥ*) is rendered below.
- वसो (*vaso*)—O Agni, who pervade everything with your radiance

- उषउषः (*uṣauṣaḥ*)—in every dawn-time
- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—the foremost place
- एषि (*eṣi*)—you obtain
- यमयोः (*yamayoḥ*)—of both day and night
- विभावा (*vibhāvā*)—as the one who illumines
- अभवः (*abhavaḥ*)—you have become
- स्वाय्कॆ (*svāykè*)—your
- तन्ने (*tanne*)—from the body
- मित्रं (*mitraṃ*)—the sun
- जनयन् (*janayan*)—producing
- सप्त पदानि (*sapta padāni*)—the seven places
- ऋताय (*ṛtāya*)—for the sacrifice
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you have held

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who pervade everything with your own radiance, you obtain the foremost place in every dawn-time. You have become the illuminator of both day and night. Producing the sun from your own body, you have held the seven places for the sacrifice.

##### English translation
Opulent Agni, you precede dawn after dawn. You are the illuminator of the twin (day and night) : engendering Mitra from your own person, you retain seven places for sacrifice

> जातप्रज्ञाग्ने अपां वृष्टिलक्षणानामुदकानां नपात् पौत्रस्त्वमेव भुवः । भवसि !
> अद्भ्यो हि मेघो जायते मेघादग्निर्विद्युद्रूपो जायत इत्यपां पौत्रस्त्वमुच्यते । यस्य यजमानस्य हव्यं हविर्जुषोषः सेवसे तस्य दूतो भुवः । भवसि #

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you become, like an eye, the illuminator of the great sacrifice (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)). You alone are its guardian (गोपा (*gopā*)), its protector. When, for the taking up of the water in the form of Soma juice, Varuṇa, that is, the Āditya, goes, then it is you alone who become him. **NOTE** O Jātavedas, Agni of born wisdom, you alone become the "grandson" (नपात् (*napāt*)) of the waters, which are the waters in the form of rain. For from the waters the cloud is born, and from the cloud Agni in the form of lightning is born; for this reason you are called the grandson of the waters. Of whichever sacrificer you enjoy the oblation, you become the messenger.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—for the sacrifice

- भुवः (*bhuvaḥ*)—you have become
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—you are the guardian of the sacrifice
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- ऋताय (*ṛtāya*)—for water (for the sacrifice)
- वेषि (*veṣi*)—you go, then
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—in the form of Varuṇa
- भुवः (*bhuvaḥ*)—you become
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, of born wisdom
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—of the waters of rain
- नपात् (*napāt*)—in the form of a grandson
- भुवः (*bhuvaḥ*)—you have become
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of whichever sacrificer
- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—the oblation
- जुजोषः (*jujoṣaḥ*)—you enjoy
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—to him as messenger
- भुवः (*bhuvaḥ*)—you have become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you are the illuminator of the sacrifice. You are its guardian. When you go for the sacrifice, then you are in the form of Varuṇa. O Agni of born wisdom, you are in the form of a grandson to the waters of rain. Of whichever sacrificer you enjoy the oblation, to him you are the messenger.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दर्शपूर्णमासयोराग्नेयस्य याज्या भुवो यज्ञस्येत्येषा, सूत्रितं च ।
> तासां याज्ञानुवाक्या अग्निर्मूर्धा भुवो यज्ञस्य । आ-१-६ । इति ॥ आग्नेयि
> काचित्काम्यॆष्टिः । तस्यामेषैव याज्या, सूत्रितं च । आग्नेय्या उत्तरे नित्ये मूर्धन्वतः । आ. २-१० । इति ॥
> हे अग्ने त्वं यत्र यस्मिन्नंतरिक्षे शिवाभिः कल्याणीभिर्नियुद्भिर्नियुत्संज्ञकाभिरश्वजातिभिः संबद्धं वायुं सचसे संगच्छसे तस्मिन्नंतरिक्षेयज्ञस्य रजसश्चोदकस्य
> च नेता प्रापयिता भुवः । भवसि । अग्निर्वा इतो वृष्टिं समीरयतीति श्रुतेः ।
> किंच दिवि द्युलोके मूर्धानं शिरोवत्पधानभूतं स्वर्षां सर्वस्य संभक्तारमादित्यं दधिषे । हविर्वहनद्वारेण धारयसि । हे अग्ने त्वं जिह्वां ज्वालां हव्यवाहं
> हविषो वोढ्रीं चकृषे । करोषि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This verse, भुवो यज्ञस्य (*bhuvo yajñasya*), is the yājyā of the offering to Agni in the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa sacrifices. Sāyaṇa cites the sūtra: तासां याज्ञानुवाक्या अग्निर्मूर्धा भुवो यज्ञस्य । (*tāsāṃ yājñānuvākyā agnirmūrdhā bhuvo yajñasya |*) (Ā. 1-6). The Āgneyī is also a certain kāmyeṣṭi, and this same verse is its yājyā. The sūtra is आग्नेय्या उत्तरे नित्ये मूर्धन्वतः (*āgneyyā uttare nitye mūrdhanvataḥ*) (Ā. 2-10).

"O Agni, in the atmosphere where you join the wind, which is linked with the auspicious horse-kinds called Niyut, you are the leader (conveyer) of the sacrifice and of the water." This is according to the śruti अग्निर्वा इतो वृष्टिं समीरयतीति (*agnirvā ito vṛṣṭiṃ samīrayatīti*). Further, "in heaven you bear Āditya, the head-like chief, the sharer of everything, by way of carrying the oblation. O Agni, you make your tongue, the flame, the bearer of the oblation."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which atmosphere
- शिवाभिः (*śivābhiḥ*)—auspicious
- नियुद्धिः (*niyuddhiḥ*)—(the wind) accompanied by horses
- सचसे (*sacase*)—you join; there
- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—for the sacrifice
### Printed p. 315
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—to the water
- नेता (*netā*)—as the conveyer
- भुवः (*bhuvaḥ*)—you become
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the heavenly world
- मूर्धानं (*mūrdhānaṃ*)—chief like the head
- स्वर्षां (*svarṣāṃ*)—pervading everywhere; (him) Āditya
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you bear
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- जिह्वां (*jihvāṃ*)—your tongue in the form of flame
- हव्यवाहं (*havyavāhaṃ*)—so as to carry the oblation
- चकृषे (*cakṛṣe*)—you make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, in the atmosphere where you join the wind accompanied by auspicious horses, you become the conveyer of the water for the sacrifice. You bear Āditya, who is chief like the head of heaven and pervades everywhere. O Agni, you make your tongue, in the form of flame, a bearer of the oblation.

##### English translation
You are the leader of the sacrifice and sacrificial water to the place in which you are associated with the auspicious steeds of the wind: you sustain the all-enjoying (sun) as chief in heaven; you, Agni, make your tongue the bearer of the oblation

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the offering made to Agni in the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa sacrifices, this Ṛk भुवो यज्ञस्य (*bhuvo yajñasya*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra तासांयाज्यानुवाक्या अग्निमूर्धा भुवो यज्ञस्य (*tāsāṃyājyānuvākyā agnimūrdhā bhuvo yajñasya*) (Ā. 1-6). And in a kāmyeṣṭi called Āgnīyā, this Ṛk is likewise to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra आग्नेया उत्तरे नित्ये मूर्धन्वतः (*āgneyā uttare nitye mūrdhanvataḥ*) (Ā. 2-10).

> स्थवीर्यवृद्ध्यर्थं यज्ञभागं वव्रे । स चेंद्रस्तस्यॆ पाणिप्रक्षालनार्थं च जलं
> यज्ञभागं च दत्तवान् । अनेन यज्ञभागेन वृद्धवीर्यस्तित एतत्संज्ञक ऋषिरेवैरात्मनो रक्षणैर्युक्तोऽंतर्यज्ञस्य मध्ये धीतिं भागमिच्छन् परस्कोत्कृष्टस्य
> पितुः सर्वस्य जगतः पालयितुरस्येंद्रस्य क्रतुना त्रिशिरसो मम वधार्थं साहाय्यभूतेन कर्मणा निमित्तेन वव्रे । सखायं वृतवान् । किंच पित्रोर्मातापितृभूतयोर्द्यावापृथिव्योरुपस्थे समीपस्थे यज्ञे सचस्यमान ऋत्विग्भिः सेव्यमानस्मितो
> जामि योग्यमिंद्रस्यानुरूपं स्तोत्रं ब्रुवाण इंद्रस्य बलवृद्ध्यर्थमुच्चारयन्नायुधानि स्वभूतानि वेति । त्वष्टपुत्रस्य मम वदार्थमागच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In this ṛc the speaker (Triśiras, Tvaṣṭṛ's son) says: "O Trita, knower of the weapons of all, he who helps me in killing Tvaṣṭṛ's son Triśiras was thus asked by Indra, and Trita chose a share of the sacrifice to increase his own strength. Indra gave him water to wash his hands and a share of the sacrifice. Strengthened by this share, Trita, the seer so named, endowed with protections for himself, desiring a share (धीतिं (*dhītiṃ*)) within the sacrifice, chose (as friend) the supreme father, the protector of the whole world, this Indra, by his act (क्रतुना (*kratunā*)), that is, the act that was to help in my, Triśiras', killing. Further, attended by the priests at the sacrifice near the parents, heaven and earth, and reciting a fitting praise of Indra to increase Indra's strength, he takes up his own weapons; he comes to kill me, Tvaṣṭṛ's son."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्रितः (*tritaḥ*)—of the seer named Trita
- एवैः (*evaiḥ*)—accompanied by (his) self-protections
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle of the sacrifice
- धीतिं (*dhītiṃ*)—a share
- इच्छन् (*icchan*)—desiring
- परस्य (*parasya*)—of the supreme
- पितुः (*pituḥ*)—protector
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra, the friendship
- क्रतुना (*kratunā*)—by reason of the act of help
- वव्रे (*vavre*)—he asked for
- पित्रोः (*pitroḥ*)—of the parents of the world, heaven and earth
- उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—at the sacrifice nearby
- सचस्यमानः (*sacasyamānaḥ*)—being attended by the priests
- जामि (*jāmi*)—praise pleasing to Indra
- ब्रुवाणः (*bruvāṇaḥ*)—reciting
- आयुधानि (*āyudhāni*)—his own weapons
- वेति (*veti*)—takes up

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seer named Trita, endowed with self-protections and desiring a share in the sacrifice, asked for the friendship of Indra, the supreme protector, as help for the killing of Triśiras. At the sacrifice near heaven and earth, the parents of the world, attended by the priests and reciting a praise pleasing to Indra, he takes up his weapon.

##### English translation
Trita by (his own) powers, desiring a share (of the sacrifice), for the sake of taking part in the exploit of the supreme protector (of the world), chose (Indra as his friend); attended (by the priests) in the proximity of the parental heaven and earth, and reciting appropriate praise, he takes up his weapons.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स पित्र्या॒ण्यायु॑धानि वि॒द्वानिंद्रे॑षित आ॒प्त्यो अ॒भ्य॑युध्यत् ।  
> त्रि॒शी॒र्षाणं॑ स॒प्तर॑श्मिं जघ॒न्वान् त्वा॒ष्टस्य॑ चि॒न्निः स॑स्यजे त्रि॒तो  
> गाः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । पित्र्याणि । अयुधानि । विद्वान् । इंद्रइषितः । आप्त्यः । अभि । आयुध्यत् ।  
> त्रिशीर्षाणं । सप्तरश्मिं । जघन्वान् । त्वाष्टस्य । चित् । निः । ससृजे । त्रितः । गाः ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अप्त्य अप्तस्य पुत्रोऽपां पुत्रो वा ॥ तकारोपजनश्चांदसः ॥ स त्रितः
> पित्राणि स्वपितृसंबंधीन्यायुधानि विद्वाञ्ज्ञानन्निंद्रेषितस्त्रिशिरसा मया सह युद्धार्थमिंद्रेण प्रेषितः सन्नभ्ययुध्यत् । अभिमुख्येन युद्धवान् । तदनंतरं सप्तरश्मिं
> शत्रुनियमनार्थं सप्तप्रग्रहहस्तं : यद्वा । सप्तरश्मिरादित्यः । तत्सदृशं । त्रिशीर्षाणं
> त्रिशिरस्कं मां जघन्तान् । हतवान् । मूर्च्छितं कृतवानित्यर्थः । किंच त्रितस्त्वाष्टृ
> चित्त्वष्टपुत्रस्य ममापि गाः पशून्नि: सस्यजे । विसृष्टवान् । अपहृतवानित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Āptya means son of Apta, or son of the waters; the त (*ta*) is a Vedic added letter. That Trita, knowing the weapons connected with his own father, and sent by Indra to fight with me, Triśiras, fought face to face. After that he slew me, the three-headed one who am seven-rayed, that is, holding seven reins in the hand to restrain enemies; or else, seven-rayed is the sun, and I am like him. The meaning is that he made me unconscious. Further, Trita released the cows, the animals, of me also, Tvaṣṭṛ's son; the meaning is that he carried them off.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आप्तः (*āptaḥ*)—the son of the waters
- सः (*saḥ*)—Trita
- पित्राणि (*pitrāṇi*)—belonging to his father
- आयुधानि (*āyudhāni*)—weapons
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—knowing
- इंद्रेषितः (*iṃdreṣitaḥ*)—and urged by Indra
- अभ्ययुध्यत् (*abhyayudhyat*)—fought with the enemy
- सप्तरश्मिं (*saptaraśmiṃ*)—one with seven rays (weapons)
- त्रिशीर्षाणं (*triśīrṣāṇaṃ*)—and with three heads, the enemy (me)
- जिघन्वान् (*jighanvān*)—killed
- त्रितः (*tritaḥ*)—Trita
- त्वाष्ट्रस्य चित् (*tvāṣṭrasya cit*)—of Tvaṣṭṛ's son
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cattle
- निः सस्यजे (*niḥ sasyaje*)—released

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Trita, the son of the waters, knowing the weapons belonging to his father and urged by Indra, fought with the enemy. He killed the enemy who had seven kinds of weapons and three heads. Trita released the cattle of Tvaṣṭṛ's son.

### Printed p. 318

##### English translation
He, the son of the waters, incited by Indra, skilled in his paternal weapons, fought against (the enemy), and slew the seven-rayed, three-headed (Asura): then Trita set free the cows of the son of Twashtri.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भूरीदिंद्र॑ उ॒दिन॑क्षंत॒मोजोऽवा॑भिन॒त्सत्प॑ति॒र्मन्य॑मानं ॥  
> त्वा॒ष्ट्रस्य॑ चिद्वि॒श्वरू॑पस्य॒ गोना॑माचक्रा॒णस्त्रीणि॑ ती॒र्षा परा॑  
> वर्क् ॥ ९ ॥

> भूरि । इत् इंद्रः । उत्ऽइनक्षंतं । ओजः । अव । अभिनत् । सत्ऽपतिः । मन्यमानं ।  
> त्वाष्ट्रस्य । चित् । विश्वरूपस्य । गोनां । आचक्राणः । त्रीणि । शीर्षा । परा ।  
> वर्गिति वर्क् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सत्पतिः सतां पालक इंद्रो भूरीद्भ्येव पूर्वतुल्यमतिरिक्तं नौजो
> बलमुदिनक्षंतं व्याप्नुवंतं मन्यमानं शूरमित्यात्मानं चिंतयंतं । यद्वा ।
> मन्यतिर्दिप्तिकर्मा क्रोधकर्मा ना । दीप्यमानं क्रुद्ध्यंतं वा । त्वष्टपुत्रं
> मामनाभिनत् । वज्रेण विदारितवान् । विदार्य त्वाष्ट्रस्य चित्त्वष्टपुत्रस्यापि
> गोनां गवां । स्वामिन इति शेषः । विश्वरूपस्य मम त्रीणि तीर्षा शीर्षाण्याचक्राण
> आ समंताच्छब्दं कुर्वन् परा वर्क् । पराङ्मुखस्य वृक्षवान् । भिन्नवानित्यर्थः ।
> ईदृशं भावि वस्तु विश्वरूपः स्वप्नांतेनेन तृचेन दृष्टवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, Satpati, protector of the good, भूरीत् (*bhūrīt*), that is, exceedingly (more than before), crushed (अवाभिनत् (*avābhinat*), split with the vajra) me, Tvaṣṭṛ's son, who was attaining ओजः (*ojaḥ*) (strength), pervading and thinking himself a hero (मन्यमानं (*manyamānaṃ*)). Or else: manyati is among the words for brilliance and for anger, so "blazing" or "angry". Having split me, he, shouting on every side (आचक्राणः (*ācakrāṇaḥ*)), cut off (परा वर्क् (*parā vark*), "turned away and cut") the three heads (त्रीणि तीर्षा (*trīṇi tīrṣā*)) of me, Viśvarūpa, who am also the lord of cattle (गोनां (*gonāṃ*), the word "lord" being understood), son of Tvaṣṭṛ. Viśvarūpa saw such a future event at the end of a dream, through this tṛca.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सत्पति: (*satpati:*)—protector of the good
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- भूरीत् (*bhūrīt*)—exceedingly
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—strength
- उदिनक्षंतं (*udinakṣaṃtaṃ*)—one possessing; and
- मन्यमानं (*manyamānaṃ*)—one with the arrogant belief that he himself is greater, namely the son of Tvaṣṭṛ
- अवाभिनत् (*avābhinat*)—split
- त्वाष्ट्रस्य चित् (*tvāṣṭrasya cit*)—the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, and
- गोनां (*gonāṃ*)—lord of the cattle
- विश्वरूपस्य (*viśvarūpasya*)—of Viśvarūpa
- त्रीणि शीर्षा (*trīṇi śīrṣā*)—the three heads
- आचक्राणः (*ācakrāṇaḥ*)—shouting
- परा वर्क् (*parā vark*)—split off
### Printed p. 319

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the protector of the good, split the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, who had exceeding strength and the arrogant belief that he himself was greater. Shouting, he split off the three heads of Viśvarūpa, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ and lord of cattle. (Thus Viśvarūpa, the seer of this sūkta, saw in his dream.)

##### English translation
Indra, the protector of the virtuous, crushed the arrogant (foe), attaining vast strength; shouting, he cut off the three heads of the multiform son of Twashtri (the lord) of cattle.

## Sūkta 9 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Pīṭhike**

The ninth sūkta. In this sūkta the presiding deities of water, the *advaitègaḷu***NOTE**, are praised. The seer of this sūkta is Triśiras, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, called त्रिशिरास्त्वाष्ट्रः (*triśirāstvāṣṭraḥ*), or Sindhudvīpa Āmbarīṣa. The sixth Ṛk of this sūkta is read as the twentieth Ṛk of the twenty-third sūkta of the first maṇḍala. But the Ṛk there, अप्पु मे सोमः (*appu me somaḥ*), has four pādas and is in the Anuṣṭubh metre, whereas the sixth Ṛk of the present sūkta has only three pādas and is a mantra in the Gāyatrī metre: the last pāda, आपश्च विश्वभेषजीः (*āpaśca viśvabheṣajīḥ*), is not there. The seer of the twenty-third sūkta of the first maṇḍala is Medhātithi, son of Kaṇva. The seer of the present sūkta, as said above, is Triśiras Tvāṣṭra or Sindhudvīpa. Likewise the 7th, 8th and 9th Ṛks of the present sūkta are read, without any difference, as the 21st, 22nd and 23rd Ṛks of the twenty-third sūkta. For this reason, that is, because these four Ṛks, the 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th of the present sūkta, were already read earlier as the 20th, 21st, 22nd and 23rd Ṛks of the twenty-third sūkta of the first maṇḍala, the bhāṣyakāra has not written the bhāṣya of these Ṛks again nor explained their meaning. Nevertheless I have written again the bhāṣya and the explanation made earlier.
This sūkta, which praises the presiding deities of water called आपः (*āpaḥ*), has special importance. By the waters consecrated by the recitation of this sūkta, the seer Sindhudvīpa removed the guilt of brahmin-slaying that had come upon Indra because he had killed his own priest, called Viśvarūpa, and made him pure…

### Printed p. 320

The text continues: it is also stated in the Bṛhaddevatā and in the Ṛgvidhāna that Sindhudvīpa made him pure. Moreover, the twice-born recite this sūkta every day, at dusk and at dawn, in the Sandhyāvandana and similar rites performed for the removal of sin, and sprinkle themselves with the water consecrated by it. The greatness of this sūkta and its power to remove sin, as set out in the work called Ṛgvidhāna, is stated here:

आपो हि स्थेति नियतः प्रयुंजीत सदा द्विजः । (*āpo hi stheti niyataḥ prayuṃjīta sadā dvijaḥ |*)
स्नानार्थं शुद्धिकामस्तु जपेत त्रिः समाहितः ॥ (*snānārthaṃ śuddhikāmastu japeta triḥ samāhitaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛgvidhāna, adhyāya 3, śloka 20)

A twice-born man who desires purity of body should, while bathing, recite this sūkta beginning आपो हि ष्ठा (*āpo hi ṣṭhā*) three times with a pure mind.

अप्पु चैव निमज्जित्वा त्रिः पठेत् सुसमाहितः ॥२१॥ (*appu caiva nimajjitvā triḥ paṭhet susamāhitaḥ ‖21‖*)
ब्रह्महा तु कपालेन खट्वांगी चीरसंवृतः । (*brahmahā tu kapālena khaṭvāṃgī cīrasaṃvṛtaḥ |*)
चरेद्द्वादश वर्षाणि स्वकर्म परिकीर्तयन् ॥२२॥ (*careddvādaśa varṣāṇi svakarma parikīrtayan ‖22‖*)
अजपन् मनसैनैतदापो हि स्थेति संस्करेत् । (*ajapan manasainaitadāpo hi stheti saṃskaret |*)
ऊर्ध्वं तु पंचमाद्वर्षाज्जपेदेव सहस्रशः ॥२३॥ (*ūrdhvaṃ tu paṃcamādvarṣājjapedeva sahasraśaḥ ‖23‖*)
अपरस्तु त्रिसाहस्रो जपः स्यात्कृत्यहं सदा । (*aparastu trisāhasro japaḥ syātkṛtyahaṃ sadā |*)
पूर्णे तु द्वादशे वर्षे ब्रह्महा विप्रमुच्यते ॥२४॥ (*pūrṇe tu dvādaśe varṣe brahmahā vipramucyate ‖24‖*)

The manner of reciting this mantra is as follows: one should go down into water up to the waist, stand there, and with an undistracted mind recite this sūkta. The man who has killed a Brāhmaṇa, for the removal of his sin, should dress in a garment of bark-fibre, carry a skull and a khaṭvāṅga (staff) in his hands, and wander for twelve years, announcing here and there to people the sinful deed he has done. Every day at the time of bathing he should bathe while uttering this sūkta aloud or reciting it in his mind. From the fifth year onward he should recite this sūkta a thousand times a day; towards the end, three thousand times every day. If he recites this sūkta in this way for twelve years, that man's guilt of Brahmahatyā is removed and he becomes pure.

समेत्य ब्राह्मणान् ब्रूयुरथ तं चरितव्रतं । (*sametya brāhmaṇān brūyuratha taṃ caritavrataṃ |*)
अचरितं भवेत्किंचिनिथ्यावादी पतेत्पुनः ॥२५॥ (*acaritaṃ bhavetkiṃcinithyāvādī patetpunaḥ ‖25‖*)
दशावरान् दश परान् हन्यास्तमन्यतं वदन् । (*daśāvarān daśa parān hanyāstamanyataṃ vadan |*)
ओं भो इति वदेद्विप्रैरनुज्ञातः शुचिर्जपेत् ॥२६॥ (*oṃ bho iti vadedviprairanujñātaḥ śucirjapet ‖26‖*)

### Printed p. 321

स्थालीपाकं च कुर्वीत सोऽग्नये व्रतचारिणे । (*sthālīpākaṃ ca kurvīta so 'gnaye vratacāriṇe |*)
एवं स मुच्च्यते पापात्सावित्रीं प्रतिपद्य च ॥२७॥ (*evaṃ sa muccyate pāpātsāvitrīṃ pratipadya ca ‖27‖*)

After reciting in this way for twelve years, he should gather the Brāhmaṇas in an assembly and, with folded hands, say: "O Brāhmaṇas, I have now performed the vow for twelve years. If, perhaps, I have not performed the vow and have spoken falsely, let me be punished again. For having spoken falsely, may there come upon me the sin of having slain ten of the elders of my line before me and ten after me." Having taken this oath and received the permission of the Brāhmaṇas, purified, he should recite the mantra once more. Then, to offer a homa addressed to Agni with अग्ने व्रतपते (*agne vratapate*), he should offer the oblation into the fire in the sthālīpāka manner and recite the Gāyatrī mantra. If he does so, the sin of Brahmahatyā he committed is removed and he becomes pure.

ब्रह्महा तु पुरा शक्रस्ताष्टं हत्वा त्वषिं प्रभुं । (*brahmahā tu purā śakrastāṣṭaṃ hatvā tvaṣiṃ prabhuṃ |*)
सिंधुद्वीपस्तमेताभिरभिषिच्य व्यमोचयत् ॥२८॥ (*siṃdhudvīpastametābhirabhiṣicya vyamocayat ‖28‖*)

Formerly Indra killed Viśvarūpa, son of Tvaṣṭṛ, who was his own priest, and so incurred the guilt of Brahmahatyā. Then Sindhudvīpa, the seer of this sūkta, recited the mantras of this sūkta, bathed Indra with the water sanctified by the mantras, and released him from the sin of Brahmahatyā.

ब्रह्मस्वं च गुरोर्द्रव्यं स्तेयं कृत्वा जपन्निमाः । (*brahmasvaṃ ca gurordravyaṃ steyaṃ kṛtvā japannimāḥ |*)
अनेनैव विधानेन षड्भिवर्षैः प्रमुच्यते ॥२९॥ (*anenaiva vidhānena ṣaḍbhivarṣaiḥ pramucyate ‖29‖*)
ब्रह्महा च सुरापश्च नियमेन जपन्निमाः । (*brahmahā ca surāpaśca niyamena japannimāḥ |*)
अनेनैवोपचारेण ब्रह्मघ्न इव मुच्यते ॥३०॥ (*anenaivopacāreṇa brahmaghna iva mucyate ‖30‖*)

The great sin that arises from stealing a Brāhmaṇa's property, or from robbing a teacher of his wealth, is removed if this sūkta is recited for six years in the manner described before, and the man becomes pure. Moreover, one who has killed a Brāhmaṇa, or one who has drunk liquor, is likewise freed from the sins he has committed if he recites this sūkta in the manner stated above.

प्रातरुत्थाय सततं कुर्यान्नार्जनमात्मनः । (*prātarutthāya satataṃ kuryānnārjanamātmanaḥ |*)
रात्रौ कृतस्य पापस्य अविज्ञातस्य निष्कृतिः ॥३३॥ (*rātrau kṛtasya pāpasya avijñātasya niṣkṛtiḥ ‖33‖*)
सायं च नित्यमेताभिः कुर्यान्मार्जनमात्मनः । (*sāyaṃ ca nityametābhiḥ kuryānmārjanamātmanaḥ |*)
दिवा कृतस्य पापस्य अविज्ञातस्य निष्कृतिः ॥३४॥ (*divā kṛtasya pāpasya avijñātasya niṣkṛtiḥ ‖34‖*)
**NOTE**

### Printed p. 322

Rising in the morning, purified by bathing and so on, one should sprinkle one's body with water while reciting the mantras of this sūkta. By this sprinkling done in the morning, the sin committed unknowingly during the night is removed. In the same way, by sprinkling oneself in the evening, the sins committed unknowingly during the day are removed. Thus the power of this sūkta to remove sin is praised.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आपो ही ति नवर्चं नवमं सूक्तं । अंबरीषस्य राज्यः पुत्रः सिंधुद्वीप
> ऋषिस्त्वष्टपुत्रस्तिशिरा वा । इदमाप इत्यादिके द्वे अनुष्टुभौ । ईशाना इति
> वर्धमाना । अपः पृणीतेति प्रतिष्ठा । शिष्टा गायत्र्यः । अपो देवता । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । आपो हि सिंधुद्वीपो वांबरीष अपं गायत्र्यं द्व्यनुष्टुबंतं
> पंचमी वर्धमाना सप्तमी प्रतिष्ठॆति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ आग्निमारुत आपो
> हि श्रेत्याद्यास्तिस्रः । सूत्रितं च । अपो हि श्रेति तिस्रो वियशमप उपस्पृशन्
> आ-५-२८ । इति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning आपो ही (*āpo hī*) has nine Ṛks and is the ninth sūkta. Its seer is Sindhudvīpa, son of Ambarīṣa the king, or else Triśiras, son of Tvaṣṭṛ. The two Ṛks beginning इदमाप (*idamāpa*) are in anuṣṭubh; the Ṛk ईशाना (*īśānā*) is vardhamānā; the Ṛk अपः पृणीत (*apaḥ pṛṇīta*) is pratiṣṭhā; the remaining Ṛks are gāyatrī. The deity is the Waters. So the Anukramaṇī says, quoted in full: आपो हि सिंधुद्वीपो वांबरीष अपं गायत्र्यं द्व्यनुष्टुबंतं पंचमी वर्धमाना सप्तमी प्रतिष्ठॆति (*āpo hi siṃdhudvīpo vāṃbarīṣa apaṃ gāyatryaṃ dvyanuṣṭubaṃtaṃ paṃcamī vardhamānā saptamī pratiṣṭhèti*). The use of the whole sūkta has been given. In the Āgnimāruta recitation the first three Ṛks, beginning आपो हि श्रेत्याद्यास्तिस्रः (*āpo hi śretyādyāstisraḥ*), are used. It is also stated in the sūtra: अपो हि श्रेति तिस्रो वियशमप उपस्पृशन् (*apo hi śreti tisro viyaśamapa upaspṛśan*) (Ā. 5-28). **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning आपो हि ष्ठा (*āpo hi ṣṭhā*) is the ninth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. Its seer is Sindhudvīpa, son of the king Ambarīṣa, or Triśiras, son of Tvaṣṭṛ. The two Ṛks of this sūkta beginning इवमापः (*ivamāpaḥ*) (Ṛks 8–9) are in the anuṣṭubh metre. The fifth Ṛk, ईशाना (*īśānā*), is in the metre called vardhamānā. The seventh Ṛk, आपः पृणीत (*āpaḥ pṛṇīta*), is in the metre called pratiṣṭhā. The other Ṛks are in gāyatrī. The deity is the Waters (āpaḥ). In the Anukramaṇī it is said: आपो हि सिंधुद्विपो वांबरीष अपं गायत्रं द्वनुष्टु बंतं पंचमी वर्धमाना सप्तमी प्रतिष्ठा (*āpo hi siṃdhudvipo vāṃbarīṣa apaṃ gāyatraṃ dvanuṣṭu baṃtaṃ paṃcamī vardhamānā saptamī pratiṣṭhā*). The use of the sūkta has been stated earlier. That the first three Ṛks of this sūkta, आपो हि ष्ठा (*āpo hi ṣṭhā*), are to be recited among the mantras of the Āgnimāruta śastra is made clear by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra आपो हि ष्ठेति तिस्रो वियतमप उपस्पृशन् (*āpo hi ṣṭheti tisro viyatamapa upaspṛśan*) (Ā. 5-20).

Sūkta 9
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 9. Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 6; Varga 5. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 9.
Seer: Triśiras, son of Tvaṣṭṛ, or Sindhudvīpa, son of Ambarīṣa.
Deity: the Waters.
Metre: 1–4, 6 gāyatrī; 5 vardhamānā; 7 pratiṣṭhā; 8–9 anuṣṭubh.

### Printed p. 323
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आपो॒ हि स्था म॑यो॒भुव॒स्ता न॑ ऊ॒र्जे द॑धातन ।  
> म॒हे रणा॑य॒ चक्ष॑से ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आपः । हि । स्थ । मयःऽभुवः । ताः । नः । ऊर्जॆ । दधातन ।  
> महे । रणाय । चक्षसे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हि यस्मात्कारणादापो या यूयं मयोभुवः सुखस्य भावयित्र्यः स्थ
> भवथ तास्तादृश्यो यूयं नोऽस्मानूर्जॆऽन्नाय दधातन । धत्त । अन्नप्राप्तियोग्यानस्मान् कुरुत । अन्नमस्मभ्यं दत्तेत्यर्थः । महे महते रणाय रमणीयाय चक्षसे दर्शनाय सम्यग्ज्ञानाय च धत्त । अस्मान् सम्यग्ज्ञानं प्रति
> योग्यान्कुरुतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Since you, Waters, are the producers of happiness, such as you are, grant us (दधातन (*dadhātana*), from धत्त (*dhatta*)) food (ऊर्जॆ (*ūrjè*)): make us fit to obtain food; that is, give us food. Grant also what is great (महे (*mahe*)), delightful (रणाय (*raṇāya*), रमणीयाय (*ramaṇīyāya*)) and for sight or right knowledge (चक्षसे (*cakṣase*): दर्शनाय सम्यग्ज्ञानाय च (*darśanāya samyagjñānāya ca*)): make us fit for right knowledge.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—O water-deities
- हि (*hi*)—by whose greatness
- मयोभुवः (*mayobhuvaḥ*)—givers of happiness
- स्थ (*stha*)—you are
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—you, possessing such greatness
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- ऊर्जे (*ūrje*)—as worthy of food
- दधातन (*dadhātana*)—make
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- रणाय (*raṇāya*)—delightful
- चक्षसे (*cakṣase*)—also for sight, make us fit

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O water-deities, by whose greatness you are givers of happiness, such as you are, make us worthy of food. Make us fit also for sight that is great and delightful.

##### English translation
Since, Waters, you are the sources of happiness, grant to us to enjoy abundance, and great and delightful perception.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has written an explanation (nirvacana) for this usage as follows:
आपः । आप आप्नोतेः । तासामेषा भवति । आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुवस्ता न ऊर्जे दधातन । महे रणाय चक्षसे ॥ आपो हि स्थ सुखभुवस्ता नोS न्याय धत्त महते च नो रणाय रमणीयाय च दर्शनाय ॥ (*āpaḥ | āpa āpnoteḥ | tāsāmeṣā bhavati | āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvastā na ūrje dadhātana | mahe raṇāya cakṣase ‖ āpo hi stha sukhabhuvastā noS nyāya dhatta mahate ca no raṇāya ramaṇīyāya ca darśanāya ‖*)
(Ni. 9-27)

### Printed p. 324

The word आपः (*āpaḥ*) is formed from the root आप्ल व्याप्त (*āpla vyāpta*); the root means "to pervade, to cause to obtain". आपः (*āpaḥ*) means the waters, which are of spreading nature, that is, pervade everywhere, and which cause happiness, health and the like to be obtained; this is the meaning of the word आपः (*āpaḥ*). To explain this meaning he took the present Ṛk itself as the example: O deities presiding over water, you cause happiness to all; such as you are, provide us with food and other nourishment, and bless us that we may see a state of happiness that is excellent and delightful. This is the intent of the explanation.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो नः॑ शि॒वत॑मो॒ रस॒स्तस्य॑ भाजयते॒ह नः॑ ।  
> उ॒श॒तीर॑व मा॒तरः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । वः । शिवतमः । रसः । तस्य । भाजयत । इह । नः ।  
> उशतीः इव । मातरः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आपः वो युष्माकं स्वभूतो यो रसः शिवतमः सुखतम इहास्मिल्लोके
> तस्य तं रसं नोऽस्मान् भाजयत । सेवयत । उपयोजयतेत्यर्थः । तत्र
> दृष्टांतः । उशतीरिवोतत्य इव पुत्रसमृद्धिं कामयमाना मातरः स्तन्यं रसं
> यथा भाजयंति प्रापयंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Waters, the sap that is your own and most auspicious (शिवतमः (*śivatamaḥ*), most pleasant) in this world, make us share in it (भाजयत (*bhājayata*): cause us to partake, to use it). The illustration: as mothers (मातरः (*mātaraḥ*)) desirous (उशतीः (*uśatīḥ*)) of the thriving of their sons cause the milk-sap to be shared, to reach their children, so you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O water-deities) वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- रसः (*rasaḥ*)—sap
- शिवतमः (*śivatamaḥ*)—is most pleasant
- तस्य (*tasya*)—that sap
- उशतीः इव (*uśatīḥ iva*)—like those who desire the thriving of a son
- मातरः (*mātaraḥ*)—mothers
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- इह (*iha*)—in this world
- भाजयत (*bhājayata*)—cause to be drunk

### Printed p. 325

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O water-deities, whatever sap of yours is most pleasant, make us drink that sap, as mothers who desire the thriving of their sons let their children suckle.

##### English translation
Give us to partake in this world of your most auspicious juice, like affectionate mothers.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तस्मा॒ अरं॑ गमाम वो॒ यस्य॒ क्षया॑य॒ जिन्न॑थ ।  
> आसो॑ ज॒नय॑था च नः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तस्मै । अरं । गमाम । वः । यस्य । क्षयाय । जिन्वथ ।  
> आपः । जनयथ । च । नः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आपः यूयं यस्य पापस्य क्षयाय विनाशायास्माञ्जनथ प्रीणयथ
> तस्मै तादृशाय पापक्षयायारं क्षिप्रं वो युष्मान् गमाम । गमयाम ।
> वयं शिरसि प्रक्षिपामेत्यर्थः । यद्वा । यस्यान्नस्य क्षयाय निवासार्थं यूयमोषधीर्जिन्वथ तर्पयथ तस्मै तदन्नमुद्दिश्य वयमरमलं पर्याप्तं यथा
> भवति तथा वो युष्मान्गमाम । गच्छाम । किंच हे आपः नोऽस्माञ्जनयथ च ।
> पुत्रपौत्रादिजनने प्रयोजयतेत्यर्थ्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Waters, for the destruction (क्षयाय (*kṣayāya*)) of whatever sin you gratify us (जिन्वथ (*jinvatha*), प्रीणयथ (*prīṇayatha*)), to that destruction of sin we swiftly (अरं (*araṃ*)) go to you (गमाम (*gamāma*), "make go"): that is, we cast you on our heads. Or else: for the abode (क्षयाय (*kṣayāya*), निवासार्थं (*nivāsārthaṃ*)) of whatever food you satisfy the plants, with regard to that food we go to you so that it may be sufficient (वयमरमलं पर्याप्तं (*vayamaramalaṃ paryāptaṃ*)). Further, O Waters, cause us to be born (जनयथ (*janayatha*)): employ yourselves in the begetting of sons, grandsons and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O water-deities) यस्य (*yasya*)—of which sin
- क्षयाय (*kṣayāya*)—for the destruction
- जिन्वथ (*jinvatha*)—you make us pleased
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—for that
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- आरं (*āraṃ*)—swiftly
- गमाम (*gamāma*)—we shall approach and take refuge
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—O water-deities
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- जनयथ च (*janayatha ca*)—and bless that sons, grandsons and the like be born

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O water-deities, for the destruction of whatever sin you make us pleased, for that we shall swiftly approach and take refuge in you; make sons, grandsons and the like be born to us.
