#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शं नो॑ दे॒वीर॒भिष्ट॑य॒ आपो॑ भवंतु पी॒तये॑ ।  
> शं योर॒भि स्र॑वंतु नः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शं । नः । देवीः । अभिष्टये । आपः । भवंतु । पीतये ।  
> शं । योः । अभि । स्रवंतु । नः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नोऽस्माकं पापापनोदद्वारेण शं सुखं भवंतु देवीर्देव्य आपः । अभिष्टयेऽस्मद्यज्ञाय भवंतु । यज्ञांगभावाय च भवन्त्यित्यर्थः । पीतये पानाय च
> भवंतु । तथा शमुत्पन्नानां रोगाणां शमनं योर्यावनमनुत्पन्नानां पृथक्करणं च कुर्वंतु । अपि च नोऽस्माकमभ्युपरि स्रवंतु । शुद्ध्यर्थं सिंचंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the divine waters, by removing our sin, be a source of happiness (शं (*śaṃ*)) to us. May they be for our desired end, that is, for our sacrifice and as an auxiliary of the sacrifice, and may they be for drinking. May they also bring about the calming (शं (*śaṃ*)) of diseases that have arisen and the keeping apart (योः (*yoḥ*)) of those that have not yet arisen. And may they flow over us, that is, sprinkle us for purification.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the deities of the waters
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- शं (*śaṃ*)—as givers of happiness
- भवंतु (*bhavaṃtu*)—may they be
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—the divine waters
- अभिष्टये (*abhiṣṭaye*)—may they bring about the accomplishment of our desired ends
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—may they be fit for our drinking
- शं (*śaṃ*)—may they bring happiness that destroys disease
- योः (*yoḥ*)—and the removal of disease
- नः अभि (*naḥ abhi*)—upon us
- स्रवंतु (*sravaṃtu*)—may they flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the deities of the waters be givers of happiness to us. May the divine waters accomplish our desired ends. May they be fit for our drinking. May they bring happiness that destroys disease, and the removal of disease. May they flow upon us.

##### English translation
May the divine waters be propitious to our worship, (may they be good) for our drinking; may they flow round us, and be our health and safety.

### Printed p. 327
#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ईशा॑ना॒ वार्या॑णां॒ क्षयं॑तीच्चर्षणी॒नां ।  
> अप्रो याचामि भेषजं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ईशानाः । वार्याणां । क्षयंतीः । चर्षणीनां ।  
> आहः । याचामि । भेषजं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वार्याणां वारिप्रभवानां व्रीहियवादीनां यद्वा वरणीयानां धनानामीशाना ईश्वराश्चर्यणीनां मनुष्याणां क्षयंतीर्निवासयित्रीरप उदकानि
> भेषजं । सुखनामैतत् । पापापनोदनं सुखं याचामि । अहं प्रार्थये ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The waters are lords (ईशानाः (*īśānāḥ*)) of the things born of water (वार्याणां (*vāryāṇāṃ*)), such as rice and barley, or else of desirable riches; they are the dwellers-giving (क्षयंतीः (*kṣayaṃtīḥ*)), that is, they provide a dwelling for men (चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*)). भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*) is a word for happiness. From the waters I ask (याचामि (*yācāmi*)) the happiness that removes sin; I pray for it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वार्याणां (*vāryāṇāṃ*)—of the rice and the like that are born of water
- ईशानाः (*īśānāḥ*)—who are the lords
- चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*)—to men and the like
- क्षयंतीः (*kṣayaṃtīḥ*)—who are the givers of dwelling
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—from the waters
- भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*)—the happiness that destroys sin
- याचामि (*yācāmi*)—I pray for

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

From the waters, who are lords of the rice and the like born of water and givers of dwelling to men and others, I pray for happiness that destroys sin.

##### English translation
Waters, sovereigns of precious (treasures), granters of habitations to men, I solicit of you medicine (for my infirmities).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒प्पु मे॒ सोमो॑ अब्रवीदं॒तर्विश्वा॑नि भेष॒जा ।  
> अ॒ग्निं च॑ वि॒श्वशं॑भुवं ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 328

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अप्सु । मे । सोमः । अब्रवीत् । अंतः । विश्वानि । भेषजा ।  
> अग्निं । च । विश्वशंभुवं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अप्पु जलेष्टंतर्मध्यॆ विश्वानि भेषजा सर्वाण्यौषधानि संतीति मे मह्यं
> मंत्रदर्शिने मुनये सोमो देवोऽब्रवीत् । तथा विश्वशंभुवं सर्वस्य जगतः
> सुखकरमेतन्नामकं चाग्निं चाप्पु वर्तमानं :सोमोऽब्रवीत् । तथा च तैत्तिरीया अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायांस इत्यनुवाके सोऽपः प्रावितदित्यग्नेरप्पु प्रवेशमामनंति । तै. सं. २-६-६-१ । लतागुल्मवृक्षमूलादीनामौषधानां वृष्टिजन्यत्वेन जलवर्तित्वं प्रसिद्धं ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, the deity, told me, the seer of the mantra, that within the waters are all medicines. Soma also told me of Agni, who is the bringer of happiness to the whole world (विश्वशंभुवं (*viśvaśaṃbhuvaṃ*)) and who is present in the waters. The Taittirīyas, in the anuvāka beginning अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायांस (*agnestrayo jyāyāṃsa*), record Agni's entry into the waters: सोऽपः प्रावित (*so 'paḥ prāvita*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-6-1). That plants, shrubs, trees, roots and other medicines are in the water, being produced by rain, is well known.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अप्पु (*appu*)—of the waters
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- भेषजा (*bheṣajā*)—that there are medicines destroying disease
- अग्निं च (*agniṃ ca*)—and Agni (who is within the water)
- विश्वशंभुवं (*viśvaśaṃbhuvaṃ*)—as the maker of happiness for the whole world
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the god Soma
- मे (*me*)—to me
- अब्रवीत् (*abravīt*)—said

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma told me that the medicines that destroy all diseases, and Agni, the maker of happiness for the whole world, are within the waters.

##### English translation
Soma has declared to me: all medicaments, as well as Agni, the benefactor of the universe, are in the waters,

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The chief point of this Ṛk is that Agni, who produces happiness for the whole world, is in the water in the form of lightning, and that all the medicines that cure the diseases of living beings are in the water itself, as Soma himself told me. On the point that Agni is in the water, the commentator quotes (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-6-1), from the anuvāka beginning अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायाग्‌ंसो भ्रातर असन् (*agnestrayo jyāyāgṃso bhrātara asan*),

### Printed p. 329
the sentence सोऽपः प्राविशत्तं देवताः प्रैषमैच्छन् (*so 'paḥ prāviśattaṃ devatāḥ praiṣamaicchan*). We have already explained it, and the explanation given in the Ṛgveda on this subject, earlier.

अग्निं च विश्वशंभुवं (*agniṃ ca viśvaśaṃbhuvaṃ*)—There is no need to describe at length the benefit that Agni brings to the whole world. Besides giving us warmth when we are cold, we use Agni for cooking food and for many other useful or indispensable tasks. Since this is known to everyone from experience, there is no need to say more.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आपः॑ पृणी॒त भे॑ष॒जं वरू॑थं त॒न्ने॒३॒॑ ३ मम॑ ।  
> ज्योत्स्ना च सूर्यं दृशे ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आपः । पृणीत । भेषजं । वरूथं । तन्ने । मम ।  
> ज्योक् । च । सूर्यं । दृशे ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आपो मम तन्ने शरीरार्थं वरूथं रोगनिवारकं भेषजमौषधं
> पृणीत । पूरयत । किंच ज्योक् चिरं सूर्यं दृशे द्रष्टुं निरोगा वयं शक्कुवामेति शेषः ॥ पृणीत । प्प पालनपूरणयोः । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनं थ । तस्य
> तस्थस्थ मिपामिति तादेशः । क्रादिभ्यः श्ना । प्वादीनां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वः । ईहल्यघोरितीत्वं । ऋवर्णाच्चेति - णत्वं । सति शिष्टस्वरबलीयस्त्वमन्यत्र विकरणेध्य इति तिजः
> स्वरः शिष्यते । आप इत्यस्यामंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदित्यविद्यमानवत्वे पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः । वरूथं । वृञ् वरणे । ज्ञवृञ् भ्यामूथन् । उ. सू. २-६ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तन्ने । जाति ह्रस्वश्च । पा. सू. १-४-६। इति नदीसंज्ञा पाक्षिकीत्याडागमाभावः।
> उदात्तयणो हल्कूर्वादिति विभक्तुदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेनोदात्तस्वरितयोरिति
> स्वरितत्वं । दृशे । दृशे वृख्ये च । पा. सू. ३-४-११ । इति तुमर्थे निपात्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O waters, fill (पृणीत (*pṛṇīta*), make full) for my body (तन्वे (*tanve*)) the medicine (भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*)) that wards off disease (वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*)). Further, may we, free of disease, be able to see the sun for a long time (ज्योक् (*jyok*)); "be able" is to be supplied. The rest is grammar.

### Printed p. 330

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—O waters, or deities presiding over the waters
- मम (*mama*)—my
- तन्वे (*tanve*)—for the body
- वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*)—that wards off disease
- भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*)—medicine
- पृणीत (*pṛṇīta*)—make full (that is, make the body full, free of disease)
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- ज्योक् (*jyok*)—for a long time
- दृशे (*dṛśe*)—I shall see (I shall be able to see, that is, able to live long)

##### Grammar

- पृणीत — प्प पालनपूरणयोः । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनं थ । तस्य तस्थस्थ मिपामिति तादेशः । क्रादिभ्यः श्ना । प्वादीनां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वः । ईहल्यघोरितीत्वं । ऋवर्णाच्चेति णत्वं । सति शिष्टस्वरबलीयस्त्वमन्यत्र विकरणेध्य इति तिजः स्वरः शिष्यते । आप इत्यस्यामंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदित्यविद्यमानवत्वे पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः ।
- वरूथं — वृञ् वरणे । ज्ञवृञ् भ्यामूथन् । उ. सू. २-६ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ।
- तन्ने — जाति ह्रस्वश्च । पा. सू. १-४-६ । इति नदीसंज्ञा पाक्षिकीत्याडागमाभावः । उदात्तयणो हल्कूर्वादिति विभक्तुदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेनोदात्तस्वरितयोरिति स्वरितत्वं ।
- दृशे — दृशे वृख्ये च । पा. सू. ३-४-११ । इति तुमर्थे निपात्यते ।

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O waters (or deities presiding over the waters), prepare (make ready) the excellent medicine so that my body may be free of disease, so that, free of disease, I may see the sun for a long time, that is, may live long.

##### English translation
Waters, bring to perfection all disease-dispelling medicaments for the good of my body, that I may long behold the Sun.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पृणीत (*pṛṇīta*)—प्य पालनपूरणयोः (*pya pālanapūraṇayoḥ*). "Make full" means: make it so that the body is free of disease and able to perform its functions in order.
वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*)—वरणीयं, रोगनिवारकं (*varaṇīyaṃ, roganivārakaṃ*): desirable, that is, disease-warding.
ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे (*jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe*)—To see the sun for a long time means to live long. Several Ṛks in the Ṛgveda convey this same sense:
तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्मः यंसज्योक् पश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरंतं (*tasmā agnirbhārataḥ śarmaḥ yaṃsajyok paśyātsūryamuccaraṃtaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-25-4.)
तन कृत्वा तवोतिभिज्योर्व्यक् पश्येम सूर्यं (*tana kṛtvā tavotibhijyorvyak paśyema sūryaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-4-6.)
शं नः क्षेत्रमुरु ज्योतींषि सोम ज्योज्नः सूर्यं दृशये रिरीहि (*śaṃ naḥ kṣetramuru jyotīṃṣi soma jyojnaḥ sūryaṃ dṛśaye rirīhi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-91-6)
उद्यंतं त्वा मित्रमहो दिवेदिने ज्योज्जीवाः प्रति पश्येम सूर्य (*udyaṃtaṃ tvā mitramaho divedine jyojjīvāḥ prati paśyema sūrya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-37-7)

### Printed p. 331
ज्योक् पश्येम सूर्यमुच्चरंतमनुमते मृळया नः स्वस्ति (*jyok paśyema sūryamuccaraṃtamanumate mṛḷayā naḥ svasti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-59-6)
Besides these, in the Yajurveda too there are many sentences conveying this sense, such as "पश्येम शरदः शतं....  ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे (*paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ....  jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe*)", "ज्योक् च पश्यामि सूर्यं (*jyok ca paśyāmi sūryaṃ*)".

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒दमा॑पः॒ प्र व॑हत॒ यत्किं च॑ दुरि॒तं मयि॑ !  
> यद्वा॒हम॑भिदु॒द्रोह॒ यद्वा॑ शे॒ष उ॒तानृ॑तं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदं । अपः । प्र । वहत । यत् । किं । च । दुः इतं । मयि  
> यत् । वा । अहं । अभिद्धुद्रोह यत् । वा । शेपे । उत । अनृतं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मयि यजमाने यत्किं च दुरितमज्ञानान्निप्पन्नं । वाथवाहं यजमानोऽभिदुद्रोह सर्वतो बुद्धिपूर्वकं द्रोहं कृतवानस्मि वाथवा शेषे साधुजनं शप्तवानस्मीति यदस्ति । उतापि चानृतमुक्तवानिति यदस्ति । तदिदं सर्वमपराधजातं प्र वहत । मत्तोऽपनीय प्रवाहेणान्यतो नयत ॥ मयि । मपर्यंतस्य
> त्वमावेकवचन इति मादेशे कृतेऽतो गुण इति पररूपे च सति योऽचीति दकारस्य
> यकारादेशः । एकादेशस्वरेण मकारात्परस्याकारस्योदात्तत्वं । दुद्रोह । द्रुह
> जिघांसायां । णलि गुणे द्विर्वचनह्रस्वहलादिशेषाः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्कोदात्तत्वं । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघाताभावः । शेषे । शप आक्रोशे । लिटि व्यत्ययेन
> तज् । उत्तमैकवचनमिट् । टेरेत्वं । अत एकहल्मध्यॆ । पा. सू. ६-४-१२० । इत्येत्वा
> भ्यासलोपौ । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तत्वं । पूर्ववन्निघाताभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Whatever sin (दुरितं (*duritaṃ*)) there is in me, the sacrificer, done through ignorance; or whatever wrong I have knowingly done on all sides (अभिदुद्रोह (*abhidudroha*)); or whatever I have cursed (शेपे (*śepe*)) good people; and also whatever untruth I have spoken: all this body of offences, O waters, carry off (प्र वहत (*pra vahata*)), remove from me and bear away elsewhere with your current. The rest is grammar.

##### Grammar

- मयि — मपर्यंतस्य त्वमावेकवचन इति मादेशे कृतेऽतो गुण इति पररूपे च सति योऽचीति दकारस्य यकारादेशः । एकादेशस्वरेण मकारात्परस्याकारस्योदात्तत्वं ।
- दुद्रोह — द्रुह जिघांसायां । णलि गुणे द्विर्वचनह्रस्वहलादिशेषाः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्कोदात्तत्वं । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघाताभावः ।
- शेपे — शप आक्रोशे । लिटि व्यत्ययेन तज् । उत्तमैकवचनमिट् । टेरेत्वं । अत एकहल्मध्यॆ । पा. सू. ६-४-१२० । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तत्वं । पूर्ववन्निघाताभावः ।

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मयि (*mayi*)—in me, the sacrificer
- यत्किंच (*yatkiṃca*)—whatever
- दुरितं (*duritaṃ*)—sins done through ignorance there may be
- वा (*vā*)—or
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- यत् अभिदुद्रोह (*yat abhidudroha*)—if I have knowingly intended harm (to anyone)
- वा (*vā*)—or
- यत् शेपे (*yat śepe*)—concerning whom I have spoken ill

### Printed p. 332
- *yat śepe*—(continued) evil words spoken in regard to whom
- उत (*uta*)—and
- अनृतं (*anṛtaṃ*)—untruth (spoken)
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—such sin
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- प्रवहत (*pravahata*)—(separating it from me) let them sweep away in the form of a current.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Whatever sins I may have committed through ignorance, or if I have plotted harm against anyone, or have spoken evil words, or have spoken untruth, may the waters (flowing water) sweep all such sins away in the form of a current.

##### English translation
Waters, take away whatever sin has been (found) in me, whether I have (knowingly) done wrong, or have pronounced imprecations (against holy men), or have spoken untruth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दुरितं—अज्ञानान्निष्पन्नं कायिकं पापं । (*duritaṃ—ajñānānniṣpannaṃ kāyikaṃ pāpaṃ |*) Duritam is sin of the body, done through ignorance or knowingly in the form of an act, that is, sins committed by the use of force such as striking someone.

Abhidudroha: plotting evil in the mind is called droha. This is a mental sin.

Śepe, anṛtam: abusing and speaking untruth and the like are sins committed through speech. This is verbal. The prayer is that flowing water may sweep away these three kinds of sin.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आपो॑ अ॒द्यान्व॑ चारिषं॒ रसे॑न॒ सम॑गस्महि ॥  
> पय॑स्वा नग्न॒ आ ग॑हि॒ तं मा॒ सं सृ॑ज॒ वर्च॑सा ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आपः । अद्य । अनु । आचारिषं । रसेन । सं । अगस्महि ।  
> पयस्वान् । अग्ने । आ । गहि । तं । मा । सं । सृज । वर्चसा ॥ ९ ॥

### Printed p. 333

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अद्यास्मिन्निनेवभृथार्थमापोऽन्वचारिषं । जलान्यनुप्रविष्टोऽस्मि । प्रविश्य च
> रसेन जलसारेण समगस्महि । संगताः स्मः । हे अग्ने पयस्वान् जले वर्तमानत्वेन
> पयोयुकस्त्वमा गहि । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । तं मा तादृशं स्नातं मां वर्चसा
> तेजसा सं सृज । संयोजय ॥ अपः । कर्मणि शसि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन जस् । आचारिषं । चर गत्यर्थः । ! लुजि च्छेः सिच् । आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः । पा. सू. ७-२-३५ ।
> इतीट्! नेटि। पा. सू. ७-२-४। इति वृद्धि प्रतिषेधेप्राप्ते तदपवादतॆयातो लांतस्य; पा।
> ७.२-२ । इत्युपधाया वृद्धिः । अगस्महि । समो गम्यच्छेत्यात्मनेपदं । पा. सू. १-३-२९ ।
> च्छेः सिच् । मंत्रे घसेत्यादिना ज्लेर्लुगभावश्चांदसः । एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तादितीट् प्रतिषेधः । ना गमः । पा. सू. १-२-१३ । इति सिचः कित्त्वादनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिदानुनासिकलोपः । गहि । लोटि गमेः सिपो हिः । अपित्वेन जुत्त्वादनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । अतो हेरिति लुग्न भवति । असिद्धवदत्राभादिति
> मलोपस्यासिद्धत्वात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Today, for the sake of this avabhṛtha bath, I have entered the waters (अन्वचारिषं (*anvacāriṣaṃ*): I have gone into the waters), and having entered I have united with their essence, the substance of the water (समगस्महि (*samagasmahi*): we have come together). "O Agni, पयस्वान् (*payasvān*)—you who, being in the water, are possessed of water—come to this rite. Join me, so bathed, with वर्चसा (*varcasā*), with brilliance; unite me." The remainder of the block is grammatical (the form अपः (*apaḥ*) as a case-substitution; आचारिषं (*ācāriṣaṃ*), अगस्महि (*agasmahi*), गहि (*gahi*)) and is left out here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आद्य (*ādya*)—now (today)
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- अन्वचारिषं (*anvacāriṣaṃ*)—I have entered (for the avabhṛtha bath); (then)
- रसेन (*rasena*)—with the essence of the water
- समगस्महि (*samagasmahi*)—we have united
- (हे) अग्ने (*(he) agne*)—O Agni
- पयस्वान् (*payasvān*)—possessed of water, that is, you who are in the water
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—come (to this rite of bathing); (and)
- तं मा (*taṃ mā*)—me (who have bathed)
- वर्चसा (*varcasā*)—with brilliance
- संस्कृज (*saṃskṛja*)—join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have now entered the water for the (avabhṛtha) bath. May all the essence that is in the water unite with us. O Agni, since you are in the water, come to this bathing rite and make me, who have bathed, radiant.

##### English translation
I have this day entered into the waters : we have mingled with their essence. Agni abiding in the waters approach, and fill me (thus bathed) with vigour.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

आपः—द्वितीयार्थे प्रथमा (*āpaḥ—dvitīyārthe prathamā*)—so Skandasvāmin has said. That is, for the word आपः (*āpaḥ*), which stands in the (first-case) ending, the sense of अपः (*apaḥ*), the second case, is to be understood. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 334
रसेन—जलसारेण (*rasena—jalasāreṇa*), with the essence of water: the idea is that pure water should remove the faults (the dirt), inward and outward, of my body.

पयस्वान् (*payasvān*)—पयसा जलेन युक्तः (*payasā jalena yuktaḥ*), or: one who stays in water, पयसि तिष्ठतीति पयस्वान् (*payasi tiṣṭhatīti payasvān*). In the Yajurveda, sentences such as सोऽपः प्राविशत् (*so 'paḥ prāviśat*) say that Agni hid himself in the water. Hence it is said in many contexts that Agni is in the water. The latter half of this Ṛk has Agni as its deity.

The supplementary mantra to be recited at the end of this sūkta:
सस्रुषीस्तदपसो दिवा नक्तं च सस्रुषीः । (*sasruṣīstadapaso divā naktaṃ ca sasruṣīḥ |*)
वरेण्यक्रतूरहमा देवीरवसे हुवे ॥ (*vareṇyakratūrahamā devīravase huve ‖*)
The chief sense of the mantra: I call, praying for my protection, the waters or the deities presiding over the waters, which flow without break by day and by night, which carry out their excellent duty, and which are endowed with intelligence.

## Sūkta 10 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
In this sūkta and in several of the following sūktas, matters concerning Yama and the Pitṛs are stated. This sūkta contains the conversation between Yama and his sister, called Yamī. Therefore the introduction to this sūkta explains only the matter of Yama and the conversation held with Yamī. The matter of the Pitṛs will be explained in the following sūktas. By Pitṛs are meant here the elders of the family, such as the father, now dwelling in the other world, the forefathers. The Ṛgveda says that those of the family's elders who have died have obtained an excellent place in the other world and live there, and that Yama is king of these Pitṛs. Therefore in the following sūktas the close relation between Yama and the Pitṛs is explained.

### Printed p. 335
**In praise of Yama**

**1. The greatness of Yama**
Since in the Ṛksaṃhitā there are many kinds of descriptions when Yama's nature is explained, it is laborious to decide that his nature is exactly so. Among Western scholars each has formed a different conception in this matter. There is also discussion whether Yama is a human person or a deity. To examine the matter from a purely modern point of view and give a fixed opinion on it would be wrong. It is proper to examine it from the scholarly point of view, in accordance with traditional contexts.

If one examines the contexts in which Yama's nature is described in the Ṛksaṃhitā, only four sūktas are found that praise Yama alone. The praise of this deity is abundant, it seems, only in the first and tenth maṇḍalas. Some Western scholars hold that in no mantra is Yama stated definitely as a deity. But there are many contexts where Yama is praised along with other deities. For example:

इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुरथो दिव्यः स सुपर्णो गरुत्मान् । (*iṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimāhuratho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān |*)
एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदंत्यग्निं यमं मातरिश्वानमाहुः ॥ (*ekaṃ sadviprā bahudhā vadaṃtyagniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānamāhuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-46)

The one Lord is called Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni. Moreover, he is Garutmān, the divine spirit, of excellent flight. The wise vipras call the one Lord, who is one Self, in many ways: Agni, Yama, Mātariśvan. This means that Yama too is a part of the original principle. It is clear that the same greatness that Varuṇa and the others have belongs to Yama as well. Moreover:

यस्मिन्वृक्षे सुपलाशे देवैः संपिबते यमः । (*yasminvṛkṣe supalāśe devaiḥ saṃpibate yamaḥ |*)
अत्रा नो विश्वतिः पिता पुराणा अनु वेनति ॥ (*atrā no viśvatiḥ pitā purāṇā anu venati ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-135-1)

In the tree full of leaves where Yama drinks soma together with the other deities, there the householder, protector of the people and lord, invites us to join those who have gone before; so it is also described.

### Printed p. 336
Yama is praised abundantly along with such deities as Varuṇa (10-14-7), Bṛhaspati (10-17-14) and Agni (10-21-5). Moreover, in the mantra महत्तदुल्बं स्थविरं (*mahattadulbaṃ sthaviraṃ*) (10-51-1) it is told that Agni hid himself secretly in the water, and that then only one god saw this Agni. But who that deity is:

ऐच्छाम त्वा बहुधा जातवेदः प्रविष्टमग्ने अप्सोषधीषु । (*aicchāma tvā bahudhā jātavedaḥ praviṣṭamagne apsoṣadhīṣu |*)
तं त्वा यनो अचिकेच्चित्रभानो दशांतरुष्यादतिरोचमानं ॥ (*taṃ tvā yano acikeccitrabhāno daśāṃtaruṣyādatirocamānaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-51-2)

O Agni, you who were hidden in the water of abundant essence, and in many forms hidden in plants and the like, we sought you in many ways. But you, whose rays spread a great light, Yama alone knew; so it is said. That in the sentence 10-51-1 the deity sought Agni, and that in this present mantra Yama himself found Agni, shows definitely that Yama is a deity. This deity is king of all the Pitṛs.

प्रेहि प्रेहि पथिभिः पूर्व्यभिर्यत्रा नः पूर्वे पितरः परेयुः । (*prehi prehi pathibhiḥ pūrvyabhiryatrā naḥ pūrve pitaraḥ pareyuḥ |*)
उभा राजाना स्वधया मदंता यमं पश्यासि वरुणं च देवं ॥ (*ubhā rājānā svadhayā madaṃtā yamaṃ paśyāsi varuṇaṃ ca devaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-7)

O departed one, set out on that path by which our former Pitṛs went. There you will see Yama, king of all the Pitṛs, and the god Varuṇa. Many such sentences describe Yama as king of all the Pitṛs. In all the sentences that praise him, the close relation between him and the Pitṛs is shown. Among them, the relation between the Aṅgirases and Yama is very close. He is praised as the giver of refuge to all the dead (10-14-9).

**2. The place of Yama**
The sentence
यत्र राजा नैवस्वतः यत्रावरोधनं दिवः ॥ (*yatra rājā naivasvataḥ yatrāvarodhanaṃ divaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-8)
and others like it, which describe the farthest region of the heavenly world as Yama's dwelling, describe Yama's dwelling-place and his lordship. Moreover, lordship over the heavenly world belongs to the two, Yama and Āditya. Of these, the place of Āditya and the place of Yama are both fixed. How, then?

### Printed p. 337
तिस्रो द्यावः सवितुद्र्वा उपस्था एका यमस्य भुवने विराषाट् । (*tisro dyāvaḥ savitudrvā upasthā ekā yamasya bhuvane virāṣāṭ |*)
आणिं न रथ्यममृताधि तस्थुरिह ब्रवीतु य उ तच्चिकेतत् ॥ (*āṇiṃ na rathyamamṛtādhi tasthuriha bravītu ya u tacciketat ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35-6)

The worlds denoted by "heaven" are three. Of them, the heavenly world and the earth are to be illumined by Āditya. The middle world, the atmosphere, belongs to Yama. The place of Yama is thus stated: living beings that die and take the form of the departed travel through this atmosphere, Yama's world. It is laborious to state a definite meaning regarding these heavenly and atmospheric worlds. For, according to the prevailing belief, the heavenly world is above the atmosphere and is better than it. If Yama's world is the atmosphere, it would not be better than the heavenly world. But in some places Yama's world is described as the very best. For example:

संगच्छस्व पितृभिः सं यमेनेष्टापूर्तेन परमे व्योमन् ॥ (*saṃgacchasva pitṛbhiḥ saṃ yameneṣṭāpūrtena parame vyoman ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-8)

In such sentences Yama's world is said to be the most excellent. Here the everlasting light shines (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-9). But this place is also known to be the place of the Sun. How?

यत्रानुकामं चरणं त्रिनाके त्रिदिवे दिवः । (*yatrānukāmaṃ caraṇaṃ trināke tridive divaḥ |*)
लोका यत्र ज्योतिष्मतस्तत्र मामृमृतं कृधींद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*lokā yatra jyotiṣmatastatra māmṛmṛtaṃ kṛdhīṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-9)

In this prayer this heavenly world is described as having everlasting radiance. It has been stated before that this heavenly world is the world of the Sun. Moreover, in many places it is praised that the best soul, which has performed the prescribed rites, as soon as it is separated from the body takes the form of a ray of the sun and obtains a lasting place in the world of the Sun.

सहस्रणीथाः कवयो ये गोपायंति सूर्यं । (*sahasraṇīthāḥ kavayo ye gopāyaṃti sūryaṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-154-5)

This point is clear also where it says: "O Yama, favour those ascetic ṛṣis, the poets of a thousand eyes, who protect the Sun." There are yet many other contexts that clearly show the identity of the abode of Āditya and the abode of Yama. For example—

### Printed p. 338

In the verse इदं यमस्य सादनं देवमानं यदुच्यते । इयमस्य धम्यते नाळीरयं गीर्भिः परिष्कृतः ॥ (*idaṃ yamasya sādanaṃ devamānaṃ yaducyate | iyamasya dhamyate nāḷīrayaṃ gīrbhiḥ pariṣkṛtaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.135.7), the word यमस्य (*yamasya*) is first explained as the Āditya, the controller of the world. Only afterwards is the second meaning, Yama, given. The world of this Yama is said to be made by the gods. Here the sound of the flute pervades the whole region with a pure note, hymns of praise resound on every side, and the whole region is described as well refined. In the next hymn (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-136-1), in the passage केशीदं ज्योतिरुच्यते (*keśīdaṃ jyotirucyate*), the light is explained as the mass of radiance of the solar orb. Thus in many places, wherever Yama's abode is indicated, an identity of Āditya and Yama is shown.

**3. The parents of Yama**

Yama's father is Vivasvān and his mother is Saraṇyū, who is Vivasvān's wife.

त्वष्टा दुहित्रे वहतुं कृणोतीतीदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति । यमस्य माता परुह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश ॥ (*tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṃ kṛṇotītīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sameti | yamasya mātā paruhyamānā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-1)

The god named Tvaṣṭṛ gave his daughter Saraṇyū in marriage to Vivasvān. This Saraṇyū is the mother of Yama and of his twin Yamī. She bore the two, Yama and Yamī (अजहादु द्वा मिथुना सरण्यः (*ajahādu dvā mithunā saraṇyaḥ*), Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-2). This Yama is often referred to as Vaivasvata (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.14-1 and elsewhere).

गंधर्वो अप्पप्या च येषा सा नो नाभिः परमं जामि तन्नौ ॥ (*gaṃdharvo appapyā ca yeṣā sā no nābhiḥ paramaṃ jāmi tannau ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-10-4)

Here Yamī, entreating Yama, declares that the two of them are the son and daughter of the Gandharva, brother and sister. But if Yama is a synonym of Āditya, what then is the meaning of the word Yamī? One must know the precise sense of these words in the Nirukta and similar works. So one should first learn how Yama's nature is described in the Ṛksaṃhitā, and on that basis consider the other meanings of the word Yama.

**4. Description of Yama's nature**

Yama is described as the presiding deity of all the fathers (Pitṛs) and as lord of the world of the fathers: यत्र राजा वैवस्वतः (*yatra rājā vaivasvataḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-13-8); वैवस्वतं संगमनं जनानां (*vaivasvataṃ saṃgamanaṃ janānāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-1)

### Printed p. 339

यमं राजानु हविषा दुवस्य (*yamaṃ rājānu haviṣā duvasya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-1); यमराज्ञो गच्छतु रिप्रवाहः (*yamarājño gacchatu ripravāhaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-16-9). In such places Yama is referred to as king. There are also many contexts in which Yama and Varuṇa are described together as lords of the world of the fathers: उभा राजाना स्वधया मदंता यमं पश्यासि वरुणं च देवं (*ubhā rājānā svadhayā madaṃtā yamaṃ paśyāsi varuṇaṃ ca devaṃ*) (10-14-7). His form is very terrible. Like the noose of Varuṇa that punishes sinners, Yama's noose too punishes sinners.

मुंचंतु मा शपथ्या ३ दधो वरुण्यादुत । अथो यमस्य पद्मीशात्सर्वस्माद्देवकिल्पिषात् ॥ (*muṃcaṃtu mā śapathyā 3 dadho varuṇyāduta | atho yamasya padmīśātsarvasmāddevakilpiṣāt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.97-16)

In this prayer, "may the plants free me from the sins born of a curse and from the noose of Varuṇa, which is a form of restraint", Yama's noose is described as पद्वीश (*padvīśa*) ("foot-fetter"); that is, a noose that binds the feet so that they cannot move. In just this way Yama's terrible nature is described in many other places. This becomes clearer when one knows what Yama's duty is.

**5. The messengers of Yama and their nature**

After death Yama leads those who have done good deeds to the excellent regions fitting each deed. For sinners he arranges the place that is fitting for them (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-1). Moreover, this Yama is Death (Mṛtyu), the cause of death for men:

यदुलूको वदति मोघमेतद्यत्कपोतः पदमग्नौ कृणोति । यस्य दूतः प्रहित एष एतत्तस्मै यमाय नमो अस्तु मृत्यवे ॥ (*yadulūko vadati moghametadyatkapotaḥ padamagnau kṛṇoti | yasya dūtaḥ prahita eṣa etattasmai yamāya namo astu mṛtyave ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-165-4)

Here the owl and the pigeon are indicated as Yama's messengers. An identity of Yama and Death is stated. For this very reason there is a belief that the cry and the sight of an owl are inauspicious. Besides this, the passage beginning यौ ते श्वान (*yau te śvāna*) (10-14-11) describes two dogs who are Yama's messengers. (The nature of these dogs, called Sārameya, will be explained later in the introduction to Sūkta 14 of the 10th Maṇḍala.) The detail that these dogs have four eyes and broad nostrils shows their monstrous forms. But those who have done good deeds need not fear these dogs; after death they guard their paths.

### Printed p. 340

The same dogs are also described in the Atharvaveda, where it is said that one of them is dark-coloured. (In Ath. Saṃ. 8-19 Yama's messengers are referred to in the plural, but they are not said to be dogs.) **NOTE**

वैवस्वतेन प्रहितान्यमदूतांश्च रतोऽपसेधामि सर्वान् (*vaivasvatena prahitānyamadūtāṃśca rato 'pasedhāmi sarvān*) (Ath. Saṃ. 8-2-11) **NOTE**

"I ward off all the messengers of Yama sent by the son of Vivasvān", it says. Whether these messengers of Yama are dogs or anyone else, the terror they inspire is dreadful. Like his messengers, Yama's weapon too is terrifying.

मा नो हेतिर्विवस्वत आदित्याः कृत्रिमा शरुः । पुरा नु जरसो वधीत् ॥ (*mā no hetirvivasvata ādityāḥ kṛtrimā śaruḥ | purā nu jaraso vadhīt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-67-20)

"O Ādityas, may the weapon of Yama, which causes fear and does harm, not harm us; may we not suffer decay as a result of its harm": so the prayer runs, and so on.

**6. Yama and Yamī**

The word Yama is used in many places in the sense of "twin". The word Yama itself indicates the two meanings, Yama and Yamī.

दुर्मन्त्वत्रामृतस्य नाम सलक्ष्मा यद्विषुरूपा भवाति (*durmantvatrāmṛtasya nāma salakṣmā yadviṣurūpā bhavāti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-12-6)

It is hard to know the form of this Yama. Though he has a single kind of mark, he has many forms, it says. When the two epithets सलक्ष्मा (*salakṣmā*) and विषुरूपा (*viṣurūpā*) are explained together in one context, the identity of Yama and Yamī, and difference within unity, appear. Yama himself says the same in his own words:

न ते सखा सख्यं वष्ट्येतत्सलक्ष्म्या यद्विषुरूपा भवाति (*na te sakhā sakhyaṃ vaṣṭyetatsalakṣmyā yadviṣurūpā bhavāti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-10-2)

But these epithets have to be explained according to context. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.10-10 Yama and Yamī are praised as जामि (*jāmi*). The word जामि (*jāmi*) means simply a close kinsman. Close kinship may exist between husband and wife, or between brother and sister. For example, Heaven and Earth (Dyāvāpṛthivī)

### Printed p. 341

are praised in many places with epithets such as जामि (*jāmi*), स्वसारा (*svasārā*) and दंपती (*daṃpatī*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-7; 1-185.5). One may say they are two forms of one principle. Just as the Sāman principle has two forms, Sāman and Ṛk (sā + ama), just as the Prajāpati principle has two principles, mind (manas) and speech (vāk), and just as Agni has two forms, Brahma and Kṣatra, so there is room to say that the Yama principle includes the two divisions Yama and Yamī.

By passages such as यमो हि जात इंद्रेण सह (*yamo hi jāta iṃdreṇa saha*) (Ni. 10-21) an identity of Yama and Agni is stated. In some places Indra and Agni are described as the Yamas. There are also passages that state an identity of Indra and Earth (Ai. Brā. 3-38). The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa says that Yama is Agni and Yamī is the Earth (Śa. Brā. 7-2-1-10). Yamī's words वृहेव रथ्येव चक्रा (*vṛheva rathyeva cakrā*) compare Yama and Yamī to the wheels of a chariot.

न्यं ० घ्नस्य मूर्धनि चक्रं रथस्य येमथुः । परि द्यामन्यदीयते । (*nyaṃ 0 ghnasya mūrdhani cakraṃ rathasya yemathuḥ | pari dyāmanyadīyate |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-30-19) **NOTE**

The two wheels that are indicated in such places are wheels that support the universe. In explaining the nature of the Aśvin deities, the authors of the Nirukta report differing opinions: some say the pair of Aśvins are Day and Night, some Heaven and Earth, and others that the word indicates some other well-known pair of deities. Some also hold that the word Aśvin may likewise indicate the union of Yama and Yamī. The epithet such as समीची (*samīcī*) with which the Aśvins are praised in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-24-4 and in the fifth verse may equally be a praise of Heaven and Earth, or of Yama and Yamī. If one examines the similes by which the Aśvins are described in Sūkta 39 of Ṛ. Saṃ. 2, it is suggested that the Aśvins are a pair of female and male. Similes such as दंपतीव (*daṃpatīva*) and चक्रवाकेव (*cakravākeva*) indicate this. (There are also similes such as ग्रावाणेव (*grāvāṇeva*).) Along with these there is the simile ओष्ठाविव (*oṣṭhāviva*). The word ओष्ठा (*oṣṭhā*) indicates the pair Heaven and Earth in many places.

In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-109-4 Indra and Agni are addressed as Aśvins.
" The same Indra and Agni are referred to as Nāsatyas.
" An identity of Heaven and Earth with the Aśvins is stated.

### Printed p. 342

Thus Sāyaṇa has in many places expressed the view that the pair indicated by the word Yama may also indicate pairs such as Indra and Agni, the Aśvins and so on. So one may examine whether there are contexts showing a similarity between the manner of origin of the Aśvins and that of Yama.

It was stated earlier that Yama arose from the couple Vivasvān and Saraṇyū, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-10-4; 10-17-1). The Bṛhaddevatā, describing Yama's origin, also explains its hidden meaning.

ततः शरण्वां बज्ञाते यमयम्या विवस्वतः । शौ जाप्यथा यमावेव जायांस्ताभ्यां तु वै यमः ॥ (*tataḥ śaraṇvāṃ bajñāte yamayamyā vivasvataḥ | śau jāpyathā yamāveva jāyāṃstābhyāṃ tu vai yamaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 6-163) **NOTE**

Then two, Yama and Yamī, were born to Saraṇyū, the wife of Vivasvān. Both were twins. But of the two, Yama is the elder, it says. As indicated above, this passage conveys the identity of Yama and Yamī with the pair of Aśvins. The authors of the Nirukta themselves were unable to state a precise opinion on what principle the Aśvin deities reflect. In the Ṛksaṃhitā itself there is room for the view that they may be named Yama and Yamī. For example:

अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते । उताश्विनावभरदत्तदासीदजहादु द्वा मिथुना सरण्यूः ॥ (*apāgūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇāmadadurvivasvate | utāśvināvabharadattadāsīdajahādu dvā mithunā saraṇyūḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-2)

When Saraṇyū, offered to Vivasvān in marriage, became invisible, the gods then offered to Vivasvān another woman of the same form. Since she also had the form of a mare, she bore the Aśvin deities, it says. In explaining this passage Sāyaṇa states: साश्वरूपिणी सरण्यूस्तदा अश्विनावभरत् (*sāśvarūpiṇī saraṇyūstadā aśvināvabharat*), that is, that Saraṇyū herself, in the form of a mare, bore the Aśvins. In यमाचिदत्र यमसूरसूत (*yamācidatra yamasūrasūta*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-39-3) too, the description of the birth of the Yamas can be explained in the same way.

In the passage of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa cited earlier (7.2-1-10), the Yama and Yamī who are referred to as Agni and Earth are, as many authorities show, two parts of a single principle. In contexts that show the two limbs and their companionship, they also point to the origin of the creation of the universe.

### Printed p. 343

स वै नैव रेमे तस्मादेकाकी न रमते स द्वितीयमैच्छत् । स हैतावानास यथा स्त्रीपुमांसौ संपरिष्वक्तौ स इमानेवात्मानं द्वेधापातयत्ततः पतिश्च पत्नि चाभवतां तस्मादिदमर्धबृगलमिव स्व इति ह स्माह याज्ञवल्क्यस्तस्मादयमाकाशः स्त्रिया पूरृत एव तां समभवत्ततो मनुष्या अजायंत । (*sa vai naiva reme tasmādekākī na ramate sa dvitīyamaicchat | sa haitāvānāsa yathā strīpumāṃsau saṃpariṣvaktau sa imānevātmānaṃ dvedhāpātayattataḥ patiśca patni cābhavatāṃ tasmādidamardhabṛgalamiva sva iti ha smāha yājñavalkyastasmādayamākāśaḥ striyā pūrṛta eva tāṃ samabhavattato manuṣyā ajāyaṃta |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-3)

In the beginning there was only a single principle, of the nature of the universal Self. Thinking that without taking on many forms no experience of delight could arise, it wished to create another person for its companionship. This principle had the greatness of attaining the union of female and male. So it caused itself to divide into a female form and a male form. Then, as two divisions, wife and husband, the two entered the relation of a married couple. Therefore, as the sage Yājñavalkya said, though the world, which is of the nature of space, was pervaded by a single principle, human beings came into being as a result of its union with a woman.

So it would not be wrong to say that the two names Vivasvat and Saraṇyū are two parts of the primal principle that possesses this unity of the universe. In explaining the origin of man, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa expresses the same matter in this way:

यमु ह तद्विचक्रुः स विवस्वा नादित्यस्तस्येमाः प्रजाः । (*yamu ha tadvicakruḥ sa vivasvā nādityastasyemāḥ prajāḥ |*) (Ka. Citra. 3. 1-4) **NOTE**

This part, formed before the creation of the universe, is the Āditya principle known by the name Vivasvān. From this Āditya named Vivasvat arises the origin of all beings. The Ṛksaṃhitā too explains this very thing:

अमी ये सप्त रश्मयस्तत्रा मे नाभिरातता (*amī ye sapta raśmayastatrā me nābhirātatā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-9)

The Taittirīya Saṃhitā also reads ततो विवस्वा नादित्योऽजायत (*tato vivasvā nādityo 'jāyata*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-6-2). (These details will be given later, when the hymns describing the order of the creation of the universe are examined.)

Above, in indicating Yama's place, contexts stating an identity of Āditya and Yama have been explained. In the present matter, all the names Vivasvān, Āditya and Yama are, in one way or another, different names of one and the same principle, or stand in the relation of cause and effect, and so

### Printed p. 344

…can be stated precisely on the strength of the Saṃhitā passages. This one principle is described in the verses of the Ṛk-saṃhitā in the following way.

यमेन दत्तं त्रित एनमायुनगिंद्र एणं प्रथमो अध्यतिष्ठत् । गंधर्वो अस्य रशनामगृभ्वात्सूरादश्वं वसवो निरतष्ट ॥ असि यमो अस्यादित्यो अर्वन्नसि त्रितो गुह्येन व्रतेन । असि सोमेन समया विपृक्त आहुस्ते त्रीणि दिवि बंधनानि ॥ (*yamena dattaṃ trita enamāyunagiṃdra eṇaṃ prathamo adhyatiṣṭhat | gaṃdharvo asya raśanāmagṛbhvātsūrādaśvaṃ vasavo nirataṣṭa ‖ asi yamo asyādityo arvannasi trito guhyena vratena | asi somena samayā vipṛkta āhuste trīṇi divi baṃdhanāni ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-163-2,3)

The wind, which moves in the three places beginning with the earth, yoked to the chariot this horse given by Yama. Indra, the foremost, mounted this horse. King Soma took hold of the bridle of this horse. The sun's rays, or Yama and the others, obtained this horse from Āditya. In such descriptions, which say that this Agni is of Yama's form, of Āditya's form, and that he is of the nature of the wind, the identity of Agni and Yama is shown.

यमो यच्छतीति सतः (*yamo yacchatīti sataḥ*) । अग्निरपि यम उच्यते (*agnirapi yama ucyate*) (Ni. 10-19): because he has the power to restrain, the Nirukta author holds that "Yama" is a synonym of Agni as well. By citing the Ṛk यमो ह जातो यमो जनित्वं (*yamo ha jāto yamo janitvaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 66. 8) he has also shown that the word Yama is a synonym of Agni. In explaining the sense of the mantra 1-66-8, Sāyaṇa gave two kinds of meaning for the word Yama. One: यच्छति ददाति स्तोतृभ्यः कामानिति यमोऽग्निरुच्यते (*yacchati dadāti stotṛbhyaḥ kāmāniti yamo 'gnirucyate*)—Agni is called Yama because he gives to devotees the things they desire. The other: इंद्राग्नोर्युगपदुत्पन्नत्वादग्नेर्यमत्वं (*iṃdrāgnoryugapadutpannatvādagneryamatvaṃ*)—since Indra and Agni were born together, Agni is called Yama. The Nirukta author's sentence यमो ह जात इंद्रेण सह संगत्य (*yamo ha jāta iṃdreṇa saha saṃgatya*) supports this second meaning.

बळित्था महिमा वामिंद्राग्नी पनिष्ठ आ । समानो नां जनिता भ्रातरा युवं यमाविहेह मातरा । (*baḷitthā mahimā vāmiṃdrāgnī paniṣṭha ā | samāno nāṃ janitā bhrātarā yuvaṃ yamāviheha mātarā |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-59-2)

Here "युवं यमौ (*yuvaṃ yamau*)", "you two are born together", states the simultaneous birth of Indra and Agni; hence the second meaning can be maintained on this ground too.

The two principles Yama and Yamī also indicate the very two parts, in the form of female and male, of the primal principle whose nature the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad passage cited above describes.

### Printed p. 345

Although the word Yama thus indicates both the male and the female form, in the present context we must examine what the nature and influence of Yama, who is the male form, are. By sentences such as यमो नो गातुं प्रथमो विवेद (*yamo no gātuṃ prathamo viveda*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-2) it is said that Yama was the first to know the path of the Fathers and is king of the departed Fathers. Yama establishes the Fathers in the highest place, which no one can overthrow. Therefore:

पितृभिश्चांगिरोभिश्च संस्तुतो दृश्यते यमः । मंत्रेषु बहुशः पादे विवस्वंतं पिता हि सः ॥ (*pitṛbhiścāṃgirobhiśca saṃstuto dṛśyate yamaḥ | maṃtreṣu bahuśaḥ pāde vivasvaṃtaṃ pitā hi saḥ ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 6-157)

Yama is praised in many ways together with the Fathers and the Aṅgirases. In the mantra विवस्वंतं (*vivasvaṃtaṃ*) he himself is regarded as a father, it says. And further:

संस्कार्यप्रेतसंयुक्तैः पितृभिःस्तूयते यमः । प्रेहि प्रेहीति तिसृषु प्रेताशिष उदाहृताः ॥ पितृणां हि पतिर्देवो यमस्तस्मात्स सूक्तभाक् । (*saṃskāryapretasaṃyuktaiḥ pitṛbhiḥstūyate yamaḥ | prehi prehīti tisṛṣu pretāśiṣa udāhṛtāḥ ‖ pitṛṇāṃ hi patirdevo yamastasmātsa sūktabhāk |*)
(Bṛ. De. 6-158-9)

Yama, united with the Fathers, is praised together with the deceased who is entitled to the funeral rites. This praise is in the three mantras beginning प्रेहि प्रेहि (*prehi prehi*) (10-14-7,8,9). This same Yama is lord of all the Fathers; therefore Yama is said to be a "सूक्तभाक् (*sūktabhāk*)" (partaker of hymns). One may examine closely what aspect of Yama the epithet "सूक्तभाक् (*sūktabhāk*)" here indicates.

The Nirukta author has divided the deities into three: those of the earth, of the atmosphere, and of the heaven. But that division has certain shortcomings; a discussion of that matter is out of place in this context. Like this division, the deities can be made into two divisions, हविर्भाजः (*havirbhājaḥ*) and सूक्तभाजः (*sūktabhājaḥ*): that is, those who partake of oblations (or Soma), and those who partake of hymns.

मातली कव्यैरमो अंगिरोभिर्बृहस्पतिर्युक्वभिर्वावृधानः । याश्च देवा वावृधुर्ये च देवान्त्स्वाहाने स्वधयान्ये मदंति ॥ (*mātalī kavyairamo aṃgirobhirbṛhaspatiryukvabhirvāvṛdhānaḥ | yāśca devā vāvṛdhurye ca devāntsvāhāne svadhayānye madaṃti ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-3)

### Printed p. 346

In mantras such as this, the groups of gods and the Fathers who are satisfied by kavya, ṛk, svāhā, svadhā and so on are specified. The number of deities and of Fathers belonging to these divisions will be discussed elsewhere. Here we need only know what Yama's place is. Yama is described as belonging to the company of the Fathers and as lord of the Fathers. These Fathers too are divided into three.

उदीरतामवर उत्परास उन्मध्यमाः पितरः सोम्यासः । (*udīratāmavara utparāsa unmadhyamāḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.15-1)

Among the Fathers there are three divisions: those of the lower world, of the higher world and of the middle world. Yama is regarded as dwelling in the atmosphere. Like the Fathers of the middle world, he receives the svadhā. But according to the Nirukta's classification Yama belongs both to the group of gods who dwell in heaven and to the atmospheric world. (The divisions सूक्तभाजः (*sūktabhājaḥ*), हविर्भाजः (*havirbhājaḥ*) and निपातभाजः (*nipātabhājaḥ*) according to the Nirukta are given at the end of this introduction.) If the question arises how one Yama can belong to both groups, Yāska and Durgācārya explain it thus. (Nirukta 12-29, Durgācārya's commentary.)

Yama, who is praised in the atmosphere, that is, in the middle world, is the presiding deity of the Fathers; and Yama, who is praised as dwelling in heaven, is of the form of Āditya. It cannot be said that this explanation is inadequate because it states two opposed aspects of one Yama. One may freely say that two aspects of one principle pervade the two worlds. Moreover, this is also the basis for saying that Yama, who belongs to the group of Fathers, is superior to the Fathers; the meaning is that Yama is better than the Fathers belonging to the middle world alone. Epithets such as संगमनं जनानां (*saṃgamanaṃ janānāṃ*) indicate this point.

The fact that Yama is a Soma-drinker, in the sentence cited earlier,

यस्मिन्वलक्ष्मी सुपलाशे देवैः संपिबते यमते (*yasminvalakṣmī supalāśe devaiḥ saṃpibate yamate*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-135-1)

also supports this.

उभा राजाना स्वधया मदंता यमं पश्यासि वरुणं च देवं (*ubhā rājānā svadhayā madaṃtā yamaṃ paśyāsi varuṇaṃ ca devaṃ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-2)

### Printed p. 347

In places such as this, the description of Yama and Varuṇa as lords who enjoy equal delight shows Yama's divinity. Like Yama, Varuṇa too belongs both to heaven and to the atmosphere. But since it is said that Yama of heaven is a Soma-drinker, while Varuṇa of heaven is worthy of hymns, it is understood that Varuṇa's position is higher than Yama's. However, it may be said that descriptions showing such different aspects point to different powers of Yama.

Yama is the power that governs the universe. That power regulates the morality of the whole world. It pervades the three worlds. This power, pervading the three worlds, may be called Āditya or Agni. The sentences showing the identity of Yama and the all-pervading Āditya were cited earlier. Sentences such as केशीदं ज्योतिरुच्यते (*keśīdaṃ jyotirucyate*) state the luminous form of Yama, who is of Āditya's form. The word विवस्वान् (*vivasvān*) too, derived from the root वस् (*vas*), shows the very same power which the sentence ईशावास्यं (*īśāvāsyaṃ*) shows as all-pervading. Agni, who pervades the three worlds, is also a transformation of this Yama. The Nirukta author also says अग्निरपि यम उच्यते (*agnirapi yama ucyate*) (Ni. 10,20); and the Bṛhaddevatā author likewise:

इह प्रजाः प्रयच्छन् स संगृहीत्वा प्रयाति च । ऋषिर्विवस्वतः पुत्रं तेनाहैनं यमो यमं ॥ (*iha prajāḥ prayacchan sa saṃgṛhītvā prayāti ca | ṛṣirvivasvataḥ putraṃ tenāhainaṃ yamo yamaṃ ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 2-48)

Here it is shown that, because Agni gives sons and the like and carries the oblations of this world to other worlds and distributes them, he too is designated by the name Yama. यमो यच्छतीति सतः (*yamo yacchatīti sataḥ*) (Ni. 10-19): "he gives"—to whom, and where? In the form of Agni he distributes in all three worlds to the Fathers, the gods and the Asuras. How? Thus—

पितृदेवासुराणां च अभवन्नग्नयस्त्रयः । हव्यकव्यवहौ चोभौ सहरक्षाश्च नाम यः ॥ (*pitṛdevāsurāṇāṃ ca abhavannagnayastrayaḥ | havyakavyavahau cobhau saharakṣāśca nāma yaḥ ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 6-160)

In relation to these three groups, the Fathers, the gods and the Asuras, Agni has three forms: the Agni who carries havya and kavya, and Saharakṣas—three divisions.

Thus it can be said that the name is famous because the word Yama has the meanings "he gives" and "he restrains", and because the principle designated by the word Yama performs all these functions through its transformations.

### Printed p. 348

Yama is the one who first extended that sacrifice which is famed in the Saṃhitās and elsewhere as the source and the regulator of the creation and the maintenance of the universe. It has been said above that Yama was the first to behold directly (10-51-1-4) Agni, who is the source and the manager of the sacrifice. It has also been said above that Yama, of Agni's form, is the cause of the condition and fortunes of the gods, the Fathers and others. Likewise, Yama is the cause of the extension of the sacrifice, which is the source and the impeller of all the affairs of the universe.

त इन्निण्यं हृदयस्य प्रकेतैः सहस्रवल्यमभि सं चरंति । यमेन ततं परिधिं वयंतोऽप्सरस उप सेदुर्वनिष्ठाः ॥ (*ta inniṇyaṃ hṛdayasya praketaiḥ sahasravalyamabhi saṃ caraṃti | yamena tataṃ paridhiṃ vayaṃto 'psarasa upa sedurvaniṣṭhāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7.33-9)

This matter is stated in sentences such as this. In such contexts Sāyaṇa has explained the word Yama as the Supreme Self, the controller of all and the causal soul of the whole universe. (विश्वनियंत्रा कारणात्मना विस्तृतं परिधिं । परिधिरित्यनेन जन्मादिप्रवाहो विवक्षितः । (*viśvaniyaṃtrā kāraṇātmanā vistṛtaṃ paridhiṃ | paridhirityanena janmādipravāho vivakṣitaḥ |*)) Moreover,

श्री कद्रु केभिः पतति हळुर्विरेकमिद्वहत् । त्रिष्टुब्जायत्री छंदांसि सर्वा याम अहिता ॥ (*śrī kadru kebhiḥ patati haḷurvirekamidvahat | triṣṭubjāyatrī chaṃdāṃsi sarvā yāma ahitā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-16)

By sentences such as this the principle of Yama as the source of sacrifice is established. In these contexts the seven metres beginning with Gāyatrī, which are the means of carrying out the sacrifice, are praised as established in Yama himself. Many such contexts also show Yama's governance of all the deities. Sentences such as देवेभ्यः कमवृणीत........ यमस्तन्वं प्रारिरेचीत् (*devebhyaḥ kamavṛṇīta........ yamastanvaṃ prārirecīt*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-13-4) also describe Yama's universal power.

Thus the Saṃhitā sentences themselves declare that the principle expressed by the word Yama regulates and carries out all three: the creation, maintenance and dissolution of the world. In the Purāṇas and elsewhere Yama is described only as a deity who is the agent of dissolution, who gives the dead the fruit suited to their deeds, and who is a terrible punisher of the cruel. But the Ṛk-saṃhitā sentences, and the Upaniṣad sentences, praise Yama's omnipotence and his governance of all in the following way.

तमंतरामिणं य इमं च लोकं परं च लोकं सर्वाणि च भूतानि येऽंतरो यमयतीति सोऽब्रवीत्पतंजलः काप्यो नाहं तं भगवन्वेदेति सोऽब्रवीत्पतंजलं काप्यं याज्ञिकांश्च यो वै तत्काप्य अ. ७. अ. ६. व. ६ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 3-19 सूत्रं विद्यात्तं चांतर्यामिणमिति ................... (*tamaṃtarāmiṇaṃ ya imaṃ ca lokaṃ paraṃ ca lokaṃ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni ye 'ṃtaro yamayatīti so 'bravītpataṃjalaḥ kāpyo nāhaṃ taṃ bhagavanvedeti so 'bravītpataṃjalaṃ kāpyaṃ yājñikāṃśca yo vai tatkāpya a. 7. a. 6. va. 6 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 3-19 sūtraṃ vidyāttaṃ cāṃtaryāmiṇamiti ...................*) …… वेद वा अहं तत्सूत्रं तं चांतर्यामिणमिति (*veda vā ahaṃ tatsūtraṃ taṃ cāṃtaryāmiṇamiti*) ……
(Bṛ. U. 7-7-1)

### Printed p. 349

Uddālaka Āruṇi tells Yājñavalkya the question which the Gandharva, who had seized the wife of Patañjala Kāpya, put to the sacrificers assembled in Kāpya's house, and expects an answer to that question from Yājñavalkya. The question is: "O sacrificers, which is that governing power, the universe-controller, that governs this world, all worlds and all beings?" When this question asked by the Gandharva is told to Yājñavalkya, he explains the nature of that power in the following way.

This power governs both the universe in its divine aspect and the universe in its personal (spiritual) aspect. How? Thus—

यः पृथिव्यां तिष्ठन् पृथिव्या अंतरो .... .... .... यः पृथिवीमंतरो यमयत्येष त आत्मांतर्याम्यमृतः ॥३॥ .... .... .... .... अपोऽंतरो यमयति .... .... .... .... ॥४॥ योऽग्नौ तिष्ठन्........ अग्निमंतरो यमयति ॥ ५ ॥ (इ. ७. २-१४) ई विश्वनियामक तत्त्ववु, पृथिवी, अप्पु, अग्नि, अंतरिक्ष, वायु, द्युलोक, सूर‍्य, दिक्कुगळु, चंद्र, आकाश, अंधकार, तेजस्सु इत्यादि सकल जगत्तिनल्लियू व्यापिसिरुत्तदॆ. अवुगळल्लि अंतरामि यागिद्दुकॊंडु अवुगळ व्यवहारगळन्नु नियमिसुत्तदॆ. इदे विश्वात्मा ऎंदु ई नियामक शक्तिय आधिदैविक शक्तियन्नु तिळिसि, नंतर, यः सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन् सर्वेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो .... .... यः सर्वाणि भूतान्यंतरो यमयति .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... एष त आत्मांतर्याम्यमृतो (*yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā aṃtaro .... .... .... yaḥ pṛthivīmaṃtaro yamayatyeṣa ta ātmāṃtaryāmyamṛtaḥ ‖3‖ .... .... .... .... apo 'ṃtaro yamayati .... .... .... .... ‖4‖ yo 'gnau tiṣṭhan........ agnimaṃtaro yamayati ‖ 5 ‖ (i. 7. 2-14) ī viśvaniyāmaka tattvavu, pṛthivī, appu, agni, aṃtarikṣa, vāyu, dyuloka, sūrya, dikkugaḷu, caṃdra, ākāśa, aṃdhakāra, tejassu ityādi sakala jagattinalliyū vyāpisiruttadè. avugaḷalli aṃtarāmi yāgiddukòṃḍu avugaḷa vyavahāragaḷannu niyamisuttadè. ide viśvātmā èṃdu ī niyāmaka śaktiya ādhidaivika śaktiyannu tiḷisi, naṃtara, yaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo .... .... yaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtānyaṃtaro yamayati .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... eṣa ta ātmāṃtaryāmyamṛto*) ॥3॥
…… अपोऽंतरो यमयति (*apo 'ṃtaro yamayati*) …… ॥4॥
योऽग्नौ तिष्ठन् (*yo 'gnau tiṣṭhan*) …… अग्निमंतरो यमयति (*agnimaṃtaro yamayati*) ॥5॥
(Bṛ. U. 7. 2-14)

This universe-governing principle pervades the whole world: earth, waters, fire, atmosphere, wind, heaven, sun, the directions, moon, space, darkness, light and so on. Being the inner controller in them, it regulates their functioning. "This is the universal Self"—having thus stated the divine power of this governing power, he then says:

यः सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन् सर्वेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो .... .... यः सर्वाणि भूतान्यंतरो यमयति .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... एष त आत्मांतर्याम्यमृतोऽदृष्टः .... .... ॥ (*yaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo .... .... yaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtānyaṃtaro yamayati .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... eṣa ta ātmāṃtaryāmyamṛto 'dṛṣṭaḥ .... .... ‖*) ……
(Bṛ. U. 15-23)

In the same way Yājñavalkya explains that this power is the inner controller and the governing power of the whole personal world: breath, speech, eye, ear, mind and so on. The glorification of Yama, of Āditya's form, which is made by sentences such as इदं यमस्य सादनं (*idaṃ yamasya sādanaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-135-7), is found in these Upaniṣad sentences too.

Some descriptions found in the Ṛks concerning Yama

Yama is the leader of all the righteous among the dead. Since the Vedas pay little attention to the world beyond, Yama is praised in only three hymns (10-14; 135;

### Printed p. 350

154). In another (10-10) there is a dialogue between Yama and his sister Yamī. Yama's name occurs about fifty times, generally in the first and tenth maṇḍalas, and especially in the tenth maṇḍala.

He is engaged in sport with the gods (7-76-4; 10-135-1). He is mentioned together with Varuṇa (10-14-7), Bṛhaspati (10-13-4; 10-14-3), and especially Agni, who conveys the departed souls to other worlds. Agni is Yama's friend (10-21-5) and priest (10-52-3). A certain god and Yama (the two are suggested to be the same) together discovered Agni, who had hidden in the waters (10-51-3). Agni, Yama and Mātariśvan are the names of one being (1-164-16). Yama is included in the lists of deities beginning with Agni (10-64-3; 10-92-11).

From the sentences stated above it may be inferred that Yama too is a deity. He is not expressly called a deity; he is said to be king of the dead (यमराज्ञः (*yamarājñaḥ*) 10-16-9). After death, what the soul sees is these two, Yama and the god Varuṇa (10-14-7). A whole hymn (10-14) speaks of the relation between Yama and the Fathers, and in it especially of the Aṅgirases. Yama comes to the sacrifice with them and rejoices (10-14-3, 4; 10-15-8). His horses, with eyes like gold and hooves of iron, are mentioned (Tai. A. 6-5-2; Āpa. Śau. Sū. 16-6). He is the one who gathers all people together (10-14-1), provides the dead with a resting place (10-14-9; Ath. Saṃ. 18-2-37) and prepares for them a separate dwelling (10-18-13). **NOTE**

Yama's place is in a corner of the sky (9-113-8). Of the three heavens, two belong to Savitṛ and one to Yama (1-35-6; compare 1-123-6); Yama's world is the third and the highest. In the Vājasaneya Saṃhitā (12-63) it is said that Yama, together with Yamī, dwells in heaven at this final height. In this place of his—which is also the place of the gods—the sound of the flute and song are heard around Yama (10-135-7).

Soma juice is prepared for Yama; ghee is offered to him (10-14-13, 14); and there is a prayer that he come to the sacrificial hall and sit on the seat (10-14-4).

Vivasvant is said to be his father (10-14-5) and Saraṇu his mother (10-17-1). He is often called Vaivasvata (10-14-1; etc.). Since no one is superior to him, Yama is greater than Vivasvant (compare Ath. Saṃ. 18-2-32; 18-3-61, 62).

### Printed p. 351
In the dialogue of Yama and Yamī the two declare that they are children of a Gandharva and of the water-goddess (Apyā Yoṣā) (10-10-4). Yamī says that Yama alone is mortal (10-10-3). It is stated that Yama gave up his body and chose death itself (10-13-4). He went to the other world, showing the way to the many who would come after; the ancient Pitṛs too have gone there (10-14-1 **NOTE**, 2). He is the first of all mortals who have died (Ath. Saṃ. 18-3-13). **NOTE**. Here "mortals" must mean human beings; but in some other contexts the gods too are meant by the word *marta*. Since Yama was the first of the dead and is very ancient, it is natural that he should be called lord of them all. He has the epithets *viśpati* (lord of all who have settled) and "our father" (10-135-1). It is through Yama that all human beings later received the name "descendants of Vivasvān Āditya" (Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-6-2; Śa. Brā. 3-1-3-4; compare also Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-9). The "horse moving in the sky" given by Yama may be the place that Yama gives to those who are to become immortal (1-163-2; compare 1-83-5); in this way a connection between Yama and Āditya may be said to be stated in the Ṛgveda also.

Death is Yama's path (1-38-5), and once (1-165-4; compare Mai. Saṃ. 2-5-6 and Ath. Saṃ. 6-28-31 and 6-93-1) he himself is called death. The fetters that Yama uses are likened to Varuṇa's noose (10-97-16). From such passages and from the characteristics of his messengers, Yama may seem terrible. Because the Atharvaveda and other Vedic narratives say that death and the sufferings after death are caused by Yama, Yama is regarded as the god of death. But even in the Purāṇas it is clear that hell is not Yama's only realm. In the other Saṃhitās too Yama is one of the list Antaka, Mṛtyu, Nirṛti (disease) (Vā. Saṃ. 39-13; Ath. Saṃ. 6-29-3; Mai. Saṃ. 2-5-6), and Mṛtyu is his messenger (Ath. Saṃ. 5-30-1 **NOTE**, 2; 18-2-27; etc.). It is said that Mṛtyu is lord of men and Yama lord of the departed (Ath. Saṃ. 5-24-13, 14), and that Sleep (the presiding goddess of sleep) comes from Yama's realm (Ath. Saṃ. 19-56-1).

The word *yama* is also used in the sense "twin", ordinarily in the masculine or feminine dual; and the word is also used in the sense "rein" or "guide". Yama and Yamī are conceived as twins (10-10). In other works, where Yama is described as god of death, punisher of the wicked and so on, it is held that the word is derived from the root *yam* (to keep under control), but it may be said that the Vedas give no support at all for this.

The Bṛhaddevatā, showing the division of the deities as those of the uktamantra and as oblation-sharers, states it thus:

> सप्तर्षयो वसवश्चापि देवा अथर्वाणो भृगवः सोमसूर्याः ।
> पथ्या स्वस्ति रोदसी चोक्तमंत्रे कुहूर्गुंगूरदितिर्धेनुरघ्न्या ॥
> असुनीतिरिळा चाप्त्या विधातानुमतिर्ह या ।
> अंगिरोभिः सहैताः स्युरुक्तमंत्राश्च देवताः ॥

That is: the seven sages, the Vasus, the gods, the Atharvans, the Bhṛgus, Soma, Sūrya, Sūrā, Pathyā, Svastī, Rodasī, Kuhū, Gungū, Aditi, Dhenu, Aghnyā, Asunīti, Iḷā, Āptyā, Anumati and the Aṅgirases.

> वैश्वानरो हि सुपर्णो विवस्वान् प्रजापतिर्दौः सुधन्वा नगोह्यः ।
> अपांनपादरमा वातजूतिरिळस्पतिश्चा पि रथस्पतिश्च ॥
> ऋभवः पर्जन्यः पर्वता ग्नाश्च दक्षो भगो देवपत्नीर्दितश्च ।
> आदित्या रुद्राः पितरोऽथ साध्या निपातिनो वैश्वदेवेषु सर्वे ॥

Vaiśvānara, Suparṇa, Vivasvān and the like are oblation-sharers. The nipāta-sharers too are included here.

**NOTE**

The dialogue between Yama and Yamī, held for the sake of sexual union.

In this dialogue the separate explanation of the words and the order of construction are not set out in difficult words; only the main substance of the conversation is given:

(1) Yamī speaks to Yama: O Yama, this island in the midst of the sea, though wide, is uninhabited, that is, a secret place. Since the time in the womb, that is, since our birth, we two have grown up together and are friends. Therefore I now, casting off the shame natural to a woman

### Printed p. 354
wish to enter with you into the union natural between woman and man, that is, sexual union. As a result of the union, may the Creator Prajāpati cause a conception in me, so that a son endowed with all good qualities, born to us both, may be born in my womb.

(2) Yama: O Yamī, although I have grown up with you since the womb and am friendly with you, I do not wish with you the union fitting between woman and man. We two are of one womb, that is, born and grown in the womb of one mother. In many respects we have like qualities. But since you are my sister, I do not desire intercourse with you. For the gods, sons of Prajāpati or Brahmā, heroes and dwellers in heaven, have declared this act, namely sexual union of brother and sister, to be forbidden.

(3) Yamī: O Yama, never think so. There are many examples of even the gods being attached to unions declared forbidden in the śāstras and the like. Did not Prajāpati, the Creator, himself become attached to his own daughter and enjoy union with her? The cause of all this is our mind. I love you wholeheartedly, and there is no doubt that you too love me. Therefore, as Prajāpati formerly had union with his daughter, you too enter me, that is, have union with me as my husband and give me pleasure.

(4) Yama: O Yamī, what the all-powerful Prajāpati did formerly we cannot do now. Until now we two have spoken only truth and have followed the path of right. We have done no forbidden act such as intercourse with a forbidden woman. Āditya, who dwells in the sky, and his wife the goddess Saraṇyū are our father and mother. Can we, sons of such parents, revered by the world, commit the forbidden act of intercourse with a forbidden woman? The relation between us is the excellent relation proper between brother and sister, not the relation of love proper between husband and wife.

(5-7) Yamī: O Yama, Tvaṣṭṛ Prajāpati, who gives to all living beings their natural forms and the like and thus regulates them, made us two grow in one womb and ordained from the time in the womb that we two should be husband and wife. No one is able to transgress this command, which is the ordinance of this all-powerful Prajāpati. Therefore, in accordance with Prajāpati's ordinance, let us live as husband and wife and enjoy pleasure in union. Heaven and Earth, the parents of the whole world, also know this relation of husband and wife that arose for us in our mother's womb.

### Printed p. 355
(6) Who will learn of the union of this first day, taking place today? This is a secret place. No one is here. Who will see our union taking place here? And how would it become known to others? The days and nights (time), the abode of Mitra and Varuṇa, are very wide; and for all the sinful and meritorious acts performed by human and other beings, the power to grant hell or heaven according to each one's deed belongs to you, Yama the king. Why should you, who have such power, be afraid? What will you say in this matter?

(7) O Yama, let desire for me arise in you. Lying together on one bed, let us enjoy the pleasure of union like husband and wife. Then, as the duty a wife must follow, I, eager for love-making, will offer my body to you with the greatest love. Afterwards, as the two wheels of a chariot carry the chariot by one and the same motion, let us two, enjoying pleasure and delight like husband and wife, fulfil dharma, artha and kāma.

(8-10) Yama: O Yamī, in this world too, spies appointed by the gods go about watching the good and bad deeds of all beings by day and night. They move about without rest even for a moment. They do not close their eyes even for a minute. They surely see the good and bad deeds we do. Therefore, O woman intent on sinful deeds, do not henceforth torment me with your shameful talk. Go far away. Unite with another man who will help you in your sinful deed, and, as you say, fulfil dharma, artha and kāma like the wheels of a chariot.

(9) May the sacrificer who performs sacrifice at night and by day offer Yama his share of the oblation in the sacrifice. May the Sun rise each day for the very satisfaction of Yama. May Day and Night, kin to each other, together with Heaven and Earth, co-operate for Yama's happiness. Let this Yamī choose another man, not her brother.

(10) O Yamī, a time will come when sisters will choose their own brothers and make them their husbands. O beautiful one, therefore give up desiring me and accept as husband another handsome man, different from me. Making your arm the pillow for the man who fulfils your desire, at the time of lying down, sport with him as you wish and give him pleasure.

(11) Yamī: O Yama, when there is a brother, and his sister, fallen into trouble, laments like one without protector, is a brother who pays no heed to it truly a brother? In the same way,

### Printed p. 356
is a sister who, having a brother, does not relieve his sorrow truly a sister? Never. Overcome by desire and tormented by it, I am entreating you in many ways for satisfaction of my desire. Join your body with mine and enjoy pleasure in union.

(12) Yama: O Yamī, I do not wish, as you say, to join my body with yours and have union with you. If a brother becomes attached to his own younger sister and has union with her, good people who know proper conduct call him a great sinner. Therefore, O beautiful one, leave me and enjoy the pleasures and delights of union with another handsome young man suitable for you. This Yama, your brother, does not wish to have union with you.

(13) Yamī: O Yama, you are very weak (foolish). This is very hard. None of us can understand your mind, what is in your mind. As a horse clasps the rope that binds it, and as creepers encircle and embrace a tree, how shall I bear to see another woman embrace you, the beautiful one, with love?

(14) Yama: O Yamī, leave me and embrace another man. Let him too embrace you. As a creeper clasps the tree that is its support, may you two embrace each other and be happy. Act according to that man's wish. Let that man too, acting according to your mind, enjoy the pleasure of union with you, fair of limb.

Regarding the muttering (japa) of this sūkta, the great sage Śaunaka in the work called Ṛgvidhāna has said as follows:

> उपतिष्ठेत राजानं यमं सूक्तेन वै द्विजः ।

The twice-born should pray to Yama Dharmarāja reciting this sūkta. Then, in both the bright and dark fortnights, on the eighth and fourteenth tithis, he should perform a homa with mantras, according to the sthālīpāka procedure, in the consecrated fire, addressed to Yama.

> अष्टम्यां च चतुर्दश्यां यजेत हविषा यमं ॥

> पुरायुषः प्रमीयेत न जातु स कथंचन ।
> प्रीयतेऽस्य यमो राजा स्मृतिं चांते प्रयच्छति ॥ ३७ ॥

(…) "To Dharmarāja, svāhā," saying this at the end of the mantra, he should offer the oblation. On the full-moon day of Vaiśākha he should always perform this rite. धर्मराजाय स्वाहेति मंत्रांते जुहायद्धविः । वैशाख्यां पौर्णमास्यां तु कर्म नित्यं प्रयोजयेत् ॥ (*dharmarājāya svāheti maṃtrāṃte juhāyaddhaviḥ | vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu karma nityaṃ prayojayet ‖*) 38 ॥

At the time of this homa the mantras of the sūkta beginning परेयिवांसं (*pareyivāṃsaṃ*) (Maṇḍala 10, sūkta 18) are to be recited while the offering is made. If this is done, death will not befall him before the span of his life is complete; that is, he will live for a hundred years, the full life of a man. By this homa Yamarāja is pleased, and at the time of that man's death he will not lose his memory but will remain conscious to the end. At the end of every mantra "धर्मराजाय स्वाहा (*dharmarājāya svāhā*)" is to be added when offering. This homa rite is to be performed chiefly on the full-moon day of the month of Vaiśākha.

अयने पर्वसु स्नात्वा यः प्रदद्यात्तिलोदकं । यमाय सगणाय्कॆव तद्भयं न स विंदते ॥ (*ayane parvasu snātvā yaḥ pradadyāttilodakaṃ | yamāya sagaṇāykèva tadbhayaṃ na sa viṃdate ‖*) 39 ॥ (Ṛgvidhāna, chapter 3)

The man who, at the times of the northern and southern solstices and at the parvan times, bathes and offers tarpaṇa with tiloda­ka (water with sesame) to Yamarāja together with his retinue, has no fear whatever from Yama.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ओ चिदिति चतुर्दशर्चं दशमं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रम्यते ॥ ओ चित् षळूना
> वैवस्वतयोर्यमयव्योः संवादः षष्ठ्ययुग्भिर्यमी मिथुनार्थं यमं
> प्रोवाच स तां नवमियुग्निरनिच्छन् प्रत्याचष्ट इति । ततः षष्ठ्यां प्रथमातृतीयाद्ययुक्षु विवस्वतः पुत्रि यम्यृषिर्यमो देवता । यस्य वाक्यं स ऋषिया
> तेनोच्यते सा देवतेति न्यायात् । तथा नवम्यां द्वितीयाचतुर्थिप्रभृतिषु
> युक्षु वैवस्वतो यम ऋषियमी देवता । अनादेशपरिभाषया त्रिष्टुप् ॥
> गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This tenth sūkta has fourteen ṛks. The Anukramaṇī says: ओ चित् षळूना वैवस्वतयोर्यमयव्योः संवादः षष्ठ्ययुग्भिर्यमी मिथुनार्थं यमं प्रोवाच स तां नवमियुग्निरनिच्छन् प्रत्याचष्ट इति । (*o cit ṣaḷūnā vaivasvatayoryamayavyoḥ saṃvādaḥ ṣaṣṭhyayugbhiryamī mithunārthaṃ yamaṃ provāca sa tāṃ navamiyugniranicchan pratyācaṣṭa iti |*). It is a dialogue between Yama and Yamī, the children of Vivasvat. In the even-numbered verses (the sixth being counted with the odd) Yamī, in the first, third and other odd verses, addresses Yama for the sake of union, and he in the ninth and the even verses refuses. Thus in the sixth verse and the odd verses beginning with the first, the daughter of Vivasvat, Yamī, is the seer and Yama the deity, by the maxim यस्य वाक्यं स ऋषिर्या तेनोच्यते सा देवता (*yasya vākyaṃ sa ṛṣiryā tenocyate sā devatā*) (the speaker of the words is the seer; the one addressed in them is the deity). Likewise in the ninth and the even verses beginning with the second and fourth, Yama, son of Vivasvat, is the seer and Yamī the deity. The metre is Triṣṭubh, by the general rule where no metre is stated. The viniyoga has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning ओ चित् (*o cit*) is the tenth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has fourteen ṛks. The Anukramaṇī says: ओ चित् षळूना वैवस्वतयोर्यमयम्योः संवादः षष्ठयुग्भिर्यमी मिथुनार्थं यमं प्रोवाच स तां नवमियुग्निरनिच्छन् प्रत्याचष्टे (*o cit ṣaḷūnā vaivasvatayoryamayamyoḥ saṃvādaḥ ṣaṣṭhayugbhiryamī mithunārthaṃ yamaṃ provāca sa tāṃ navamiyugniranicchan pratyācaṣṭe*). In this sūkta, between Yama, the son of Vivasvān,

### Printed p. 358
and his sister, the woman Yamī, there is a conversation for the sake of mutual union. Verses 1, 3, 5–7, 11, 13 are spoken by Yamī and verses 2, 4, 8–10, 12, 14 by Yama, each addressing the other. Therefore for the odd-numbered verses 1, 3 etc. and for the sixth verse, the woman Yamī Vaivasvatī is the seer and Yama is the deity. By the maxim "the one whose words they are is the seer; the one spoken of by them is the deity", whoever recites the words in a ṛk is its seer, and the subject set forth in the words is its deity. Accordingly, the odd verses 1, 3 etc. (omitting the ninth) and the sixth are spoken by the woman Yamī, so Yamī is their seer; in them Yama is the subject, so Yama is their deity. In the same way, for the even verses 2, 4 etc. (omitting the sixth) and for the odd ninth verse, Yama Vaivasvata is the seer and Yamī is the deity. The metre is Triṣṭubh. The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Sūkta 10
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 10.
Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 6; Vargas 6, 7, 8.
Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 14.
Seer: verses 1, 3, 5–7, 11, 13: Yamī Vaivasvatī; verses 2, 4, 8–10, 12, 14: Yama Vaivasvata.
Deity: verses 1, 3, 5–7, 11, 13: Yama Vaivasvata; verses 2, 4, 8–10, 12, 14: Yamī Vaivasvatī.
Metre: Triṣṭubh.

> इत्युक्तत्वात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In this sūkta a dialogue of Yama and Yamī, the children of Vivasvat, is told. In this ṛk Yamī speaks to Yama. तिरः (*tiraḥ*) means hidden, not shining, that is, a solitary place. Yamī has gone to पुरु चित् (*puru cit*), a very wide, part of the ocean, an island within it. चित् (*cit*) is in the sense of honour: the honoured, the beloved, the best. She says she turns (ववृत्यां (*vavṛtyāṃ*)) towards her friend Yama, who has been her companion since the womb, for सख्या (*sakhyā*), the friendship born of the union of woman and man: standing before him, giving up shame, she enjoys union with him, because by the maxim *dharmasya tvaritā gatiḥ* desire is hasty. Moreover, for the son who will be born, the father (Yama), अधि क्षमि (*adhi kṣami*), on the earth, that is, in her womb, which stands in the place of earth, प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*) excellent, endowed with all qualities, the नपातं (*napātaṃ*), offspring in the form of an embryo, may वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*), the creator Prajāpati, दीध्यानः (*dīdhyānaḥ*) reflecting on the birth of a son suited to the two of them, place it. This is because it is said: प्रजापतिर्धाता गर्भं दधातु ते (*prajāpatirdhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu te*), Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-184-1.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—to the solitary region
- पुरु चित् (*puru cit*)—and very wide
- अर्णवं (*arṇavaṃ*)—lying in the midst of the ocean, to that region
- जगन्वान् (*jaganvān*)—I have come
- चित् (*cit*)—the best
- सखायं (*sakhāyaṃ*)—and intimate Yama
- सख्या (*sakhyā*)—for gaining the love of us two
- ओ ववृत्यां (*o vavṛtyāṃ*)—I shall make him turn towards me
- वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*)—Prajāpati the creator
- दीध्यानः (*dīdhyānaḥ*)—having reflected fully
- पितुः (*pituḥ*)—for the child born of our (my and Yama's) relation
- अधि क्षमि (*adhi kṣami*)—in my womb, which stands in the place of earth
- प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*)—most excellent
- नपातं (*napātaṃ*)—the embryo
- आ दधीत (*ā dadhīta*)—may he place

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have come to this island, solitary, very wide, in the midst of the ocean. I shall make Yama, the best and my intimate, turn towards me for gaining the love of us both. May Prajāpati the creator, after full reflection, place the most excellent embryo in my womb, which stands in the place of earth, for the child that will be born of the relation between me and Yama.

##### English translation
(Yami speaks). I invite my friend to friendship, having come o'er vast and desert ocean ; may Vedhas, after reflecting, place in my womb the offspring (of you) the father, endowed with excellent qualities.

> यम आत्मानं परोक्षीकृत्य यमीं प्रत्युवाच । हे यमि ते तव सखा
> गर्भवासलक्षणेन सखीभूतो यम एतदीदृशं त्वयोक्तं स्त्रीपुरुषलक्षणं सख्यं
> न वष्टि । न कामयते। यद्यस्मात्कारणाद्यमी सलक्ष्मा समानयोनित्वलक्षणा विषुरूपा
> भगिनीत्वाद्विसमरूपा भवाति भवति । तस्मान्न वष्टीत्यर्थः । इदानीं तिरः पुरू
> चिदर्णवं जगन्वानित्यस्य प्रतिवचनमुच्यते । महो महतोऽसुरस्य प्राणवतः
> प्रज्ञावतो वा प्रजापतेः पुत्रासः पुत्रभूता वीराः । वीरो वीरयत्यमित्रान्वेतेन् स्याद्गतिकर्मणो वीरयतेन्वा । नि. १-७ । इति निरुक्तं । शत्रुणां विविधमीरयितारो धर्तारो धारयितारो दिवो द्युलोकस्य । प्रदर्शनमेतत् ।
> द्युप्रभृतीनां द्युलोकानामित्यर्थः ॥ .... .... .... ॥ [धर्तारः उर्विया उरवः मां
> परिचक्षते न कर्तव्यमिति वदंति]

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yama, speaking of himself in the third person, answers Yamī. O Yamī, your friend Yama, who has been your companion since the womb, does not desire एतत् (*etat*), this kind of friendship of woman and man which you have spoken of. The reason: Yamī is सलक्ष्मा (*salakṣmā*), of the same womb, and being a sister is विषुरूपा (*viṣurūpā*), of unlike form; therefore he does not desire it. Now the reply to "तिरः पुरू चिदर्णवं जगन्वान् (*tiraḥ purū cidarṇavaṃ jaganvān*)" is given. महः (*mahaḥ*): of the great असुरस्य (*asurasya*), Prajāpati, who has life or wisdom, the sons are वीराः (*vīrāḥ*). The Nirukta says: वीरो वीरयत्यमित्रान्वेतेन् स्याद्गतिकर्मणो वीरयतेन्वा (*vīro vīrayatyamitrānveten syādgatikarmaṇo vīrayatenvā*) (Ni. 1-7). They are scatterers of enemies in many ways, धर्तारः (*dhartāraḥ*) upholders of the heaven; this is an illustration: of the heavens beginning with Dyu. [Bracketed gloss: धर्तारः उर्विया उरवः मां परिचक्षते न कर्तव्यमिति वदंति (*dhartāraḥ urviyā uravaḥ māṃ paricakṣate na kartavyamiti vadaṃti*).]

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Yamī) यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- विषुरूपा (*viṣurūpā*)—you, who as a woman are of a form different from mine
- सलक्ष्मा भवाति (*salakṣmā bhavāti*)—are born in the same womb, therefore
- ते (*te*)—your
- सखा (*sakhā*)—I, your intimate
- एतत् (*etat*)—the kind of
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—relation indicated by you
- न वष्टि (*na vaṣṭi*)—do not desire
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of the great-souled
- असुरस्य (*asurasya*)—Prajāpati
- पुत्रासः (*putrāsaḥ*)—the sons
- वीराः (*vīrāḥ*)—the mighty
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- धर्तारः (*dhartāraḥ*)—the upholders
- उर्विया (*urviyā*)—and the exceedingly great, the gods
- परि ख्यन् (*pari khyan*)—speak as forbidding this act

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yamī, because you, being of a form different from mine (though a woman), are born in the same womb, I, your intimate, do not desire the relation indicated by you. The sons of the great-souled Prajāpati, the mighty ones, the upholders of the heavenly world, the exceedingly great gods, speak as forbidding this act.

### Printed p. 361

##### English translation
(Yama speaks). Your friend desires not this friendship, for although: of one origin, she is of different form; the hero sons of the great Asura (prajapati) the upholders of heaven, enjoying vast renown, do not permit this intercourse.

> नि ते॒ मनो॒ मन॑सि धाय्य॒स्मे जन्युः॒ पति॑स्त॒न्व१॒॑ १ मा वि॑विश्याः ॥
