> नि । ते । मनs । मनसि । धायि । अस्मेइति । जन्युः । पतिः । तन्नं । आ । विविश्याः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुनरपि यमा यमं प्रत्युवाच । घेति निपातोऽप्यर्थे । हे यम ते
> प्रसिद्धा अमृतासः प्रजापत्यादयोऽपि देवा एतदीदृशं शास्त्रेणागम्यत्वेनोक्तं
> त्यजसं । त्यज्यते परस्मै प्रदीयत इति त्यजसं दुहितृभगिन्यादिस्त्रीजातं । उशंति ।
> कामयंते । एकस्य चित् सर्वस्य जगतो मुख्यस्यापि प्रजापत्यादेः स्वदुहितृभगिन्यादीनां संबंधोऽस्तीति शेषः । अतः कारणात्ते तव मनश्चित्तमस्मे अस्माकं ।
> ममेत्यर्थः । मनसि चित्ते नि धायि । निधीयतां । अहं त्वां कामये त्वं मामपि
> कामयस्वत्यर्थः । अपि च । जन्युरिति लुप्तोपममेतत् । जन्युरिव यथा जनयिता
> प्रजापतिः पतिर्भर्ता भूत्वा स्वदुहितुः शरीरं संभोगेनाविष्टवान् तथा त्वमपि
> मम पतिर्भूत्वा तन्नं मदीयं शरीरमा विविश्याः । संभोगेनाविश । योन्ना
> प्रजननप्रक्षेपोपगूहनचुंबनादिना मां संभुक्षेत्रार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yamī again speaks to Yama. घ (*gha*) is a particle in the sense of "even". O Yama, those well-known immortals, even gods such as Prajāpati, उशंति (*uśaṃti*) desire this kind of त्यजसं (*tyajasaṃ*), which scripture declares impermissible; त्यजसं (*tyajasaṃ*) means what is given away to another (त्यज्यते परस्मै प्रदीयत (*tyajyate parasmai pradīyata*)), that is, the class of women such as daughter and sister. Even in the case of एकस्य चित् (*ekasya cit*), the chief of the whole world, Prajāpati and others, there is such a relation with their own daughters and sisters (this is the supplied remainder). Therefore let your mind be placed, नि धायि (*ni dhāyi*), in my mind: I desire you, and you too desire me. Further, जन्युः (*janyuḥ*) is an elided comparison: as the begetter Prajāpati, becoming husband, entered the body of his own daughter in union, so you also, becoming my husband, आ विविश्याः (*ā viviśyāḥ*), enter त्वं (*tvaṃ*), my body, in union; that is, enjoy me by the insertion of the generative organ, embracing, kissing and the like.

### Printed p. 362

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Yama) ते (*te*)—the well-known
- अमृतासः (*amṛtāsaḥ*)—even the gods
- एतत् (*etat*)—such
- त्यजसं (*tyajasaṃ*)—forbidden relation of sister and the like also
- उशंति (*uśaṃti*)—desire
- एकस्य चित् (*ekasya cit*)—in the case of Prajāpati, lord of the whole universe, too, such a relation is well known
- ते (*te*)—your
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind
- अस्मे (*asme*)—my
- मनसि (*manasi*)—with the mind
- नि धायि (*ni dhāyi*)—let it be made one
- जन्युः (*janyuḥ*)—as Prajāpati, the begetter of all, becoming husband to his daughter gave happiness to her body, so
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—my body
- आ विविश्याः (*ā viviśyāḥ*)—entering, make it joyful

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yama, even the well-known gods desire such a forbidden relation as that of sister and the like. Such a relation is well known in the case of Prajāpati, lord of the whole universe. Let your mind become one with my mind. As Prajāpati, the begetter of all, becoming husband to his daughter, gave happiness to her body, so enter my body and make it joyful.

##### English translation
(Yami speaks). Even the immortals take pleasure in (a union) like this which is forbidden to every mortal; let your mind then concur with mine, and as prajapati the progenitor (of all) was the husband (of his own daughter), so you enjoy my person.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this ṛk, while Yamī urges Yama to unite with her, Yama says that union between brother and sister is forbidden. In reply Yamī says: the gods themselves have done many such forbidden acts; why should we not? There is no fault in it. Did not Prajāpati the creator, in the past, become infatuated with his own daughter and sport with her? Thus she cites as example the improper act done by the gods. Therefore it is necessary here to indicate the story told of Prajāpati's delighting in his own daughter. This matter is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, chapter 13, eighth khaṇḍa, and we explain it here:

प्रजापतिर्वै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यध्यायद्दिवमित्यन्य आहुरुषसमित्यन्ये तामृ शोभूत्वा रोहितं भूतामभ्यैत्तं देवा अपश्यन्नकृतं वै प्रजापतिः करोतीति ते तम्मैच्छन्य एनमारिष्यत्येशमन्योन्यस्मिन्नाविंदंस्तेषां या (*prajāpatirvai svāṃ duhitaramabhyadhyāyaddivamityanya āhuruṣasamityanye tāmṛ śobhūtvā rohitaṃ bhūtāmabhyaittaṃ devā apaśyannakṛtaṃ vai prajāpatiḥ karotīti te tammaicchanya enamāriṣyatyeśamanyonyasminnāviṃdaṃsteṣāṃ yā*)

### Printed p. 363

एव घोरतमास्तन्न आसंस्ता एकधा समभरंस्ताः संभृता एष देवोऽभवत्तदस्यैतद्भूतवन्नाम भवति वै स योऽस्यैतदेवं नाम वेद ॥ (*eva ghoratamāstanna āsaṃstā ekadhā samabharaṃstāḥ saṃbhṛtā eṣa devo 'bhavattadasyaitadbhūtavannāma bhavati vai sa yo 'syaitadevaṃ nāma veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-33)

In former times Prajāpati, the creator, looked on his own daughter with desire and set his mind on taking his pleasure with her. There is a difference of opinion as to who this daughter was. Some seers say she was the deity presiding over the heavenly world, others that she was Uṣas. Be that as it may. Then Prajāpati took the form of a kind of deer with spots, called ṛśya. The daughter took the form of a red-coloured doe. Then Prajāpati sported with her in the act of union. The gods saw Prajāpati engaged in this evil act and said to one another: "This Prajāpati, the creator himself, is doing such a deed, forbidden by all. We must stop him and punish him suitably." They resolved this and questioned each of them in turn as to who among them was able to do the deed boldly. They found that none of them was so able. They therefore all joined and devised a plan. All those among the gods who were the most fierce, that is, of terrible form, gathered their several terrible forms into one and made a single figure. They saw that it was a man of very fearsome appearance and called him Rudra. Because the body of this Rudra was fearful, with the form of a bhūta, he was also named Bhūtavān, that is, lord of beings (bhūtapati). One who knows this becomes bhūtimān, that is, a man of wealth.

तं देवा अब्रुवन्नयं वै प्रजापतिरकृतमकरिमं विध्येति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्स वै वो वरं वृणा इति वृणीष्टेति स एकमेव वरमवृणीत पशूनामाधिपत्यं तदस्यैतत्पशुमन्नाम पशुमान्भवति योऽस्यैतदेवं नाम वेद ॥ (*taṃ devā abruvannayaṃ vai prajāpatirakṛtamakarimaṃ vidhyeti sa tathetyabravītsa vai vo varaṃ vṛṇā iti vṛṇīṣṭeti sa ekameva varamavṛṇīta paśūnāmādhipatyaṃ tadasyaitatpaśumannāma paśumānbhavati yo 'syaitadevaṃ nāma veda ‖*)

Then the gods, seeing Rudra of fearsome form, entreated him: "O Rudra, Prajāpati, enamoured of his own daughter, has committed an unnatural deed contrary to the world. Therefore, to punish him, strike him with your arrow." Rudra said: "Very well, I shall do so. But for doing this work you must grant me a boon." The gods agreed and said, "Ask the boon you wish." Rudra said: "I must become lord of all cattle; that is, I must gain lordship over the cattle and be famed by the name Paśupati. This is the boon I ask." The gods consented and granted the boon, saying, "So be it." One who knows this obtains the wealth of cattle, cows and the rest, and lives in comfort.

तमभ्यायत्याविध्यत्स विद्ध ऊर्ध्व उदप्रपतत्तमेतं मृग इत्याचक्षते य उ एव मृगव्याधः स उ एव स या रोहित्सा रोहिणी यो एवेषुस्त्रिकांडा सो एवेषुस्त्रिकांडा । (*tamabhyāyatyāvidhyatsa viddha ūrdhva udaprapatattametaṃ mṛga ityācakṣate ya u eva mṛgavyādhaḥ sa u eva sa yā rohitsā rohiṇī yo eveṣustrikāṃḍā so eveṣustrikāṃḍā |*)

### Printed p. 364

Then Rudra fitted an arrow to his bow, drew the string to his ear, aimed at Prajāpati who was in the form of a deer, and shot. Pained by the arrow, Prajāpati leapt upward into the sky, still in the form of the deer. Seeing this, all people say that Prajāpati in the form of the deer shines in the sky as the constellation Mṛgaśīrṣā (stars in the Orion), between the stars Rohiṇī and Ārdrā. Rudra, who struck Prajāpati with the arrow, became famed by the name Mṛgavyādha. He became known as this very Mṛgavyādha (name of star), famed among the people, who is seen in the sky among the stars. The daughter of Prajāpati, who was in the form of the red doe, became the star Rohiṇī (constellation), shining in the sky with a red colour. The arrow that Rudra shot had three parts, shaft, steel and point (kāṇḍa, loha, tuḍi), and these three parts are still found together in the arrows that people use.

तद्वा इदं प्रजापते रेतः सिक्तमधावत्तत्सरोऽभवत्ते देवा अब्रुवन्मेदं प्रजापते रेतो दुषदिति यदब्रुवन्मेदं प्रजापते रेतो दुषदिति तन्मादुषमभवत्तन्मादुषस्य मादुषत्वं माडुषं ह वै नामैतद्यन्मानुषं सन्मानुषमित्याचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः ॥ (*tadvā idaṃ prajāpate retaḥ siktamadhāvattatsaro 'bhavatte devā abruvanmedaṃ prajāpate reto duṣaditi yadabruvanmedaṃ prajāpate reto duṣaditi tanmāduṣamabhavattanmāduṣasya māduṣatvaṃ māḍuṣaṃ ha vai nāmaitadyanmānuṣaṃ sanmānuṣamityācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-23) **NOTE**

The semen that Prajāpati, in the form of the deer, had discharged into his daughter in the form of the doe was so abundant that it fell on the earth, flowed as a stream and stood in a low-lying place. It became a great lake. The gods saw this and praised it, saying, "This semen of Prajāpati is not to be despised (dūṣya), nor is it untouchable." Because of this the semen became famed by the name Māduṣam ("not to be despised"). In truth, since this semen is free of fault, it is right to call it Māduṣa. When people speak, they change the letter du in the word Māduṣa into nu by transposition and say Mānuṣa. Therefore the bodies of Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas and the rest, produced from the semen of Prajāpati, are called mānuṣa. This is the reason why human beings have the name Mānuṣa. But it is not so with the gods. They do not change the letters of the word Māduṣa and use it as Māduṣa. This word Māduṣa is not in common use. For the gods are fond of the indirect (parokṣa), and so they like to use words with a hidden meaning, not saying what is as it is, that is, not in such a way as to be clearly understood.

तदग्निना पर्यादधुस्तन्मरुतोऽधून्वंस्तदग्निर्न प्राच्यावयत्तदग्निना वैश्वानरेण पर्यादधुस्तन्मरुतोऽधून्वंस्तदग्निर्वैश्वानरः प्राच्यावयत्तस्य यद्रेतसः प्रथममुददीप्यत तदसावादित्योऽभवद्यद्वितीयमासीत्त- द्भृगुरभवत्तं वरुणो नृगृह्णीत तस्मात्स भृगुर्वारुणिरथ यत्तृतीयमदीदेदिव त आदित्या अभवन्येऽज्जारा आसंस्तेऽज्गरसोऽभवन्यदंगाराः पुनरवशांता उददीप्यंत तद्बृहस्पतिरभवत् । (*tadagninā paryādadhustanmaruto 'dhūnvaṃstadagnirna prācyāvayattadagninā vaiśvānareṇa paryādadhustanmaruto 'dhūnvaṃstadagnirvaiśvānaraḥ prācyāvayattasya yadretasaḥ prathamamudadīpyata tadasāvādityo 'bhavadyadvitīyamāsītta- dbhṛgurabhavattaṃ varuṇo nṛgṛhṇīta tasmātsa bhṛgurvāruṇiratha yattṛtīyamadīdediva ta ādityā abhavanye 'jjārā āsaṃste 'jgaraso 'bhavanyadaṃgārāḥ punaravaśāṃtā udadīpyaṃta tadbṛhaspatirabhavat |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-34)

### Printed p. 365

After the gods had made the semen of Prajāpati, standing in the form of a lake, free of fault, they thought it would be hard to keep it if it stayed liquid. They resolved to separate the liquid, the watery part, from it. So they set fire all round that lake of semen, and tried by its heat to make the semen dry up, lose its liquid state and become solid lumps. When a fire is burning, the wind naturally blows. The gods thought that the wind would help the liquid of the lake to dry up, and so they made the wind blow together with the fire. But the lake was churned and thrown into turmoil by the strong wind that blew, and however great the heat of the fire, the semen did not become solid. It remained liquid. Because the semen in the lake contained a great deal of liquid, it was impossible for the fire to turn it into lumps. Seeing this, the gods thought again and, as before, set the fire called Vaiśvānara all round the lake. Vaiśvānara is a special form of Agni. This Vaiśvānara fire, in the form of heat in the bellies of living beings, digests the food and the rest that they eat. On this point,

अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः । प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधं ॥ (*ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ | prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidhaṃ ‖*)

the Lord himself has said. That is: "I myself (the Lord), in the form of the Vaiśvānara fire, remain in the bodies of living beings together with the vital airs called prāṇa and apāna, and digest the four kinds of food, anna and the rest, that living beings eat." Since this is said, it follows that Vaiśvānara has special power and ability beyond the ordinary fire. Thereupon this Vaiśvānara fire, by its power, made the liquid semen in the lake free of liquid and solid, and turned it into many lumps (balls). From the first lump, blazing in the contact of Vaiśvānara's flames, Āditya (the sun) came into being. From the second lump the seer Bṛgu was produced. Varuṇa took this seer Bṛgu as his own son. For this very reason the followers of the Taittirīya branch (students of the Yajurveda) recite बृगुर्वै वारुणिः । वरुणं पितरमुपससार (*bṛgurvai vāruṇiḥ | varuṇaṃ pitaramupasasāra*). That is, Bṛgu, the son of the god Varuṇa, approached his father Varuṇa and put a question to him in this manner; this is its meaning. By this Bṛgu became famed as the son of Varuṇa. Then from the third lump, which was burning, the Ādityas, that is, the sons of Aditi or the twelve Ādityas, were produced

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । वर्तिः । यातं । जयुषा । वि । पर्वतं । अपिन्वतं । शयवे । धेनुं । अश्विना ।  
> वृकस्य । चित् । वर्तिकां । अंतः । आस्यात् । युवं । शचीभिः । ग्रसितां । अमुंचतं ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनाश्विन् ता तौ युवां जयुषा जयशीलेन रथेन पर्वतमुद्रिं प्रति
> वर्तिर्मार्गं वि यातं । विविधं गच्छथः । तथा च निगमांतरं । वि जयुषा रथ्या
> यातमद्रिं श्रुतं हवं वृषणा वध्रिमत्याः । ऋ. सं. ६ ६२.७ । इति । किंच युवां
> शयवे शयोरर्थाय धेनुमपिन्वतं । निवृत्तप्रसवां वृद्धां गां प्रभूतस्य
> पयसो दोग्धीं कृतवंतौ स्थ इत्यर्थः । तथा च निगमांतरं । युवं धेनुं
> शयवे नाधितायापिन्वतमश्विना पूर्वाय । ऋ. सं. १-११८-८ । इति । किंच युवं
> युवां वृकस्यांतरनुप्रविष्टां ग्रसितां वृकेण ग्रस्तां वर्तिकां । वर्तिका नाम
> चटका । तामास्याद्वृकस्य मुखाच्छचीभिः प्रज्ञाभिः कर्मभिर्वामुंचतं । अमोचयतं । तथा च निगमांतरं । अजोहवीदश्विना वर्तिका वामास्नो यत्सीममुंचतं वृकस्य । ऋ. सं. १.११३-१६! इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the two Aśvins: with your victorious chariot (जयुषा (*jayuṣā*), "of conquering habit") you go variously along the path (वर्तिः (*vartiḥ*)) towards the mountain (पर्वतं (*parvataṃ*), the rock). He cites another Ṛk for this: वि जयुषा रथ्या यातमद्रिं श्रुतं हवं वृषणा वध्रिमत्याः । (*vi jayuṣā rathyā yātamadriṃ śrutaṃ havaṃ vṛṣaṇā vadhrimatyāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6 62.7). Further, you made the cow (धेनुं (*dhenuṃ*)) swell with milk for Śayu: you made a cow that was old and had ceased to bear a yielder of abundant milk. He cites: युवं धेनुं शयवे नाधितायापिन्वतमश्विना पूर्वाय (*yuvaṃ dhenuṃ śayave nādhitāyāpinvatamaśvinā pūrvāya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-8). Further, you released the quail (वर्तिकां (*vartikāṃ*); vartikā is the name of the caṭakā), that had been swallowed by the wolf and had gone into it, from the mouth of the wolf, by your wisdoms or by your deeds (शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)). He cites: अजोहवीदश्विना वर्तिका वामास्नो यत्सीममुंचतं वृकस्य (*ajohavīdaśvinā vartikā vāmāsno yatsīmamuṃcataṃ vṛkasya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.113-16).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- ता (*tā*)—you
- जयुषा (*jayuṣā*)—with the victorious chariot
- पर्वतं वर्तिः (*parvataṃ vartiḥ*)—on the mountain path
- वि यातं (*vi yātaṃ*)—travel about in many ways
- शयवे (*śayave*)—for Śayu
- धेनुं अपिन्वतं (*dhenuṃ apinvataṃ*)—you made the barren cow nourished so that she became a milch cow **NOTE**
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you
- वृकस्य अंतः (*vṛkasya aṃtaḥ*)—inside the wolf's mouth
- ग्रसितां (*grasitāṃ*)—swallowed
- वर्तिकां (*vartikāṃ*)—the bird called vartikā
- आस्यात् (*āsyāt*)—from its mouth
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—by your deeds
- अमुंचतं (*amuṃcataṃ*)—you released

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, travel about in many ways on the mountain path with your victorious chariot. For Śayu you made the barren cow a cow that gives milk. You released the sparrow that was swallowed inside the wolf's mouth, from its mouth.**NOTE**

##### English translation
Do you two, Ashwins, climb the path to the mountain with your triumphant chariot ; you have renovated for Shayu the (barren) milch cow : you liberated by your acts the quail that had been seized from the jaws of the wolf.

### Printed p. 367

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमो यमीं पुनर्ब्रूते । पुरा पूर्वं प्रजापतेर्यदगम्यागमनपरिमितसामर्थ्योपेतत्वात्कृतं तथा वयं न चक्रम । नाकुर्म । वयमृतानि सत्यानि
> वदंतो ब्रुवंतोऽनृतमसत्यं कद्ध कदा खलु नूनं निश्चितं रपेम । वदेम । न
> कदाचिदपीत्यर्थः । आगम्यागमनं न कुर्म इति यावत् । अपि चाप्पु । अंतरिक्षनामैतत् । अंतरिक्षे स्थितो गंधर्वो गवां रश्मीनामुदकानां वा धारयितादित्योऽप्यांतरिक्षस्था सा प्रसिद्धा योषादित्यस्य भार्यासरण्यूश्च नो नानावयोर्नाभिरुत्पत्ति स्थानं । मातापितरावित्यर्थः । तत्तस्मात्कारणान्नाववयोर्जामि बांधवमुत्कृष्टं । एवं सत्यावयोरगम्यागमनरूपत्वात्कर्तुमयुक्तं तस्मादेतन्न
> करोमीत्यभिप्रायः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yama speaks again to Yamī. What Prajāpati did formerly, because he was endowed with a measureless capacity for approaching a woman not to be approached, we have not done. How, speaking truths (*ṛtāni*), could we ever, certainly, speak untruth? The meaning is that we never will; that is, we do not do what is union with the forbidden. Further, अप्पु (*appu*): this is a name of the atmosphere. The Gandharva standing in the atmosphere, the Āditya, upholder of the rays of cows or of the waters, and that well-known woman of the atmosphere, the wife of Āditya, Saraṇyū, are the nābhi of us two, that is, the place of our origin; the meaning is that they are our mother and father. Therefore the kinship (जामि (*jāmi*)) of us two is excellent. This being so, it is improper for us two to do what would be union with the forbidden, and therefore, is his intention, "I do not do this." **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरा (*purā*)—formerly (O Yamī)
- यत् (*yat*)—what deed Prajāpati did
- न चक्रम (*na cakrama*)—I cannot do it
- ऋता (*ṛtā*)—true words
- वदंतः (*vadaṃtaḥ*)—speaking
- अनृतं (*anṛtaṃ*)—untruth
- कत् ह (*kat ha*)—how indeed
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—certainly
- रपेम (*rapema*)—can we speak
- अप्पु (*appu*)—the one standing in the atmosphere
- गंधर्वः (*gaṃdharvaḥ*)—Āditya
- अप्या सा (*apyā sā*)—the well-known woman of the atmosphere
- योषा च (*yoṣā ca*)—and the woman (the wife of Āditya), Saraṇyū
- नः (*naḥ*)—to both of us
- नाभिः (*nābhiḥ*)—are the place of origin
- तत् (*tat*)—therefore
- नौ (*nau*)—of both of us
- जामि (*jāmi*)—kinship
- परमं (*paramaṃ*)—is most excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yamī, what the all-powerful Prajāpati did formerly I cannot do now. Having spoken true words up to now, how can we speak untruth now? The Āditya who stands in the atmosphere and Saraṇyū, the wife of Āditya, who also stands in the atmosphere, are the common place of origin of both of us. Therefore the kinship of both of us, as brother and sister, is most excellent. (Our relation as husband and wife is not possible.)

##### English translation
(Yama speaks). We connot do what was done formerly; for how can we who speak truth, utter now that which is untrue? Gandharva (the sun) was in the watery (firmament), and the water was his bride She is our common parent, hence our near affinity.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गर्भे॒ नु नौ॑ जनि॒ता दंप॑ती कर्दे॒वस्त्वष्टा॑ सवि॒ता वि॒श्वरू॑पः ।  
> नकि॑रस्य॒ प्र मि॑नंति व्र॒तानि॒ वेद॑ नाव॒स्य पृ॑थि॒वी उ॒त द्यौः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गर्भे । नु । नौ । जनिता । दंपती इति दंपती । कः । देवः । त्वष्टा । सविता । विश्वरूपः ।  
> नकिः । अस्य । प्र । मिनंति । व्रतानि । वेद । नौ । अस्य । पृथिवी । उत । द्यौः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वष्टा रूपाणां कर्ता सविता सर्वेषां शुभाशुभस्य प्रेरको विश्वरूपः
> सर्वात्मको देवो दानादिगुणयुक्तो जनिता जनयिता प्रजापतिर्गर्भे नु
> गर्भावस्थायामेव नावानां दंपती जायापती कः । कृतवान् एकोदरे सहवासित्वात् । अस्य प्रजापतेर्व्रतानि कर्माणि नकिः प्र मिनंति । न केचित्पहिंसंति । न
> लोपयंतीत्यर्थः । अतः कारणाद्गर्भावस्थायामेवावयोः प्रजापतिकृते
> दंपतित्वे सति संभोगं कुर्वित्यर्थः । अपि च नावावयोरस्येदं मातुरुदरे
> सहवासजनितं दंपतित्वं पृथिवी भूमिर्वेद । जानाति । उतापि च द्यौर्द्युलोकोऽपि
> जानाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Tvaṣṭṛ, the maker of forms; Savitṛ, the impeller of all to good and bad; Viśvarūpa, the all-formed; the god endowed with the qualities of generosity and the rest; the begetter (जनिता (*janitā*)), Prajāpati: he made us two a couple (दंपती (*daṃpatī*)), husband and wife, in the womb itself (गर्भे नु (*garbhe nu*)), since we dwelt together in one womb; कः (*kaḥ*) is glossed कृतवान् (*kṛtavān*), "he made". None (नकिः (*nakiḥ*)) violate (प्र मिनंति (*pra minaṃti*)) the vratas, the deeds, of this Prajāpati; none injure or neglect them. For this reason, the two of us having been made a couple by Prajāpati in the womb itself, the meaning is: "Have union." Further, the earth (पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)) knows this coupledom of us two, born of living together in the mother's womb, and heaven (द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)), the heavenly world, also knows it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*)—the maker of the forms of the world
- सविता (*savitā*)—the impeller of all
- विश्वरूपः (*viśvarūpaḥ*)—the all-formed
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the divine one
- जनिता (*janitā*)—Prajāpati, the begetter of all
- नौ (*nau*)—us
- गर्भॆ नु (*garbhè nu*)—while we were in the womb
- दंपती (*daṃpatī*)—as husband and wife
- कः (*kaḥ*)—has made
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Prajāpati
- व्रतानि (*vratāni*)—the deeds
- नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—no one at all
- प्र मिनंति (*pra minaṃti*)—can injure
- नौ (*nau*)—our
- अस्य (*asya*)—this relation of husband and wife
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the earth
- वेद (*veda*)—has known
- उत (*uta*)—and
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—heaven also has known

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Prajāpati, the maker of the forms of the world, the impeller of all, the self of all, the divine self, the begetter of all, made us husband and wife while we were still in the womb. No one at all can injure the deeds of this Prajāpati. Both heaven and earth have known this relation of ours as husband and wife.

### Printed p. 369

##### English translation
(Yami speaks). The divine omniform generator Twashtri, the progenitor, made us two husband and wife, even in the womb : none frustrate his undertaking ; earth and heaven are conscious of this our (union)

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> को अ॒स्य वे॑द प्रथ॒मस्याह्नः॒ क ईं॑ ददर्श॒ क इ॒ह प्र वो॑चत् ।  
> बृ॒हन्मि॒त्रस्य॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ धाम॒ कदु॑ ब्रव आहनो॒ वीच्या॒ न्नान् ॥६॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कः । अस्य । वेद । प्रथमस्य । अह्नः । कः । ईं । ददर्श । कः । इह । प्र । वोचत् ।  
> बृहत् । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । धाम । कत् । ऊं इति। ब्रवः । आहनः । वीच्या । न्यान् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रथमस्याह्नः संबंध्यस्येदमन्योन्यसंगमनं को वेद । जानाति । प्रथमेs
> हनि यत्क्रियते तदनुमानमाश्रित्य न कश्चिदपि ज्ञातुं शक्नोतीत्यर्थः । इहास्मिन्देशे प्रत्यक्षतः क ईमिदं संगमनं ददर्श । पश्यति । कः प्र वोचत् । प्रख्यापयति ।
> न कोऽपीत्यर्थः ॥ मत्रस्य वरुणस्य मित्रावरुणयोर्बृहन्महद्दाम स्थानमहोरात्रं यदस्ति तत्र न्यान्मनुष्यान् वीच्या नरकेण हे आहन आहंतर्मर्यादया
> हिंसितः । स्वकृतशुभाशुभकर्मापेक्षया मनुष्यादिप्राणिनां नरकपातेन स्वर्गप्रापणेन निग्रहानुग्रहयोः कर्तरित्यर्थः । एवंभूत हे यम त्वं कदु ब्रवः ,
> किं वा ब्रवीषि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa takes the verse as Yamī's speech. Who knows this mutual union belonging to the first day? Whatever is done on the first day, no one can know it by inference. Who has seen this union here, directly, in this place? Who will proclaim it? No one. The great abode of Mitra and Varuna is day and night. In that abode, O Āhana, you restrain men by hell, and by sending them to heaven you are the agent of both restraint and favour for men and other beings, according to the good and evil deeds each has done. Being such, O Yama, what do you say, or what will you answer?

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रथमस्य अह्नः (*prathamasya ahnaḥ*)—of the first day
- अस्य (*asya*)—this mutual union
- कः वेद (*kaḥ veda*)—who indeed knows
- इह (*iha*)—in this place
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this union
- कः ददर्श (*kaḥ dadarśa*)—who has seen
- कः प्रवोचत् (*kaḥ pravocat*)—who can proclaim and tell
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—of Mitra
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of Varuna
- बृहत् धाम (*bṛhat dhāma*)—in the great abode, day and night
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—men
- वीच्या (*vīcyā*)—by hell
- आहनः (*āhanaḥ*)—O Yama, who afflict
- कदु ब्रवः (*kadu bravaḥ*)—what will you say in this matter?

### Printed p. 370

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Who indeed knows this mutual union of the first day? Who has seen this union in this place? Who can proclaim it? O Yama, you who afflict men in the form of hell in the great abode of Mitra and Varuna, namely day and night, what will you say in this matter?

##### English translation
(Yami speaks). Who knows anything of this (his) first day (of intercourse)? Who will behold it? Who will here reveal it? The dwelling of Mitra and of Varuna is vast. What do you say, you who punish men with hell?

> यमस्य । मा । यम्यं। कामः। आ । अगन् । समाने । योन् । सहशेय्याय ।  
> जायाऽइव । पत्ये । तन्वं । रिरिच्यां । वि । चित् । वृहेव । रथ्या इव । चक्रा ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमस्य तव कामोऽभिलाषो यम्यं यमीं मां मां प्रत्यागन् ।
> आगच्छतु । मनोपरि तव यमस्य संभोगेच्छा जायतामित्यर्थः : किमर्थं ।
> समाने योनावेकस्मिन् स्थाने शय्याख्ये सहशेय्याय सहशयनार्थं । तदनंतरं
> पूर्णमनोरथा सती जायेव पत्ये यथा भार्या पत्युरर्थाय परया प्रीत्या

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yama, may your desire, your longing, come towards me, Yamī; that is, may the wish for union arise in you. For what purpose? For lying together in one place, called the bed. Thereafter, as a wife whose wishes are fulfilled, trusting her husband and wishing for love, displays her body to him with the highest affection, so may I lay bare my own body for you.

### Printed p. 371

> विश्वस्ता सती रतिकामा स्वशरीरं प्रकाशयति एवं तन्नमात्मीयं शरीरं रिरिच्यां
> विविच्यां । त्वदर्थं प्रकाशयेयमित्यर्थः । किंच । चिदिति पूरणः । विवृहेव !! वृहू
> उद्यमने ॥ धर्मार्थकामान्विविधमुद्यच्छावः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथ्येव चक्रा
> रथस्यावयवभूते चक्रे यथा रथमुद्यच्छतस्तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Moreover, चित् (*cit*) is an expletive." The word विवृहेव (*vivṛheva*) is from the root वृहू (*vṛhū*) in the sense of lifting up: let us both exert ourselves in various ways for dharma, artha and kāma. The illustration is रथ्येव चक्रा (*rathyeva cakrā*): as two wheels, being parts of a chariot, bear up the chariot, so we.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समाने योन् (*samāne yon*)—in one bed
- सहशेय्याय (*sahaśeyyāya*)—to lie together
- यमस्य (*yamasya*)—of you, Yama
- कामः (*kāmaḥ*)—desire
- यम्यं (*yamyaṃ*)—me, who am named Yamī
- मा (*mā*)—me (to join me)
- आगन् (*āgan*)—may arise
- पत्ये (*patye*)—for her husband
- जायेव (*jāyeva*)—as a wife offers her body completely
- तन्वं (*tanvaṃ*)—my body
- रिरिच्यां (*riricyāṃ*)—I will offer to you
- चक्रा (*cakrā*)—the wheels of a chariot
- रथ्येव (*rathyeva*)—as they bear the chariot together
- वि वृहेव (*vi vṛheva*)—let us both together carry out dharma, artha and kāma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yama, may the desire arise in you to cooperate with me, that we two may lie together in one bed. As a wife offers her body completely to her husband, I will offer my body to you. As the wheels of a chariot bear the chariot together, let us two together carry out dharma, artha and kāma.

##### English translation
(Yami speaks). O yama, the desire may come to you to lie with me in the same bed ; I will abandon my person to you as a wife to her husband; let us exert ourselves in union like the two wheels of a waggon.

#### Ṛk 8

> अ॒न्येन॒ मदा॑हनो याहि॒ तूयं॒ तेन॒ वि वृ॑ह॒ रथ्ये॑व च॒क्रा ॥

### Printed p. 372

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यम्या प्रख्यातो यमः पुनराह । इहास्मिल्लोके देवानां संबंधिनो
> ये स्पशोऽहोरात्रादयश्चाराश्चरंति सर्वॆषां शुभाशुभलक्षणकर्मप्रत्यवेक्षणार्थं परिभ्रमंति एते चाराः क्षणमात्रमपि चरणव्यापाररहिता न तिष्ठंति । न नि
> मिषंति । मेषणं न कुर्वंति । शुभमशुभं वा यः करोति तं निरीक्षंते चेत्यर्थः।
> हे आहनो ममापहंत्र्यसह्यभाषणेन दुःखयित्रि त्वं मन्मत्तोऽन्येन त्वत्सदृशेन
> सह तूयं क्षिप्रं याहि । संगच्छ । गत्वा च तेन वि वृह । धर्मार्थकामानुद्यच्छ ।
> तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथ्येव चक्रा यथा रथावयवभूते चक्रे रथमुद्यच्छतस्तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yama, thus addressed by Yamī, speaks again. Here in this world the spies, the day-and-night and other watchers belonging to the gods, roam about to observe everyone's deeds, good and evil. These spies do not stand still, free from movement, even for a moment; they do not wink, that is, they do not close their eyes; they watch whoever does good or evil. O Āhanā, you who afflict me with unbearable speech, go quickly, join one other than me, one like you; and having gone, वि वृह (*vi vṛha*) with him: carry out dharma, artha and kāma. The illustration is रथ्येव चक्रा (*rathyeva cakrā*): as two wheels, parts of a chariot, bear up the chariot.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Yamī) देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—appointed by the gods
- ये स्पशः (*ye spaśaḥ*)—the spies who exist, they
- इह चरंति (*iha caraṃti*)—move about everywhere here
- एते (*ete*)—they
- न तिष्ठंति (*na tiṣṭhaṃti*)—do not rest even a little
- न निमिषंति (*na nimiṣaṃti*)—watch everything without closing the eyes
- आहनः (*āhanaḥ*)—O Yamī, who afflict me with your sinful desire
- मत् (*mat*)—than me
- अन्येन (*anyena*)—with another
- तूयं (*tūyaṃ*)—quickly
- याहि (*yāhi*)—enter into a relation
- चक्रा (*cakrā*)—the wheels of a chariot
- रथ्येव (*rathyeva*)—as they bear the chariot together
- तेन (*tena*)—joined with him
- वि वृह (*vi vṛha*)—may you two together carry out your tasks

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yamī, the spies appointed by the gods move about everywhere here. They do not rest even a little. They watch everything without closing the eye. O Yamī, you who afflict me by your sinful desire, quickly enter a relation with one other than me. As the wheels of a chariot bear the chariot together, join him and let you two together carry out your tasks.

##### English translation
(Yama Speaks)- The spies of the Gods who wander upon earth, never stop, never close their eyes. Associate quickly, destructress, with some other than with me, ond exert yourselves in union, like the two wheels of a waggon.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

To explain the meaning of the word आहने (*āhane*), Yāska has given an etymology for the latter half of this Ṛk:

### Printed p. 373
आहनः । अन्येन मदाहनो याहि तूयं । अन्येन मवहनो गच्छ क्षिप्रमाहंसीव भाषमाणेत्यसभ्यभाषणादाहना इव भवत्येतस्मादाहनः स्यात् ( (*āhanaḥ | anyena madāhano yāhi tūyaṃ | anyena mavahano gaccha kṣipramāhaṃsīva bhāṣamāṇetyasabhyabhāṣaṇādāhanā iva bhavatyetasmādāhanaḥ syāt (*) (Se. 5-2)**NOTE**

That is: O immodest woman, leaving me, go quickly with another man of another family. O woman of bad conduct, leaving me, go off quickly with another man. This way you speak causes me great anguish. The word आहना (*āhanā*) means one who speaks bad words, that is, speaks like the speech of women of immodest behaviour, adulterous women. आहनः (*āhanaḥ*) is a word in the vocative singular. For this too the meaning stated above applies.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दिपा । पृथिव्या । मिथुना । सबंधू इति सबंधू । यमीः । यमस्य । बिभृयात् ।  
> अजामि ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रात्रिभिरहभिरहोरात्रयोरस्मै यमाय कल्पितं भागं सर्वो यजमानो
> दशस्येत् । प्रयच्छतु । सूर्यस्य संबंधि चक्षुस्तेजो मुहुर्मुहुरस्यॆ
> यमायोन्मिमियात् । उदेतु । दिवा पृथिव्या द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां सह मिथुनौ
> सबंधू समानबंधू अहोरात्रे अस्मै यमाय । एतज्जात्वेयं यमीर्यमस्याजाम्यभ्रातरं बिभृयात् । धारयतु । यत्नेन परिगृह्णातित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Let every sacrificer give to this Yama, in the nights and days, the portion appointed for him. Let the eye, the brightness, of the Sun rise again and again for this Yama. Day and night, a pair, kindred, together with heaven and earth, are for this Yama. Knowing this, let this Yamī bear, that is, take up with effort, the non-brother of Yama.**NOTE**

### Printed p. 374

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्मै (*asmai*)—addressing this Yama
- रात्रीभिः (*rātrībhiḥ*)—in the times of night
- अहभिः (*ahabhiḥ*)—in the days
- दशस्येत् (*daśasyet*)—let the sacrificer offer the oblation
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the Sun
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—the brightness
- मुहुः (*muhuḥ*)—many times
- उन्मिमायात् (*unmimāyāt*)—let it appear for this Yama
- दिवा पृथिव्या (*divā pṛthivyā*)—with heaven and earth
- मिथुना (*mithunā*)—joined together
- सबंधू (*sabaṃdhū*)—having equal kinship: let day and night be for Yama's satisfaction
- यमीः (*yamīḥ*)—this Yamī
- यमस्य (*yamasya*)—with Yama
- अजामि (*ajāmi*)—a relation that is not brotherly
- बिभृयात् (*bibhṛyāt*)—let her attain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Throughout days and nights let sacrificers offer the oblation to this Yama alone. At many times let the Sun's brightness appear for this Yama alone. Let day and night, joined with heaven and earth and having equal kinship, be for Yama's satisfaction. Let Yamī attain with Yama a relation that is not brotherly (a conjugal one).

##### English translation
(Yama speaks). To him (Yama) let every worshipper sacrifice both day and night, on him let the eyes of the Sun repeatedly rise; (for him may) the kindred pair (day and night unite) with heaven and earth. Yamī will adhere to the non-affinity of Yama.

#### Ṛk 10 (continued)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत्र येषु कालेषु जामयो भगिन्योऽजाम्यभ्रातरं पतिं कृणवन्
> करिष्यंति ता तान्त्युत्तराणि युगानि कालविशेषा आ गच्छान् । आ गमिष्यंति । घेति
> पूरणः । यस्मादेवं तस्माद्दे सुभगे त्वमिदानीं मन्मत्तोन्यं पतिं भर्तारमिच्छस्व ।
> कामयस्व । तदनंतरं वृषभाय तव येनौ रेतः सेक्रे पुरुषायात्मीयं
> बाहुमुप बर्बृहि । शयनकाल उपबर्हणं कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that in the times when sisters (जामयः (*jāmayaḥ*)) will take as husbands men who are not brothers, those later ages, those special periods, will come. घ (*gha*) is an expletive. Since this is so, the auspicious one should now seek another husband than himself. After that she should make her arm a pillow (उपबर्हणं (*upabarhaṇaṃ*)) for the bull-like man, at the time of lying down.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which times
- जामयः (*jāmayaḥ*)—sisters
- अजामि (*ajāmi*)—those who are not brothers
- कृणवन् (*kṛṇavan*)—will make their husbands
- ता (*tā*)—such
- उत्तरा (*uttarā*)—coming later
- युगानि (*yugāni*)—special periods
- आ अगच्छान् (*ā agacchān*)—will arrive (therefore)
- सुभगे (*subhage*)—O beautiful one
- मत् (*mat*)—than me
- अन्यं (*anyaṃ*)—another
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—as your husband
- इच्छस्व (*icchasva*)—desire
- वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*)—for that powerful man
- बाहुं (*bāhuṃ*)—your arm
- उपबर्बृहि (*upabarbṛhi*)—make into a pillow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yamī, the times will come when sisters will take as their husbands men who are not their brothers. Therefore, O beautiful one, desire and choose as your husband one other than me. Make your arm a pillow for that man, who has the power to fulfil your desire, and give him pleasure.

##### English translation
(Yama speaks). The subsequent ages will come, when sisters will choose one who is not a brother (as a husband); therefore, auspicious one. choose another husband than me, and make your arm a pillow for your mate.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the meaning of the word जामिः (*jāmiḥ*), Yāska has given this explanation of the Ṛk:
आ घा ता गच्छानुत्तरा युगानि यत्र जामयः कृणवन्नजामि। उप बर्ब्बहि वृषभाय बाहुमन्यमिच्छस्व सुभगे पतिं मत्॥ आगमिष्यति तान्युत्तराणि युगानि यत्र जामयः करिष्यंत्यजामिकर्माणि । जाम्यतिरेकनाम। (*ā ghā tā gacchānuttarā yugāni yatra jāmayaḥ kṛṇavannajāmi| upa barbbahi vṛṣabhāya bāhumanyamicchasva subhage patiṃ mat‖ āgamiṣyati tānyuttarāṇi yugāni yatra jāmayaḥ kariṣyaṃtyajāmikarmāṇi | jāmyatirekanāma|*)

### Printed p. 376
बालिशस्य ना । असमानजातीयस्य वोपजनः । उपधेहि वृषभाय बाहुमन्यमिच्छस्व सुभगे पतिं मदिति व्याख्यातं ॥ (*bāliśasya nā | asamānajātīyasya vopajanaḥ | upadhehi vṛṣabhāya bāhumanyamicchasva subhage patiṃ maditi vyākhyātaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 4-20)

The word जामि (*jāmi*) has the meaning "kinsman", and it also has the meaning "sister" and "fool". अजामि (*ajāmi*) means an act done by those who are not kinsmen, an action practised mutually. That is, before marriage the bridegroom and the bride have no relationship at all: the bride's family is one, the bridegroom's another. It is the custom that people of different families choose each other and marry. This kind of act too is called जामि (*jāmi*). अजामि (*ajāmi*) means the act opposite to it: where the bride and groom belong to the same family, and moreover are brother and sister, their marriage is forbidden. This kind of forbidden act is called अजामि (*ajāmi*). In the present Ṛk it is indicated that the time will come when brothers and sisters perform this forbidden act of sexual union. That is, now (in the seer's time) sexual union between brother and sister is forbidden. "Later and later" means that in the future, in the Kali age, people will abandon such good conduct and, wilfully, become attached to the forbidden act of union between brothers and sisters. Such a time will come. Therefore, O beautiful one, the seer describes: leave me, take as your husband another man who will satisfy you with the pleasure of love, give him shelter on the pillow of your arm, and enjoy the pleasure of love with him.

### Printed p. 377

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमी यमेन प्रत्याख्याता पुनराह । यद्यस्मिन्भ्रातरि सति स्वसादिकमनाथं नाथरहितं भवति स भ्राता किमसत् । किं भवति । न भवतीत्यर्थः । किंच यस्यां
> भगिन्यां सत्यां भ्रातरं निर्ऋतिर्दुःखं निगच्छात् नियमेन गच्छति प्राप्नोति सा
> स्वसा किमु । किं वा भवति । भ्रातृभगिन्योश्च परस्परं प्रीतिर्येन केनचिदुपायेनावश्यं कार्येत्यभिप्रायः । साहं काममूता कामेन मूर्छिता सती बहुनानाप्रकारमेतदीदृशमुक्तं वक्ष्यमाणं च रपामि । प्रलपामि । एतज्ञात्वा
> मे मम तन्ना शरीरेण तन्नं शरीरं सं पिपृग्धि । संपर्चय । संभोगेन
> संश्लेषय । मां सम्यग्भुंक्षेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yamī, refused by Yama, speaks again. Is he a brother (भ्राता (*bhrātā*)) when, he being there, a sister and the rest are left without protector? He is not. And is she a sister when, she being there, misfortune (निर्ऋतिः (*nirṛtiḥ*), sorrow) surely comes to the brother? The intention is that love between brother and sister must be maintained by some means or other. Overcome by desire, she says all this and what is yet to be said, and prattles. Knowing this, let him unite his body with hers, join her in enjoyment; the meaning is "enjoy me fully".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् असत् (*yat asat*)—when there is a brother
- अनाथं भवाति (*anāthaṃ bhavāti*)—the sister is without protector
- भ्राता किं (*bhrātā kiṃ*)—is he truly called a brother?
- यत् (*yat*)—when there is a sister
- निर्ऋतिः (*nirṛtiḥ*)—sorrow
- निगच्छात् (*nigacchāt*)—reaches the brother and torments him
- स्वसा किमु (*svasā kimu*)—is she truly called a sister? (O Yama)
- कामभूता (*kāmabhūtā*)—tormented by desire **NOTE**
- बहु (*bahu*)—in many ways
- एतत् (*etat*)—in this form of entreaty
- रपामि (*rapāmi*)—I am begging
- मे (*me*)—my
- तन्वा (*tanvā*)—with body
- तन्वं (*tanvaṃ*)—your body
- सं पिपृग्गि (*saṃ pipṛggi*)—join and enjoy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yama, is he truly called a brother when, he being there, the sister is without protector? Is she truly called a sister when, she being there, sorrow torments the brother? Tormented by desire, I am begging in many ways in this form of entreaty. Join your body with my body and enjoy.

##### English translation
(Yami speaks). Is he a brother whose sister has no supporter in her brother ? Is she a sister who will allow (her brother) to approach misfortune? Overcome by desire, I strongly urge this one request ; unite your person with mine-

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमो यमीं प्रत्युक्तवान् । हे यमि ते तव तन्ना शरीरेण तन्नमात्मीयं शरीरं न वै सं पपृच्यां । नैव संपर्चयामि। नैवाहं त्वां संभोक्तुमिच्छामीत्यर्थः । यो भ्राता स्वसारं भगिनीं निगच्छात् नियमेनोपगच्छति ।
> संभुंक्ते इत्यर्थः । तं पापं पापकारिणमाहुः । शिष्टा वदंति । एतज्ञात्वा हे
> सुभगे सुष्टु भजनीये हे यमि त्वं मन्मत्तोऽन्येन त्वद्योगेन पुरुषेण सह
> प्रमुदः संभोगलक्षणान्हर्षान्कल्पयस्व । समर्थय । ते तव भ्राता यम
> एतदीदृशं त्वया सह मैथुनं कर्तुं न वष्टि । न कामयते । नेच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yama replies to Yamī. O Yamī, he will not unite his own body with her body; he does not wish to enjoy her. The brother who approaches a sister, who goes to her and enjoys her, the wise call a sinner. Knowing this, O fortunate one, let her find the joys of union with a man other than himself, one suited to her. Her brother Yama does not desire such intercourse with her.

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the brother who
- स्वसारं (*svasāraṃ*)—his own sister
- निगच्छात् (*nigacchāt*)—approaches (him)
- पापं (*pāpaṃ*)—as a sinner
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—the wise call
- सुभगे (*subhage*)—O beautiful one
- मत् (*mat*)—than me
- अन्येन (*anyena*)—together with another man

- कल्पयस्व (*kalpayasva*)—obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yamī, I will certainly not unite my body with your body. The wise call a brother who approaches his sister a sinner. O beautiful one, unite with a man other than me and obtain many kinds of pleasure. I, your brother, do not desire this relationship.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ब॒तो ब॑तासि यम॒ नैव ते॒ मनो॒ हृद॑यं चाविदाम ।  
> अ॒न्या किल॒ त्वां क॒क्ष्ये॑व यु॒क्तं परि॑ ष्वजाते॒ लिबु॑जीव वृ॒क्षं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बतः । बत । असि । यम । न । एव । ते । मनः । हृदयं । च । अविदाम ।  
> अन्या । किल । त्वां । कक्ष्या इव । युक्तं । परि । स्वजाते । लिबुजाइव । वृक्षं ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमी प्रत्युवाच । हे यम त्वं बतो दुर्बलोऽसि । बतेति निपातः
> खेदानुकंपयोः । अनुकंप्यश्चासि । ते त्वदीयं मनो मनोगतं संकल्पं हृदयं च बुद्धिगतमध्यवसायं च नैवाविदाम । वयं न जानीम एव । मत्तोऽन्या
> काचित्स्ने त्वां परि ष्वजाते किल । तत्र दृष्टांतद्वयमुच्यते । कक्षेव युक्तं
> यथा कक्ष्या रज्जुर्युक्तमात्मना संबद्धमश्व परिष्वजते तद्वत् । लिबुजीव वृक्षं
> यथा लिबुजा व्रततिर्गाढं वृक्षं परिष्वजते तद्वच्च । अन्यस्यां स्त्रियामासक्तस्वं
> मां परिष्वक्तुं नेच्छसीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yamī answers. O Yama, you are feeble (बतः (*bataḥ*)); बत (*bata*) is a particle (निपातः (*nipātaḥ*)) of distress and pity, and you are an object of pity. We do not know your mind, the intention lodged in it, nor your heart, the resolve lodged in the intellect. Some woman other than me embraces you. Two illustrations are given: as a girth (कक्ष्या (*kakṣyā*)), a rope, embraces the horse yoked to it and bound to itself; and as a creeper (लिबुजा (*libujā*)) firmly embraces a tree. The meaning is: "you, attached to another woman, do not wish to embrace me."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यम (*yama*)—O Yama
- बत (*bata*)—certainly (you)
- बतः (*bataḥ*)—feeble
- असि (*asi*)—are
- ते (*te*)—your
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind
- हृदयं च (*hṛdayaṃ ca*)—and heart
- नैव अविदाम (*naiva avidāma*)—we certainly cannot know
- कक्ष्या इव (*kakṣyā iva*)—as a rope ties the horse that is yoked to it
- लिबुजा इव (*libujā iva*)—as a creeper embraces a tree
- अन्या किल (*anyā kila*)—another woman
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- परि ष्वजाते (*pari ṣvajāte*)—embraces

### Printed p. 380

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yama, you are certainly feeble. We certainly cannot know your mind or your heart. As a rope ties the horse that is yoked to it, and as a creeper embraces a tree, another woman embraces you.

##### English translation
(Yami speaks). Alas, Yama, you are feeble ; we understand not your mind or your heart. Some other female embraces you as a girth a horse, or as a creeper a tree.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the meaning of the word बतः (*bataḥ*), Yāska has given the explanation of the present Ṛk:
बत इति निपातः खेदानुकंपयोः । बतो बतासि यम नैव ते मनो हृदयं चाविदाम । अन्या किल त्वां कक्ष्येव युक्तं परिष्वजाते लिबुजीव वृक्षं ॥ बतो बलाददीतो भवति । दुर्बलो बतासि यम नैव ते मनो हृदयं च विजानीमोऽन्या किल त्वां परिष्वंक्ष्यते कक्ष्येव युक्तं लिबुजीव वृक्षं । लिबुजा व्रततिर्भवति लीयते विभजंतीति । व्रततिर्वणाच्च संयनाच्च ततनाच्च ॥ (*bata iti nipātaḥ khedānukaṃpayoḥ | bato batāsi yama naiva te mano hṛdayaṃ cāvidāma | anyā kila tvāṃ kakṣyeva yuktaṃ pariṣvajāte libujīva vṛkṣaṃ ‖ bato balādadīto bhavati | durbalo batāsi yama naiva te mano hṛdayaṃ ca vijānīmo 'nyā kila tvāṃ pariṣvaṃkṣyate kakṣyeva yuktaṃ libujīva vṛkṣaṃ | libujā vratatirbhavati līyate vibhajaṃtīti | vratatirvaṇācca saṃyanācca tatanācca ‖*) (Ni. 6-28)

The word बत (*bata*) is a particle (an indeclinable) expressing sorrowful wonder, or distress and pity. O Yama, your mind is not firm; it is very weak. That is, there is no steadiness of mind. We cannot understand your mind as being right in this way. Alas, what pain! As a creeper winds round the tree near it, another woman will clasp you tightly with her arms. To see and bear this is very painful. लिबुजा (*libujā*) means a kind of creeper. It winds round, spreading its tendrils all over the tree. Because it divides or spreads and joins itself to the tree in this way, लिबुजा (*libujā*) is the name of the व्रतति (*vratati*), the creeper. Likewise the word प्रतति (*pratati*) too may be formed from the root वृ (*vṛ*), meaning "choose the tree one wants", or from the root सि (*si*), meaning "bind round", or from the root तनु (*tanu*), meaning "spread all round". This word means creeper, vine.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमः पुनरस्याह । हे यमि त्वमन्यमु अन्यं पुरुषमेव सु सुष्टु परिष्वज!

> वल्ली गाढं वृक्षं परिष्वजते तद्वत् । तथा सति । वाशब्द: समुच्चये । त्वं तस्य च
> पुरुषस्य मन इच्छॆ । कामयि । तस्य त्वं वशवर्तिनी भवेत्यर्थः । स च पुरुषस्तव मन
> इच्छतु । अधाध परस्परवशवर्तित्वानंतरं त्वं तेन सह सुभद्रां सुकल्याणीं संविदं
> परस्परसंभोगसुखसंवित्तिं कृणुष्ट । कुरुष्ट ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yama speaks to Yamī again. "O Yamī, embrace another man alone, and embrace him well. Another man will embrace you, as a creeper (लिबुजीव (*libujīva*)) embraces a tree, that is, as a vine clasps a tree tightly." The word वा (*vā*) is used in the sense of joining. "Desire the mind of that man", that is, be obedient to him. "And let that man desire your mind. Then, once you are mutually obedient, make with him a most auspicious union (संविदं (*saṃvidaṃ*)), a knowledge of the pleasure of mutual enjoyment."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यमि (*yami*)—O Yamī
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अन्यमु (*anyamu*)—another man alone

- लिबुजा (*libujā*)—a creeper
- वृक्षं इव (*vṛkṣaṃ iva*)—as it clasps a tree
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- परि ष्वजाते (*pari ṣvajāte*)—embraces
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that man
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind
- इच्छॆ (*icchè*)—desire
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- तव (*tava*)—let him desire you (love you)
- सुभद्रां (*subhadrāṃ*)—auspicious
- संविदं (*saṃvidaṃ*)—union
- कृणुष्ट्वा (*kṛṇuṣṭvā*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Yamī, embrace another man exceedingly. Let the other man embrace you as a creeper clasps a tree. Love him; let him love you deeply. Build an auspicious union with him.

### Printed p. 382

##### English translation
(Yama speaks). You, Yami, embrace another ; and let another embrace you as a creeper a tree : seek his affection, let him seek yours ; and make a happy union.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the word Yamī, Yāska has given the following etymological explanation for the present Ṛk: यमी व्याख्याता । तस्यैषा भवति। अन्यमू षु त्वं यम्यन्य उ त्वां परि ष्वजाते लिबुजीव वृक्षं । तस्य वा त्वं मन इच्छा स वा तनाधा कृणुस्व संविदं सुभद्रां ॥ अन्यमेव हि त्वं यम्यन्यस्त्वां परिष्वंक्ष्यते लिबुजीव वृक्षं तस्य वा त्वं मन इच्छ स वा तनाधानेन कुरुष्ट संविदं सुभद्रां कलाणभद्रां ॥ यमी यमं चकमे तां प्रत्याचक्षेत्याख्यानं ॥ (*yamī vyākhyātā | tasyaiṣā bhavati| anyamū ṣu tvaṃ yamyanya u tvāṃ pari ṣvajāte libujīva vṛkṣaṃ | tasya vā tvaṃ mana icchā sa vā tanādhā kṛṇusva saṃvidaṃ subhadrāṃ ‖ anyameva hi tvaṃ yamyanyastvāṃ pariṣvaṃkṣyate libujīva vṛkṣaṃ tasya vā tvaṃ mana iccha sa vā tanādhānena kuruṣṭa saṃvidaṃ subhadrāṃ kalāṇabhadrāṃ ‖ yamī yamaṃ cakame tāṃ pratyācakṣetyākhyānaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 11-34).
The word Yamī has been explained earlier. The present Ṛk is a mantra addressed to the woman Yamī: O Yamī, truly, embrace another man (leaving me), clasping him tightly as a creeper winds round a tree. You understand his mind and let him understand yours, and behave accordingly. O Yamī, with him, through this kind of pleasure of love, obtain excellent happiness and joy and be glad. This is what Yama said to Yamī in the past, when the woman Yamī loved her own elder brother Yama and desired sexual union with him.

## Sūkta 11 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषेति नवर्चमेकादशं सूक्तमांगेर्हविर्धानस्यार्षमाग्नेयं । सप्तम्याद्यास्ति प्रस्रिष्टुभः शिष्टा जगत्यः। तथा चानुक्रांतं । वृषा नवांगिर्हविर्धान आग्नेयं
> तु त्रित्रिष्टुबंतमिति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The eleventh sūkta, वृषा (*vṛṣā*), has nine Ṛks. Its seer is Havirdhāna Āṅgi, its deity Agni. From the seventh Ṛk onward the verses are triṣṭubh and the rest are jagatī. The Anukramaṇī says the same. The use of the sūkta has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta वृषा (*vṛṣā*) is the eleventh sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. Its seer is Havirdhāna Āṅgi; its deity is Agni; the three Ṛks from the seventh onward are in the triṣṭubh metre. The remaining

### Printed p. 383
Ṛks are in the jagatī metre. The Anukramaṇī says: वृषा नवांगिर्हविर्धान आग्नेयं तु त्रित्रिष्टुबंतं (*vṛṣā navāṃgirhavirdhāna āgneyaṃ tu tritriṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). The use of the sūkta has been stated earlier.

Sūkta 11
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 11.
Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 6; Vargas 9, 10.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 9.
Seer: Havirdhāna Āṅgi. **NOTE**
Deity: Agni.
Metre: 1-6 Jagatī; 7-9 Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृषा॒ वृष्णे॑ दुदुहे॒ दोह॑सा दि॒वः पयां॑सि य॒ह्वो अदि॑ते॒रदा॑भ्यः ।  
> विश्वं॒ स वे॑द॒ वरु॑णो॒ यथा॑ धि॒या स य॒ज्ञियो॑ यजतु  
> य॒ज्ञिया॑ ऋ॒तून् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषा । वृष्टे । दुदुहे । दोहसा । दिवः । पयांसि । यह्वः । अदितेः । अदाभ्यः ।  
> विश्वं । सः । वेद । वरुणः । यथा । धिया । सः । यज्जियः । यजतु । यज्जियान् ।  
> यतून् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषाहुतिद्वारेण वृष्टेर्वर्षिता यहो महानदाभ्यः केनाप्यहिंस्योऽग्निरदितेरक्षणायागक्रियस्य वृष्णो यज्ञद्वारेण स्तुतीनां हविषां वा वर्षितुर्यजमानस्यार्थाय दोहसा दोहनेन महता प्रक्षारणेन दिवः सकाशात्पयांसि वृष्टिलक्षणान्युदकानि दुदुहे । दोग्धि । प्रक्षारयति । किंच यथा वरुण आदित्यो
> धियात्मानुरूपया प्रज्ञया विश्वं सर्वं वेद जानाति तथा सोऽयमग्निर्जानातीत्यर्थः । यज्जियो यज्ञार्हो यज्जियान् यज्ञार्हानृतून्यजतु। पूजयतु!

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is the showerer (वृषा (*vṛṣā*)): through the oblation he is the rainer of rain. He is great (यह्वः (*yahvaḥ*)) and unharmed by anyone (अदाभ्यः (*adābhyaḥ*)). For the protection of the sacrificer, whose sacrificial work is imperishable (अदितेः (*aditeḥ*)), and who is the showerer of praises or oblations through the sacrifice, he milks (दुदुहे (*duduhe*)) with a great milking (दोहसा (*dohasā*)), that is, a great pouring out, the waters in the form of rain from heaven. Further, as Varuṇa, that is Āditya, knows everything by his understanding (धिया (*dhiyā*)) suited to himself, so does this Agni know. Fit for sacrifice (यज्जियः (*yajjiyaḥ*)), may he worship the seasons fit for sacrifice (यज्जियान् (*yajjiyān*)).

- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the giver of desired objects
- यह्वः (*yahvaḥ*)—the great
- अदाभ्यः (*adābhyaḥ*)—the unharmed Agni
- अधितेः (*adhiteḥ*)—of the one whose sacrificial work is imperishable
- वृष्टः (*vṛṣṭaḥ*)—for the sacrificer who offers oblations
- दोहसा (*dohasā*)—by squeezing and milking the cloud
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the atmosphere
- पयांसि (*payāṃsi*)—the waters of rain
- दुदुहे (*duduhe*)—he milks
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Āditya
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—by his understanding
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—everything
- वेद (*veda*)—knows, so
- सः (*saḥ*)—Agni also knows
- यज्जियः (*yajjiyaḥ*)—fit for sacrifice
- सः (*saḥ*)—Agni
- यज्जियान् (*yajjiyān*)—worthy of worship
- ऋतून् (*ṛtūn*)—relying on the sacrificial seasons
- यजतु (*yajatu*)—let him worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the giver of desired objects, the great, the unharmed, squeezes the clouds and pours rain for the sacrificer, whose sacrificial work is imperishable and who offers oblations. As Āditya knows everything by his understanding, so also does Agni know. May Agni, who is fit for sacrifice, worship, relying on the sacrificial seasons that are worthy of worship.

##### English translation
The great, the unconquerable (Agni), the showerer, milks openly with a (great) milking the streams (of prosperity) from heaven for the un-wearying sacrifice; like Vaurna, he knows everything by his under-standing : may he who is skilled in sacrifice observe the sacrificirl seasons.

> इ॒ष्टस्य॒ मध्यॆ॒ अदि॑ति॒र्निधा॑तु नो॒ भ्राता॑ नो ज्ये॒ष्ठः प्र॑थ॒मो  ॑

> रपत् । गंधर्वीः । अप्या । च । योषणा । नदस्य । नादे । परि । पातु । मे । मनः ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रसद्रपितवत्यग्निगुणानुक्तवती गंधर्वीर्गंधर्वस्य स्त्रैस्याद्भिः संस्कृता
> योषणाहुतिलक्षणा स्त्री च । अग्निं तर्पितवतीति शेषः । नदस्य । स्तोतृनामैतत् ।
> स्तोतुर्मे मम स्वभूतं मनो नादे स्तुतिलक्षणे शब्दे परि पातु । अग्निः सम्यग्रक्षतु । अहं समाहितमना भूत्वा सम्यक् स्तुतिं करोमीत्यर्थः । किंचादितिरुखंडनीयोऽग्निर्नोऽस्मानिष्टस्य यागस्य मध्यॆ नि धातु । निदधातु । नितरां स्थापयतु ।
> प्रथमः सर्वेषां यजमानानां मुख्यो नोऽस्माकं ज्येष्ठो भ्राता वि वोचति ।
> विशेषेण ब्रवीति । स्तौतीत्यर्थः । नाहमेव केवलो यजनशीलः किंतु सर्व
> एवास्मत्कुलीनो देवयागप्रिय इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

रपत् (*rapat*) is the one who speaks, that is, who has spoken the qualities of Agni. गंधर्वीः (*gaṃdharvīḥ*) is the Gandharva's woman, and अप्या (*apyā*) means consecrated with waters; योषणा (*yoṣaṇā*) is the woman in the form of the oblation. The supplied word is "has gratified Agni". नदस्य (*nadasya*) is a name for a praiser. Let Agni fully guard my own mind, mine who am the praiser, in the sound (नादे (*nāde*)) which is praise. The meaning is: I, with a collected mind, make the praise properly. Further, let Agni, Aditi, the unbreakable one, place us in the midst of the sacrifice (इष्टस्य (*iṣṭasya*)). The first, the chief of all sacrificers, our elder brother, speaks specially, that is, praises. The meaning is that not I alone am given to sacrificing, but everyone of our family loves the worship of the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रपत् (*rapat*)—reciting the qualities of Agni
- गंधर्वीः (*gaṃdharvīḥ*)—the Gandharvī
- अप्या (*apyā*)—she who is consecrated with water
- योषणा च (*yoṣaṇā ca*)—and the woman possessing the form of the oblation **NOTE**
- नदस्य (*nadasya*)—of the praiser
- मे (*me*)—my
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind
- नादे (*nāde*)—in the sound in the form of praise
- परिपातु (*paripātu*)—let her guard completely
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—the perfect Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- इष्टस्य (*iṣṭasya*)—of the sacrifice
- मध्यॆ (*madhyè*)—in the middle
- नि धातु (*ni dhātu*)—let him establish
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—the chief among the sacrificers
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ज्येष्ठः भ्राता (*jyeṣṭhaḥ bhrātā*)—elder brother
- वि वोचति (*vi vocati*)—recites the praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the Gandharvī who recites the qualities of Agni, the woman consecrated with water and having the form of the oblation, make my mind, the mind of the praiser, rest in the act of praise. May the perfect Agni establish us in the middle of the sacrifice. The chief of all sacrificers, our elder brother also, recites the praise.

##### English translation
The Gandharvi and the water-consecrated feminine oblation praise Agni: may He be favourable to the thought of me, raising my voice in his praise: may Agni place us in the midst of the sacrifice; the chief (of the worshippers), our elder brother, repeats his various laudations.

> xxvii 25

> सो इति । चित् । नु । भद्रा । क्षुमती । यशस्वती ! उषाः । उवास । मनवे ।  
> स्वःसवती ।  
> यत् । ईं । उशंतं । उशतां । अनु । क्रतुं । अग्निं । होतारं । विदथाय ।  
> जीजनत् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भद्रा भजनीया क्षुमती शब्दवती यशस्वत्यन्नवती कीर्तिमती ना सो चित्
> सैव प्रसिद्धोषा मनवे मनुष्याय यजमानाय स्वर्व्यादित्यवती सती नु
> क्षिप्रमुवास । उषितवती । उदितवतीत्यर्थः । कदोदितवतीति उच्यते । यद्यदोशंतं स्तुतिं हविश्च कामयमानमुशतां यष्टुं कामयमानानां संबंधिनं
> होतारं देवानामाह्वातारं होमनिष्पादकं वेमेनमग्निमनु क्रतुं स्तुतिकर्मणः पश्चाद्विदथाय यजनीयाय यज्ञार्थं जीजनन् । ऋत्विग्यजमाना
> जनयंतीत्यर्थः । तदोदितवतीति संबंधः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

भद्रा (*bhadrā*) is the lovely one (to be resorted to), क्षुमती (*kṣumatī*) the one possessing sound, यशस्वती (*yaśasvatī*) the one possessing food and fame. That same well-known Uṣas, accompanied by the sun (स्वर्वती (*svarvatī*)), has quickly dawned (उवास (*uvāsa*)) for man (मनवे (*manave*)), the sacrificer, that is, she has risen. When did she rise? It is said: when, after the act of praise, for the sacrifice (विदथाय (*vidathāya*)), the priests and sacrificers beget this Agni, who desires praise and oblation, who is connected with those wishing to sacrifice, the invoker of the gods and accomplisher of the oblation. The meaning is that the priests and sacrificers bring him forth; she rose then.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- उशंतं (*uśaṃtaṃ*)—the one who desires the oblation
- उशतां (*uśatāṃ*)—for the gods who desire the oblation
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the one who gives the invocation
- ईं अग्निं (*īṃ agniṃ*)—this Agni
- अनुक्रतुं (*anukratuṃ*)—only after the act of praise
- विदथाय (*vidathāya*)—for the sacrifice
- जीजनन् (*jījanan*)—when the priests produce, then
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—the auspicious one
- क्षुमती (*kṣumatī*)—the one possessing sound
- यशस्वती (*yaśasvatī*)—the one possessing food
- सो चित् उषाः (*so cit uṣāḥ*)—that same famous goddess Uṣas
- मनवे (*manave*)—for the benefit of man
- स्वर्वती (*svarvatī*)—accompanied by Āditya
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- उवास (*uvāsa*)—has risen

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the priests, for the sacrifice and only after the act of praise, produce this Agni, who himself desires the oblation and who gives the invocation to the gods who desire the oblation, then that same famous goddess Uṣas, auspicious, possessing sound and food, accompanied by Āditya, has quickly risen for the benefit of man.

### Printed p. 387

##### English translation
That very auspicious, resounding, famous Dawn, ascends bringing the sun to man; when for the sacrifice after the worship they give birth to that Agni, the desirer, the invoker of the desiring (gods).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध॒ त्यं द्र॒प्सं वि॒भ्वं॑ विचक्ष॒णं विराभ॑रदिष॒तः श्ये॒नो अ॑ध्व॒रे ।  
> यदी॒ विशो॑ वृ॒णते॑ द॒स्ममार्या॑ अ॒ग्निं होता॑र॒मध॒ धीर॑जायत ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । त्यं । द्रप्सं । विभ्वं । विचक्षणं । विः । आ । अभरत् । इषितः । श्येनः , अध्वरे  
> यदि । विशः । वृणते । दस्मं । आर्याः । अग्निं । होतारं । अध । धीः i अजायत !

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अधाथानंतरं श्येनः श्येनाख्यो वि पक्ष्यध्वरे याग इषितोऽग्निप्रेषितो
> विभ्वं महांतं विचक्षणं सर्वस्य विशेषेण द्रष्टारं त्यं तं प्रसिद्धं द्रप्पं नात्यल्पं
> नातिबहुलं सोममाभरत् । आह्ृतवान् । अपि च यदि यदार्या अभिगमनीयं
> तं व्रजंतो विशो यजमाना मनुष्या दस्म्यं दर्शनीयं शत्रूणामुपक्षपयितारं वा होतारमग्निं वृणते प्रार्थयंते अध तदा धीर्यागादिक्रियाजायत :
> यज्जभिः प्रतायत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that after this (अध (*adha*)), the bird called Śyena, sent by Agni to the sacrifice, brought that famous Soma drop (द्रप्सं (*drapsaṃ*)). The Soma is great (विभ्वं (*vibhvaṃ*)), a seer of all in a special way (विचक्षणं (*vicakṣaṇaṃ*)), and is "not too little and not too much". Further, when the Āryas, that is, the sacrificers, the men who go to him as one to be approached, choose Agni the Hotṛ, whom he glosses as "fair to look upon" or "the one who destroys enemies" (दस्मं (*dasmaṃ*)), and pray to him, then the rite (धीः (*dhīḥ*)), the sacrificial action, came into being, that is, it was extended by the sacrifices.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध (*adha*)—afterwards
- श्येनः (*śyenaḥ*)—named Śyena
- विः (*viḥ*)—the bird
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- इषितः (*iṣitaḥ*)—impelled by Agni
- विभ्वं (*vibhvaṃ*)—the great one
- विचक्षणं (*vicakṣaṇaṃ*)—the one of subtle sight
- त्यं (*tyaṃ*)—the famous one
- द्रप्सं (*drapsaṃ*)—the flowing Soma
- आभरत् (*ābharat*)—brought
- यदि (*yadi*)—when
- आर्याः (*āryāḥ*)—worshippers of Agni
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—the sacrificers
- दस्म्यं (*dasmyaṃ*)—one of attractive form
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the Hotṛ
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- वृणते (*vṛṇate*)—pray to
- अध (*adha*)—then
- धीः (*dhīḥ*)—the action in the form of the sacrifice
- अजायत (*ajāyata*)—began

### Printed p. 388

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The bird called Śyena, sent by Agni to the sacrifice, brought the great, subtle-sighted, famous, flowing Soma. When the sacrificers, worshippers of Agni, pray to Agni, who is of attractive form and is the Hotṛ, then the action in the form of the sacrifice was begun.

##### English translation
The hawk sent (by Agni) to the sacrifice has brought the dripping copious all-seeing (soma) libration. When the Arya people choose the victorious Agni as the ministrant priest, then the sacred rite is celebrated.

> भूरिभिः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं सदा सततं रणोऽसि । रमणीयो भवसि । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> यवसेव पुष्यते यथा यवसानि तृणानि च पुष्टिं कुर्वते हस्त्यस्वगोमहिषादिचतुष्पदाय सर्वदा रमणीयानि भवंति तद्वत् । अपि च हे अग्ने मनुषो
> मनुष्यस्य स्वभूतैर्होत्राभिः । होत्रेति यज्ञनामैतत् । यज्ञैः स्वध्वरः
> शोभनयज्ञो भवेति शेषः। विप्रस्य वा स्तोतुर्वा यद्यस्य यजमानस्य वा स्वभूतमुक्थं स्तोत्रं शशमानः प्रशंसन् वाजं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं ससवान् संभजमानश्च
> भूरिभिर्बहुभिर्देवैः सहोपयासि उपगच्छसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, you are always delightful (रण्वः (*raṇvaḥ*))." The illustration: as grasses and fodder (यवसानि (*yavasāni*)), which nourish elephants, horses, cows, buffaloes and other quadrupeds, are always pleasing to them, so are you. Further, O Agni, with the sacrifices of man (होत्राभिः (*hotrābhiḥ*); होत्रा (*hotrā*) is a name for sacrifice), be one of fair sacrifice (स्वध्वरः (*svadhvaraḥ*)), "be" being the word to supply. Praising the hymn (उक्थं (*ukthaṃ*)) belonging to the wise one, the singer, or to the sacrificer, and enjoying the food in the form of the oblation (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)), you come (उपयासि (*upayāsi*)) together with many gods.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, as pasture is attractive to cattle and others who desire their nourishment, so you are always attractive to us. Be worshipped in the best manner with the sacrifices of man. Praising the hymn of the singer of praise or of the sacrificer, and partaking of the food in the form of the oblation, come near to our sacrifice with many gods.

You, Agni, are ever pleasing (to your worshippers), as pasture satisfies (the herds); be well-worshipped with man's sacrifices; if commending the praise of the wise, and partaking of the (sacrificial) food, you come with many (divinities to the rite).

> हे अग्ने त्वदीयं ज्योतिः पितरा पितरौ सर्वप्राणिनां मातापितृभूते

> मत्या बुद्धा वेपते । कर्मवैगुण्याद्भिभ्यत्कंपते । हे अग्ने यतो यजमानः
> सर्वर्त्वजश्च स्वस्वकर्म कर्तुं त्वामागच्छंति अतस्त्वं शीघ्रमुद्दमयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, send up your light towards the parents (पितरा (*pitarā*)), Heaven and Earth, who are mother and father of all beings. The illustration: the particle आ (*ā*) is in the sense of comparison. Because he brings to an end (*jarayitṛtvāt*) the night and the lights of the stars and the like, the Sun is जार (*jāra*); as he sends up towards Heaven and Earth his adorable light (भगं (*bhagaṃ*)), so do you. The sacrificer wishes to worship (इयक्षति (*iyakṣati*)) the gods who desire the sacrifice, and with his heart he longs (इष्यति (*iṣyati*); the root इषि (*iṣi*) has the sense of going, and the plain form is to be seen as preceded by a prefix, "he approaches to worship the gods"). विवक्ति (*vivakti*) is "he wishes to speak" the praises in the form of śastras. The bearer (वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)), the Hotṛ, who conveys the praises to the gods, wishes to do his own good work (स्वपस्यते (*svapasyate*)). मखः (*makhaḥ*) is a name for sacrifice; here the Adhvaryu, who performs it, is meant; he "wishes to increase" (तविष्यते (*taviṣyate*); the root तविषि (*taviṣi*) has the sense of growth and here includes a desiderative meaning) the praises in the form of stotras. असुरः (*asuraḥ*) is "possessed of life or of wisdom", the Brahman priest being supplied; he trembles (वेपते (*vepate*)) in thought through fear of a defect in the rite. Since the sacrificer and all the priests come to you to do their own work, you should therefore rise up quickly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जारः (*jāraḥ*)—the Sun
- भगं (*bhagaṃ*)—as he spreads his adorable splendour
- पितरा (*pitarā*)—towards Heaven and Earth
- उदीरय (*udīraya*)—spread your splendour
- हर्यतः (*haryataḥ*)—the gods who desire the sacrifice
- आ इयक्षति (*ā iyakṣati*)—the sacrificer wishes to worship
- हृत्तः (*hṛttaḥ*)—with the mind
- इष्यति (*iṣyati*)—wishes
- विवक्ति (*vivakti*)—wishes to recite the praise
- वह्नः (*vahnaḥ*)—the Hotṛ
- स्वपस्यते (*svapasyate*)—wishes to do excellent work
- मखः (*makhaḥ*)—the Adhvaryu
- तविष्यते (*taviṣyate*)—wishes to increase the praise
- असुरः (*asuraḥ*)—the Brahman
- मती (*matī*)—together with his understanding
- वेपते (*vepate*)—becomes intent on the rite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, as the Sun spreads his adorable splendour, spread your splendour towards Heaven and Earth. The sacrificer wishes to worship the gods who desire the sacrifice; he wishes it with all his heart; he wishes to recite the praise. The Hotṛ wishes to do excellent work, the Adhvaryu wishes to increase the praise. The Brahman, together with his understanding, becomes intent on the rite.

##### English translation
Wake up the parents, as the Sun his splendour: (the worshipper) desires to offer worship to (the deities) who are pleased by it; with all his

### Printed p. 391

heart he wishes (to do so); he desires to repeat (your praise); the bearer (of the oblation) is anxious to effect the good work; the sacrifice longs for augmentation, the prudent (sacrificer) trembles in his thoughts.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the various meanings of the word आ (*ā*) in this Ṛk, Yāska says that आ (*ā*) also has the sense of comparison, and cites this Ṛk in that connection:
अथाप्युपमार्थे दृश्यते । जार आ भगं । जार इव भगं । आदित्योऽत्र जार उच्यते । रात्रेजरयिता । स एव भासां ॥ (*athāpyupamārthe dṛśyate | jāra ā bhagaṃ | jāra iva bhagaṃ | ādityo 'tra jāra ucyate | rātrejarayitā | sa eva bhāsāṃ ‖*) (Ni. 3-16)
The prefix आ (*ā*) is also used in the sense of comparison, that is, of likeness. In the sentence जार आ भगं (*jāra ā bhagaṃ*) of the present Ṛk, the word आ (*ā*) has the sense of comparison, "like", so that it means "adorable like the Sun". Here the word जार (*jāra*) means the Sun. रात्रेजरयिता तदुदये हि रात्रिर्जीर्यते विपरिणमतीत्यर्थः (*rātrejarayitā tadudaye hi rātrirjīryate vipariṇamatītyarthaḥ*)—that is, because he brings the night to an end, the Sun is called जार (*jāra*). The meaning is that with the rising of the Sun the time of night comes to an end.

> बुद्धिं यो मर्तो मनुष्यो यजमानोऽक्षत् अश्नुते । अनुग्रहशीलं त्वां

> प्रकर्षेण श्रूयते । प्रख्यातो भवतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशः । इषमन्नं वधानोऽथिभ्यः

> द्युस्थानवान्वामवान्बलवाना ड्यून् । दुरित्यहर्नाम ॥ कालाद्वनोरत्यंतसंयोग
> इत्येषा द्वितीया ॥ आदित्यकर्तृकाण्यहानि । आचंद्रार्कमित्यर्थः । भूषति । भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, son of strength (सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*), "son of might"), the mortal, the human sacrificer, who obtains (अक्षत् (*akṣat*), "attains") your good, gracious mind (सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)), that is, serves you, who are gracious by nature, with praises and oblations, becomes widely renowned (अति प्रशृण्वे (*ati praśṛṇve*)), heard of beyond all worlds. Of what kind is he? He gives food (इषं (*iṣaṃ*)) to petitioners and is borne by horses. Moreover he alone, after the falling of the body, is radiant (द्युमान् (*dyumān*)), possessed of a place in heaven or of strength (अमवान् (*amavān*)). द्यून् (*dyūn*) is a name for days; the accusative here is the second case taught by the rule "for time and road, continuous connection". The days are those caused by the Sun, that is, as long as the moon and sun last. भूषति (*bhūṣati*) is भवति (*bhavati*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O son of strength
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ते (*te*)—your
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—excellent gracious mind
- यः मर्तः (*yaḥ martaḥ*)—the sacrificer who
- अक्षत् (*akṣat*)—obtains
- सः (*saḥ*)—that sacrificer
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- दधानः (*dadhānaḥ*)—giving to petitioners
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—by horses
- वहमानः (*vahamānaḥ*)—being borne
- अति प्रशृण्वे (*ati praśṛṇve*)—obtains renown in abundance
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same sacrificer
- आ द्यून् (*ā dyūn*)—every day
- द्युमान् (*dyumān*)—radiant
- अमवान् (*amavān*)—powerful
- भूषति (*bhūṣati*)—becomes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of strength, the sacrificer who obtains your excellent gracious mind gives food to petitioners, is borne by horses, and obtains renown in abundance. That same sacrificer becomes, every day, radiant and powerful.

##### English translation
Agni, son of strength, the mortal who obtains your fovaur is widely celebrated: possessing abundant food, and being conveyed by horses, illustrious and vigorous, he graces the days of his existence.

> अस्माभिः स्तूयंत इज्यंते चेत्यर्थः । हे स्वधावो हविर्लक्षणान्नवन्नग्ने त्वं
> यद्यदा रत्ना च रत्नानि रमणीयानि धनानि स्तोतृभ्यो यष्टृभ्यश्च विभजासि विभजसि
> अत्र तदानीं तथा नोऽस्मान्प्रति वसुमंतं धनवंतं नानाधनावयवभूतं भागमंशं नीतात् ॥ वी गत्यादिषु । स्तुह्योस्तातज्ञाशिष्यन्यतरस्यां । पा-७-१-३५ । इति
> हे स्थाने तातज् । अंतर्णीतण्यर्थश्चात्र द्रष्टव्यः ॥ वयय । आगमय । अस्मभ्यं
> प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāvrata, when the Marutvatīya has been completed, one should offer ghee drawn four times with this verse, यदग्न एषा (*yadagna eṣā*); so it is laid down in the Fifth Āraṇyaka: यदग्न एषा समितिर्भवाति (*yadagna eṣā samitirbhavāti*) (Ai. Ā. 5.1-1). Sāyaṇa's gloss: O adorable Agni, when this united body of praise, composed by us, shines as a goddess among the gods who are to be worshipped (we praise and worship the gods to be worshipped), and when you, O owner of oblation-food, distribute lovely treasures to the singers and to the sacrificers, then at that time bring us also a share made up of wealth, a portion consisting of various parts of riches. The root वी (*vī*) is used in the sense of going and the like; by Pā. Sū. 7-1-35 tātaṅ replaces the ending hi. A causative sense is to be understood within it: cause to go, bring, give to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)—O you who have food in the form of oblation
- यजत्र (*yajatra*)—O worshipful one
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- *eṣā samitiḥ*—this multitude of our praises
- यजता (*yajatā*)—by those worthy of worship
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—joining the gods
- देवी (*devī*)—shining
- भवाति (*bhavāti*)—becomes
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- रत्ना च (*ratnā ca*)—lovely treasures
- विभजासि (*vibhajāsi*)—you apportion to the singers
- अत्र (*atra*)—at that time
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us also
- भागं (*bhāgaṃ*)—a share
- वसुमंतं (*vasumaṃtaṃ*)—endowed with wealth
- वीशात् (*vīśāt*)—grant

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who have food in the form of oblation and are worshipful: when this multitude of our praises, joining the worshipful gods, shines forth, and when you apportion lovely treasures to the singers, then at that time grant us also a share endowed with wealth.

### Printed p. 394

##### English translation
When, adorable Agni, this united praise is resplendent amongst the adorable gods, and when you, bearer of the oblation, apportion the precious (treasures), then allot to us a valuable share

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

While the Mahāvrata rite is being performed, in the Marutvatīya śastra mantras, ghee is to be taken four times with this Ṛk beginning यदग्न एषा (*yadagna eṣā*), placed in the sruk-ladle and offered as a homa. This is laid down in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, in the fifth Āraṇyaka, by the sentence यदग्न एषा समितिर्भवाति (*yadagna eṣā samitirbhavāti*).
#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्रु॒धी नो॑ अग्ने॒ सद॑ने स॒धस्थे॑ यु॒क्त्वा रथ॑म॒मृत॑स्य द्रवि॒त्नुं।  
> आ नो॑ वह॒ रोद॑सी दे॒वपु॑त्रे॒ माकि॑र्दे॒वाना॒मप॑ भूरि॒ह  ॑
> स्याः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रुधि । नः । अग्ने । सदने । सधस्थे । युक्षव रथं । अमृतस्य । द्रवित्नुं ।  
> आ । नः । वह । रोदसी इति । देवपुत्रे इति देवपुत्रे । माकिः । देवानां । अप ।  
> भूः । इह । स्याः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने सधस्थे सहस्थाने सर्वदेवतासाधारणे सदने यज्ञगृहे स्थितः सन्नोऽस्मदीयं वचनं श्रुधि । शृणु । किं तद्वचनं उच्यते । अमृतस्य देवपानस्य मधुनो द्रवित्नुं द्रावकं रथमात्मीयं युक्ष्व । आह्वानार्थं देवान्प्रति गमनायाश्वै: संयुक्ष्व । संयुक्तेन रथेन गत्वा नोऽस्माकं यज्ञं प्रति देवपुत्रे
> देवस्य प्रजापतेर्दुहितरौ यद्वा देवाः पुत्रा ययोस्ते रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावा वह । प्रापय । देवानां मध्यॆ कश्चिद्देवोऽप भूरपभवितास्मद्यज्जादपगंता
> माकिः स्यात् । त्वं चेहास्मिन्यज्ञे स्याः । संनिहितो भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, being in the house of sacrifice, the common seat of all deities, hear our word. What is it? Yoke your own chariot, which makes flow the ambrosia, the divine drink of honey; yoke it with horses to go to the gods and invite them. Having gone by the yoked chariot, bring to our sacrifice the two daughters of the god Prajāpati, or else the two whose sons are gods, heaven and earth. Let no god among the gods be one who stays away from our sacrifice; and may you yourself be here in this sacrifice, be present.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, being in the house of sacrifice where all the gods assemble, hear our praise. Yoke your chariot that pours out ambrosia. Bring to our sacrifice heaven and earth, the daughters of Prajāpati. Let none among the gods stay away from our sacrifice. You also be near us.

##### English translation
Agni, present in the dwelling common (to the deities) hear us : harness your swift chariot of ambrosia: bring to us the heaven and earth, the daughters of the divine (Prajapati), let none of the gods be absent, and you yourself be present.
## Sūkta 12 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्यावेति नवर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तमांगेर्हविर्धानस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमाग्नेयं । द्यावेत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The twelfth sūkta, of nine verses, beginning द्यावा (*dyāvā*); the seer is Havirdhāna Āṅgi, the deity Agni, the metre Triṣṭubh. So the Anukramaṇī records: द्यावेत्यनुक्रांतं (*dyāvetyanukrāṃtaṃ*). The ritual application has been given.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning द्यावा (*dyāvā*) is the twelfth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. Its seer is Havirdhāna Āṅgi; its deity is Agni; its metre is Triṣṭubh. The application of the sūkta has been stated earlier.

### Printed p. 396

> असुं । यन् ॥ १ ॥

> सत्यवाचा सत्यवाचौ सत्यवादिन्यौ प्रथमे प्रधानभूते द्यावा क्षामाद्युक्षामे
> द्यावापृथिव्यावृतेन सत्यभूतेन देवयजनेन सहाभिश्रावे । अभिमुख्येन श्रूयत
> इत्यभिश्राव आह्वानं । तस्मिन्नस्यद्यज्ञनिमित्तेऽग्नेः संबंधिन्याह्वाने भवतः ॥ लोडर्थे
> लट् ॥ भवतां । यद्यदा देवो द्योतमानोऽग्निर्यजथाय यज्ञाय मर्तान्मनुष्यान् क्वण्वन्रेरयन् प्रत्यजाह्वानार्थं देवानां प्रत्यंचिता स्वमसुमात्मीयं ज्वालालक्षणं प्राणं यन् प्राप्नुवन् होता देवानामाह्वाता सीदत् वेद्यां
> निषेदति । तदास्मद्यजनकाले द्यावापृथिवी प्रमुखोऽग्निराह्वयत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Heaven and earth, truthful in speech, the two foremost, are present together with the true rite of divine worship at the invocation, अभिश्रावे (*abhiśrāve*): what is heard face to face is the *abhiśrāva*, the call. At that call connected with Agni and occasioned by this sacrifice they are present (the present tense is used in the sense of the imperative: let them be). When the shining god Agni, urging mortals to sacrifice, moves facing the gods to invite them, attaining his own life-breath in the form of flame, and sits on the altar as the Hotṛ, the caller of the gods, then, at our sacrifice, may Agni, with heaven and earth foremost, call the gods.

- यजथाय (*yajathāya*)—for sacrifice
- मर्तान् (*martān*)—men
- कृण्वन् (*kṛṇvan*)—urging
- प्रत्यज् (*pratyaj*)—in front of them

- यन् (*yan*)—attaining
- होता (*hotā*)—in the form of Hotṛ

- सत्यवाचा (*satyavācā*)—those whose speech is true
- प्रथमे (*prathame*)—the foremost
- द्यावा क्षामा (*dyāvā kṣāmā*)—heaven and earth

- भवतः (*bhavataḥ*)—let them be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the shining Agni, urging men to sacrifice and spreading his flame before them, sits in the place of the Hotṛ, then may heaven and earth, true in speech and foremost, together with the divine people who are of the nature of truth, accept Agni's invocation.

##### English translation
Haven and earth, declarers of truth, principal (of things), be present at the invocation, associated with the rite, when the divine (Agni), exciting mortals to sacrifice, sits down in their presence as the invoker (of the gods) putting forth his flame.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The shining Agni, you, surrounding the gods, Indra and the others, by way of calling them and carrying the oblation, grasping them, carry our oblation, together with the sacrifice, to them; bring it.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

What manner of being are you? The first, the chief of the gods; चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*), knowing all; धूमकेतुः (*dhūmaketuḥ*), maker of smoke, or having smoke as banner, or having smoke as his mark; by समिधा (*samidhā*), kindling, he is भायुजीकः (*bhāyujīkaḥ*), of straight radiance, that is, flaming upward; मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*), praiseworthy; the Hotṛ, the caller; नित्यः (*nityaḥ*), constant; and by speech the best of sacrificers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समिधा (*samidhā*)—by the act of kindling
- भायुजीकः (*bhāyujīkaḥ*)—having an upward-turned flame
- मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*)—worthy of praise
- होता (*hotā*)—in the form of Hotṛ
- नित्यः (*nityaḥ*)—eternal
- वाचा (*vācā*)—with praise
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—worshipper of the gods
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—shining
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods, Indra and others
- परिभूः (*paribhūḥ*)—encompassing
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—with sacrifice

- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, chief among all the gods, knower of everything, having a banner in the form of smoke, having by the act of kindling an upward-turned flame, worthy of praise, shining: encompassing the gods, Indra and the others, convey our oblation to them with the sacrifice.

##### English translation
You, bright (Agni), surrounding the gods, carry our oblation with due rites; you, who are the chief (of the deities), the wise, the smoke-bannered, fuel-kindled, straight-flaming, adorable, the invoker, the constant sacrificer with prayer. -

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, for the word भायजीकः (*bhāyajīkaḥ*) Yāska gives the explanation: भायजीक प्रसिद्धभाः (*bhāyajīka prasiddhabhāḥ*) ! धूमकेतुः समिधा भायजीकः इत्यपि निगमो भवति (*dhūmaketuḥ samidhā bhāyajīkaḥ ityapi nigamo bhavati*) (Ni. 6-4). That is, the word भायजीकः (*bhāyajīkaḥ*) means "having a well-known radiance". In this matter he says that the sentence of the present Ṛk, धूमकेतुः समिधा भायजीकः (*dhūmaketuḥ samidhā bhāyajīkaḥ*), is itself the scriptural illustration.
