> देवस्याग्नेः स्वावृक् स्वार्जनममृतमुदकं स्वतेजसः सकाशाद्यदि यदोत्पद्यते तदातोऽस्माद्गॊरुदकाज्ञातास उत्पन्ना ओषधॆय उर्वी द्यावापृथिव्यौ
> धारयंति । विश्वे देवाः सर्वॆ स्तोतारस्ते तव संबंधि तद्यजुरुदकस्य तद्दानमनु
> गुः । अनुगायंति । एनी श्वेता दीप्तिर्दिव्यं दिवि भवं धृतं क्षरद्यद्वा वृष्टिलक्षणं
> यदुदकं दुहे दोग्धि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of the divine Agni, the self-won ambrosia, which is water, arises from his own brightness. When it arises, the plants born from this water, उर्वी (*urvī*) (heaven and earth), sustain them. विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*) are all the praisers. *tadyajuḥ* is that gift of water, belonging to you, Agni, and they sing after it. एनी (*enī*) is the white gleam (flame). It milks out the celestial ghee, that is, the water in the form of rain, that streams forth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of the divine Agni
- स्वावृक् (*svāvṛk*)—self-aggregated
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—water
- यदि (*yadi*)—when it is produced, then
- अतः गोः (*ataḥ goḥ*)—from that same water
- जातासः (*jātāsaḥ*)—the plants produced
- उर्वी (*urvī*)—sustain heaven and earth
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- एनी (*enī*)—your shining flames
- दिव्यं (*divyaṃ*)—belonging to the heavenly world
- घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*)—flowing
- वाः (*vāḥ*)—water in the form of rain
- दुहे (*duhe*)—milk out
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the praisers
- ते (*te*)—given by you
- तत् यजुः (*tat yajuḥ*)—that gift of water
- अनु गुः (*anu guḥ*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the self-aggregated water of the divine Agni arises, then the plants born from that same water sustain heaven and earth. O Agni, when your shining flames milk out the water that belongs to the heavenly world, that flows, and that is in the form of rain, then all the praisers praise that gift of water given by you.

##### English translation
When the self-aggregated ambrosia of the divine Agni is generated from his radiance, then the products from it sustain both heaven and earth ,

### Printed p. 400

##### English translation
all the worshippers glorify this your oblation, the celestial nutritious water which your white lustre milks forth.

> अहा॒ यद्दावोऽसु॑नीति॒मय॒न्मध्वा॑ नो॒ अत्र॑ पि॒तरा॑ शिशीतां ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वमपो मदीयं यज्ञरूपं कर्म वर्धाय प्रोत्सर्पिते सति
> हे धृतस्नू वृष्ट्युदकस्य प्रसवित्र्य हे द्यावाभूमिा द्यावापृथिव्यौ नां युवामर्चामि ॥ ऋच स्तुतौ ॥ स्वामि । हे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ युवां मे
> मदीयं स्तोत्रं शृणुतं । यद्यस्मिन्नहा अहःशब्दसामर्थादहोरात्रसाध्यं
> कर्मोच्यते ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्येकवचनस्याजादेशः ॥ अहन्यहोरात्रसाध्यकर्मणि द्यावः स्तोतारोऽसुनीतिं । असुः प्रज्ञा । तया नीयत इत्यसुनीति
> स्तुतिः । तामयन् गच्छंति अत्रास्मिन्कर्मणि पितरा सर्वस्य मातापितृभूते द्यावापृथिव्यौ नोऽस्मान्वृष्ट्युदकेन शिशीतां । स्नानपानादिना संस्कुरुतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, when you advance my sacrificial rite, हे धृतस्नू (*he dhṛtasnū*), O you two that pour out the rain-water (the pada reads घृतस्नू (*ghṛtasnū*)), हे द्यावाभूमिा (*he dyāvābhūmiā*), heaven and earth, I praise you. हे रोदसी (*he rodasī*), heaven and earth, hear my hymn. अहा (*ahā*): from the force of the word अहः (*ahaḥ*) it means a rite accomplished by day and night. In that rite, द्यावः (*dyāvaḥ*), the praisers, go to असुनीतिं (*asunītiṃ*): असुः (*asuḥ*) is understanding, and that by which one is led is असुनीति (*asunīti*), praise. In this rite let पितरा (*pitarā*), heaven and earth, the mother and father of all, sanctify us with rain-water, with bathing, drinking and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अपः (*apaḥ*)—my sacrificial rite
- वर्धाय (*vardhāya*)—make it prosper
- घृतस्नू (*ghṛtasnū*)—you that pour out water
- द्यावाभूमी (*dyāvābhūmī*)—O heaven and earth
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- अर्चामि (*arcāmi*)—I praise
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—O heaven and earth
- मे (*me*)—my hymn
- शृणुतं (*śṛṇutaṃ*)—hear
- अहा (*ahā*)—accomplished by day and night
- यत् (*yat*)—in which rite
- द्यावः (*dyāvaḥ*)—the praisers

- असुनीतिं (*asunītiṃ*)—praise
- अयन् (*ayan*)—compose
- अत्र (*atra*)—in that rite
- पितरा (*pitarā*)—heaven and earth, mother and father of the world
- मध्वा (*madhvā*)—with rain-water
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- शिशीतां (*śiśītāṃ*)—let them sanctify

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, make my sacrificial rite prosper. O heaven and earth, who pour out water, I praise you. O heaven and earth, hear my hymn. In whatever rite, accomplished by day and night, the praisers compose praise, in that rite let heaven and earth, the mother and father of the world, sanctify us with rain-water.

##### English translation
I worship you, waters that pour forth ghee, and you, heaven and earth, for your increase ; hear me, you worlds ; when worshippers at the daily or nightly rite proceed to their pious purpose, then may the parents (of all) sanctify us with ambrosia.

> मित्रः । चित् । हि । स्म । जुहुराणः । देवान् । श्लोकः । न । यातां । अपि । वाजः ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> किंस्विच्छब्दो वितर्कार्थे । किंवा राजा दीप्यमानोऽग्निर्नोऽस्माकं स्वभूतानि हवींषि स्तुतीश्च जगृहे परिगृह्लीयात् किंवास्याग्नेरिति व्रतमतिपूजितं परिचरणाख्यं कर्म चक्रम वयं क्रियास्म । कर्मवैगुण्याद्भीतस्य पूर्वार्ध एतद्वचनमु-
> xxvii 26
> xxvii 26

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The word किंस्वित् (*kiṃsvit*) is in the sense of conjecture. Will the shining king Agni accept our own oblations and praises? And have we performed for this Agni the highly honoured rite called service? The first half of the verse is said by one who fears a defect in the rite; now, in the second half, that fear is removed.

### Printed p. 402

> क्तं । उत्तरार्ध इवानीं तन्निराक्रियते । हि स्त्रीतिमा पूरणा । चिदित्युपमार्थे ।
> जुहुराणः स्निग्धमाहूयमानो मित्रः स्निग्धो यथा गच्छेत् तथा । नेति संप्रत्यर्थे । श्लोकोऽस्मदीया स्तुतिलक्षणा वाग्देवानिंद्रादीन्यातां । गच्छतु । अपि
> वाजो हविराख्यं चान्नं यदस्ति तदपि देवान्प्रति गच्छतु । देवाः स्तुतिं हविश्च प्रतिगृह्णंतित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

हि स्म (*hi sma*) is a mere filler. चित् (*cit*) is in the sense of comparison. जुहुराणः (*juhurāṇaḥ*) means "affectionately invited": as a friend who is dear goes when so invited. न (*na*) is in the sense of "now". Let our श्लोकः (*ślokaḥ*), our speech consisting of praise, go to the gods, Indra and the others. And whatever food called oblation there is, let that also go to the gods. The meaning is that the gods accept both praise and oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजा (*rājā*)—the shining Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—our oblations
- किं स्वित् जगृहे (*kiṃ svit jagṛhe*)—will he indeed accept?
- अस्य (*asya*)—directed to Agni
- अतिव्रतं (*ativrataṃ*)—the rite of the nature of service
- तत् चक्रम (*tat cakrama*)—have we really performed it?
- कः वि वेद (*kaḥ vi veda*)—who knows this?
- जुहुराणः (*juhurāṇaḥ*)—invited with trust
- मित्रश्चित् (*mitraścit*)—as a friend goes with affection
- श्लोकः (*ślokaḥ*)—our praise
- देवान् (*devān*)—to the gods, Indra and the rest
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—let it go and reach them
- अपि (*api*)—and
- वाजः अस्ति (*vājaḥ asti*)—whatever food in the form of oblation there is, let that also go and reach them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Will the shining Agni indeed accept our oblations? Have we really performed the rite of service directed to this Agni? Who knows this? As a friend invited with trust goes with affection, let our praise go and reach the gods, Indra and the rest. Let the oblation offered by us also go and reach them.

##### English translation
But will the royal Agni accept our oblations? Have we duly performed our vows to him? Who decides? As a friend affectionately invited, so let our praise now proceed to the gods; together with the sacrificial food that is left over.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्रास्मिन्कर्मणि कृतेऽमृतस्य यमस्य नाम दुर्मंतु दुर्वचनं भवति ।
> यद्यस्मै सलक्ष्मा विषमरूपा भगिनी भार्या भवति । तत्तु न तथा इति यमं यः
> स्तौति सुवचनमस्य नामेति तं स्तोतारं दर्शनीयाग्ने अप्रयुच्छन् अप्रमाद्यन्
> रक्षः ॥
> यद्यस्य अमृतस्य मरणधर्मरहितस्य सूर्यस्य । अस्य मरणधर्मराहित्यं
> तु सूर्यो विषमा सजामीत्यस्यां ऋचि प्रसिद्धं । तादृशस्य संबधि नाम नाम कमुदकं अत्र अस्यां पृथिव्यां विषुरूपा नानारूपं भवाति भवति । उदकस्य नानारूपत्वं या आपो दिव्या इति मंत्रे स्पुटमुक्तं । कीदृशं तत् । दुर्मंतु
> निरपराधं प्रह्वस्वभावत्वात् । पुनः कीदृशं । सलक्ष्म्य मधुररसरूपलक्षणोपेतं ।
> किं च यः सूर्यः यमस्य संयमिनीपतेः सुमंतु सुतरामपराधं मातृताडनरूपं मनवते अवबुध्यते सर्वज्ञत्वात् । यद्वा धातूनामनेकार्थत्वात् क्षमत
> इत्यर्थः । तं तादृशं जलजनकं सर्वज्ञं क्षमाशीलं सूर्यं हे ऋष्ट महन्नग्ने
> अप्रयुच्छन् अप्रमाद्यन् त्वं पाहि । आहुतिप्रदानेन रक्षणद्वारात्मरक्षणं प्रार्थयते ऋषिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

First explanation: when the rite has been performed here, the name of the immortal Yama is दुर्मंतु (*durmaṃtu*), ill to speak, because his wife, a sister with the same marks but of unlike form, comes to be. That is not so. Whoever praises Yama, saying "his name is well spoken", that praiser, O beautiful Agni, protect, unslothful and heedful.

Second explanation (यद्वा (*yadvā*)): of the immortal Sūrya, who is free from the nature of death. His deathlessness is well known in the ṛc *sūryo viṣamā sajāmi*. His name, the नाम (*nāma*), is water; here on this earth it becomes विषुरूपा (*viṣurūpā*), of many forms. The manifold nature of water is stated plainly in the mantra या आपो दिव्या (*yā āpo divyā*). How is that water? दुर्मंतु (*durmaṃtu*), faultless, because of its humble nature. And सलक्ष्मा (*salakṣmā*), endowed with the marks of a sweet taste.

Further, the Sūrya who, being omniscient, understands the very great fault, in the form of beating the mother, of Yama, lord of Saṃyamanī; or, because roots have many meanings, who forgives it. That Sūrya, the producer of water, omniscient and forbearing, O great Agni, protect, unslothful. The seer asks for his own protection by way of the protection given through the offering of oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अत्र (*atra*)—at the time of this rite
- यमस्य (*yamasya*)—of Yama
- नाम (*nāma*)—the nature
- दुर्मंतु (*durmaṃtu*)—it is hard to understand
- यत् सलक्ष्मा (*yat salakṣmā*)—although of one kind of mark
- विषुरूपा (*viṣurūpā*)—possessed of many kinds of form
- भवाति (*bhavāti*)—he is
- सुमंतु (*sumaṃtu*)—who understands his nature well
- ऋष्ट्व (*ṛṣṭva*)—and is a great soul
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- मनवते (*manavate*)—beneficial to men
- यमस्य (*yamasya*)—to Yama
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whoever offers worship
- तं (*taṃ*)—him
- अप्रयुच्छन् (*aprayucchan*)—free of sloth
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the time of this rite the nature of Yama is hard to understand. Although he has one kind of mark, he is of many kinds of form. O Agni, who understand his nature well and are a great soul, protect, free of sloth, whoever offers worship to Yama, who is beneficial to men.

##### English translation
Hard to understand is the nature of the immortal, for although of one origin, she is of a different form ; cherish him delegently, great Agni, who understands Yama's nature easy to be understood.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्मिन्नग्नौ यज्ञस्य प्रधानांशे सति देवा इंद्रादयो विदथे यज्ञॆ मादयंते हविषात्मानं तर्पयंति तृप्यंति वा । अपि च विवस्वतो मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य स्वभूते सदने वेद्याख्ये स्थाने धारयंते । आत्मानं स्थापयंति च ।
> किंच सूर्ये ज्योतिरहराख्यं तेजोऽदधुः । स्थापितवंतः । मासि चंद्रमस्यक्कूनात्रिः स्थापितवंतः । तदनंतरमजस्रानुपक्षीणौ सूर्याचंद्रमसौ द्योतनिं
> दीप्तिं परि चरतः । परिगच्छतः । सर्वत्र प्राप्नुतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In that Agni, the principal part of the sacrifice, the gods, Indra and the others, delight at the विदथे (*vidathe*), the sacrifice; they gratify themselves, or are gratified, with the oblation. Moreover, in the सदने (*sadane*), the place called the altar, belonging to the sacrificer, the man विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*), they hold themselves and establish themselves. Further, they have set in the sun the light called day, the radiance; in the moon they have set the nights. After that, the sun and moon, unfailing and undiminished, go about द्योतनिं (*dyotaniṃ*), the brightness, and reach it everywhere.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in that famous Agni, by offering oblation
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Indra and the others
- विधथे (*vidhathe*)—in the sacrificial house
- मादयंते (*mādayaṃte*)—obtain delight
- विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)—of the sacrificer
- सदने (*sadane*)—in the sacrificial house
- धारयंते (*dhārayaṃte*)—establish their existence (therefore)
- सूर्ये (*sūrye*)—in the sun
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—radiance
- अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*)—they have established
- मासि (*māsi*)—in the moon
- अक्तून् (*aktūn*)—the nights they have established
- अजस्रा (*ajasrā*)—the eternal sun and moon
- द्योतनिं (*dyotaniṃ*)—their brightness
- परि चरतः (*pari carataḥ*)—spread all around

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Through the offering of oblation in the famous Agni, the gods, Indra and the others, obtain delight in the sacrificial house. They are established in the sacrificer's sacrificial house. Because they have obtained delight in this way, they have established radiance in the sun and have established the night in the moon. The eternal sun and moon spread their brightness all around.

### Printed p. 405

##### English translation
In him the gods find pleasure at the sacrifice; they seat themselves on the altar of the sacrificer. They placed light in the sun; beams in the moon; and these untiring shed their light around.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्मि॑न्दे॒वा मन्म॑नि सं॒चरं॑त्यपी॒च्ये॒३॒॑ ३ न व॒यम॑स्य विद्म ।  
> मि॒त्रो नो॒ अत्रादि॑ति॒रना॑गान्त्सवि॒ता दे॒वो वरु॑णाय  
> वोचत् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्मिन् । देवाः । मन्मनि । संचरंति । अपीच्ये । न । वयं । अस्य । विद्म ।  
> मित्रः । नः । अत्र । अदितिः । अनागान् । सविता । देवः । वरुणाय । वोचत् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवा इंद्रादयो यस्मिन्नग्नौ मन्मनि ज्ञानभूते ज्ञानवत्सर्वप्रकाशके सति
> संचरंति स्वाधिकारे संप्रवर्तंते अपीच्येऽंतर्हिते स्थितमग्नेः स्वरूपं वयं न
> विद्म । तत्त्वतो न जानीमः । आत्रास्मिन्यज्ञेऽंगभावाय वर्तमानो मित्रो वरुणाय सर्वेषां पापानां निवारयित्रेऽग्नये नोऽस्माननागानपापान्वोचत् ।
> ब्रवीतु । तथादितिर्देवमाता सविता सर्वस्य प्रेरको देवश्च ब्रवीतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, Indra and the others, move about, that is, go on with their own duties, when Agni is present as "mannani", that is, as the embodiment of knowledge, the knowing illuminator of all. When that form of Agni stands "अपीच्ये (*apīcye*)", hidden from view, we do not know it; we do not truly know it. Mitra, who is present here in this sacrifice as a part of it, is to speak of us as sinless to Varuṇa, that is, to Agni, the averter of all sins. In the same way Aditi, the mother of the gods, and Savitṛ, the god who impels everything, are to speak.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Indra and the others
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—that same Agni
- मन्मनि (*manmani*)—when he is manifest to our sight
- संचरंति (*saṃcaraṃti*)—they move about
- अस्य (*asya*)—this one's form
- अपीच्ये (*apīcye*)—when Agni is hidden
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- न विद्म (*na vidma*)—cannot know
- अत्र (*atra*)—taking a share in this sacrifice
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—the god Mitra
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—before Agni, the averter of sin
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अनागान् (*anāgān*)—as free from sin
- वोचत् (*vocat*)—let him declare
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aditi also
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the god in nature
- सविता (*savitā*)—Savitṛ also, let him declare and speak

### Printed p. 406

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When this Agni becomes visible to all of us and an object of knowledge, the gods, Indra and the others, move about here. When Agni is hidden we cannot know his form. May the god Mitra, who takes a share in this sacrifice, declare us sinless before Agni, the averter of sin. May Aditi, and Savitṛ, divine in nature, declare us sinless.

##### English translation
When he, the all-illumining, is there, the gods assemble ; but when he concealed, we know not (his abode) ; so at this sacrifice let Mitra and Aditi and Savitri proclaim us to Varuna as free from sin.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्रु॒धी नो॑ अग्ने॒ सद॑ने स॒धस्थे॑ यु॒क्त्वा रथ॑म॒मृत॑स्य द्रवि॒त्नुं।  
> आ नो॑ वह॒ रोद॑सी दे॒वपु॑त्रे॒ माकि॑र्दे॒वाना॒मप॑ भूरि॒ह  ॑
> साः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रुधि । नः । अग्ने i सदने । सधस्थे । युक्षव रथं । अमृतस्य । द्रवित्नुं ।  
> आ । नः । वह । रोदसी इति । देवपुत्रे इति देवपुत्रे । माकिः । देवानां । अप ।  
> भूः । इह । स्याः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने सधस्थे सहस्थाने सर्वदेवतासाधारणे सदने यज्ञगृहे स्थितः सन्नोस्मदीयं वचनं श्रुधि । शृणु । किं तद्वचनं उच्यते । अमृतस्य देवपानस्य मधुनो द्रवित्नुं द्रावकं रथमात्मीयं युक्ष्व । आह्वानार्थं देवान्प्रति गमनायाश्चै: संयुक्ष्व । संयुक्तेन रथेन गत्वा नोऽस्माकं यज्ञं प्रति देवपुत्रे
> देवस्य प्रजापतेर्दुहितरौ यद्वा देवाः पुत्रा ययोस्ते रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावा वह । प्रापय । देवानां मध्यॆ कश्चिद्देवोऽप भूरपभवितास्मद्यज्ञादपगंता
> माकिः स्यात् । त्वं चेहास्मिन्यज्ञे स्याः । संनिहितो भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, being seated in the "sadana", the sacrificial house, which is the "sadhasthe", the place shared by all the deities, hear our words. What are they? Harness your own chariot, which makes the ambrosia, the honey drunk by the gods, flow; harness it with horses so as to go to the gods to invite them. Having gone with the harnessed chariot, bring to our sacrifice "devaputre", the two daughters of the god Prajāpati, or else the two "रोदसी (*rodasī*)", heaven and earth, whose sons are the gods. Let no god among the gods be "अप भूः (*apa bhūḥ*)", fall away or go away from our sacrifice; and you also be here, present at this sacrifice.

- सधस्थे (*sadhasthe*)—where all the gods assemble
- सदने (*sadane*)—being in the sacrificial house
- नः (*naḥ*)—our praise
- श्रुधि (*śrudhi*)—hear
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—ambrosia
- द्रवित्नुं (*dravitnuṃ*)—that makes flow

- युक्षव (*yukṣava*)—harness

- देवपुत्रे (*devaputre*)—the daughters of Prajāpati
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, being in the sacrificial house where all the gods assemble, hear our praise. Harness your chariot that makes ambrosia flow. Bring to our sacrifice heaven and earth, the daughters of Prajāpati. Let none among the gods escape our sacrifice. You too be near us.

##### English translation
Agni, present in the dwelling common (to the deities) hear us : harness your swift chariot of ambrosia: bring to us the heaven and earth, the daughters of the divine (Prajapati), let none of the gods be absent, and you yourself be present.

## Sūkta 13 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Pīṭhike**

The Havirdhāna carts.

The carts that serve as the means of bringing Soma, king of the Gandharvas, to the sacrificial ground are called Havirdhāna carts. Just as Soma is lord over gods, men and the rest, so these carts that carry him are also in the form of lords over gods, men and the rest.

सप्त क्षरंति शिशवे मरुत्वते पित्रे पुत्रासो अप्यवीवतन्नृतं । उभे इदस्योभयस्य राजत उभे यतेते उभयस्य पुष्यतः ॥ (*sapta kṣaraṃti śiśave marutvate pitre putrāso apyavīvatannṛtaṃ | ubhe idasyobhayasya rājata ubhe yatete ubhayasya puṣyataḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-13-5)

### Printed p. 408
In this verse Soma is praised as a son to the Havirdhāna carts, and the Havirdhāna carts that have such a son are praised as lords over all gods, men and the rest, and also as nourishers of them all. Just as Soma is an indispensable means to the sacrifice, which nourishes and upholds the world, so the carts that bring that Soma are also means to it. Just as Soma is born of a divine portion, so these Havirdhāna carts too are born of a divine portion. The order of their origin is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows.

देवासुरा वा एषु लोकेषु समयतंत ते ना असुरा इमानेव लोकान् पुरोऽकुर्वत यथौजीयांसो बलीयांस एवं ते ना अयस्मयामेवेमामकुर्वत रजतामंतरिक्षं हरिणीं दिवं ते तथेमान् लोकान् पुरोऽकुर्वत ते देवा अब्रुवन् पुरो वा इमेऽसुरा इमान् लोकानक्रत पुर इमान् लोकान् प्रतिकरवामहा इति तथेति ते सद एवास्याः प्रत्यकुर्वताग्नीध्रमंतिक्षाद्दविर्धाने दिव .... ॥ (*devāsurā vā eṣu lokeṣu samayataṃta te nā asurā imāneva lokān puro 'kurvata yathaujīyāṃso balīyāṃsa evaṃ te nā ayasmayāmevemāmakurvata rajatāmaṃtarikṣaṃ hariṇīṃ divaṃ te tathemān lokān puro 'kurvata te devā abruvan puro vā ime 'surā imān lokānakrata pura imān lokān pratikaravāmahā iti tatheti te sada evāsyāḥ pratyakurvatāgnīdhramaṃtikṣāddavirdhāne diva .... ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 1-23)

The gods and the Asuras contended for mastery over these worlds. Then the Asuras made all the worlds into strongholds: the earth a fortress of steel, the atmosphere one of silver, and the heaven a fortress of gold. Then all the gods assembled and resolved: "The Asuras have made these worlds into strongholds. Let us too, in opposition to them, make strongholds of greater power than theirs." So they strove, and made the Sadas from this earth, the Āgnīdhra from the atmosphere, and the Havirdhānas from the heaven; so it is stated. From this it is understood that the Havirdhānas are not merely helpful to the world but are protectors of the gods. Moreover the greatness of the Havirdhāna is praised exceedingly in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. What is the Havirdhāna? How did the name Havirdhāna come to be? What is its importance? These matters are described as follows in the passages quoted below.

पुरुषो वै यज्ञः । पुरुषस्तेन यज्ञो यदेनं पुरुषस्तनुत एष वै तायमानो यावानेव पुरुषस्तावान्विधीयते तस्मात्पुरुषो यज्ञः ॥ (*puruṣo vai yajñaḥ | puruṣastena yajño yadenaṃ puruṣastanuta eṣa vai tāyamāno yāvāneva puruṣastāvānvidhīyate tasmātpuruṣo yajñaḥ ‖*)
(Ka. Brā. 3-5-3-1) **NOTE**

The sacrifice is of the form of a man. Because the man extends and spreads out the sacrifice, there is identity between the sacrifice and the man. By such extension the sacrifice too attains just the measure of the man. Because of this likeness of measure, and also because of the relation of maker and the one made, the sacrifice has the name "man".

### Printed p. 409
शिर एवास्य हविर्ध्नं । वैष्णवं देवतयाथ यदस्मिन्सोमो भवति हविर्वै देवानाग्ं सोमस्तस्माद्दविर्ध्नं नाम ॥ ( (*śira evāsya havirdhnaṃ | vaiṣṇavaṃ devatayātha yadasminsomo bhavati havirvai devānāgṃ somastasmāddavirdhnaṃ nāma ‖ (*)
(Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-2)

For this sacrifice the Havirdhāna is the head; Viṣṇu is the deity of this Havirdhāna. Soma is contained in it. Soma is the oblation offered to the gods. Because it is filled with this Soma, this cart has the name Havirdhāna.

उभयतोद्वारग्ं हविर्धानं भवति । उभयतोद्वारग्ं सदस्तस्मादयं पुरुष अंतग्ं संतृणः प्रणिक्ते हविर्धाने उपतिष्ठते (*ubhayatodvāragṃ havirdhānaṃ bhavati | ubhayatodvāragṃ sadastasmādayaṃ puruṣa aṃtagṃ saṃtṛṇaḥ praṇikte havirdhāne upatiṣṭhate*)
(Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-7)

This Havirdhāna has doors on both sides. In the same way the Sadas also has doors on both sides. The man too is in the same condition. After being purified he enters it.

There is one Havirdhāna on the south side and one on the north. The southern Havirdhāna is the larger of the two; it is under the leadership of the Adhvaryu. The northern one is under the leadership of the Pratiprasthātṛ, the Adhvaryu's assistant. Both of them carry their respective Havirdhānas toward the west. Then, proceeding in pradakṣiṇa fashion, both lead them to the neighbourhood of the inner enclosure of the sacrificial altar.

ते समवर्तयंति । दक्षिणेनैव दक्षिणमुत्तरेणोत्तरं यद्वर्षीयस्तद्दक्षिणं स्यात् ॥ (*te samavartayaṃti | dakṣiṇenaiva dakṣiṇamuttareṇottaraṃ yadvarṣīyastaddakṣiṇaṃ syāt ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. ?-5-3-8) **NOTE**

Then, in pradakṣiṇa fashion, they take those two Havirdhānas to the south and the north. The Havirdhāna of the south is the larger of the two.

तयोः समववृक्तयोः। धदिरधिनिदधति । यदि छदिर्न विंदेयुष्फदिः संमितां भित्तिं प्रत्यानह्यंति रराट्यां परिश्रयंत्युच्छ्रायीभ्यां छदिः पश्चादधिनिदधति छदिः सम्मितां वा भित्तिं (*tayoḥ samavavṛktayoḥ| dhadiradhinidadhati | yadi chadirna viṃdeyuṣphadiḥ saṃmitāṃ bhittiṃ pratyānahyaṃti rarāṭyāṃ pariśrayaṃtyucchrāyībhyāṃ chadiḥ paścādadhinidadhati chadiḥ sammitāṃ vā bhittiṃ*)
(Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-9)

After the circumambulation they place them on the sacrificial altar and cover them with grass called "chadi" (or a mat made of darbha grass). Or, if a mat of reed grass is not found, a reed mat of equal size may be spread. They also set them between two straight screens. And they place a second mat behind the first one and cover them.

### Printed p. 410
विप्रा विप्रस्य बहृतो विपश्चितः । .... .... मही देवस्य सवितुः परिष्टुतिः स्वाहेति तत्सावित्रं प्रसवाय जुहोति (*viprā viprasya bahṛto vipaścitaḥ | .... .... mahī devasya savituḥ pariṣṭutiḥ svāheti tatsāvitraṃ prasavāya juhoti*)
(Śa. Brā. 3-5-3.12)

Then the priests are the Brahma-knowers, the most intelligent among the learned, and the inspirers of supreme faith and knowledge मही देवस्य सवितुः परिष्टुतिः (*mahī devasya savituḥ pariṣṭutiḥ*): "The praise of the god Savitṛ, divine in nature, is great." With these words of praise (the Adhvaryu) offers an oblation of ghee to Savitṛ, the impeller of all.

अथापरं चतुर्गृहीतमाज्यं गृहीत्वा । उपनिष्क्रामति दक्षिणया द्वारा पत्नीं निष्क्रामयंति स दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्य दक्षिणायां वर्तन्याग्ं हिरण्यं निधाय जुहोतीदं विष्णुर्विचक्रमे त्रेधा निदधे पदं । समूढमस्य पाग्ं सुरे स्वाहेति सग् स्रवं पत्नैः पाणावानयति साक्षस्य संतापमुपानक्ति देवश्रुता देवेष्टाघोषतमिति प्रयच्छति प्रतिप्रस्थात्रेस्रुचं चाज्यविलापनीं च पर्याणयंति पत्निमुभौ जघनेनाग्नी (*athāparaṃ caturgṛhītamājyaṃ gṛhītvā | upaniṣkrāmati dakṣiṇayā dvārā patnīṃ niṣkrāmayaṃti sa dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasya dakṣiṇāyāṃ vartanyāgṃ hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya juhotīdaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame tredhā nidadhe padaṃ | samūḍhamasya pāgṃ sure svāheti sag sravaṃ patnaiḥ pāṇāvānayati sākṣasya saṃtāpamupānakti devaśrutā deveṣṭāghoṣatamiti prayacchati pratiprasthātresrucaṃ cājyavilāpanīṃ ca paryāṇayaṃti patnimubhau jaghanenāgnī*)
(Śa. Brā. 3-5.3-13)

The sacrificer takes ghee drawn four times and comes out a second time by the front door. His wife is led out by the door on the south side. Then the sacrificer places a gold coin on the right-hand wheel-track of the southern Havirdhāna and then recites the praise of Viṣṇu beginning इदं विष्णुर्विचक्रमे (*idaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame*) … समूढं (*samūḍhaṃ*) …: "Viṣṇu strode across these three worlds. By the dust raised by the stepping of his foot three times, this whole world was pervaded" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 22. 17), and offers the ghee. The remaining part of the ghee he pours into his wife's hand. Then she, praying "The gods are to be informed of this arrival", smears with that ghee the linchpin fixed into the axle of the wheel of that chariot (the Havirdhāna). Afterwards the sacrificer entrusts the ghee vessel and the pin (saṃtāpa) to his assistant. Then his wife goes in by the door at the back.

चतुर्गृहीतमाज्यं गृहीत्वा प्रतिप्रस्थातोत्तरस्य हविर्धानस्य दक्षिणायां वर्तन्यां हिरण्यं निधाय जुहोतिरावती धेनुमती ही भूतग्ं सूय वसिनी मनवे वशस्या । व्यस्नभ्नात् रोदसी विष्णुवेते दाधर्थ पृथिवीमभितो मयूख्यैः स्वाहेति सग्ग स्रवं पत्नैश्च पाणावानयति साक्षस्य संतापमुपानक्ति देवश्रुता देवेष्टाघोषतमिति तद्यदेवं जुहोति (*caturgṛhītamājyaṃ gṛhītvā pratiprasthātottarasya havirdhānasya dakṣiṇāyāṃ vartanyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya juhotirāvatī dhenumatī hī bhūtagṃ sūya vasinī manave vaśasyā | vyasnabhnāt rodasī viṣṇuvete dādhartha pṛthivīmabhito mayūkhyaiḥ svāheti sagga sravaṃ patnaiśca pāṇāvānayati sākṣasya saṃtāpamupānakti devaśrutā deveṣṭāghoṣatamiti tadyadevaṃ juhoti*)

Then, taking ghee drawn four times, the assistant places a gold coin on the wheel-track of the northern chariot (Havirdhāna) and, with the words "O Viṣṇu, may you, endowed with wealth of cattle and wealth of food, be a benefactor to Mānava (the sacrificer). You have set these two worlds apart and established them. By your radiance you have upheld this earth on every side", with this praise of Viṣṇu

### Printed p. 411

The praise of Viṣṇu so described is recited (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7. 99. 3), and the ghee is offered with the call svāhā. Then he pours the remaining part into the wife's hand. As before, she prays, "Let the gods be informed of this arrival," and anoints with ghee the pin that is fixed to the axle of that cart-wheel. The reason for offering the ghee-oblation and anointing the axle-pin in this way is as follows:

> देवा ह वै यज्ञं तन्वानाः । तेऽसुर रक्षकेभ्य आसंगाद्भिभयां चक्रुर्वज्रो वा आज्यं त एतेन वज्रेणाज्येन दक्षिणतो नाष्ट्रा रक्षाग् स्यवाघ्नंस्तथैषां नियानं नान्ववायंस्तथो एवैष एतेन वज्रेणाज्येन दक्षिणतो नाष्ट्रा रक्षाग् स्यवहंति तथास्य नियानं नान्ववयंति तद्यद्वैष्णवीभ्यामृग्भ्यां जुहोति वैष्णवग् हि हविर्भानं (श. ब्रा. ३-५-३-१५)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the gods were spreading the sacrifice they feared an attack from the asura-rakṣases. Ghee is a thunderbolt; with this thunderbolt of ghee they struck the rakṣases from the south, and so the rakṣases could not follow their path. In the same way the performer now strikes the rakṣases from the south with the thunderbolt of ghee, and they do not follow his path. He offers with two Viṣṇu verses because the havirdhāna belongs to Viṣṇu. (Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-15)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Once, when the gods were performing a sacrifice, they feared that an attack by asuras and rākṣasas might occur. With the help of ghee, which is equal to the thunderbolt weapon, they warded off the danger that could arise from the south. So even now, by offering ghee to the havirdhāna and anointing with it, the danger from that direction is averted. And since the havirdhāna belongs to the deity Viṣṇu, Viṣṇu must be praised and worshipped with Ṛk mantras. The need for the sacrificer's wife also to take part in this is as follows:

> अथ यत्पत्न्यक्षस्य संतापमुपानक्ति । प्रजननमेवैतत्क्रियते यदा वै

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As for the wife anointing the tip of the axle: this is done as an act of procreation. When a woman and a man are heated together, seed is shed, and from that there is birth. He anoints it outward (पराग् (*parāg*)), for seed is shed outward. Then he says, "Recite to the two havirdhānas as they are being moved forward." (Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-16)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

There is a hidden meaning in the wife's anointing the axle-pin, called saṃtāpa, with ghee. When husband and wife take pains together, the shedding of seed occurs and offspring is born. In the same way, even now their togetherness, and the wife's anointing of the pin with ghee while she stays beside the sacrificer, is the root of the production. As soon as she has anointed, he says to the hotṛ, "Recite the sentences praising the havirdhānas while they are moving."

> अथ वाचयति । प्राची प्रेतमध्वरं कल्पयंती इत्यध्वरो वैयज्ञः प्राची

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Then he has it recited: "Go eastward, preparing the sacrifice." Adhvara is the sacrifice; so this says, "Go eastward, preparing the sacrifice." "Lead the sacrifice upward; do not delay" means: lead this sacrifice upward to the world of the gods, do not delay. Then the text goes on to the asuric voice at the axle, that it must not (नेदिहासुर्या वाग्वादादि यद्युत्सर्जेतां (*nedihāsuryā vāgvādādi yadyutsarjetāṃ*)) sound here if the two should let it loose. (Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-17 **NOTE**) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 412

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

"O havirdhānas, move forward; make the sacrificial arrangement proceed" — he gives the direction to recite thus. The aim of this prayer is that the sacrifice be carried to the gods without suffering any deficiency. By the prayer "do not make this sacrifice halt," the meaning is that the sacrificer should be made to remain one whose rite is complete, not turning away from duty. Since the sound that arises at the axle is an asura sound, let the cart-wheel carry the cart forward without letting it sink. The creaking sound that arises in the region of the axle is a sign of ill omen. But if that asura-related creaking sound should arise — (here the Āsuryā Vāk is described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as Vāruṇī Durvāk; the praise of the havirdhāna in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā will be explained further on) —

> एतद्वाचयेत् । स्वं गोष्ठमावदतं देवी दुर्य्य आयुर्मा निर्वादिष्टं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

One should have this recited: "Make sound only in your own cattle-pen, O divine door-posts (or: divine ones); do not sound away my life, do not sound away my offspring." This is its expiation. (Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-18 **NOTE**)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

One must pray that no harm comes from that evil sound: "O you who have divine shelter, make your sound only for yourselves; do not cause the death of my life nor the cutting off of my progeny." The sacrificer must recite this. This is the remedy for it.

> तदाहुः । उत्तरवेदेः प्रत्यज् प्रकामेत्रीन् विक्रमांस्तद्धविर्धाने स्थापयेत्सा हविर्धानयोर्मात्रॆति नात्रमात्रास्ति यत्रैव स्वयं मनसा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They say: for this expiation to be effective, he should go three paces westward from the northern altar and set the havirdhānas there; this is the measure of the two havirdhānas. But there is no fixed measure here: where he himself thinks fit in his mind, he may set them, neither very near nor far. (Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-19 **NOTE**)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For this expiatory rite to succeed, he should go westward from the northern altar to a distance of three paces and set the havirdhānas there. This is the limit of the havirdhānas. But there is no fixed measure in this; he may set them wherever a place seems convenient to him. But that place must be neither very far from nor very near the northern altar.

> तेऽभिमंत्रयते । अत्र रमेथां वर्षन् पृथिव्या इति वर्ष हैतत्पथिव्यै

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He addresses them with a mantra: "Delight here on the height (वर्ष्मन् (*varṣman*)) of the earth." This is the height of the earth; the Āhavanīya is placed in heaven, as it were; he makes them stand on the navel, and that is the form of well-being. (Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-20)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Reciting "Delight on this high region of the earth," one should salute the havirdhānas. This altar is the highest region on earth (high is to be understood as excellent), and he makes the havirdhānas stand resting on their navel. The navel is the support of good standing.

### Printed p. 413

> अथोत्तरेण पर्येत्याध्वर्युः । दक्षिणग्ं हनिर्धानमुपस्तभ्नाति विष्णोर्नुकं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Then the Adhvaryu goes round by the north and props up the southern havirdhāna, reciting "I have proclaimed the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who measured the earthly regions, who propped up the upper abode, striding three times, far-going" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 154. 1), then "To Viṣṇu you" — and strikes in the wedge-post (मेधीं (*medhīṃ*)); it is different from what is done in ordinary human practice. (Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-21)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Then the Adhvaryu goes round from the north and gives support to the southern havirdhāna and makes it stand. For it to stand firm, he recites (1. 154. 1): "I proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who has made in a special way all the worlds such as the earth; who moves variously in the worlds he created; who, having built the very wide intermediate region, has established all the worlds firmly; who is all-pervading," and makes it stand firm. It is set up in a way more special than the order of setting up in ordinary time. This setting up is made secure with Viṣṇu as its object.

> अथ प्रतिप्रस्थाता । उत्तरग्ं हविर्धानमुपस्तभ्नाति दिवो वा विष्णवुत वा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Then the Pratiprasthātṛ props up the northern havirdhāna with "O Viṣṇu, from heaven or from the earth, or from the great wide intermediate region, fill both hands with wealth and give from right and left," and "To Viṣṇu you," and strikes in the wedge-post elsewhere than in ordinary practice. They serve with Viṣṇu formulas because the havirdhāna belongs to Viṣṇu.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Then the Pratiprasthātṛ, the Adhvaryu's assistant, sets up the northern havirdhāna. "O Viṣṇu, from the heaven-world, from the earth, or from the very wide intermediate region, come with both your hands filled with wealth, and make us covered with wealth on both our left and right sides" — thus praising Viṣṇu, he sets it in a place different from that of the ordinary setting up. Since the havirdhāna belongs to Viṣṇu, the praise of Viṣṇu is absolutely necessary.

> अथ मध्यमं छदिरुपस्पृश्य वाचयति । प्रतद्विष्णुः स्तवते वीर्येण मृगो

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Then, touching the middle cover (छदि (*chadi*)), he has it recited: "Viṣṇu is praised for his might, fearsome like a wild beast, roaming where he will, dwelling on the mountains, in whose three wide strides all beings abide" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 154. 2). This is the head-skull (*śīrṣakapālaṃ*) of this [havirdhāna]; the other skulls rest on it, and therefore he says "they abide upon." (Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-21)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Covering the reed mat spread in the middle he recites: "Viṣṇu, in whose very wide, three-numbered foot-strides all beings stand established, and who, like lions and other forest beasts, is terrible to enemies, a great tormentor of enemies and dwelling on the high regions of the mountains — that Viṣṇu is especially praised together with his heroic deeds" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-2). 

### Printed p. 414

This reed mat is the head-skull form of the havirdhāna (of Viṣṇu). All the other skulls rest on it. Therefore he recites the best praise.

> अथ रराट्यामुपस्पृश्य वाचयति विष्णो रराटमसीति ललाटग्ं हैवास्यैतदस्योच्छ्राय्या उपस्पृश्य वाचयति विष्णोः श्नप्रे स्थ इति प्रक्वे हैवा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Then, touching the front band (*rarāṭī*), he has it recited, "You are the forehead of Viṣṇu"; this is, as it were, his forehead. Touching the upright pieces he has it recited, "You two are the jaws (श्नप्रे (*śnapre*)) of Viṣṇu"; these are as it were his jaws. And as for the cover at the back, it is the head-skull. **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Then, touching the front binding, he praises: "O binding, you are the head-band, the ornament of Viṣṇu." Then, touching the straight upper strips, he praises: "You are the jaw regions of Viṣṇu." The cover at the back is the head-skull.

> अथ लस्पूजन्या स्पंद्यया प्रसीव्यति । विष्णोः सूर्यसीत्यथ ग्रंथिं करोति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Then he sews with a needle and a thread, "You are the weaver of Viṣṇu"; then he makes a knot, "You are the firm one of Viṣṇu," lest it fall off; he undoes it when the rite in hand is finished, so that no seizure (*grāhaḥ*) finds the Adhvaryu or the sacrificer. He touches the finished work: "You are Viṣṇu's," for the havirdhāna is Viṣṇu's. (Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-25) **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Praising "You are Viṣṇu's weaver," he threads the needle and sews the upper binding. So that it may not fall down, he tightens it with a knot and praises, "You are Viṣṇu's firm knot." As soon as the rite reaches the end of its recitation, he undoes that knot. For this reason no sloth touches either the Adhvaryu or the sacrificer. Since the havirdhāna itself belongs to Viṣṇu, he praises it, "You are connected with the self of Viṣṇu."

Although the Taittirīya Saṃhitā also praises these same parts in this praise and description of the havirdhāna, there are some differences in the account there; therefore the passages there are cited here. The praise of the havirdhāna in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā is as follows —

> बद्वमव स्यति वरुणपाशादेवैने मुंचति प्रणेनेक्ति मेध्यॆ एवैैने करोति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He unties the bound ones; thus he frees them from Varuṇa's noose; he cleanses them and makes them fit for sacrifice. Having offered with a verse addressed to Savitṛ, he sets the havirdhānas in motion; thus he sets them moving when impelled by Savitṛ. The ill-voice (दुर्वाक् (*durvāk*)) of Varuṇa is bound at both ends; if the axle should let it go, it would let it go against the sacrificer's houses; therefore he says "Speak well, O Speech divine (सुवाग्देव (*suvāgdeva*)), the ill-voice"; houses are the ill-voice's; the wife anoints them. (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-9-1) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 415

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as the binding is loosened, it is as if Varuṇa's noose has been loosened, and the havirdhānas become fit to take part in the sacrificial act. After reciting a mantra addressed to the deity Savitṛ and offering the oblation, he brings the havirdhānas forward. Savitṛ's impulsion itself is what helps in bringing them forward thus. The reed strip that is joined on both sides belongs to Varuṇa. It must not make the creaking evil sound. If it makes that sound, trouble comes to the sacrificer's house. "It makes a sound aiming at the houses; it makes them ill-fortuned." — they cause trouble to the sacrificer's houses. "O Goddess of Speech, make a good sound fit to do good to our houses" — thus he prays. Then his wife anoints them with ghee.

> पत्नी हि सर्वस्य मित्रं मित्रत्वाय यद्वै पत्नी यज्ञस्य करोति मिथुनं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The wife is a friend to all, for friendship; what the wife does for the sacrifice is a pairing (मिथुनं (*mithunaṃ*)), and this is the wife's continued taking-up of the sacrifice, for its unbrokenness. Following the track, the rakṣases would try to slay the sacrifice; he offers on the track with two Viṣṇu verses; the sacrifice is Viṣṇu; thus he strikes off the rakṣases from the sacrifice. If the Adhvaryu were to offer an oblation where there is no fire, he would become blind, and the rakṣases would strike the sacrifice.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer's wife is a friend to all who take part in the sacrificial work. It is through the wife's participation that the pairing favourable to the sacrifice is obtained. As described in sentences such as "For the continuity of the sacrifice the wife takes hold" (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-1-1), she holds the sacrificial thread so that the sacrifice may be accomplished without obstacle. In the present case she is the one who stops the sound of the cart's axle by anointing with ghee. If not, the rākṣasas would follow that sound, come, and cause obstacles to the sacrifice. To avoid that, the sacrificer follows yet another remedy. He recites mantras praising Viṣṇu and offers the oblation. The sacrifice itself is of Viṣṇu's form. Therefore with the help of reciting these Viṣṇu mantras he drives out the rākṣasas. If the Adhvaryu were to offer the oblation in a place without fire, he would become blind. Even then the rākṣasas might come and do violence to the sacrifice. Therefore —

> हिरण्यमुपास्य जुहोत्यग्निवत्येव जुहोति नांधोद्वर्युर्भवति न यज्ञग्ं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Having thrown gold (*hiraṇyaṃ*) he offers; thus he offers as if in fire, the Adhvaryu does not become blind, and the rakṣases do not strike the sacrifice. "Go eastward, preparing the sacrifice" he says; thus he makes them go to the heavenly world. "Delight here on the height of the earth" he says, for the place of divine worship is the height of the earth. The havirdhāna is the head of the sacrifice. With the verse "From heaven or from Viṣṇu or from the earth" he strikes the wedge-post of the southern havirdhāna; thus from the head of the sacrifice the sacrificer wins blessings.

### Printed p. 416

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

To reflect Agni at the front of the cart, he puts a gold coin there before offering the oblation. Then his oblation becomes as if offered in fire. The Adhvaryu does not become blind. The sacrifice too has no harm from the rākṣasas. Then, addressing the havirdhānas, "Go forward towards the sacrifice," he prays and makes them go to heaven. Since the sacrificial altar is the very highest place, he prays to the havirdhānas set on that altar, "Delight on the high region."

This havirdhāna is the head of the sacrifice. Reciting the mantra "दिवो वा विष्णो (*divo vā viṣṇo*)" he sets up the havirdhāna of the southern side. Therefore the sacrificer receives blessings right at the beginning of the sacrifice.

> दंडो वा औपरस्तृतीयस्य हविर्धानस्य वषट्कारेणाक्षमच्चिनद्यत्तृतीयं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The staff (*daṃḍaḥ*) of the Upara [pit] broke the axle of the third havirdhāna by the vaṣaṭ call. The third cover is cited among the two havirdhāna covers for the winning of the third havirdhāna. The havirdhāna is the head of the sacrifice; "You are the forehead of Viṣṇu, you are the back of Viṣṇu," he says; therefore this head is (so) joined. "You are the weaver of Viṣṇu, you are the firm one of Viṣṇu," he says; for the havirdhāna is Viṣṇu's by deity. The first knot that is tied should not be left unloosed, lest the Adhvaryu die from retention of urine; therefore it should be loosened. (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-9-4) **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

By reciting the vaṣaṭkāra, the staff belonging to the Upara bamboo broke the axle of the third havirdhāna. Therefore, in the present case, the third cover spread over the havirdhāna is the representative of the third havirdhāna. The havirdhāna is the head of the sacrifice. "O havirdhāna, you are the forehead of Viṣṇu, you are the back of Viṣṇu" — thus he praises it. Therefore this head is divided many times. "You are Viṣṇu's thread; you are Viṣṇu's eternal state" — it is also praised thus. This havirdhāna is wholly of Viṣṇu as its deity. At the end there is the loosening of the knot (undoing). If the knot tied first is not undone, the Adhvaryu's bladder would be blocked and he might perish. Therefore this loosening of the knot is absolutely necessary — thus, and so on, is the praise of the havirdhāna. The true nature of these same havirdhāna carts and their greatness are described in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows (Ai. Brā. 1-23). It directs the order of reciting the mantras praising it.

> हविर्धानाभ्यां प्रोह्यमाणाभ्यामनुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Adhvaryu says: "Recite to the two havirdhānas as they are being carried forward."

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Addressing the havirdhānas that are to be brought to the sacrificial ground, the Adhvaryu tells the hotṛ, "Recite the mantras praising them." Of these, first,

### Printed p. 417

Hotṛ recites युजे वां ब्रह्म पूर्व्यं नमोभिरित्यन्वाह (*yuje vāṃ brahma pūrvyaṃ namobhirityanvāha*) (Ai. Brā. 1-29). "O havirdhānas, reciting the most ancient mantras, I yoke you together with the oblations and the rest." With this, the Hotṛ recites this mantra first. Why this mantra should be recited is explained thus:

ब्रह्मणा ना एते देवा अयुंजत युद्धविर्धाने ब्रह्मणैवैने एतद्युंक्ते न वै ब्रह्मण्वद्रिष्यति ॥ (*brahmaṇā nā ete devā ayuṃjata yuddhavirdhāne brahmaṇaivaine etadyuṃkte na vai brahmaṇvadriṣyati ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 1-29)

In the past the gods themselves yoked the havirdhānas with this very mantra, and so the same rule holds now. One who has this mantra-power suffers no destruction. Therefore he first recites this mantra and afterwards recites the original mantras that praise Heaven and Earth. They are as follows:

प्रेतां यज्ञस्य शंभुवेति तृचं द्यावापृथिवीयमन्वाह (*pretāṃ yajñasya śaṃbhuveti tṛcaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīyamanvāha*)

These are the three mantras 1) प्रेतां यज्ञस्य शंभुवा (*pretāṃ yajñasya śaṃbhuvā*); 2) द्यावा नः पृथिवी इमं (*dyāvā naḥ pṛthivī imaṃ*); 3) आवामुपस्थमद्रुहा (*āvāmupasthamadruhā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2, 41. 19-21). When these mantras are recited, room is left for another doubt. It is this:

— तदाहुर्यद्धविर्धानाभ्यां प्रोह्यमाणाभ्यामनुवाचाहाथ कस्मात्तृचं द्यावापृथिवीयमन्वाह (*— tadāhuryaddhavirdhānābhyāṃ prohyamāṇābhyāmanuvācāhātha kasmāttṛcaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīyamanvāha*) (Ai. Brā. 1-29)

The doubt is: when mantras of praise are to be recited addressing the havirdhānas that are being carried to the sacrificial ground, what need is there here for reciting mantras addressed to Heaven and Earth? But there is no room for that doubt. Heaven and Earth were formerly the havirdhānas of the gods, and they are still the gods' havirdhānas. Since all oblations and all the other things as well are contained within Heaven and Earth, the name havirdhāna is well established for them. For that reason the three mantras addressed to them are to be recited. Afterwards,

यमे इव यतमाने यदैतं प्र वां भरन्मानुषा देवयंतः । (*yame iva yatamāne yadaitaṃ pra vāṃ bharanmānuṣā devayaṃtaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-13-2)

this fifth mantra is to be recited. The excellences praised in this mantra are as follows. In the first pāda:

### Printed p. 418

1) यमे इव हैते यतमाने प्रबाहुगितः (*yame iva haite yatamāne prabāhugitaḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 1-29). In the world, as twin girls born together in the womb of one mother stay together, so these two carts too always stay together for the benefit of the world. Like twin girls, the two resemble each other and shine with qualities common to both; therefore they are to be praised by reciting the mantra यमे इव (*yame iva*). In the second pāda:

2) प्रवां भरन्मानुषा देवयंतः इति देवयंतो ह्येने मानुषाः प्रभरंति । (*pravāṃ bharanmānuṣā devayaṃtaḥ iti devayaṃto hyene mānuṣāḥ prabharaṃti |*). O havirdhānas, by that greatness of yours by which you labour for the benefit of living beings, the priests and sacrificers devoted to the worship of the gods bring you to the sacrificial ground with exceeding devotion; thus the havirdhānas' nature of benefiting the world is indicated. Third (in the second half):

3) आसीदतं स्वमु लोकं विदाने स्नासस्थे भवतमिंदवे नः इति सोमो वै राजेंदुः सोमाय्कॆ वैने एतद्राज्ञ आसदेऽचीक्षृपत् ॥ (*āsīdataṃ svamu lokaṃ vidāne snāsasthe bhavatamiṃdave naḥ iti somo vai rājeṃduḥ somāykè vaine etadrājña āsade 'cīkṣṛpat ‖*). O havirdhānas, you are the most excellent seats for King Soma; therefore, knowing your places on the sacrificial ground, sit down — so it prays. Then follows the recitation of the sixth mantra. At this time he recites

अधि द्वयोरदधा उक्थं १ वच इति द्वयोर्ह्यतत्तृतीयं छदिरथि निधीयते । (*adhi dvayoradadhā ukthaṃ 1 vaca iti dvayorhyatattṛtīyaṃ chadirathi nidhīyate |*) (Ai. Brā. 1-29).

This is the praise of the third havirdhāna. The third havirdhāna means the chadi, which is its substitute. The covering that is spread to set Soma in place inside a havirdhāna is called chadi. Such chadis are spread over both havirdhānas and a third chadi is to be laid over them; this is also called the third havirdhāna. This is described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as दंडो ना औपरस्तेयस्य हविर्धानस्य (*daṃḍo nā auparasteyasya havirdhānasya*). Quoting and explaining this sentence (a variant reading is दंडो ना औदुंबरः (*daṃḍo nā auduṃbaraḥ*)), the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa states द्वयोर्ह्यतत्तृतीयं छदिरदि निधीयते (*dvayorhyatattṛtīyaṃ chadiradi nidhīyate*).

उक्थं वच इति यदाह यज्जियं वै कर्मोक्ष्यं वचो यज्ञमेवैतेन समर्धयति । (*ukthaṃ vaca iti yadāha yajjiyaṃ vai karmokṣyaṃ vaco yajñamevaitena samardhayati |*)

### Printed p. 419

That is, the import of this mantra (1. 83. 3) is as follows. As one common chadi is spread over both havirdhānas, so one single praise-mantra is offered in respect of both havirdhānas. This mantra is the means for the sacrificial rite; by this means the sacrifice prospers.

यतस्रुचा मिथुना या सपर्यतः । असंयत्तो व्रते ते क्षेति पुष्यतीति (*yatasrucā mithunā yā saparyataḥ | asaṃyatto vrate te kṣeti puṣyatīti*)

As newly married couples are honoured, so these havirdhānas, prepared with the ladle vessels, are honoured. The Adhvaryu who keeps such havirdhānas ready for the sacrifice becomes rich in peace.

यदेवादः पूर्वं यत्तवद्वदमाह तदेवैतेन शांत्या शमयति ॥ (*yadevādaḥ pūrvaṃ yattavadvadamāha tadevaitena śāṃtyā śamayati ‖*)

The word असंयत्तः (*asaṃyattaḥ*) that is used indicates abundance of peace. Thereby the Hotṛ (and the sacrificer and the Adhvaryu) performs the sacrificial work free from strife.

भद्रा, शक्तिर्यजमानाय सुन्नत इत्याशिषमाशास्त्रे ॥ (*bhadrā, śaktiryajamānāya sunnata ityāśiṣamāśāstre ‖*)

By the last pāda of this mantra a blessing is also recited: may all good fortune come to the sacrificer who, having finished the Soma-pressing rite, offers the oblation in the form of Soma. Next, seventh:

विश्वारूपाणि प्रतिमुंचते कविरिति विश्वरूपामन्वाह स रराट्यामीक्षमाणोS नुब्रूयात् ! विश्वमिव हि रूपं रराट्याः शुक्लमिव च कृष्णमिव च । विश्वं रूपमवरुंध आत्मने च यजमानाय च यत्रैवं विद्वानेतां रराट्यामीक्षमाणोऽन्वाह । (*viśvārūpāṇi pratimuṃcate kaviriti viśvarūpāmanvāha sa rarāṭyāmīkṣamāṇoS nubrūyāt ! viśvamiva hi rūpaṃ rarāṭyāḥ śuklamiva ca kṛṣṇamiva ca | viśvaṃ rūpamavaruṃdha ātmane ca yajamānāya ca yatraivaṃ vidvānetāṃ rarāṭyāmīkṣamāṇo 'nvāha |*)

Then the Hotṛ recites the mantra विश्वा रूपाणि (*viśvā rūpāṇi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-2). It is said that this mantra is to be recited while looking at the rarāṭī. The garland of darbha grass that is to be tied on the eastern side of the havirdhāna pavilion is called rarāṭī. Because this garland shows many forms, white, black and so on, if one recites this mantra while looking at this garland of universal form, he obtains for himself and provides for the sacrificer a prosperity of universal form: progeny, cattle and other wealth. Therefore this rite is prescribed. At the end the eighth mantra is recited.

परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिर इत्युत्तमया परिदधाति । स यदैवं हविर्धाने संपरिश्रिते मन्येताथ परिदध्यात् । (*pari tvā girvaṇo gira ityuttamayā paridadhāti | sa yadaivaṃ havirdhāne saṃpariśrite manyetātha paridadhyāt |*)

### Printed p. 420

With the mantra परि त्वा (*pari tvā*) (1-10-12) he brings this rite to completion. "O god who delight in praise, may these words of praise that we make come around you on all sides and give you joy. Because these words give you joy, may they increase your life; as a result, may our life too increase and may I also have joy" — such is the import of this mantra. This mantra is to be recited when the Hotṛ covers the havirdhānas completely with the chadi.

अनग्नंभावुका ह होतुश्च यजमानस्य च भार्या भवंति यत्रैवं विद्वानेतया हविर्धानयोः संपरिश्रितयोः परिदधाति ॥ (*anagnaṃbhāvukā ha hotuśca yajamānasya ca bhāryā bhavaṃti yatraivaṃ vidvānetayā havirdhānayoḥ saṃpariśritayoḥ paridadhāti ‖*)

If the Hotṛ who knows this principle recites this mantra after covering the havirdhānas with the chadi, then the wives of the Hotṛ and of the sacrificer too do not experience nakedness but are covered and adorned with garments of every kind.

यजुषा वा एते संपरिश्रियेते यद्धविर्धाने यजुषैवेने एतत्परिश्रयंति। तौ यदैवाध्वर्युश्च प्रतिप्रस्थाता चोभयतो मेथ्यौ निहन्यातामथ परिद ध्यात् । अत्र हि ते संपरिश्रिते भवतः ॥ (*yajuṣā vā ete saṃpariśriyete yaddhavirdhāne yajuṣaivene etatpariśrayaṃti| tau yadaivādhvaryuśca pratiprasthātā cobhayato methyau nihanyātāmatha parida dhyāt | atra hi te saṃpariśrite bhavataḥ ‖*)

The havirdhānas are to be covered by reciting the Yajus mantra दिवो वा विष्णुवुत (*divo vā viṣṇuvuta*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2.13); and so they cover them reciting that very Yajus mantra. As explained above, this covering rite is accomplished when the Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ touch the medhīs (the door-posts, in the form of ends) on both sides.

ता एता अष्टावन्वाह रूपसमृद्धा एतद्वैयज्ञस्य समृद्धं यद्रूपसमृद्धं यत्कर्म क्रियमाणमृगभिवदति तासां त्रिः प्रथमामन्वाह त्रिरुत्तमां ता द्वादश संपद्यंते द्वादश वै मासाः संवत्सरः संवत्सरः प्रजापतिः प्रजापत्यायतनाभिरेवाभी राध्योति य एवं वेद त्रिः प्रथमां त्रिरुत्तमामन्वाह यज्ञस्यैव तद्वर्सौ नह्यति स्थेन्ने बलायाविस्रंसाय ॥ (*tā etā aṣṭāvanvāha rūpasamṛddhā etadvaiyajñasya samṛddhaṃ yadrūpasamṛddhaṃ yatkarma kriyamāṇamṛgabhivadati tāsāṃ triḥ prathamāmanvāha triruttamāṃ tā dvādaśa saṃpadyaṃte dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatyāyatanābhirevābhī rādhyoti ya evaṃ veda triḥ prathamāṃ triruttamāmanvāha yajñasyaiva tadvarsau nahyati sthenne balāyāvisraṃsāya ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 1. 29)

The Hotṛ recites eight mantras rich in rūpa at this time of the havirdhāna worship. Rūpa-richness means reciting mantras whose meaning accords with the rite being performed. Only a rite performed with such richness of form attains completeness. Of these eight mantras he recites the first three times and the last three times. That makes twelve in all. The year has twelve limbs consisting of the months.

### Printed p. 421

Prajāpati is of the form of this year. One who knows this principle dwells in the excellent houses of Prajāpati, consisting of the year and in the form of months (he obtains happiness at all times). Thus, by reciting the first mantra three times and the last mantra three times, it is as if this sacrifice were tied with a firm knot so that it does not come undone. This firm knot helps the life of the sacrificer and the rest toward security, abundance of wealth and unchecked growth.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> युजे वामिति पंचर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं । आदितेः पुत्रस्य विवस्वत आर्षं .
> हविर्धानाख्ये ये द्वे शकटे तद्देवत्यमिदं । अंत्या जगती शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । युजे पंच विवस्वानादित्यो हाविर्धानं जगत्त्यंतमिति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ हविर्धानप्रवर्तने युजे वामित्येका । सूत्रितं च । अंतरा वर्त्मपादयोर्युजे वां ब्रह्म पूर्व्यं नमोभिः । आ. ४-९ ॥ इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta युजे वां (*yuje vāṃ*) is the thirteenth sūkta and has five Ṛks. Its seer is Vivasvat, son of Aditi. Its deity is the two carts called havirdhāna. The last verse is a Jagatī and the rest are Triṣṭubhs. So the Anukramaṇī says: युजे पंच विवस्वानादित्यो हाविर्धानं जगत्त्यंतमिति ॥ (*yuje paṃca vivasvānādityo hāvirdhānaṃ jagattyaṃtamiti ‖*). The use of the sūkta has already been stated. In the havirdhāna-pravartana rite the first verse, युजे वां (*yuje vāṃ*), is used. It is also laid down in the sūtra अंतरा वर्त्मपादयोर्युजे वां ब्रह्म पूर्व्यं नमोभिः (*aṃtarā vartmapādayoryuje vāṃ brahma pūrvyaṃ namobhiḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 4-9).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta युजे वां (*yuje vāṃ*) is the thirteenth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is Vivasvān, the son of Aditi. The deity of this sūkta is the two carts that bring the Soma plants in sacrifices and the like known as havirdhāna. The last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Jagatī metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said युजे पंच विवस्वानादित्यो हाविर्धानं जगत्तंतं (*yuje paṃca vivasvānādityo hāvirdhānaṃ jagattaṃtaṃ*). The use of the sūkta has been stated earlier. That the first Ṛk, युजे वां (*yuje vāṃ*), is to be recited in the havirdhāna-pravartana rite is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra अंतरा वर्त्म पादयोर्युजे वां ब्रह्म पूर्वं नमोभिः (*aṃtarā vartma pādayoryuje vāṃ brahma pūrvaṃ namobhiḥ*) (Ā. 4-9).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 13. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 13. Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 6; Varga 13. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Vivasvān Āditya. Deity: the havirdhānas. Metre: 1-4 Triṣṭubh; 5 Jagatī.

> यु॒जे वां॒ ब्रह्म॑ पू॒र्व्यं नमो॑भि॒र्वि श्लोक॑ एतु प॒थ्ये॑व  ॒
> सूरेः ।  
> शृ॒ण्वंतु॒ विश्वे॑ अ॒मृत॑स्य पु॒त्रा आ ये धामा॑नि दि॒व्यानि॑ त॒स्थुः ॥

> शृण्वंतु । विश्वे । अमृतस्य । पुत्राः । आ । ये : धामानि । दिव्यानि । तस्थुः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे हविर्धानशकटे वां युवामहं पूर्व्यं पूर्वस्मिन्काले भवं । अनादिकालप्रवृत्त मित्यर्थः । एवंभूतं ब्रह्म मंत्रं । उच्चार्योति शेषः । नमोभिः
> सोमादिहनिर्लक्षणैरन्नैर्युजे । युनज्जि । युवयोरुपरि सोमादिकमारोप्य
> पत्नीशालातो हविर्धानं प्रति युना नयामित्यर्थः । एवंभूतयोर्युवयोः
> श्लोकः शब्दो व्येतु । विश्वान्गेवान्प्रति विविधं गच्छतां । तत्र दृष्टांतः । पथ्येव
> सूरेः यथा स्तोतुः स्वभूता पथ्या परिणामसुखावहाहुतिर्विश्वानेवान्प्रति विविधं गच्छति तद्वत् । अमृतस्यामरणधर्मणः प्रजापतेः पुत्रा विश्वे देवा एवंभूतं
> शब्दं शृण्वंतु ये देवा दिव्यानि दिवि भवानि धामानि स्थानान्या तस्थुः अधिष्ठितवंतः ।
> ते शृण्यंतित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O havirdhāna carts, I join you, पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*), that is, belonging to an earlier time, in other words occurring from beginningless time, ब्रह्म (*brahma*), a mantra (to be supplied: having uttered it), नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*), with food in the form of the oblations such as Soma: I yoke you. That is: having loaded Soma and the rest upon you, I lead you from the wives' hall toward the havirdhāna." Of you, so constituted, may the श्लोकः (*ślokaḥ*), the sound, go forth in different directions to all the gods. Illustration: पथ्येव सूरेः (*pathyeva sūreḥ*) — as the beneficial oblation of the worshipper, which brings happiness in its result, goes in various ways to all the gods. May all the gods, the sons of the immortal Prajāpati, who is not subject to death, hear such a sound — those gods who occupy the heavenly places (dhāmāni, i.e. abodes). The meaning is: they hear it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नां (*nāṃ*)—(O carts) addressing you
- पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*)—ancient
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—reciting a hymn of praise
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with oblations
- युजे (*yuje*)—I fill you
- सूरेः (*sūreḥ*)—of the seer
- पथ्येव (*pathyeva*)—as praise resorts to the various directions and joins the gods
- श्लोकः (*ślokaḥ*)—your sound
- वि एतु (*vi etu*)—may it go and reach all the gods
- ये (*ye*)—which gods
- दिव्यानि (*divyāni*)—belonging to the heavenly world
- धामानि (*dhāmāni*)—places
- आ तस्थुः (*ā tasthuḥ*)—have occupied, such ones also
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—of Prajāpati, who is free of the nature of death
- पुत्राः (*putrāḥ*)—who are sons
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all the gods
- शृण्वंतु (*śṛṇvaṃtu*)—may they hear your sounds

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O carts, addressing you and reciting an ancient hymn of praise, I fill you with oblations. As the seer's praise resorts to the various directions and joins the gods, so may your sound go and reach all the gods. May all the gods, those who occupy the places belonging to the heavenly world and who are the sons of Prajāpati, who is free of the nature of death, hear your sounds.

### Printed p. 423

##### English translation
I load you two with sacred offerings, repeating an ancient prayer ; may the sound (of your approach) reach (the gods) like the path of the worshipper, may all the sons of the immortal (Prajapati) who inhabit the celestial regions hear (the sound).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒मे इ॑व॒ यत॑माने॒ यदैतं॒ प्र वां॑ भर॒न्मानु॑षा देव॒यंतः॑ ।  
> आ सी॑दतं॒ स्वमु॑ लो॒कं विदा॑ने स्वास्॒थे भ॑वत॒मिंद॑वे नः ॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यमे इवेति यमेऽइव । यतमाने इति । ऋत् । ऐतं । प्र । वां । भरत्  
> मानुषाः । देवयंतः ।  
> आ । सीदतं । स्वं । ऊं इति । लोकं । विदाने इति । स्वास्थे इति सुआस्थे । भवतं  
> इंदवे । नः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्रैव हविर्धानप्रवर्तने यमे इव इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । यमे इव
> यतमाने यदैतमधिद्वयोरदधा उक्थ्यं वच इत्यर्धर्च अरमेत् । आ. ४-९ । इति॥
> यमे इव यथा सहोत्पन्ने अपत्ये संचरतः तथा यतमाने गमनहविर्धारणादिस्वाधिकारकर्मणि प्रवर्तमाने हविर्धानशकटे युवां यद्यदैतं हविर्धानस्थानं प्रतिगच्छतः तदा देवयंतो देवकामा मानुषा यजमाना वां
> युवां प्र भरन् ! प्रभरंति । किंच युवां स्वमु लोकमात्मीयमेव हविर्धानाख्यं स्थानं विदाने जानती आ सीदतं । ततो नोऽस्माकमिंदवे सोमार्थं
> स्नानस्थे शोभननिवासस्थाने भवतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The verse यमे इव (*yame iva*) is used in the rite of setting the Havirdhāna carts in motion. The sūtra says: यमे इव यतमाने यदैतमधिद्वयोरदधा उक्थ्यं वच इत्यर्धर्च अरमेत् (*yame iva yatamāne yadaitamadhidvayoradadhā ukthyaṃ vaca ityardharca aramet*) (Ā. 4-9): he is to begin with the half-verse. Like twins born together who move about together, the two Havirdhāna carts are busy in their own task of going and carrying the oblations. When you two reach the place of the Havirdhāna, the sacrificers, desiring the gods, bring you forward. Knowing your own place, called Havirdhāna, settle in it. Then, for our Soma, be a good, pleasant dwelling-place.

### Printed p. 424

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यमे इव (*yame iva*)—like twins born together
- यतमाने (*yatamāne*)—O carts, engaged together in the work of the gods
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- ऐतं (*aitaṃ*)—you come to the place of the Havirdhāna, then
- देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*)—devoted to the worship of the gods
- मानुषाः (*mānuṣāḥ*)—the sacrificers
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- प्र भरन् (*pra bharan*)—receive abundantly
- स्व मु लोकं (*sva mu lokaṃ*)—your own Havirdhāna place
- विदाने (*vidāne*)—making for yourselves
- आ सीदतं (*ā sīdataṃ*)—settle in it
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- इंदवे (*iṃdave*)—for the Soma
- स्वासस्थॆ (*svāsasthè*)—a good dwelling-place
- भवतं (*bhavataṃ*)—be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O carts, engaged together in the work of the gods like twins born together: when you come to the place of the Havirdhāna, the sacrificers, devoted to the worship of the gods, welcome you abundantly. Settle in your own Havirdhāna place. Be makers of a good dwelling-place for your Soma.

##### English translation
When you two came, like twins, busily engaged, then devout worshippers brought you forward: knowing your place there abide and be fair storehouses for our Soma.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this verse, यमे इव (*yame iva*), is to be recited in the rite called Havirdhāna-pravartana is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, यमे इव यतमाने यदैतमधिद्वयोरदधा उक्तं वच इत्यर्धर्च आरमेत् (*yame iva yatamāne yadaitamadhidvayoradadhā uktaṃ vaca ityardharca āramet*) (Ā. 4-9).

### Printed p. 425

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रुपो यष्टृणां स्वर्गमारोपयितुर्यज्ञस्यांगत्वेन संबंधीनि पंचसंख्याकानि धानासोमपशुपुरोडाशाज्याख्यानि पदानि वृष्टिहेतुत्वेन देवान्प्रति
> गंत्यणि हवींप्यन्वरोहं । अनुरोहामि । शकटयोः स्थापनवहनानंतरं करणं
> करोमीत्यर्थः । किंच चतुष्पदीं चतुर्भिः पादैर्युक्तां त्रिष्टुबादिच्छंदसं
> क्रियां व्रतेन प्रयोगकर्मणान्वेमि। अनुगच्छामि । यथाकालं प्रयुनज्मीत्यर्थः ।
> अक्षरेण प्रणवाख्येनैतामुपस्थितां प्रतिगरक्रियां प्रति मिमे । निर्ममे । अपि
> चर्तस्य यज्ञस्य । अधीति सप्तम्यर्थ्यानुवादी । नाभौ नाभिभूते वेद्याख्ये स्थाने सं
> पुनामि । संशोधयामि । दशापवित्रेण सोमं संस्करोमीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The five oblations connected with the sacrifice, which raise the sacrificer to heaven — grain, Soma, animal, cake and ghee — I make ascend, i.e. I make them be carried, to the gods as a cause of rain; the meaning is that after the carts have been set up and made to carry, I perform the act. Further, I follow with the observance, i.e. the rite of application, the four-footed (Triṣṭubh and other metre) act; I employ it at the proper time. With the syllable called praṇava I fashion this present act called pratigara. And in the navel of the sacrifice, the place called the Vedi, I purify, i.e. I prepare the Soma with the ten-strand filter.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O carts) रुपः (*rupaḥ*)—the sacrificial
- पंच पदानि (*paṃca padāni*)—five kinds of oblation: grain, Soma, animal, cake, ghee
- अन्वरोहम् (*anvaroham*)—I make them be carried by you
- चतुष्पदीं (*catuṣpadīṃ*)—praises furnished with four feet (in metre)
- व्रतेन (*vratena*)—with the prescribed rites
- अन्वेमि (*anvemi*)—I employ at the proper time
- अक्षरेण (*akṣareṇa*)—with the syllable of the form of praṇava
- एतां (*etāṃ*)—this act called pratigara
- प्रति मिमे (*prati mime*)—I fashion
- ऋतस (*ṛtasa*) आधि (*ādhi*)—in the sacrifice
- नाभौ (*nābhau*)—in the Vedi, which is of the form of a navel
- सं पुनामि (*saṃ punāmi*)—I prepare the Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O carts, I make you carry the five kinds of oblation connected with the sacrifice — grain, Soma, animal, cake and ghee. I employ four-footed (metrical) praises with the prescribed rites at the proper time. With the syllable of the form of praṇava I fashion this act called pratigara. In the sacrifice, on the Vedi which is of the form of a navel, I prepare the Soma.

##### English translation
I make the five stages of the sacrifice ascend ; I take four steps by pious observances; with the sacred syllable, I perfect this (adoration); I purify (the Soma) on the navel of the sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वेभ्यः॒ कम॑वृणीत मृ॒त्युं प्र॒जायै॒ कम॒मृतं॒ नावृ॑णीत ।  
> बृह॒स्पतिं॑ य॒ज्ञम॑कृण्वत॒ ऋषिं॑ प्रि॒यां य॒मस्त॒न्वं१॒॑ १ प्रारि॑रेचीत् ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 426

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवेभ्यः । कं । अवृणीत । मृत्युं । प्रजायै । कं । अमृतं । न । अवृणीत ।  
> बृहस्पतिं । यज्ञं । अकृण्वत । ऋषिं । प्रियां । यमः । तन्वं । प्र । अरिरेचीत् ॥४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवेभ्यो देवानां मृत्युं मारयितारं कं स्वपुरुषमवृणीत । प्रार्थयते । प्रयुंक्ते । किंच प्रजायै देवव्यतिरिक्ताया मनुष्यादिकायाः प्रजाया
> अमृतममारकमनिनाशकं कं वा स्वपुरुषं नावृणीत । न प्रयुंक्ते । हविर्धारणक्रियायां प्रवृत्तायां सत्यां पूर्वोक्तानां सर्वेषां स्थितेरवश्यंभावित्वान्न
> कंचिदपि विनाशकं स्वपुरुषं यमो निरूपयतीत्यर्थः । अपि च बृहस्पतिं बृहतां
> देवानां हविर्धारणे पालकं बृहतां मंत्राणां स्वामिनं वर्षिं सर्वस्य दृष्टादृष्टफलस्य द्रष्टारं यज्ञमकृण्वत । ऋत्विग्यजमानाः कुर्वंति । अपि च यमः
> प्रियां तन्वमस्मदीयमिष्टं शरीरं प्रारिरेचीत् ! धातूनामनेकार्थत्वाद्रिचिरत्र
> परिहारार्थ वर्तते । प्ररेचयति । मृत्योऽसकाशात्परिहरति । कर्मवैगुण्यजनितदोषभावादस्माकं जीवितं नापहरतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For the gods, Yama has chosen (appointed, employed) some man of his own as a slayer, मृत्युं (*mṛtyuṃ*). And for the progeny other than the gods — men and the rest — he has not chosen any man of his as immortal, i.e. non-slaying, non-destroying. The meaning is that, once the act of carrying the oblations is under way, since the continued existence of all those mentioned before is certain, Yama appoints no destroyer at all. Further, the priests and sacrificers have made Bṛhaspati — protector of the great gods in carrying the oblations, lord of the great mantras, the seer, beholder of all visible and invisible fruit — into the sacrifice. And Yama has प्रारिरेचीत् (*prārirecīt*) our dear body: since roots have many meanings, the root ric here has the sense of avoiding; he turns it away from death. The meaning is that because no fault arises from any defect in the rite, he does not take away our life.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—to the gods
- मृत्युं (*mṛtyuṃ*)—as slayer
- कं (*kaṃ*)—which man
- अवृणीत (*avṛṇīta*)—(Yama) has appointed
- प्रजाय्कॆ (*prajāykè*)—to mankind
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—one who is not a destroyer
- कं (*kaṃ*) (वा (*vā*))—whom indeed
- नावृणीत (*nāvṛṇīta*)—has he not appointed
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—called Bṛhaspati
- ऋषिं (*ṛṣiṃ*)—the seer
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—as the sacrifice
- अकृण्वत (*akṛṇvata*)—the priests and sacrificers have made
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—the god Yama
- प्रियां (*priyāṃ*)—dear
- तन्नं (*tannaṃ*)—our body
- प्रारिरेचीत् (*prārirecīt*)—has kept safe

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Which man, a slayer for the gods, has Yama appointed? Whom, one who is not a destroyer, has he not appointed for mankind? The priests and sacrificers have made the seer called Bṛhaspati into the sacrifice. The god Yama has kept our dear body safe.

##### English translation
Whom has he selected as the slayer of the gods? Whom has he not selected as non-slayer of the human race? They have made the Rishi Brihaspati the sacrifice, Yama preserves our loved bodies.
