##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परेयिवांसं । प्रवतः । महीः । अनु । बहुभ्यः । पंथां । अनुपस्पशानं ।  
> वैवस्वतं । संगमनं । जनानां । यमं । राजानं । हविषा । दुवस्य ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मदीयांतरात्मन् यजमान वा त्वं राजानं पितृणां स्वामिनः यमु
> हविषा पुरोडाशादिना दुवस्य । परिचर । कीदृशं । प्रवतः प्रकष्टकर्मवतो भूलोकवर्तिभोगसाधनं पुण्यमनुष्ठितवतः पुरुषान्महीस्तत्तद्योगोचितभूप्रदेशविशेषाननु परेयिवांसं क्रमेण मरणादूर्ध्वं प्रापितवंतं तथा बहुभ्यः स्वर्गार्थिभ्यः
> पुण्यकृद्भ्यः पुण्यकृतार्थे पंथां स्वर्गस्योचितं मार्गमनुपस्पशानमबाधमानं ।
> पापिन एव पुरुषान् स्वर्गमार्गबाधेन नरकं प्रापयति न तु पुण्यकृत इत्यर्थः ।
> वैवस्वतं विवस्वतः सूर्यस्य पुत्रं जनानां पापिनां संगमनं गंतव्यस्थानरूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O my inner self, or O sacrificer, serve Yama, king, lord of the Pitṛs, with an oblation such as the puroḍāśa." Of what kind? प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*): men of excellent action, who on earth have performed merit that is the means of enjoyment; महीः अनु (*mahīḥ anu*): to the several regions of earth fitting to each; परेयिवांसं (*pareyivāṃsaṃ*): who has in due order led them onward after death. Likewise बहुभ्यः (*bahubhyaḥ*), for the many who desire heaven and have done meritorious acts, पंथां (*paṃthāṃ*) the fitting path to heaven, अनुपस्पशानं (*anupaspaśānaṃ*) not obstructing it. He sends to hell only sinners, by blocking their way to heaven, not the meritorious. वैवस्वतं (*vaivasvataṃ*): the son of Vivasvat, the sun; *janānāṃ saṃgamanaṃ*: the place to which sinners must go.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*)—men who have performed excellent acts (O sacrificer)
- महीः अनु (*mahīḥ anu*)—to the respective excellent regions
- परेयिवांसं (*pareyivāṃsaṃ*)—who leads them after death
- बहुभ्यः (*bahubhyaḥ*)—to many doers of merit
- पंथां (*paṃthāṃ*)—the paths to heaven and so on
- अनुपस्पशानं (*anupaspaśānaṃ*)—who provides them without harm
- वैवस्वतं (*vaivasvataṃ*)—son of Vivasvat
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—for sinners
- संगमनं (*saṃgamanaṃ*)—who brings them to the place fit for them
- राजानं (*rājānaṃ*)—king, lord of the Pitṛs
- यमं (*yamaṃ*)—Yama
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblations
- दुवस्य (*duvasya*)—serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sacrificer, serve with oblations Yama, who after death leads men who have performed excellent acts to the respective excellent regions, who provides many doers of merit with the paths to heaven and the rest without harm, the son of Vivasvat, who brings sinners to the place fit for them, and the lord of the Pitṛs.

### Printed p. 455

##### English translation
Worship with oblations Yama, king (of the Pitris), son of Vivaswat, the aggregation of mankind, who conducts those who are virtuous over the earth, and opens to many the path (of heaven).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यमं (*yamaṃ*)—Who Yama is and what his function is, we have explained at length in the introduction to this sūkta. Yāska, explaining the word Yama, says: यमः । यमो यच्छतीति सतः । तस्यैषा भवति । (*yamaḥ | yamo yacchatīti sataḥ | tasyaiṣā bhavati |*) (Ni. 10-20). The word Yama is derived from the root यम् (*yam*), meaning to restrain, to hold in check. Yama, as guardian of the world of the Pitṛs, restrains and keeps under control the fathers and others who belong to him; hence the name. But Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, explains the word differently: यमः । यच्छति उपरमयति जीवितात् सर्वं भूतग्राममिति यमः । (*yamaḥ | yacchati uparamayati jīvitāt sarvaṃ bhūtagrāmamiti yamaḥ |*) Because he brings to an end the life of all beings on earth, that is, causes their death, he is called Yama. To give an example of a ṛk containing the word Yama, Yāska chose the present ṛk and gave its explanation:
परेयिवांसं प्रवतो महीरनु ऎंब सूत्रदिंद (आ. २-१९) विनृतवागिरुवुदु. सूक्त—१४ मंडल—१० । अनुवाक—१ । सूक्त—१४ । अष्टक—७ । अध्याय—६ । वर्ग—१४, १५, १६ । सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—१६ । ऋषिः—यमः । देवता—१-५, १३-१६. यमः । ६. लिंगोक्तदेवताः। ७-९. लिंगोक्तदेवताः पितरो पा । १०-१२. श्वानौ ॥ छंदः—१-१२. त्रिष्टुप् । १३, १४, १६. अनुष्टुप् । १५. बृहती॥ परेयिवांसं प्रवतो महीरनु बहुभ्यः पंथामनुपस्पशानं । वैवस्वतं संगमनं जनानां यमं राजानं हविषा दुवस्य ॥ (*pareyivāṃsaṃ pravato mahīranu èṃba sūtradiṃda (ā. 2-19) vinṛtavāgiruvudu. sūkta—14 maṃḍala—10 | anuvāka—1 | sūkta—14 | aṣṭaka—7 | adhyāya—6 | varga—14, 15, 16 | sūktadalliruva ṛksaṃkhyè—16 | ṛṣiḥ—yamaḥ | devatā—1-5, 13-16. yamaḥ | 6. liṃgoktadevatāḥ| 7-9. liṃgoktadevatāḥ pitaro pā | 10-12. śvānau ‖ chaṃdaḥ—1-12. triṣṭup | 13, 14, 16. anuṣṭup | 15. bṛhatī‖ pareyivāṃsaṃ pravato mahīranu bahubhyaḥ paṃthāmanupaspaśānaṃ | vaivasvataṃ saṃgamanaṃ janānāṃ yamaṃ rājānaṃ haviṣā duvasya ‖*)
परेयिवांसं पर्यागतवंतं प्रवत उद्वर्तो निवत इति । अवतिर्गतिकर्मा । बहुभ्यः पंथानमनुपस्पाशयमानं वैवस्वतं संगमनं जनानां यमं राजानं हविषा दुवस्येति । दुवस्यती राध्योतिकर्मा ॥ (*pareyivāṃsaṃ paryāgatavaṃtaṃ pravata udvarto nivata iti | avatirgatikarmā | bahubhyaḥ paṃthānamanupaspāśayamānaṃ vaivasvataṃ saṃgamanaṃ janānāṃ yamaṃ rājānaṃ haviṣā duvasyeti | duvasyatī rādhyotikarmā ‖*) (Ni. 10-20)
In this ṛk the seer addresses the sacrificer or his own inner self thus: O sacrificer, offer oblation to Yama and serve him. This Yama comes round about; that is, wherever beings may be, he comes there at the time of death. And since only the word प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*) is in this ṛk, the two words उद्वतः (*udvataḥ*) and निवतः (*nivataḥ*) must be supplied in connection with it.

### Printed p. 456
प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*) means men, उद्वतः (*udvataḥ*) gods, निवतः (*nivataḥ*) animals. He carries off the departed bodies of these gods, men and animals after death, according to each one's action, to bring them to the places (worlds) they are fit to attain. अनुपस्पशानं (*anupaspaśānaṃ*) means: because these beings have done such action, to give them their due fruit he brings about their death through various diseases and the like, and after death binds their departed bodies with a noose and conducts them by various paths to the excellent worlds such as heaven if they have done merit, and to places such as hell if they have done sin. संगमनं जनानां (*saṃgamanaṃ janānāṃ*) means one who, without partiality toward people, gives them fruit according to their action. Serve and honour such Yama, king, the king of the Pitṛs, with oblations and the like: this is the purport of the Nirukta explanation.
अग्निरपि यम उच्यते । तमेता ऋचोऽनुप्रवदंति । (*agnirapi yama ucyate | tametā ṛco 'nupravadaṃti |*) (Ni. 10-20)
In some contexts it is customary to call Agni Yama. In this matter the following ṛks make the sense plain; and so saying, as examples Yāska gives Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-66-7 and 8, सेनेव सृष्टा (*seneva sṛṣṭā*), and states their explanation also.
परेयिवांसं (*pareyivāṃsaṃ*)—There is much difference between Yāska's explanation of this word and the commentator's. Yāska's sense is given in the Nirukta on this ṛk: there परेयिवांसं (*pareyivāṃsaṃ*) is पर्याप्तवंतं (*paryāptavaṃtaṃ*), one who fetches from all around, that is from wherever one is, and brings one there. But the commentator explains क्रमेण मरणादूर्ध्वं प्रापितवंतं (*krameṇa maraṇādūrdhvaṃ prāpitavaṃtaṃ*): one who conducts to the other world the departed spirit that goes forth from the dead body after death.
A doubt arises here. What does it mean to take a man to the other world after he is dead? When the body itself is destroyed, whom is one taking? The answer is this: when a man or animal has died, all the actions of his body cease and the body is dissolved. It gradually merges into the five elements, earth and the rest; that is, the body, formed from the union of the five elements, at last merges and is absorbed into them. The five elements are earth, water, fire, air and ether; here they are to be taken respectively as solid substance, liquid, heat, air and space. That these five kinds of things are in the body is known to all. Skin, flesh, bone, nails and other solid substances are parts of earth. After death they join the soil and become soil.

### Printed p. 457
Liquids such as blood and saliva are parts of water; they dissolve in water. The heat (fire) that is in the body until the time of death mingles with radiance, or fire. Hence a dead body has no warmth; it is cold. After death the movement of air in inhalation and exhalation stops, and the five airs, prāṇa and the rest, merge in the air-principle, that is, the external air. That the stopping of breath is the chief sign of death is known by experience. As for ether or space, it is not a visible thing, so its merging in outer space is perceptible to no one. When all the parts of the dead body have thus merged in their respective principles, does nothing remain? It does. While the man or animal was alive, there was a conscious entity which impelled his activities and watched the working of the sense-organs of knowledge such as the eye. "Entity" here is not a sensible earthly thing. It is far subtler than earthly things, and though the body perishes, it alone does not perish. It is called the ātman. After the destruction of the earthly body a subtle other body comes to this ātman. At the outset it is called the departed-spirit body (pretaśarīra). Being very subtle, it cannot be seen with the outer eye. This subtle body has no organs of action, but it has the elements of the organs of knowledge; that is, pleasure, pain and the like are experienced. The impression (vāsanā: the subtle part) of the pleasures and pains it experienced while living on earth, and of love and hatred toward kinsmen and relatives, remains with this body. The ātman remains for some time in this departed-spirit body, that is, until the later rites performed for the dead body are completed, and then goes to another world according to its action. Then a body still subtler than the departed-spirit body is obtained. As the worlds are, so the beings living in them have bodies made of the same kind of substance. On earth, beings have bodies made of gross earthly matter. So also in heaven, hell and the rest. Since the world of heaven is made of very subtle substance, the gods, men and others who dwell there have very subtle bodies. Since the people on earth can see only gross things with their eyes, they cannot see the world of the gods or the gods, which are of subtle form. Where is the world of the gods? As said in the śruti sentence अंतर्हितो हि देवलोको मनुष्यलोकात् (*aṃtarhito hi devaloko manuṣyalokāt*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6.1-1-2), it is interwoven with this world of men, that is, mutually inherent. Although some part of heaven is in the atmosphere around us, we cannot see and know it. The electric current in subtle form flows in wires, yet it cannot be seen. In the same way, with the limbs of our gross body we can see neither the subtly formed heaven nor its dwellers.

### Printed p. 458
But the dwellers in heaven, if they wish, can see us. The sentences in the present sūkta and in some following sūktas addressed to the dead man are to be understood as addressed to the living being in the departed-spirit body obtained after death.
प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*)—प्रकृष्टकर्मवतो भूलोकवर्तिभोगसाधनं पुण्यमनुष्ठितवत पुरुषान् (*prakṛṣṭakarmavato bhūlokavartibhogasādhanaṃ puṇyamanuṣṭhitavata puruṣān*): the commentator explains this as men who have done excellent sacrifices and other acts and have earned the merit that is the means of the enjoyments experienced on earth. That is, men who, having done meritorious good deeds, desire after death the heaven and the rest that are the fruit of those deeds. Yāska goes further in this matter and explains प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*), उद्वतः (*udvataḥ*), निवतः (*nivataḥ*) as men, gods and animals. Men are of two kinds: those who have done good deeds and those who have done sin. The world they attain is likewise different.
बहुभ्यः पंथां अनुपस्पशानं (*bahubhyaḥ paṃthāṃ anupaspaśānaṃ*)—As said above, the paths to the other worlds are also many. That is, the path to heaven and the rest is one, the path to the worlds fit for the punishment suffered by the wicked is another. The meaning is that he conducts beings to the respective worlds by the many paths that lead to the worlds according to each one's action.
वैवस्वतं (*vaivasvataṃ*)—The son of Vivasvat is called Vaivasvata. Vivasvat is a son of Aditi, mother of the gods. On this:
अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेः । .... .... ताननुक्रमष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अगंतश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्श्वेत्येते ॥ (*aṣṭau putrāso aditeḥ | .... .... tānanukramaṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agaṃtaśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāgśvetyete ‖*) (Tai. Ā. 1-13-3)
As the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka says, Aditi has eight sons: Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Aryamā, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān. **NOTE**  Here the eighth, Vivasvān, and Indra are the two twin children.
The son of this Vivasvat is Yama. It is customary to call him king. Because Yama is lord of the world of the Pitṛs, and because it is explained that Varuṇa also is there, it is the usage to call both Yama and Varuṇa kings.
संगमनं जनानां (*saṃgamanaṃ janānāṃ*)—Because he takes the dead beings to his own world and gathers and keeps them together there, संगमनं जनानां (*saṃgamanaṃ janānāṃ*) has the sense of one who assembles people in one place

### Printed p. 459
(The first lines continue the sentence from the previous page.) Yama is described by these words. *Saṅgamanam* means the place to be reached, that is, the region where living beings must go and gather. It may be heaven or hell: for the virtuous it is to be understood as heaven, for the sinful as hell.

> उ ।  
> यत्रा॑ नः॒ पूर्वे॑ पि॒तरः॑ परे॒युरे॒ना ज॑ज्ञा॒नाः प॒थ्या॒३॒॑ ३ अनु॒  
> स्वाः ॥ २ ॥

> यमः । नः । गातुं । प्रथमः । विवेद । न । एषा । गव्यूतिः । अपभर्तवै । ऊं इति ।  
> यत्र । नः । पूर्वे । पितरः । पराईयुः । एना । जज्ञानाः । पथ्याः । अनु । स्वाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रथमः सर्वेषां मुख्यो यमो नोऽस्माकं प्रजानां गारुशुभाशुभनिमित्तं विवेद । जानाति । एषा गव्यूतिर्नापभर्तवा उ । अतिशयज्ञानयोगाद्यमस्य
> न केनचिदपहर्तुमपनेतुं शक्यत इत्यर्थः । यत्र यस्मिन्मार्गे नोऽस्माकु पूर्वे
> पितरः परेयुः एनानेन मार्गेण गच्छंतो जज्ञाना जाताः सर्वॆ स्वाः स्वभूताः
> पथ्याः स्वकर्ममार्गभूता गतीरनु गच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yama, first, that is chief of all, knows for us, his subjects, the road of what is auspicious and inauspicious. "This pasture is not to be taken away": because of Yama's surpassing knowledge, no one can take it from him or remove it. On the road by which our forefathers went, going along it, all who are born follow their own paths, the courses that are the road of their own actions.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—chief of all
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—Yama
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गातुं (*gātuṃ*)—the path of travel
- विवेद (*viveda*)—has known
- एषा गव्यूतिः (*eṣā gavyūtiḥ*)—this fruitful road
- न अपभर्तवै (*na apabhartavai*)—not to be taken away by others
- यत्र (*yatra*)—on whichever road that accords with action
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- पूर्वे पितरः (*pūrve pitaraḥ*)—all the earlier forefathers
- परेयुः (*pareyuḥ*)—went after death
- एना (*enā*)—on just such roads
- जज्ञानः (*jajñānaḥ*)—all who are born
- स्वाः (*svāḥ*)—their own individual
- पथ्याः (*pathyāḥ*)—roads that are the fruit of action
- अनु (*anu*)—following, they go

### Printed p. 460

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Yama, chief of all, knows our paths of travel. This fruitful road is not to be taken away by others. On the roads that accord with action, by which all our earlier forefathers went after death, on just those roads all who are born go, following their own individual fruits of action.

##### English translation
Yama, the chief (of all), knows our well-being : this pasture no one can take from us. By the road by which our forefathers have gone, all who are born (proceed) along the paths they have made for themselves.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yamaḥ naḥ gātuṃ prathamaḥ viveda—for the word प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*) in this sentence the commentator, following Yāska's explanation, takes "प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)" to mean "the chief one". But Western scholars such as Muir take the word as an indeclinable and explain that Yama was the first to find the way to the world of the fathers: "Yama was the first who found for us the way. This home is not to be taken from us. Those who are now born (follow) by their own paths to the place whither our ancient fathers departed." So he says.

Eṣā gavyūtiḥ apabhartavai u—अतिशयज्ञानयोगात् यमस्य न केनचिदपहर्तुं शक्यत इत्यर्थः । (*atiśayajñānayogāt yamasya na kenacidapahartuṃ śakyata ityarthaḥ |*) The commentator has given no explanation of the word गव्यूतिः (*gavyūtiḥ*) in this sentence. Elsewhere he explains the word gavyūti as अतिविस्तृतं मार्गं (*ativistṛtaṃ mārgaṃ*). That meaning may be given here too; or it may be taken to mean the excellent place that is under Yama's lordship.

> आ. ५-२० । इति.

> पितृभिः सह ववृधानो वर्धमानो भवति । यमश्चांगिरोभिः पितृविशेषैः सह
> वर्धमानो भवति ।........। तत्र देवा इंद्रादयो यांश्च कव्यभागादीन्पित्थन्ववृधुः
> वर्धयंति ये च कव्यभागादयः पितरो देवानिंद्रादीन्वर्धयंति तेषां मध्येऽन्य
> इंद्रादयः स्वाहा मदंति । स्वाहाकारेण हृष्यंति । अन्ये पितरः स्वधया स्वधाकारेण हृष्यंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The verse मातली कव्यैः (*mātalī kavyaiḥ*) is a dhāyyā in the Agnimāruta (śastra). It is stated in the sūtra: इमं यम प्रस्तरमा हि सीद मातली कव्यैर्यमो अंगिरोभिरुदीरतामवर उत्परासः । (*imaṃ yama prastaramā hi sīda mātalī kavyairyamo aṃgirobhirudīratāmavara utparāsaḥ |*) (Ā. 5-20). Mātali is Indra's charioteer; Indra who has him is Mātalī. He prospers together with the Kavyas, the fathers who share in kavya. Yama prospers together with the Aṅgirases, a special class of fathers. The gods, Indra and the rest, augment those fathers who share in kavya and so on, and those fathers augment the gods, Indra and the rest; among them some, Indra and the others, rejoice at the svāhā; the other fathers rejoice at the svadhā.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मातली (*mātalī*)—Indra
- कव्यैः (*kavyaiḥ*)—with the fathers who share in kavyas
- ववृधानः (*vavṛdhānaḥ*)—attains growth
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—Yama
- अंगिरोभिः (*aṃgirobhiḥ*)—attains growth with the Aṅgirases
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*)—is strengthened with the praisers
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Indra and others
- यांश्च (*yāṃśca*)—whichever fathers
- ववृधुः (*vavṛdhuḥ*)—they cause to grow
- ये च (*ye ca*)—and whichever fathers
- देवान् (*devān*)—cause the gods, Indra and others, to grow; among them
- अन्ये (*anye*)—one group of gods
- स्वाहा (*svāhā*)—partaking of the oblation offered with "स्वाहा (*svāhā*)"
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—attain delight
- अन्ये (*anye*)—another group, the fathers
- स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—are delighted with the kavyas offered in the form of svadhā

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra attains growth together with the fathers who share in kavyas, Yama with the Aṅgirases, and Bṛhaspati with the praisers. Among those whom the gods, Indra and others, cause to grow, and those fathers who are the cause of the growth of the gods, Indra and others, one group, the gods, partake of the oblation offered with "स्वाहा (*svāhā*)" and attain delight. The other group, the fathers, are delighted with the offerings made in the form of svadhā.

### Printed p. 462

##### English translation
Matalin prospers with the Kavyas; Yama with the Angirasas; Brihaspati with the Rikwans; they whom the gods augment, and they who augment the gods, these rejoice in Swaha, those in the Swadha.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Agnimāruta śastra mantras this Ṛk, "मातली कव्यैः (*mātalī kavyaiḥ*)", is to be recited as a dhāyyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, इमं यम प्रस्तरमा हि सीद मातली कव्यैर्यमो अंगिरोभिरुदीरतामवर उत्परासः (*imaṃ yama prastaramā hi sīda mātalī kavyairyamo aṃgirobhirudīratāmavara utparāsaḥ*) (Ā. 5-20).

Mātalī—Mātali is well known as Indra's charioteer. Mātalī means Indra, who has the charioteer Mātali.

Kavyaiḥ—kavya is the food offered to the fathers. The food offered to the gods is called havis or havya.

In this Ṛk it is said that the gods increase the fathers and the fathers the gods. Three kinds of fathers are also indicated here. The fathers worthy of kavya, or who consume kavya (कव्यभाग्भिः (*kavyabhāgbhiḥ*)), gain growth together with Indra. The fathers called Aṅgirases grow together with Yama. The fathers called Ṛkvas (praisers) are increased together with Bṛhaspati. Having indicated the three kinds of fathers, the seer then declares the rule of how havya and kavya are to be offered to gods and fathers. As in the Śruti sentence स्वाहा देवेभ्यः स्वधा पितृभ्य इत्याह (*svāhā devebhyaḥ svadhā pitṛbhya ityāha*), when the oblation is offered to the gods with the utterance of svāhā, and when kavya is offered to the fathers preceded by the word svadhā, they are pleased; so the seer declares.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मं य॑म प्रस्त॒रमा हि सीदांगि॑रोभिः पि॒तृभिः॑ संविदा॒नः ।  
> आ त्वा॒ मंत्राः॑ कविश॒स्ता व॑हंते॒ना रा॑जन्ह॒ विषा॑ मादयस्व ॥४॥

### Printed p. 463

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमं । यम । प्रस्तरं। आ । हि । सीद । अंगिरःभिः । पितृभिः । संविदानः ।  
> आ । त्वा । मंत्राः । कविशस्त्राः । वहंतु । एना । राजन् । हविषा । मादयस्व ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महापितृयज्ञे यमस्यॆमं यमेत्यादिके द्वे अनुवाक्ये । इमं यम
> प्रस्तरमा हि सिदेति द्वे । आ. २-१९ । इति हि सूत्रितं ॥ सैषाग्निमारुतेऽपि धाय्या ।
> सूत्रं पूर्वमेवोदाहृतं ॥
> हे यम अंगिरोभिरेतन्नामकैः पितृभिः संविदान ऐकमत्यं गतस्त्वमिमं
> प्रस्तरं विस्तीर्णं यज्ञविशेषमा सीद । आगत्योपविश हि यस्मादेवं तस्मात्कविशस्ता
> विद्वद्भिर्युत्विग्भिः प्रयुक्ता मंत्रास्त्वा त्वामा वहंतु । हे राजन् एनैतेन हविषा
> तुष्टो मादयस्व । यजमानं हर्षय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, "इमं यम (*imaṃ yama*)" and the following are the two anuvākyās of Yama; the sūtra says इमं यम प्रस्तरमा हि सीदांगिरोभिः पितृभिः संविदानः । आ त्वा मंत्राः कविशस्ता वहंतेना राजन्ह विषा मादयस्व ॥४॥ इमं । यम । प्रस्तरं। आ । हि । सीद । अंगिरःभिः । पितृभिः । संविदानः । आ । त्वा । मंत्राः । कविशस्त्राः । वहंतु । एना । राजन् । हविषा । मादयस्व ॥ ४ ॥ महापितृयज्ञे यमस्यॆमं यमेत्यादिके द्वे (*imaṃ yama prastaramā hi sīdāṃgirobhiḥ pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ | ā tvā maṃtrāḥ kaviśastā vahaṃtenā rājanha viṣā mādayasva ‖4‖ imaṃ | yama | prastaraṃ| ā | hi | sīda | aṃgiraḥbhiḥ | pitṛbhiḥ | saṃvidānaḥ | ā | tvā | maṃtrāḥ | kaviśastrāḥ | vahaṃtu | enā | rājan | haviṣā | mādayasva ‖ 4 ‖ mahāpitṛyajñe yamasyèmaṃ yametyādike dve*) (Ā. 2-19). This verse is also a dhāyyā in the Agnimāruta (śastra); the sūtra was quoted earlier. O Yama, agreed with the fathers named Aṅgirases, sit down at this spread-out sacrifice, the prastara. Since it is so, let the mantras uttered by the wise priests bring you. O king, delighted with this oblation, gladden the sacrificer.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यम (*yama*)—O god Yama
- अंगिरोभिः (*aṃgirobhiḥ*)—with the fathers called Aṅgirases
- पितृभिः (*pitṛbhiḥ*)—with the fathers
- संविदान? (*saṃvidāna?*)—united
- प्रस्तरं इमं (*prastaraṃ imaṃ*)—on this sacrificial seat widely spread
- आ सीद (*ā sīda*)—sit down
- हि (*hi*)—therefore
- कविशस्ताः (*kaviśastāḥ*)—recited by the poets
- मंत्राः (*maṃtrāḥ*)—the praise-mantras
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आ वहंतु (*ā vahaṃtu*)—let them bring here
- राजन् (*rājan*)—Yama, the lord
- एना हविषा (*enā haviṣā*)—satisfied with these oblations
- मादयस्व (*mādayasva*)—gladden the sacrificer too

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Yama, united with the fathers called Aṅgirases, sit down on this widely spread seat. Let the praise-mantras recited by the poets bring you here. O Yama, lord, satisfied with these oblations, gladden the sacrificer too.

##### English translation
Yama, who are associated with the Angirasa Pitris, sit down at this Sacrifice; may the prayers recited by the priests bring you hither; be exhilarated, Sovereign (Yama), by this oblation.

### Printed p. 464

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the homa made to Yama in the Mahāpitṛyajña, this Ṛk "इमं यम (*imaṃ yama*)" and the Ṛk that follows it are to be recited as anuvākyā mantras; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, इमं यम प्रस्तरमा हि सीदेति द्वे (*imaṃ yama prastaramā hi sīdeti dve*) (Ā. 2-19). The sūtra sentence has been given earlier, that this mantra is also to be recited as a dhāyyā mantra in the Agnimāruta śastra mantras.

Prastaram—प्रस्तरं-विस्तीर्णं यज्ञविशेषं । (*prastaraṃ-vistīrṇaṃ yajñaviśeṣaṃ |*) Come and sit at this sacrifice that is proceeding at length; or the meaning is: come and sit on the darbha grass called barhis, spread here as a seat for this sacrifice.

O Yama, in this sacrifice now going on in your honour, the priests are reciting mantras and invoking you. Hearing their invocation, graciously come to this our sacrifice together with the Aṅgirases and the fathers, sit on the seat of darbha prepared here, and, satisfied with the oblation we offer, gladden the sacrificer too. This is the main purport of this Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अंगि॑रोभि॒रा ग॑हि य॒ज्ञिये॑भि॒र्यम॑ वैरू॒पैरि॒ह मा॑दयस्व ।  
> विव॑स्वंतं हुवे॒ यः पि॒ता ते॒ऽस्मिन्य॒ज्ञॆ ब॒र्हिष्या नि॒षद्य॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अंगिरःभिः । आ । गहि । यज्ञियेभिः । यम । वैरूपैः । इह । मादयस्व ।  
> विवस्वंतं । हुवे । यः । पिता । ते । अस्मिन् । यज्ञे । बर्हिषि । आ । निऽसद्य ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यम वैरूपैर्विविधरूपयुक्तैर्वैरूपसामप्रियैर्वा यज्ञियेभिर्यज्ञयोग्यैरंगिरोभिः सहा गहि । आगच्छ । अगत्य चेहास्मिन्यज्ञे मादयस्व ।'
> यजमानं हर्षय । यो विवस्वांस्ते तव पितास्ति अस्मिन्यज्ञे तं विवस्वंतं हुवे ।
> आह्वयामि । स चास्त्रीर्णे बर्हिष्या निषद्योपविश्य यजमानं हर्षयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Yama, come with the Aṅgirases, who are fit for sacrifice and who are of many forms or fond of the Vairūpa sāman. Having come, rejoice here in this sacrifice; gladden the sacrificer. Vivasvān, who is your father, I invoke in this sacrifice. Let him too sit down on the spread barhis and gladden the sacrificer.

#### Ṛk 5 (continued)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यम (*yama*)—O god Yama
- वैरूपैः (*vairūpaiḥ*)—those having many forms
- यज्ञियेभिः (*yajñiyebhiḥ*)—and worthy of worship
- अंगिरोभिः (*aṃgirobhiḥ*)—together with the Aṅgirases
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be gracious, come
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- मादयस्व (*mādayasva*)—gladden the sacrificer
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Vivasvat
- ते (*te*)—to you
- पिता (*pitā*)—is father
- विवस्वंतं (*vivasvaṃtaṃ*)—that Vivasvat
- अस्मिन् यज्ञे (*asmin yajñe*)—in this sacrifice
- हुवे (*huve*)—I call
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—on the seat of darbha grass
- आ निषद्य (*ā niṣadya*)—having sat down, let him too gladden the sacrificer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Yama, come together with the Aṅgirases, who have many forms and are worthy of worship. Gladden the sacrificer in this sacrifice. I call in this sacrifice Vivasvat, who is your father. Seated on the seat of darbha grass, may he too gladden the sacrificer.

##### English translation
Come hither, Yama, with the venerable multiform Angirasas, and be exhilarated; I summon Yivaswat, who is your father, to this sacrifice; may he seated on the sacred grass (delight the sacrificer).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk too, Yama is prayed to come to this sacrifice together with the Aṅgirases and the other Pitṛs of various forms. And Vivasvat, Yama's father, is invoked. The bhāṣyakāra explains the word वैरूपैः (*vairūpaiḥ*) as विविधरूपयुक्तैर्वैरूपसामप्रियैर्वा (*vividharūpayuktairvairūpasāmapriyairvā*): that is, Pitṛs having forms of various kinds; or, in accord with the Śruti sentence वैरूपग्ं साम भवति (*vairūpagṃ sāma bhavati*), Pitṛs who are fond of hearing the chanting of the special sāman-mantra called Vairūpa.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अंगि॑रसो नः पि॒तरो॒ नव॑ग्वा॒ अथ॑र्वाणो॒ भृग॑वः सो॒म्यासः॑ ।  
> तेषां॑ व॒यं सु॑म॒त् य॒ज्ञिया॑ना॒मपि॑ भ॒द्रे सौ॑मन॒से  ॑
> स्याम ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अंगिरसः । नः । पितरः । नवग्वाः । अथर्वाणः । भृगवः । सोम्यासः ।  
> तेषां । वयं । सुमतौ । यज्ञियानां । अपि । भद्रे । सौमनसे । स्याम ॥ ६ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अंगिरसोऽंगिरोनामका अथर्वाणोऽथर्वनामका भृगवो भृगुनामकाश्च
> नोऽस्माकं पितरो नवग्वा अभिनवगमनयुक्ताः । यद्वा । नूतनवस्त्रीतिजनका
> इत्यर्थः । ते च सोम्यासः सोममर्हंतीति सोम्याः । यज्ञियानां यज्ञार्हाणां तेषां सुमतावनुग्रहयुक्तायां बुद्धौ वयं स्याम । सर्वदा तिष्ठेम । अपि
> च सौमनसे भद्रे सौमनसस्य कारणे कल्याणे फले स्याम । सर्वदा तिष्ठेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Aṅgirases, Atharvans and Bhṛgus, so named, are our fathers (pitṛs), "नवग्वाः (*navagvāḥ*)": endowed with fresh movement (coming anew); or else, producers of delight through new things. They are "सोम्याः (*somyāḥ*)", worthy of Soma. May we always remain in the favouring mind (sumati) of these sacrifice-worthy ones, and also in the auspicious result that is the cause of good-heartedness (saumanasa).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—the Aṅgirases
- अथर्वाणः (*atharvāṇaḥ*)—the ṛṣis called Atharvans
- भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*)—the Bhṛgus
- नवग्वाः (*navagvāḥ*)—givers of fresh vitality
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—fathers (pitṛs)
- सोम्यासः (*somyāsaḥ*)—are worthy of the offering of Soma
- यज्ञियानां (*yajñiyānāṃ*)—worthy of worship
- तेषां (*teṣāṃ*)—their
- सुमता (*sumatā*)—in the mind of favour
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be
- अपि (*api*)—and
- भद्रे (*bhadre*)—auspicious
- सौमनसे (*saumanase*)—may we also be worthy of (their) affection

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirases, the ṛṣis called Atharvans, and the Bhṛgus, our fathers, givers of fresh vitality, are worthy of the offering of Soma. May we become worthy of the auspicious favour and affection of those worthy of worship.

##### English translation
The Angirasas, the Atharvas, the Bhrigus, who are entitled to the Soma, are our recent progenitors; may we ever have a place in the favour of these venerable (pitris); may we be ever held in their auspicious regard.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the words अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*), पितरः (*pitaraḥ*), अथर्वाणः (*atharvāṇaḥ*), भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*) in this Ṛk, Yāska has given a nirvacana for the present Ṛk. The Aṅgirases and the others mentioned are Pitṛ-deities.

### Printed p. 467
They are *mādhyamikas*, that is, Pitṛs of the middle region; Yama is their king. Therefore: माध्यमिकोयम इत्याहुः । तस्मान्माध्यमिकान् पित्थन्मन्यंते (*mādhyamikoyama ityāhuḥ | tasmānmādhyamikān pitthanmanyaṃte*) (Ni. 11-19). It is said that Yama too is a deity of the middle region.

अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—अंगारेष्टंगिराः । अंगारा अंगनाः (अंचनाः) (*aṃgāreṣṭaṃgirāḥ | aṃgārā aṃganāḥ (aṃcanāḥ)*) Ni. 3-17. The Aṅgirases are very famous ṛṣis. Formerly Prajāpati united with his daughter; the semen that fell from him dropped on the earth and stood in the form of a lake. The gods, wishing to dry it up, set Vaiśvānara fire around it. Then, as that semen blazed in the heat of the fire, first Āditya arose from it, and from the embers there the Aṅgirā ṛṣis, as stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, which we explained earlier. It is customary to say that these Aṅgirā ṛṣis are very famous Pitṛs. अंगाराः (*aṃgārāḥ*) means embers. After they have gone out and turned black, if one touches them the whole hand becomes sooty (अंचनाः (*aṃcanāḥ*)); hence the name अंगाराः (*aṃgārāḥ*).

पितर: (*pitara:*)—पिता पाता ना पालयिता वा (*pitā pātā nā pālayitā vā*) (Ni. 4-21). The word pitṛ means one who protects or guards. Who the Pitṛs are and what concerns them we have explained at length in the introduction to this sūkta.

अथर्वाण: (*atharvāṇa:*)—The root थर्व (*tharva*) means "to move" (थर्वतिः चरतिकर्मा (*tharvatiḥ caratikarmā*)). The word थर्वणः (*tharvaṇaḥ*) formed from it means those who move. The word अथर्वाणः (*atharvāṇaḥ*) conveys its negation: those who do not move but remain steady, of steady nature.

भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*)—अर्चिषि भृगुः संबभूव । भृगर्भृज्यमानो न देहे (*arciṣi bhṛguḥ saṃbabhūva | bhṛgarbhṛjyamāno na dehe*) (Ni. 3-17). As said above, when Prajāpati's semen was heated by Vaiśvānara fire, the ṛṣi Bhṛgu arose from the flame, as the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says. Because he shone like a flame he got the name Bhṛgu. The descendants of this ṛṣi are called भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*). They are famous Pitṛ-groups. Now we shall set out Yāska's nirvacana of the present Ṛk:

अंगिरसो नः पितरो नवगतयो नवनीतगतयो वाथर्वाणो भृगवः सोम्याः सोमसंपादिनस्तेषां वयं सुमत्कल्याण्यां मत्कल्याणियानामपि चैषां भद्रे भंदनीये भाजनवति वा कल्याणे मनसि स्यामेति ॥ (*aṃgiraso naḥ pitaro navagatayo navanītagatayo vātharvāṇo bhṛgavaḥ somyāḥ somasaṃpādinasteṣāṃ vayaṃ sumatkalyāṇyāṃ matkalyāṇiyānāmapi caiṣāṃ bhadre bhaṃdanīye bhājanavati vā kalyāṇe manasi syāmeti ‖*) (Ni. 11-19)

Here the Pitṛ-deities अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*), पितरः (*pitaraḥ*), भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*), अथर्वाणः (*atharvāṇaḥ*) have been explained above. Now अंगिरसो नः (*aṃgiraso naḥ*)… नवग्वाः (*navagvāḥ*) means नवगतयो नवनीतगतयो वा (*navagatayo navanītagatayo vā*): "of new movement", that is,

### Printed p. 468
those who come every month or every year to the Pitṛ-sacrifices (śrāddhas) to receive the kavya offering; or those who come with great longing for नवनीत (*navanīta*), butter. Thus Yāska explains the word नवग्वाः (*navagvāḥ*). सोम्याः (*somyāḥ*)—सोमसंपादिनः (*somasaṃpādinaḥ*): those who crush and press the soma plants and prepare the soma juice to offer to the gods. Since in the time of their sacrifices they prepared the soma juice thus, offered it to the gods and thereby obtained an excellent station, they got the name सोम्यासः (*somyāsaḥ*). The chief purport of the Nirukta statement is: may we remain in the excellent, praiseworthy, auspicious, favouring mind of those worship-worthy (or sacrifice-worthy) Pitṛs; that is, may we become worthy of their excellent favour.

माध्यमिको देवगण इति नैरुक्ताः । पितर इत्याख्यानं ॥ (*mādhyamiko devagaṇa iti nairuktāḥ | pitara ityākhyānaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 11-20). The authors of the Nirukta say that the Aṅgirases and the others mentioned belong to the divine group of the middle region (antarikṣa). Others hold that all of them were formerly ṛṣis who obtained an excellent station through their good deeds, and so all of them should be called Pitṛs.

> परेयुः ।  
> उ॒भा राजा॑ना स्व॒धया॒ मदं॑ता य॒मं प॑श्यासि॒ वरु॑णं च  ॒
> देवं ॥ ७ ॥

> उभा । राजाना । स्वधया । मदंता । यमं । पश्यासि । वरुणं । च । देवं ॥ ७ ॥

> शंसनीयाः । सूत्रितं च । प्रेहि प्रेहि पथिभिः पूर्व्यभिरिति पंचानां तृतीयामुद्धरेत् । अ. ६-१० । इति ॥
> यत्र यस्मिन्स्थाने नोऽस्माकं पूर्वे पुरातनाः पितरः पितामहादयः परेयुः पूर्वेभिः पूर्वस्मिन्काले भवैः । अनादिकालप्रवृत्तैरित्यर्थः । पथि-

**NOTE**

> भिर्मार्गैर्हे मत्सितः तत्स्थानं प्रेहि । प्रगच्छ । शीघ्रं गच्छ । गत्वा च स्वधयामृतान्नेन मदंतौ तृप्यंतौ राजाना राजानापुभोभौ यमं देवं द्योतमानं
> वरुणं च पश्यासी । पश्य ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When an initiated sacrificer dies in the midst of a sattra, the five Ṛks beginning प्रेहि (*prehi*), omitting the third, are to be recited by the Hotṛ. It is stated in the sūtra: प्रेहि प्रेहि पथिभिः पूर्व्यभिरिति पंचानां तृतीयामुद्धरेत् (*prehi prehi pathibhiḥ pūrvyabhiriti paṃcānāṃ tṛtīyāmuddharet*) (Ā. Sū. 6-10). "Where" (यत्र (*yatra*)), in which place, our ancient fathers, grandfathers and the rest, went forth; by the former paths, that is, paths that have been in use from beginningless time, go, go quickly, to that place.

### Printed p. 469
Having gone, see the two kings, Yama the shining god and Varuṇa, delighting (मदंतौ (*madaṃtau*)) in स्वधया (*svadhayā*), the immortal food.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O father) यत्र (*yatra*)—by which path
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- पूर्वे (*pūrve*)—ancient
- पितर: (*pitara:*)—grandfathers and others
- परेयुः (*pareyuḥ*)—went after death
- पूर्व्यभिः (*pūrvyabhiḥ*)—beginningless
- पथिभिः (*pathibhiḥ*)—by those same paths
- प्रेहि (*prehi*)—set out
- स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—with the immortal food
- मदंता (*madaṃtā*)—who have attained satisfaction
- राजाना (*rājānā*)—and are lords
- यमं (*yamaṃ*)—Yama
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—shining
- वरुणं च (*varuṇaṃ ca*)—and Varuṇa
- उभा (*ubhā*)—both these
- पश्यासि (*paśyāsi*)—you will see there

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O father, by the path on which our ancient grandfathers and others went after death, by those same beginningless paths set out. There you will see Yama and the shining Varuṇa, who are satisfied with the immortal food and are lords.

##### English translation
Depart, depart, by the former paths by which our forefathers have departed; there should you behold the two monarchs Yama and the divine Varuna rejoicing in the Swadha.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In a sattra, a sacrifice performed over a long time, if the sacrificer who has undergone the initiation dies before the sacrifice is completed, the Hotṛ should recite the following five Ṛks beginning प्रेहि (*prehi*) (7-11), omitting the third (the 9th). In this matter the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra is cited: प्रेहि प्रेहि पथिभिः पूर्व्यभिरिति पंचानां तृतीयामुद्धरेत् (*prehi prehi pathibhiḥ pūrvyabhiriti paṃcānāṃ tṛtīyāmuddharet*) (Ā. 6-10).

It should be understood that the seer of this sūkta recited this Ṛk and the next one addressing his dead father, who, while the body was (burning in the fire), had left the earthly body and was in the form of a departed spirit. Therefore, addressing the departed one, he prays: O father, go by the very ancient path by which our elders, famous and deceased in our line, went and reached the world of the Pitṛs. The ancient path means

### Printed p. 470
the path by which, from beginningless time until now, countless departed ones, dwelling in the departed-spirit body, have gone before and reached the world of the Pitṛs. If you go by such a path you will go to the Pitṛ-world and there see Yama and Varuṇa, the lords of that world, says the seer. It should be understood that the ancient seers believed that in the Pitṛ-world Varuṇa too dwells there besides Yama.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सं ग॑च्छस्व पि॒तृभिः॒ सं य॒मेने॑ष्टापू॒र्तेन॑ पर॒मे व्यो॑मन् ।  
> हि॒त्वाया॑व॒द्यं पुन॒रस्त॒मेहि॒ संग॑च्छस्व त॒न्वा॑ सु॒वर्चाः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । गच्छस्व । पितृभिः । सं । यमेन । इष्टापूर्तेन । परमे । विओमन् ।  
> हित्वाय । अवद्यं । पुनः । अस्तं । आ । इहि । सॆं । गच्छस्व । तन्वा । सुवर्चाः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मदीय पितः ततस्त्वं परम उत्कृष्टे व्योमन्वॊमनि स्वर्गाख्ये स्थाने
> स्वभूतैः पितृभिः सह सं गच्छस्व । इष्टापूर्तेन श्रौतस्मार्तदानफलेन सं गच्छस्व । तत
> इष्टापूर्तेन सहागम्यावद्यं पापं हित्वा परित्यज्यास्तं वियमानाख्यं गृहमेहि ।
> आगच्छ । ततः सुवर्चाः । तृतीयार्थे प्रथमा । सुवर्चसा शोभनदीप्तियुक्तेन
> तन्ना स्वशरीरेण सं गच्छस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O my father, then, in the supreme, excellent heaven called व्योमन् (*vyoman*), unite with the Pitṛs who are your own. Unite with इष्टापूर्तेन (*iṣṭāpūrtena*), the fruit of the gifts enjoined by Śruti and Smṛti. Then, having come with the इष्टापूर्त (*iṣṭāpūrta*), abandon अवद्यं (*avadyaṃ*), sin, and come to your home called अस्तं (*astaṃ*). Then सुवर्चाः (*suvarcāḥ*) (nominative in the sense of the instrumental) means: unite with your own body, possessed of fair radiance.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O father) परमे (*parame*)—in the supremely excellent
- व्योमन् (*vyoman*)—heaven-station
- पितृभिः (*pitṛbhiḥ*)—with the Pitṛs
- सं गच्छस्व (*saṃ gacchasva*)—unite
- इष्टापूर्तेन (*iṣṭāpūrtena*)—joined with the fruits that fulfil your desires
- यमेन (*yamena*)—with Yama
- सं (*saṃ*)—unite
- अवद्यं (*avadyaṃ*)—the body that is the root of sin
- हित्वाय (*hitvāya*)—having abandoned
- अस्तं (*astaṃ*)—to the excellent home
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- एहि (*ehi*)—come and join
- सुवर्चाः (*suvarcāḥ*)—having fair radiance
- तन्वा (*tanvā*)—with the body
- सं गच्छस्व (*saṃ gacchasva*)—unite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O father, in the supremely excellent heaven-station unite with the Pitṛs. Unite with Yama, who satisfies your desire. Abandon the body that is the root of sin and come again to the excellent home. Unite with a body of fair radiance.

### Printed p. 471

*English Translation.*

Be united with the Pitṛs, with Yama, and with the fulfilment of your wishes in the highest heaven; discarding iniquity, return to your abode, and unite yourself to a luminous body.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As said in the previous Ṛk, after one's own father (or the father who is in the departed body) has gone by the ancient path to the world of the Pitṛs, the seer states in this Ṛk what he should do.

O Pitṛ, after you have gone to the world of the Pitṛs (this may be called heaven), the earlier Pitṛs, our elders who died in former times, are there. Join them, and meet Yama. Then, in that divine world, enjoy the wishes you desire. That is, the fruits that were due for the sacrificial and other good works you performed while living on earth — enjoy those fruits now in this divine world. Here, if the word इष्टापूर्तेन (*iṣṭāpūrtena*) is divided into इष्ट (*iṣṭa*) + अपूर्तेन (*apūrtena*), the word means desires that you wished for until now but that remain unfulfilled. Since such desires could not be enjoyed while living on earth, the seer says: enjoy them now in this divine world. And after coming to this divine world, he voices the prayer: give up the sins you may have committed so far and the sorrow that is their fruit, obtain a excellent body of the nature of light, that is, a shining body, so as to be happy in this divine world, and dwell in an excellent abode.

> पैतृमेधिके कर्मणि स्मशानायतनं प्रोक्षत्यपेत वीतेति । सूत्रितं च ।

> शृशाने पूर्वं स्थिता हे पिशाचादयः अतोऽस्मादृतयजमानदहनस्थानादपेत i अपगच्छत । वीत । विशेषेण गच्छत । वि सर्पत च । इदं स्थानं परित्यज्य
> नानाभावेन दूरतरं देशं गच्छतेत्यर्थः । पितरोऽस्मै मृतयजमानस्यार्थायैतं लोकमिदं दहनस्थानमक्रन् । यमस्याज्ञयान्नकुर्वन् । यमोऽप्यहोभिर्दिवसैरद्भिरभ्युक्षणोदकैरक्तुभी रात्रिभिर्व्यक्तं संगतं । शुद्धिनिमित्तैः कालोदकादिभिः शोधितमित्यर्थः । अवसानं दहनस्थानमस्मै मृतयजमानस्यार्थाय ददाति ।
> दत्तवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the funeral rite (Paitṛmedhika) he sprinkles the cremation ground with the verse अपेत वीत (*apeta vīta*). This is enjoined in the sūtra: going round the site three times counter-clockwise (prasavya) with a branch of the śamī and water from the pit, he sprinkles, saying *apeta vīta vi ca sarpatātaḥ* (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-2-18). Piśācas and others who stood earlier in the cremation ground: depart from this place where the dead sacrificer is to be burnt; go away in particular; leave this place and disperse in various ways to a farther region. The Pitṛs have made this place, the cremation ground, for the sake of the dead sacrificer, by Yama's command. Yama too has given the cremation ground to the dead sacrificer, joined with days, with waters of sprinkling and with nights, that is, purified by purifying agents such as time and water.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O piśācas and others) अतः (*ataḥ*)—from this cremation place
- अपेत (*apeta*)—move far away
- वीत (*vīta*)—go off to a great distance (वीत (*vīta*))
- वि सर्पत च (*vi sarpata ca*)—scatter to various directions
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for this dead man
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—the Pitṛs
- एतं लोकं (*etaṃ lokaṃ*)—this place
- अक्रन् (*akran*)—have prepared
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—Yama also
- अहोभिः (*ahobhiḥ*)—with days
- अद्भिः (*adbhiḥ*)—with waters
- अक्तुभिः (*aktubhiḥ*)—with nights
- व्यक्तं (*vyaktaṃ*)—joined
- अवसानं (*avasānaṃ*)—the cremation place
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to this sacrificer
- ददाति (*dadāti*)—has appointed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O piśācas and others, move away from this cremation place. Go off to a distant land. Scatter in various directions. The Pitṛs have prepared this place for the dead man; Yama too has given to the dead man, the sacrificer, this cremation place joined with days, waters and nights.

##### English translation
Depart from hence, begone, go far off, (evil spirits); the Pitris have assigned this place to him, Yama has given him a place of cremation consecrated by days, streams and nights.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Pitṛ-rites, that is, the funeral rites, the verse अपेत वीत (*apeta vīta*) is to be recited and the appointed spot in the cremation ground sprinkled with water, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra गर्तोदकेन शमीशाखया त्रिःप्रसव्यमायतनं परिव्रजन् प्रोक्षत्यपेत वीत वि च सर्पतातः (*gartodakena śamīśākhayā triḥprasavyamāyatanaṃ parivrajan prokṣatyapeta vīta vi ca sarpatātaḥ*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-2-10).

### Printed p. 473

In this Ṛk the seer says that the piśācas and others who may be at the place where the dead body is burnt in the cremation ground should leave that place and move far away.

यमो ददात्यवसानमस्मै (*yamo dadātyavasānamasmai*)—Yama himself has given this cremation place for this dead man, that is, has arranged it. Since a man after death must come to his own world, the world of the Pitṛs, Yama takes interest in this matter and has already determined and arranged, in the cremation ground, the place where the dead body of the man about to come to his world will be burnt. Therefore, O piśācas and others, leave this place and go away. This region has been purified with water and the like for the dead man's funeral rite; so leave this region and move far away — thus the seer describes. Here अवसान (*avasāna*) means the cremation place (last resting place), the place where the dead body is burnt with fire. A spot in the cremation ground is designated, purified by sprinkling with water and so on, and the cremation takes place there. That is what is described here by the word अवसानं (*avasānaṃ*).

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अति॑ द्रव सारमे॒यौ श्वानौ॑ चतुर॒क्षौ श॒बलौ॑ सा॒धुना॑ प॒था ।  
> अथा॑ पि॒त्थन्सु॑ वि॒दत्तौ॒ उपे॑हि य॒मेन॒ ये स॑ध॒मादं॒  
> मदं॑ति ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अति । द्रव । सारमेयौ । श्वानौ । चतुःs अक्षौ । शबलौ । साधुना । पथा ।  
> अथ । पित्थन् । सुविदत्रान् । उप । इहि । यमेन । ये । सधर्मादं । मदंति ॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनुस्तरण्या वृक्कौ पार्श्वयोराम्रफलाकृती । तावुद्धृत्य प्रेतस्य हस्तयोर्निदधात्यति द्रव सारमेयाविति द्वाभ्यां । सूत्रितं च । वृक्कावुद्धृत्य पाण्योरादध्यादति द्रव सारमेयौ श्वानौ । आ. गृ. सू. ४-३-२० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the funeral rite, the two lumps (वृक्कौ (*vṛkkau*)) in the shape of mango fruits, taken from the *anustaraṇi* (cow) at the sides, are placed in the hands of the dead man with the two verses अति द्रव सारमेयौ (*ati drava sārameyau*). It is laid down in the sūtra: वृक्कावुद्धृत्य पाण्योरादध्यादति द्रव सारमेयौ श्वानौ (*vṛkkāvuddhṛtya pāṇyorādadhyādati drava sārameyau śvānau*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-3-20).

### Printed p. 474

> हे अग्ने साधुना पथा समीचीनेन मार्गेण श्वानावुभावति द्रव । अतिक्रम्य
> गच्छ । यमसंबंधिनौ यौ श्वानौ प्रेतस्य बाधकौ तौ परित्यज्य समीचीनेन मार्गेण
> प्रेतं नयेत्यर्थः । कीदृशौ श्वानौ । सारमेयौ । सरमा नाम काचित्प्रसिद्धा देवशुनी । तस्याः पुत्रौ चतुरक्षौ उपरिभागे पुनरप्यक्षिद्वयं ययोस्तादृशौ । अथ
> शोभनमार्गेण गमनानंतरं ये पितरो यमेन सधमादं सहर्षं मदंति
> प्राप्रुवंति तान्सुविदत्रान् सुष्पभिज्ञानित्थनुपेहि । उपगच्छ ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, pass by the good path beyond the two dogs; leaving the two dogs of Yama who harass the departed, lead the departed by the good path. What are the dogs like? Sārameyas: Saramā is a well-known divine bitch, and these are her sons; four-eyed, having another pair of eyes above. Then, after going by the good path, go to those Pitṛs who rejoice joyfully with Yama, who are well-knowing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O departed one) साधुना पथा (*sādhunā pathā*)—following the very best path
- सारमेया (*sārameyā*)—born of Saramā
- शबलौ (*śabalau*)—of variegated colour
- चतुरक्षौ (*caturakṣau*)—having four eyes
- श्वानौ (*śvānau*)—Yama's messengers (the dogs)
- अति द्रव (*ati drava*)—escape and pass beyond
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- ये (*ye*)—which Pitṛs
- यमेन (*yamena*)—with Yama
- सधमादं (*sadhamādaṃ*)—together
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—rejoice
- सुविदत्रान् (*suvidatrān*)—excellent, wise
- पित्थन् (*pitthan*)—those Pitṛs
- उपेहि (*upehi*)—join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O departed one, follow the excellent path. Escape and pass beyond these two dogs, born of Saramā, of variegated colour, with four eyes. Then join those Pitṛs, excellent and wise, who rejoice together with Yama.

##### English translation
Pass by a secure path beyond the two spotted four-eyed dogs, the progeny of Sarama, and join the wise Pitris who rejoice joyfully with Yama.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the funeral rite, two flour lumps the size of a mango fruit are placed in the hands of the corpse and the two Ṛks beginning अतिद्रव सारमेयौ (*atidrava sārameyau*) are to be recited, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra अति द्रव सारमेयौ श्वानौ (*ati drava sārameyau śvānau*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-3-20).

In this Ṛk and the next, the two dogs called Sārameyas, the pups of the divine bitch Saramā, are mentioned. How Saramā, the divine bitch, being with Indra, greatly helped the gods in searching for the cows carried off by the Paṇis

### Printed p. 475

is described in the 108th sūkta of this Maṇḍala. Setting out at Indra's command to search for the cows, she travelled far, crossed the deep and very watery river Rasā, went to the region where the Paṇis were, conversed with them, explained to them the power of Indra and the gods and told them to give back the cows; when they did not agree, she returned from there, reported the whole matter to Indra and helped him — this is stated in that sūkta. It is said that the two dogs called Sārameyas, sons of this Saramā, were Yama's guards, punished the people who came to the world of the Pitṛs, but did not trouble those who had done good deeds. Even so, the seer warns that these dogs may cause trouble to the departed who leaves the dead body and goes to the world of the Pitṛs; and in the 12th Ṛk, praying to Agni, he describes that the departed should be led by a different, circuitous path, avoiding the region where these dogs are.

On the basis of what is described in Ṛks 10–12 of this sūkta, these things appear: the two dogs are with Yama and guard his house and the like; each has four eyes; each has a long snout; they are always alert and watch the path on which the Pitṛs travel; they are famed as Yama's messengers.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O king Yama, hand over this departed one to those two dogs of yours, for protection. What are the dogs like? Guardians of Yama's

> धेहि । संपादय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

house; four-eyed, endowed with four eyes; guardians of the road; नृचक्षसौ (*nṛcakṣasau*), proclaimed by men (the text says that men versed in Śruti, Smṛti and Purāṇa proclaim them). Having given the departed to those two dogs, grant him welfare (स्वस्ति (*svasti*), security) and also freedom from disease (अनमीवं (*anamīvaṃ*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजन् (*rājan*)—O lord
- यम (*yama*)—O god Yama
- रक्षितारौ (*rakṣitārau*)—able to guard your house
- चतुरक्षौ (*caturakṣau*)—having four eyes
- पथिरक्षी (*pathirakṣī*)—guarding the paths
- नृचक्षसौ (*nṛcakṣasau*)—praised by men
- यौ तेश्वान् (*yau teśvān*)—which dogs of yours there are
- ताभ्यां (*tābhyāṃ*)—to them
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this departed one

- अनमीवं च (*anamīvaṃ ca*)—freedom from disease
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—bring about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O lord Yama, commit this departed one for protection to those dogs of yours that can guard your house, have four eyes, guard the paths and are praised by men. (Let the departed be protected by them.) Bring about welfare and freedom from disease for this departed one.

##### English translation
Entrust him, O king, to your two dogs, which are your protectors, Yama, the four-eyed guardians of the road, renowned by men, and grant him prosperity and health.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

रक्षितार् (*rakṣitār*)—this word is an adjective of the word श्वानौ (*śvānau*). These dogs guard Yama's house. Or it can be understood to mean that they protect the Pitṛs newly arriving in the world of the Pitṛs.

चतुरक्षौ (*caturakṣau*)—अक्षिचतुष्टययुक्तौ (*akṣicatuṣṭayayuktau*). Ordinary dogs have only two eyes; these dogs have four eyes, that is, two on each side, four in all. These four eyes help them to watch the road and the house carefully.

पथिरक्षी (*pathirakṣī*)—मार्गस्य रक्षकौ (*mārgasya rakṣakau*). Besides Yama's house they also watch the path by which the Pitṛs come from the earth to Yama; that is, the departed who, devoted to the performance of good works, died

### Printed p. 477
Out of the whole passage here the sense is that the dogs mean to punish only those who have done wrong, without troubling anyone else. Therefore the seer warns the departed one to be very careful with regard to these dogs, and Agni is prayed to lead the departed one to Yama by another, circuitous road, so that he does not fall under their eyes.

नृचक्षसौ—मनुष्यैःख्याप्यमानौ । श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणाभिज्ञाः पुरुषास्तौ प्रख्यापयंति । (*nṛcakṣasau—manuṣyaiḥkhyāpyamānau | śrutismṛtipurāṇābhijñāḥ puruṣāstau prakhyāpayaṃti |*) They are praised by men. That is, good men who know the Śruti, Smṛti, Purāṇas and the like praise greatly the commendable work of these dogs; for the dogs do not trouble good men but injure only the sinful, and so these men praise with open voice the dogs' discernment of what is fitting and unfitting.

In the second half of this Ṛk, Yama is prayed to protect well the body of the departed one who comes to Yama, so that it is free from the affliction of diseases.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two dogs, Yama's messengers, move everywhere among people, with the living beings as their object. They are of what kind? उरुणसौ (*uruṇasau*): having long noses; असुतृपौ (*asutṛpau*): taking the life-breaths of others and being sated by them; उदुंबलौ (*uduṃbalau*): of wide strength. Those two messengers are asked to give back to us today, in this rite, that good, auspicious life-breath, for the seeing of the sun.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उरूणसौ (*urūṇasau*)—having long noses
- असुतृपौ (*asutṛpau*)—getting satisfaction by sucking the life-breaths of others
- उदुंबलौ (*uduṃbalau*)—having exceedingly great strength
- यमस्य (*yamasya*)—of Yama
- दूतौ (*dūtau*)—these dogs, who are messengers
- जनान् अनु (*janān anu*)—seeking out living beings
- चरतः (*carataḥ*)—they roam
- त्वा (*tvā*)—those two dogs
- सूराय्य (*sūrāyya*)—of the sun
- दृशये (*dṛśaye*)—for the sight
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrificial rite
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—auspicious

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Sārameyas, long-snouted, getting satisfaction by sucking the life-breaths of others, of exceeding strength, and messengers of Yama, roam seeking living beings. May those two dogs today, in this sacrificial rite, give us again the auspicious life-breath, for the seeing of the sun.

##### English translation
The messengers of Yama, broad-nosed, and of exceeding strength, and satiating themselves with the life (of mortals), hunt mankind ; may they allow us this day a prosperous existence here, that we may look upon the sun.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk it is said that Yama's dogs roam among people; that is, they keep searching for beings who are about to die, in order to carry them to Yama. In the Atharvaveda too these dogs are described in many places. In some places they are said to be two, in others many, and they are said to be the messengers who carry the departed spirits of beings to Yama after they die.

In the second half of this Ṛk, तावस्मभ्यं.... .... .... ..... भद्रं (*tāvasmabhyaṃ.... .... .... ..... bhadraṃ*), the prayer is that Yama's dogs, who roam among people and carry off their life-breaths, should not trouble us, that is, should not carry us to Yama, but should let us go on living for some time more on this earth, seeing the sun, and should do us good.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O priests, press Soma, the creeper-soma, for Yama as deity, and likewise offer the oblation for Yama. The sacrifice in which Agni is the messenger is "Agni-messenger"; Agni's being a messenger is recorded elsewhere: अर्गिर्दूतो यस्मिन्यज्ञे सोऽयमग्निदूतः । अग्नेर्दूतत्वमन्यत्राम्नातं । अग्निर्देवानां दूत आसीत् । तै. सं. २-५- ८.५ । इति । (*argirdūto yasminyajñe so 'yamagnidūtaḥ | agnerdūtatvamanyatrāmnātaṃ | agnirdevānāṃ dūta āsīt | tai. saṃ. 2-5- 8.5 | iti |*). अरंकृतः (*araṃkṛtaḥ*): furnished with many substances as ornaments. Such a sacrifice goes to Yama alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यमाय (*yamāya*)—with Yama as the object
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- सुनुत (*sunuta*)—press
- यमाय (*yamāya*)—with Yama as the object
- हविः (*haviḥ*)—the oblation
- जुहुत (*juhuta*)—offer
- अग्निदूतः (*agnidūtaḥ*)—having Agni himself as messenger
- अरंकृतः (*araṃkṛtaḥ*)—adorned with many substances
- यज्ञ: (*yajña:*)—this sacrifice
- यमं ह (*yamaṃ ha*)—Yama himself
- गच्छति (*gacchati*)—approaches

(The address "O priests" is supplied before यमाय (*yamāya*).)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, press Soma for Yama. Offer the oblation for Yama. This sacrifice, which has Agni himself as messenger and is adorned with many substances, approaches Yama.

##### English translation
Pour out the Soma for Yama; to Yama offer the oblation, the decorated sacrifice of which Agni is the messenger proceeds to Yama.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk and in the next two Ṛks the seer prays the priests to offer the oblation in the fire with Yama as the object. Since neither Yama nor the other deities come in person to the sacrificial ground to receive the offering, the oblations offered to them must be made in the consecrated fire. अरंकृतः (*araṃkṛtaḥ*) in this Ṛk means अलंकृतः (*alaṃkṛtaḥ*), prepared and adorned. 

### Printed p. 480
The prayer expressed here is that Agni, thus prepared and adorned, should carry, in the manner of a messenger, the offerings made in him for Yama to Yama, and make them reach him.

- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- दीर्घमायुः (*dīrghamāyuḥ*)—long life
- आ यमत् (*ā yamat*)—may he give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, offer the oblation provided with ghee, with Yama as the object. Approach him and pray. May Yama, well-known among the gods, give us long life for an excellent life.

##### English translation
Offer the oblation of clarified butter to Yama, and stand nigh (to the altar); It is he who among the gods gives us a long life to live

### Printed p. 481

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

O priests, offer in the fire, with mantras, the oblation mixed with ghee, with Yama as the object. The chief sense of this Ṛk is that Yama, who is among the gods gratified by it, should favour us by giving a long life, so that we may live for a long time.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒माय॒ मधु॑मत्तमं॒ राज्ञे॑ ह॒व्यं जु॑होतन ।  
> इ॒दं नम॒ ऋषि॑भिः पूर्व॒जेभ्यः॒ पूर्वे॑भ्यः पथि॒कृद्भ्यः॑ ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यमाय । मधुमर्तमं । राज्ञे । हव्यं । जुहोतन ।  
> इदं । नमः । ऋषिभ्यः । पूर्वजेभ्यः । पूर्वेभ्यः । पथिकृत्भ्यः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋत्विजः यमाय राज्ञे मधुमत्तममतिशयेन मधुरं हव्यं पुरोडाशादिकं हविर्जुहोतन । जुहुत । पूर्वजेभ्यः सृष्ट्पादावुत्पन्नेभ्यः आत एव
> पूर्वेभ्योऽस्मत्तः पूर्वभाविभ्यः पथिकृद्भ्यः शोभनमार्गकारिभ्य ऋषिभ्य इदं प्रत्य.
> क्षं यथा भवति तथा नमोऽस्तु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O priests, offer to king Yama the most sweet oblation (cake and the like); जुहोतन (*juhotana*) means जुहुत (*juhuta*). To the sages who were born at the beginning of creation, and therefore are earlier than ourselves, who make good paths, let there be this adoration, as if in visible presence.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O priests) राजे (*rāje*)—to the lord
- यमाय (*yamāya*)—with Yama as the object
- मधुमत्तमं (*madhumattamaṃ*)—most sweet
- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—the oblation
- जुहोतन (*juhotana*)—offer
- पूर्वजेभ्यः (*pūrvajebhyaḥ*)—born earlier
- पूर्वेभ्यः (*pūrvebhyaḥ*)—ancient
- पथिकृद्भ्यः (*pathikṛdbhyaḥ*)—guides of the way
- ऋषिभ्यः (*ṛṣibhyaḥ*)—to the sages
- इदं नमः (*idaṃ namaḥ*)—these my salutations

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, offer the most sweet oblation with the lord Yama as the object. These my salutations to the sages, born earlier, ancient, and guides of the way.

### Printed p. 482

##### English translation
Offer to the royal Yama this most sweet oblation; (let) this our adoration (be addressed) to the ancient sages, the first followers of (virtuous) paths.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Besides praying the priests to offer the oblation in the fire through the offering, with Yama as the object, the seer, in the second half of this Ṛk, salutes his ancestors: "Here I bow" to the sages who lived formerly on this earth, died, and now dwell near Yama in the world of the fathers, to our elders who have died, and to the other fathers who have made clear the way to Yama's world.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्रिक॑द्रुकेभिः पतति॒ षळु॒र्वीरेक॒मिद्बृ॒हत् ।  
> त्रि॒ष्टुब्ब्गा॑य॒त्री छंदां॑सि॒ सर्वा॒ ता य॒म आहि॑ता ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्रिकद्रुकेभिः । पतति । षट् । उर्विः । एकं । इत् । बृहत् ।  
> त्रिस्तुप् । गायत्री । छंदांसि । सर्वा । ता । यमे । अहिता ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्रिकद्रुकेभिः । द्वितीयार्थे तृतीयैषा । त्रिकद्रुकान् । ज्योतिर्गौरायुरिति
> त्रयो यागविशेषास्त्रिकद्रुका उच्यंते । तात्पत्यंगभावाय संरक्षणार्थं च पतति।
> यमस्तान् प्राप्नोति । षट्संख्याका उर्वीर्भूमिः कृताकृतप्रत्यवेक्षणाय
> प्राप्नोति । ताश्चोर्व्यः शाखांतरमंत्रे समाम्नाताः ! षण्मोर्वीरंहसस्पांतु
> द्याश्च पृथिवी चापश्चौषधयश्चोर्क्च सूनृता चेति । एकमिदेकमेव बृहद्महज्जगद्यमश्च प्रतिपालनीयः प्राप्नोति । किंच यानि त्रिष्टुब्जायत्रादीनि च्छंदांसि संति
> सर्वाणि तानि च्छंदांसि यम आहितानि । ऋत्विग्भिः स्तुतिश्वेनावस्थितानि !!

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

त्रिकद्रुकेभिः (*trikadrukebhiḥ*): this instrumental stands for the accusative; it means the त्रिकद्रुकान् (*trikadrukān*). Three special sacrifices, Jyotis, Gau and Āyus, are called Trikadrukas. Yama reaches them, for the sake of their being his auxiliaries and for their protection. The six उर्वीः (*urvīḥ*), the earths, he reaches to inspect what has been done and not done; those six wide ones are recorded in the mantra of another śākhā: षण्मोर्वीरंहसस्पांतु द्याश्च पृथिवी चापश्चौषधयश्चोर्क्च सूनृता चेति । (*ṣaṇmorvīraṃhasaspāṃtu dyāśca pṛthivī cāpaścauṣadhayaścorkca sūnṛtā ceti |*). *ekamit*: the one great world, to be protected by Yama, he reaches. Moreover, all the metres, Triṣṭubh, Gāyatrī and the rest, are placed in Yama; that is, they stand by the priests' praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्रिकद्रुकेभिः (*trikadrukebhiḥ*)—the three sacrifices called Jyotis, Gau, Āyus
- पतति (*patati*)—Yama gets
- षट् उर्वीः (*ṣaṭ urvīḥ*)—he occupies the six wide earths
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—great …

### Printed p. 483

(Continuing the Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 14 of the previous sūkta:) …having a great form. एकमित् (*ekamit*)—he pervades the whole world. त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*)—the one named Triṣṭup. गायत्री (*gāyatrī*)—the one named Gāyatrī and the rest. छंदांसि (*chaṃdāṃsi*)—the seven metres that are well known. सर्वा ता (*sarvā tā*)—all of them. यमे (*yame*)—in Yama. अहिता (*ahitā*)—are established.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Yama takes part in the three sacrifices called Jyotiḥ, Gauḥ and Āyuḥ. He traverses the six wide earths. He pervades the whole world, which has a great form. All the seven metres that are well known, such as Triṣṭup and Gāyatrī, are established in Yama.

##### English translation
(Yama) acquires the three Trikadruka srcrifices; the six earths, the one great (moving world); the Trishtubh, Gayatri, all the sacred metres converge in Yama.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

षट् उर्विः (*ṣaṭ urviḥ*)—the six kinds of earth, namely षण्मोर्वीरंहसस्पांतु द्यौश्च पृथिवी चापश्चौषधयश्शोर्क् च सूनृता च (*ṣaṇmorvīraṃhasaspāṃtu dyauśca pṛthivī cāpaścauṣadhayaśśork ca sūnṛtā ca*). That is: Yama comes and takes part in the rites performed on the three days of the Agniṣṭoma, called Jyotiḥ, Gauḥ and Āyuḥ. Besides, he comes to the six kinds of earth, namely the atmosphere, the earth, the waters, the plants and trees, Ūrk and Sūnṛtā, to watch the movements, that is, the good and evil deeds, of all the creatures that may be in those regions. This is the explanation given here: there is no place where Yama does not come; he comes everywhere and always watches the deeds of creatures. The seer praises Yama thus: the priests praise such a Yama with the mantras of many (all) metres, Triṣṭup, Gāyatrī and the rest.

What the work called Bṛhaddevatā says about this sūkta is given here:

परेयिवांसमित्यत्र स्तूयते मध्यमो यमः । (*pareyivāṃsamityatra stūyate madhyamo yamaḥ |*)
अथर्वाणोऽथ भृगवोऽज्गरसः पितरः सह । (*atharvāṇo 'tha bhṛgavo 'jgarasaḥ pitaraḥ saha |*)
षष्ठ्यां देवगणास्तत्र संस्तूयंते द्युभक्तयः । (*ṣaṣṭhyāṃ devagaṇāstatra saṃstūyaṃte dyubhaktayaḥ |*)
पितृभिश्चांगिरोभिश्च संस्तुतो दृश्यते यमः । (*pitṛbhiścāṃgirobhiśca saṃstuto dṛśyate yamaḥ |*)
मंत्रेषु बहुशः पादे विवस्वंतं पिता हि सः । (*maṃtreṣu bahuśaḥ pāde vivasvaṃtaṃ pitā hi saḥ |*)
संस्कार्यप्रेतसंयुक्तैः पितृभिः स्तूयते यमः । (*saṃskāryapretasaṃyuktaiḥ pitṛbhiḥ stūyate yamaḥ |*)
प्रेहि प्रेहीति तिसृषु प्रेताशिष उदाहृताः । (*prehi prehīti tisṛṣu pretāśiṣa udāhṛtāḥ |*)

### Printed p. 484

पित्थाणां हि पतिर्देवो यमस्तस्मात्स सूक्तभाक् । (*pitthāṇāṃ hi patirdevo yamastasmātsa sūktabhāk |*)
अति द्रव तृचे श्वानौ परं पित्र्यमुदीरतां । (*ati drava tṛce śvānau paraṃ pitryamudīratāṃ |*)
(Bṛ. De. 7-155 to 159)

Since we have explained the particulars stated in the above verses in the introduction of this sūkta and in the special topics of the Ṛks, there is no need to explain them again here. These Ṛks are used in the funeral rites and the like performed in the later (apara) rites.

## Sūkta 15 (Maṇḍala 10)

Introduction: The Ṛks of this sūkta beginning उदीरतां (*udīratāṃ*) and of the next sūkta beginning मैनमग्ने (*mainamagne*) are used in the later rites performed in the cremation ground, as the Bṛhaddevatā says:

परं पित्र्यमुदीरतां । (*paraṃ pitryamudīratāṃ |*) (preceded by abridgement dots)
उत्तरेण तु सूक्तेन स्मशाने कर्म शंसति । (*uttareṇa tu sūktena smaśāne karma śaṃsati |*)
पितृदेवासुराणां च अभवन्नग्नयस्त्रयः । (*pitṛdevāsurāṇāṃ ca abhavannagnayastrayaḥ |*)
हव्यकव्यवहौ चोभौ सहरक्षाश्च नाम यः । (*havyakavyavahau cobhau saharakṣāśca nāma yaḥ |*)
तत्र मैनमिति त्वैतत्कव्यवाहनसंस्तुतिः । (*tatra mainamiti tvaitatkavyavāhanasaṃstutiḥ |*)
इतराणि तु दैव्यस्य स्तुतिर्नास्यासुरस्य च । (*itarāṇi tu daivyasya stutirnāsyāsurasya ca |*)
(Bṛ. De. 7, 159-160)

The Ṛks in उदीरतां (*udīratāṃ*) (sūkta 15) and मैनमग्ने (*mainamagne*) (sūkta 16) describe the later rites performed in the cremation ground. The fire used in this rite is called Kavyavāha. It is said here that, according to the rites, there are three fires used in the respective rites. The fire that carries the oblation to the gods in sacrifices is Havyavāhana; the fire that carries the offering to the fathers in the rites for the fathers is Kavyavāhana; the fire that protects the sacrificial rite from Rākṣasas and the like is called Saharakṣāḥ: thus there are three varieties of Agni. Since these sūktas describe the later rites, the praise of the fire called Kavyavāhana is the principal one. Besides, in the sūkta मैनमग्ने (*mainamagne*) there is praise of the Kavyavāhana fire and also of other deities. In some places Agni is praised with the word Kravyāda. Kravya means flesh, Kravyāda means one who eats flesh.

### Printed p. 485

The meaning is "eater of flesh". Does Agni eat flesh? Since the dead body is burnt in the fire, the fire consumes it. Therefore in Ṛks such as मैनमग्ने (*mainamagne*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-16-1), शृतं यदा (*śṛtaṃ yadā*) (10-16-2), क्रव्यादमग्नि (*kravyādamagni*) (10-16-9), यो अग्निः क्रव्यवाहनः (*yo agniḥ kravyavāhanaḥ*) (10-16-11) and the like, Agni is praised with the epithet Kravyāda.

Funeral rites: In the Vedas, passages concerning death are few. Where they occur, rarely, it is only to pray that death befall enemies and that long life be one's own. Only at the time of the corpse-rites does the thought of the other world arise. Both burning and burying of corpses were in practice. In 10-16 the rite of cremation is stated, and in another (10-18-10 to 13) burial. A house of earth is also mentioned in one place (7-89-1). Both kinds of fathers are found: those burnt by fire and those not burnt (10-15-14, Ath. Saṃ. 18-2-34). Cremation is the right way for the dead to go to the upper world. In the books describing the rites, it is laid down that only the ashes and bones of the cremated, infants and ascetics are to be buried (compare Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-1).

The history of life in the other world is connected with the funeral rite itself. Agni takes the dead body to the other world, to the neighbourhood of the fathers and gods (10-16-1 to 4; 10-17-3). He places the mortal in the highest immortality (1-31-7). Men go, through Agni, the bird of the world of the gods, to the highest place of Sūra to which the ancient seers, born in the beginning, have gone, to the highest heaven, or to the world of the good (Vā. Saṃ. 18-51, 52). The Gārhapatya fire carries the dead to the world of the good (Ath. Saṃ. 1-120-1). Agni first burns the body of the dead and afterwards places him in the world of the living (Ath. Saṃ. 18-3-71). The fire that burns corpses (Kravyāda) is different from the fire that carries the oblation to the gods (10-16-9). There is a prayer to Agni to burn the goat, which is his portion, and to protect the body (10-16-4). During the rite the corpse is laid on the skin of a black goat, and an animal or a goat is offered in the sacrifice. In the rite prayer is made to Agni and Soma to heal any wounds that may have been inflicted on the body by a bird, animal, ant or snake (10-16-6).

It is believed that the dead soul goes to heaven with the smoke (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4.4-7). It is a very long way; there Pūṣan is the guardian and Savitṛ shows the way

### Printed p. 486

(10-17-4). The offered goat goes ahead to the fathers and announces the arrival of the dead soul; going so, it must pass the black darkness on the way and then reach the third storey of heaven, the abode of the fathers (Ath. Saṃ. 9-5-1, 3; compare 8-1-8). For use in the other-world life, ornaments and clothes are provided for the dead person; this custom is still in practice (18-4-31). There are traces here and there that his wife and weapons were also burnt with the corpse (10-18-8, 9). A bundle of firewood was tied to the corpse; its purpose was that the departed spirit of the dead should not know the way to come back (compare Ath. Saṃ. 5-19-12; Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-18-2 and 19-97-16).

The soul: Fire or the grave destroys only the body; they cannot destroy the personality of the dead. The belief is that even in a state of unconsciousness the life can be separated from the body, and that life exists even after the body is destroyed. The whole of sūkta 10-58 calls back to return the life of one lying as if dead. In the Ṛgveda there seems to be no basis for belief in the soul's obtaining another body; but in the Brāhmaṇa it is said that one who has not performed the sacrifice in the prescribed manner, having died, is born again and becomes subject to death (Śa. Bā. 10-4-3-10). Prāṇa, ātman, asu (bodily force, 1-113-16; 1-140-8), manas (the seat of thought and feeling, located in the heart; 8-89-5): all these are words for life. Many passages, especially in the Atharvaveda, say that where there is asu or manas there is life, and where there is none, death. Asunīti or asunīta is the name of the way that leads the lives of the dead from this world to the upper world (10-15-4; 10-16-2). In the mantras used in the funeral rite the words asu or manas are not used; pitṛ, mātṛ and the like are used. Hence the soul is not like a shadow; it too has a personality. Although men attain immortality only after leaving the body (Śa. Brā. 11-4-3-9), the worlds such as heaven are also material (prākṛta), so the corpse too has a principal place. The body has a share in the existence of the other worlds (10-16-5, Ath. Saṃ. 18-2-26). A body free from all faults (Ath. Saṃ. 6-120-3) cannot be called an ordinary earthly body; it may be called a body purified by the power of Agni (compare 10-16-6), or the "subtle body" of the later Vedāntins. It is said that if the fires to be collected after the cremation are destroyed, that is the severest punishment (Śa. Brā. 11-6-3-11; 14-6-9-28); from this one can see how important the position of the corpse is. In 10-16-3 it is said that the eye of the dead should go to Sūra and the breath to Vāyu. Since Agni takes the dead to the other world,

### Printed p. 487

it does not seem fitting that each limb goes to a separate place. Perhaps it is said so in accordance with the description of Virāṭpuruṣa. In the same passage (10-16-3; also in 10-58-7) it is said that the life of the dead enters the waters or plants; perhaps this is the beginning of entry into another body.

Continuing along the path followed by the fathers (10-14-7), the life of the dead goes to the world of eternal light (9-113-7); then, endowed with splendour equal to the gods (Ath. Saṃ. 11-1-37), he goes on a chariot, or on wings (Ath. Saṃ. 4.34.4), or on the wings that Agni uses when killing the evil beings (Vā. Sa. 18-52). Borne upward by the Marut, breathing the pleasant wind and cooled by raindrops, the soul regains its ancient form (Ath. Saṃ. 18-2-21 to 26) and, endowed with glory, together with Yama reaches the highest heaven where the fathers pass their time in joy (10-14-8, 10; 10-154-4, 5). The attainment of heaven in this way is described as returning home (अस्तं (*astaṃ*); 10-14-8). Yama, knowing him as his own (Ath. Saṃ. 18-2-37), gives him too a resting place (19-14-9).

According to the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, the dead leave this world and pass between two fires; those fires burn the evil soul and let only the good go forward. The good souls that go ahead take either the path to the fathers or the path to Sūra (Śa. Brā. 1-9-3-2; etc.). In the Upaniṣads two paths are stated for those who have attained knowledge of Brahman. One (for the perfectly knowing) is going to Brahman. The second is the way to heaven; as soon as the fruit of their full works is exhausted, they come from this heaven and are born again on earth. Those who have no acquaintance with the ātman at all go to the world of evil deities or of ghosts and spirits, or, becoming wicked, are born again on earth.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उदीरतामिति चतुर्दशर्चं पंचदशं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रम्यते । उदीरतां
> षळूना तंखः पित्र्यं जगत्येकादशी । यामायना: परे पंचेति वचनाद्यमपुत्रः
> शंखाख्य ऋषिः । अग्निष्वात्ता इत्येषा जगती शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । पितरो देवता ॥ गतः
> सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ अष्टकायामुदीरतामवर इत्याद्या अष्टावृचो होमार्थाः ॥
> सूत्रितं च । उदीरतामवर उत्परास इत्यष्टाभिर्हुत्वा । आ. गृ. २ ४-६ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning उदीरतां (*udīratāṃ*) is the fifteenth and has fourteen Ṛks. The Anukramaṇī says: उदीरतां षळूना तंखः पित्र्यं जगत्येकादशी (*udīratāṃ ṣaḷūnā taṃkhaḥ pitryaṃ jagatyekādaśī*). By the statement यामायना: परे पंच (*yāmāyanā: pare paṃca*) the seer is the son of Yama, called Śaṅkha. The eleventh Ṛk, अग्निष्वात्ताः (*agniṣvāttāḥ*), is a Jagatī; the rest are Triṣṭubh. The deity is the Pitṛs. The use of the sūkta has been stated (earlier). In the Aṣṭakā rite the eight Ṛks beginning उदीरतामवर (*udīratāmavara*) are for oblation, and the sūtra says उदीरतामवर उत्परास इत्यष्टाभिर्हुत्वा (*udīratāmavara utparāsa ityaṣṭābhirhutvā*) (Ā. Gṛ. 2 4-6).

> महापितृयज्ञे पितरः सोमवंत इत्यस्यानुवाक्योदीरतामित्येषा । सूत्रितं च ।
> पितरोग्निष्वात्ता यम उदीरतामवर उत्परासः । आ. २-१९ । इति ॥ अग्निमारुतेऽप्येषा धाय्या । सूत्रितं च । मातली कवैर्यमो अंगिरोभिरुदीरतामवर
> उत्परासः । अ. ५-२० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, the Ṛk उदीरतां (*udīratāṃ*) is the anuvākyā for the offering to पितरः सोमवंतः (*pitaraḥ somavaṃtaḥ*); the sūtra says पितरोग्निष्वात्ता यम उदीरतामवर उत्परासः (*pitarogniṣvāttā yama udīratāmavara utparāsaḥ*) (Ā. 2-19). This Ṛk is also the dhāyyā in the Agnimāruta (śastra); the sūtra says मातली कवैर्यमो अंगिरोभिरुदीरतामवर उत्परासः (*mātalī kavairyamo aṃgirobhirudīratāmavara utparāsaḥ*) (Ā. 5-20).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning उदीरतां (*udīratāṃ*) is the fifteenth in the first anuvāka. It has fourteen Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: उदीरतां षळूना शंखः पित्र्यं जगत्येकादशी (*udīratāṃ ṣaḷūnā śaṃkhaḥ pitryaṃ jagatyekādaśī*). Since the Anukramaṇī says यामायनः परे पंच (*yāmāyanaḥ pare paṃca*) (the seer of the next five sūktas is a son of Yama), the seer of this sūkta is Śaṅkha, the son of Yama. The eleventh Ṛk, अग्निष्वात्ताः (*agniṣvāttāḥ*), is in Jagatī metre. The remaining Ṛks are in Triṣṭup metre; the deity is the Pitṛs; the use of the sūkta was stated earlier. In the rite called Aṣṭakā the first eight Ṛks of this sūkta, beginning उदीरतामवरे (*udīratāmavare*), are to be used for oblation, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya sūtra उदीरतामवर उत्परास इत्यष्टाभिर्हुत्वा (*udīratāmavara utparāsa ityaṣṭābhirhutvā*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 2-4-6). In the Mahāpitṛyajña, in the oblation made to the special group of fathers called पितरः सोमवंतः (*pitaraḥ somavaṃtaḥ*), the first Ṛk उदीरतां (*udīratāṃ*) is to be recited as anuvākyā mantra, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta sūtra पितरोग्निष्वात्ता यम उदीरतामवर उत्परासः (*pitarogniṣvāttā yama udīratāmavara utparāsaḥ*) (Ā. 2-19); and among the mantras of the Agnimāruta śastra this Ṛk उदीरतां (*udīratāṃ*) is to be recited as dhāyyā mantra, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta sūtra मातली कनैर्यमो अंगिरोभिरुदीरतामवर उत्परासः (*mātalī kanairyamo aṃgirobhirudīratāmavara utparāsaḥ*) (Ā. 5-20).
