##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्रिविधाः पितर उत्तमा मध्यमा अधमाश्चति । यथाविधं श्रौतं कर्मानुष्ठाय पितृत्वं प्राप्ता उत्तमाः । स्मार्तकर्ममात्रपरा मध्यमाः । आत्रापि कैश्चित्संस्कारैर्विकला अधमाः । एतदेवाभिप्रेत्य ये अग्निदग्धा ये अनग्निदग्धा इत्यादिमंत्र
> अन्नातः । तेष्ववरे निकृष्टा उदीरतां । उत्तमं हविः प्राप्नुवंतु । परास उत्तमाः
> पितर उदीरतां । मध्यमाः पितरश्चोदीरतां । ते सर्वॆऽप्यस्मद्विषये सोम्यासः
> सोम्या अनुग्रहपराः संतु । ये पितरोऽवृका वृकवदरण्यश्ववदस्मासु हिंसामकुर्वंत ऋतज्ञा अस्मदनुष्ठितं यज्ञं जानंतोऽसुमस्मत्पाणमायुः रक्षितुं
> प्राप्ताः ते पितरो हवेष्वस्मदीयॆष्वाह्वानेषु नोऽस्मानवंतु । रक्षंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says the Pitṛs are of three kinds: the best, the middling and the lowest. Those who performed the Vedic (śrauta) rites as prescribed and so attained the state of Pitṛs are the best. Those devoted only to the Smārta rites are the middling. Those among them who are deficient in some sacraments are the lowest. With just this in view the mantra beginning ये अग्निदग्धा (*ye agnidagdhā*) ("those who are fire-burnt, those who are not fire-burnt") and the like was composed. Of these, the "lower" (अवरे (*avare*)), the inferior ones, are to rise up, that is, to receive the best oblation. The "higher" (परासः (*parāsaḥ*)), the best Pitṛs, are to rise up, and the middling Pitṛs are to rise up. May all of them be सोम्यासः (*somyāsaḥ*), that is, gracious towards us. Those Pitṛs who are अवृकाः (*avṛkāḥ*), that is, who do not harm us as a wolf or a forest-horse would, who are ऋतज्ञाः (*ṛtajñāḥ*), that is, who know the sacrifice performed by us, and who have come to protect our life-breath (असुं (*asuṃ*)), our life-span: may those Pitṛs protect us at our invocations (हवेषु (*haveṣu*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अवरे (*avare*)—the Pitṛs in the lower region
- उदीरतां (*udīratāṃ*)—let them receive our oblation
- परासः (*parāsaḥ*)—those who are in the best world
- उत् (*ut*)—let them receive our oblation
- मध्यमाः (*madhyamāḥ*)—those in the middle world
- पितरः उत् (*pitaraḥ ut*)—let the Pitṛs also accept
- सोम्यासः (*somyāsaḥ*)—may all of them be of a gracious mind towards us
- ये पितरः (*ye pitaraḥ*)—those Pitṛs who
- अवृकाः (*avṛkāḥ*)—not cruel like wolves
- ऋतज्ञाः (*ṛtajñāḥ*)—who know our sacrificial rites
- असुं (*asuṃ*)—our life-breath
- ईयुः (*īyuḥ*)—have come to protect
- ते (*te*)—they
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- हवेषु (*haveṣu*)—at the times of our invocation
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*)—let them protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the Pitṛs in the lower world, those in the best world and those in the middle world accept our oblations. May all of them be gracious towards us. May those Pitṛs who are not cruel like wolves, who know our sacrificial rites and who have come to protect our life-breath protect us at the time of our invocation.

##### English translation
Let the lower, the upper, the intermediate Pitris, rise up, accepting the Soma libation : may those progenitors who, unlike wolves, acknowledging our offerings, have come to preserve our lives, protect us upon our invocations.

### Printed p. 490

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given an etymological explanation of this Ṛk: उदीरतामवर उदीरतां पर उदीरतां मध्यमाः पितरः सोम्याः सोमसंपादिनस्तेऽसुं प्राणमन्वीयुरवृका अनमित्राः सत्यज्ञा वा यज्ञज्ञा वा ते न आगच्छंतु पितरो ह्वानेषु ॥ (*udīratāmavara udīratāṃ para udīratāṃ madhyamāḥ pitaraḥ somyāḥ somasaṃpādinaste 'suṃ prāṇamanvīyuravṛkā anamitrāḥ satyajñā vā yajñajñā vā te na āgacchaṃtu pitaro hvāneṣu ‖*) (Ni. 11-19).

अवरे (*avare*): the Pitṛs in the lower part, that is, on the earth, or in the lower part of the world of the Pitṛs; परासः (*parāsaḥ*): the Pitṛs dwelling in the heavenly world; मध्यमाः (*madhyamāḥ*): the Pitṛs of the middle station, dwelling in the atmosphere; सोम्यासः (*somyāsaḥ*): those who formerly prepared and offered Soma in the sacrifice for offering to the gods. Those who have come to protect our life-breath, those who do no harm of any kind to anyone, those who are not enemies, that is, who do not wish ill, those who know the nature of truth or of sacrifice — whichever Pitṛs there are, may all of them come to us at the invocation we are now making and protect us.

On the word अवृकाः (*avṛkāḥ*): वृकः (*vṛkaḥ*) is a wolf. The nature of the wolf is to do harm. When the word is used of men it means those who do harm, wicked people. अवृकाः (*avṛkāḥ*) means those who are not wolves, who harm no one, good people.

अनमित्रा: (*anamitrā:*): मित्र (*mitra*) means friend, benefactor. अमित्र (*amitra*) is one who is not a friend, an enemy; अनमित्र (*anamitra*) is one who is not an enemy, that is, a friend, a benefactor. Thus मित्र (*mitra*) and अनमित्र (*anamitra*) have the same meaning. Because two negative prefixes occur in this word, (Two negetives make one affirmative) the word indicates the original meaning.

The commentator has said that there are three kinds of Pitṛs: उत्तमा मध्यमा अधमाश्चेति (*uttamā madhyamā adhamāśceti*). Thus:

उत्तमाः (*uttamāḥ*): यथाविधं श्रौतं कर्मानुष्ठाय पितृत्वं प्राप्ता उत्तमाः (*yathāvidhaṃ śrautaṃ karmānuṣṭhāya pitṛtvaṃ prāptā uttamāḥ*). Those who performed the best rites, sacrifices and the like, in due form, and as the fruit of that good conduct obtained the station of Pitṛs, are renowned as the best among the Pitṛs.

मध्यमाः (*madhyamāḥ*): स्मार्तकर्मपरा मध्यमाः (*smārtakarmaparā madhyamāḥ*). The Pitṛs who, as stated in the Smṛtis, Purāṇas and so on, worshipped the gods and obtained the state of Pitṛs through that merit are the middling.

### Printed p. 491
अधमाः (*adhamāḥ*): अत्रापि कैश्चित्संस्कारैर्विकला अधमाः (*atrāpi kaiścitsaṃskārairvikalā adhamāḥ*). Those who, through faults and omissions in the above rites, were unable to carry them out completely are counted the lowest among the Pitṛs. Thus the nature of the three kinds of Pitṛs, best, middling and lowest, and their stations have been explained. In accordance with this there is also the mantra ये अग्निदग्धाः (*ye agnidagdhāḥ*). That is, those whose dead body is burnt in the fire with mantra-accompanied sacraments attain the best station among the Pitṛs; they are called "fire-burnt". Those, on the other hand, who without the fire-sacraments are drowned in water, or for whom there is no one to perform the later rites, or who are not sanctified by rites as prescribed, are all called "not fire-burnt". These obtain the middle or the lowest station among the Pitṛs. The purport of this Ṛk is that all such Pitṛs, who acquire Soma, are free from harm, protect life and know the performance of sacrifices, should heed our invocation and protect us.

> च । आहं पितृन्सु विदत्रा अवित्सीदं पितृभ्यो नमो अस्त्वद्य स्वादुष्किलायमिति

> य ईयुः पितृलोकं प्राप्ताः । ये चान्य उपरासो यजमानजन्मन उपर्यु-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, for the verse पितरो बर्हिषदः (*pitaro barhiṣadaḥ*) the verse इदं पितृभ्यः (*idaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ*) is the second anuvākyā. The sūtra was quoted before: Ā. 2-19. इदं पितृभ्य इत्येषा धाय्या (*idaṃ pitṛbhya ityeṣā dhāyyā*); and it is also prescribed: आहं पितृन्सु विदत्रा अवित्सीदं पितृभ्यो नमो अस्त्वद्य स्वादुष्किलायमिति चतस्रः । (*āhaṃ pitṛnsu vidatrā avitsīdaṃ pitṛbhyo namo astvadya svāduṣkilāyamiti catasraḥ |*) (Ā. 5-20). पूर्वासः (*pūrvāsaḥ*) are those born before the sacrificer, such as elder brothers and grandfathers, who have gone (ईयुः (*īyuḥ*)) to the world of the Pitṛs. And the others, उपरासः (*uparāsaḥ*), born after the sacrificer's birth, such as younger brothers and his own sons, have gone to the world of the Pitṛs.

> तन्नाः कनिष्ठभ्रातृस्वपुत्रादय ईयुः पितृलोकं प्राप्ताः । येऽप्यन्ये पार्थिवे
> पृथिवीसंबंधिनि रजसि रजोगुणकार्येऽस्मिन्कर्मण्या निषत्ता हविः स्वीकर्तुमागत्योपविष्टाः । ये वा केचिदन्ये बंधुवर्गरूपाः पितरो विक्षु बंधुरूपासु
> प्रजास्वा निषत्ताः श्राद्धादिस्वीकारायागत्योपविष्टाः । कीदृशीषु विक्षु ! सुवृजनासु ।
> व्यज्यते परित्यज्यते दारिद्रमनेनेतिवृजनं धनं । शोभनं वृजनं यासां ताः
> सुवृजनाः । तादृशीषु । धनसमृद्ध्या श्राद्धादिकर्मपरास्वित्यर्थः । सर्वेभ्य उक्तेभ्यः
> पितृभ्योऽद्यास्मिन्कर्मणेदं नमोऽस्तु । अयमाहुतिप्रदानपूर्वको नमस्कारो
> भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Also the others who are seated (आ निषत्ताः (*ā niṣattāḥ*)) in the terrestrial (पार्थिवे (*pārthive*)) रजसि (*rajasi*), in this rite, a product of the quality rajas, having come to receive the oblation. Or any other Pitṛs of the class of kinsmen who are seated among the people (विक्षु (*vikṣu*)), the kinsfolk, having come to accept śrāddha and the like. What sort of people? सुवृजनासु (*suvṛjanāsu*): वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*) is wealth, by which poverty is cast off; those who have good wealth are सुवृजनाः (*suvṛjanāḥ*), people devoted to śrāddha and other rites through abundance of wealth. To all the Pitṛs mentioned, today, in this rite, let there be this homage (नमः (*namaḥ*)): let this act of homage, preceded by the giving of the oblation, take place.

- अस्तु (*astu*)—let there be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among the elder Pitṛs and grandfathers and others, those who have joined the world of the Pitṛs; among those younger than we, those who have died; those who have come to the terrestrial world for the oblation and are seated; and whichever other Pitṛs are seated among excellent wealthy people: to all such Pitṛs I make obeisance at this time of the sacrifice.

##### English translation
Let this our adoration be to-day addressed to those Pitris our predecessors, to those our successors, who have departed (to the world of the manes); to those who are seated in the terrestrial sphere, to those who are present among opulent people.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the oblation-rite called Mahāpitṛyajña, when the offering is made to the group of Pitṛs beginning पितरो बर्हिषदः (*pitaro barhiṣadaḥ*), this Ṛk इदं पितृभ्यः (*idaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ*) is to be recited as the second anuvākyā mantra, as stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, already quoted before (Ā. 2-19). In the Agnimāruta-śastra mantras too this Ṛk इदं पितृभ्यः (*idaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ*) is to be recited as a dhāyyā mantra, as set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: आहं पित्थन्सुविदत्ता अवित्सीदं पितृभ्यो नमो अस्त्वद्य स्वादुष्किलायमिति चतस्रः (*āhaṃ pitthansuvidattā avitsīdaṃ pitṛbhyo namo astvadya svāduṣkilāyamiti catasraḥ*) (Ā. 5-20).

### Printed p. 493
In this Ṛk the seer describes the different forms of certain Pitṛs.
पूर्वासः यजमानोत्पत्तेः पूर्वमुत्पन्ना ज्येष्ठभ्रातृपितामहादयः (*pūrvāsaḥ yajamānotpatteḥ pūrvamutpannā jyeṣṭhabhrātṛpitāmahādayaḥ*): those who came into being before the birth of the sacrificer (or the seer), that is, older in age than himself, elder brothers, paternal grandfathers and the like, who have died and are in the station of Pitṛs.
उपरासः यजमानजन्मन उपरि उत्पन्नाः कनिष्ठभातृस्वपुत्रादयः (*uparāsaḥ yajamānajanmana upari utpannāḥ kaniṣṭhabhātṛsvaputrādayaḥ*): younger brothers, sons and the like, younger in age than himself, who for some reason died before him and are in the world of the Pitṛs.
पार्थिवे रजसि आ निषत्ताः (*pārthive rajasi ā niṣattāḥ*): those who have come here, to this earthly world, to the Pitṛ-sacrifice now being performed, to receive the oblation, and are seated.
ये वा नूनं सुवृजनासु विक्षु (*ye vā nūnaṃ suvṛjanāsu vikṣu*): some further Pitṛs who, though not belonging directly to our own lineage, belong to our circle of kinsmen and have come and are seated to receive oblations at śrāddha and the like. The seer describes himself as making obeisance to the Pitṛs of these various kinds.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, the sacrificer, have obtained (अवित्सि (*avitsi*)), face to face, the Pitṛs who are सुविदत्रान् (*suvidatrān*), who know my devotion well. I have also obtained the नपातं (*napātaṃ*), the non-perishing, of the pervading (विष्णोः (*viṣṇoḥ*)) sacrifice, and its विक्रमणं (*vikramaṇaṃ*), its special progress. The Pitṛs who are बर्हिषदः (*barhiṣadaḥ*), who sit on the sacred grass, have come (आगमिष्ठाः (*āgamiṣṭhāḥ*)) here to this rite in abundance: having come with respect, together with the food of the sacrifice, स्वधया (*svadhayā*), with cakes and the like, they partake (भजंत (*bhajaṃta*): serve, make use of) of the share of the food (पित्वः (*pitvaḥ*)) of the Soma that has been pressed (सुतस्य (*sutasya*)).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, the sacrificer, have brought before me the Pitṛs who know my devotion exceedingly. We have obtained the freedom from destruction of the pervading sacrifice and its orderly expansion. The Pitṛs who rest on seats of darbha grass have come to our sacrifice. They partake of the pressed Soma together with the food called svadhā.

##### English translation
I have brought to my presence the Pitris who are well cognizant (of my worship), the infallibility, and progressive advance of the sacrifice ; (the Pitris) who sit on the sacred grass frequently coming hither worship the food of the effused (Soma) with the sacrificial cake.

> पितरो बर्हिषद इत्यत्र श्रुतत्वाद्यागं कृत्वा प्रेत्य पितृलोकं प्राप्ता बर्हिषदः ।
> तादृशा हे पितरः अर्वागर्वाचीनानामस्माकमूती रक्षा भवद्भिः कर्तव्येति शेषः। वो
> युष्मदर्थमिमा हवैतानि हवींषि चक्रम । अतस्तानि जुषध्वं । ते हविर्जुष्टवंतो
> यूयं शंतमेन सुखतमेनावसा रक्षणेन निमित्तभूतेना गत । अभिमुख्येनास्मान्नाप्नुत । अथानंतरं नोऽस्मभ्यं शं सुखं योर्दुःखवियोगमरपः पापरहितं
> च दधात । दत्त ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses बर्हिषदः (*barhiṣadaḥ*) as "those who sit at the sacrifice". He cites the passage "those who are sacrificers are the Fathers, the Barhiṣads" (the statement that those who performed the sacrifice, on dying reached the world of the Fathers and became Barhiṣads). He addresses such Fathers: "O Fathers, for us who are turned towards you, you must provide protection" (this is the supplied remainder of the sentence). "We have made these oblations for you; therefore enjoy them. Having enjoyed the oblations, come to us with your most pleasant protection, facing us. Then bestow upon us happiness (शं (*śaṃ*)), separation from sorrow (योः (*yoḥ*)) and freedom from sin (अरपः (*arapaḥ*))."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बर्हिषदः (*barhiṣadaḥ*)—those seated at the sacrifice
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—O Fathers
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—to us, seated facing you
- ऊती (*ūtī*)—your protection is necessary
- वः (*vaḥ*)—addressing you
- इमा हव्या (*imā havyā*)—these oblations
- चक्रम (*cakrama*)—we have prepared
- जुषध्वं (*juṣadhvaṃ*)—partake of them
- ते (*te*)—you who have partaken of the oblation
- शंतमेन (*śaṃtamena*)—most happiness-giving
- अवसा (*avasā*)—with protection
- आ गत (*ā gata*)—come facing us
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- शं (*śaṃ*)—happiness
- योः (*yoḥ*)—freedom from sorrow
- अरपः (*arapaḥ*)—freedom from sin
- दधात (*dadhāta*)—bring about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Fathers seated at the sacrifice, your protection is absolutely necessary for us who sit facing you. We have prepared these oblations for you. Partake of them. Having partaken of the oblation, come to us with your most happiness-giving protection, facing us. Afterwards grant us happiness, freedom from sorrow and freedom from sin.

##### English translation
Pitris, Barhishads, protect (us who are) in your presence; we have made these oblations for you, accept them: come with your most felicitous protection, and bestow upon us health and happiness, and pardon from sin-

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the words शं योः (*śaṃ yoḥ*) in this Ṛk, Yāska gives an etymology and explains the meaning: शंयोः । (शंयुः सुखंयुः) अथानः शंयोररपो दधात । रपो रिप्रमिति पापनामनी भवतः । शमनं रोगाणां यावनं च भयानां ॥ (*śaṃyoḥ | (śaṃyuḥ sukhaṃyuḥ) athānaḥ śaṃyorarapo dadhāta | rapo ripramiti pāpanāmanī bhavataḥ | śamanaṃ rogāṇāṃ yāvanaṃ ca bhayānāṃ ‖*) (Ni. 4-21)

### Printed p. 496
शंयुः (*śaṃyuḥ*) means desiring peace or happiness. The meaning of the example sentence is: "Grant us happiness and peace free from sin." The two words रपः (*rapaḥ*) and रिप्रं (*ripraṃ*) are synonyms denoting sin. The intention is: bring about cessation (that is, release) from diseases and the removal of fear.

बर्हिषद पितरः (*barhiṣada pitaraḥ*)—who such Fathers are, the commentator explains thus: बर्हिषदः यज्ञे सीदंतीति बर्हिषदः । अत्रापि-ये वै यज्ञानस्ते पितरो बर्हिषदः (*barhiṣadaḥ yajñe sīdaṃtīti barhiṣadaḥ | atrāpi-ye vai yajñānaste pitaro barhiṣadaḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 1.6.9) इत्यत्र श्रुतत्वाद्यागं कृत्वा प्रेत्य पितृलोकं प्राप्ता बर्हिषदः (*ityatra śrutatvādyāgaṃ kṛtvā pretya pitṛlokaṃ prāptā barhiṣadaḥ*). The word बर्हिषदः (*barhiṣadaḥ*) means those who have come and sit upon the darbha grass called बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*), spread as a seat at the sacrifice. Such a grass seat is prepared at sacrifices so that the invoked gods may come and sit. The Fathers spoken of in the present Ṛk are those who formerly performed sacrifices according to rule and, after death, went to the world of the Fathers; these are called Barhiṣads, so the commentator explains the word.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महापितृयज्ञे पितरः सोमवंत इत्यस्य याज्योपहूताः पितर इत्येषा ।
> सूत्रितं च । उपहूताः पितरः स्कोम्यासस्त्वं सोम प्र चिकितो मनीषा ।
> आ. २-१९ । इति ॥
> सोम्यासः सोम्या अस्मदनुग्रहपराः सोमसंपादिनो वा पितरो बर्हिषेषु यागार्हेषु प्रियेषु तृप्तिकरेषु निधिषु निधिसदृशेषु हविःषु निमित्तभूतेषु सत्सूपहूता अस्माभिराहूतास्ते पितर आ गमंतु । आगच्छंतु । अगत्य चेहास्मि-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, this verse उपहूताः पितरः (*upahūtāḥ pitaraḥ*) is the yājyā for the offering to the Fathers "possessed of Soma" (पितरः सोमवंतः (*pitaraḥ somavaṃtaḥ*)). It is prescribed in the sūtra: उपहूताः पितरः स्कोम्यासस्त्वं सोम प्र चिकितो मनीषा (*upahūtāḥ pitaraḥ skomyāsastvaṃ soma pra cikito manīṣā*) (Ā. 2-19). सोम्यासः (*somyāsaḥ*): Fathers worthy of Soma, bent on favouring us, or procurers of Soma. They are invoked by us, when the oblations that are fit for the sacrifice, dear and satisfying, like treasures, are present; let those Fathers come. Having come, let them here, in this rite, hear the praises we address; and having heard, let them speak in our favour, "this sacrificer is good", declaring it with regard. Let those Fathers protect us.

> रक्षंतु ॥

- आस्मान् (*āsmān*)—us
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*)—let them protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Fathers whom we invoke to receive the oblations that are fit for sacrifice and pleasing: let such Fathers come, showing favourable disposition towards us. Let them hear our praises recited at the times of this rite. Let them speak words of praise concerning us. Let them protect us.

##### English translation
May the Pitris who are entitled to the Soma come, when invoked by us, to the agreeable treasures connected with the sacred grass; let them here listen (to our praises). let them protect us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, in the homa made to the Fathers of the group "possessed of Soma", this Ṛk उपहूताः पितरः (*upahūtāḥ pitaraḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is stated by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra उपहूताः पितरः सोम्यासस्त्वं सोम प्र चिकितो मनीषा (*upahūtāḥ pitaraḥ somyāsastvaṃ soma pra cikito manīṣā*) (Ā. 2.19).

> पित्थणामयं स्वाभाविको धर्मः अथैनं पितरः प्राचीनावीतिनः सव्यं
> जान्वाच्य । शत-२-४-२-२ । इति वचनात् ! हे पितरः विश्वे सर्वॆ यूयं जान्वाच्य
> भूमौ निपात्य दक्षिणतो दक्षिणपार्श्वे निषद्योपविश्येममस्मदीयं यज्ञमभि
> गृणीत । अभिष्टुत ! विशिष्टतृप्तियोगात्परया प्रीत्या सगुणोऽयं यज्ञ इति प्रशंसतेत्यर्थः । अपि च वो युष्माकं यत्किंचित्कर्मवैगुण्यजनितवागोऽपराधं
> पुरुषता मनुष्यत्वेन हेतुना कराम वयं कृतवंतः हे पितरः तेन केन चिदप्यपराधेन नोऽस्मान्मा हिंसिष्ट ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the natural custom of the Fathers, by the statement अथैनं पितरः प्राचीनावीतिनः सव्यं जान्वाच्य (*athainaṃ pitaraḥ prācīnāvītinaḥ savyaṃ jānvācya*) (Śa. 2-4-2-2). O Fathers, all of you, having bent the knee and placed it on the ground, having sat down on the right side, praise this sacrifice of ours (अभि गृणीत (*abhi gṛṇīta*)): from the special satisfaction obtained, with the highest delight, commend "this sacrifice is accompanied by its qualities". Further, whatever offence of yours, arising from some defect in the rite, we have committed by reason of our being human, O Fathers, do not harm us for any such offence.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—O Fathers
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all of you
- जानु आच्य (*jānu ācya*)—resting on the knee
- दक्षिणतः (*dakṣiṇataḥ*)—on the right side
- निषद्य (*niṣadya*)—having sat
- इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*)—this sacrifice of ours
- अभि गृणीत (*abhi gṛṇīta*)—praise
- वः (*vaḥ*)—with regard to you
- यत् आगः (*yat āgaḥ*)—whatever sin
- पुरुषता (*puruṣatā*)—through the ignorance natural to man
- कराम (*karāma*)—if we have done
- केन चित् (*kena cit*)—for whatever kind of sin
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा हिंसिष्ट (*mā hiṃsiṣṭa*)—do not harm

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Fathers, all of you, resting on the knee and sitting on the right side, praise this sacrifice of ours. If we have committed any sin with regard to you through the ignorance natural to man, do not harm us for any such sin.

##### English translation
Having sat down on the right side with bended knee, you all accept this sacrifice. Harm us not, Pitris, for any offence which through human (infirmity) we may have committed towards you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

आच्य जानु दक्षिणतः निषद्य (*ācya jānu dakṣiṇataḥ niṣadya*)—पितृणामयं स्वाभाविको धर्मः । अथैनु पितरः प्राचानावीतिनः सव्यं जान्वाच्य (*pitṛṇāmayaṃ svābhāviko dharmaḥ | athainu pitaraḥ prācānāvītinaḥ savyaṃ jānvācya*) (Śa. Brā. 2-4-2-2) इति वचनात् (*iti vacanāt*). Addressing the Fathers

### Printed p. 499
the seer speaks thus: "O Fathers, bending your right knee, with the sacred thread worn on the left, come and sit on the seat prepared on the south side of this sacrificial altar." The commentator says that sitting with the knee bent, facing south, is the natural custom prescribed for the Fathers, and to support this he gives as illustration a statement of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आसी॑नासो अरु॒णीना॑मु॒पस्थे॑ र॒यिं ध॑त्त दा॒शुषे॒ मर्त्या॑य ।  
> पु॒त्रेभ्यः॑ पितर॒स्तस्य॒ वस्वः॒ प्र य॑च्छत॒ त इ॒होर्जं॑ दधात ॥७॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आसीनासः । अरुणीनां । उपस्थे । रयिं । धत्त । दाशुषे । मर्त्याय ।  
> पुत्रेभ्यः । पितरः । तस्य । वस्वः । प्र । यच्छत । ते । इह । ऊर्जं । दधात ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अरुणीनामारोचमानानां ज्वालानां वा देवतानां वोपस्थे समीपस्थाने
> वेद्याख्य आसीनास उपविष्टाः पितरः यूयं दाशुषे हर्विदर्तवते मत्याय
> मनुष्याय यजमानाय रयिं धनं धत्त । दत्त । हे पितरः यूयं तस्य यजमानस्य पुत्रेभ्यो वस्वो वसु धनं प्र यच्छत । ते तादृशा यूयमिहास्मिन्नस्मदीये कर्मण्यर्जं धनं दधात । निधत्त ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अरुणीनां (*aruṇīnāṃ*): of the shining flames, or of the deities; in their proximity, on the altar, seated, O Fathers, bestow wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)) on the mortal, the sacrificer, who has given the oblation (दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)). O Fathers, give wealth to that sacrificer's sons. Such as you are, establish vigour, that is wealth (ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)), here in this rite of ours.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—O Fathers
- अरुणीनां (*aruṇīnāṃ*)—of the attractive flames
- उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—in the proximity
- आसीनासः (*āsīnāsaḥ*)—you who are seated
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the one who has offered the oblation
- मर्त्याय (*martyāya*)—to the sacrificer
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- धत्त (*dhatta*)—give
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that sacrificer
- पुत्रेभ्यः (*putrebhyaḥ*)—to the sons
- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—wealth
- प्र यच्छत (*pra yacchata*)—give
- ते (*te*)—you, the renowned
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrificial rite of ours
- ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)—wealth
- दधात (*dadhāta*)—establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Fathers, you who sit in the proximity of the attractive flames, give wealth to the sacrificer who has offered the oblation. Provide wealth for that sacrificer's son. You, the renowned, establish wealth in this sacrificial rite of ours.

### Printed p. 500

##### English translation
Seated in the proximity of the radiant (flames of the altar), bestow riches on the mortal donor (of the oblation); give wealth, Pitris, to his sons ; you are present, grant us vigour.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये नः॒ पूर्वे॑ पि॒तरः॑ सो॒म्यासो॑ऽनूहि॒रे सो॑मपी॒थं  ॑
> वसि॑ष्ठाः ।  
> तेभि॑र्य॒मः सं॑ररा॒णो ह॒वींष्यु॒शन्नु॒शद्भिः॑ प्रतिका॒मम॑त्तु ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । नः । पूर्वे । पितरः । सोम्यासः। अनुऊहिरे । सोमपीथं । वसिष्ठाः ।  
> तेभिः । यमः । संरराणः । हवींषि । उशन् । उशत्भिः । प्रतिकामं । अत्तु ॥८॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोम्यासः सोमसंपादिनो वसिष्ठा वस्त्रतमाः कृताच्छादना धनवत्तमा
> ना नोऽस्माकं ये पूर्वे पितरः सोमपीथं सोमपानमनूहिरे आनुपूर्व्यण
> देवेभ्यश्च पितृभ्यश्च प्राप्नुवंतः । दत्तवंत इत्यर्थः । उशन् पितृभिः सह संभोगं
> कामयमानो यमः पितृपतिरुशद्भिर्यमेन सह संभोगं कामयमानस्तेभिस्तैरस्यदीयैः पितृभिः सह रराणो रममाणो हवींष्यस्माभिर्दत्तानि प्रतिकामं
> कामं कामं प्रत्यत्तु । यानि यानि हवींषि कामयते तानि तानि भक्षयत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सोम्यासः (*somyāsaḥ*): procurers of Soma; वसिष्ठाः (*vasiṣṭhāḥ*): best clothed, who have given clothing, richest. Those of our former Fathers who have obtained the Soma-drinking (सोमपीथं (*somapīthaṃ*)) in due order for the gods and for the Fathers (अनूहिरे (*anūhire*)), that is, who have given it. उशन् (*uśan*): Yama, lord of the Fathers, desiring communion with the Fathers; and (उशद्भिः (*uśadbhiḥ*)) the Fathers desiring communion with Yama. Yama, rejoicing (रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*)) with those Fathers of ours, let him eat (अत्तु (*attu*)) the oblations given by us, according to his desire (प्रतिकामं (*pratikāmaṃ*)): whichever oblations he desires, let him consume each of them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नः (*naḥ*)—our (their) सोम्यासः (*somyāsaḥ*)—those who offered Soma according to rule
- वसिष्ठाः (*vasiṣṭhāḥ*)—most excellent
- पूर्वे (*pūrve*)—ancestors
- ये पितरः (*ye pitaraḥ*)—which Fathers
- सोमपीथं (*somapīthaṃ*)—Soma-drinking
- अनूहिरे (*anūhire*)—caused to be performed for the gods
- तेभिः (*tebhiḥ*)—such
- उशद्भिः (*uśadbhiḥ*)—(desiring connection with Yama) with the Fathers
- रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*)—he who takes delight

#### Ṛk 8 (continued)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- *naḥ*—our (your)
- *somyāsaḥ*—those who offered the Soma according to rule
- *vasiṣṭhāḥ*—the most excellent
- *pūrve*—the ancestors
- ये पितरो (*ye pitaro*)—which Pitṛs
- *somapīthaṃ*—the drinking of Soma
- *anūhire*—caused the gods to partake
- *tebhiḥ*—with such
- *uśadbhiḥ*—Pitṛs who desire (connection with Yama)
- *rarāṇaḥ*—he who rejoices
- उशन् (*uśan*)—he who desires our oblations
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—Yama
- हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*)—the oblations offered by us
- प्रतिकामं (*pratikāmaṃ*)—as he wishes
- अत्तु (*attu*)—let him accept

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let Yama, who rejoices in the company of those Pitṛs, and who desires our oblations, accept as he wishes the oblations offered by us, together with those Pitṛs who offered their Soma according to rule, who are most excellent and are our ancestors, who caused the gods to partake of the Soma-drinking, and who desire connection with Yama.

##### English translation
May yama, being propitiated, desirous (of the offering), partake at pleasure of the oblations along with those our ancient progenitors the Saumyas, the possessors of great wealth, who also desire it, and who conve-yed the Soma beverage (to the gods and to the Pitris) in order.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये ता॑तृ॒षुर्दे॑व॒त्रा जेह॑माना होत्रा॒विदः॒ स्तोम॑तष्टासो अ॒र्कैः ।  
> आग्ने॑ याहि सुवि॒दत्रे॑भिर॒र्वाज् स॒त्यैः क॒वैः पि॒तृभि॑र्घर्म॒सद्भिः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । ततृषुः । देवत्रा । जेहमानाः । होत्राविदः । स्तोमतष्टासः । अर्क्यैः ।  
> आ । अग्ने । याहि । सुविदत्रेभिः । अर्वाज् । सत्यैः । कव्यैः । पितृभिः । घर्मसत्भिः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महापितृयज्ञेऽग्नेः कव्यवाहनस्य ये तातृषुरित्येषा प्रथमानुवाक्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । ये तातृषुर्देवत्रा जेहमानास्त्वदग्ने काव्या त्वन्मनीषाः । आ. २.१९ ।
> इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, for Agni Kavyavāhana, this Ṛk ये तातृषुः (*ye tātṛṣuḥ*) is the first anuvākyā. It is prescribed in the sūtra: ये तातृषुर्देवत्रा जेहमानास्त्वदग्ने काव्या त्वन्मनीषाः (*ye tātṛṣurdevatrā jehamānāstvadagne kāvyā tvanmanīṣāḥ*) (Ā. 2.19).

### Printed p. 502

> देवत्रा देवाइच्छीहमानाः क्रमेण गच्छंतः । क्रमेण देवत्वं प्राप्ता
> इत्यर्थः । हॊत्राविदो यज्ञान्सम्यक्कर्तुं वेदितारोऽर्कैरर्चनीयैः स्तोत्रैः
> स्तोमतष्टासः स्तोमानां च सम्यक्कर्तारो ये पितरस्तातृषुः तृष्यंति हे अग्ने
> त्वं तैः पितृभिरर्वाजिस्मदभिमुख आ याहि । आगच्छ । कीदृशैः । सुविदत्रेभिः सुविदत्रैः
> सत्यैरविसंवादिभिः कव्यैः । कव्यं नाम पितृदेवत्यं हविः । तत्संबंधिभिः । यद्वा ।
> कव्यैः कविभिर्मेधाविभिः ॥ स्वार्थिको यत् ॥ घर्मसद्धिर्यज्ञसादिभिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

देवत्रा (*devatrā*): going in due order, wishing for the gods; that is, having attained godhood in due order. होत्राविदः (*hotrāvidaḥ*): those who know how to perform sacrifices properly. अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*): with praise-songs worthy of worship. स्तोमतष्टासः (*stomataṣṭāsaḥ*): those who duly fashion the stomas. The Pitṛs who thus thirst (तातृषुः (*tātṛṣuḥ*))—O Agni, come toward us with those Pitṛs. Of what kind are they? सुविदत्रेभिः (*suvidatrebhiḥ*) (सुविदत्रैः (*suvidatraiḥ*)), true (not contradicting one another), कव्यैः (*kavyaiḥ*): kavya is the oblation that has the Pitṛs as its deity, so, connected with it; or else कव्यैः (*kavyaiḥ*) means kavis, the wise (the affix yat is used without change of sense). घर्मसद्भिः (*gharmasadbhiḥ*): those who sit at the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- देवत्रा (*devatrā*)—godhood
- जेहमानाः (*jehamānāḥ*)—those who have attained it in due order
- होत्राविदः (*hotrāvidaḥ*)—those who know the order of the sacrifice
- अर्कॆः (*arkèḥ*)—with praises
- स्तोमतष्टासः (*stomataṣṭāsaḥ*)—those who refine the stomas
- ये (*ye*)—which Pitṛs
- ततृषुः (*tatṛṣuḥ*)—who desire connection with the gods; such
- घर्मसद्भिः (*gharmasadbhiḥ*)—performers of the sacrifice
- सुविदत्रेभिः (*suvidatrebhiḥ*)—those of excellent knowledge
- सत्यैः (*satyaiḥ*)—of truthful nature
- कव्यैः (*kavyaiḥ*)—the wise
- पितृभिः (*pitṛbhiḥ*)—with the Pitṛs
- अर्वाज् (*arvāj*)—facing us
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—graciously come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, graciously come, facing us, with those Pitṛs who have attained godhood in due order, who know the order of the sacrifice, and who refine the stomas with praises, such Pitṛs as desire connection with the gods—performers of the sacrifice, of excellent knowledge, of truthful nature, and wise.

##### English translation
Come, Agni, to our presence with the Pitris, who are possessed of knowledge, who having attained a seat amongst the gods, thirst (for the Soma), skilled in sacrifices, reciters of praises with hymns, truth-speaking, seers, frequenters of sacrifices.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, in the homa made to Agni Kavyavāhana, this Ṛk ये तातृषुः (*ye tātṛṣuḥ*) is to be recited as the first anuvākyā mantra. This is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra: ये तातृषुर्देवत्रा जेहमानास्त्वदग्ने काव्या त्वन्मनीषाः (*ye tātṛṣurdevatrā jehamānāstvadagne kāvyā tvanmanīṣāḥ*) (Ā. 2-19).

### Printed p. 503

सुविदत्रेभिः (*suvidatrebhiḥ*)—for this word Yāska has given the explanation: सुविदत्रः कल्याणविद्यः आग्नेयाहि सुविदत्रेभिरर्वाज् इत्यपि निगमो भवति (*suvidatraḥ kalyāṇavidyaḥ āgneyāhi suvidatrebhirarvāj ityapi nigamo bhavati*). सुविदत्रः (*suvidatraḥ*) means a benevolent mind or a generous mind, generosity. The Vedic passage quoted above is itself the example in this matter.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये स॒त्यासो॑ हवि॒रदो॑ हवि॒ष्पा इंद्रे॑ण दे॒वैः स॒रथं॒  ॑
> दधानाः ।  
> आग्ने॑ याहि स॒हस्रं॑ देववं॒दैः परैः॒ पूर्वैः॑ पि॒तृभि॑र्घर्म॒सद्भिः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । सत्यासः । हविःs अदः । हविःऽपाः । इंद्रेण । देवैः । सरथं । दधानाः ।  
> आ । अग्ने । याहि । सहस्रं । देववंदैः । परैः । पूर्वैः । पितृभिः । घर्मसत्भिः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सत्यासः सत्या ये पितरो हविरदो भक्षणयोग्यस्य हविषोत्तारो भक्षयितारो हविष्पाः पानयोग्यस्य हविषः पातार इंद्रेण देवैः सरथं समानमेकं
> तुल्यं वा रथं दधानाः ॥ लडर्थे शानच् ॥ गमनाय सदा धारयंति हे अग्ने तैः
> पितृभिः सहा याहि । आगच्छ । कीदृशः । सहस्रं । तृतीयार्थे प्रथमा । सहस्रेण ।
> बहुभिरित्यर्थः । देववंद्यर्देवसंबंधिभिः स्तोत्रैर्युक्तः । परैः परकालीनैः
> पूर्वैः पूर्वकालीनैर्घर्मसद्धिर्यज्ञसादिभिर्महावीरसादिभिरादित्यसादिभिर्वा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सत्यासः (*satyāsaḥ*): the true Pitṛs; हविरदः (*haviradaḥ*): eaters of the oblation fit for eating; हविष्पाः (*haviṣpāḥ*): drinkers of the oblation fit for drinking; इंद्रेण देवैः सरथं (*iṃdreṇa devaiḥ sarathaṃ*): holding always, for going, a chariot common to them, one or equal, with Indra and the gods. O Agni, come with those Pitṛs. Of what kind? सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*) stands in the first case for the third: with a thousand, that is, with many; देववंदैः (*devavaṃdaiḥ*): accompanied by praises connected with the gods; परैः (*paraiḥ*): those of later time; पूर्वैः (*pūrvaiḥ*): those of earlier time; घर्मसद्भिः (*gharmasadbhiḥ*): sitters at the sacrifice, sitters at the Mahāvīra, or sitters at the Āditya (vessel).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- सत्यासः (*satyāsaḥ*)—of truthful nature
- ये (*ye*)—which Pitṛs
- हविरदः (*haviradaḥ*)—who are eaters of the oblation
- हविष्पाः (*haviṣpāḥ*)—who are drinkers of the oblations such as Soma
- इंद्रेण (*iṃdreṇa*)—with Indra and others
- देवैः (*devaiḥ*)—with the gods
- सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)—equality
- दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)—who have attained; such
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—thousands in number
- देववंद्यॆ (*devavaṃdyè*)—those united with the gods
- परैः (*paraiḥ*)—those belonging to later time
- पूर्वैः (*pūrvaiḥ*)—those belonging to former time
- घर्मगद्भिः (*gharmagadbhiḥ*)—performers of the sacrifice
- पितृभिः (*pitṛbhiḥ*)—with the Pitṛs
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—graciously come

### Printed p. 504

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, graciously come with those Pitṛs, of truthful nature, who are eaters of the oblation, drinkers of oblations such as Soma, and who have attained equality with Indra and the other gods—thousands in number, united with the gods, belonging to later and earlier time, performers of the sacrifice.

##### English translation
Come, Agni, with thousands of Pitris, of both past and future (time), frequenters of sacrifices, eulogists of the gods ; those who are true, who feed on oblations, and drink oblations, possessing equality with Indra and the gods.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्नि॑ष्वात्ताः पितर॒ एह ग॑च्छत॒ सदः॑सदः सदत सुप्रणीतयः ।  
> अ॒त्ता ह॒वींषि॒ प्रय॑तानि ब॒र्हिष्यथा॑ र॒यिं सर्व॑वीरं दधातन ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निस्वात्ताः । पितरः । आ । इह । गच्छत । सदःसदः । सदत । सुप्रनीतयः ।  
> अत्त । हवींषि । प्रयतानि । बर्हिषि । अथ । रयिं । सर्ववीरं । दधातन ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महापितृयज्ञे पितरोऽग्निष्वात्ता इत्यस्याग्निष्वात्ताः पितर इत्येषा प्रथमानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । अग्निष्वात्ताः पितर एह गच्छत ये चेह पितरो ये च नेह ।
> अ-२-१९ । इति ॥
> अग्निष्टात्ता अग्निना स्वादिता एतन्नामका पितरः यूयमिहास्मिन्पितृकर्मण्या
> गच्छत । आगत्य च हे सुप्रणीतयोऽभिपूजितप्रणयनाः यूयं सदः सदस्तत्तत्स्थानं
> सदत । सीदत । तत्र तत्र स्थाने यथेष्टमुपविशतेत्यर्थः । उपविश्य च बर्हिष्यासादितानि
> प्रयतानि स्रुचि हवींष्यत्त । भक्षयत । अथानंतरं सर्ववीरु सर्वैर्विरैः पुत्रपौत्रैरुपेतं रयिं धनं वधातन । अस्मभ्यं दत्त ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, for the Pitṛs, this Ṛk अग्निष्वात्ताः पितर (*agniṣvāttāḥ pitara*) is the first anuvākyā. It is prescribed in the sūtra: अग्निष्वात्ताः पितर एह गच्छत ये चेह पितरो ये च नेह (*agniṣvāttāḥ pitara eha gacchata ye ceha pitaro ye ca neha*) (A-2-19).**NOTE**
अग्निष्टात्ता (*agniṣṭāttā*): the Pitṛs of this name, "savoured by Agni". You come here, to this rite for the Pitṛs. Having come, O सुप्रणीतयः (*supraṇītayaḥ*), you whose guidance is honoured, sit in each place (सदः सदः (*sadaḥ sadaḥ*)), that is, take your seats as you wish in each place. Having sat, eat the oblations that are set in the ladle, placed on the sacred grass. Then grant us wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)) accompanied by all heroes, that is, by sons and grandsons.

### Printed p. 505

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निष्वात्ताः (*agniṣvāttāḥ*)—those called Agniṣvātta
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—O Pitṛs
- इह (*iha*)—to this our sacrificial rite
- आ गच्छत (*ā gacchata*)—come
- सुप्रणीतयः (*supraṇītayaḥ*)—you who are excellent guides
- सदः सदः (*sadaḥ sadaḥ*)—in the several places
- सदत (*sadata*)—sit down
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—on the seats of darbha grass
- प्रयतानि (*prayatāni*)—that are placed
- हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*)—the oblations
- अत्त (*atta*)—eat
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- सर्ववीरं (*sarvavīraṃ*)—accompanied by sons, grandsons and so on
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- दधातन (*dadhātana*)—give to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pitṛs called Agniṣvātta, come to this our sacrificial rite. You who are excellent guides, sit down in the several places. Eat the pure oblations placed on the seats of darbha grass. Afterwards give us wealth accompanied by sons, grandsons and so on.

##### English translation
Agnishwatta Pitris, come to this solemnity; sit down, directors in the right way, in your appropriate places: eat the oblations spread on the sacred grass and grant us riches and male posterity.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, in the homa made for the Pitṛs called पितरोऽग्निष्वात्वाः (*pitaro 'gniṣvātvāḥ*), this Ṛk अग्निष्टात्ताः पितरः (*agniṣṭāttāḥ pitaraḥ*) is to be recited as the first anuvākyā mantra. This is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra: अग्निष्वात्ताः पितर एह गच्छत ये चेह पितरो ये च नेह (*agniṣvāttāḥ pitara eha gacchata ye ceha pitaro ye ca neha*) (Ā. 2-19).

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वम॑ग्न ईळि॒तो जा॑तवे॒दोऽवा॑ड्ड॒व्यानि॑ सुर॒भीणि॑ कृ॒त्वी ।  
> प्रादाः॑ पि॒तृभ्यः॑ स्व॒धया॒ ते अ॑क्षन्न॒द्धि त्वं दे॑व॒ प्रय॑ता  ॒॑
> हवींषि ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । अग्ने । ईळितः । जातवेदः । अवाट् । हव्यानि । सुरभीणि । कृत्वी :  
> प्र । अदाः । पितृभ्यः । स्वधया । ते । अक्सन् । अद्धि । त्वं । देव । प्रयता । हवींषि ॥

### Printed p. 506

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महापितृयज्ञे वषट्कारक्रियायां त्वमग्न ईळित इत्येषास्विष्टकृतो याज्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । योऽग्निः कव्यवाहनस्त्वमग्न ईळितो जातवेद इति संयाज्ये । आ-२-१९ ।
> इति ॥
> हे जातवेदः । जातं सर्वं जगद्वेत्तीति जातवेदाः । तथाविध हे अग्ने
> ईळितोऽस्माभिः स्तुतस्त्वं हव्यान्यस्मदीयानि हवींषि सुरभीणि सुगंधीनि कृत्वि
> कृत्वावाट् । वहनं कृतवानसि । कृत्वा च पितृभ्यः प्रादाः । ते च पितरः स्वधया स्वधा.
> कारेण दत्तं हविरक्षन् । आदंतु । हे देव त्वमपि प्रयता । प्रयत्नसंपादितानि
> हवींष्यद्धि । भक्षय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, in the act of the vaṣaṭkāra, this Ṛk त्वमग्न ईळितः (*tvamagna īḷitaḥ*) is the yājyā of the Sviṣṭakṛt. It is prescribed in the sūtra: योऽग्निः कव्यवाहनस्त्वमग्न ईळितो जातवेद इति संयाज्ये (*yo 'gniḥ kavyavāhanastvamagna īḷito jātaveda iti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-19).
O जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*): he who knows all that is born, the whole world, is Jātavedas. O Agni, thus described, praised by us, you have made our oblations fragrant and have borne them; having done so you gave them to the Pitṛs. And let those Pitṛs eat the oblation given with the svadhā-call. O god, you too eat the oblations prepared by effort.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—in the form of Jātavedas
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ईळितः (*īḷitaḥ*)—praised by us
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- हव्यानि (*havyāni*)—our oblations
- सुरभीणि (*surabhīṇi*)—fragrant
- कृत्वी (*kṛtvī*)—having made
- अवाट् (*avāṭ*)—you have borne
- पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*)—to the Pitṛs
- प्रादाः (*prādāḥ*)—you have offered
- ते (*te*)—those Pitṛs
- स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—the oblations offered with svadhā
- अक्षन् (*akṣan*)—let them eat
- देव (*deva*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you also
- प्रयता (*prayatā*)—well procured
- हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*)—the oblations
- अद्धि (*addhi*)—eat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, in the form of Jātavedas, praised by us, you have made our oblations fragrant and borne them for the Pitṛs. You have offered them to them. Let those Pitṛs eat the oblations offered with svadhā. O Agni, you too eat the oblations well procured.

##### English translation
Agni Jatavedas, who are glorified (by us), having made our oblations fragrant, you have borne them off, and have presented them to the Pitris: may they partake of them with the Swadha; and you also, divine Agni feed upon the offered oblations.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, in the homa of the vaṣaṭkāra act, this Ṛk त्वमग्न ईळितः (*tvamagna īḷitaḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra of the Sviṣṭakṛt homa. This is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra: योऽग्निः कव्यवाहनस्त्वमग्न ईळितो जातवेद इति संयाज्ये (*yo 'gniḥ kavyavāhanastvamagna īḷito jātaveda iti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-19).

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये चे॒ह पि॒तरो॒ ये च॒ नेह यांश्च॑ वि॒द्म या उ॑ च॒ न  ॒॑
> प्र॑वि॒द्म ।  
> त्वं वे॑त्थ॒ यति॒ ते जा॑तवेदः स्व॒धाभि॑र्य॒ज्ञं सुकृ॑तं जुषस्व ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । च । इह । पितरः । ये । च । न । इह । यान् । च । विद्म । यान् । ऊं इति ।  
> च । न । प्रविद्म ।  
> त्वं । वेत्थ । यति । ते । जात्यवेदः । स्वधाभिः । यज्ञं । सुकृतं । जुषस्व । १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महापितृयज्ञे ये चेहेति द्वितीयानुवाक्या । सूत्रमुक्तं ॥
> ये च पितर इहास्मत्समीपे वर्तंते ये चेह न संति । याश्च पित्थन्विद्म
> संनिकृष्टत्वाज्ञानीमः या उ च नापि च न प्रविद्द विप्रकृष्टत्वाद्वयं न विजानीमः ।
> यति ते यावंतस्ते भवंति तान्सर्वान्यथोक्तान् हे जातवेद उत्पन्नसर्ववस्तु।-
> विषयज्ञानाग्ने त्वं वेत्थ । जानासि । स्वधाभिर्हविर्लक्षणैरन्नॆः सुकृतं साधु कृतं
> यज्ञं जुषस्व । प्रीत्या गृहाण ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, the Ṛk beginning ये चेह (*ye ceha*) is the second anuvākyā; the sūtra has been stated. The Pitṛs who are here near us, and those who are not here; those whom we know because they are close, and those whom we do not know well, because they are remote — Agni, *Jātavedas* (one who has knowledge of every object that has arisen), you know how many of them there are, all of them as described. Accept lovingly the well-made sacrifice with the svadhās, that is, with food in the form of oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, in the form of Jātavedas
- ये च पितरः (*ye ca pitaraḥ*)—those Pitṛs who
- इह (*iha*)—are near us
- ये च (*ye ca*)—and those who
- इह (*iha*)—near us
- न (*na*)—are not
- यांश्च (*yāṃśca*)—and those Pitṛs whom
- विद्म (*vidma*)—we know
- या उ च (*yā u ca*)—and whom
- न प्रविद्म (*na pravidma*)—we do not know well, those also
- यति ते (*yati te*)—their full number also
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- वेत्थ (*vettha*)—know
- स्वधाभिः (*svadhābhiḥ*)—with oblations in the form of svadhā
- सुकृतं (*sukṛtaṃ*)—well-prepared
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—sacrifice
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—partake of

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, in the form of Jātavedas, you know those Pitṛs who are near us, those who are not near us, those Pitṛs whom we know, those whom we do not know well, and their full number. Partake of the well-prepared sacrifice with oblations in the form of svadhā.

### Printed p. 508

##### English translation
You know, Jatavedas, those Pitris, how many they may be, who are not in this world, those who are not in this world, those whom we know, and those whom we do not fully know : enjoy this pious sacrifice offered together with Swadhas.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That in the Mahāpitṛyajña this Ṛk beginning ये चेह (*ye ceha*) is to be recited as the second anuvākyā mantra, as stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, has already been explained earlier.

> पूर्वोक्त एव यागे ये अग्निदग्धा इत्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च । ये
> अग्निदग्धा ये अनग्निदग्धा इमं यम प्रस्तरमा हि सीदेति द्वे । आ-२-१९ । इति ॥
> ये पितरोऽग्निदग्धा अग्निना भस्मीकृताः । स्मशानं प्राप्ता इत्यर्थः । ये च
> पितरोऽनग्निदग्धाः स्मशानकर्म न प्राप्ता मध्ये दिवो द्युलोकस्य मध्ये स्वधया
> हविर्लक्षणेनान्नेन मादयंते तृप्यंति हे अग्ने स्वराट् स्वकर्मोऽपभोगेन दीप्यमानस्तेभिस्तैः पितृभिः सहितः सन्नसुनीतिं प्राणानां विषयेषु नेतारमस्मत्पित्रंतरा-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the same sacrifice as stated before, the Ṛk ये अग्निदग्धा (*ye agnidagdhā*) is the yājyā. It is also given in the sūtra: ये अग्निदग्धा ये अनग्निदग्धा इमं यम प्रस्तरमा हि सीदेति द्वे (*ye agnidagdhā ye anagnidagdhā imaṃ yama prastaramā hi sīdeti dve*) (Ā. 2-19). The Pitṛs who are "agnidagdha" are those burnt to ashes by fire, that is, who have reached the cremation ground; those who are "anagnidagdha" have not undergone the cremation rite. They are gratified in the middle of heaven (the middle of the world of heaven) with svadhā, food in the form of oblations. O Agni, "स्वराट् (*svarāṭ*)", shining by the enjoyment of your own works, being united with those Pitṛs, make fit and adapt, according to your wish, this body of the deity — which is *asunīti*, the leader of the vital breaths among the objects of sense, another self of our Pitṛs

> त्मानमेतां तन्वमेतद्देवताशरीरं यथावशं यथाकामं कल्पयस्व समर्थयस्व ।
> ग्रासयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continued) — that is, cause them to partake of the offering.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) ये (*ye*)—those Pitṛs who
- अग्निदग्धाः (*agnidagdhāḥ*)—have been burnt by fire
- ये (*ye*)—and those who
- अनग्नि दग्धाः (*anagni dagdhāḥ*)—have not been burnt by fire
- मध्यॆ दिवः (*madhyè divaḥ*)—are in the middle of the world of heaven
- स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—may all of them, with the oblation in the form of svadhā
- मादयंते (*mādayaṃte*)—attain satisfaction
- तेभिः (*tebhiḥ*)—united with them
- स्वराट् (*svarāṭ*)—you who are self-luminous
- असुनीतिं (*asunītiṃ*)—in the form of the Pitṛs' vital breath (containing it)
- एतां तन्वं (*etāṃ tanvaṃ*)—this body of the deity
- यथावशं (*yathāvaśaṃ*)—according to your will
- कल्पयस्व (*kalpayasva*)—fashion

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, may those Pitṛs who have been burnt by fire, and those who have not been burnt by fire, who are in the middle of the world of heaven, all attain satisfaction with the oblation in the form of svadhā. United with them, you, the self-luminous, fashion according to your will this body of the deity, which contains the vital breath of the Pitṛs.

##### English translation
May those who are Agnidagdhas, and those who are not, be satisfied with Swadha in the midst of heaven; and you, supreme Lord, associated with them, construct at your pleasure that body that is endowed with breath.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That in the sacrifice called Mahāpitṛyajña, mentioned before, this Ṛk ये अग्निदग्धाः (*ye agnidagdhāḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra ये अग्निदग्धा ये अनग्निदग्धा इमं यम प्रस्तरमा हि सीदेति द्वे (*ye agnidagdhā ye anagnidagdhā imaṃ yama prastaramā hi sīdeti dve*) (A. 2-19).**NOTE**
Agnidagdhāḥ, anagnidagdhāḥ: Those whose dead bodies, when their rites are performed after death, are burnt in fire and consecrated with the prescribed mantras are called "agnidagdha Pitṛs", Pitṛs burnt by fire. Those who have died without anyone to perform the fire-rite, or by drowning in water and similar causes, or by other kinds of untimely death, so that the fire-rite could not be performed, and who have gone to the world of the Pitṛs by their own good deeds alone, and are there, are called "anagnidagdha Pitṛs", Pitṛs not burnt by fire.

### Printed p. 510
## Sūkta 16 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
In this sūkta and in the next are mantras relating to the Pitṛ deities and used in the actions performed in the later (funerary) rite. We have explained the subject of the Pitṛ deities at length in the earlier sūktas. Even so, it is necessary to describe briefly the nature of heaven and hell as found in the Ṛgveda and the other Vedas.

Heaven: The abode where the Pitṛs and Yama dwell is in the middle of the sky, the seat of imperishable radiance (10-15-14); in the highest heaven (12-14-8); in the third heaven; in the deepest regions of the sky (9-113-7 to 9). Likewise in the Atharvaveda: a world extremely high (Ath. Saṃ. 11-4-11)**NOTE** and full of masses of radiance (4.34-2); the end of the sky (Ath. Saṃ. 18-2.47); the third आकार (*ākāra*)**NOTE** and the third heaven (Ath. Saṃ. 18-2-48) — these are said to be the places of the Pitṛ-worlds and of Yama. In the Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā (Mai. Saṃ. 1-10-18; 2.3.9) the world of the Pitṛs is the third world. The world of the Pitṛs is the highest region of the sun's orb (9.113-9). The Pitṛs have gone together with Sūra (the sun), or protect Sūra (10-107-2; 10-154-5), or have joined the sun's rays (1-109.7; compare Śa. Brā. 1-9-3-10), and Sūra shines for them alone (5-125-6). They are connected with the foot of Viṣṇu (10-15-3), and the righteous rejoice in that dear abode, in the third step of Viṣṇu (1-154.5). As Viṣṇu took three strides to the region where the gods rejoice, so Sūra, following Uṣas, goes to the place where good men offer oblations.

The radiances of the good men going to the world of heaven are the stars (Tai. Saṃ. 5-4-1-3; Śa. Brā. 6-5-4-8), and the seven ancient ṛṣis were raised to the circle of the stars (Tai. Ā. 1-11-1-2).

In the Ṛgveda a tree is mentioned, near which Yama sits with the gods and drinks (10-135-1); in the Atharvaveda (Ath. Saṃ. 5.4.3) it is said to be a fig tree.

Mention of life in the next world is found especially and abundantly in the ninth and tenth maṇḍalas, and in general in the first. For those who practise hard austerity, heaven is the fruit of their austerity, and the same fruit is for those who die in battle (10-154-2 to 5). But above all these, heaven is the fruit for those who offer oblations generously (10-154-3; 1-125.5; 10-107-2). The fruits obtained by such performers of sacrifices are described very fully in the Atharvaveda.

### Printed p. 511
The dead enjoy in heaven a very delightful life (10-14-8; 10-15-14; 10-16-2, 5); here all desires are fulfilled (9-113.9, 11); the life is among the gods (10-14-14), and in particular in the presence of Yama and Varuṇa (10-14-7). There is no old age (10-27-21). Possessing beautiful bodies, they become dear and beloved to the gods (10-14-8; 10-16-5; 10-56-1). There they see father, mother, children and others (Ath. Saṃ. 6-120-3), and are reunited with wife, sons and others (Ath. Saṃ. 12-3-17). In that life there is not the least fault or defect, nor any bodily suffering (10-14-8; Ath. Saṃ. 6-120.3). Diseases all remain on earth; there are no defects such as crooked or lame hands and feet (Ath. Saṃ. 3-28-5); it is said in the Atharvaveda and the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa that in that world they have complete bodies.

The dead are happy and rejoice in heaven (मदंति (*madaṃti*), मादयंते (*mādayaṃte*), 10-14-10, 12-15-14, etc.). The bliss of life in heaven is given very fully in 9-113-7 to 11. There the light is constant, water flows swiftly, and the stream is not obstructed (compare Tai. Brā. 3-12-2.9). There is food in the form of svadhā (the food offered to the Pitṛs) and satisfaction; there are joy, delight, fulfilment of desires and all such things. What is said vaguely as delight and joy is explained further on as sensual pleasure (compare Tai. Brā. 2-4-6-6; Śa. Brā. 2-4-4-4; Śa. Brā. 10.4.4.4). In the Atharvaveda it is said that sensual pleasure is obtained as much as one wishes (Ath. Saṃ. 4-34-2). A hundredfold more pleasure than the greatest pleasure enjoyed on earth is enjoyed there (Śa. Brā. 14-7-1-32, 33). In that world of the meritorious, the sound of the flute and song are heard (10-135-7); for them Soma juice, ghee and honey flow (Ath. Saṃ. 4-34-5-6; Śa. Brā. 11-5-6-4). Clear cows of various colours, granting desires, are always ready (कामदुघाः (*kāmadughāḥ*), Ath. Saṃ. 4-34-8). There is no distinction between poor and rich, great and small (Ath. Saṃ. 3-29-3). This heavenly bliss described in the Saṃhitās and Brāhmaṇas is said in the Upaniṣads to be impermanent and not the best, and that only to those who know the principle of immortality come oneness with Brahman and the eternal bliss of knowledge of That. Therefore the idea is that those who have done good deeds spend time after death in the world of heaven, absorbed in pleasure, like idlers.

### Printed p. 512
Heaven is more splendid than this world and full of sensual pleasure. It is the world of the doers of good deeds (10-16-4); here those who know ritual action pass the time in joy. They enjoy the fruit of the oblations they made and the gifts they gave; and the more they gave to the Ṛtvijs and others, the more their happiness increases (10.154-3). Those who performed sacrificial rites in the prescribed manner attain oneness not only with the worlds of Āditya and Agni, but with the worlds of Vāyu, Indra, Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, Prajāpati and Brahmā (Śa. Brā. 2-6-4-8, 11-4-4-21, 11-6-2-3, 3, Tai. Brā. 3-10-11-6). It is said (Tai. Brā. 3-10-9-11) that a ṛṣi, by the power of his knowledge, took the form of a golden swan, went to the world of heaven, and attained oneness with Sūra. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā there is the view that, if certain rites are performed, a man can obtain heaven with this very physical body (Tai. Brā. 6-6-9-2).**NOTE**
Those who have studied the Veda in the prescribed manner can become free of the fear of birth and death and attain equality with Brahman (Śa. Brā. 10-5-6-9). As a result of knowing some secret matter, a man is born again (Śa. Brā. 1-5-3-14). In these one can see the beginnings of the doctrines of the fruit of sin and of the attainment of another body. In the Upaniṣads such as the Chāndogya, Bṛhadāraṇyaka and Kaṭha, and in the sūtras, these are fully set forth. In the Kaṭha Upaniṣad is the story of Naciketas, whose main part is the dialogue of Naciketas and Yama. Yama taught Naciketas that those not qualified for heaven and liberation become again subject to death, caught in the wheel of saṃsāra, and are born on earth as embodied beings or as inert matter; that he who has the power of self-control can reach the world of Viṣṇu; and that for those unable to attain liberation there is hell.

Hell
Since the good attain the fruit of heaven and so on in the next world, there must be a separate place for the most sinful, even if punishments are not prescribed for them. In the Atharvaveda and the Kaṭha Upaniṣad it is clearly said that such persons experience in hell the fruit of their sinful deeds. As the counterpart to the world of heaven (Ath. Saṃ. 12-4-36) there is the world of hell (the nether world) where female piśācas and the like dwell (Ath. Saṃ. 2-14-3; 5-19-3); in this very world the murderer suffers punishment (Vā. Saṃ. 30-5). This world is described as darkness (तमस्सु (*tamassu*)) in the lowest region (Ath. Saṃ. 8-8-24; etc.), darkness enveloped in gloom (Ath. Saṃ. 5-30-11), blind darkness (अंधंतमस्सु (*aṃdhaṃtamassu*), Ath. Saṃ. 18-3-3), and so on. The sufferings of hell are described in Ath. Saṃ. 5-19 and still more fully in Śa. Brā. 11.6-1. The same Brāhmaṇa says: after the death of everyone he is born again;

### Printed p. 513

…they weigh his deeds in the balance, and according to his good and evil deeds experiences happiness and sorrow (compare Śa. Brā. 11-2-7-33; 12-9-1-1). Yet the Ṛgveda too is not without a basis for the existence of such a place of suffering. (This is *gabhīraṃ padam*:) "This deep place has been created for the most sinful, the speakers of untruth and the untruthful" (4-5-5). Indra and Soma are entreated to hurl the sinful into the nether world, into bottomless darkness, so that not one of them rises up again (7-104-3). Let the rākṣasī too, who roams like an owl so that no one sees her, fall into the darkness (7-104-12). Let the hater and the robber fall beneath the three earths (7-104-11). These sentences tell only that there is, beneath the earth, a region covered in darkness. The happiness of the world of the earth is the chief aim; happiness and sorrow after death are not so important. In the Brāhmaṇas it is said that those who did good deeds and those who did evil deeds are born again in another world and experience the fruits of their respective deeds (Śa. Brā. 6-2-2-27; 10-6-3-1); but the length of time of this reward or punishment is not stated. There is also a belief that those who do not rightly know the procedure of the sacrificial rites and do not perform them depart from the world of the earth to another world before the time fixed for them (Śa. Brā. 11-2-7-33).

It may be said that the Vedas give no basis for the belief that after death each person undergoes a judgement, as good or bad, according to his own deeds. The one or two sentences quoted above are not clear. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (Tai. Ā. 6-5-13) it is said that Yama separates those who walk the good path from those who walk the bad path; it is not said that he is the supreme authority for making this decision.

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मैनमिति चतुर्दशर्चं षोडशं सूक्तं । यमपुत्रस्य दमनस्यार्षं ।
> आदितो दश त्रिष्टुभः ततश्चतस्रोऽनुष्टुभः । अग्निर्देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> मैनं दमन आग्नेयं चतुरनुष्टुबंतमिति ॥ दीक्षितमरण आद्याः षडृचः शंसनीयाः ।
> सूत्रिशं च । मैनमग्ने वि दहो माभि शोच इति षट् पूषा त्वेतश्वावयतु प्र
> विद्वान् । आ. ६-१०- । इति ॥ दह्यमानस्य प्रेतस्कोपस्थानेऽप्येताः शंसनीयाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the sixteenth sūkta, "मैनं (*mainaṃ*)", of fourteen Ṛks. Its seer is Damana, son of Yama. The first ten Ṛks are in triṣṭubh, the following four in anuṣṭubh; the deity is Agni. He quotes the Anukramaṇī: मैनं दमन आग्नेयं चतुरनुष्टुबंतमिति (*mainaṃ damana āgneyaṃ caturanuṣṭubaṃtamiti*). When one who has undergone the dīkṣā dies (dīkṣitamaraṇa), the first six Ṛks are to be recited (śaṃsanīya), and the Sūtra (Ā. 6-10) says: मैनमग्ने वि दहो माभि शोच इति षट् (*mainamagne vi daho mābhi śoca iti ṣaṭ*) and so on. These six are also to be recited when the body of the dead man is being burnt, at the Agni-upasthāna.

##### Anuvāda (Kannada)

This sūkta "Mainam" is the sixteenth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has fourteen Ṛks. Its seer is Damana, son of Yama. 

### Printed p. 514

The first ten Ṛks of this sūkta are in the triṣṭubh metre; the next four are in the anuṣṭubh metre; Agni is the deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: Mainam, Damana, Āgneya, with four anuṣṭubh at the end. If the sacrificer who is performing a sacrifice has taken the sacrificial consecration and dies before the sacrifice is completed, then the first six Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited; this is explained by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, "Mainamagne vidaho mābhi śoca iti ṣaṭ pūṣā śvetaś cāvayatu pra vidvān" (Ā. 6-10). In the funeral rite, while the dead body is being burnt, these six Ṛks are recited and Agni is to be approached (upasthāna).

Sūkta 16
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 16.
Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 6; Varga 20, 21, 22.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 14.
Ṛṣi: Damana Yāmāyana.
Devatā: Agni.
Metre: 1-10 triṣṭubh; 11-14 anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मैन॑मग्ने॒ वि द॑हो॒ माभि शो॑चो॒ मास्य॒ त्वचं॑ चिक्षिपो॒ मा  ॑
> शरीरं ।  
> य॒दा शृ॒तं कृ॒णवो॑ जातवे॒दोऽथे॑मेनं॒ प्र हि॑णुतात्पि॒तृभ्यः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । एनं । अग्ने । वि । दहः । मा । अभि । शोचः । मा । अस्य । त्वचं । चिक्षिपः ।  
> मा । शरीरं ।  
> यदा । शृतं । कृणवः । जातवेदः । अथ । ईं । एनं । प्र । हिणुतात् । पितृभ्यः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने एनं प्रेतं मा वि दहः । विशेषेण दग्धं भस्मीभूतं मा कुरु ।
> माभि शोचः । अभितः शोकेन संतापेन युक्तं मा कुरु । अस्य त्वचं मा चिक्षिपः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, do not burn this dead man utterly (vi dahaḥ): do not make him wholly burnt to ashes. Do not afflict him (mā abhi śocaḥ): do not make him joined with grief, with scorching, on all sides. Do not scatter (mā cikṣipaḥ) his skin: do not make it flung here and there; and do not scatter the body either."

### Printed p. 515

> इतस्ततो विक्षिस्तं मा कुरु । शरीरमपि विक्षिप्तं मा कुरु । हे जातवेदोऽग्ने
> यदा त्वं शृतं पक्वं सुदग्धं कृणवः करिष्यसि अथ तदानीमीमेनं प्रेतं पितृभ्यः
> प्र हिणुतात् । पितृसमीपे प्रेरय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Jātavedas Agni, when you make him cooked (śṛtam), that is, well burnt, then send (pra hiṇutāt) this dead man to the Pitṛs: dispatch him to the Pitṛs' presence."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this dead man
- मा वि दहः (*mā vi dahaḥ*)—do not burn completely
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this dead man
- त्वचं (*tvacaṃ*)—the skin
- मा चिक्षिपः (*mā cikṣipaḥ*)—do not scatter
- शरीरं (*śarīraṃ*)—the body also
- मा (*mā*)—do not scatter
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni
- यदा (*yadā*)—when
- शृतं (*śṛtaṃ*)—so as to be cooked
- कृणवः (*kṛṇavaḥ*)—you make
- अथ (*atha*)—immediately then
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this dead man
- पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*)—to the Pitṛs
- प्रहिणुतात् (*prahiṇutāt*)—send away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, do not burn this dead man completely. Do not torment him greatly either. Do not scatter either the skin or the body of this dead man. O Agni, when you have made it cooked, immediately send it to the world of the Pitṛs.

##### English translation
Agni, consume him not entirely ; afflict him not ; scatter not (here and there) his skin nor his body ; when Jatavedas, you have rendered him mature, then send him to the Pitris

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It is said that the particle (indeclinable) आ (*ā*) also has the sense of combination ("and"), and in support of this the very sentence of this Ṛk, देवेभ्यश्च पितृभ्य आ (*devebhyaśca pitṛbhya ā*), is given as an example. The word आ (*ā*) in this sentence has the meaning "and" (च (*ca*)).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शृ॒तं य॒दा कर॑सि जातवे॒दोऽथे॑मेनं॒ परि॑ दत्तात्पि॒तृभ्यः॑ ।  
> य॒दा गच्छा॒त्यसु॑नीतिमे॒तामथा॑ दे॒वानां॑ वश॒नीर्भ॑वाति ॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कृतं । यदा । करसि । जातवेदः । अथ । ईं । एनं । परि । दत्तात् । पितृभ्यः ।  
> यदा । गच्छति । आसुनीतिं । एतां । अथ । देवानां । वश्यनीः । भवाति ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 516

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जातवेदः यदा प्रेतशरीरं शृतं पक्वं करसि करिष्यसि अथें तदानीमेवैनं प्रेतं पितृभ्यः परि दत्तात् । प्रयच्छ । यदायं प्रेत एतामग्निना
> कृतामसुनीतिं प्राणस्य नयनं प्राणप्रेरणं गच्छाति प्राप्नोति अथ तदानीमेव
> देवानां वशनीर्दॆवानां वशं प्रापितो भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Jātavedas, when you make (karasi, for 'will make') the dead man's body cooked, then at that very time give him over (pari dattāt) to the Pitṛs: hand him over. When this dead man reaches this asunīti made by Agni, the leading (nayana) of the breath, the impelling of the breath, then at that very time he is brought under the control of the gods (devānāṃ vaśanīḥ)."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni
- यदा (*yadā*)—when
- शृतं करसि (*śṛtaṃ karasi*)—you make this body cooked
- अथ ईं (*atha īṃ*)—immediately then
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this (this dead man)
- पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*)—into the control of the Pitṛs
- परि दत्तात् (*pari dattāt*)—send away
- यदा (*yadā*)—when
- एतां असुनीतिं (*etāṃ asunītiṃ*)—this bodiless state of a Pitṛ **NOTE**
- गच्छाति (*gacchāti*)—he reaches
- अध (*adha*)—immediately then
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—to the gods
- वशनीः (*vaśanīḥ*)—subject
- भवाति (*bhavāti*)—becomes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, when you make this dead man cooked, then send him to the presence of the Pitṛs. As soon as he attains the bodiless state of a Pitṛ, he becomes subject to the gods.

##### English translation
When you have rendered him mature, then give him up, Jatavedas, to the Pitris; when he proceeds to that world of spirits, then he becomes subject to the will of the gods.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सूर्यं॒ चक्षु॑र्गच्छतु॒ वात॑मा॒त्मा द्यां च॑ गच्छ पृथि॒वीं च॒  ॑
> धर्मणा ।  
> अ॒पो वा॑ गच्छ॒ यदि॒ तत्र॑ ते हि॒तमोष॑धीषु॒ प्रति॑ तिष्ठा॒  ॑
> शरीरैः ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 517

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सूर्यं । चक्षुः । गच्चतु । वातं । आत्मा । द्यां । च । गच्छ । पृथिवीं । च । धर्मणा ।  
> अपः । वा । गच्छ । यदि । तत्र । ते । हितं । ओषधीषु । प्रति । तिष्ठ । शरीरैः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे प्रेत ते त्वदीयं चक्षुरिंद्रियं सूर्यं गच्छतु । प्राप्नोतु । आत्मा
> प्राणो वातं वाह्यं वायुं गच्छतु ! अपि च त्वमपि धर्मणा सुकृतेन तत्पलं
> भोक्तुं द्यां च । अत्र चशब्दो विकल्पार्थे । द्युलोकं वा पृथिवीं च पृथिवीं
> वा गच्छ । प्राप्नुहि । अपो वांतरिक्षलोकं गच्छ । प्राप्नुहि । तत्रांतरिक्षे हितं
> स्थापितं ते तव कर्मफलमोषधीषु शरीरैः शरीरावयवै प्रति तिष्ठ ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O dead man, let your eye, the organ of sight, go to the sun: let it reach it. Let your self (ātmā), the breath, go to the wind (vāta), the external air. Further, you also, by dharma, by your meritorious deed, to enjoy its fruit, go to heaven (dyām) and to the earth; here the word च (*ca*) has the sense of option: go to the heaven-world or reach the earth. Or go to the waters (apaḥ), the world of the atmosphere: reach it. There, in the atmosphere, whatever is placed (hitam) as the fruit of your deed, abide (prati tiṣṭha) in the plants (oṣadhīṣu) with your limbs (śarīraiḥ), the parts of the body."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—(O dead man) your organ of sight
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—to the sun **NOTE**
- गच्छतु (*gacchatu*)—let it go and join
- अत्मा (*atmā*)—your breath
- वातं (*vātaṃ*)—let it join the wind
- धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*)—according to your deed
- द्यां च (*dyāṃ ca*)—whether to the heaven-world
- पृथिवीं च (*pṛthivīṃ ca*)—or to the earth-world
- गच्छ (*gaccha*)—go and join
- यदि (*yadi*)—if
- तत्र (*tatra*)—there
- ते (*te*)—to you
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—it is favourable
- अपो वा (*apo vā*)—or to the world of the atmosphere
- गच्छ (*gaccha*)—go and join
- शरीरैः (*śarīraiḥ*)—with the parts of your body
- ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*)—in the plants
- प्रति तिष्ठ (*prati tiṣṭha*)—be established

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O dead man, let your organ of sight go to the sun and join it. Let your breath join the wind. According to your deed, let it go and join either the heaven-world or the earth-world. If it is favourable to you, be established in the atmosphere; let the parts of your body be established in the plants.

##### English translation
Let the eye repair to the sun; the breath to the wind; go you to the heaven or to the earth, according to your merit; or go to the waters if it suits you (to be) there, or abide with your members in the plants.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒जो भा॒गस्तप॑सा॒ तं त॑पस्व॒ तं ते॑ शो॒चिस्त॑पतु॒ तं ते॑ अ॒र्चिः।  
> यास्ते॑ शि॒वास्त॒न्वो॑ जातवेद॒स्टाभि॑र्वहैनं सु॒कृता॑मु लो॒कं॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> “जः । भागः । तपसा । तः तपस्त्युं ते शोचॆः । तपतु । तं । शे ' अर्चः ।  
> याः । ते । शिवा । तन्न । जात्रवेदः । ताभिः । वह । एनं । सुकृतां । ऊं इति ।  
> लोकं ॥ ४

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अजो जननरहितः शरीरेंद्रियादिभागव्यतिरिक्तोऽंतरपुरुषलक्षणो यो
> भागोऽस्ति हे अग्ने ते त्वदीयेन तपसा तापनेन तं तादृशं भागं तपस्व . तप्तं
> कुरु । कथा ते तव शोचिः शोकहेतुज्वालाविशेषस्तं भागं तपतु । संस्करोतु ।
> अपि च ते तवार्चिर्भासको ज्वालाविशेषस्तं भागं तपतु : संस्करोतु । तपःशोचि.
> रचीशब्दानां संतापतारतम्येन भेदः । हे जातवेदः ते तव यास्तन्वो मूर्तयः
> शिवा सुखहेतवो न तु तापप्रदाः ताभिरेनं तनूभिः प्रेतं सुकृतां शोभनकर्मकारिणां लोकं स्थानं वह । प्रापय । उशब्दः पूरणः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"The portion (bhāga) that is unborn (ajaḥ), without birth, distinct from the parts such as body and organs, of the nature of the inner person: O Agni, with your heat (tapasā), your scorching, heat that portion (tapasva). Let your śociḥ, a special flame that is a cause of burning grief, heat it, that is, purify it (saṃskarotu). And let your arciḥ, a shining special flame, heat it, purify it. The words tapas, śociḥ and arciḥ differ by degrees of heat. O Jātavedas, those bodies (tanvaḥ), forms, of yours that are auspicious (śivā), causes of happiness and not givers of heat: with those bodies carry (vaha) this dead man to the world, the place, of those who did good deeds (sukṛtām). The word उ (*u*) is a filler."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अजः (*ajaḥ*)—that which is not born
- भागः (*bhāgaḥ*)—whatever portion there is
- तं (*taṃ*)—that portion
- तपसा (*tapasā*)—with your flame
- तपस्व (*tapasva*)—burn
- ते (*te*)—your
- शोचिः (*śociḥ*)—special flame
- तं (*taṃ*)—that portion
- तपतु (*tapatu*)—let it purify
- ते (*te*)—your
- अर्चिः (*arciḥ*)—the shining flame let it purify
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni
- याः तन्वः (*yāḥ tanvaḥ*)—whichever parts of your body
- शिवाः (*śivāḥ*)—are auspicious
- ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*)—with them
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this dead man
- सुकृतां (*sukṛtāṃ*)—of the doers of good deeds
- लोकं (*lokaṃ*)—to the place
- वह (*vaha*)—carry

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, burn with your flame whatever portion there is that is not born. Let your śociḥ and arciḥ (special flames) purify that portion. O Agni, with whichever parts of your body are auspicious, carry this dead man to the place of those who did good deeds.

##### English translation
The unborn portion ; burn that, Agni, with your heat ; let your flame, your splendour, consume it ; with those glorious members which you have given him, Jatavedas, bear him to the world (of the virtuous).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अव॑ सृज॒ पुन॑रग्ने पि॒तृभ्यो॒ यस्त॒ आहु॑त॒श्चर॑ति स्व॒धाभिः॑ ।  
> आयु॒र्वसा॑न॒ उप॑ वेतु॒ शेषः॒ सं ग॑च्चतां त॒न्वा॑ जातवेदः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अव । सृज । पुनः । अग्ने । पितृभ्यः । यः । ते । आहुतः । चरति । स्वधाभिः ।  
> आयुः । वसानः । उप । वेतु । शेषः । सं । गच्छतां । तन्वा । जातवेदः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने य प्रेतः पुमानाहुतश्चितौ मंत्रेण समर्पितः सन् स्वधाभिः स्वधाकारसमर्पितैरुदकादिभिः सह चरति तं प्रेतं पितृभ्यः पितृप्राप्त्यर्थं पुनरव सृज ।
> भूयः प्रेरय । अयं प्रेत आयुर्जीवनं वसान आच्छादयन् । आयुषा युक्त
> इत्यर्थः । शेषः शिष्यमाणमस्थिलक्षणं यजनीयं शरीरमुप वेतु । उपगच्छतु ।
> हे जातवेदः तव प्रसादात्तन्वा शरीरेण सं गच्छतां । संगतो भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, the dead man who, offered (āhutaḥ) on the pyre with a mantra, moves with the svadhās, the water and the like offered with the svadhā-cry: send that dead man again (punaḥ ava sṛja) to the Pitṛs, in order to reach the Pitṛs; impel him once more. Let this dead man, clothing himself in life (āyuḥ vasānaḥ), that is, joined with life, let the remainder (śeṣaḥ), the remaining bony body fit for sacrifice, come up (upa vetu), approach. O Jātavedas, by your grace let him be united (saṃ gacchatām) with a body (tanvā), become joined."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, who knows all that is born
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the dead man who
- ते (*te*)—your
- आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*)—offered on the pyre
- स्वधाभिः (*svadhābhiḥ*)—with water and the like in the form of svadhā
- चरति (*carati*)—moves; that dead man
- पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*)—to the presence of the Pitṛs
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- अव सृज (*ava sṛja*)—send away
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—the life of the world of the Pitṛs
- वसानः (*vasānaḥ*)—having attained
- शेषः (*śeṣaḥ*)—the portion remaining after burning
- उपवेतु (*upavetu*)—let it approach the world of the Pitṛs
- तन्ना (*tannā*)—with that body
- सं गच्छतां (*saṃ gacchatāṃ*)—let it be united

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who are Jātavedas, send again to the presence of the Pitṛs the dead man who, offered on your pyre, moves with the water and the like in the form of svadhā. Let him attain the life of the world of the Pitṛs, and, as the remainder of what was burnt, approach the world of the Pitṛs. Let him be united with that body.

##### English translation
Dismiss again to the Pitris, Agni him who, offered on you, comes with the Swadhas : putting on (celestial) life, let the remains (of bodily life) depart : let him, Jatavedas, be associated with a body.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> युत्ते॑ कृ॒ष्णः श॑कु॒न आ॑तु॒तोद॑ पिपी॒लः स॒र्प उ॒त वा॒ श्वाप॑दः।  
> अ॒ग्निष्टद्वि॒श्वाद॑ग॒दं कृ॑णोतु॒ सोम॑श्च॒ यो ब्रा॑ह्म॒णा आ॑वि॒वेश॑ ॥ ६ ॥

> अग्निः । तत् । विश्वअत् । अगदं । कृणोतु । सोमः । च । यः । ब्राह्मणान् । आविवेश ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मृतशरीर ते तव संबंधि यदंगं कृष्णः शकुनः काकाख्य आतुतोद ।
> आजीषदर्थे । ईषत्तुन्नवान् ! तथा पिपीलः पिपीलिका वा सर्पो वोत वापि वा
> श्वापदश्च शृगालादिः । एतेषामन्यतमो यदि तुन्नवानित्यर्थः। विश्वात् सर्वस्यात्ताग्निस्तत्तादृशमंगमगदं कृणोतु । दोषरहितं करोतु । संस्करोत्वित्यर्थः । तथा
> सोमश्च देवतारूप ओषधिरूपो वा संस्करोतु । यः सोमो ब्राह्मणानृश्विगादीनाविवेश प्रविष्टवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O dead body, whatever limb of yours a black bird, the crow, has pecked a little, or an ant, or a snake, or else a beast of prey such as a jackal—if any one of these has pecked it—let Agni, the consumer of everything, make that limb free of defect, that is, purify it. Likewise let Soma, whether as deity or as the plant, purify it, that Soma who has entered the Brahmins, the officiating priests and others. आतुतोद (*ātutoda*) is explained as having the sense of "a little" (आजीषदर्थे (*ājīṣadarthe*)), that is, "has pecked slightly".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—your
- यत् (*yat*)—which limb
- कृष्णः (*kṛṣṇaḥ*)—black-coloured
- शकुनः (*śakunaḥ*)—a crow
- आतुतोद (*ātutoda*)—harms; or
- पिपीलः (*pipīlaḥ*)—an ant
- सर्पः (*sarpaḥ*)—a snake
- उत वा (*uta vā*)—or
- श्वापदः (*śvāpadaḥ*)—dogs and jackals harm
- तं (*taṃ*)—that whole part
- विश्वात् (*viśvāt*)—burning everything
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- अगदं (*agadaṃ*)—free of defect
- कृणोतु (*kṛṇotu*)—let him make
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Soma
- ब्राह्मणान् (*brāhmaṇān*)—priests and others
- आविवेश (*āviveśa*)—has entered
- सोमश्च (*somaśca*)—let that Soma also purify this part

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O dead body, whatever limb of yours a black crow, an ant, or dogs and jackals bite and harm, let Agni, who burns everything, make that part free of defect. Let Soma, who enters the bodies of the priests and others, also purify that part.
