##### English translation
Should the black crow, the ant, the snake, the wild beast, harm (a limb) of you, may Agni the all-devourer, and the Soma that has pervaded, the Brahmans, make it whole.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्नेर्वर्म॒ परि॒ गोभि॑र्व्ययस्व॒ सं प्रोर्णु॑स्व॒ जीव॑सा॒ ॑ 
> मेदसा च ।  
> नेत्वा॑ धृ॒ष्णुर्हर॑सा॒ जर्हर्॑षाणो द॒धृग्वि॑ध॒क्षन्॑र्यं॒खया॑ते ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्नेः । वर्म । परि । गोभिः । व्ययस्व । सं । प्र । ऊर्णुष्व । पीवसा । मेदसा ।  
> च ।  
> न । इत् । त्वा । धृष्णुः । हरसा । जर्हर्षाणः । दधृक् । विधक्षन् । परिअंखियाते ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनुस्तरण्या वसया प्रेतस्य मुखमग्नेर्वर्मेत्यनया प्रोर्णुयात् ।
> सूत्रितं च । अनुस्तरण्या वसामुत्पिद्य शिरोमुखं प्रच्छादयेदग्नेर्वर्म परि
> गोभिर्व्ययस्वेति । आ. गृ. सू. ४-३-१९ । इति ॥
> हे प्रेत अग्नेः स्वभूतं वर्म ज्वालालक्षणं कवचं गोभिरनुस्तरणीगोचर्मणा परि व्ययस्व । परितः संवृणु । किंच पीवसा स्कूलेन मेदसा मांसेन
> सम्यक् प्रोर्णुष्ट्व । आच्छादय । एवं कृते सति हरसा तेजसा धैष्णुर्धर्षणशीलो
> जह्र्हषाणोऽत्यर्थं हृष्यन् दधृग्धृष्टः प्रगल्भः ॥ ऋत्विगित्यादिना दधृक्‌शब्दो
> निपापिततः ॥ विधक्ष्यन् विविधं भस्मीकरिष्यन् एवंभूतोऽग्निस्ता त्वां नेत्परंखयाते !
> नैव सर्वतो विस्तारयति ॥ अखेर्गत्यर्थाल्लेट्यडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk, with the anustaraṇī cow's fat (vasā), one should cover the face of the dead. It is stated in the sūtra: अनुस्तरण्या वसामुत्पिद्य शिरोमुखं प्रच्छादयेदग्नेर्वर्म परि गोभिर्व्ययस्वेति । (*anustaraṇyā vasāmutpidya śiromukhaṃ pracchādayedagnervarma pari gobhirvyayasveti |*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-3-19). O dead one, wrap Agni's own armour, in the form of flames, around you with the cow-hide of the anustaraṇī. Further, cover yourself well with thick fat and flesh. When this is done, Agni, bold with heat, delighting greatly, daring, intending to burn in many ways, will not spread all round you. The word दधृक् (*dadhṛk*) is established by the rule beginning *ṛtvig*; the root अख (*akha*) has the sense of motion, and the augment aṭ comes in the leṭ.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—Agni's
- वर्म (*varma*)—the armour in the form of flames
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with the cow-hide
- परिव्ययस्व (*parivyayasva*)—cause to be covered
- पीवसा (*pīvasā*)—thick
- मेदसा च (*medasā ca*)—and with fat

### Printed p. 522
- सं प्रोर्णुष्ट (*saṃ prorṇuṣṭa*)—cause to be wrapped round (then)
- हरसा (*harasā*)—with brilliance
- धृष्णुः (*dhṛṣṇuḥ*)—the assailant of enemies
- जर्हर्षाणः (*jarharṣāṇaḥ*)—greatly delighted
- दधृक् (*dadhṛk*)—bold
- विधक्ष्यन् (*vidhakṣyan*)—Agni, who will burn in many ways
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- *na it paryaṃkhayāte*—does not surround and harm

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O dead one, cause Agni's armour in the form of flames to be covered with cow-hide. Cause yourself to be surrounded also with thick fat. Then Agni, brilliant, the assailant of enemies, greatly delighted, bold, who burns in many ways, will not surround you and harm you.

##### English translation
Enclose the mail of Agni with the (hide of the) cow ; cover it with the fat and marrow : then will not (Agni), bold, exulting in his fierce heat, proud, embrace you roundabout to consume you (to ashes).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When the funeral rite is performed, while reciting this Ṛk अग्नेर्वर्म (*agnervarma*), the face of the dead body is to be covered with the anustaraṇī. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya sūtra अनुस्तरण्या वसामुत्पिद्य शिरोमुखं प्रच्छादयेदग्नेर्वर्म परि गोभिर्वयस्व (*anustaraṇyā vasāmutpidya śiromukhaṃ pracchādayedagnervarma pari gobhirvayasva*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-3-19).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मम॑ग्ने चम॒सं मा वि जि॑ह्वरः प्रि॒यो दे॒वाना॑मु॒त  ॒॑
> सोम्यानां ।  
> ए॒ष यश्च॑म॒सो दे॑व॒पान॒स्तस्मि॑न्दे॒वा अ॒मृता॑ मादयंते । ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमं । अग्ने । चमसं । मा । वि । जिह्वरः । प्रियः । देवानां । उत । सोम्यानां ।  
> एषः । यः । चमसः । देवपानः । तस्मिन् । देवाः । अमृताः । मादयंते ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 523

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इममग्ने चमसमित्यनया प्रणीताप्रणयनमनुमंत्रयते । सूत्रितं च ।
> इममग्ने चमसं मा वि जिह्वर इति प्रणीताप्रणयनमनुमंत्रयते । आ. गृ.
> ४-३-२४ । इति ॥
> हे अग्ने इमं चमसं प्रणीताप्रणयनं मा वि जिह्वरः । मा विचालीः ।
> यश्चमसो देवानामिंद्रादीनां प्रिय उतापि च सोम्यानां सोमार्हाणां
> पितृणां प्रियः । किंच य एष चमसो देवपानः । देवाः पिबंत्यस्मिन्निति । देवपानस्थानियो भवति तस्मिंश्चमसेऽमृता मरणवर्जिता देवाः पितरश्च मादयंते ।
> हव्यैश्च हृष्टा भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk one addresses the Praṇītā vessel's conveyance. It is stated in the sūtra: इममग्ने चमसं मा वि जिह्वर इति प्रणीताप्रणयनमनुमंत्रयते (*imamagne camasaṃ mā vi jihvara iti praṇītāpraṇayanamanumaṃtrayate*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-3-24). O Agni, do not shake this ladle, the Praṇītā vessel. The ladle is dear to the gods, Indra and the rest, and also dear to the Pitṛs who are worthy of Soma. Further, this ladle is the gods' drinking-vessel (the gods drink in it); in that ladle the deathless gods and the Pitṛs rejoice, and are delighted with the oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- इमं चमसं (*imaṃ camasaṃ*)—this vessel of oblation
- मा वि जिह्वरः (*mā vi jihvaraḥ*)—do not displace (do not cause to move) (this vessel)
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—to the gods
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—dear
- उत (*uta*)—and
- सोम्यानां (*somyānāṃ*)—dear also to the Pitṛs worthy of Soma
- यः एषः चमसः (*yaḥ eṣaḥ camasaḥ*)—this ladle which
- देवपानः (*devapānaḥ*)—is the means of drinking for the gods
- तस्मिन् (*tasmin*)—in that very vessel
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—deathless
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—gods
- मादयंते (*mādayaṃte*)—attain delight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, do not cause this vessel of oblation to move. This vessel is dear to the gods, and dear also to the Pitṛs who are worthy of Soma. In the very ladle that is the gods' means of drinking, the deathless gods attain delight.

##### English translation
Agni, shake not this ladle, for it is dear to the gods, and to the (Pitris) who are worthy of the Soma: this which is the drining ladle of the gods, in this the immortal gods delight.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the after-rite, when the Praṇītā vessel is conveyed, the Ṛk इममग्ने चमसं (*imamagne camasaṃ*) is to be recited. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya sūtra इममग्ने चमसं मा वि जिह्वर इति प्रणीताप्रणयनमनुमंत्रयते (*imamagne camasaṃ mā vi jihvara iti praṇītāpraṇayanamanumaṃtrayate*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-3-24).

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क्र॒व्याद॑म॒ग्निं प्रहि॑णोमि दू॒रं य॒मरा॑ज्ञो गच्छतु रिप्रवा॒हः ।  
> इ॒हैवायमित॑रो जा॒तवे॑दा दे॒वेभ्यो॑ ह॒व्यं व॑हतु प्रजा॒नन् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> क्रव्यअदं । अग्निं । प्र । हिणोमि । दूरः । यमराज्ञः । गच्छतु । रिप्रवाहः ।  
> इह ! एव । अयं । इतरः । जातवेदाः । देवेभ्यः । हव्यं । वहतु । प्रजानन् ॥९॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आहिताग्निमरण एतदादिके द्वे ऋचावौपाससोद्वासने विनियुक्ते । तत्र
> प्रथमायाः पूर्वार्धेन दक्षिणस्यां दिशि चतुष्षथादावौपासनाग्निं निरस्यति । उत्तरेण शांतिकर्मार्थमादत्ते । आ. गृ. सू. ४-६ । क्रव्यादं । क्रव्यमामिषं । तस्यात्तारं
> तीव्रमग्निं दूरं विप्रकृष्टदेशे प्र हिणोमि । प्रगमयामि ॥ हि गत् स्वादिः ॥
> रिप्रवाहः । रिप्रं पापं । तस्य वोढा सोऽग्निर्यमराज्ञो यमो राजा येषां
> तान्यमराजकानन्यप्रदेशान्गच्छतु । प्राप्नोतु । अथ शांतिकर्मार्थमुपासन इतरः
> क्रव्यादादन्नो जातवेदा जातानां वेदिता जातधनो वा प्रजानन् सर्वैर्विज्ञायमानोऽग्निरिहैव देशे देवेभ्यो देवार्थं हव्यं हवनयोग्यं हविर्वहतु ।
> प्रापयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the death of one who keeps the sacred fire, this Ṛk and the next are applied at the dismissal of the Aupāsana fire. Of the first, with the first half he casts the Aupāsana fire out at a crossroads in the southern quarter; with the latter he takes up (another fire) for the rite of propitiation (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-6). क्रव्यादं (*kravyādaṃ*): क्रव्य (*kravya*) is raw flesh; I send far away, to a distant place, the fierce fire that devours it. रिप्रवाहः (*ripravāhaḥ*): रिप्र (*ripra*) is sin; the fire that carries it away is to go to the regions of which Yama is king, that is, to places under Yama's rule. Then, for the propitiation rite, the other fire at the Upāsana, the Jātavedas (knower of what is born, or possessed of wealth that is born), known to all, is to convey here itself, to the gods, the oblation fit for offering. The root हि (*hi*) is of the svādi class, in the sense of going.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- क्रव्यादं (*kravyādaṃ*)—eating kravya (flesh)
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- दूरं (*dūraṃ*)—far
- प्र हिणोमि (*pra hiṇomi*)—I send
- रिप्रवाहः (*ripravāhaḥ*)—Agni, destroyer of sin
- यमराज्ञः (*yamarājñaḥ*)—to the regions under Yama's sovereignty
- गच्छतु (*gacchatu*)—let him go
- इतरः (*itaraḥ*)—the one of another form
- आयंजातवेदाः (*āyaṃjātavedāḥ*)—this Agni in the form of Jātavedas
- प्रजानन् (*prajānan*)—becoming visible to all
- इहैव (*ihaiva*)—staying in this very place
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—to the gods
- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—the oblation
- वहतु (*vahatu*)—let him carry

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I send the flesh-eating Agni far away. Let the Agni who destroys sin go to the regions under Yama's rule. Let the other Agni, of another form, in the form of Jātavedas, visible to all, staying in this very place, carry the oblation to the gods.

### Printed p. 525

##### English translation
I send the flesh-devouring Agni to a distance : let him bearing away sin repair to (the realm of) king Yama ; but let this other Jatavedas who is known (by all) convey the oblation to the gods.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो अ॒ग्निः क्र॒व्यात्प्र॑वि॒वेश॑ वो गृ॒हमि॒मं पश्य॒न्नित॑रं जा॒तवे॑दसं ।  
> तं ह॑रामि पितृय॒ज्ञाय॑ दे॒वंस घ॒र्ममि॑न्वात्पर॒मे स॒धस्थे॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । अग्निं । क्रव्यत् । प्रविवेश । वः । गृहं । इमं । पश्यन् । इतरं । जातवेदसं ।  
> तं । हरामि । पितृयज्ञाय । देवं । सः । घर्मं । इन्वात् । परमे । सधस्थे ॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः क्रव्यादोऽग्निर्देवो युष्माकं गृहिणां गृहं प्रविवेश प्रविष्ट
> वान् तं क्रव्यादं देवं हरामि । गृहाद्बहिर्निष्क्रामयामीत्यर्थः । किमर्थ० ।
> पितृयज्ञाय तदर्थ० । किं कुर्वन् । इममितरं तस्मादन्यं हव्यवाहं जातवेदसं
> पश्यन् पर्यालोचयन् । तथा सति क्रव्यादात्परोऽग्निः परम उत्कृष्टे सधस्थे
> सहस्थाने घर्म० यज्ञमिन्वात् । प्राप्नोतु । पितृभिर्घर्मपैः सहेति शेषः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The flesh-eating Agni, the god, who has entered the house of you householders: that flesh-eating god I carry out, that is, I cause to leave the house. For what purpose? For the Pitṛyajña, for that purpose. Doing what? Looking at this other one, the oblation-bearing Jātavedas, that is, considering him. That being so, let the Agni other than the flesh-eater attain the sacrifice (घर्म (*gharma*)) in the supreme, excellent common abode; the supplement is "together with the Pitṛs who drink the gharma".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- क्रव्यात् यः अग्निः (*kravyāt yaḥ agniḥ*)—the Agni named Kravyāt, who
- वः गृहं (*vaḥ gṛhaṃ*)—your house
- प्रविवेश (*praviveśa*)—has entered
- तं देवं (*taṃ devaṃ*)—that god Agni
- पितृयज्ञाय (*pitṛyajñāya*)—for the worship of the Pitṛs
- इमं इतरं जातवेदसं (*imaṃ itaraṃ jātavedasaṃ*)—this other Agni, in the form of Jātavedas
- पश्यन् (*paśyan*)—looking at
- हरामि (*harāmi*)—I carry out of the house
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni in the form of Jātavedas
- परमे (*parame*)—in the excellent
- सथस्थे (*sathasthe*)—place
- घर्मं (*gharmaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- इन्वात् (*invāt*)—let him pervade

### Printed p. 526

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni called Kravyāt, who has entered your house: while looking at that other Agni, who is Jātavedas, I carry him out of the house for the worship of the Pitṛs. May the Agni who is Jātavedas pervade the sacrifice in the most excellent place.

##### English translation
The fleeh-devouring deity Agni, who has entered your dwelling, I turn him out, for the worship of the Pitris, upon beholding this other (Agni) Jatavedas; let him celebrate the sacrifice (to the Pitris) in the most excellent assembly.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो अ॒ग्निः क॑व्य॒वाह॑नः पि॒त्थान्यक्ष॑दृता॒वृधः॑ ।  
> प्रेदु॑ ह॒व्यानि॑ वोचति दे॒वेभ्य॑श्च पि॒तृभ्य॒ आ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । अग्निः । कव्यवाहनः । पित्थन् । यक्षत् । ऋत्यवृधः ।  
> प्र । इत् । ऊं इति ! हव्यानि । वोचति । देवेभ्यः । च । पितृभ्यः । आ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महापितृयज्ञे वषट्कारक्रियायां यो अग्निः कव्यवाहन इत्येषा स्विष्टकृतो याज्या । सूत्रितं च । यो अग्निः कव्यवाहनस्त्वमग्न ईळितो जातवेद इति
> संयाज्ये । आ. २-१९ । इति ॥
> कव्यवाहनः कव्यस्य हविषो वोढा योऽग्निः पितृनृतावृध ऋतस्य यज्ञस्योदकस्य वा वर्धयित्थन् सत्येन वृद्धान्वा देवान् । एतत्पितृविशेषणं वास्तु । तान्यक्षत्
> यजति । यजेर्लेटि सिबडागमः ॥ सोऽग्निर्हव्यानि हवींषि प्र वोचतु । पितृयज्ञे
> प्रब्रवीतु । युष्मदर्थं मायानीतानीति । इदू पूर्णौ । केभ्यः । देवेभ्यश्च
> पितृभ्यश्च । आकारः समुच्चये ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, in the vaṣaṭkāra rite, the verse यो अग्निः कव्यवाहन (*yo agniḥ kavyavāhana*) is the yājyā of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering. It is stated in the sūtra: यो अग्निः कव्यवाहनस्त्वमग्न ईळितो जातवेद इति संयाज्ये (*yo agniḥ kavyavāhanastvamagna īḷito jātaveda iti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-19).
कव्यवाहनः (*kavyavāhanaḥ*) is the Agni who carries the kavya oblation. He is ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*), the increaser of ṛta, that is, of the sacrifice or of water; or the word qualifies the Pitṛs, or the gods, who are strengthened by truth. He worships (यक्षत् (*yakṣat*)) them; in the Leṭ the augment siṭ is added. May that Agni proclaim the oblations in the Pitṛyajña: "These have been brought for you." इदू (*idū*) are complete words. For whom? For the gods and for the Pitṛs; the ā has the sense of conjunction.

### Printed p. 527

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कव्यवाहनः (*kavyavāhanaḥ*)—the bearer of the oblation called kavya
- यः अग्निः (*yaḥ agniḥ*)—which Agni
- पित्थान् (*pitthān*)—the Pitṛs
- ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—the gods who increase truth
- यक्षत् (*yakṣat*)—he who worships; that Agni
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the gods
- पितृभ्यः च (*pitṛbhyaḥ ca*)—and for the Pitṛs
- हव्यानि (*havyāni*)—the oblations, specified
- प्र वोचति (*pra vocati*)—may he declare them distinctly and make them known

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the Agni who carries the oblation called kavya, and who worships the Pitṛs and the gods who increase truth, offer the oblations assigned to the gods and to the Pitṛs and make known their respective portions.

##### English translation
Let Agni the bearer of the Kavya worship the Pitris, who are magnified by truth, let him declare which are the offerings to the gods, which to the Pitris.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Mahāpitṛyajña, when the Sviṣṭakṛt oblation is made with the vaṣaṭkāra, this Ṛk यो अग्निः कव्यवाहनः (*yo agniḥ kavyavāhanaḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra: यो अग्निः कव्यवाहनस्त्वमग्न ईळितो जातवेदॆ इति संयाज्ये (*yo agniḥ kavyavāhanastvamagna īḷito jātavedè iti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-19).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महापितृयज्ञ उशंतस्त्वेत्येषा सामिधेनी । सूत्र्यते हि । उशंतस्ता नि
> धीमहीत्येतां त्रिरनवानं ताः सामिधेन्यः । आ.२.१९ । इति ।
> हे अग्ने उशंतः कामयमाना वयं त्वा त्वां नि धीमहि । कर्मार्थं
> स्थापितवंतः । उशंतो वयं समिधीमहि । संदीपयामः । त्वमप्युशन् कामयमानो हविरादिकमुशत आगंतुकामान्पित्यनस्मिन्यज्ञ आ वह । हविषेऽस्माभिः
> प्रत्तं हविरत्तवेऽत्तुं ॥ अदेस्तुमर्थे तवेन्प्रत्ययः । क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति
> कर्मणः संप्रदानसंज्ञा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāpitṛyajña the verse उशंतस्त्वा (*uśaṃtastvā*) is a sāmidhenī. It is stated in the sūtra: उशंतस्ता नि धीमहीत्येतां त्रिरनवानं ताः सामिधेन्यः (*uśaṃtastā ni dhīmahītyetāṃ triranavānaṃ tāḥ sāmidhenyaḥ*) (Ā. 2.19).
O Agni, longing, we place you for the rite; longing, we kindle you. You too, longing, bring to this sacrifice the Pitṛs who long to come, to eat (अत्तवे (*attave*)) the oblation offered by us. The affix tavai is used in the sense of the infinitive of अद (*ada*). The object receives the designation sampradāna.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) उशंतः (*uśaṃtaḥ*)—we who desire your worship
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- नि धीमहि (*ni dhīmahi*)—we have established for the rite
- उशंतः (*uśaṃtaḥ*)—we who desire you
- समिधीमहि (*samidhīmahi*)—we have made you blaze
- उशन् (*uśan*)—you who desire our worship
- उशतः (*uśataḥ*)—who desire our oblations
- पितृन् (*pitṛn*)—the Pitṛs
- हविषे (*haviṣe*)—our oblations
- अत्तवे (*attave*)—to eat
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, we who desire your worship have established you for the rite. We who desire you have made you blaze. You who desire our worship, bring the Pitṛs who desire our oblations, to eat our oblations.

##### English translation
Longing we set you down; longing we kindle you ; do you longing bring the longing Pitris to eat of the (sacrificial) viands.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Mahāpitṛyajña this Ṛk उशंतस्त्वा (*uśaṃtastvā*) is to be recited as the sāmidhenī mantra. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra: उशंतस्त्वा नि धीमहीत्येतां त्रिरनवानं ताः सामिधेन्यः (*uśaṃtastvā ni dhīmahītyetāṃ triranavānaṃ tāḥ sāmidhenyaḥ*) (A. 2.19).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, the place which you burned completely at the time of the cremation of the Pitṛs: cool that very place again. Here, in this place, let there grow कियांबु (*kiyāṃbu*), a pond or the like with some measure of water, and let there arise व्यल्कशा (*vyalkaśā*), of many branches, and ripe पाकदूर्वा (*pākadūrvā*), fully ripened durvā grass.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni

- यं (*yaṃ*)—which region
- समदहः (*samadahaḥ*)—you burned at the time of the cremation of the Pitṛs
- तमु (*tamu*)—that region
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again

- अत्र (*atra*)—in this region
- कियांबु (*kiyāṃbu*)—pond-plants and the like that grow in a little water
- रोहतु (*rohatu*)—let grow
- व्यल्कशा (*vyalkaśā*)—having many branches
- पाकदूर्वा (*pākadūrvā*)—the ripe durvā plant (grass blades): let it grow

O Agni, the region which you burned at the time of the cremation of the Pitṛs, make it cool again. In this region let pond-plants and the like that grow in a little water, and durvā plants of many branches, grow abundantly (grass blades).

##### English translation
Cool again, Agni, the spot which you have burned, there let the water-lily grow, and the ripe Durva with its many stalks.

> गमेर्लुजु व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ॥ तत इममग्निं सु सुष्टु हर्षय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the collecting of the bones, one sprinkles the cremation-ground thrice, keeping it to the left, with milk and water by means of a branch of the śamī, reciting शीतिके शीतिकावती (*śītike śītikāvatī*). It is stated in the sūtra: क्षीरोदकेन शमीशाखया त्रिः प्रसव्यं परिव्रजन्प्रोक्षति शीतिके शीतिकावतीति (*kṣīrodakena śamīśākhayā triḥ prasavyaṃ parivrajanprokṣati śītike śītikāvatīti*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-5-3).
O शीतिके (*śītike*), possessed of coolness; O शीतिकावति (*śītikāvati*): शीतिकाः (*śītikāḥ*) are cool herbs, and you possess them. O ह्लादिके (*hlādike*), gladdener; O ह्लादिकावति (*hlādikāvati*), possessed of trees with gladdening fruit. O earth, unite well (सु सं गमः (*su saṃ gamaḥ*)) with मंडूक्या (*maṃḍūkyā*), the female frog dear to rain. The Parasmaipada of *gam* is by vyatyaya. Then gladden this Agni well.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शीतिके (*śītike*)—she who is possessed of coolness
- शीतिकावति (*śītikāvati*)—she who is possessed of cool herbs
- ह्लादिके (*hlādike*)—she who gives joy
- ह्लादिकावति (*hlādikāvati*)—O earth, who is endowed with gladdening trees and the like
- मंडूक्या (*maṃḍūkyā*)—with frogs that grow by rain
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- सं गमः (*saṃ gamaḥ*)—unite
- इमं अग्निं (*imaṃ agniṃ*)—this Agni
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- हर्षय (*harṣaya*)—gladden

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O earth, possessed of coolness, of cool herbs, giver of joy, endowed with gladdening trees and the like: unite abundantly with the frogs that grow by rain (with the female frogs). Gladden this Agni abundantly.

##### English translation
(Oh earth), cool and filled with cool (herbs), gladsome and filled with gladsome (trees), be thronged with female frogs and give joy to this Agni.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the rite of collecting the bones, a subsidiary part of the funeral rites, one sprinkles the cremation-ground where the dead body was burned, thrice, keeping it to the right, with milk and water by means of a branch of the śamī tree, reciting this Ṛk शीतिके शीतिकावति (*śītike śītikāvati*).

### Printed p. 531
This is explained by the Āśvalāyana-gṛhya-sūtra: क्षीरोदकेन शमीशाखया त्रिः प्रसव्यं परिव्रजन् प्रोक्षति शीतिके शीतिकावतीति (*kṣīrodakena śamīśākhayā triḥ prasavyaṃ parivrajan prokṣati śītike śītikāvatīti*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-5-3).

## Sūkta 17 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
Saraṇyū and Vivasvān.
At the beginning of this sūkta, this introduction briefly sets out details such as who Saraṇyū, the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, was; her marriage to Vivasvān; and the birth of Yama and Yamī, Manu and the Aśvins from them. Further, under the respective Ṛks, Yāska's Nirukta relating to this matter is explained as it stands there; and in the last part of the introduction the account of the goddess Saraṇyū is also given as told in the Bṛhaddevatā attributed to Śaunaka.
These mantras (10-17-1-2) which tell of Saraṇyū may be placed together with the mantras known as brahmodya. Mantras belonging to this group of brahmodya occur in many places in the Saṃhitās and Brāhmaṇas, for example (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164; Ath. Saṃ. 9-9, 10; Vā. Saṃ. 23-9 to 12; Tai. Saṃ. 7-4-18; Ai. Brā. 5-25; Śa. Brā. 13. 2. 6. 9 to 17; 5. 2. 11-21 etc.). They differ somewhat from one another in composition. In the present case one must examine what the basis is for the mantra त्वष्टा दुहित्रे (*tvaṣṭā duhitre*) belonging to this group. First, if one examines the composition of the mantra and its purport, they can be observed in many respects.
त्वष्टा दुहित्रे वहतुं कृणोतीतीदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति । यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश । (*tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṃ kṛṇotītīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sameti | yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-1)
Tvaṣṭṛ was arranging the marriage of his daughter, and on that account the whole world (all beings) gathered together. But Yama's mother (Saraṇyū), who had just entered the state of wifehood with Vivasvān, vanished.
अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते । उताश्विनावभरदत्तदासीदजुहादु द्वा मिथुना सरण्यूः ॥ (*apāgūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇāmadadurvivasvate | utāśvināvabharadattadāsīdajuhādu dvā mithunā saraṇyūḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-2)

### Printed p. 532
After Saraṇyū vanished, the gods hid her, the immortal one, so that mortal men should not know, created another woman-form like her, and offered it to Vivasvant. She gave birth to the Aśvin deities. Afterwards Saraṇyū bore two children (Yama and Yamī). So it is stated. In this account there are many elements that show the characteristics of a Brahmodya. In a Brahmodya, however, it is customary that a question and an answer (some problem, and its answer) occur together. For example, to the question पृच्छामि त्वा (*pṛcchāmi tvā*) (1-164-34) the answer इयं वेदिः परो अंतः पृथिव्या (*iyaṃ vediḥ paro aṃtaḥ pṛthivyā*) (1-164.35) comes naturally. If it be objected that there is no question in the present mantra, one may say that here the question too is contained together with an unambiguous answer. There is no doubt that this context is the statement of a problem. To see what the picture of Saraṇyū, the main subject of this problem, is like, one must note the seven epithets describing her here. They are:

1. त्वष्टुः दुहिता (*tvaṣṭuḥ duhitā*)—daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ.
2. यमस्य माता (*yamasya mātā*)—mother of Yama (and of Yamī).
3. विवस्वतः पत्नि (*vivasvataḥ patni*)—wife of Vivasvant.
4. अमृता (*amṛtā*)—without death (without destruction).
5. तस्याः सवर्णा (*tasyāḥ savarṇā*)—one who is her substitute, having her very form.
6. अश्विन्योः माता (*aśvinyoḥ mātā*) (?)—mother of the Aśvin deities (?).
7. अजहादु द्वा मिथुना (*ajahādu dvā mithunā*)—one who abandoned the twin children.

If, in this context, we ask who is the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, who is the mother of Yama, and so on, only one answer comes to all the questions: Saraṇyū. But who this Saraṇyū is, that is a secret principle. Even so, this hidden meaning surely carries an exceedingly great import. For that very reason this situation is mentioned and described at length in the Purāṇas and Itihāsas. Yāska and Śaunaka (in the Bṛhaddevatā) have shown its importance and explained this situation. Explaining the mantra of the Ṛk Saṃhitā quoted above (10-17-2), Yāska has stated as follows:

अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः । कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वतेऽप्यश्विनावभरदत्तदासीदजहाद्वा मिथुनौ सरण्यूर्मध्यमं च माध्यमिकां च वाचमिति नैरुक्ताः । (*apāgūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ | kṛtvī savarṇāmadadurvivasvate 'pyaśvināvabharadattadāsīdajahādvā mithunau saraṇyūrmadhyamaṃ ca mādhyamikāṃ ca vācamiti nairuktāḥ |*) यमं च यमीं चेत्यैतिहासिकाः (*yamaṃ ca yamīṃ cetyaitihāsikāḥ*) तत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते— (*tatretihāsamācakṣate—*)

### Printed p. 533
त्वाष्ट्री सरण्यूर्निवस्वत अदित्याद्यमौ मिथुनौ जनयांचकार । सा सवर्णामन्यां प्रतिनिधायाश्वं रूपं कृत्वा प्रदुद्राव । स विवस्वा नादित्य आश्व- मेव रूपं कृत्वा तामनुग्रत सुखभाव ! ततोऽश्विनौ जज्ञाते सवर्णायां मनुः । तदभिवादिनिन्येऽगर्भवति ॥ (*tvāṣṭrī saraṇyūrnivasvata adityādyamau mithunau janayāṃcakāra | sā savarṇāmanyāṃ pratinidhāyāśvaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtvā pradudrāva | sa vivasvā nāditya āśva- meva rūpaṃ kṛtvā tāmanugrata sukhabhāva ! tato 'śvinau jajñāte savarṇāyāṃ manuḥ | tadabhivādininye 'garbhavati ‖*) (Ni. 12-10)

The gods hid that immortal woman from men so that they should not know. They created another woman like her and offered her to Vivasvant. Saraṇyū gave birth to the Aśvin deities, abandoned those twins on the spot, and went away; and in this connection the meaning of the word यम (*yama*) is also discussed. The Nirukta-authors say that it means (1) Indra of the middle world and (2) the speech of the middle region, while the Aitihāsikas say it means Yama and Yamī; thus two opinions are stated. Saying that there is an itihāsa in this matter, it has also explained it. It is this: Saraṇyū, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ and wife of Vivasvant, who is of the form of Āditya, bore two twin children, Yama and Yamī. Afterwards she placed another woman in that place as her substitute, took the form of a mare and ran away from there. Vivasvant, who is of Āditya form, also took the form of a stallion, followed her and united with her; as a result the Aśvin deities were born. In the woman who had been placed as Saraṇyū's substitute, Manu was born. This, the Nirukta-author explains, is what is stated in the mantra beginning त्वष्टा दुहित्रॆ (*tvaṣṭā duhitrè*). The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā have stated the same matter thus.

अभवन्मिथुनं त्वष्टुः सरण्यूस्त्रिशिराः सह । स वै सरण्यूं प्रायच्छत् स्वयमेव विवस्वते ॥ (*abhavanmithunaṃ tvaṣṭuḥ saraṇyūstriśirāḥ saha | sa vai saraṇyūṃ prāyacchat svayameva vivasvate ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 6. 162)

Tvaṣṭṛ had a daughter, Saraṇyū, and a son named Triśiras. He gave his daughter Saraṇyū in marriage to Vivasvant.

ततः सरण्वां जज्ञाते यमयम्या विवस्वतः । ता चाप्युभौ यमानेव ज्यायांस्ताभ्यां तु नै यमः ॥ (*tataḥ saraṇvāṃ jajñāte yamayamyā vivasvataḥ | tā cāpyubhau yamāneva jyāyāṃstābhyāṃ tu nai yamaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De, 6. 163)

Afterwards two children, Yama and Yamī, were born to Saraṇyū, the wife of Vivasvant. Those two were twins born together; of the two, Yama was the first.

सृष्टाव भर्तुः परोक्षं तु सरण्यूः सदृशीं स्त्रियं । निक्षिप्य मिथुनं तस्यां अश्वा भूत्वापचक्रमे ॥ (*sṛṣṭāva bhartuḥ parokṣaṃ tu saraṇyūḥ sadṛśīṃ striyaṃ | nikṣipya mithunaṃ tasyāṃ aśvā bhūtvāpacakrame ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-1)

### Printed p. 534
When her husband was absent, Saraṇyū created another woman resembling herself, entrusted her twin children to her, took the form of a mare, left that place, and, unknown to Vivasvant, went to another place and became invisible.

अविज्ञानाद्विवस्वांस्तु तस्यामजनयन्मनुं । राजर्षिरभवत्सोऽपि विवस्वानिव तेजसा ॥ (*avijñānādvivasvāṃstu tasyāmajanayanmanuṃ | rājarṣirabhavatso 'pi vivasvāniva tejasā ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7.2)

But Vivasvant, without knowing this, united with that woman who was Saraṇyū's substitute. As a result Manu was born. Manu too, like his father, became radiant, a great royal sage. His fame spread in all the worlds.

स विज्ञाय त्वपक्रांतां सरण्यमश्वरूपिणीं । त्वाष्ट्रीं प्रति जगामाशु वाजी भूत्वा सलक्षणः ॥ (*sa vijñāya tvapakrāṃtāṃ saraṇyamaśvarūpiṇīṃ | tvāṣṭrīṃ prati jagāmāśu vājī bhūtvā salakṣaṇaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-3)

In the end true knowledge came to Vivasvant. When he learned that Saraṇyū had gone away in the form of a mare, he too took the form of a stallion, followed the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ to the place where she had gone, and tried to join her.

सरण्यूश्च विवस्वंतं विदित्वा हयरूपिणं । मैथुनायोपचक्राम तां च तत्रारुरोह सः ॥ (*saraṇyūśca vivasvaṃtaṃ viditvā hayarūpiṇaṃ | maithunāyopacakrāma tāṃ ca tatrāruroha saḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-4)

Saraṇyū, knowing that Vivasvant had followed her in the form of a horse, desired the pleasure of union with him. Then Vivasvant fulfilled her wish.

ततस्तयोस्तु वेगेन शुक्रं तदपतद्भुवि । उपाजिघ्रच्च सा त्वश्वा तच्चुक्रं गर्भकाम्यया ॥ (*tatastayostu vegena śukraṃ tadapatadbhuvi | upājighracca sā tvaśvā taccukraṃ garbhakāmyayā ‖*) (Bṛ पे (*pe*) 7-5)**NOTE**

In the time of their mutual ardour Vivasvant's semen fell to the ground. Then Saraṇyū, with the wish to conceive, smelled it.

आघ्रातमात्राच्चुक्रात्तु कुमारौ संबभूवतुः । नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च यौ स्तुतावश्विनाविति ॥ (*āghrātamātrāccukrāttu kumārau saṃbabhūvatuḥ | nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca yau stutāvaśvināviti ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-6)**NOTE**

As soon as she smelled that semen, conception arose in her, and from it two youths, Nāsatya and Dasra, were born; afterwards they were called by the name Aśvin deities, and their greatness spread through all the worlds.

### Printed p. 535
इतिहासमिमं यास्कः सरण्यदेवति त्वजे ! विवस्वतश्च त्वष्टुश्च त्वष्टेति सह मन्यरे ॥ (*itihāsamimaṃ yāskaḥ saraṇyadevati tvaje ! vivasvataśca tvaṣṭuśca tvaṣṭeti saha manyare ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-7)**NOTE**

Yāska has taken the two mantras composed with Saraṇyū as deity (10-17-1) and (10.17-2) as the context in which the history of these two, Vivasvant and Tvaṣṭṛ, is explained. Yāska's explanation has been given above (Ni 12-10,11).

In the present case it must be examined what the characteristic of a Brahmodya is in the Ṛk Saṃhitā mantra that describes this situation. On the one hand there is the discord arising from the giving of Saraṇyū, a divine woman, in marriage to Vivasvant, a man; on the other, the effort made to set this discord right. Thus the problem that appears in this episode and the effort to resolve it are the chief element. That Vivasvant is one of the Ādityas is well known throughout the Vedic texts. But the doubt naturally arises how an immortal deity can be called a mortal man. That he is a mortal man is plainly stated in the Vedic texts themselves.

That at the time of Saraṇyū's marriage not only the gods but the people of all the worlds came and gathered is told by the sentence इदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति (*idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sameti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-1). प्रायच्छत् स्वयमेव विवस्वते (*prāyacchat svayameva vivasvate*) (Bṛ. De.) says that Tvaṣṭṛ himself gave Saraṇyū to the man named Vivasvant. That, although all the gods had come and assembled at this marriage of the svayaṃvara type, Tvaṣṭṛ of his own accord gave her to Vivasvant (a man) is itself problematic. It is also clearly stated that Saraṇyū too expressed her dissatisfaction with this relation.

That Vivasvant is mortal is the root matter of this problem. This point is stated clearly both in the Bṛhaddevatā and in the Mahābhārata.

ततो विवस्वानादित्योऽजायत, तस्य वा इयं प्रजा यन्मनुष्याः । (*tato vivasvānādityo 'jāyata, tasya vā iyaṃ prajā yanmanuṣyāḥ |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-6-2)

Afterwards Vivasvant, one of the Ādityas, was born. The Taittirīya Saṃhitā supports this by saying that all the people, those of human form, were born from this Vivasvant. Not only this, many other Vedic sentences too make his mortality clear. For example:

सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिरुपप्रृत्पूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजाय्कॆ मृत्यवे त्वत्पुनर्मार्तांडमाभरत् ॥ (*saptabhiḥ putrairaditirupaprṛtpūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāykè mṛtyave tvatpunarmārtāṃḍamābharat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-22.9)

### Printed p. 536
Aditi had eight sons. With seven of them she went, joined the gods, and mingled with her earlier offspring. But the eighth, Mārtāṇḍa, she kept here, for the sake of the stream of saṃsāra in the form of birth, death and so on. So it is said. Who this Mārtāṇḍa is:

अष्टौ ह वै पुत्रा अदितेः । यांस्त्वेतद्देवा आदित्या इत्याचक्षते सप्त हैव तेऽविकृतग्ं हाष्टमं जनयांचकार मार्तांडग्ं संदेघो हैवास यावानेवोर्ध्वस्तानांस्तिर्यज् पुरुषसंमित इत्यु हैत आहुः ॥ (*aṣṭau ha vai putrā aditeḥ | yāṃstvetaddevā ādityā ityācakṣate sapta haiva te 'vikṛtagṃ hāṣṭamaṃ janayāṃcakāra mārtāṃḍagṃ saṃdegho haivāsa yāvānevordhvastānāṃstiryaj puruṣasaṃmita ityu haita āhuḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-1-3-3)

Aditi had eight children. But the sons of Aditi who are called by the name of deities are only seven. To the eighth, Mārtāṇḍa, she did not give a complete form. It was merely a lump of body having a bulk equal to its height. The knowing ones say that it was equal to the measure of a man.

त उ हैत ऊचुः । देवा आदित्या यदस्मानन्वजनिमा तदमुयेव भूद्धंतेमं विकरवामेति तं विचक्रुर्यथायं पुरुषो विकृतस्तस्य यानि माग्‌ंसानि संकृत्य संन्यासुस्ततो हस्ती समभवत्तस्मादुहुर्न हस्तिनं प्रतिगृह्णीयात्परुषाजानो हि हस्तीति यमु ह तद्विचक्रुः स विवस्वानादित्यस्तस्यॆमाः प्रजाः ॥ (*ta u haita ūcuḥ | devā ādityā yadasmānanvajanimā tadamuyeva bhūddhaṃtemaṃ vikaravāmeti taṃ vicakruryathāyaṃ puruṣo vikṛtastasya yāni māgṃsāni saṃkṛtya saṃnyāsustato hastī samabhavattasmāduhurna hastinaṃ pratigṛhṇīyātparuṣājāno hi hastīti yamu ha tadvicakruḥ sa vivasvānādityastasyèmāḥ prajāḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-1-3-4)

Then the seven sons of Aditi, of divine form, together resolved: "This lump must not be wasted. We must give it a form", and they made an existence for it in the form of a man. When the man was being made from that lump, the pieces of flesh cut off at the time of forming the limbs appeared in the form of the elephant. For that very reason it is said that an elephant should not be accepted as a gift. He who was refined into the form of a man is Vivasvant. That Āditya from whom this progeny arose is this Vivasvant. So it is stated. Moreover there are still many other proofs showing Vivasvant's mortality and humanity:

यामथर्वा मनुष्पिता दध्यज् धियमत्नत । तस्मिन् ब्रह्माणि पूर्वथेंद्र उक्त्वा समग्मतार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥ (*yāmatharvā manuṣpitā dadhyaj dhiyamatnata | tasmin brahmāṇi pūrvatheṃdra uktvā samagmatārcannanu svarājyaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ, 1-80-16)

In such places (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-9-4; Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-1 etc.) the Manu who is designated as the father of men, to that same Manu, the human father, Vivasvant is known to be the father.

### Printed p. 537
यथा मनौ विवस्वति सोमं शक्रापिबः सुतं । यथा त्रिते छंद इंद्र जुजोषस्यायौ मादयसे सचा ॥ (*yathā manau vivasvati somaṃ śakrāpibaḥ sutaṃ | yathā trite chaṃda iṃdra jujoṣasyāyau mādayase sacā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-52.1)

ततोऽश्विनौ जज्ञाते । सवर्णायां मनुः । (*tato 'śvinau jajñāte | savarṇāyāṃ manuḥ |*) (Sirutte. 12-10)**NOTE**

मनुर्वैवस्वतो राजेत्याह । तस्य मनुष्या विशस्त इम आसत । (*manurvaivasvato rājetyāha | tasya manuṣyā viśasta ima āsata |*) (Śa. Brā. 13-4-3-3)

In many such places Manu is clearly called the son of Vivasvant. Descriptions such as विवस्वतः सदने (*vivasvataḥ sadane*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-34-7; ) also show Vivasvant to be an excellent host (1-53-1; 3-51-3; 10-12-7 etc.).

Saraṇyū, wedded to such a man, though at first she joined him, must in due course have become aware that her husband did not fully possess divinity. This point is stated clearly in the Harivaṃśa. As follows:

भर्तृरूपेण नातुष्यद्रूपयौवनशालिनी (*bhartṛrūpeṇa nātuṣyadrūpayauvanaśālinī*) (Harivaṃśa. 547)

It is clearly stated that Saraṇyū, endowed with youth and beauty, was not satisfied with her husband's form. That, dissatisfied with such a husband, she turned into the form of a mare is not stated plainly in the Ṛk Saṃhitā; but the sentence "she bore the Aśvin deities" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-17-2)**NOTE** tells this matter.

When Saraṇyū, having taken the form of a mare, joined the gods, her natural kinsmen, they hid her from Vivasvant the man and from his sons Yama and Yamī, who are likewise human in form. Therefore:

अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते । (*apāgūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇāmadadurvivasvate |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-2)

It is plain that they hid her from Vivasvant the man and his sons, created another woman of the same form as hers, and gave her to him. That Manu, born of this Savarṇā, became the brother of Yama is made clear by the sentences of the Nirukta and the Bṛhaddevatā. Besides this, no sentence praising the brotherhood of Manu and Yama is anywhere in the Ṛk Saṃhitā. It is suggested only in the Atharvaveda. As follows:

### Printed p. 538
तस्य (विराजः) यमो राजा वत्स आसीत् । (*tasya (virājaḥ) yamo rājā vatsa āsīt |*) (Ath. Saṃ. 8-10-23, 24) **NOTE**

From this passage, "Yama was the calf-form for that Virāṭ Puruṣa; Manu, the son of Vivasvān, was also the calf-form," the brotherhood of the two is indicated. Further:

मनुर्वैवस्वतो राजा तस्य मनुष्या विश्व.......यमो वैवस्वतो राजा तस्य पितरो विशः ॥ (*manurvaivasvato rājā tasya manuṣyā viśva.......yamo vaivasvato rājā tasya pitaro viśaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 13-3-3-7-5)

Manu, son of Vivasvān, is the lord of all humans, and Yama, son of Vivasvān, is the lord of the whole world of the Pitṛs; thus their brotherhood is indicated. What we need here is evidence showing that Vivasvān is the original ancestor of all humans and that he possessed humanity and mortality. The same point is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā in this way:

ततो विवस्वा नादित्योऽजायत तस्य वा इयं प्रजायन्मनुष्याः (*tato vivasvā nādityo 'jāyata tasya vā iyaṃ prajāyanmanuṣyāḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-6-2)

Besides saying that Vivasvān, who is of the nature of the Āditya, had human subjects, the difference between this Āditya and the other Ādityas has been explained above.

Moreover, in सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते (*savarṇāmadadurvivasvate*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-2), what the word सवर्णा (*savarṇā*) means is not settled either. It gives room for doubt whether सवर्णा (*savarṇā*) means "one having the same colour," because, as the substitute for the vanished Saraṇyū, she resembled her form; or whether सवर्णा (*savarṇā*) is a proper name. Manu is designated by the two epithets सावर्णि (*sāvarṇi*) and सावर्ण्य (*sāvarṇya*). To know the correct sense of these epithets, one must examine the contexts in which these usages occur.

न तमश्नोति कश्चन दिव इव सान्वारभं । सावर्णस्य दक्षिणा वि सिंधुरिव पप्रथे ॥ (*na tamaśnoti kaścana diva iva sānvārabhaṃ | sāvarṇasya dakṣiṇā vi siṃdhuriva paprathe ‖*) (Ya. Saṃ. 10-62-9) **NOTE**

The gift of Manu, who is famed as Sāvarṇya, is surpassing; no one can exceed it. His gift spreads widely, like the flow of a river.

सहस्रदा ग्रामणीर्मा रिषन्मनु: सूर्येणास्य यतमानैतु दक्षिणा । सावणर्देर्देवाः प्र तिरन्त्वायुर्यस्मिन्नश्रांता असनाम वाजं ॥ (*sahasradā grāmaṇīrmā riṣanmanu: sūryeṇāsya yatamānaitu dakṣiṇā | sāvaṇarderdevāḥ pra tirantvāyuryasminnaśrāṃtā asanāma vājaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-62-11)

### Printed p. 539
Let Manu, the giver of thousands of cows and the lord of the community, not be harmed by anyone; let his gift grow widely, like the radiance of the Āditya. Let the gods make the life of this Sāvarṇi grow long. Let us also enjoy the food obtained by his unceasing toil: so it says. In these contexts the Bhāṣya explains Sāvarṇya and Sāvarṇi as the son of the woman called Savarṇā. But no male person named Savarṇa, a father of Manu, is mentioned anywhere. For Manu this must be an epithet connected with the mother's name. It may freely be said that the young woman called Savarṇā who was given to Vivasvān is the mother of this Manu.

Vivasvān, as soon as he learns that Saraṇyū, dissatisfied with his humanity, has vanished, follows her. Knowing that she has taken the form of a mare, he too takes the form of a stallion. Following her in this form and approaching her, he enchants her and she desires union with him. As a result, the birth of the Aśvin deities is made plain. Another important point must be examined here. It is this:

यमस्य माता परुह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश । (*yamasya mātā paruhyamānā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-1)

What the Nirukta author says as the purport of the statement that Yama's mother, the wife of Vivasvān (that is, Saraṇyū), vanished is noteworthy.

रात्रिरादित्यस्यादित्योदयेऽंतर्थीयते (*rātrirādityasyādityodaye 'ṃtarthīyate*) (Ni. 12-11)

He gives the purport that as soon as the Āditya rises, the night disappears. Durgācārya explains this very point further:

यमस्य मध्यमस्य माता देवधर्मेण । अथवा द्युस्थानस्य यैव चाया सा मातेति । रात्रिरादित्यस्य .... .... उषा जाया सा अदित्यस्कोदये अंतर्थीयते ॥ (*yamasya madhyamasya mātā devadharmeṇa | athavā dyusthānasya yaiva cāyā sā māteti | rātrirādityasya .... .... uṣā jāyā sā adityaskodaye aṃtarthīyate ‖*) (Durgācāryavṛtti 12-11)

The wife of the Āditya, lord of the heavenly world, is the sense intended here. This wife of the Āditya is called Uṣas; he says the purport is that as soon as the Āditya rises, the goddess Uṣas becomes invisible. It was stated earlier that one of the Ādityas is famed as Vivasvān. Because Uṣas moves at once on the manifestation of this Āditya, she may also bear the name Saraṇyū. For the Nirukta author, showing the etymology of this word,

### Printed p. 540
सरण्यू सरणि (*saraṇyū saraṇi*) (3. 2-9) **NOTE**

says that the name is due to her moving nature. If this etymology and the explanation of Durgācārya above are taken as the basis, then the purport becomes that Tvaṣṭṛ wished to give this goddess Uṣas to an excellent bridegroom in marriage. No impropriety is seen in stating the purport thus. Contexts that show this point are well known in many places in Vedic passages. For example:

प्रजापतिर्नै सोमाय राज्ञे दुहितरं प्रायच्छत्सूर्यां । (*prajāpatirnai somāya rājñe duhitaraṃ prāyacchatsūryāṃ |*) (Ai. Brā. 4-7) **NOTE**

It says that Prajāpati gave his daughter Sūryā to King Soma in marriage. But there is doubt as to who this daughter is. Although the passage quoted here says Sūryā, in some other places there are differences of meaning. For example:

प्रजापतिर्वै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यध्यायद्दिवमित्यन्य आहुरुषसमित्यन्ने तामृश्यो भूत्वा रोहितं भूतां । (*prajāpatirvai svāṃ duhitaramabhyadhyāyaddivamityanya āhuruṣasamityanne tāmṛśyo bhūtvā rohitaṃ bhūtāṃ |*) (Ḍi. Brā. 3-33) **NOTE**

Prajāpati desired his own daughter. Some say she was the presiding deity of the heavenly world, some say Uṣas. It says that she, having the form of a doe, was followed by Prajāpati in the form of a stag. The Ṛksaṃhitā also tells this very thing:

पिता यत्स्वां दुहितरमधिष्कन् क्षया रेतः संजग्मानो नि षिंचत् । स्वाध्योऽजनयन् ब्रह्म देवा वास्तोष्पतिं व्रतपां निरतक्षन् ॥ (*pitā yatsvāṃ duhitaramadhiṣkan kṣayā retaḥ saṃjagmāno ni ṣiṃcat | svādhyo 'janayan brahma devā vāstoṣpatiṃ vratapāṃ niratakṣan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 11.61-7) **NOTE**

When Prajāpati united with his own daughter, the gods created Brahman; they also created the protector of the sacrifice. Even here, they have explained this daughter as Uṣas or the presiding deity of the heavenly world. It has been shown, on the authority of the Nirukta and the like, that the very person indicated as Uṣas in the contexts quoted here may be the one indicated as Saraṇyū in the present sūkta (10-17). The only peculiarity is that Tvaṣṭṛ (Prajāpati) gave her to another man in marriage.

In sum, it is well known in the Śruti that such descriptions occur in contexts that tell of the union of the female and male powers preceding the creation of beings. The transformed forms, asva–aśvī (stallion–mare) and mṛga–mṛgī (stag–doe)

### Printed p. 541
are also described in traditional contexts. Such transformations are natural in the efforts made when the resolve to create arises. For example:

स वै नैव रेमे तस्मादेकाकी न रमते स द्वितीयमैच्छत् । स हैतावानास यथा स्त्रीपुमांसौ संपरिष्टक्तौ स इममेवात्मानं द्वेधापातयत्ततः पतिश्च पत्नि चाभवतां शस्मादिदमर्धबृगलमिव स्व इति ह स्माह याज्ञवल्कस्तस्मादयमाकाशः स्त्रिया पूरृत एव तां समभवत्ततो मनुष्या अजायंत ॥ (*sa vai naiva reme tasmādekākī na ramate sa dvitīyamaicchat | sa haitāvānāsa yathā strīpumāṃsau saṃpariṣṭaktau sa imamevātmānaṃ dvedhāpātayattataḥ patiśca patni cābhavatāṃ śasmādidamardhabṛgalamiva sva iti ha smāha yājñavalkastasmādayamākāśaḥ striyā pūrṛta eva tāṃ samabhavattato manuṣyā ajāyaṃta ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-3)

Before creation, the single principle, having no other companion, could not attain any kind of delight. Therefore it desired a second principle. It grew to the extent of a woman and a man embracing. Then it divided into two parts. Then it was called by the forms of husband and wife. Therefore each individual (if there is no marital relation) is called only half of an individual. The ether was filled with the female principle, and since the male principle united with it, the progeny of man was born and grew in the universe.

सो हेयमीक्षांचक्रे । कथं नु मात्मन एव जनयित्वा संभवति हंत तिरोऽसानीति सा गौरभवत् वृषभ इतरस्तां समेवाभवत्ततो गावोऽजायंत वडवेतराभवदश्ववृष इतरो गर्दभीतरा गर्दभ इतर सां समेवाभवत्तत एकशफमजायताजेतराभवद्बस्त इतरोऽविरितरा मेष इतरस्तां समेवाभवत्ततोऽजावयोऽजायंतैवमेव यदिदं किंच मिथुनमा पिवीलिकाभ्यस्तत्सर्वमसृजत ॥ (*so heyamīkṣāṃcakre | kathaṃ nu mātmana eva janayitvā saṃbhavati haṃta tiro 'sānīti sā gaurabhavat vṛṣabha itarastāṃ samevābhavattato gāvo 'jāyaṃta vaḍavetarābhavadaśvavṛṣa itaro gardabhītarā gardabha itara sāṃ samevābhavattata ekaśaphamajāyatājetarābhavadbasta itaro 'viritarā meṣa itarastāṃ samevābhavattato 'jāvayo 'jāyaṃtaivameva yadidaṃ kiṃca mithunamā pivīlikābhyastatsarvamasṛjata ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-4)

Then that female person thought: "I have been created from this primal principle itself; I have become as a daughter to it. How can it unite with me, its own daughter?" and hid herself so that it should not know. She was transformed into the form of a cow. Then the primal principle took the form of a bull and united with her. As a result, cattle were born. She took the form of a mare, and the primal principle became a stallion. As a result, hoofed animals came into being. She became a she-goat, and the primal principle a he-goat. In the same way they also took the forms of ewe and ram. As a result the progeny of goats and sheep grew. In this way he created all kinds of creatures fit for pairing, down to the ants: so it says.

Thus, since the relation of father and daughter is present in this relation of female and male preceding creation, this defect, that the relation is contrary to morality, has been shown in one way or another.

### Printed p. 542
It is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa that the gods were displeased when Prajāpati desired his daughter Uṣas. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka states that the primal principle should not desire the female person created by itself, and that for this very reason she vanished from him (disappeared). Likewise in the present case too (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-1, 2) there is an indication that Saraṇyū, not wholly wishing to build a relation with Vivasvān, shows her dissatisfaction. In sum, the substance of this context can be stated thus.

When Tvaṣṭṛ intended to offer his daughter Saraṇyū in marriage to someone, the whole world came and assembled there. Meanwhile Tvaṣṭṛ developed full regard for Vivasvān. But he was a mortal, a human. Therefore, immediately after the marriage, Saraṇyū bore the twins famed in the world, Yama and Yamī, left them with Vivasvān and vanished. Then she became a mare. Vivasvān too became a stallion. As a result the Aśvin deities were born. In Savarṇā, who was Saraṇyū's substitute, Manu was born. Yama and Manu, the sons of Vivasvān, became the original ancestors of the human race.

Regarding this sūkta, the sage Śaunaka has said in the work called Bṛhaddevatā:

अभवन्मिथुनं त्वष्टुः सरण्यूस्त्रिशिराः सह । स वै सरण्यूं प्रायच्छत्स्वयमेव विवस्वते ॥ १६२ ॥ ततः सरण्यां जज्ञाते यमयम्यौ विवस्वतः । ता चाप्युधौ यमावेव ज्यायांस्ताभ्यां तु वै यमः ॥ (*abhavanmithunaṃ tvaṣṭuḥ saraṇyūstriśirāḥ saha | sa vai saraṇyūṃ prāyacchatsvayameva vivasvate ‖ 162 ‖ tataḥ saraṇyāṃ jajñāte yamayamyau vivasvataḥ | tā cāpyudhau yamāveva jyāyāṃstābhyāṃ tu vai yamaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. Adhyāya 6-162, 163)

Tvaṣṭṛ Prajāpati had twin children. Among them were a daughter named Saraṇyū and a son named Triśiras. He gave in marriage his daughter Saraṇyū to Vivasvān, son of Aditi. In that goddess Saraṇyū twins were born. Of them Yama was the elder, and Yamī the younger.

सृष्ट्वा भर्तुः परोक्षं तु सरण्यू: सदृशीं स्त्रियं । निक्षिप्य मिथुनं तस्यामश्वा भूत्वापचक्रमे ॥ १ ॥ अविज्ञानाद्विवस्वांस्तु तस्यामजनयन्मनुं । राजर्षिरभवत्सोऽपि विवस्वानिव तेजसा ॥ (*sṛṣṭvā bhartuḥ parokṣaṃ tu saraṇyū: sadṛśīṃ striyaṃ | nikṣipya mithunaṃ tasyāmaśvā bhūtvāpacakrame ‖ 1 ‖ avijñānādvivasvāṃstu tasyāmajanayanmanuṃ | rājarṣirabhavatso 'pi vivasvāniva tejasā ‖*)

One day Saraṇyū, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, without her husband Vivasvān's knowledge, created another woman like herself in beauty and form, placed her and her twin children Yama and Yamī

### Printed p. 543
in her own husband's house, and, assuming the form of a mare, went away with the intention of roaming freely. Vivasvān, who had gone somewhere and returned home, took the woman in his house, who was with his children Yama and Yamī (the woman created by Saraṇyū), to be his wife and took pleasure with her. From that, a son named Manu was born in that woman. Like his father Vivasvān he shone with divine radiance, grew up and became famed as a royal sage.

स विज्ञाय त्वपक्रांतां सरण्यूमश्वरूपिणीं । त्वाष्ट्रीं प्रति जगमाशु वाजी भूत्वा सलक्षणः ॥ ३ ॥ सरण्यूश्च विवस्वंतं विदित्वा हयरूपिणं । मैथुनायोपचक्राम तां च तत्रारुरोह सः ॥ (*sa vijñāya tvapakrāṃtāṃ saraṇyūmaśvarūpiṇīṃ | tvāṣṭrīṃ prati jagamāśu vājī bhūtvā salakṣaṇaḥ ‖ 3 ‖ saraṇyūśca vivasvaṃtaṃ viditvā hayarūpiṇaṃ | maithunāyopacakrāma tāṃ ca tatrāruroha saḥ ‖*)

Then Vivasvān learned that the woman in his house, with whom he had taken pleasure, was not his wife, and that his wife, the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, had gone off somewhere in the form of a mare. So Vivasvān himself took the form of an excellent horse and went to her, searching for Saraṇyū. Saraṇyū, taking Vivasvān in the form of a horse to be her own husband, became ready to unite with him. Vivasvān also played with her.

ततस्तयोस्तु वेगेन शुक्रं तदपतद्भुवि । उपाजिघ्रच्छ सा त्वश्वा तच्चुक्रं गर्भकाम्यया ॥ ५ ॥ आघातमात्राच्चुक्रात्तु कुमारौ संबभूवतुः । नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च यौ स्तुतावश्विनाविति ॥ (*tatastayostu vegena śukraṃ tadapatadbhuvi | upājighraccha sā tvaśvā taccukraṃ garbhakāmyayā ‖ 5 ‖ āghātamātrāccukrāttu kumārau saṃbabhūvatuḥ | nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca yau stutāvaśvināviti ‖*)

While Saraṇyū and Vivasvān, who had taken the forms of horses, were playing, Vivasvān's seed fell by emission on the ground. Saraṇyū in mare form, desiring that a child should be conceived in her, sniffed that seed lying on the ground. By the mere sniffing, twins were born in her. Of them one became famed as Nāsatya and the other as Dasra, and they are praised by people as the Aśvin deities.

इतिहासमिमं यास्कः सरण्यदेवते द्वृचे । विवस्वतश्च त्वष्टुश्च त्वष्टेति सह मन्यते ॥ (*itihāsamimaṃ yāskaḥ saraṇyadevate dvṛce | vivasvataśca tvaṣṭuśca tvaṣṭeti saha manyate ‖*)

This history told above has been explained by Yāska in his Nirukta (Ni. 12-11). There, in the first two Ṛks of the sūkta त्वष्टा दुहित्रे (*tvaṣṭā duhitre*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17), a description of the matter concerning Vivasvān and the goddess Saraṇyū, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, is given.

पूषेति पादौ पौष्ण द्वावाग्नेयावुत्तरा तु यौ । स्यातृतीयोऽपि ना पौष्णं तिस्रश्चान्याः परास्तु याः ॥ (*pūṣeti pādau pauṣṇa dvāvāgneyāvuttarā tu yau | syātṛtīyo 'pi nā pauṣṇaṃ tisraścānyāḥ parāstu yāḥ ‖*)

### Printed p. 544

The editor's Kannada continues: of the third Ṛk of the sūkta त्वष्टा दुहित्रे (*tvaṣṭā duhitre*) mentioned above, the first two pādas of the first half have Pūṣan as deity, and the two pādas of the latter half have Agni as deity. Or else Pūṣan alone may be the deity of the third pāda. The three Ṛks that follow it (Ṛks 4–6) also have Pūṣan as deity.

The Bṛhaddevatā says: अपां स्तुतिस्तृगत्रैका तृचात्सारस्वतात्परा । स्तुतः परोक्षः सोमस्तु द्रप्स इत्युत्तरे तृचे ॥ ९ ॥ अब्देवताशीर्वादो ना पयस्वत्युत्तरा तु या । (*apāṃ stutistṛgatraikā tṛcātsārasvatātparā | stutaḥ parokṣaḥ somastu drapsa ityuttare tṛce ‖ 9 ‖ abdevatāśīrvādo nā payasvatyuttarā tu yā |*) (Bṛ. De. Adhyā. 7-1 to 9).

The three Ṛks that follow (Ṛks 7–9) have Sarasvatī as deity; after them the 10th Ṛk is addressed to the Waters. In the three Ṛks after that (Ṛks 11–13) there is praise of the Waters, yet indirectly the deity Soma is praised. In the last Ṛk, the fourteenth, पयस्वतीः (*payasvatīḥ*), a blessing on the Waters is stated. This is the explanation.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्वितीयेऽनुवाके त्रयोदश सूक्तानि । तत्र त्वष्टा दुहित्र इत्येतच्छतुर्दशर्चं
> प्रथमं सूक्तं । यमपुत्रो देवश्रवा नामर्षिः । आदितो द्वादश त्रिष्टुभः । त्रयोदशीचतुर्दश्यावनुष्टुभौ । यद्वा त्रयोगशी पुरस्ताद्बृहती । आदितो द्वयोः
> सरण्यर्देवता । पूषा त्वेत इत्याद्याश्चतस्रः पूषदेवत्याः । सरस्वतीं देवयंत
> इत्याद्यास्ति स्रः सरस्वतीदेवताकाः । आपो अस्मानित्याद्याः पंचर्चोऽब्देवताकाः ।
> तत्र द्रप्सक्कंदेत्याद्यास्ति स्रः सोमदेवत्या ना । अथ चानुक्रांतं । त्वष्टा देवश्रवा द्वे सरण्यदेवते पौष्ट्यश्चतस्रः सारस्वत्यस्ति स्रः पंचाप्यो द्रप्सस्ति स्रः सौम्यो
> वांत्ये अनुष्टुभावप्रांत्या पुरस्ताद्बृहती वेति : गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । त्वष्टनामकस्य देवस्य सरण्यस्त्रीशिराश्चति स्त्रीपुंसात्मकमपत्यद्वयमभूत् । ततस्त्वष्टा सरण्यनामिकां पुत्रीं विवस्वते प्रायच्छत् । ततस्तस्यां विविस्वतः
> सकाशाद्यमयम् विजज्ञाते । ततः कदाचिदात्मसदृश्या देवजनितायाः स्त्रियः
> समीपे तदपत्यद्वयं निधाय स्वयमाश्वं रूपं कृत्तोत्तरान्कुरून्प्रतिजगाम ।
> अथ विवस्वानेतां स्त्रियं सरण्यमिति मत्वा तामरंसीत् । तल्यां मनुर्नाम राजर्षिरजायत । ततो विवस्वानेषा सरण्यर्न भवतीति विज्ञाय स्वयमष्यश्लो भूत्वा
> तामश्वरूपिणीं प्रायासीत् ; ततः संक्रीडमानयोस्तयोः स्वभूतं रेतः पृथिव्यां
> पपात ! अथ सा गर्भकामनया तत्पतितं रेत अजघ्नौ । ततस्तस्याः सकाशान्नासत्यो
> दस्रश्चेत्युभावश्विनावजायेतामिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second anuvāka contains thirteen sūktas, of which the first is this sūkta of fourteen Ṛks, त्वष्टा दुहित्रे (*tvaṣṭā duhitre*). Its seer is Devaśravas, son of Yama. The first twelve Ṛks are triṣṭubh; the thirteenth and fourteenth are anuṣṭubh; or else the thirteenth is purastād-bṛhatī. The deity of the first two Ṛks is Saraṇyū. The four beginning पूषा त्वेत (*pūṣā tveta*) have Pūṣan as deity; the three beginning सरस्वतीं देवयंत (*sarasvatīṃ devayaṃta*) have Sarasvatī; the five Ṛks beginning आपो अस्मान् (*āpo asmān*) have the Waters, among which the three beginning द्रप्सक्कंद (*drapsakkaṃda*) have Soma as deity. He then quotes the Anukramaṇī: त्वष्टा देवश्रवा द्वे सरण्यदेवते पौष्ट्यश्चतस्रः सारस्वत्यस्ति स्रः पंचाप्यो द्रप्सस्ति स्रः सौम्यो वांत्ये अनुष्टुभावप्रांत्या पुरस्ताद्बृहती वेति : (*tvaṣṭā devaśravā dve saraṇyadevate pauṣṭyaścatasraḥ sārasvatyasti sraḥ paṃcāpyo drapsasti sraḥ saumyo vāṃtye anuṣṭubhāvaprāṃtyā purastādbṛhatī veti :*). The use of the sūkta in ritual has been stated already.

Here they relate an itihāsa. The god named Tvaṣṭṛ had two children, Saraṇyū and Triśiras (a daughter and a son). Tvaṣṭṛ gave his daughter Saraṇyū to Vivasvat, and from Vivasvat she bore the twins Yama and Yamī. Then once she placed the two children beside a woman born of the gods who resembled herself, took the form of a mare and went to the Uttarakurus. Vivasvat, taking that woman to be Saraṇyū, took his pleasure with her, and from her was born the royal sage named Manu. Then Vivasvat, realising that this was not Saraṇyū, himself became a stallion and went after her in her mare's form. While they sported, his semen fell on the earth; she, desiring offspring, sniffed the fallen semen, and from her were born the two Aśvins, Nāsatya and Dasra.

### Printed p. 545

##### Anuvāda (Kannada)

The second anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala contains thirteen sūktas; of them this sūkta त्वष्टा दुहित्रे (*tvaṣṭā duhitre*) is the first. It has fourteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Devaśravas, son of Yama. Its first twelve Ṛks are in the triṣṭubh metre; the thirteenth and fourteenth Ṛks are in the anuṣṭubh metre; or else the thirteenth Ṛk is in the purastād-bṛhatī metre. The deity of the first two Ṛks of this sūkta is the woman Saraṇyū. The four Ṛks from the Ṛk पूषा श्वेतः (*pūṣā śvetaḥ*) onward (Ṛks 3–6) have Pūṣan as deity; the next three Ṛks beginning सरस्वती देवयंतः (*sarasvatī devayaṃtaḥ*) (Ṛks 7–9) have Sarasvatī as deity; the next five Ṛks beginning आपो अस्मान् (*āpo asmān*) (Ṛks 10–14) have the Waters as deity. Of these, the three Ṛks beginning द्रप्पश्चस्कंद (*drappaścaskaṃda*) (Ṛks 11–13) have the Waters, or else Soma, as deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: त्वष्टा. देवश्रवा द्वे सरण्यदेवते पौश्यश्चतस्रः सारस्वत्यस्ति स्रः पंचाप्यो द्रप्पस्ति स्रः सौम्यो वांत्ये अनुष्टुभावुषांत्या पुरस्तादृहती वा (*tvaṣṭā. devaśravā dve saraṇyadevate pauśyaścatasraḥ sārasvatyasti sraḥ paṃcāpyo drappasti sraḥ saumyo vāṃtye anuṣṭubhāvuṣāṃtyā purastādṛhatī vā*). The use of the sūkta in ritual has been stated earlier.

There is an itihāsa concerning this sūkta. The god named Tvaṣṭṛ had two children, a daughter Saraṇyū and a son Triśiras. Tvaṣṭṛ gave his daughter Saraṇyū in marriage to Vivasvat. To this couple, Saraṇyū and Vivasvat, twins were born, the son Yama and the daughter Yamī. Then one day Saraṇyū set the twins beside a goddess-woman who resembled herself, took the form of a mare and departed for the country of the Uttarakurus. Thereupon Vivasvat, thinking that woman to be his wife the goddess Saraṇyū, took his pleasure with her; and in that woman was born the royal sage named Manu. Afterwards Vivasvat learned that this woman was not his wife Saraṇyū. Then Vivasvat took the form of a horse and went to Saraṇyū, who was likewise in mare's form. While the two, in horse form, were absorbed in love-play, Vivasvat's semen fell on the ground. Then the woman in mare's form, desiring children, sniffed the semen that had fallen; from it the two Aśvin deities, Nāsatya and Dasra, were born in her. This is the story the bhāṣyakāra tells in this context.

**Sūkta particulars**

Sūkta 17. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 17. Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 6; Vargas 23, 25, 25 **NOTE**. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 14. Ṛṣi: Devaśravas Yāmāyana. Deity: 1, 2 Saraṇyū; 3–6 Pūṣan; 7–9 Sarasvatī; 10–14 Āpaḥ **NOTE**; 11–13 the Waters or Soma. Metre: 1–12 triṣṭubh; 13 anuṣṭubh or purastād-bṛhatī; 14 anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वष्टा॑ दुहि॒त्रे व॑ह॒तुं कृ॑णो॒तीती॒दं विश्वं॒ भुव॑नं॒ समे॑ति ।  
> य॒मस्य॑ मा॒ता प॑र्यु॒ह्यमा॑ना म॒हो जा॒या विव॑स्वतो  
> ननाश ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वष्टा । दुहित्रे । वहतुं । कृणोति । इति । इदं । विश्वं । भुवनं । सं । एति ।  
> यमस्य । माता । परिउह्यमाना । महः । जाया । विवस्वतः । ननाश ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वष्टैतन्नामको देवो दुहित्रे । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । दुहितुः सरण्यूनामिकाया वहतुं वहनं विवाहं ॥ एधिवहोश्चतुः । उ. सू. १-७९ । इति वहेश्चतुप्रत्ययः ॥ तं कृणोति । करोति । इत्येतेन हेतुनेदं वित्वं सर्वं भुवनं
> भूतजातं समेति । तं विवाहं समागमत् । पर्युह्यमाना विवस्वतोद्वोढव्या
> यमस्य यम्याश्च माता महो मह 'रो विवस्वतो जाया भार्या सरणूर्ननाश।
> उत्तरान्कुरून्प्रति नष्टा । अगच्छदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The god named Tvaṣṭṛ, for his daughter (the dative stands in the sense of the genitive), Saraṇyū by name, makes the वहतुं (*vahatuṃ*), that is, the carrying away, the marriage. For this reason the whole world, all beings, come together to that marriage. Saraṇyū, who was to be led away in marriage by Vivasvat, the mother of Yama and Yamī, the wife of the great Vivasvat, "was lost": she went away towards the Uttarakurus.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*)—the god named Tvaṣṭṛ
- दुहित्रे (*duhitre*)—for his daughter Saraṇyū
- वहतुं (*vahatuṃ*)—the marriage
- कृणोति (*kṛṇoti*)—performs
- इति (*iti*)—for that reason
- इदं विश्वं भुवनं (*idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ*)—this whole assemblage of beings
- समेति (*sameti*)—come together
- पर्युह्यमाना (*paryuhyamānā*)—she who is to be given by Vivasvat
- यमस्य (*yamasya*)—of Yama
- माता (*mātā*)—the mother
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of the great
- विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)—Vivasvat
- जाया (*jāyā*)—the wife, Saraṇyū
- ननाश (*nanāśa*)—became invisible

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Hearing the news that the god named Tvaṣṭṛ was performing the marriage of his daughter Saraṇyū, all beings assembled. But Saraṇyū, who was to be made ready for the marriage, the mother of Yama and the wife of the great Vivasvat, became invisible.

Twashtri celebrates the marriage of his daughter : therefore the whole world is assembled ; but the mother of Yama, the newly-married-wife of the mighty Vivaswat, disappeared.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has stated the Nirukta for this verse **NOTE**—

त्वष्टा दुहित्रे वहतुं कृणोतीतीदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति । यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश ॥ (*tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṃ kṛṇotītīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sameti | yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-1)

त्वष्टा दुहितुर्वहनं करोतीदं विश्वं भुवनं समेतीमानि च सर्वाणि भूतान्यभिसमागच्छंति यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना महतो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश । रात्रिरादित्यस्यादित्योदयेऽन्तर्धीयते ॥ ( (*tvaṣṭā duhiturvahanaṃ karotīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sametīmāni ca sarvāṇi bhūtānyabhisamāgacchaṃti yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā mahato jāyā vivasvato nanāśa | rātrirādityasyādityodaye 'ntardhīyate ‖ (*) (Ni. 12-11)

For this Ṛk Yāska has given two kinds of explanation, according to the Tvaṣṭṛ view and according to the Āditya view.

On the Tvaṣṭṛ view: here Tvaṣṭṛ is said to be Viśvakarman, who creates everything, Prajāpati. When this Tvaṣṭṛ-Prajāpati set about giving his daughter, the goddess Saraṇyū, in marriage to Vivasvat, all the beings of this world (gods, men, animals and all others) gathered in one place, that is, in the marriage pavilion, to see that marriage. At a wedding it is natural for kinsmen and others to gather together for joy. Then, that is, after the marriage, the goddess Saraṇyū, mother of Yama and wife of the venerable Vivasvat, disappeared somewhere; that is, she made a goddess-woman in her own place instead of herself, put her there, took the form of a mare and went away. This is the sense.

On the Nairukta or Āditya view: below we give the bhāṣya and explanation that Durgācārya, commentator on the Nirukta, wrote for this Ṛk in the Āditya sense—

त्वष्टा मध्यमः तमोभागस्य उषसः दुहित्रे दुहितुः दूरे हितायाः प्रकाशरूपायाः वहतुं वहनं विवस्वतः करोति । इदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति । प्रभातमिति मत्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि स्वासु स्वास्त्विति कर्तव्यतासु अभिसमागच्छंति । यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना-यमस्य मध्यमस्य माता देवधर्मेण अथवा द्युस्थानस्य यैव जाया सा मातेति । जायतेऽस्यां पुत्रत्वेन पतिः जाया भार्या। महतो विवस्वतः प्रकाशेन प्रोत्सार्यमाणा ननाश नश्यति । संक्षेपतो भाष्यकारोऽर्थं निराहरात्रिरादित्यस्य । उषा जाया सा आदित्यस्कोदयेऽन्तर्धीयते इति ॥ (*tvaṣṭā madhyamaḥ tamobhāgasya uṣasaḥ duhitre duhituḥ dūre hitāyāḥ prakāśarūpāyāḥ vahatuṃ vahanaṃ vivasvataḥ karoti | idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sameti | prabhātamiti matvā sarvāṇi bhūtāni svāsu svāstviti kartavyatāsu abhisamāgacchaṃti | yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā-yamasya madhyamasya mātā devadharmeṇa athavā dyusthānasya yaiva jāyā sā māteti | jāyate 'syāṃ putratvena patiḥ jāyā bhāryā| mahato vivasvataḥ prakāśena protsāryamāṇā nanāśa naśyati | saṃkṣepato bhāṣyakāro 'rthaṃ nirāharātrirādityasya | uṣā jāyā sā ādityaskodaye 'ntardhīyate iti ‖*) (2. Kṛtya) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 548

That is: here Tvaṣṭṛ is the deity of the middle region, the sun or Āditya. दुहित्रे वहतुं (*duhitre vahatuṃ*) means: for the far-off (sun) to bear light, or to spread it around. At the end of the night, when the dawn-time begins, all the creatures of the world see the sun rising in the distance to drive away the darkness, and knowing that the darkness has been destroyed and morning has come, they engage in their several occupations. यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना (*yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā*): the mother of Yama, the middle deity, Āditya, is the heaven-world (the atmosphere); or else, as stated in the śruti sentence आत्मा वै पुत्रनामासि (*ātmā vai putranāmāsi*), because the husband himself is born, in the form of a portion of himself, as son in his wife, the wife is called जाया (*jāyā*). Hence night, or Uṣas, is the wife of the sun. Since after that night (when the night has passed) the sun is born in the form of a portion, night becomes the sun's wife; that is, night or the goddess Uṣas is said to be the sun's wife. जाया विवस्वतो ननाश (*jāyā vivasvato nanāśa*) means रात्रिरादित्यस्यादित्योदयेऽन्तर्धीयते (*rātrirādityasyādityodaye 'ntardhīyate*): the sun's wife, night or Uṣas, perishes after sunrise, that is, becomes invisible. This is the main intent of the Āditya view.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमृतां मरणधर्मरहितामेतां सरण्यूं मर्त्येभ्यो मनुष्येभ्यस्तदुत्पत्यर्थमपागूहन् । अपगूहितवंतः । संवृतवंतः । देवा उपनीतवंतः इत्यर्थः ।
> किंच सवर्णां सरण्यूसदृशीमन्यां स्त्रीयुं कृत्वा तस्मै विवस्वते देवा अददुः।
> प्रायच्छन् । उतापि च साश्वरूपिणी सरण्यूस्तदाश्विनावभरत् । स्वोदरे गर्भभूतौ
> धारितवती । यद्यदा तज्जायापतिभ्यामश्वरूपात्मना संभोगकाले रेतः पतितमासीत् तदाश्विन् जनयामासेत्यर्थः । तथा सरण्यूः सरणवत्येतन्नामिका द्वा मिथुना
> द्वा मिथुनौ यमयम्यावजहात् । त्यक्तवती । जनितवतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा ! सरण्यूरेतन्नामिका मध्यमस्थाना देवता मध्यममग्निं माध्यमिकां वाचं चोत्पादितवती॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods hid this immortal Saraṇyū, free from the nature of death, from mortals (men), for the sake of begetting offspring: अपागूहन् (*apāgūhan*) means they concealed, covered, took her away. Moreover, having made another woman like Saraṇyū, सवर्णां (*savarṇāṃ*), the gods gave her to Vivasvat. And that Saraṇyū, in mare's form, bore the two Aśvins in her own womb as embryos: when, in union in horse form, the semen of the wife and husband fell, then she begot the Aśvins. Likewise Saraṇyū, so named, abandoned, that is, bore, the two twins, Yama and Yamī. Or else Saraṇyū, a deity of the middle region, produced the middle Agni and the speech of the middle region.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमृतां (*amṛtāṃ*)—Saraṇyū, free from the nature of death
- मर्त्येभ्यः (*martyebhyaḥ*)—from men
- अपागूहन् (*apāgūhan*)—hiding
- सवर्णां (*savarṇāṃ*)—another woman of the same form
- कृश्वी (*kṛśvī*)—having made
- विवस्वते (*vivasvate*)—to Vivasvat
- अददुः (*adaduḥ*)—the gods gave
- उत (*uta*)—and
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- तत् आसीत् (*tat āsīt*)—when the horse-formed fall of semen occurred, then
- अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*)—the two Aśvin deities
- अभरत् (*abharat*)—that woman obtained
- सरण्यः (*saraṇyaḥ*)—Saraṇyū
- द्वा मिथुना (*dvā mithunā*)—Yama and Yamī
- अजहात् (*ajahāt*)—gave birth to

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Having hidden the deathless Saraṇyū from men and made another woman of the same form, the gods gave her to Vivasvat. And when the horse-formed fall of semen occurred, that woman obtained the Aśvin deities. Saraṇyū obtained Yama and Yamī.

##### English translation
The Gods concealing the immortal (Saranyu) for the sake of mortals
and having formed a woman resembling her, gave her to Vivaswat. She
bore the two Ashwins when this had happened, and then Saranyu gave birth
to two twins.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska, in explaining the derivation of the word सरण्यः (*saraṇyaḥ*), states the Nirukta on this Ṛk and relates an itihāsa concerning Saraṇyū.

सरण्यः । सरण्यः सरणात् । तस्यैषा भवति । (*saraṇyaḥ | saraṇyaḥ saraṇāt | tasyaiṣā bhavati |*) अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते । उताश्विनावभरदत्तदासीदजहादु द्वा (*apāgūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇāmadadurvivasvate | utāśvināvabharadattadāsīdajahādu dvā*)

### Printed p. 550

मिथुना सरण्यः ॥ (*mithunā saraṇyaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17.2). अप्पगूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वतेऽप्यश्विनावभरदत्तदासीदजहाद्वा मिथुनौ सरण्यर्मध्यमं च माध्यमिकां च वाचमिति नैरुक्ताः । यमं च यमीं चैत्यैतिहासिकाः ॥ (*appagūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇāmadadurvivasvate 'pyaśvināvabharadattadāsīdajahādvā mithunau saraṇyarmadhyamaṃ ca mādhyamikāṃ ca vācamiti nairuktāḥ | yamaṃ ca yamīṃ caityaitihāsikāḥ ‖*)

तत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते-त्वाष्ट्री सरण्यूर्निवस्वत आदित्याद्यमौ मिथुनौ जनयांचकार । सा सवर्णामन्यां प्रतिनिधायाश्वं रूपं कृत्वा प्रदुद्राव । स विवस्वानादित्य अश्वमेव रूपं कृत्वा तामनुसृत्य संबभूव । ततोऽश्विन् जज्ञाते सवर्णायां मनुः ॥ (*tatretihāsamācakṣate-tvāṣṭrī saraṇyūrnivasvata ādityādyamau mithunau janayāṃcakāra | sā savarṇāmanyāṃ pratinidhāyāśvaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtvā pradudrāva | sa vivasvānāditya aśvameva rūpaṃ kṛtvā tāmanusṛtya saṃbabhūva | tato 'śvin jajñāte savarṇāyāṃ manuḥ ‖*) (Ni. 12-10 **NOTE**)

The word सरण्य (*saraṇya*) is formed from the root सृ (*sṛ*), meaning "to move". The literal sense of the word is: she who goes forward and forward, she who is in motion. The nirvacana of the Ṛk अपागूहन् (*apāgūhan*), in which this word is used, is as follows: the gods hid that goddess Saraṇyū, who is without death, that is, imperishable, so that she was invisible to the eyes of men, and put her away; and having made another woman of the same form and shape, they gave her to Āditya. At this time, that is, when the goddess Saraṇyū was invisible (when, having taken a mare's form, she was in another region, as the fruit of the union with Āditya (Vivasvat), who had taken a horse's form), she obtained the Aśvin deities, and she abandoned the twin children Yama and Yamī whom she had obtained before. Here the word मिथुनौ (*mithunau*) has been explained in two ways: the middle region, that is, Indra of the atmosphere, and the speech-deity of the atmosphere, according to the Nirukta authors; Yama and Yamī, according to the itihāsa authors.

There is an itihāsa on this point: the goddess Saraṇyū, Tvaṣṭṛ's daughter, obtained from Āditya (Vivasvat) two twin children, Yama and Yamī. Afterwards she set another goddess-woman like herself beside Āditya as her substitute, and herself ran away in mare's form. (This goddess-woman of the same form is customarily called by the name Chāyā. And in this woman Manu was born from Āditya. Afterwards Āditya, learning that this woman was not his wife Saraṇyū,) then himself took a horse's form, followed the mare-formed Saraṇyū, and stayed near her. Then, as the fruit of the mutual union of these two, the Aśvin deities were born, and in the woman of the same form Manu was born. This is the intent of the Nirukta statement.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the death of a man consecrated for a sacrifice, three verses beginning पूषा त्वेत (*pūṣā tveta*) are to be recited, and the sūtra says: four verses beginning "Pūṣā tvetaś cyāvayatu pra vidvān" (Ā. 6.10). Pūṣan, the nourisher, bearing this name, is to make you move away from this place, this world, and to take you onward to the best world. What kind of god is he? He is "knowing", aware of our devotion; "of unlost cattle", possessed of imperishable cattle, in whose care all cattle remain and do not perish; and the protector of all that has come into being. Further, the same Pūṣan is to give you over to these fathers. Likewise Agni is to give you to the सुविदत्रियेभ्यः (*suvidatriyebhyaḥ*): सुविदत्रं (*suvidatraṃ*) is knowledge or wealth, and those worthy of it are सुविदत्रियाः (*suvidatriyāḥ*). So he is to give you to the gods of excellent knowledge, the possessors of good wealth, and to establish you in their world.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—one who knows everything
- अनष्टपशुः (*anaṣṭapaśuḥ*)—one whose cattle are not lost
- भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)—of all beings
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—the protector
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- इतः (*itaḥ*)—from this world
- प्र च्यवयतु (*pra cyavayatu*)—let him carry to the best world
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same god Pūṣan
- एतेभ्यः पितृभ्यः (*etebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ*)—to these fathers
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- परि ददत् (*pari dadat*)—let him hand over
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- सुविदत्रियेभ्यः (*suvidatriyebhyaḥ*)—to those of full knowledge (or of wealth)
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—to the gods too, let him hand over

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the god Pūṣan, who knows everything, whose cattle are never lost, and who is the protector of all beings, carry you from this world to the best world. May the same Pūṣan hand you over to these fathers. May Agni hand you over to the gods of full knowledge (or of wealth).

### Printed p. 552

##### English translation
May the discriminating Pushan, whose cattle are never lost, the protector of all beings, transfer you hence (to a better world): may he give you to these Pitris : may Agni (give) you to the beneficent gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

To support, as an example, the praise of two deities separately in a single Ṛk, the exposition of this Ṛk has been given: अथाप्याग्नापौष्णं हविर्न तु संस्तवः ! तत्रैतां विभक्तिस्तु तिमृचमुदाहरंति । पूषा त्वेतश्चावयतु प्र विद्वाननष्टपशुर्भुवनस्य गोपाः । स त्वैतेभ्यः परिददत्पितृभ्योऽग्निर्दॆवेभ्यः सुविदत्रियेभ्यः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१७-३) । पूषा त्वेतः प्रच्यावयतु विद्वाननष्टपशुर्भुवनस्य गोपा इत्येष हि सर्वॆषां भूतानां गोपायितादित्यः स त्वैतेभ्यः परिददत् पितृभ्य इति सांशयिकस्तृतीयः पादः । पूषा पुरस्तात्तस्यान्वादेश इत्येकमग्निरुपरिष्कात्तस्य प्रकीर्तनेत्यपरं । अग्निर्दॆवेभ्यः सुविदत्रियेभ्यः । सुविदत्रं धनं भवति विंदतेर्वैकोपसर्गाद्ददातेर्वा स्याद्व्युपसर्गात् ॥ (*athāpyāgnāpauṣṇaṃ havirna tu saṃstavaḥ ! tatraitāṃ vibhaktistu timṛcamudāharaṃti | pūṣā tvetaścāvayatu pra vidvānanaṣṭapaśurbhuvanasya gopāḥ | sa tvaitebhyaḥ paridadatpitṛbhyo 'gnirdèvebhyaḥ suvidatriyebhyaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-17-3) | pūṣā tvetaḥ pracyāvayatu vidvānanaṣṭapaśurbhuvanasya gopā ityeṣa hi sarvèṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ gopāyitādityaḥ sa tvaitebhyaḥ paridadat pitṛbhya iti sāṃśayikastṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ | pūṣā purastāttasyānvādeśa ityekamagnirupariṣkāttasya prakīrtanetyaparaṃ | agnirdèvebhyaḥ suvidatriyebhyaḥ | suvidatraṃ dhanaṃ bhavati viṃdatervaikopasargāddadātervā syādvyupasargāt ‖*) (Ni. 7-9).
In some Ṛks, even though two deities are praised, it is not a joint praise (saṃstava); that is, it is not as if the two were praised together. Though the names of two occur, the praise of each of them is separate. For example, in this Ṛk Pūṣan and Agni are praised, yet it is not a joint praise; the two are praised separately.
This god Pūṣan knows everything. Therefore, by remembering him or by his knowledge, cattle do not stray. Cattle that have strayed for some reason are certainly recovered again through Pūṣan's knowledge of the way. For this reason Pūṣan is called here "of unlost cattle". This god protects the whole world. May such Pūṣan, in the form of the Āditya, separate you, the dead body, from the path of this world and give you into the keeping of the fathers; and may Agni from there give you into the keeping of the gods, the givers of wealth. Some have expressed doubt about the meaning of the third pāda of this Ṛk. The meaning stated in this pāda, that Pūṣan is to give you (the dead) to the fathers, is open to doubt. For here it is said that Pūṣan gives you to the fathers, and then that Agni gives him to the gods. Besides this pāda's naming Pūṣan as deity, others hold that the third and fourth pāda both belong to Agni, so that the meaning that Agni himself gives this dead body to both the fathers and the gods is evident here.

### Printed p. 553
As to the word सुविदत्रियेभ्यः (*suvidatriyebhyaḥ*) in this Ṛk: सुविदत्र (*suvidatra*) means wealth. The explanation is that this word may be formed either from the root विद् (*vid*) in the sense of "obtain", with the single prefix सु (*su*), or from the root दा (*dā*) in the sense of "give", with the two prefixes सु (*su*) and वि (*vi*).
The sacrificer who has taken the consecration for a sacrifice, on his death, is to recite four Ṛks beginning पूषा त्वेतः (*pūṣā tvetaḥ*) (verses 3-6 of this sūkta); this is set out in the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra पूषा त्वेतश्चावयतु प्र विद्वानिति चतस्रः (*pūṣā tvetaścāvayatu pra vidvāniti catasraḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 6-10).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*) is the wind (vāyu) that goes everywhere, to all; the loss of the letter va is Vedic. Alternatively, the form is made with the affix *uṇ* in the Veda, with vṛddhi; the meaning is "the goer", the wind. त्वां परि पासति (*tvāṃ pari pāsati*): may he protect you all round, by Pūṣan's leave. प्रपथे (*prapathe*): on the excellent path, in heaven; Pūṣan, being first of all, himself is to protect you, the deceased sacrificer. Where the doers of good deeds abide, or where those good-doers have gone **NOTE**, (continued in the next block).

> प्राप्ताः तत्र तस्मिन्स्थाने देवो दीप्यमानः सविता सर्वस्य स्वस्वकर्मणि प्रेरक
> एतन्नामको देवस्त्वा त्वां दधातु । निदधातु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

...there, in that place, the shining god Savitṛ, the impeller of everyone in his own work, bearing this name, is to place you, to set you down.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)—all-pervading
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—the wind
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- परि पासति (*pari pāsati*)—let him protect
- प्रपथे (*prapathe*)—in the most excellent heaven
- पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)—being first of all
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you, the sacrificer
- पातु (*pātu*)—let him protect
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which region
- सुकृतः (*sukṛtaḥ*)—doers of good deeds
- आसते (*āsate*)—abide
- यत्र (*yatra*)—where
- ते सुकृतः ययुः (*te sukṛtaḥ yayuḥ*)—where the people who do good go
- तत्र (*tatra*)—in that place
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the shining
- सविता (*savitā*)—god Savitṛ

- दधातु (*dadhātu*)—let him establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the all-pervading wind protect you. May the god Pūṣan, who is first of all in the most excellent heaven, protect you, the sacrificer. In the region where the doers of good deeds abide, to which those good-doers go, in that place may the shining god Savitṛ establish you.

##### English translation
May the all-pervading, Vayu protect you, may Pushan (preserve) you, (going) first on the excellent path (to heaven): may the divine Savitri place you, where the virtuous abide, whither they have gone.
