> सत्यस्मान् । प्रमिते यजमानो ब्रवीति पुत्रमुखेन याजकमुखेन वा । अस्मानभयतमेनात्यंतं भयरहितेन मार्गेण नेषत् । नयतु । कथं । स्वस्तिदाः कल्याणस्य
> दाताघृणिरागतदीप्तियुक्तः सर्ववीरः सर्वैर्विरैः कर्मणि समर्थैर्युत्विग्निरुपेतोऽप्रयुच्छन्नप्रमाद्यन् प्रजानन्नस्माकं फलाफले विजानानः सन् पुर एतु ।
> अस्माकं पुरस्ताद्गच्छतु । यथास्माकं भयं न भवति तथा गच्छत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This verse is the anuvākyā for the offering of the eleven-fold animal to Pūṣan; the sūtra says so (Ā. 3-7), citing the verse together with the following pāda. The god Pūṣan knows all these quarters, east and the rest, in order: he knows in sequence which are to be travelled with ease and which not. This being so, the deceased sacrificer speaks, through his son or through the priest: let him lead us by the most fearless path, a path wholly free of fear. How? As giver of welfare, endowed with radiance that has come to him, सर्ववीरः (*sarvavīraḥ*), accompanied by all the heroes, the priests capable in the rite, not neglecting anything, knowing the good and bad outcome for us, let him go before us; that is, let him go in front of us so that we may have no fear.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- सर्वाः (*sarvāḥ*)—all
- इमा आशाः (*imā āśāḥ*)—all these quarters
- अनु वेद (*anu veda*)—knows
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- अभयतमेन (*abhayatamena*)—by the path wholly free of fear
- नेषत् (*neṣat*)—let him lead
- स्वस्ति दाः (*svasti dāḥ*)—giver of welfare
- आघृणिः (*āghṛṇiḥ*)—very radiant
- सर्ववीरः (*sarvavīraḥ*)—accompanied by all the priests
- अप्रयुच्छन् (*aprayucchan*)—not in the least careless
- प्रजानन् (*prajānan*)—knowing what is good for us
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—before us
- एतु (*etu*)—let him go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Pūṣan knows all these quarters. May he lead us by a path wholly free of fear. Being giver of welfare, very radiant, accompanied by all the priests, not in the least careless, and knowing our welfare, may he go before us.

##### English translation
Pushan knows all these regions severally; let him conduct us by (the path) that is most free from peril: let him precede us, who is the giver of prosperity, endowed with radiance, accompanied by all pious men, ever vigilant, and knowing our (deserts).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice to Pūṣan called Ekādaśin, when the oblation is offered, this Ṛk beginning पूषेमा (*pūṣemā*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra

### Printed p. 556
in the sūtra beginning with this verse (Ā. 3-7).
#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रप॑थे प॒थाम॑जनिष्ट पू॒षा प्रप॑थे दि॒वः प्रप॑थे पृथि॒व्याः ।  
> उ॒भे अ॒भि प्रि॒यत॑मे स॒धस्थे॒ आ च॒ परा॑ च चरति प्रजा॒नन् ॥६॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रपथे । पथां । अजनिष्ट । पूषा । प्रपथे । दिवः । प्रपथे । पृथिव्याः ।  
> उभे इति । अभि । प्रियतमे इति प्रियतमे । सधस्थे इति सधस्थे । आ । च । परा ।  
> च । चरति । प्रजानन् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एकादशिनस्य पौष्णस्य पशोः पुरोडाशस्य प्रपथे पथामिति याज्या । सूत्रितं
> च । प्रपथे पथामजनिष्ट पूषा पथस्पथः परिपतिं वचस्या । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> पथामंतरिक्षगमनहेतुभूतानां मार्गाणां मध्यॆ प्रपथे यः प्रकृष्टः
> पंथास्ति तत्र पूजाजनिष्ट । प्रादुरभूत् । पुण्यकर्मणां सुगतिप्रापणार्थमवस्थित
> इति भावः । तथा दिवो द्युलोकस्य च मार्गाणां मध्यॆ प्रपथे प्रकृष्टे मार्गे
> जातः । तथा पृथिव्याः प्रपथे प्रकृष्टे मार्गे मनुष्याणां तत्तत्कर्मणि प्रवर्तनार्थं प्रादुर्भूत इत्यर्थः । सोऽयं पूषा प्रियतमे सर्वस्यॆष्टतमे सधस्थे
> सर्वेषां सहावस्थानभूते उभे द्यावापृथिव्यावभिलक्ष्या चरति । अभिमुख्येन चरति ।
> सुकृतिनां सुकृतफलप्रदर्शनायानुकूलं चरतीत्यर्थः । तथा परा चरति । दुष्कर्मणां प्रतिकूलं गच्छति । किं कुर्वन् । प्रजानन् अनेनेदं कर्म कृतमस्य कर्मण
> इदं फलमित्यविशेषेण जानानः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This verse is the yājyā for the puroḍāśa of the eleven-fold animal offering to Pūṣan; the sūtra says so (Ā. 3-7), citing the verse. Among the paths by which one travels through the sky, on the excellent path, Pūṣan was born, that is, appeared; the sense is that he stands there to bring the doers of good deeds to a good destination. Likewise, among the paths of heaven, he was born on the excellent path; and on the excellent path of the earth he appeared in order to set men to their several acts. This Pūṣan moves towards both heaven and earth, the dearest to all, the common dwelling of all; he moves towards them, facing them. The meaning is that he moves favourably to the good-doers, to show them the fruit of their good deeds; and he goes परा (*parā*), away, adversely, to the doers of evil. Doing what? Knowing without distinction: "by this man this act was done; this is the fruit of this act".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पथां (*pathāṃ*)—among all the paths
- प्रपथे (*prapathe*)—on the most excellent path
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- अजनिष्ट (*ajaniṣṭa*)—has been born
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of heaven
- प्रपथे (*prapathe*)—on the most excellent path he has been born too
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- प्रपथे (*prapathe*)—on the excellent path he has been born too (that same Pūṣan)
- प्रियतमे (*priyatame*)—the dearest to all
- सधस्थे (*sadhasthe*)—the common abode of all
- उभे (*ubhe*)—between the two, heaven and earth
- आ चरति (*ā carati*)—he moves
- प्रजानन् (*prajānan*)—knowing the acts and what follows them
- परा (चरति) (*parā (carati)*)—he moves facing those who have fallen from their rites

### Printed p. 557

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Pūṣan has been born on the most excellent of the paths. He has been born on the most excellent path of the heavenly world and on the excellent path of the earth. The same Pūṣan moves between the two, heaven and earth, which are dear to all and are a common abode for all. Knowing the differences among the dead between those who have performed rites and those who have fallen from rites, he moves facing away from those who have fallen from rites and facing toward those who have performed rites.

##### English translation
Pushan has been born on the best path of paths, on the best path of heaven, on the best path of earth, he goes forward and backward over both (worlds), the assemblies longed for by all, discriminating (the merits of the dead)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal offering called Ekādaśinī, which belongs to Pūṣan, when the cake (puroḍāśa) is offered, this Ṛk, "प्रपथे पथां (*prapathe pathāṃ*)", is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra प्रपथे पथामजनिष्ट पूषा पथस्पथः परिपतिं वचस्या (*prapathe pathāmajaniṣṭa pūṣā pathaspathaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā*) (Ā. 3-7).

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सर॑स्वतीं देव॒यंतो॑ हवंते॒ सर॑स्वतीमध्व॒रे ता॒यमा॑ने ।  
> सर॑स्वतीं सु॒कृतो॑ अह्वयंत॒ सर॑स्वती दा॒शुषे॒ वार्यं॑  
> दात् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सरस्वतीं । देवयंतः । हवंते । सरस्वतीं । अध्वरे । तायमाने ।  
> सरस्वतीं । सुकृतः । अह्वयंत । सरस्वती । दाशुषे । वार्यं । दात् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> व्यूहस्य दशराश्रस्य तृतीये छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रे सारस्वततृचस्य सरस्वतीं
> देवयंत इत्येषाद्या । सूत्र्यते हि । प्र ब्रह्माणो अंगिरसो नक्षंत सरस्वतीं
> देवयंतो हवंते । आ. ८-११ । इति ॥

**NOTE**

> देवयंतो देवान्यष्टुं स्तोतुं च कामयमाना यजमानाः सरस्वतीमेतन्नामिकां मध्यमस्थानदेवतां हवंते । कर्मावयवत्वायाह्वयंति । तथा
> तायमाने स्तुतिभिर्हविर्भिश्च विस्तीर्णमाणेऽध्वरे यज्ञे सरस्वतीं यजंतीति
> शेषः । सुकृतः पुण्यकर्माणः सरस्वतीमह्वयंत । फलप्रदानाय ह्ययंते । यत
> एवमतः कारणात्सरस्वती देवी दाशुषे हवींषि दत्तवते यजमानाय वार्यं
> वरणीयं कर्मफलं दात् । प्रयच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is the first of the Sārasvata triad (tṛca) in the Praüga recitation of the third Chandoma day of the ten-night rite व्यूहस्य दशराश्रस्य (*vyūhasya daśarāśrasya*). It is prescribed in the sūtra: प्र ब्रह्माणो अंगिरसो नक्षंत सरस्वतीं देवयंतो हवंते (*pra brahmāṇo aṃgiraso nakṣaṃta sarasvatīṃ devayaṃto havaṃte*) (Ā. 8-11).

### Printed p. 558
*Gist (continued):* The sacrificers, wishing to worship and praise the gods (देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*)), call upon Sarasvatī, the deity of the middle region, as part of the rite. In the sacrifice (अध्वरे (*adhvare*)) that is spread out with praises and oblations they worship Sarasvatī (this is the supplied remainder). The doers of good deeds (सुकृतः (*sukṛtaḥ*)) call Sarasvatī in order that she may give the fruit. Since this is so, may the goddess Sarasvatī give the sacrificer who has offered oblations the desirable (वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)) fruit of his rite.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*)—those who desire the gods
- सरस्वतीं (*sarasvatīṃ*)—the goddess Sarasvatī
- हवंते (*havaṃte*)—they call, praying
- तायमाने (*tāyamāne*)—which is being performed at length
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- सरस्वतीं (*sarasvatīṃ*)—they worship Sarasvatī
- सुकृतः (*sukṛtaḥ*)—those who do excellent rites
- सरस्वतीं (*sarasvatīṃ*)—Sarasvatī
- अह्वयंत (*ahvayaṃta*)—they call, for the attainment of the fruit
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—the goddess Sarasvatī
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who has offered the oblation
- वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)—the desired fruit
- दात् (*dāt*)—may she give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those who desire the gods call upon the goddess Sarasvatī with prayer. In the sacrifice that is performed at length they worship Sarasvatī. Those who do excellent rites call Sarasvatī for the attainment of the fruit. May the goddess Sarasvatī give the desired fruit to the sacrificer who has offered the oblation.

##### English translation
The devout invoke Saraswati; they worship Saraswati at the strewn sacrifice ; the virtuous call upon Saraswati : may Saraswati bestow blessings upon the donor (of the oblation).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the third Chandoma day of the ten-night sacrifice called Vyūḍha, when the Praüga-śastra mantras are recited, the three Ṛks 7-9 addressed to the deity Sarasvatī, beginning "Sarasvatīṃ devayantaḥ", are to be recited. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra प्र ब्रह्माणो अंगिरसो नक्षंत सरस्वतीं देवयंतो हवंते (*pra brahmāṇo aṃgiraso nakṣaṃta sarasvatīṃ devayaṃto havaṃte*) (Ā. 8-11).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒सद्या॒स्मिन्ब॒र्हिषि॑ मादयस्वा नमी॒वा इष॒ आ धे॑ह्य॒स्मे ॥ ८ ॥

> आसद्य । अस्मिन् । बर्हिषि । मादयस्व । अनमीवाः । इषः । आ । धेहि । अस्मे इति ॥८॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सरस्वति हे देवि या त्वं सरथं पितृभिः सह समानेन रथेन युक्तं यथा
> भवति तथा ययाथ ! अस्मदीयं यज्ञं प्राप्तासि । किं कुर्वती । पितृभिः सह स्वधाभिर्हविर्लक्षणैरन्नैर्मदंती माद्यंती यज्ञं गच्छसीति संबंधः । सा त्वं बर्हिष्यस्मिन्वेदिस्तरणे यज्ञ आसद्योपविश्य मादयस्व । हविर्भिस्तृप्ता भव । आत्मानं तर्पय
> वा ! ततस्तृप्ता सती त्वमनमीवाः । अमीवा रोगः तद्वर्जितान्यारोग्यजननानीषोऽन्नान्यस्मे अस्मभ्यमा धेहि । पर्याप्तं प्रयच्छ !!

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Sarasvatī, O goddess, you who go to our sacrifice in the same chariot (सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)) with the Pitṛs, rejoicing together with the Pitṛs in the foods (स्वधाभिः (*svadhābhiḥ*)) that are the oblations — such as you are, seat yourself on this sacred grass (बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)), the strewing of the altar at this sacrifice, and be delighted. Be satisfied with the oblations, or gratify yourself. Then, being satisfied, grant us foods (इषः (*iṣaḥ*)) that are free from अमीवा (*amīvā*), which means disease, and that produce health. Give them in sufficiency."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवि (*devi*)—divine one
- सरस्वति (*sarasvati*)—O Sarasvatī
- या (*yā*)—you who
- पितृभिः (*pitṛbhiḥ*)—sitting with the Pitṛs
- स्वधाभिः (*svadhābhiḥ*)—with the oblations that are of the nature of svadhā
- मदंती (*madaṃtī*)—rejoicing
- सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)—sitting with them in one chariot
- ययाथॆ (*yayāthè*)—you go; such a one as you
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—on this
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—seat of sacred grass
- आसद्य (*āsadya*)—having sat
- मादयस्व (*mādayasva*)—be satisfied
- अनमीवाः (*anamīvāḥ*)—free from disease and the like
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us
- आ धेहि (*ā dhehi*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Sarasvatī, you who sit with the Pitṛs, rejoice in the oblations that are of the nature of svadhā, and go sitting with them in one chariot — such as you are, sit on this seat of sacred grass and be satisfied. Give us foods that are free from disease and the like.

### Printed p. 560

##### English translation
Divine Saraswati, who rides in the same chariot with the Pitris, and is delighted (along with them) by the (sacrificial) viands, seated on the sacred grass be gratified (by our offering), and grant us wholesome food.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यां त्वां सरस्वतीं पितरो हवंते आह्वयंति । कीदृशाः । दक्षिणा ॥ दक्षिणादाजित्याच् प्रत्ययः । पा. सू. ५-३-३६ ॥ दक्षिणत आगत्य यज्ञमभिनक्षमाणा अभिशो
> गच्छंतो व्याप्नुवंतः । अत्रास्मिन्यज्ञे सहस्रार्घं बहुभिः पूजनीयमुपयोज्यमिलोऽन्नस्य भागं रायो धनस्य पोषं पुष्टिं च यजमानेषु त्वं धेहि । स्थापय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Pitṛs call you, Sarasvatī. What are they like? They come from the south (दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)) to the sacrifice and approach it (अभिनक्षमाणाः (*abhinakṣamāṇāḥ*)), that is, they pervade it. In this sacrifice, establish (धेहि (*dhehi*)) among the sacrificers a portion of food (इळः (*iḷaḥ*)) that is सहस्रार्घं (*sahasrārghaṃ*), worthy of honour by many and fit for use, and the prosperity (पोषं (*poṣaṃ*)) of wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)—in the manner of circumambulation
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- अभिनक्षमाणाः (*abhinakṣamāṇāḥ*)—going round
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—the Pitṛs
- यां सरस्वतीं (*yāṃ sarasvatīṃ*)—whichever Sarasvatī
- हवंते (*havaṃte*)—they call; that Sarasvatī
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this sacrifice
- सहस्रार्घं (*sahasrārghaṃ*)—sufficient for the praise and satisfaction of many
- इळः (*iḷaḥ*)—of food
- भागं (*bhāgaṃ*)—the portion
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—the wealth
- पोषं (*poṣaṃ*)—the prosperity
- यजमानेषु (*yajamāneṣu*)—among the sacrificers
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—may she establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that Sarasvatī whom the Pitṛs, going round the sacrifice with circumambulation, call, establish (give) in this sacrifice among the sacrificers a portion of food sufficient for the praise and satisfaction of many, and wealth and prosperity.

### Printed p. 561

##### English translation
Saraswati, whom the Pitris invoke when circumambulating the sacrifice on the right, bestow upon the worshippers at this sacrifice a portion of food fit for thousands, and increase of riches.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अवभृथस्थान आपो अस्मानित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । तत आचम्याप्लवंत अपो

> शोधयंतु । तथा धृतप्पः । धृतमुदकं । तेनान्यान्सुनंतीति । तास्त्रथोक्ता आपः ।
> यद्वा । धृतप्पः । धृतं गव्यं । तेन पुनंति । तथा ब्राह्मणं । धृतेन नो धृतप्पः
> पुनंतीति तद्वै सुपूतं यद्धृतेन पूयत इति । ता आपोऽस्माङ्खंधयोदकेन
> नोऽस्माङ्खंधयंतु । हि यस्माद्देवीर्देव्यो देवनशीला आपो विश्वं सर्वं रिप्रं
> पापं प्रवहंति पुरुषसकाशात्पगमयंति । अपनयंतीति यावत् । अनंतरमाभ्योऽद्भ्य आ पूत अभिमुख्येन शुद्धः सन् स्तोताहमुदेमि । उद्दच्छामि । ऊर्ध्वं
> स्वर्गं गच्छामोत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk, "आपो अस्मान् (*āpo asmān*)", is used at the place of the avabhṛtha. It is prescribed by the sūtra: तत आचम्याप्लवंत अपो अस्मान्मातरः शुंधयंतु (*tata ācamyāplavaṃta apo asmānmātaraḥ śuṃdhayaṃtu*) (Ā. 6-13). It is also used on the tenth day at the wiping of the vapā; the sūtra is: इदमापः प्र वहतेत्येतस्याः स्थान आपो अस्मान्मातरः शुंधयंतु (*idamāpaḥ pra vahatetyetasyāḥ sthāna āpo asmānmātaraḥ śuṃdhayaṃtu*) (Ā. 8-12). The mothers (मातरः (*mātaraḥ*)) are the waters, who stand as mothers of the world; may they purify us, cleanse us by sprinkling. So too the धृतप्पः (*dhṛtappaḥ*): धृतं (*dhṛtaṃ*) is water, and they purify others with it; the waters so described. Or else धृतप्पः (*dhṛtappaḥ*) are those who purify with धृतं (*dhṛtaṃ*), the product of the cow. The Brāhmaṇa says likewise: धृतेन नो धृतप्पः पुनंतीति तद्वै सुपूतं यद्धृतेन पूयत इति (*dhṛtena no dhṛtappaḥ punaṃtīti tadvai supūtaṃ yaddhṛtena pūyata iti*). May those waters purify us with water. Because the divine waters, of a shining nature, carry away all sin (रिप्रं (*ripraṃ*)) from a man, that is, remove it, afterwards I, the praiser, purified by these waters, go up (उदेमि (*udemi*)), that is, go upward to heaven.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मातरः (*mātaraḥ*)—the mother-like
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—waters
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- शुंधयंतु (*śuṃdhayaṃtu*)—may they purify
- धृतप्पः (*dhṛtappaḥ*)—the purifying waters
- घृतेन (*ghṛtena*)—with their flow

- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पुनंतु (*punaṃtu*)—may they purify
- हि (*hi*)—for
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—the waters that are divine
- विश्वं हि (*viśvaṃ hi*)—all
- रिप्रं (*ripraṃ*)—sin
- प्रवहंति (*pravahaṃti*)—they sweep away and destroy
- आभ्यः (*ābhyaḥ*)—by these waters
- आ पूतः शुचिः (*ā pūtaḥ śuciḥ*)—I who have become purified
- उदेमि (*udemi*)—I go up to heaven

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the waters, who are like mothers, purify us. May the purifying waters make us holy by their flow. The divine waters sweep away and destroy all our sin. I, purified by these waters, go up to heaven.

##### English translation
May the maternal waters purify us; may the shedders of water purify us with the effusion; for the divine (waters) bear away all sin; I come away from them purified (to heaven).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk, "आपो अस्मान् (*āpo asmān*)", is to be recited at the avabhṛtha place. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra अचम्याप्लवंत आपो अस्मान् मातरः शुंधयंतु (*acamyāplavaṃta āpo asmān mātaraḥ śuṃdhayaṃtu*) (Ā. 6-13). It is also to be recited on the tenth day at the time of the wiping of the vapā, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra इदमापः प्र वहतेत्वेतस्या स्थान आपो अस्मान्मातरः शुंधयंतु (*idamāpaḥ pra vahatetvetasyā sthāna āpo asmānmātaraḥ śuṃdhayaṃtu*) (Ā. 8-12). **NOTE**

Mātaraḥ āpaḥ: here the waters, or the deities presiding over the waters, are described by the word मातरः (*mātaraḥ*). For just as mothers nourish and rear their children with milk and the like, these waters rear plants and the like, and nourish us (all living beings) with the food and so on obtained from them. Therefore it is natural to call the waters, whose nature is to nourish like mothers, मातरः (*mātaraḥ*), a word that shows respect.

Śuṃdhayantu: प्रोक्षणेन शोधयंतु (*prokṣaṇena śodhayaṃtu*). The assurance expressed here is that the waters should purify us by sprinkling and the like. That water purifies everything is a matter of experience. By bathing and the like we purify our body, by washing our clothes and the like, by sweeping and the like our houses and the like, by rinsing our vessels and the like. That is, water is needed to purify anything. Besides this kind of external purification, there is also inner purification inside the body by sipping water and the like, as the Taittirīya Śruti sentence declares: अपोऽश्नात्यंतरत एव मेध्यो भवति (*apo 'śnātyaṃtarata eva medhyo bhavati*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6.1.1.3).

### Printed p. 563
**Dhṛtapvaḥ**—two kinds of meaning can be given to this word. धृतमुदकं तेनान्यान् पुनंतीति । (*dhṛtamudakaṃ tenānyān punaṃtīti |*) तास्तथोक्ता आपः । (*tāstathoktā āpaḥ |*) Dhṛta means water (Ni. 2-24). Because with this water others, or other things, are purified, the first meaning is "waters that cause purification". यद्वा । (*yadvā |*) धृतं गव्यं । (*dhṛtaṃ gavyaṃ |*) तेन पुनंति । (*tena punaṃti |*) Likewise there is a Brāhmaṇa: धृतेन नो धृतप्पः पुनंतीति तद्वै सुपूतं यद्धृतेन पूयते (*dhṛtena no dhṛtappaḥ punaṃtīti tadvai supūtaṃ yaddhṛtena pūyate*) (Śa. Brā. 3-1-2-11). Or else dhṛta means ghee, the product of the cow, or ājya. It is said that they purify by smearing with it. On this point the Bhāṣyakāra has cited a Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa sentence whose meaning is that whatever thing is mixed with (smeared with, or blended with) ghee is regarded as pure.

**Viśvaṃ hi ripraṃ pravahanti devīḥ**—ripra means sin. The prayer is voiced here that the waters may carry away all our sin. On this point there is also the support of the Śruti sentence इदमापः प्रवहत यत्किंच दुरितं मयि (*idamāpaḥ pravahata yatkiṃca duritaṃ mayi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-9-8).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the day of pressing (sutya), the two ṛks beginning द्रप्सश्चस्कंद (*drapsaścaskaṃda*) are for the vipuḍ-homa. It is laid down in the sūtra: द्रप्सश्चस्कंदेति द्वाभ्यां विपुड्धोमौ हुत्वा (*drapsaścaskaṃdeti dvābhyāṃ vipuḍdhomau hutvā*) (Ā. 5.2). In the touching of spilled oblation too, this ṛk beginning द्रप्स (*drapsa*).

> इत्येषा । आहुतिर्बहिष्परिधि यदि स्कंदेत् तदानीमाग्नीध्रोऽनया जुहुयात् ।

> अत्र वाजसनेयकं । असौ ना आदित्यो द्रप्पः स दिवं च पृथिवीं च स्कंदतीमं च
> योनिमनु यश्च पूर्व इतीमं च लोकममुं चेत्येतत् समानं योनिमनु

> होत्रा इत्यसौ ना आदित्यो द्रप्पो दिशः सप्त होत्रा अमुं तदादित्यं दिक्षु
> प्रतिष्ठापयति । श. ब्रा. ७-४-१-२८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ṛk is used in this way: if an oblation falls outside the outer enclosing sticks (bahiṣparidhi), then the Āgnīdhra should offer with it. This is laid down in the sūtra, introduced with "one should touch what has fallen": द्रप्सश्चस्कंदेत्याहुतिश्चेद्बहिष्परिध्याग्नीध्र एनां जुहुयात् (*drapsaścaskaṃdetyāhutiścedbahiṣparidhyāgnīdhra enāṃ juhuyāt*) (A. 3-13)**NOTE**.

Drapsa is the juice of the Soma being pressed. It has "gone" (caskanda) with regard to the first (prathamān, that is, earlier-existing) earthly worlds and the shining (dyūn) worlds of heaven. He states this same thing: it has followed this visible yoni, the world that is the place, and that which exists before it. Common (samāna, shared) yoni is the place made up of heaven and earth; the drapsa, the Soma juice that is the vipuḍ-oblation, moves well (saṃcarantam) along it. The seven hotrāḥ are the seven who perform the vipuḍ-homa, the hotṛ and the rest; "we" offer in due order; जुहोमि (*juhomi*) stands for जुहुमः (*juhumaḥ*).

Or else: hotrāḥ is the sacrificial act performed by the seven hotṛs; after (anu) those, I, the adhvaryu, offer.

Or else: because it moves swiftly, drapsa is said to mean Āditya. That Āditya goes to earth and to heaven, taking the intermediate space as the common yoni. Having in view that Āditya who moves well, the seven hotrāḥ are the seven directions, those other than the direction in which the Sun stands; afterwards (anu) I offer. In whichever direction he stands, I give that direction as the offering-substance; that is, I establish him there. On this the Vājasaneyaka (Brāhmaṇa) says: असौ ना आदित्यो द्रप्पः स दिवं च पृथिवीं च स्कंदतीमं च योनिमनु यश्च पूर्व इतीमं च लोकममुं चेत्येतत् समानं योनिमनु पंचरंतमिति समानं हेष एतं योनिमनु संचरति द्रप्पं जुहोम्यनु सप्त होत्रा इत्यसौ ना आदित्यो द्रप्पो दिशः सप्त होत्रा अमुं तदादित्यं दिक्षु प्रतिष्ठापयति । (*asau nā ādityo drappaḥ sa divaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca skaṃdatīmaṃ ca yonimanu yaśca pūrva itīmaṃ ca lokamamuṃ cetyetat samānaṃ yonimanu paṃcaraṃtamiti samānaṃ heṣa etaṃ yonimanu saṃcarati drappaṃ juhomyanu sapta hotrā ityasau nā ādityo drappo diśaḥ sapta hotrā amuṃ tadādityaṃ dikṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati |*) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1-28).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- द्रप्सः (*drapsaḥ*)—the pressed Soma juice
- प्रथमान् (*prathamān*)—the earthly worlds, the first region
- द्यून् अनु (*dyūn anu*)—having in view the worlds of heaven
- चस्कंद (*caskaṃda*)—they flow
- इमं योनिं (*imaṃ yoniṃ*)—to the world visible here (and)
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- पूर्वः (*pūrvaḥ*)—exists from before
- तं अनु (*taṃ anu*)—having that in view, it flows
- समानं (*samānaṃ*)—common to all
- योनिं अनु संचरंतं (*yoniṃ anu saṃcaraṃtaṃ*)—flowing through all the worlds
- द्रप्सं (*drapsaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- सप्त होत्राः (*sapta hotrāḥ*)—we, the seven hotṛs
- अनु जुहोमि (*anu juhomi*)—offer in the form of an oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The pressed Soma juice flows through heaven and earth, which have existed from beginningless time. It flows through the worlds that are visible to us and those that exist from before. We, the seven hotṛs, offer in the form of an oblation the Soma juice that flows through all the worlds.

### Printed p. 565

##### English translation
The juice of the Soma has risen to the earthly and heavenly (worlds), both this visible world, and that which (existed) before (it): I offer that juice flowing through the common region (of heaven and earth) after the sacrifices (offered by the) seven (officiating priests).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the day of pressing the Soma juice in the sacrifice, this ṛk द्रप्सश्चस्कंद (*drapsaścaskaṃda*) and the ṛk after it are to be used for the vipuḍ-homa; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, द्रप्सश्चस्कंदेति द्वाभ्यां विपुड्ढोमौ हुत्वा (*drapsaścaskaṃdeti dvābhyāṃ vipuḍḍhomau hutvā*) (Ā. 5-2). In the touching of spilled oblation too, this ṛk द्रप्सः (*drapsaḥ*) is to be recited. If the oblation-substance of an offering has spilled outside the enclosing sticks (paridhi) placed on all four sides of the fire, then the priest called Āgnīdhra is to make the offering with this ṛk and touch (abhimarśana) the spilled oblation-substance; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, द्रप्सश्चस्कंदेत्याहुतिश्चेद्वहिष्परिध्याग्नीध्र एनां जुहुयात् (*drapsaścaskaṃdetyāhutiścedvahiṣparidhyāgnīdhra enāṃ juhuyāt*) (Ā. 3-13).

**Drapsaḥ**—this word has two meanings. अभिषूयमाणस्य सोमस्य रसः । (*abhiṣūyamāṇasya somasya rasaḥ |*) The juice drawn out by crushing and pressing the Soma plants with a stone is called drapsa. Or else: द्रुतगामित्वाद्द्रप्स उच्यते । (*drutagāmitvāddrapsa ucyate |*) Because he has the nature of moving swiftly, drapsa also means Āditya (the Sun).

The Bhāṣyakāra says that this ṛk can also be explained as referring to Āditya, and he cites a Vājasaneya (Śukla Yajurveda) Brāhmaṇa sentence: असौ वा आदित्यो द्रप्सः स दिवं च पृथिवीं च स्कंदतीमं च योनिमनु यश्च पूर्व इतीमं च लोकममुं चेत्येतत्समानं योनिमनु संचरंतमिति समानं ह्येष एतं योनिमनु संचरति द्रप्सं जुहोम्यनु सप्त होत्रा इत्यसौ वा आदित्यो द्रप्सो दिशः सप्त होत्रा अमुं तदादित्यं दिक्षु प्रतिष्ठापयति । (*asau vā ādityo drapsaḥ sa divaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca skaṃdatīmaṃ ca yonimanu yaśca pūrva itīmaṃ ca lokamamuṃ cetyetatsamānaṃ yonimanu saṃcaraṃtamiti samānaṃ hyeṣa etaṃ yonimanu saṃcarati drapsaṃ juhomyanu sapta hotrā ityasau vā ādityo drapso diśaḥ sapta hotrā amuṃ tadādityaṃ dikṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati |*) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1-20)**NOTE**.

यश्च द्रप्सः (*yaśca drapsaḥ*)—the swift-moving Āditya who, rising facing east, goes toward (चस्कंद (*caskaṃda*)) the earth (प्रथमान् (*prathamān*)) and this world of heaven (द्यून् इमं (*dyūn imaṃ*)); समानं योनिं (*samānaṃ yoniṃ*)—in the intermediate space, the common place; अनु संचरंतं (*anu saṃcaraṃtaṃ*)—

### Printed p. 566
who moves there; द्रप्पं (*drappaṃ*)—having in view Āditya; अनु (*anu*)—afterwards; सप्त होत्राः (*sapta hotrāḥ*)—having in view the seven directions, leaving aside, among the eight directions, the one in which the Sun stands; जुहोमि (*juhomi*)—I offer the oblation (that is, I establish Āditya there).

This very meaning is explained in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa sentence cited above.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उपस्थात् ।  
> अ॒ध्व॒योर्वा॒ परि॑ वा॒ यः प॒वित्रा॒त्तं ते॑ जुहोमि॒ मन॑सा॒  ॑

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । ते । द्रप्सः । स्कंदति । यः । ते । अंशुः । बाहुच्युतः । धिषणायाः । उपस्थात् ।  
> अध्वयोः । वा । परि । वा । यः । पवित्रात् । तं । ते । जुहोमि । मनसा ।  
> वषट्कृतं ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम ते त्वदीयो यो द्रप्पो रसः स्कंदति अधिषवणचर्मणोऽन्यत्र
> गच्छति ! यश्च ते त्वदीयोऽंशू रसादितरः सन् स्कंदति । बाहुच्युतोऽध्वर्योर्बाहुभ्यां प्रच्युतः सन् स्कंदति । यद्वा । बाहुवत्साधनभूता ग्रावाणः । तैः
> प्रच्युतोऽभिषुतः सन् धिषणायाः । धिषणेत्यधिषवणफलकनाम । प्रत्येकविवक्षय्यॆकवचनं । अधिषवणफलकयोरुपस्थात्पदेशादन्यत्र गच्छति । तथाध्वर्योर्वाभिषुण्वतोऽध्वर्योर्हस्तात्संदति । वापि वा पवित्राद्दशापवित्रात्परिस्कंदति । तं सर्वं
> द्रप्पं ते त्वदीयं रसं मनसांतःकरणेन स्तोत्रेण वा सह वषट्कृतं वषट्कारेण
> स्वाहाकारेण कृतं जुहोमि । अग्नौ प्रक्षिपामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, your drapsa, your juice, which falls (स्कंदति (*skaṃdati*)), goes elsewhere than the pressing hide. And your aṃśu, other than the juice, falls, slipping from the arms of the adhvaryu (बाहुच्युतः (*bāhucyutaḥ*))." Or else: the pressing stones are instruments like arms; released by them, pressed out, it goes elsewhere than the neighbourhood (उपस्थात् (*upasthāt*)) of the dhiṣaṇā; dhiṣaṇā is a name for the pressing board, and the singular is used because each is meant separately; thus it goes from the vicinity of the two pressing boards. Likewise it falls from the hand of the adhvaryu who is pressing; or it flows around from the pavitra, the woollen filter with fringe (दशापवित्रात् (*daśāpavitrāt*)). All that drapsa, your juice, I offer (जुहोमि (*juhomi*)), that is, cast into the fire, with the mind, that is, with the inner organ, or with a hymn of praise, and with what is made by vaṣaṭ (वषट्कृतं (*vaṣaṭkṛtaṃ*)), that is, by the vaṣaṭ-call, the svāhā-call.

- (O Soma) ते (*te*)—your
- यः द्रप्सः (*yaḥ drapsaḥ*)—which juice
- स्कंदति (*skaṃdati*)—goes out of the pressing hide and flows
- ते (*te*)—your
- यः अंशुः (*yaḥ aṃśuḥ*)—which thing in the form of a plant or the like

- बाहुच्युतः (*bāhucyutaḥ*)—goes out from the arm of the adhvaryu
- धिषणायाः (*dhiṣaṇāyāḥ*)—out from the boards of pressing
- उपस्थात् (*upasthāt*)—goes out
- अध्वर्योर्वा (*adhvaryorvā*)—is offered by the adhvaryu
- वा (*vā*)—or
- पवित्रात् (*pavitrāt*)—going out from the daśā-pavitra
- परि (*pari*)—flows
- तं (*taṃ*)—that
- ते (*te*)—your juice
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with praise
