> परं । मृत्यो इति । अनु । परा । इहि । पंथां । यः । ते । स्वः । इतरः । देवयानात् ।  
> चक्षुष्मते । शृण्वते । ते । ब्रवीमि । मा । नः । प्रजां । रीरिषः । मा । उत ।  
> वीरान् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मृत्यो सर्वेषां मारकैतन्नामक देव परमन्यं पंथां पंथानमन्वानुपूर्व्येण परेहि । पराङ्मुखो गच्छ । यजमानादिति शेषः । कोऽसौ पंथाः ।
> ते तव स्वः स्वभूतः देवयानात् । देवा अनेन मार्गण गच्छंतीति देवयानो
> देवमार्गः । तस्मादितरो यः पंथास्तं प्रगच्छ । न केवलमतः परागच्छ आपि तु
> चक्षुष्मते दर्शनवते शृण्वते सर्वं । अप्रतिहतसर्वेंद्रियविज्ञानायेत्यर्थः । ते
> तुभ्यं ब्रवीमि कथयामि : नोऽस्माकं प्रजां दुहितृदौहित्रात्मिकां मा रिरिषः ।
> मा हिंसीः । उतापि च वीरान्पुत्रपौत्रादीन्मा हिंसीः । तत्परागमनेन रक्षेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mṛtyu, the god of that name who slays all, go away in order, turning away, by another path—from the sacrificer, is the understood supplement. Which path? Your own, देवयानात् (*devayānāt*): the gods go by this way, hence devayāna is the path of the gods; go along the path other than that. Not only go away: to you who have sight and hearing—that is, whose knowledge through all the senses is unobstructed—I say it. Do not harm our offspring, daughters and daughters' sons; and do not harm our heroes, sons, grandsons and the like. Protect them by your going away, is the sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मृत्यो (*mṛtyo*)—O Mṛtyu
- परं पंथां अनु (*paraṃ paṃthāṃ anu*)—taking another path
- परेहि (*parehi*)—go away, turned away
- ते (*te*)—your
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—own
- देवयानात् (*devayānāt*)—than the path of movement of the gods
- इतरः (*itaraḥ*)—different
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whichever path there is, follow that
- चक्षुष्मते (*cakṣuṣmate*)—possessing eyes
- शृण्वते (*śṛṇvate*)—possessing ears
- ते (*te*)—to you
- ब्रवीमि (*bravīmi*)—I say
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- प्रजां (*prajāṃ*)—sons and the like
- मा रिरिषः (*mā ririṣaḥ*)—do not harm
- उत (*uta*)—and
- वीरान् (*vīrān*)—heroic sons and the like
- मा (*mā*)—do not harm

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mṛtyu, take another path and turn away. Go following your own path, different from the path of the gods. I pray to you who have eyes and ears. Do not harm our sons and the like, and do not harm heroic sons and the like.

##### English translation
Depart, Mrityu, by a different path : by that which is your own, and distinct from the path of the gods ; I speak to you who have eyes, who have ears : do no harm to our offspring, nor to our male progeny.

### Printed p. 597

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the word mṛtyu, Yāska says: मृत्युः । मृत्युर्मारयतीति सतः । मृतं च्यावयतीति ना शतबलाक्षो मौद्गल्यः ॥ तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*mṛtyuḥ | mṛtyurmārayatīti sataḥ | mṛtaṃ cyāvayatīti nā śatabalākṣo maudgalyaḥ ‖ tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 11-6)

He is named Mṛtyu because he kills living beings. Or, because he removes the dead, that is, the soul, from that place to the other world, he is named Mṛtyu: this is the view of the sage Śatabalākṣa, son of Mudgala. The Ṛk containing this word is cited here:

परं मृत्यो अनु परेहि पंथां यस्ते स्व इतरो देवयानात् । चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते ते ब्रवीमि मा नः प्रजां रीरिषो मोत वीरान् ॥ (*paraṃ mṛtyo anu parehi paṃthāṃ yaste sva itaro devayānāt | cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmi mā naḥ prajāṃ rīriṣo mota vīrān ‖*)

परं मृत्यो ध्रुवं मृत्यो ध्रुवं परेहि मृत्यो कथितं तेन मृत्यो मृतं च्यावयते भवति मृत्यो मदेर्वा मुदेर्वा ॥ (*paraṃ mṛtyo dhruvaṃ mṛtyo dhruvaṃ parehi mṛtyo kathitaṃ tena mṛtyo mṛtaṃ cyāvayate bhavati mṛtyo madervā mudervā ‖*) (Ni. 11-7)

O Mṛtyu, depart from here certainly; O Mṛtyu, depart, depart. O Mṛtyu, the man whom you have brought to death belongs to you alone. Taking him, depart by your own path, the pitṛyāṇa. Others go to the other world by the devayāna path. O god Mṛtyu, you have eyes to see and ears to hear. What I say to such as you is: do not harm our offspring, that is, sons and the like, and do not harm our people who are heroes. The word mṛtyu may be derived from the root mad or from the root mud: this is the intention of the etymology.

In this Ṛk the seer praises the deity Mṛtyu. Mṛtyu means one who destroys, who kills all living beings. When the measure of life appointed for men and other beings is complete, he makes them die by many causes such as disease and accidents. The seer also indicates here that there is a separate path by which the spirits of the dead go to reach the world of Mṛtyu. The path on which the gods travel is called devayāna. The other path than this devayāna is the pitṛyāṇa, the path by which the Fathers go to the other world. The seer describes this path as the own path of Mṛtyu (Yama), because by this very path the Fathers and the spirits of the dead

### Printed p. 598

go to and reach the world of Mṛtyu; therefore the seer calls it Mṛtyu's own path. Depart by that very path; and the prayer is stated here: do not harm us, nor our kinsfolk, sons, grandsons, daughters, daughters' sons and the like, nor our heroic warriors. For the words चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते (*cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate*) in this Ṛk the commentator explains अप्रतिहतसर्वेंद्रियविज्ञानाय (*apratihatasarveṃdriyavijñānāya*): that all the senses of this Mṛtyu, eye, ear and the rest, have power and capacity that no one can obstruct. Moreover the use of the words चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते (*cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate*) points to a kind of hidden meaning. In whatever place in the world any creature dies, Mṛtyu sees it at once, and at once hears of it through his spies and knows. That is, it is to be understood that this use of words conveys that the matter of the dead is known to him immediately.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मृ॒त्योः प॒दं यो॒पयं॑तो॒ यदैत॒ द्राघी॑य॒ आयुः॑

> दधानाः ।  
> आप्यायमानाः । प्रजया । धनेन । शुद्धाः । पूताः । भवत । यज्ञियासः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मृतस्य ज्ञातयः मृत्योः परागच्छतस्तस्य पदं पद्यतेऽस्मिन्निति पदं
> पितृयाणः । तं योपयंतो विमोहयंतः परिवर्जयंतो यद्यस्मादैत
> देवयानीयपथा गतवंतः तस्माद्राघीयो दीर्घतरमायुर्जीवनं प्रतरं
> प्रकृष्टतरमत्यर्थं दधाना धारयंतो भवथ । किंच हे यज्ञियासो यज्ञार्हा
> यज्ञसंपादिनो यजमानाः प्रजया पुत्रपौत्रादिकया धनेन गवाश्वादिकेन

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O kinsmen of the dead: of Mṛtyu who is going away—पदं (*padaṃ*) is that in which one goes, the pitṛyāṇa path. Avoiding it, bewildering it, since you have gone by the devayāna path, therefore you will be bearing a longer life, much more excellent, in the extreme. Moreover, O sacrificers, worthy of sacrifice, performers of sacrifice, with offspring such as sons and grandsons, with wealth such as cattle and horses ….

### Printed p. 599

> चाप्यायमाना वर्धमानाः संतः शुद्ध जन्मांतरसंचितदुरितक्षयाच्चुद्ध भवत ।
> पूता वर्तमानजन्मोपचितदुरितक्षयाच्च पूता भवत ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मृत्योः (*mṛtyoḥ*)—of death (O relatives of the dead man)
- पदं (*padaṃ*)—the place
- योपयंतः (*yopayaṃtaḥ*)—abandoning
- यत् (*yat*) यस्मात् (*yasmāt*) ऐत (*aita*)—because you travel by the path of the gods; as its result
- द्राघीयः (*drāghīyaḥ*)—long
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life-span
- प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*)—most excellently
- दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)—having obtained
- यज्ञियासः (*yajñiyāsaḥ*)—O sacrificers, performers of the sacrifice
- प्रजया (*prajayā*)—with progeny
- धनेन (*dhanena*)—with wealth
- आप्यायमानाः (*āpyāyamānāḥ*)—having grown
- शुद्धाः (*śuddhāḥ*)—free of sin
- पूताः (*pūtāḥ*)—free of stain
- भवत (*bhavata*)—you become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O relatives of the dead man, you abandon the place of death, and as the result of travelling by the path of the gods you obtain a long life-span most excellently. O sacrificers, joined with progeny and wealth, you become increased, free of sin and free of stain.

##### English translation
If, avoiding the path of death, you go (on the path of the gods), assuming a longer and better life, (my friends) then may you, (O, sacrificers), diligent in sacrifice, enriched with progeny and affluence, be cleansed and pure.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the seer speaks to the dead man's kinsmen, that is, his relatives. In this Ṛk and some following ones, grief for the dead man is expressed: he has left us and gone from this world. We who still live should not fall to death as he did, but live long, growing through sons, grandsons and so on, and through wealth and the like — this is the sense expressed. Those who still live, seeing the dead and grieving, fearing that this fate may come to them too, pray that all may live long without falling under death's power; this prayer is stated in this Ṛk and the next three.

### Printed p. 600
The sense of the Ṛk, phrase by phrase: मृत्योः पदं योपयंतः यत् ऐत (*mṛtyoḥ padaṃ yopayaṃtaḥ yat aita*)—O kinsmen of the dead, Death has taken your relative to his own world by his own path of the Fathers. But you who live, do not go toward the Fathers' path, the path of Death. That path is appointed only for the dead. Leave it and take refuge in the path of the gods. For द्राघीय आयुः प्रतरं दधानाः (*drāghīya āyuḥ prataraṃ dadhānāḥ*)—obtain long life so as to live a long time. Why should you who are long-lived have a liking for the Fathers' path, the path of the dead?
यज्ञियासः प्रजया धनेन आप्यायमानाः शुद्धाः पूता भवत (*yajñiyāsaḥ prajayā dhanena āpyāyamānāḥ śuddhāḥ pūtā bhavata*)—O kinsmen, performing sacrifices and the like, growing through sons, grandsons and offspring and through wealth, released from all sins done in former births and in this one, live as pure ones: this assurance is stated here.
Because one kinsman has died, the other relatives need not suffer long in grief. His death came from the fruit of his own deeds. What use is it for you who live to grieve in vain? Strive to live long. May your span of life increase. Performing sacrifices, and as the fruit of those good deeds growing day by day through sons, grandsons and wealth, shed your sins and live happily: this is the main sense of this Ṛk.

> व्यावृत्ता भवंतु । एते न म्रियंतामिति भावः । किंचाद्यास्मिन्निने नोऽस्माकमशौचे विसृष्टे देवहूतिः देवानामाह्वानं यत्र स देवहूतिः पितृमेधाख्यो
> यज्ञो भद्रा कल्याणोऽभूत् । भवतु । तत उत्तरं वयं प्रांचः प्राज्मुखांचना अगाम । गच्छेम । प्रत्यंच इति भावः । नृतये नर्तनाय कर्मणि गात्रविक्षेपाय । स्वकर्मानुष्ठानायेति भावः । हसाय हसनाय पुत्रादिभिः सह क्रीडनाय ।
> कीदृशा वयं । द्राघीय आयुः प्रतरं दधानाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Pitṛmedha rite the attendants go back turned round (to the left), reciting *ime jīvā vi mṛtaiḥ*; and it is prescribed in a sūtra: इमे जीवा वि मृतैरिति सन्यावृतो व्रजंति (*ime jīvā vi mṛtairiti sanyāvṛto vrajaṃti*), Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-499. These living men, in relation to the dead — fathers and others — should turn away from them; the sense is, let these not die. Further, today, with our impurity (of death) discharged, the sacrifice called Pitṛmedha, in which the gods are invoked (देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*)), is to be auspicious. After that we go forward (प्रांचः (*prāṃcaḥ*)), facing east, that is, not backwards. नृतये (*nṛtaye*) means for dancing, for the movement of the limbs in action, that is, for performing our own rites. हसाय (*hasāya*) means for laughter, for playing with sons and others. What are we like? Possessing a longer and better life-span.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इमे जीवाः (*ime jīvāḥ*)—these living men
- मृत्यैः (*mṛtyaiḥ*)—more than the dead, fathers and others
- नि आ अववृत्रन् (*ni ā avavṛtran*)—may they live separately
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*)—the sacrifice called Pitṛmedha
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—auspicious
- अभूत् (*abhūt*)—may it be
- प्राज्ञाः (*prājñāḥ*)—facing the east
- अगाम (*agāma*)—let us go
- नृतये (*nṛtaye*)—for dancing
- हसाय (*hasāya*)—for laughing
- द्राघीयः (*drāghīyaḥ*)—very long
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life-span
- प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*)—most excellently
- दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)—we who have obtained, let us set out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May these living men live apart from the dead fathers and others. Today may our sacrifice called Pitṛmedha be auspicious. Let us go facing east. Let us be those who have obtained a very long life-span most excellently, for dancing and for a joyful life.

##### English translation
May those who are living remain separate from the dead : may our invocation of the gods to-day be successful : let us go forward to dancing and laughter, assuming a longer and better life.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the funeral rite called Pitṛmedha, the kinsmen return from that place reciting this Ṛk इमे जीवाः वि मृत्यैः (*ime jīvāḥ vi mṛtyaiḥ*), as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra इमे जीवा वि मृत्यैंति सव्यावृतो व्रजंति (*ime jīvā vi mṛtyaiṃti savyāvṛto vrajaṃti*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-4-9). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 602
In this Ṛk too the duty of the kinsmen performing the last rites for the dead man is explained.
इमे जीवाः मृत्यैः वि अववृत्रन् (*ime jīvāḥ mṛtyaiḥ vi avavṛtran*)—Since the last rites for the dead fathers and others have been completed in the burial ground, let the dead man's kinsmen who are alive leave this burial ground and return, facing their homes.
अद्य नः देवहूतिः भत्रा अभूत् (*adya naḥ devahūtiḥ bhatrā abhūt*)—Since the last rite we perform today has ended, our impurity of death is removed. Therefore may there be auspiciousness for us in the sacrifice called Pitṛmedha that we perform for the gods and the Fathers. **NOTE**
प्रांचो आगाम नृतये हसाय (*prāṃco āgāma nṛtaye hasāya*)—When this rite is over, freed from grief for the dead man, let us return from this burial ground and go facing east to our homes, so as to be active in our own rites, and to pass the time with sons and others in play and amusement.
द्राघीयः आयुः प्रतरं दधानाः (*drāghīyaḥ āyuḥ prataraṃ dadhānāḥ*)—Let us go from this place toward our homes, in order to obtain a long life and live long.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मं जी॒वेभ्यः॑ परि॒धिं द॑धामि॒ मैषां॒ नु गा॒दप॑रो॒ अर्थ॑मे॒तं ।  
> श॒तं जी॑वंतु श॒रदः॑ पुरू॒चीरं॒तर्मृ॒त्युं द॑धतां॒ पर्व॑तेन ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमं । जीवेभ्यः । परिधिं । दधामि । मा । एषां । नु । गात् । अपरः । अर्थं ।  
> एतं ।  
> शतं । जीवंतु । शरदः । पुरूचीः । अंतः । मृत्युं । दधतां पर्वतेन ॥४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आनया जीवरक्षार्थं पाषाणं परिधिरूपेण स्थापयंति । जीवेभ्यो
> जीवद्भ्यः पुत्रपौत्रादिभ्यस्तेषां रक्षणार्थमेवं परिधिं मृत्योः परिधानभूतं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk they set up a stone as a boundary-wall (परिधि (*paridhi*)) to protect the living. For the living, sons, grandsons and the rest, to protect them, I set this boundary, a stone that serves as a barrier against Death,

### Printed p. 603

> पाषाणं दधामि । निदधामि । तत एषां जीवतां मध्येऽपरोऽन्य एतमिमनुर्थं ॥
> आर्तॆरिदं रूपं ॥ गंतव्यं मरणाख्यं मार्गं नु क्षिप्रं मा गात् । मा गच्छतु ।
> एतदर्थं परिधिं स्थापयामीति संबंधः । किंच पुरूचीर्बह्वंचना बहुगमना:
> शतं शरद एतत्संख्याकान्वर्षान्जीवंतु । स्वस्वप्राणान्धारयंतु । तथा पर्वतेन
> शिलोच्चयेन मृत्युं सर्वेषां मारकमेतन्नामकमंतर्दधतां । अंतर्हितं
> कुर्वंतु । यथा नागच्छति तथा कुर्वतामित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I place it. Then, among these living, let no other go quickly upon this path called death, the "goal" (अर्थं (*arthaṃ*), from the root ऋ (*ṛ*), to go), the way to be travelled; I set the boundary for this purpose — such is the connection. Further, पुरूचीः (*purūcīḥ*) means going many ways: let them live a hundred autumns, that many years, and hold their own breaths. And let them put out of sight, by a mountain (पर्वतेन (*parvatena*)), a heap of stone, Death, the slayer of all, who is so named; let them make it hidden, that is, act so that he does not come.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जीवेभ्यः (*jīvebhyaḥ*)—for the protection of those who live
- इमं परिधिं (*imaṃ paridhiṃ*)—this circle of stone
- दधामि (*dadhāmi*)—I construct
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—among these living men
- अपरः (*aparaḥ*)—anyone at all
- एतं अर्थं (*etaṃ arthaṃ*)—this path of death
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- मा गात् (*mā gāt*)—let him not reach
- पुरूचीः (*purūcīḥ*)—very long
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—a hundred in number
- शरदः (*śaradaḥ*)—autumns
- जीवंतु (*jīvaṃtu*)—let them live
- पर्वतेन (*parvatena*)—by masses of stone
- मृत्युं (*mṛtyuṃ*)—Death
- अंतः दधतां (*aṃtaḥ dadhatāṃ*)—let them hide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the protection of the living I construct this circle of stone. Let none of these living men reach this path of death. Let them live for very long, a hundred autumns (a hundred years). By masses of stone let them hide Death.

##### English translation
I erect this circle (of stones) for (the protection of) the living, that none other of them may approach this path; may they live a hundred years, occupied by many holy works, and keep death hidden by this mound.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It is the custom to recite this Ṛk while placing small stones around as a boundary, as a protective binding, so that Death may not approach the living kinsmen. In worldly practice, to protect a house, or fields, from wild beasts and from other people, a wall or a fence is put around. In the same way, it appears that the custom arose of making such an enclosure of stones around, so that the deity Death should not come and carry off others among the living. Although Death cannot be prevented from coming in this way, it is understood that people in former times held such a superstition.

### Printed p. 604
Many such precautionary measures and customs are still found among forest peoples of some countries. After one of them has died, it is natural to follow such a precaution so that this fate may not come to any of the rest.
इमं जीवेभ्यः परिधिं दधामि (*imaṃ jīvebhyaḥ paridhiṃ dadhāmi*)—So that Death may not approach us who remain alive and our own people, sons, grandsons and others, and to protect them, I set around them this boundary in the form of stones, that is, a kind of enclosure all around. For that I place stones around and prevent Death from coming here.
एषां अपरः एतं अर्थं नु मा गात् (*eṣāṃ aparaḥ etaṃ arthaṃ nu mā gāt*)—Because one man among us has now died, we are in very great sorrow. Therefore let no other one among us quickly follow the path of Death, that is, fall to death. For this I make this protection. For the word अर्थं (*arthaṃ*) in this sentence the commentator explains: आर्तेरिदं रूपं गंतव्यं मरणाख्यं मार्गं (*ārteridaṃ rūpaṃ gaṃtavyaṃ maraṇākhyaṃ mārgaṃ*); the word अर्थं (*arthaṃ*), formed from the root ऋ (*ṛ*) meaning "go", means "path".
शतं जीवंतु शरदः पुरूची (*śataṃ jīvaṃtu śaradaḥ purūcī*)—Let those who now remain alive, moving about strong and sturdy, live a hundred years. Here the word शरदः (*śaradaḥ*) indicates a year. Although the word शरत् (*śarat*) generally means the autumn season or the cold season, since autumn comes only once in a year, it is the custom in the Vedas to use the word शरत् (*śarat*) when indicating a period of one year. Therefore here शतं शरदः (*śataṃ śaradaḥ*) is said, "a hundred years". Since the full limit of a man's life is said to be a hundred years, when it says "let them live a hundred years" the sense is that a man should live until his span of life is complete.
पर्वतेन मृत्युं अंतः दधतां (*parvatena mṛtyuṃ aṃtaḥ dadhatāṃ*)—पर्वत (*parvata*) means a heap of stones, a mass of rocks. The sense is that this enclosure in the form of a boundary has been made, using many stones, to prevent Death from staying there and coming out.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथाहा॑न्यनुपू॒र्वं भवं॑ति॒ यथ॑ ऋ॒तव॑ ऋ॒तुभि॒र्यंति॑  ॒
> साधु ।

### Printed p. 605

> यथा न पूर्वमपरो जहात्येवा धातरायूंषि कल्पय्यैषां ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । अहानि । अनुपूर्वं । भवंति । यथा । ऋतवः । ऋतुभिः । यंति । साधु ।  
> यथा । न । पूर्वं । अपरः । जहाति । एव । धातः । आयूंषि । कल्पय । एषां ॥५॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यथा येन प्रकारेणाहान्यहोरात्रात्मकानि दिनान्यनुपूर्वं पूर्वंपूर्वमनुक्रमेण भवंति परिवर्तंते । यथा चर्तवो वसंतादय ऋतुभिः सह
> साधु शोभनमविपर्यासेन यंति गच्छंति । यथा च पूर्वं पूर्वकालीनं
> पितरमपरोऽर्वाक्कालीनः पुत्रो न जहाति न परित्यजति पूर्वमरणेन ॥ एवैवं
> तेनैवोक्तप्रकारेण हे धातः सर्वॆषां धारयितरेतन्नामक देव विषामस्मत्कुलीनानां जीवानामायूंषि जीवनानि कल्पय । समर्थय ! कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains: just as the days, consisting of day and night, come one after another in succession and revolve; just as the seasons, spring and the rest, move well and without disorder together with the other seasons; and just as the later-born son does not abandon his earlier-born father by dying before him; even so, O Dhātṛ, sustainer of all, grant (कल्पय (*kalpaya*)) the life-spans of these people of our family, that is, make them fit and complete.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धातः (*dhātaḥ*)—O Creator
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- अहानि (*ahāni*)—the days that consist of day and night
- अनुपूर्वं भवंति (*anupūrvaṃ bhavaṃti*)—undergo change in one and the same order
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- ऋतवः (*ṛtavaḥ*)—the seasons, spring and the rest
- ऋतुभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ*)—with the other seasons
- साधु (*sādhu*)—with excellent change
- यंति (*yaṃti*)—move on
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*)—the father of the earlier time
- अपरः (*aparaḥ*)—the son of the later time
- न जहाति (*na jahāti*)—does not leave but follows
- एव (*eva*)—in the same manner
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of those living here
- आयूषि (*āyūṣi*)—the life-spans
- कल्पय (*kalpaya*)—fashion

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Creator, as the days consisting of day and night change in one and the same order, as the seasons, spring and the rest, move in excellent succession with the other seasons, and as the son of a later time follows the father of an earlier time without leaving him, in the same way fashion the life-spans of those who live here.

### Printed p. 606

##### English translation
As days pass along in succession; as seasons are duly followed by seasons; as the successor does not abandon his predecessor, so, Dhatri' support the lives of these (my kinsmen).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यथा अहानि अनुपूर्वं भवंति यथा ऋतवः ऋतुभिः यंति साधु (*yathā ahāni anupūrvaṃ bhavaṃti yathā ṛtavaḥ ṛtubhiḥ yaṃti sādhu*)—After one day passes, another day comes. The seasons likewise come in a changing order: after summer the rainy season, after the rainy season the cold season, one becoming the next. That is, time goes on unbroken and continuous. However many years we live, the change of days and seasons keeps going throughout our lifetime. This is natural.

यथा पूर्वं अपरः न जहाति (*yathā pūrvaṃ aparaḥ na jahāti*)—Among the people of a family the elders are older in age, the younger ones are younger. It is natural for the very aged to die. Those still younger live long and die afterwards. This too is natural. But it is not natural that the younger, that is sons, grandsons and the like (children, grandchildren), die while the elders, that is the father and others, are still alive. That is contrary to the rule. Therefore the prayer is voiced here that, against the order of the world, sons and others may not die before their parents.

एव धातः एषां आयूंषि कल्पय (*eva dhātaḥ eṣāṃ āyūṃṣi kalpaya*)—Therefore, O Dhātṛ, that is, O regulator of the universe, fashion the measure of life of each of those now living so that sons and others do not meet death before fathers and others. The seer prays to Dhātṛ, regulator of the world, to fashion the lives of all of us who are alive according to our ages, so that, against the way of the world, the younger do not die before the elders.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ रो॑ह॒तायु॑र्ज॒रसं॑ वृणा॒ना अ॑नुपू॒र्वं यत॑माना॒ यति॒  
> ष्ठ ।  
> इ॒ह त्वष्टा॑ सु॒जनि॑मा स॒जोषा॑ दी॒र्घमायुः॑ करति जी॒वसे॑  
> वः ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 607

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । रोहत । आयुः । जरसं । वृणानाः । अनुपूर्वं । यतमानाः । यति । स्थ ।  
> इह । त्वष्टा । सुजनिमा । सजोषाः । दीर्घं । आयुः । करति । जीवसे । वः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मृतस्य स्वजनाः पुत्रपौत्रादयः जरसं जरां वृणानाः संभजमाना
> यूयमायुर्जीवनमा रोहत। अधितिष्ठत । अनुपूर्वमानुपूर्व्येण । अव्ययाभावः । पूर्वो जैष्ठः । जैष्ठानुपूर्वा यतमानाः प्रयत्नं कुर्वंतो
> यूयं यति स्थ यत्संख्याका भवथ ॥ यच्छब्दाच्छांदसो डतिः ॥ सुजनिमा
> शोभनजननस्त्वष्टैतन्नामको देवः सजोषा भवद्धिः संगतः सन्निहास्मिन्कर्मणि
> प्रवृत्तानां वो युष्माकं जीवसे जीवनाय दीर्घं प्रभूतमायुः करति ।
> करोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O kinsmen of the dead man, sons, grandsons and the rest: choosing (वृणानाः (*vṛṇānāḥ*)) old age, that is, attaining it, mount (आ रोहत (*ā rohata*)) life, that is, take your stand on it. अनुपूर्वं (*anupūrvaṃ*) is "in due order" (an avyayībhāva compound): the eldest first, in order of seniority. Striving, making effort, you are यति स्थ (*yati stha*), that is, you are of whatever number you may be; the डति (*ḍati*) affix is Vedic. Tvaṣṭṛ, the god of that name, of good birth (सुजनिमा (*sujanimā*)), united with you (सजोषा (*sajoṣā*)), here in this rite, for the life of you who are engaged in it, shall make a long, abundant life.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O kinsmen of the dead man) यति स्थ (*yati stha*)—however many of you there may be
- जरसं (*jarasaṃ*)—old age
- वृणानाः (*vṛṇānāḥ*)—until you attain
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life
- आ रोहत (*ā rohata*)—take your stand on
- अनुपूर्वं (*anupūrvaṃ*)—in keeping with your ages
- यतमानाः (*yatamānāḥ*)—be engaged in rites
- सुजनिमा (*sujanimā*)—of excellent birth
- त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*)—the god Tvaṣṭṛ
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—joining with you
- इह (*iha*)—in this rite
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—for life
- दीर्घं (*dīrghaṃ*)—long
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life-span
- करति (*karati*)—let him make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O kinsmen of the dead man, however many of you there are, take your stand on life until you reach old age. Be engaged in rites in keeping with your ages. May the god Tvaṣṭṛ, of excellent birth, joining with you in this rite, make a long life-span for your living.

##### English translation
(You kinsmen of the dead man), choosing c age, attain length of life, striving one after the other; how many you may be: may Twashtri, the creator of good races of men, being at one (with you), grant you (busy) at this (sacrifice), a long life.

### Printed p. 608

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The seer here explains and prays, in another way, the very matter stated in the latter half of the previous Ṛk. O kinsmen and relatives of the dead man, you,

आ रोहत आयुः जरसं वृणानाः (*ā rohata āyuḥ jarasaṃ vṛṇānāḥ*)—here आयुः जरसं (*āyuḥ jarasaṃ*) means the measure of life that runs on until the body wears out. Carry on your life until then, that is, live long.

अनुपूर्वं यतमानाः यति स्थ (*anupūrvaṃ yatamānāḥ yati stha*)—there is an order in living long. Among those now alive, that is, among the dead man's kinsmen, there are many, and their ages vary. Some may be sixty or seventy years old, some forty or fifty, some twenty or thirty, and some merely boys. Since ages differ thus, even if all live long according to the rule of the world, those of greater age die first, and afterwards those younger than they, having lived the length of their own span, should die. That is, first the elders, then the younger ones should die. To leave this order and for the younger to die before the elders is unnatural. Live according to the rule of the world so that this does not happen. In this matter the seer prays that the god Tvaṣṭṛ (or Tvaṣṭṛ may be understood here simply as the regulator of the universe), cooperating with you, may increase the measure of your lives so that you live a long time.

> अ॒न॒श्रवो॑ऽनमी॒नावाः सु॒रत्ना॒ आ रो॑हंतु॒ जन॑यो॒ योनि॒मग्रे॑ ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 609

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अविधवाः । धवः पतिः । अविगतपतिकाः । जीवद्वर्तृका इत्यर्थः । सुपत्निः
> शोभनपतिका इमा नारीर्नार्य आंजनेन सर्वतोऽंजनसाधनेन सर्पिषा घृतेनाक्तनेत्राः सत्यः सं विशंतु । स्वगृहान्द्रविशंतु । तथानश्रवोऽश्रुवर्जिता आरुदत्योऽनमीवाः । अमीवा रोगः । तद्वर्जिताः मानसदुःखवर्जिता इत्यर्थः । सुरत्नाः शोभनधनसहिता जनयः । जनयंत्यपत्यमिति जनयो भार्याः । ता अग्रे
> सर्वेषां प्रथमत एव योनिं गृहमा रोहंतु । आगच्छंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अविधवाः (*avidhavāḥ*): धवः (*dhavaḥ*) is the husband; they are women whose husbands have not departed, that is, whose husbands are alive. सुपत्निः (*supatniḥ*): having good husbands. These women, their eyes anointed all round with आंजनेन सर्पिषा (*āṃjanena sarpiṣā*) (ghee as the means of anointing), shall enter (सं विशंतु (*saṃ viśaṃtu*)) their own houses. Likewise अनश्रवः (*anaśravaḥ*), free of tears, not weeping; अनमीवाः (*anamīvāḥ*): अमीवा (*amīvā*) is disease, so free of it, that is, free of mental sorrow. सुरत्नाः (*suratnāḥ*): possessed of fine wealth. जनयः (*janayaḥ*): wives, so called because they bear offspring. Let them first of all, before everyone, ascend (आ रोहंतु (*ā rohaṃtu*)), that is, come to, the योनिं (*yoniṃ*), the house.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अविधवाः (*avidhavāḥ*)—those who have the marks of wedlock
- सुपत्निः (*supatniḥ*)—those who have excellent husbands
- इमाः नारीः (*imāḥ nārīḥ*)—these women
- आंजनेन (*āṃjanena*)—with collyrium
- सर्पिषा (*sarpiṣā*)—adorning themselves with kajal
- सं विशंतु (*saṃ viśaṃtu*)—let them enter the houses
- अनश्रवः (*anaśravaḥ*)—without tears
- अनमीवाः (*anamīvāḥ*)—free of disease
- सुरत्नाः (*suratnāḥ*)—having fine ornaments
- जनयः (*janayaḥ*)—wives
- अग्रे (*agre*)—before all
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—the house
- आ रोहंतु (*ā rohaṃtu*)—let them enter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let women who have the marks of wedlock and excellent husbands adorn themselves with kajal mixed with collyrium and enter the houses. Let wives, without tears, free of disease and with fine ornaments, enter the house before all others.

##### English translation
Let these women who are not widows, who have good husbands, enter (anointed) with unguent and butter. Let women without tears, without sorrow, and decorated with jewels, first proceed to the house,

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Up to now the seer has spoken in general of the dead man's kinsmen and friends; now in this Ṛk he takes up the women and how they should behave, and in the next Ṛk the dead man's wife.

अविधवाः सुपत्नीः इमाः नारीः आंजनेन सर्पिषा सं विशंतु (*avidhavāḥ supatnīḥ imāḥ nārīḥ āṃjanena sarpiṣā saṃ viśaṃtu*)—धवः (*dhavaḥ*) means husband; विधवा (*vidhavā*) means a woman without a husband, that is, one who has lost her husband by his death.

### Printed p. 610
अविधवाः (*avidhavāḥ*) means those who are not women who have lost their husbands, that is, wives of living men. सुपत्निः (*supatniḥ*) means शोभनपतिकाः (*śobhanapatikāḥ*), those who have excellent husbands, wives of excellent men. Therefore these women, not widows and wives of excellent men, should give up grieving for this dead man who is their relative, adorn themselves with ghee and other anointing substances (kajal, black), and enter their own houses. This is the sense of the sentence. The seer speaks this sentence and the sentence in the latter half of this Ṛk to women who have followed the dead body of a relative (father, brother or other kinsman) to the burial ground and are grieving.

अनश्रवः अनमीवाः सुरत्नाः जनयः योनिं अग्रे आ रोहंतु (*anaśravaḥ anamīvāḥ suratnāḥ janayaḥ yoniṃ agre ā rohaṃtu*)—Let these women stop weeping with tears, reduce the surge of sorrow in the mind, that is, restrain mental grief as far as possible, then, adorned with fine jewellery, enter their own houses before the men. That is, among the kinsmen and relatives returned from the burial ground, the women should enter the house first, and afterwards the men. This is the sense.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उदी॑र्ष्व नार्य॒भि जी॑वलो॒कं ग॒तासु॑मे॒तमुप॑ शेष॒ एहि॑ ।  
> ह॒स्त॒ग्रा॒भस्य॑ दिधि॒षोस्तवे॒दं पत्यु॑र्जनि॒त्वम॒भि सं ब॑भूथ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ईर्ष्व । नारि । अभि । जीवलोकं । गतअसुं । एतं । उप । शेषे । आ । इहि ।  
> हस्तग्राभस्य । दिधिषोः । तव । इदं । पत्युः । जनित्वं । अभि । सं । बभूथ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवरादिकः प्रेतपत्नीमुदीर्घ नारीत्यनया भर्तृसकाशादुत्थापयेत् ।
> सूत्रितं च । तामुत्थापयेद्देवरः पतिस्थानीयोंतेवासी जरद्दासो वोदीर्घ
> नार्यभि जीवलोकं । आ. गृ- ४-२-१८ । इति ॥
> हे नारि मृतस्य पत्नि जीवलोकं जीवानां पुत्रपौत्रादीनां लोकं
> स्थानं गृहमभिलक्ष्योदीर्ष्व । अस्मात्सा नादुत्तिष्ठ ॥ ईर गतौ आदादिकः ॥ गता-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

A brother-in-law or other such person shall raise the dead man's wife from beside her husband with this verse, *udīrgha nāri*. It is laid down in a sūtra: तामुत्थापयेद्देवरः पतिस्थानीयोंतेवासी जरद्दासो वोदीर्घ नार्यभि जीवलोकं । आ. गृ- ४-२-१८ । इति॥ (*tāmutthāpayeddevaraḥ patisthānīyoṃtevāsī jaraddāso vodīrgha nāryabhi jīvalokaṃ | ā. gṛ- 4-2-18 | iti‖*) Then: O woman, wife of the dead man, rise up (उदीर्ष्व (*udīrṣva*)) towards the जीवलोकं (*jīvalokaṃ*), the world of the living, sons, grandsons and the rest, that is, the place, the house; rise up from this place. The root ईर (*īra*) is in the sense of going, of the adādi class.

### Printed p. 611

> सुमपक्रांतप्राणमेतं पतिमुप शेषे । तस्य समीपे स्वपिषि । तस्मात्त्वमेहि ।
> आगच्छ ! यस्मात्त्वं हस्तग्राभस्य पाणिग्राहं कुर्वतो दिधिषोर्गर्भस्य निधातुस्तवास्य
> पत्युः संबंधादागतमिदं जनित्वं जायात्त्वषुभिलक्ष्य सं बभूथ सं भूतासि अनुमरणनिश्चयमकार्षिः तस्मादागच्च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains the verse as addressed to the wife of the dead man. "I who lie beside this man whose life-breath has departed", he says, "you are lying near him; therefore come. Since you, in respect of him who took your hand and was the begetter of the child, have turned toward this state of being his wife, you have resolved to die with him (anumaraṇa); therefore come away."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नारि (*nāri*)—O wife of the dead man
- जीवलोकं अभि (*jīvalokaṃ abhi*)—to the house, the abode of your sons, grandsons and the rest
- उदीर्ष्व (*udīrṣva*)—rise from here and set out
- गतासुं (*gatāsuṃ*)—one whose life has gone
- एतं (*etaṃ*)—near this husband
- उप शेषे (*upa śeṣe*)—you are lying
- एहि (*ehi*)—come home
- हस्तग्राभस्य (*hastagrābhasya*)—of him who took your hand in marriage
- दिधिषोः (*didhiṣoḥ*)—and caused you to conceive
- तव पत्युः (*tava patyuḥ*)—with your husband
- इदं जनित्वं अभि (*idaṃ janitvaṃ abhi*)—honouring your state of being his wife
- सं बभूथ (*saṃ babhūtha*)—you have resolved to die with him (give that up and come home)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wife of the dead man, rise from here and go to the house, the abode of your sons and grandsons. You are lying near this husband whose life has gone; come home. Honouring your state of being the wife of the husband who took your hand and caused you to conceive, you have resolved to die with him; give that up and come home.

##### English translation
Rise, woman, (and go) the world of living beings : come, this man near whom you sleep is lifeless : you have enjoyed this state of being the wife of your husband, the suitor who took you by the hand.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-2-18) prescribes that when the wife of the dead man, clinging to his body, is set on going with him in sahagamana, she is to be raised and brought away from the body with the ṛk "udīrṣva nārī". The sūtra: तामुत्थापयेद्देवरः पतिस्थावीयोऽन्तेवासी जरद्दासो पोदीर्ष नार्यभि जीवलोकं (*tāmutthāpayeddevaraḥ patisthāvīyo 'ntevāsī jaraddāso podīrṣa nāryabhi jīvalokaṃ*).
"हे नारि जीवलोकं अभि उत् ईर्ष्व (*he nāri jīvalokaṃ abhi ut īrṣva*)": O wife of the dead man, do not grieve, rise. What is in the dead body? His self has left that body and gone to the other world. Therefore leave contact with the dead body and come here. Make ready to go to this world where living kinsmen dwell, that is, to your house. The living must strive to live in this world of the living as long as their life lasts; it is not proper to cherish attachment to the lifeless body left behind after departure to the other world. Therefore leave the body of your husband there and rise and come.
"गतासुं एतं उप शेषे, एहि (*gatāsuṃ etaṃ upa śeṣe, ehi*)": O woman, the body of your husband that you embrace has no breath. It is a corpse, a mere inert thing. Why lie near it? The breath that has left the body does not return. Therefore leave that body and come.
When the dead man's wife, unable to be apart from his body, embraces it and laments, heeds no one and is resolved to go with that body in sahagamana, her brother-in-law (devara), that is, the dead man's younger brother, should try to turn her from this and bring her back home. If the dead man has no younger brother, the purohita, a pupil, or a long-serving servant of the dead man may do this task of consoling the wife and bringing her back. In the present ṛk the brother-in-law addresses her with the words "उदीर्ष्व (*udīrṣva*)".

### Printed p. 612
"Hastagrābhasya didhiṣoḥ tava patyuḥ idaṃ janitvaṃ abhi saṃ babhūtha": O woman, in respect of this husband of yours, who took your hand at the wedding but was not able to make you conceive a womb for the sake of a son, you have set your mind, following a wife's duty, on going with his dead body in sahagamana. Do not do so. Since no son who would extend the family has been born to you, give up this resolve, in order to obtain such a son from the devara (brother-in-law) and bring your husband a good state in the other world; leave your husband's body, rise and come. This is what the devara, the husband's younger brother, says to her.
In former times, that is, in the Vedic period, if a husband died without a son, his wife used to obtain from the devara, her husband's brother, one son only, for the sake of a son. For this reason the present ṛk speaks of the brother-in-law holding back the dead man's wife from sahagamana and bringing her back to his own house. So that there may be no cause for doubt whether a brother-in-law could have intercourse with his elder brother's wife, or whether such a custom existed, the subject is mentioned elsewhere in the Ṛgveda itself—

### Printed p. 613
कुह स्विद्दोषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतुः कुहोषतुः । को नां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मर्यं न योषा कृणुते सधस्थ आ ॥ (*kuha sviddoṣā kuha vastoraśvinā kuhābhipitvaṃ karatuḥ kuhoṣatuḥ | ko nāṃ śayutrā vidhaveva devaraṃ maryaṃ na yoṣā kṛṇute sadhastha ā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-40-2)
The woman Ghoṣā, seer of this ṛk, speaks thus to the Aśvins: O Aśvins, where were you at night? Where by day? Where was your lodging today? In the house of which sacrificer did you lie? In whose house did you spend the night, as the wife of a dead man resorts at night to her brother-in-law (her husband's younger brother) for intercourse? Thus she questions the Aśvins in various ways. In this ṛk the sentence "vidhavēva dēvaraṃ maryaṃ na yōṣā kṛṇutē sadhastha ā" shows the present matter clearly. Its meaning is: as a widow who has lost her husband lies on one bed with her brother-in-law, a man, and makes him face her and attends on him. On this Yāska gives the etymology—
क्व वसथः । को वां शयने विधवेव देवरं । देवरः कस्मात् । द्वितीयो वर उच्यते । विधवा विधातृका भवति । विधवनाद्वा । (*kva vasathaḥ | ko vāṃ śayane vidhaveva devaraṃ | devaraḥ kasmāt | dvitīyo vara ucyate | vidhavā vidhātṛkā bhavati | vidhavanādvā |*)
(Ni. 3-15)
That is: O Aśvins, where did you lie at night? Did you spend the night lying somewhere else, as a husbandless widow lies on one bed with her brother-in-law? Here the word dēvara means the second husband (vara). The dead husband is the woman's first husband; the devara, the brother-in-law, is the widow's second. The word vidhavā is explained by its parts as a woman who has lost the husband who nourished and protected her, a woman without a husband, or one who after her husband's death runs to others and takes refuge with them.
In Smṛti and other works the following is found:
यस्या म्रियेत कन्याया वाचा सत्ये कृते पतिः । कामनेन विधानेन निजो विंदेत देवरः ॥ (*yasyā mriyeta kanyāyā vācā satye kṛte patiḥ | kāmanena vidhānena nijo viṃdeta devaraḥ ‖*)
It says that if the husband to whom a maiden had been promised in words (vāc) dies, after the verbal rite (vāṅmukhya) of the wedding was done but before the marriage rite was completed, then his younger brother, the brother-in-law, should marry that woman in due order. If the dead man has no brother,

### Printed p. 614
it says that those of his relatives who are fit should take the dead man's wife. The sage Parāśara says—
नष्टे मृते प्रव्रजिते क्लीबे च पतितेऽपत् । पंचस्वापत्सु नारीणां पतिरन्यो विधीयते ॥ (*naṣṭe mṛte pravrajite klībe ca patite 'pat | paṃcasvāpatsu nārīṇāṃ patiranyo vidhīyate ‖*)
That is: when the husband she married dies, or goes abroad for a long time, or it is not certain whether he lives, or he is unfit for intercourse and impotent, or he is fallen (patita), outcaste through evil deeds and the like, in these cases the woman may marry another husband. The custom that when a husband dies his younger brother or a near relative marries the woman is still found today among forest peoples of many other countries.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> धनु॒र्हस्ता॑द॒दादा॑नो मृ॒तस्या॒स्मे क्ष॒त्राय॒ वर्च॑से॒ बला॑य ।  
> अत्रै॒व त्वमि॒ह व॒यं सु॒वीरा॒ विश्वाः॒ स्पृधो॑ अ॒भिमा॑तीर्जयेम ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> धनुः । हस्तात् । आददानः । मृतस्य । अस्मे इति । क्षत्राय । वर्चसे । बलाय ।  
> अत्र । एव । त्वं । इह । वयं । सुवीराः । विश्वाः । स्पृधः । अभिमातीः । जयेम ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> क्षत्रियस्य धनुर्हस्तादित्यनया धनुः प्रहरेत् । सूत्रितं च । धनुर्हस्तादाददानो मृतस्येति धनुः । अ. गृ. ४-२-२० । इति ॥
> मृतस्य क्षत्रियस्य हस्ताद्धनुराददानः । किमर्थं । अस्मे अस्माकं क्षत्राय
> प्रजापालनसमर्थाय बलाय वर्चसे तेजसे बलाय सेनालक्षणाय च धनुराद.
> दानोऽहं ब्रवीमीति शेषः । किमिति । त्वमत्र्यैवास्मिन्स्थान एव भव वयं चेहास्मिल्लोके सुवीराः सुपुत्रयुक्ता भवंतो विश्वाः सर्वानभिमातीरभिमन्यमानान्
> स्पृधः संघर्षयित्रिन्बाधकात्यत्रूञ्चयेम । सहेमहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ṛk "धनुर्हस्तात् (*dhanurhastāt*)" is used for taking up the bow of a dead Kṣatriya. Sāyaṇa cites the sūtra धनुर्हस्तादाददानो मृतस्येति धनुः (*dhanurhastādādadāno mṛtasyeti dhanuḥ*). The speaker takes the bow from the hand of the dead Kṣatriya: for what purpose? For our kṣatra, capacity to protect the people, for varcas, brilliance, and for bala, strength in the form of an army. "I who take the bow say: you remain here in this very place, and we here in this world, with good sons, may overcome all who assail us, all the opponents, the harmful enemies." The verb "may we overcome" is glossed "may we overpower".

- वर्चसे (*varcase*)—for brilliance
- बलाय (*balāya*)—for vigour
- मृतस्य (*mṛtasya*)—of this dead Kṣatriya

- आददानः (*ādadānaḥ*)—having taken (I say thus)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Taking the bow from the hand of this dead Kṣatriya, for our strength, brilliance and vigour, I say thus: O dead man, remain right here. In this world, with excellent sons and grandsons, we conquer all the enemies who attack and harm us.

##### English translation
Taking his bow from the hand of the dead man, for the sake of our vigour, energy and strength, (I say) you are there; may we (who are) here, blessed with male offspring, overcome all the enemies who assail us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

If the dead man is a Kṣatriya, this ṛk "धनुर्हस्तात् (*dhanurhastāt*)" is to be recited when the bow in his hand is taken, as shown by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-2-20): धनुर्हस्तादाददानो मृतस्येति धनुः (*dhanurhastādādadāno mṛtasyeti dhanuḥ*).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the death of a dīkṣita, four ṛks beginning "उप सर्प मातरं (*upa sarpa mātaraṃ*)" are to be recited (śaṃsanīya). Sāyaṇa cites the sūtra उप सर्प मातरं भूमिमेतामुरुव्यचसं पृथिवीं सुशेवां । ऊर्णम्रदा युवतिर्दक्षिणावत एषा त्वा पातु निर्ऋतेरुपस्थात् ॥ १० ॥ उप । सर्प । मातरं । भूमिं । एतां । उरुऽव्यचसं । पृथिवीं । सुशेवां । ऊर्णम्रदाः । युवतिः । दक्षिणावते । एषा । त्वा । पातु । निःऋतेः । उप- । स्थात् ॥ १० ॥ दीक्षितमरण उप सर्प मातरमित्याद्याश्चतस्रः शंसनीयाः । सूत्रितं च । उप सर्प मातरं भूमिमेतामिति चतस्रः सोम एकेभ्यः । अ. ६-१० । इति ॥ (*upa sarpa mātaraṃ bhūmimetāmuruvyacasaṃ pṛthivīṃ suśevāṃ | ūrṇamradā yuvatirdakṣiṇāvata eṣā tvā pātu nirṛterupasthāt ‖ 10 ‖ upa | sarpa | mātaraṃ | bhūmiṃ | etāṃ | uru 'vyacasaṃ | pṛthivīṃ | suśevāṃ | ūrṇamradāḥ | yuvatiḥ | dakṣiṇāvate | eṣā | tvā | pātu | niḥṛteḥ | upa- | sthāt ‖ 10 ‖ dīkṣitamaraṇa upa sarpa mātaramityādyāścatasraḥ śaṃsanīyāḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | upa sarpa mātaraṃ bhūmimetāmiti catasraḥ soma ekebhyaḥ | a. 6-10 | iti ‖*) and another: with "upa sarpa" they should lay the gathered bones in a pit (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-5-5). *Mātaram*: the Earth, who is our mother; "creep up to her" as she is placed in the earth by us, that is, enter her. What is she like? Wide-expanding (uruvyacas), pervading much; Pṛthivī, broad; suśevā, very pleasant, the giver of happiness to all. Go to her. She is a young woman (yuvati), this earth in woman's form, to the sacrificer who is rich in dakṣiṇā, a giver of fees to the priests, she is ūrṇamradā: soft like wool (ūrṇa), like a woollen thing; she is very tender; the meaning is that she does not hurt. May this Earth protect you, the sacrificer in the form of bones, from the lap, the proximity, of Nirṛti, the goddess of death.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उरुव्यचसं (*uruvyacasaṃ*)—all-pervading
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—spread out widely
- सुशेवां (*suśevāṃ*)—giver of happiness
- मातरं (*mātaraṃ*)—in the form of a mother
- एतां भूमिं (*etāṃ bhūmiṃ*)—to this Earth
- उप सर्प (*upa sarpa*)—enter
- युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*)—this Earth, having the nature of a woman
- दक्षिणावते (*dakṣiṇāvate*)—to the sacrificer who has given generously
- ऊर्णम्रदाः (*ūrṇamradāḥ*)—is soft like wool
- एषा (*eṣā*)—this Earth
- निर्यतेः (*niryateḥ*)—of the goddess of death
- उपस्थात् (*upasthāt*)—from the nearness
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- पातु (*pātu*)—may she protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Enter this Earth, all-pervading, widely spread, in the form of a mother and giver of happiness. This Earth, having the nature of a woman, is soft like wool to the sacrificer who has given generously. May this Earth protect you from the nearness of the goddess of death.

### Printed p. 617

##### English translation
Go to this your mother-earth, the wide-spread, delightful earth ; this virgin (earth is) as soft as wool, to the liberal (worshipper); may she protect you from the proximity of Nirriti.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

If a sacrificer who has taken up the sacrificial consecration dies before the sacrifice is completed, the four Ṛks beginning उप सर्प (*upa sarpa*) (Ṛks 10–13) are to be recited. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra उप सर्प भूमिमेतामिति चतस्रः सोम एकेभ्यः (*upa sarpa bhūmimetāmiti catasraḥ soma ekebhyaḥ*) (Ā. 6-10). In the funeral rite, after the body has been burnt and the bones gathered, this mantra is to be recited when the bones are put into a pit (or into water such as a river). This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra by the sūtra सर्प इत्यनया संचितान्यस्थीनि गर्तॆ निदध्युः (*sarpa ityanayā saṃcitānyasthīni gartè nidadhyuḥ*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-5-5). **NOTE**

For this Ṛk and the next three, Sāyaṇa says that the mantras are those recited when the bones of the dead man are laid down, and he explains the meaning accordingly. Since the Ṛks contain no word for bones or any word that conveys that sense, many Western scholars hold that these Ṛks describe the burial of the dead body in the earth, and therefore think that besides the custom of burning the corpse in fire, burial in the earth was also current at that time. It cannot be said that this opinion is wrong.

### Printed p. 618

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उच्छ्वंचस्वेत्येतया पांसूनवकिरेत् । सूत्र्यते हि । उत्तरया पांसूनवकिरेत् । आ. गृ. सू. ४-५-६ । इति ॥
> हे पृथिवि उच्छ्वंचस्व । ऊर्ध्वंगतोच्छ्वासमेनं कुरु । अधस्तान्मा कृथा
> इत्यर्थः । किंच मा नि बाधथाः । मा संपीडय । तथास्मै यजमानार्थं सूपायना शोभनोपगमना सूपचारिका भवेत्यर्थः । सूपवंचना । उपवंचनं
> प्रलंभनं शोभनप्रलंभा सुप्रतिष्ठा भव । अपि च माता पुत्रमात्मीयं बालकं
> सिचा वस्त्रांतेन यथाच्छादयति तद्वद्धे भूमि एनमस्थिरूपं यजमानं त्वमभ्यूर्णुहि । आभिमुख्येनाच्छादय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

One is to scatter dust with this Ṛk उच्छ्वंचस्व (*ucchvaṃcasva*); for it is taught in the sūtra: "With the following (Ṛk) he should scatter the dust" (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-5-6). "O earth, rise up", that is, make him raised up and breathing freely; do not make (the earth) sink beneath him. Further, "do not oppress" him; do not crush him. Be gracious and attentive (सूपायना (*sūpāyanā*), one of good approach, a good attendant) for this sacrificer. सूपवंचना (*sūpavaṃcanā*): उपवंचनं (*upavaṃcanaṃ*) is प्रलंभनं (*pralaṃbhanaṃ*), a good support; so be one of good support, well established. And as a mother covers her own child with the end of a garment, so, O earth, cover this (sacrificer, now in the form of bones) all over, covering him facing towards him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पृथिवि (*pṛthivi*)—O earth
- उच्छ्वंचस्व (*ucchvaṃcasva*)—make him breathe upward
- मा नि बाधथाः (*mā ni bādhathāḥ*)—do not oppress him
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to this sacrificer
- सूपायना (*sūpāyanā*)—be excellent, a giver of comfort
- सूपवंचना भव (*sūpavaṃcanā bhava*)—be an excellent giver of shelter
- माता (*mātā*)—the mother
- पुत्रं (*putraṃ*)—the son
- सिचा (*sicā*)—with the end of her garment
- यथा (*yathā*)—as she covers
- भूमे (*bhūme*)—O earth
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this dead sacrificer
- अभ्यूर्णुहि (*abhyūrṇuhi*)—hide, cover

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O earth, make him breathe upward. Do not oppress him. Be an excellent giver of comfort to this sacrificer. Be an excellent giver of shelter. As a mother covers her son with the end of her sari, O earth, cover this dead sacrificer.

##### English translation
Earth, rise up above him ; oppress him not ; he attentive to him (and) comfortable ; cover him up earth, as a mother covers her echild with the sklrt of her garment.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When the dead body or the urn of bones is buried in the earth and covered by throwing earth over it, this Ṛk उच्छंचस्व (*ucchaṃcasva*) is to be recited. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra by the sūtra उत्तरया पांसूनवकिरेत् (*uttarayā pāṃsūnavakiret*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-5-6).

> तृतीयार्थे प्रथमा । मित इति निष्कांतं रूपं । व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनस्यैकवचनं ।
> स्वरो वृषादित्वाद्दृष्टव्यः । सहस्रेण संमिता बहुसंख्याकाः । पार्थिवाः पांसव
> उप श्रयंतां । एनमुपसेवंतां । तं सपरिवार्य तिष्ठंत्यर्थः । हिरवधारणे ।
> तथा ते पांसवोऽस्मै गृहासो गृहा भवंतो धृतश्चुतो धृतस्योदकस्य
> सर्पिषो वा क्षारयितारो भवंतु । अत्रास्मिल्लोके विश्वाहा सर्वेस्वहःसु सर्वदास्मा अस्य शरणाः संतु । आश्रयभूता भवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They recite this while the bones are being covered with dust. May the earth, rising upward, pressing down upon the urn of bones, stand firm, be well established. Further, may the thousand, that is the thousandfold number of, मितः (*mitaḥ*) (things) thrown in. (मितः (*mitaḥ*): from the root *minoti* by an Uṇādi affix in the sense of the object; the augment tuk after a kvip; then jas.) Or else: सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*) is the first case in the sense of the third; मित (*mita*) is a derived form, the plural put for the singular by exchange, and the accent is to be understood as in वृष (*vṛṣa*) and the like. Then the sense is: the many earthly dust-particles, measured by a thousand, उप श्रयंतां (*upa śrayaṃtāṃ*), let them attend upon him, stand surrounding him. हि (*hi*) is for emphasis. Likewise may those dust-particles be houses for him, धृतश्चुतः (*dhṛtaścutaḥ*), makers of ghee, of water or of clarified butter, flow. अत्र (*atra*), in this world, विश्वाहा (*viśvāhā*), on all days, always, may they be a refuge for him, may they be a shelter.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उच्छ्वंचमाना (*ucchvaṃcamānā*)—spread over the dead man
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the earth
- सु तिष्ठतु (*su tiṣṭhatu*)—let it find a firm place
- मितः (*mitaḥ*)—placed upon him
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—thousands of
- उप श्रयंतां (*upa śrayaṃtāṃ*)—let the dust-particles surround him
- ते (*te*)—these dust-particles
- गृहासः (*gṛhāsaḥ*)—be shelters for the dead man
- धृतश्चुतः (*dhṛtaścutaḥ*)—and streamers of water
- भवंतु (*bhavaṃtu*)—let them be
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this place
- विश्वाहा (*viśvāhā*)—on all days
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for this sacrificer
- शरणाः संतु (*śaraṇāḥ saṃtu*)—let them provide shelter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the earth spread over the body of the dead man find a firm place. May the thousands of particles laid upon him surround him. May these particles be shelters for the dead man and streamers of water. In this place on all days may they provide shelter for this sacrificer.

### Printed p. 620

##### English translation
May the earth heaped over him lie light : may thousands of particles (of dust) envelope him ; may these mansions distil ghee (for him); may they every day be an asylum to him in this world.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्ते॑ स्तभ्नामि पृथि॒वीं त्वत्परी॒मं लो॒गं नि॒दध॒न्मो अ॒हं  ॑
> रिषं ।  
> ए॒तां स्तूणां॑ पि॒तरो॑ धारयंतु॒ तेत्रा॑ य॒मः साद॑ना ते  
> मिनोतु ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ते । स्तभ्नामि । पृथिवीं । त्वत् । परि । इमं । लोगं । निदधत् । मो इति ।  
> अहं । रिषं ।  
> एतां । स्तूणां । पितरः । धारयंतु । ते । अत्र । यमः । सदना । ते । मिनोतु ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत्ते स्तभ्नामीति कपालेनास्थीन्यपिदध्यात् । सूत्रितं च । उत्ते स्तभ्नामीति
> कपालेनापिधाय । आ. गृ. सू. ४-५-८ । इति ॥
> हे अस्थिकुंभ त्वत्परि । परिशब्दयोगे पंचमी । तवोपरि ते त्वदीयेन
> कपालेन पृथिवीमुत्सभ्यामि । प्रतिबध्नामि । यथा पृथिवी तवोपरि मा गच्छति
> तथापिदधामित्यर्थः । इमं लोगं कपाललक्षणं लोष्टं निदधदुपरि स्थापयन्नहं
> मो रिषं ! मा हिंसिषं । किंचैतां मया निहितां स्फूणां ते त्वदीयां पृथिव्या
> धारयित्रीं कपाललक्षणां पितरो धारयंतु । निश्चलां कुर्वंतु । ततस्ते त्वदीयेऽस्मिन्सा ने यमः पितृपतिः सदनानि स्थानानि मिनोतु । परिच्चिनत्तु । करोत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With उत्ते स्तभ्नामि (*utte stabhnāmi*) he should cover the bones with a potsherd. It is stated in the sūtra: "Having covered with the potsherd (reciting) उत्ते स्तभ्नामि (*utte stabhnāmi*)" (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-5-8). "O urn of bones, त्वत्परि (*tvatpari*)" (the fifth case is by association with परि (*pari*)), that is, above you, with your own potsherd I *utsabhyāmi*, I hold back the earth, so that the earth may not come upon you; thus I cover. Placing above (you) this clod, लोगं (*logaṃ*), which is the potsherd, may I मो रिषं (*mo riṣaṃ*), not harm (you). Further, this your स्फूणां (*sphūṇāṃ*), the potsherd that holds up the earth, placed by me, may the Pitṛs sustain, make it immovable. Then in this place of yours may Yama, lord of the Pitṛs, मिनोतु (*minotu*), fix, that is, make, dwellings.

- (O urn of bones) त्वत्परि (*tvatpari*)—above you
- ते (*te*)—with your own potsherd
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—earth
- उत् स्तभ्नामि (*ut stabhnāmi*)—I spread
- इमं लोगं (*imaṃ logaṃ*)—this clod of earth
- निदधत् (*nidadhat*)—while placing
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- मो रिसं (*mo risaṃ*)—may I not harm you
- एतां (*etāṃ*)—this, placed by me
- ते (*te*)—your
- स्तूणां (*stūṇāṃ*)—this memorial pillar
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—the Pitṛs
- धारयंतु (*dhārayaṃtu*)—let them make it stand firm
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—Yama
- ते (*te*)—for you
- अत्र (*atra*)—here
- सदना (*sadanā*)—a dwelling
- मिनोतु (*minotu*)—let him build

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O urn of bones, above you I take earth with this potsherd and spread it. While placing this clod of earth may I not harm you. May the Pitṛs make this memorial pillar of yours, placed by me, stand firm. May Yama build for you a dwelling here.

##### English translation
I heap up the earth around you, placing (upon you) this clod of earth: may I not be injured: may the Pitris sustain this your monument; may Yama make you a dwelling here.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Reciting this Ṛk उत्ते स्तभ्नामि (*utte stabhnāmi*), one should bury the bones in the earth and cover them by spreading earth over them with a potsherd. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra by the sūtra उत्ते स्तभ्नामीति कपालेनापिधाय (*utte stabhnāmīti kapālenāpidhāya*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 4-5-8).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र॒ती॒चीने॒ मामह॒नीष्वाः॑ प॒र्णमि॒व द॑धुः ॥

> प्रतीचीं । जग्रभ । वाचं । अश्वं । रतनया । यथा ॥ १४ ॥

### Printed p. 622

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया प्रजापतिः प्रार्थते । हे प्रजापते प्रतीचीने प्रतिपूज्ये अहनि
> तदुपलक्षिते संवत्सरात्मके मां संकुसुकमृषिं आ दधुः निहितवंतः सर्वे देवाः ।
> किमिव । इष्टाः बाणस्य पर्णमिव । पक्षमिव पक्षं यथा बाणस्य मूले स्थापयंते
> तद्वज्जगन्नूले त्वयि मां स्थापितवंतः । अतो मदीयां प्रतीचीं प्रतिपूज्यां
> पूज्यां वाचु स्तुतिरूपां जग्रभ गृहाण । कथमित्युच्यते । अश्वं आशुगामिनं हयं
> रशनया रज्जा यथा गृह्णंति तद्वत्कर्णाभ्यां मत्कृतां स्तुतिं गृहाणेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk Prajāpati is addressed in prayer. "O Prajāpati, in the day that is to be honoured in return (प्रतीचीने प्रतिपूज्ये (*pratīcīne pratipūjye*)), marked by it, of the nature of the year, all the gods have placed me, the seer Saṃkusuka." Like what? Like the feather of an arrow: as the feathers are fixed at the base of an arrow, so they have set me in you, the root of the world. Therefore take, जग्रभ (*jagrabha*), my song of praise, honoured in return and worthy of honour. How? As they hold a swift horse, अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*), with a rope, रशनया (*raśanayā*), so take with your ears the praise made by me. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Prajāpati) प्रतीचीने (*pratīcīne*)—that has reached its last time
- अहनि (*ahani*)—in this twilight time
- इष्टाः पर्णं इव (*iṣṭāḥ parṇaṃ iva*)—as the wings of a bird fold up
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- आ दधुः (*ā dadhuḥ*)—they have laid down here
- यथा (*yathā*)—as
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—a horse
- रशनया (*raśanayā*)—with a bridle they hold
- प्रतीचीं (*pratīcīṃ*)—this praise of mine
- जग्रभ (*jagrabha*)—listen with your ear and hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Prajāpati, in this twilight, the last time of the day, they have laid me down here, as the wings of a bird fold up. As a horse is held with a bridle, so listen with your ear and hear this praise of mine.

##### English translation
At the decline of the day they have placed me (in the grave) like the feathers of an arrow ; I have restrained my declining voice as (they check) a horse with a bridle

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Prajāpati is prayed to. Since there is no Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya for this Ṛk, we have written here the commentary on this Ṛk, collected and printed at the end of page 33 of the fourth volume of the Ṛgveda with commentary published by the Vaidika Saṃśodhana Maṇḍala of Poona. It is not Sāyaṇa's commentary. It cannot be said who wrote it.

### Printed p. 623
## Sūkta 19 (Maṇḍala 10)

The end of the sixth adhyāya is marked here: the sixth adhyāya in the seventh aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, with Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya and a Kannada translation, is completed. Then follows the opening of the next adhyāya: the seventh adhyāya in the seventh aṣṭaka; the nineteenth sūkta in the tenth maṇḍala.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ द्वादशानुवाकात्मकस्य दशममंडलस्य द्वितीयेऽनुवाके त्रयोदश
> सूक्तानि । तत्र निवर्तध्वमित्यष्टर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं । अस्य यमपुत्रो मथिताख्य
> ऋषिर्वरुणपुत्रो भृगुर्वाथवा भार्गवश्चवनः । षष्ठी गायत्रि शिष्टा अनुष्टुभः ।
> इदमद्भवताकं गोदेवताकं वा । अग्निषोमा पुनर्वसू इत्यर्धर्चोऽग्नीषोमदेवताकः । कथा चानुक्रांतं। नि वर्तध्वमष्टौ मथितो भृगुर्वा वारुणिर्भार्गवश्चवनो पापं गव्यं वानुष्टुभमग्नीषोमीयो द्वितीयोऽर्थर्चः षष्ठि
> गायत्रीति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥
> xxvii 40

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The tenth maṇḍala consists of twelve anuvākas. Its second anuvāka contains thirteen sūktas. Of these, the third is the sūkta of eight ṛks beginning निवर्तध्वं (*nivartadhvaṃ*). Its seer is Mathita, son of Yama; or else Bhṛgu, son of Varuṇa; or Cyavana, descendant of Bhṛgu. The sixth ṛk is in Gāyatrī metre and the rest are in Anuṣṭubh. The deity is the waters or the cows. The second half of the first ṛk, अग्नीषोमा पुनर्वसू (*agnīṣomā punarvasū*), has Agni and Soma as its deities. He confirms this by the Anukramaṇī. The viniyoga has already been stated.

### Printed p. 626

The Anuvāda: this tenth maṇḍala has twelve anuvākas, and its second anuvāka has thirteen sūktas. The first two of these were explained in the previous adhyāya. The sūkta now explained, नि वर्तध्वं (*ni vartadhvaṃ*), is the third sūkta of the second anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. Its seer is Mathita, son of Yama; or the seer Bhṛgu, son of Varuṇa; or Cyavana, son of Bhṛgu, may also be the seer. The sixth ṛk of this sūkta is in Gāyatrī metre and the remaining ṛks are in Anuṣṭubh. Its deity is the waters or the cows; for the second half of the first ṛk, beginning अग्नीषोमा पुनर्वसू (*agnīṣomā punarvasū*), the deities are Agni and Soma. The Anukramaṇī is cited as saying the same. The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Sūkta 19. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 19. Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 7; Varga 1. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 8.

Ṛṣi: Mathita Yāmāyana; or Bhṛgu Vāruṇi; or Cyavana Bhārgava.

Devatā: of ṛk 1, the first half, and of ṛks 2–8: the waters or the cows. Of ṛk 1, the second half: Agni and Soma.

Chandas: ṛks 1–5 and 7–8: Anuṣṭubh. Ṛk 6: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि व॑र्तध्वं॒ मानु॑ गाता॒स्मान्सि॑षक्त रेवतीः ।  
> अग्नी॑षोमा पुनर्वसू अ॒स्मे धा॑रयतं र॒यिं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । वर्तर्ध्वं । मा । अनु । गात । अस्मान् । सिसक्त । रेवतीः ।  
> अग्नीषोमा । पुनर्वसू इति पुनःवसू । अस्मे इति । धारयतं । रयिं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे गावो हे आपो वा यूयं नि वर्तर्ध्वं । अस्मान्प्रत्यागच्छत । मानु
> गात । अस्मद्वृतिरिक्तं यजमानं मा गच्छत । अगत्य च हे रेवती रेवत्यो धन_

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He addresses the cows or the waters: "Turn back (नि वर्तध्वं (*ni vartadhvaṃ*)); come back to us. Do not go to a sacrificer other than us." Then, not going away, "O wealthy ones (रेवतीः (*revatīḥ*)), you who possess wealth, …".

### Printed p. 627

> वत्यो यूयमस्मान्सिषक्त । सेचयत । अवगाहत । गोदोहनस्नानपानादिद्वारेण सेवध्वमित्यर्थः ! हे पुनर्वसू! पुनःपुनर्वस्तारौ स्तोत्थाणां यष्ट्णणामाच्छादयितारावेतन्नामकौ देवौ युवामस्मे अस्मासु रयिं व्रीह्यादिलक्षणं
> धनं धारयतं । स्थापयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"…you, the wealthy ones, सिषक्त (*siṣakta*) us": that is, sprinkle us, bathe us; the meaning is, serve us by way of milking, bathing, drinking and the like. "O Punarvasu": two deities of this name, who again and again are givers of wealth (or, as he also explains, coverers of the worshippers and praisers); "you two hold, establish, in us the wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)) that consists of rice and the like."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नि वर्तध्वं (*ni vartadhvaṃ*)—(O cows) turn back
- मानु गात (*mānu gāta*)—do not go to another sacrificer
- रेवतीः (*revatīḥ*)—you who are endowed with wealth
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—to us
- सिसक्त (*sisakta*)—pour out milk
- पुनर्वसू (*punarvasū*)—you who again and again give dwelling to the sacrificers (or, who clothe them with garments and the like)
- अग्नीषोमा (*agnīṣomā*)—O deities Agni and Soma
- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- धारयतं (*dhārayataṃ*)—establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O cows, return to us. Do not go to another sacrificer. Wealthy as you are, pour out milk for us. O Agni and Soma, who again and again clothe the sacrificers with garments and the like, establish wealth in us.

##### English translation
Come back : go not elsewhere; abounding in wealth, sprinkle us ; Agni and Soma, you who clothe (your worshippers) again, bestow upon us riches.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पुन॑रेना॒ नि व॑र्तय॒ पुन॑रेना॒ न्या कु॑रु ।  
> इंद्र॑ एणा॒ नि य॑च्छत्व॒ग्निरे॑ना उ॒पाज॑तु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुनः । एनाः । नि । वर्तय । पुनः । एनाः । नि । आ । कुरु ।  
> इंद्रः । एनाः । नि । यच्छतु । अग्निः । एनाः । उपअजतु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> : अत्र मंत्रद्रष्टा स्मात्मानं प्रतिब्रूते । हे मदीयात्मन् त्वमेना एता
> अन्यतोऽभिगंत्रिर्गा अपो वा पुनर्निवर्शय । पुनःपुनर्मदभिमुखीकुरु ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here the mantra-seer addresses his own self: "O my self, turn these cows (or waters), who are being drawn from elsewhere, back again; again and again make them face me."

### Printed p. 628

> तदनंतरमेना एताः पुनर्भूयो भूयो न्या कुरु । नियता आत्मायत्ताः कुरु ।
> किंचेंद्रोऽपि तव सहायभूतः सन्नेना एता नि यच्छतु । त्वदायत्ताः करोतु ।
> अग्निश्चैना एता गा अपो वोपाजतु । उपगमयतु । उपक्षिपतु ना । उपयोग्याः करोश्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

After that, "make these again and again subject, make them restrained and dependent on yourself. Moreover, let Indra also, being your helper, restrain them and make them dependent on you. And let Agni bring these cows or waters near": that is, make them come near, throw them near; the meaning is, make them fit for use.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एनाः (*enāḥ*)—these cows
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- नि वर्तय (*ni vartaya*)—make them turn back
- एनाः (*enāḥ*)—these
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- न्या कुरु (*nyā kuru*)—make them subject
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- एनाः (*enāḥ*)—these
- नि यच्छतु (*ni yacchatu*)—let him make them subject to us
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni also
- एनाः (*enāḥ*)—these
- उपाजतु (*upājatu*)—let him make them useful to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Make these cows turn back again. Make them subject again. Let Indra make them subject to us. Let Agni also make them useful to us.

##### English translation
Bring them back again, render them obedient: may Indra restore them; may Agni bring them nigh.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पुन॑रे॒ता नि व॑र्तंताम॒स्मिन्पु॑ष्यंतु॒ गोप॑त् ।  
> इ॒हैवाग्ने॒ नि धा॑रये॒ह ति॑ष्ठतु॒ या र॒यिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुनः । एताः । नि । वर्तंतां । अस्मिन् । पुष्यंतु । गोऽपतौ ।  
> अह । एव । अग्ने । नि । धारय । इह । शिष्ठतु । या । रयिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एना एता ईदृश्यो गाव आपो वा पुनर्नि वर्तंतां । भूयो भूयो
> मां प्रत्यागच्छंतु । अगत्य च गोपत् सास्नादिमतीनां धेनूनां वृष्टिलक्षणाना-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"May these cows, or waters, of this kind turn back again; may they come back to me again and again. And having come, in this one who is the protector (गोपत् (*gopat*)) of milch cows, with udders, and of the waters in the form of rain …".

### Printed p. 629

> मपां पालकेऽस्मिन्नीदृशे मयि पुष्यंतु । आत्मायत्तत्वेन स्थित्वा पुष्टा भवंतु ।
> पुष्टाः सतीस्ता हे अग्ने त्वमिहैवास्मिन्नेव मयि नि धारय । नियमेन स्थापय ।
> या रयिर्यदपि व्रीह्यादिकं धनमस्ति तदपि धनं गोसहितमिहास्मिन्नेव गोपता
> मयि शिष्ठतु हनिवसतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"… may they thrive in me, such a protector; staying dependent on themselves, may they become fat. Being nourished, O Agni, hold them here, in me alone; establish them firmly. Whatever wealth there is, such as rice and the like, let that wealth also, together with cows, remain here, in me alone, the protector of cows; let it dwell."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एताः (*etāḥ*)—these cows
- पुनः नि वर्तंतां (*punaḥ ni vartaṃtāṃ*)—let them come back to me again
- गोपत् (*gopat*)—(me) the nourisher of cows
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—in me
- पुष्यंतु (*puṣyaṃtu*)—let them grow
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- इहैव (*ihaiva*)—in me alone
- नि धारय (*ni dhāraya*)—establish those cows permanently
- या रयिः (*yā rayiḥ*)—whatever well-known wealth there is, of cows and the like
- इह (*iha*)—in me alone
- तिष्ठतु (*tiṣṭhatu*)—let it stay permanently

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let these cows come back to me again. Let them grow in me, the nourisher of cows. O Agni, establish those cows in me alone, permanently. Let whatever well-known wealth of cows and the like there is remain in me alone, permanently.

##### English translation
May they come back to me and be fostered under this (their) protector : do you, Agni, keep them here; may whatever wealth (there is) remain here,

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यन्नि॒यानं॒ न्यय॑नं सं॒ज्ञानं॒ यत्प॒राय॑णं ।  
> आ॒वर्त॑नं नि॒वर्त॑नं॒ यो गो॒पा अपि॒ तं हु॑वे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । निऽयानं । निऽअयनं । संज्ञानं । यत् । पराऽअयनं ।  
> आवर्तनं । निवर्तनं । यः । गोपाः । अपि । तं । हुवे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नियानं ॥ अधिकरणे ल्युट् ॥ नियमेन यत्यागच्छंति गावोऽत्रेति नियानं
> गोष्ठाख्यं स्थानं । यत् अस्तीति शेषः । यच्छब्दयोगात्तच्छब्दोऽध्याहर्तव्यः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

नियानं (*niyānaṃ*) is formed with the affix lyuṭ in the locative sense: the place called the cowpen, where the cows regularly come. The words यत् अस्तीति (*yat astīti*) are to be supplied ("which there is"), and because of the word यत् (*yat*) the word तत् (*tat*) must be supplied.

### Printed p. 630

> हुव इति क्रियापदं सर्वत्रानुषज्यते । तत्स्थानं हुवे । आह्वयामि । आह्वानमभिमुखीकरणं तेन चात्र तत्पूर्विका प्रार्थना लक्ष्यते । गोसहितं गोष्ठं प्रार्थय
> इत्यर्थः । न्ययनं ॥ भावे ल्युट् ॥ नियमेन गृहं प्रति प्राप्तिलक्षणं गमनं
> यदस्ति तदपि प्रार्थये । निवर्तनं वने चरित्वा गृहं प्रति यदागमनमस्ति तदपि
> प्रार्थये । योऽपि गोपा गवां पालकोऽस्ति तमपि हुवे । प्रार्थये ।
> सर्वगुणोपेता गाः प्रार्थय इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The verb हुवे (*huve*) is carried on to every item: "I invoke that place," that is, I call it. Calling is making it face one, and thereby a prayer preceded by that is meant here: the meaning is "I pray for the cowpen together with its cows." न्ययनं (*nyayanaṃ*) is formed with lyuṭ in the sense of the action: the going, which consists of arriving regularly at the house, "that too I pray for." निवर्तनं (*nivartanaṃ*): after grazing in the forest, the coming back to the house, "that too I pray for." And whoever is the keeper (गोपा (*gopā*)) of the cows, "him too I invoke, I pray to"; the meaning is, "I pray for cows endowed with every good quality."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नियानं यत् (*niyānaṃ yat*)—whatever movement of those cows there is, that also
- नयनं (*nayanaṃ*)—the returning also
- संज्ञानं (*saṃjñānaṃ*)—the knowledge of their whereabouts also
- यत् परायणं (*yat parāyaṇaṃ*)—their going back again (to graze) also
- आवर्तनं (*āvartanaṃ*)—their moving about there also
- निवर्तनं (*nivartanaṃ*)—their coming back home from there also, I pray for
- यः गोपाः (*yaḥ gopāḥ*)—whoever is the protector of those cows
- तं अपि (*taṃ api*)—him also
- हुवे (*huve*)—I pray to

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When they are out of sight, I pray for knowledge of the movement of those cows, for their coming back to us from out of sight, for their going back again to graze, for their moving about there among them, and for their coming back home from there. I pray also to whoever is the protector of those cows.

##### English translation
I invoke the knowledge of the place, of their going of their coming, of their departure, of their wandering, of their returning : (I invoke) him who is their keeper.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य उ॒दान॒ड्वय॑नं॒ य उ॒दान॑ट्प॒राय॑णं ।  
> आ॒वर्त॑नं नि॒वर्त॑न॒मपि॑ गो॒पा नि व॑र्ततां ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । उत्आनट् । विअयनं । यः । उत्आनट् । पराअयनं ।  
> आवर्तनं । निवर्तनं । अपि । गोपाः । नि । वर्ततां ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 631

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो गोपा गोपालो व्ययनं नष्टानां गवामन्वेषणार्थं विविधं
> गमनमुदानट् व्याप्योति अनुभवति । यः परायणं परागमनमुदानट्
> व्याप्नोति । वनं प्रति गवां चरणाय गमनमित्यर्थः । यश्चावर्तनं वनचारिणीभिर्गोभिः सह प्रवर्तनमनुभवति । योऽपि गोपा निवर्तनं गोभिः सह वनादृहं
> प्रति निर्गमनमनुभवति । सोऽपि गोपालो नि वर्ततां । गोभिः सह वनादृहं
> प्रति क्षेमेणागच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The keeper of cows (gopā) who goes about in many directions to search for the lost cows, the one who reaches them as they go away, the one who experiences going with the forest-grazing cows, and the one who returns with the cows from the forest to the house: may that herdsman also return. That is, may he come back safely with the cows from the forest to the house.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (गोपाः) (*yaḥ (gopāḥ)*)—the herdsman who
- व्ययनं (*vyayanaṃ*)—searching for those lost cows
- उदानट् (*udānaṭ*)—comes near them
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whoever
- परायणं (*parāyaṇaṃ*)—their roaming at will
- उदानट् (*udānaṭ*)—finds out and approaches
- आवर्तनं (*āvartanaṃ*)—goes about together with them
- निवर्तनं (*nivartanaṃ*)—stays with them when they return
- अपि गोपाः (*api gopāḥ*)—that herdsman also
- नि वर्ततां (*ni vartatāṃ*)—let him return along with them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The cowherd who, searching for those lost cows, comes near them; who finds out their roaming at will, approaches them and goes about with them; who stays with them when they return home: may that herdsman also return with them.

##### English translation
May the keeper return (with them); he who reaches them when lost ; who reaches them when straying ; who reaches them when wandering, and returning.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नि॑वर्त॒ नि व॑र्तय॒ पुन॑र्न इंद्र॒ गा दे॑हि ।  
> जी॒वाभि॑र्भुनजामहै ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अ । निवर्त । नि । वर्तय । पुनः । नः । इंद्र । गाः । देहि ।  
> जीवाभिः । भुनजामहै ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 632

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वमा निवर्त । आनिवर्तस्व । अस्मदभिमुखो भव । ततोऽन्यतो
> गच्छंतीर्गा नि वर्तय । अस्मदभिमुखीः कुरु । एवं कृत्वा च हे इंद्र त्वं पुनः
> पश्चान्नोऽस्मभ्यं गा देहि । प्रयच्छ । त्वया दत्ताभिर्जिवाभिश्चिरं जीवंतीभिः
> सर्वस्य जीवयित्रिभिर्वा गोभिर्भुनजामहै । वयं भुंजीमहि । यद्वा ।
> भुजिरत्रांतर्भावितण्यर्थः । देवपित्थन्संभोजयेमहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, turn back, turn towards us; the cows that are going elsewhere, make them turn to face us. Having done so, O Indra, give us the cows again. With the cows given by you, which are long-living (jīvābhiḥ) or give life to all, may we enjoy (bhunajāmahai)." Alternatively, the root bhuj here has the causative sense included in it: "may we cause the gods and the fathers to be fed."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- आ निवर्त (*ā nivarta*)—turn back towards us
- नि वर्तय (*ni vartaya*)—make the cows
- (continued) turn towards us
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows
- देहि (*dehi*)—give
- जीवाभिः (*jīvābhiḥ*)—together with all the living cows
- भुनजामहै (*bhunajāmahai*)—may we enjoy happiness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, turn back towards us. Make the cows turn towards us. Give us the cows again. May we enjoy happiness together with all the living cows.

##### English translation
Indra, come back and bring back (the cattle); give us our cows again, may we rejoice in our cows being alive.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॑ वो वि॒श्वतो॑ दध ऊ॒र्जा घृ॒तेन॒ पय॑सा ।  
> ये दे॒वाः के च॑ य॒ज्ञिया॒स्ते र॒य्या सं सृ॑जंतु नः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । वः । विश्वतः । दधे । ऊर्जा । धृतेन । पयसा ।  
> ये । देवाः । के । च । यज्ञियाः । ते । रय्या । सं । सृजंतु । नः ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 633

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवाः विश्वतः सर्वतः स्थितान्वो युष्मानूर्जा गोसंबंधिना दधिलक्षणेनान्नेन धृतेनाज्येन पयसा क्षीरेण च परि दधे । संधारयामि । युष्मभ्यं
> हविर्द्वारेण प्रयच्छामि । न केवलमात्मानं पुष्णामीत्यर्थः । एतज्ञात्वा ये
> के च देवा यज्ञिया यज्ञार्हाः संति ते देवा नोऽस्मान्रय्या गोलक्षणेन
> धनेन सं सृजंतु । सं योजयॆंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O gods, I sustain you, who are stationed everywhere, with ūrj, the food of curds connected with cows, with ghee (ghṛta, ājya) and with milk (payas); I offer them to you through the oblation. I do not nourish only myself." Knowing this, whatever gods are worthy of sacrifice (yajñiya), may those gods unite us with wealth (rayi) in the form of cows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O gods) विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—being everywhere
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- ऊर्जा (*ūrjā*)—with curds
- घृतेन (*ghṛtena*)—with ghee
- पयसा (*payasā*)—with milk
- परि दधे (*pari dadhe*)—I fill you and make you well nourished
- ये के च देवाः (*ye ke ca devāḥ*)—whichever gods
- यज्ञियाः (*yajñiyāḥ*)—are worthy of sacrifice
- ते (*te*)—all of them
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- रय्या (*rayyā*)—with wealth
- सं सृजंतु (*saṃ sṛjaṃtu*)—let them unite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, I fill you, who are present everywhere, with curds, ghee and milk and make you well nourished. Whatever gods are worthy of sacrifice, may all of them unite us with wealth.

##### English translation
I nourish you gods, who are everywhere present, with curds, with butter, with milk ; may all those deities who are entitled to worship reward us with riches.

> भूम्या॒श्चत॑स्रः प्र॒दिश॒स्ताभ्य॑ एना॒ नि व॑र्तय ॥ ८ ॥

> मंत्रद्रष्टर्षिः स्वात्वानं गाश्च संबोध्याह । हे मदीयात्मन् त्वं गा आ

> आनिवर्तध्वं । अभिमुख्यॆनागच्छत । पुनरप्याह । हे मदीयात्मन् त्वं नि वर्तय ।
> गोसंचरणस्थानादपगच्छंतीर्गा इतोऽभिगंत्रिः कुरु । यूयमपि हे गावः
> निवर्तमानाः सत्यो निवर्तन । निवर्तध्वं । इदानीं स्वात्मा गावश्चर्षि० प्रति ब्रुवते।
> हे ऋषे अहं कुतो गा निवर्तयामिति कुतो वयं निवर्तयामह इत्यात्मना
> गोभिश्च पृष्टः सन्नाह । भूम्याः पृथिव्याश्चतस्रः प्रदिशश्च तुःसंख्यायुक्ताः प्रकृष्टा
> या दिशः संति ताभ्यो दिग्ध एना गा नि वर्तय । हे आत्मन् मदभिमुखीः कुरु ।
> हे गावः यूयमपि ताभ्यो दिग्भो निवर्तर्ध्वमिति सामर्थ्यल्लब्धं । यद्वा ।
> अब्दैवतपक्षेऽपि सूक्तार्थो यथा घटते तथा योजना कर्तव्या ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer addresses himself and the cows. "O my self, make the cows turn to face me" (the āṅ is construed with this verb as well), meaning: win them over by praise and sacrifice and bring them near. "O cows, being propitiated, you too come back facing us." Again: "O my self, bring back (ni vartaya) the cows that are going away from the pasture, make them come hither. You also, O cows, being turned back, return." Now the self and the cows address the seer: "O seer, from where am I to bring the cows back, from where are we to return?" Asked thus by his self and by the cows, he says: the earth has four directions (pradiśaḥ); from those directions bring these cows back, O self, make them face me. "O cows, you too return from those directions" is obtained by implication. Alternatively, the interpretation should be made so that the meaning of the sūkta fits also on the view that its deity is the waters (abdaivata).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आ वर्तय (*ā vartaya*)—make the cows turn back
- निवर्तन (*nivartana*)—O cows, return
- निवर्तय (*nivartaya*)—make them come back to the house
- निवर्तन (*nivartana*)—come to the house
- भूम्यूः (*bhūmyūḥ*)—the earth
- चतस्रः (*catasraḥ*)—four
- प्रदिशः (*pradiśaḥ*)—directions there are
- ताभ्यः (*tābhyaḥ*)—from all those directions
- एनाः (*enāḥ*)—these cows
- निवर्तय (*nivartaya*)—make them turn back

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Make the cows turn back. O cows, you also come back. Return to the house. The earth has four directions. From all those directions bring the cows back.

##### English translation
Come back (you cows), bring them back; return (you cows), bring them back; and (you cows) coming back, return; there are four quarters of the earth, bring them back from them,
