## Sūkta 20 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भद्रमिति दशर्चं चतर्थं सूक्तं । अद्यैकपदा दशाक्षरा विराट् । अग्निमीळे
> भुजामित्येषानुष्टुप् नवमी विराट् दशमी त्रिष्टुप् मध्यॆ पड्डायत्रः । इदमादीनां सप्तसूक्तानामिंद्रपुत्रः प्रजापतिपुत्रो वा विमद ऋषिर्वसुक्रपुत्रो
> वसुकृदाख्यो वा । इदमुत्तरं चाग्नेयं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । सप्पोत्तराण्यंद्रो विमदः प्रजापत्यो वा वासुको वसुकृद्वा भद्रं दशाग्नेयं तु गायत्रमाद्यैकपदा पाद एव ना शांत्यर्थः परानुष्टुबंत्ये विराट् त्रिष्टुभाविति ॥ गतो
> विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*) has ten ṛks and is the fourth sūkta (of the anuvāka). Its first verse is a one-footed (ekapadā) virāj of ten syllables; the second, अग्निमीळे भुजां (*agnimīḷe bhujāṃ*), is an anuṣṭubh; the ninth is a virāj, the tenth a triṣṭubh, and the middle ones are gāyatrī. For the seven sūktas beginning with this one the seer is Vimada, the son of Indra or of Prajāpati, or Vasukṛt, son of Vasukra. This and the following sūkta are addressed to Agni. He cites the Anukramaṇī: सप्पोत्तराण्यंद्रो विमदः प्रजापत्यो वा वासुको वसुकृद्वा भद्रं दशाग्नेयं तु गायत्रमाद्यैकपदा पाद एव ना शांत्यर्थः परानुष्टुबंत्ये विराट् त्रिष्टुभाविति ॥ (*sappottarāṇyaṃdro vimadaḥ prajāpatyo vā vāsuko vasukṛdvā bhadraṃ daśāgneyaṃ tu gāyatramādyaikapadā pāda eva nā śāṃtyarthaḥ parānuṣṭubaṃtye virāṭ triṣṭubhāviti ‖*) The viniyoga has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda (Kannada)

This sūkta beginning भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*) is the fourth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It contains ten ṛks. The first ṛk is of the metre called ekapadā virāj of ten syllables. The second ṛk, अग्निमाळे भुजां (*agnimāḷe bhujāṃ*), is in anuṣṭubh; the remaining six are in gāyatrī. For the seven sūktas from this one onward the seer is Vimada, son of Indra or of Prajāpati, or Vasukṛt, son of Vasukra. Agni is the deity of this sūkta and of the next. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: सप्तोत्तराण्यंद्रो विमदः प्राजापत्यो वा वसुक्रो वसुकृद्वा भद्रं दशाग्नेयं तु गायत्रमाद्यैकपदा पाद एव नाशांत्यर्थः परानुष्टुबंत्ये विराट्‌त्रिष्टुभौ (*saptottarāṇyaṃdro vimadaḥ prājāpatyo vā vasukro vasukṛdvā bhadraṃ daśāgneyaṃ tu gāyatramādyaikapadā pāda eva nāśāṃtyarthaḥ parānuṣṭubaṃtye virāṭtriṣṭubhau*). The viniyoga has been stated earlier.

Sūkta—20
Maṇḍala—10; Anuvāka—2; Sūkta—20.
Aṣṭaka—7; Adhyāya—7; Varga—2, 3.
Number of ṛks in the sūkta—10.
Seer: Vimada Aindra, or Prājāpatya, or Vasukṛt Vāsukra.
Deity: Agni.
Metre: 1. Ekapadā (पाद एव ना शांत्यर्थः (*pāda eva nā śāṃtyarthaḥ*)); 2. Anuṣṭubh; 3–8. Gāyatrī; 9. Virāj; 10. Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भ॒द्रं नो॒ अपि॑ वातय॒ मनः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भद्रं नो अपि वाशय मनः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 636

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं नोऽस्माकं मनो भद्रं शुभयुक्तमपि वातय । अपिरत्र
> धात्वर्थानुवादी । अगमय । त्वत्संबंधिस्तोत्रकरणे प्रेरयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, cause our mind to go (vātaya) towards what is auspicious (bhadra)." The word अपि (*api*) here merely repeats the sense of the root: "make go", that is, "impel us to the making of praise addressed to you."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—auspicious
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind
- नः (*naḥ*)—towards us
- अपि वातय (*api vātaya*)—cause to turn

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, turn your gracious and auspicious mind towards us and favour us.

##### English translation
(Agni), manifest towards us a favourable mind.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निमी॑ळे भु॒जां यवि॑ष्ठं शा॒सा मि॒त्रं दु॒र्धरी॑तुं ।  
> यस्य॒ धर्म॒न्तस्मिन् १ १॒॑रेनीः॑ सप॒र्यंति॑ मा॒तुरूधः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निं । ईळे । भुजां । यविष्ठं । शासा । मित्रं । दुःधरीतुं ।  
> यस्य । धर्मन् । स्वः । एनीः । सपर्यंति । मातुः । ऊधः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भुजां हविर्भुजां देवानां मध्यॆ यविष्ठ महन्यहन्यग्निहोत्रादिकर्मार्थं
> जायमानत्वादतिशयेन युवानं शासानुशासनेन मित्रं । यस्मादिदं कर्तव्यमिदं न कर्तव्यमिति सर्वमनुशास्ति तस्मात्सर्वस्य मित्रभूतमित्यर्थः । दुर्धरीतुं
> दुर्धरणीयं संग्रामे शत्रुभिर्दुर्निवारणेयं एवंभूतमग्निमीळे। सौमि । अपि
> च यस्याग्नेर्धर्मन्धर्मण्यग्निहोत्रादिके कर्मणि स्वर्द्युलोकमादित्यं सर्वं देवजातं वैनीरेन्यः प्रतिगंत्र आहुतयः स्तुतयश्च सपर्यंति परिचरंति सेवंते । यद्वा। स्वः सपर्यंतीत्यनयोः सामानाधिकरण्यं। अत्र स्वरित्यव्ययं सर्वशब्दो निपातः !

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among the oblation-eating gods (bhujām) Agni is yaviṣṭha, exceedingly young, being born day after day for the agnihotra and other rites. He is a friend by instruction (śāsā), since he instructs "this is to be done, this is not to be done"; thus he is a friend of all. He is durdharītu, hard to hold, hard for enemies to ward off in battle. Such an Agni I praise. Also, in the rite (dharman) of that Agni, the offerings and praises that go to the heavenly world (svar), to Āditya and to all the hosts of gods, serve and attend upon him. Alternatively स्वः (*svaḥ*) and सपर्यंति (*saparyaṃti*) are construed in apposition; here स्वः (*svaḥ*) is the indeclinable, a particle meaning "all". **NOTE**

### Printed p. 637

> स्वः सर्वे देवा एनीरात्मनः प्रतिगंत्रीराहुतीः स्तुतीश्च सपर्यंति सेवंते । उपजीवंतीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । लुप्तोपममेतत्। मातुर्गॊरूधः क्षीरोपसंहारस्थानं प्रति यथा वत्सा उपजीवंति तद्वत् । तमग्निमीळ इति पूर्वेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Sanskrit explains that all the gods approach (serve) the oblations and praises that go to them, that is, they live on them. The example: as calves live on the udder of the mother cow, the place where milk is gathered. This is an elliptical comparison. The sentence is connected with the preceding "I praise that Agni."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मातुः (*mātuḥ*)—of the mother cow
- ऊधः (*ūdhaḥ*)—as the calf lives by drinking the milk of the udder
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Agni
- धर्मन् (*dharman*)—in rites such as the Agnihotra
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—heavenward
- एनीः (*enīḥ*)—the oblations that go
- सपर्यंति (*saparyaṃti*)—the gods partake of them and are nourished; such is he
- भुजां (*bhujāṃ*)—among the gods who partake of the oblation
- यविष्ठं (*yaviṣṭhaṃ*)—the most youthful
- शासा (*śāsā*)—by instruction
- मित्रं (*mitraṃ*)—one who is a friend
- दुर्धरीतुं (*durdharītuṃ*)—unconquered in battles
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- ईळे (*īḷe*)—I praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a calf takes shelter at the udder of its mother cow and drinks the milk, so the gods take shelter in the oblations that go heavenward in the Agnihotra and other rites of whichever Agni, and partake of them. I praise that Agni, the most youthful among the gods who partake of the oblation, a friend through his instruction, and unconquered in battles.

##### English translation
I glorify Agni, the young of the feeders (on oblations), friendly in counsel, difficult to resist, at whose rite the oblations seek heaven, as (calves) the udder of the mother cow,

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यमा॒सा कृ॒पनी॑ळं भा॒साके॑तुं व॒र्धयं॑ति ।  
> भ्राज॑ते॒ श्रेणि॑दन् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । आसा । कृपनीळं । भासाकेतुं । पर्धयंति ।  
> भ्राजते । श्रेणिदन् ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 638

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्तोतारो यष्टारश्चासा स्तुतिहविर्लक्षणेनोपासनेन यमग्निं वर्धयंति ।
> कीदृशं । कृपनीळं कर्मस्थानं । कर्माधारमित्यर्थः । भासाकेतुं ज्वालालक्षणज्ञापकं दीप्तेः कर्तारं वा । यच्छब्दश्रुतेस्तच्छब्दोऽध्याहार्यः । सोऽग्निः श्रेणिदन्
> स्तोतृभ्यो यष्टृभ्योऽभीष्टफलमूहप्रदः शत्रुभ्यो ज्वालापंक्तिप्रदो वा
> एवंभूतः सन् भ्राजते । भासते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The singers and sacrificers magnify Agni with their mouth, that is, with the worship consisting of praise and oblation. What kind of Agni? He is the "place of rites" (कृपनीळं (*kṛpanīḷaṃ*)), the support of rites; and भासाकेतुं (*bhāsāketuṃ*), one whose sign is the flame, or the maker of brightness. Because the relative "yam" is heard, the demonstrative "that" must be supplied. That Agni, श्रेणिदन् (*śreṇidan*), giving the desired fruit to praisers and sacrificers (or giving rows of flame to enemies), shines.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कृपनीळं (*kṛpanīḷaṃ*)—the support of rites
- भासाकेतुं (*bhāsāketuṃ*)—one whose sign is the flame
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Agni
- आसा (*āsā*)—with praises and oblations
- वर्धयंति (*vardhayaṃti*)—the praisers and sacrificers nourish; that Agni
- श्रेणिदन् (*śreṇidan*)—giving excellent wealth to worshippers
- भ्राजते (*bhrājate*)—shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni who is the support of all rites and whose sign is the flame, whom praisers and sacrificers nourish with praises and oblations, shines, giving excellent wealth to worshippers.

##### English translation
He whom (the worshippers) magnify with their mouth, the sustainer of pious works ; whose banner is the light, he shines, bestowing upon them all their desires.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क॒विर॒भ्रं दीद्या॑नः ॥ ४ ॥

> कविः । अभ्रं । दीद्यानः । ४ ॥

### Printed p. 639

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विशां यजमानमनुष्याणामर्यो गंतव्यो गातुर्गमनशीलोऽग्निर्दि
> द्यानो दीप्यमानो यद्यदैति ऊर्ध्वं गच्छति तदा दिवो द्युलोकस्यांतान्पर्यंतान्यविर्मेधावी सोऽग्निः प्राणट् । प्रकर्षेण व्याप्न्नोति । अभ्रं मेघोपलक्षितमंतरिक्षं च व्याप्न्नोति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is the lord (अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)), the one to be approached, of the people, the human sacrificers, and is of moving nature. When, shining, he goes upward, then that sage Agni pervades fully the ends of the heaven, and also the atmosphere marked by clouds.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विशां (*viśāṃ*)—of the sacrificers and others
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—the lord
- गातुः (*gātuḥ*)—Agni, of moving nature
- दीद्यानः (*dīdyānaḥ*)—shining
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- एति (*eti*)—he goes upward, then
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—the wise Agni
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heaven
- अंतान् (*aṃtān*)—the end portions
- प्र अनट् (*pra anaṭ*)—pervades fully
- अभ्रं (*abhraṃ*)—pervades the atmosphere also

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the lord of sacrificers and others, of moving nature, when he goes upward shining, pervades fully the ends of the heaven and the atmosphere.

##### English translation
The refuge of the people, the mover, who when he moves, penetrates to the ends of the sky ; the sage illumining the firmament.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मानुषस्य यजमानस्य यज्ञे यजनीये यागे हव्या हव्यानि हवींषि
> जुषत्सेवमानोग्नि र्यभ्वोरुभूतो बहुज्वालोपेत ऊर्ध्वस्तस्थौ ! उत्तिष्ठति ।
> ऊर्ध्वं ज्वलतीत्यर्थः। अपि चायमग्निः प्राग्वंशादारभ्य सद्मदनं सौमिकीं वेदिं
> मिन्वन् परिच्छिंदन् पुरः पुरस्तादुत्तरवेदिशालामुखीयात्प्रणीयमानः सन्नेति ।
> गच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the sacrifice of the human sacrificer, Agni, partaking of the oblations, stands upward, becoming large, with many flames; that is, he blazes upward. Further, this Agni, beginning from the Prāgvaṃśa, measuring out (मिन्वन् (*minvan*)) the Soma altar (the seat), advances in front, being led forward from the front towards the entrance of the northern altar-hall.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मानुषस्य (*mānuṣasya*)—of the sacrificer
- यज्ञे (*yajñe*)—in the sacrifice
- हव्या (*havyā*)—the oblations
- जुषत् (*juṣat*)—Agni who partakes
- ऋभ्वा (*ṛbhvā*)—with exceedingly large flame
- ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)—upward
- तस्थौ (*tasthau*)—stands
- सद्म (*sadma*)—the place of sacrifice
- मिन्वन् (*minvan*)—measuring
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—in front
- एति (*eti*)—moves

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the sacrifice of the sacrificer, Agni, partaking of the oblations, stands upward with an exceedingly large flame. Measuring the place of sacrifice, he moves in front.

##### English translation
Accepting the oblations (offered) at the sacrifice of the worshipper, he blazes up, with a mighty flame ; fixing his abode, he advances.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य उक्तगुणविशिष्टोऽग्निः । हीत्येतदवधारणे । स एवाग्निः क्षेमः कुशलहेतुः । सर्वस्य परिपालनहेतुरित्यर्थः । हविः पुरोडाशादिकं च स एव हविषस्तन्निमित्तत्वात् । यज्ञो यागोऽपि स एव तस्यापि तद्धेतुत्वात् । किंच श्रुष्टित् क्षिप्रमेवास्याग्नेर्गातुर्गमनशीलोऽधिष्ठात्रात्मैति । देवानामाह्वानार्थं गच्छति ।
> गत्वा च प्रत्यागच्छंतं वाशीमंतं स्तुतिलक्षणया वाचोपेतमग्निं प्रति देवा अपि
> गच्छंतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni endowed with the stated qualities (हि (*hi*) is for emphasis) is himself the cause of well-being, the protector of all. The oblation, the cake and the rest, is he himself, since he is its cause; the sacrifice too is he, since he is its cause. Further, quickly the moving spirit, the presiding self of this Agni, goes to invite the gods; and having gone, the gods also go towards Agni, who returns bearing praise-laden speech (the verb is to be supplied).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सः (*saḥ*)—the famous
- क्षेमः (*kṣemaḥ*)—the bringer of auspiciousness
- हविः (*haviḥ*)—the oblation in the form of cake and the rest
- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—he himself is the sacrifice
- श्रुष्टीत् (*śruṣṭīt*)—quickly
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- गातुः (*gātuḥ*)—the moving power
- एति (*eti*)—goes to the gods
- वाशीमंतं (*vāśīmaṃtaṃ*)—endowed with praise
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni himself
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods also approach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The famous Agni is the bringer of auspiciousness. He himself is the sacrifice and the oblation in the form of cake and the rest. The moving power of this Agni approaches the gods. The gods too approach Agni, who is endowed with praise.

##### English translation
Agni is capable (of protecting all men), he is himself the oblation, and the sacrifice ; rapidly indeed does his spirit move. The gods come to Agni, who bears the praises.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अश्रैतवाक्यताय्कॆ यत्तच्छब्दावध्याहार्यौ । अपरार्धर्चिः पूर्वं व्याख्येयः । आयुं देवानामाह्वानार्थं दूत्येन गंतारं यमग्निमद्रेः सूनुमत्मनः
> पुत्रमाहुः त्वमद्भ्यस्तमत्कनस्परि । ऋ. सं. २-१-१ । इत्येववादयो मंत्रा वदंति ।
> यज्ञसहं यागस्य वोढारं । धारयितारमित्यर्थः । तमग्निमभिलक्ष्य दुवः परिचरणमिषे । इच्छामि । किमर्थं । पूर्वस्य । आत्र पूर्वशब्द उत्कृष्टवाची । उत्कृष्टस्य
> शेवस्य स्वर्गापवर्गलक्षणसुखस्य प्राप्तर्थमिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Since the sentence is not complete, "yat" and "tat" are to be supplied. The latter half of the verse is to be explained first. Agni, who goes as messenger to invite the gods, is called by Mantras such as त्वमद्भ्यस्तमत्कनस्परि । ऋ. सं. २-१-१ । (*tvamadbhyastamatkanaspari | ṛ. saṃ. 2-1-1 |*) "the son of the stone" (अद्रेः सूनुं (*adreḥ sūnuṃ*)), that is, of himself (?). यज्ञसहं (*yajñasahaṃ*) is the bearer of the sacrifice, the one who sustains it. Having Agni in view, I desire (इषे (*iṣe*)) the service (दुवः (*duvaḥ*)). For what? पूर्वस्य (*pūrvasya*): here *pūrva* means excellent: to obtain excellent happiness (शेवस्य (*śevasya*)), consisting of heaven and liberation (the words "for obtaining" are to be supplied). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आयुं (*āyuṃ*)—who approaches the gods
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- अद्रॆः सूनुं (*adrèḥ sūnuṃ*)—as the son of the stone (Adri)
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—the Mantras praise
- पूर्वस्य (*pūrvasya*)—excellent
- शेवस्य (*śevasya*)—for happiness
- यज्ञसहं (*yajñasahaṃ*)—of Agni the bearer of the sacrifice
- दुवः (*duvaḥ*)—the service
- इषे (*iṣe*)—I desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Mantras praise Agni, who approaches the gods, as the son of Adri. I desire the service of Agni, the bearer of the sacrifice, for the gain of excellent happiness.

##### English translation
Agni, who goes to (summon the gods), the bearer of the oblations, whom men call the sow of the stone ; him I desire to worship (for the sake) of supreme felicity.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नरो नेतारो ये के च ये कीचित्पुत्रपौत्रादयोऽस्मदस्माकं संति ।
> आकारः पूरकः । ते पुत्रपौत्रादयो वामे वननीये संभजनीये विश्वेद्विश्वस्मिन्नेव
> पश्वादिधन आ स्युः । आ समंताद्भवेयुः । उपविशेयुरित्याशास्महे । किं कुर्वंतः ।
> अग्निमंगनादिगुणविशिष्टं देवं हविषा पुरोडाशादिकेन वर्धंतो वर्धयंतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Men," leaders, whoever of our sons, grandsons and others there are (the ā is a filler): may those sons and grandsons be settled in the desirable (वामे (*vāme*)), the enjoyable, entire wealth of cattle and the like. We hope they may be seated all around. Doing what? Increasing Agni, the god endowed with the qualities of limb-adornment and so on, with oblations such as the cake.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—belonging to us
- ये के च (*ye ke ca*)—whichever
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—sons and others there are
- ते (*te*)—all of them
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblations
- वर्धंतः (*vardhaṃtaḥ*)—nourishing
- वामे (*vāme*)—excellent
- विश्वेत् (*viśvet*)—with all wealth
- आ स्युः (*ā syuḥ*)—may they be united

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all whichever sons, grandsons and others belong to us, nourishing Agni with oblations, be united with excellent and entire wealth.

##### English translation
May all the men who belong to us be (gratified) in all that is desirable, augmenting Agni with oblations.

### Printed p. 644

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र यच्छब्दमध्याहृत्य योज्यं । यामः । याति गच्छत्यस्मिन्निति यामो
> रथः प्रजापतिना निर्मितः । कीदृशः । कृष्णोऽसितवर्णः श्वेतः सितवर्णोरुऽष
> आरोचमानो ब्रध्नो महानृज ऋजुगाम्युतापि च शोणो रक्तवर्णो यशस्वान्कीर्तिमान् । यद्वा । यश इति धननाम । हविर्लक्षणेन धनेन युक्तः । हिरण्यरूपं सुवर्णसदृशं तं रथमस्याग्नेरर्थाय जनिता सर्वस्य जगतो जनयिता
> प्रजापतिर्जजान । जनयामास । अस्मै दत्तवानित्यर्थः । कथमेकस्यॆव रथस्य कृष्णादिनानारूपत्वं संभवतीति चेत् अग्नेः सामर्थ्यतिशयेन संभवतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा ।
> हिरण्यरूपमिति रथवाचिना शब्देन सह सामानाधिकरण्यात्कृष्णादिशब्दा द्वितीयांतॆ_
> त्वेन योज्याः । अत्र सर्वगुणोक्तरथवत्तयाग्निः स्तूयत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says the relative word यत् (*yat*) is to be supplied and construed here. यामः (*yāmaḥ*) is the chariot in which one goes, created by Prajāpati. Of what kind? कृष्णः (*kṛṣṇaḥ*) is dark-coloured, श्वेतः (*śvetaḥ*) white, अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*) shining, ब्रध्नः (*bradhnaḥ*) great, ऋज्रः (*ṛjraḥ*) going straight, शोणः (*śoṇaḥ*) red, and यशस्वान् (*yaśasvān*) famous. Or else *yaśaḥ* is a name for wealth: it is endowed with wealth in the form of oblations. Prajāpati, the begetter of the whole world, produced (जजान (*jajāna*)) for this Agni that chariot, gold-like in form; that is, he gave it to him. If it is asked how one chariot can have the various forms black and so on, the answer is that it is possible through Agni's surpassing power. Or else, because of their agreement in case with the chariot-denoting word हिरण्यरूपं (*hiraṇyarūpaṃ*), the words "black" and so on are to be construed as in the accusative. The sense is that Agni is here praised as possessing a chariot with all these qualities.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यशस्वान् (*yaśasvān*)—very famous
- यामः (*yāmaḥ*)—the chariot of this Agni
- कृष्णः (*kṛṣṇaḥ*)—black-coloured
- श्वेतः (*śvetaḥ*)—white-coloured
- अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—golden-hued
- ब्रध्नः (*bradhnaḥ*)—great
- ऋज्रः (*ṛjraḥ*)—going straight
- उत (*uta*)—and
- शोणः (*śoṇaḥ*)—red-coloured, it is
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- हिरण्यरूपं (*hiraṇyarūpaṃ*)—the chariot of golden form
- जनिता (*janitā*)—Prajāpati, the begetter of all
- जजान (*jajāna*)—produced

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The chariot of this very famous Agni is black, white, golden-hued, great, going straight, and red. The begetter of all, Prajāpati, produced this golden chariot of Agni.

##### English translation
His chariot is black, white red, tawny, dark red, crimson, and glorious; the progenitor of all has given him a chariot of Gold.

> अभारित्यभाः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एवमुक्तप्रकारेण हे उर्जो नपादोषधिवनस्पतिपितृभूतस्यान्नस्य पौत्र
> हे अग्ने अमृतेभिरमृतैर्हविलक्षणैरन्नॆः सजोषाः संगतो विमदो नामर्षिर्मनीषां प्रकृष्टां बुद्धिं कामयमानः संस्थे तुभ्यं गिरः स्तुतिलक्षणा वाच आ
> वक्षत् । अभिमुख्येनोक्तवान् ॥ वक्तेश्छंदसि लेटि रूपं ॥ ततस्त्वमेतज्ञा त्वा
> सुमतीरियानः शोभनलक्षणा बुद्धिः संगमयन्निषमन्नमूर्जं क्षीरादिकं रसं च
> सुक्षितिं शोभननिवासं । यद्वा । क्षितयो मनुष्याः । शोभनपुत्रपौत्रादिकं ।
> यत्किंचिद्देयमस्ति तद्विश्वं धनं चाभाः । तस्मै विमदायाहर । देहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the manner stated, O Agni, grandson of strength (ऊर्जो नपात् (*ūrjo napāt*)), that is, grandson of the food that is plants, trees and ancestors: united with the immortal foods, the oblations, the seer named Vimada, desiring मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*), excellent understanding, has addressed to you speech in the form of praise; आ वक्षत् (*ā vakṣat*) means he has spoken facing you, a Leṭ form of the root *vac* in the Veda. Therefore you, knowing this and bringing about सुमतीः (*sumatīḥ*), good understanding, convey to him food (इषं (*iṣaṃ*)), strength (ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)), that is, milk and other juice, and सुक्षितिं (*sukṣitiṃ*), a good dwelling. Or else क्षितयो (*kṣitayo*) are men: good sons, grandsons and the like. Whatever is to be given, all that, and wealth, bring (आभाः (*ābhāḥ*)) to that Vimada; give.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऊर्जो नपात् (*ūrjo napāt*)—grandson of food
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अमृतेभिः (*amṛtebhiḥ*)—with foods in the form of oblations
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—united
- विमदः (*vimadaḥ*)—the seer named Vimada
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—desiring discernment
- ते (*te*)—addressing you
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—speech in the form of praise
- आ वक्षत् (*ā vakṣat*)—recites and offers
- सुमतीरियानः (*sumatīriyānaḥ*)—you who bring about excellent knowledge
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)—milk and the like
- सुक्षितिं (*sukṣitiṃ*)—excellent dwellings
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—all wealth
- आभाः (*ābhāḥ*)—bring to him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, grandson of food, the seer Vimada, united with foods in the form of oblations and desiring discernment, recites and offers to you speech in the form of praise. You who bring about excellent knowledge, bring to him food, milk and the like, excellent dwellings and all wealth.

##### English translation
Grandson of strength, Agni, who are gratified by the ambrosial (viands), Vimada, (desirous of) wisdom, has recited your praises; do you, approaching with a kind intention, bestow upon us food, strength, and a prosperous abode.

### Printed p. 646
## Sūkta 21 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निं नेत्यष्टर्चं पंचमं सूक्तमास्तारपंक्तिच्छंदस्कं । आद्यौ गायत्रा
> पादौ ततो द्वौ जागत् सास्तारपंक्तिः । ऋषिदेवते पूर्ववत् । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> अग्निं नाष्टावास्तारपांक्तमिति ॥ पृष्ठस्य चतुर्थेऽहन्याग्निं न स्वव्यक्तिभिरित्याज्यं ।
> आ. ७-११ । इति ॥ महाव्रत अग्निमारुते यावतीष्त्वक्ष्विळांदं साम स्तुवीरन्
> तदानीमादितस्तावत्य ऋचोऽनुरूपार्थाः । सूत्रितं च । यदीळांदं भूयसीषु
> चेत् स्तुवीरन्नाग्निं न स्वव्यक्तिभिरिति तावतीरनुरूपः । ऐ. आ. ५-३-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta अग्निं न (*agniṃ na*) has eight Ṛks and is the fifth sūkta; its metre is Āstārapaṅkti. The first two pādas are Gāyatra, then two are Jagatī; that is Āstārapaṅkti. Seer and deity as before. The Anukramaṇī says: अग्निं नाष्टावास्तारपांक्तमिति (*agniṃ nāṣṭāvāstārapāṃktamiti*). On the fourth day of the Pṛṣṭha rite it is the Ājya (hymn): *agniṃ na svavyaktibhirityājyaṃ* (Ā. 7-11). In the Mahāvrata, when at the Agnimāruta the Sāman called Iḷānda is chanted, the Ṛks from the beginning, as many as there are, serve as Anurūpa verses. It is stated in the sūtra: यदीळांदं भूयसीषु चेत् स्तुवीरन्नाग्निं न स्वव्यक्तिभिरिति तावतीरनुरूपः (*yadīḷāṃdaṃ bhūyasīṣu cet stuvīrannāgniṃ na svavyaktibhiriti tāvatīranurūpaḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-3-2).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning आग्निं न (*āgniṃ na*) is the fifth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer and deity are the same as in the preceding sūkta. Its metre is Āstārapaṅkti: if in a Ṛk the first two pādas are like the Gāyatrī metre and the remaining two like the Jagatī metre, that Ṛk is Āstārapaṅkti. The Anukramaṇī's statement आग्निं नाष्टावास्तारपांक्तं (*āgniṃ nāṣṭāvāstārapāṃktaṃ*) is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra आग्निं न स्वव्यक्तिभिरित्याज्यं (*āgniṃ na svavyaktibhirityājyaṃ*) (Ā. 7-11): this sūkta is to be recited for the Ājyaśastra mantras on the fourth day of the Pṛṣṭha sacrifice. When the Āgnimāruta śastra mantras are recited in the Mahāvrata rite, praise is to be made with the Sāman mantra called Iḷānda; then the mantras of this sūkta are to be recited at the beginning as Anurūpa mantras, as explained by the Aitareya Āraṇyaka sentence यदीळांदं भूयसीषु चेत् स्तुवीरन्नाग्निं न स्वव्यक्तिभिरिति तावतीरनुरूपः (*yadīḷāṃdaṃ bhūyasīṣu cet stuvīrannāgniṃ na svavyaktibhiriti tāvatīranurūpaḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-3-2).

Sūkta 21. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 21; Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 7; Vargas 4, 5. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8. Ṛṣi: Vimada Aindra, or Prājāpatya, or Vasukṛt Vāsukra. Devatā: Agni. Metre: Āstārapaṅkti.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आग्निं न स्ववृ॑क्तिभि॒र्होता॑रं त्वा वृणीमहे ।  
> य॒ज्ञाय॑ स्ती॒र्णब॑र्हिषे॒ वि वो॒ मदे॑ शी॒रं पा॑व॒कशो॑चिषं॒  ॑
> विवक्षसे ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 647

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । अग्निं । न । स्ववृक्तिभिः । होतारं । त्वा । वृणीमहे ।  
> यज्ञाय । स्तीर्णबर्हिषे । वि । वः । मदे । शीरं । पावकशोचिषं । विवक्षसे ॥१॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने वस्तव स्वभूते विमद एतदाख्य ऋषौ मयियायं स्तुतिः प्रवृत्तास्ति ।
> नेति संप्रत्यर्थे । आतो वयमिदानीं स्वव्यक्तिभिः स्वयंकृताभिर्दोषवर्जिताभिः
> स्तुतिभिर्होतारं देवानामाह्वातारं होमनिष्पादकं वाग्निं त्वा त्वामा वृणीमहे । अभिमुख्येन संभजामहे । किमर्थं । स्तीर्णबर्हिषे यज्ञाय ॥ तादर्थ्ये
> चतुर्थी ॥ यज्ञार्थं । कीदृशं । शीरमोषध्यादिशु सर्वत्रानुशायिनं पावकशोचिषं शोधकदीप्तिं । विवक्षसे । महन्नामैतत् । हे अग्ने त्वमपि महान्भवसि ।
> यद्वा । विमदे यज्ञस्य संबंधिनः सोमस्य पानजन्यविविधमदार्थं त्वामावृणीमह इति योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, in me, the seer named Vimada, who belong to you, this praise has arisen. न (*na*) is in the sense of "now". Therefore we now invoke (आ वृणीमहे (*ā vṛṇīmahe*)) you, the Hotṛ, the summoner of the gods or the accomplisher of the offering, Agni, with our own faultless praises, स्वव्यक्तिभिः (*svavyaktibhiḥ*) made by ourselves, facing you. For what? For the sacrifice with strewn sacred grass (स्तीर्णबर्हिषे (*stīrṇabarhiṣe*)), the dative being of purpose. Of what kind is he? शीरं (*śīraṃ*), lying within plants and the like everywhere; पावकशोचिषं (*pāvakaśociṣaṃ*), with purifying brilliance. विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*) is a name meaning "great": you, Agni, too are great. Or else: we invoke you for the manifold exhilaration (विमदे (*vimade*)) arising from drinking the Soma belonging to the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni,) वः (*vaḥ*)—belonging to you
- विमदे (*vimade*)—in me, named Vimada, praise has arisen
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—who calls the gods
- शीरं (*śīraṃ*)—who lies hidden in plants and the like
- पावकशोचिषं (*pāvakaśociṣaṃ*)—who has purifying radiance
- अग्निं त्वा (*agniṃ tvā*)—you
- स्तीर्णबर्हिषे (*stīrṇabarhiṣe*)—where the seat of darbha grass is spread and ready
- यज्ञाय (*yajñāya*)—for the conduct of the sacrifice
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—with excellent praises
- आ वृणीमहे (*ā vṛṇīmahe*)—we worship and call
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—(O Agni) you are great

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, in me, Vimada, who belong to you, praise has arisen. You who call the gods, who lie hidden in plants and the like, and who have purifying radiance, we worship and call with excellent praises for the conduct of the sacrifice at which the darbha seat is spread. O Agni, you are great.

##### English translation
We invoke you now, Agni, invoker (of the gods), with our voluntary (praises) for the sacrifice, at which the sacredgrass is spread; you, who underlie (all things), who (diffuse) purifying radiance, (we invoke) for your exhilaration ; you are mighty.

> वेति । त्वां । उपसेचनी । वि । वः । मदे । ऋजीतिः । अग्ने । आहुतिः । विवक्षसे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वाभुवः स्वप्रकाशेन दीप्यमाना अश्वराधसो व्याप्तधनास्ते यजमाना हे
> अग्ने त्वामु त्वामेव शुंभंति । शोभयंति । यज्ञे हविर्भिर्दिर्पयंतीत्यर्थः ।
> किंचोपसेचनी तवोपरिक्षरणशीलर्जितिऋजुगामिनी हूयमानाहुतिर्हे अग्ने
> त्वां वेति । गच्छति । किमर्थं । वस्तव मदे मदनिमित्ते । तृप्त्यर्थमित्यर्थः । किंच
> त्वमपि विवक्षसे । महान्भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificers, self-radiant (स्वाभुवः (*svābhuvaḥ*)) and possessed of pervasive wealth (अश्वराधसः (*aśvarādhasaḥ*)), adorn you alone, O Agni (शुंभंति (*śuṃbhaṃti*)); that is, they make you shine with oblations at the sacrifice. Further, the उपसेचनी (*upasecanī*), the oblation being offered, which tends to flow over you and goes straight, goes (वेति (*veti*)) to you, O Agni. For what? For मदे (*made*), for exhilaration, that is, for satisfaction. And you too are विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*): you are great.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni,) स्वाभुवः (*svābhuvaḥ*)—self-radiant
- अश्वराधसः (*aśvarādhasaḥ*)—possessing pervasive wealth
- ते (*te*)—the sacrificers
- त्वां उ (*tvāṃ u*)—you alone
- शुंभंति (*śuṃbhaṃti*)—adorn
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- उपसेचनी (*upasecanī*)—that which is offered over you
- ऋजीतिः (*ṛjītiḥ*)—going straight
- आहुतिः (*āhutiḥ*)—the oblation
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—for special satisfaction
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- वेति (*veti*)—approaches
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are great

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the sacrificers, self-radiant and possessed of pervasive wealth, adorn you alone. O Agni, the oblation poured over you, going straight, approaches you for your special satisfaction. O Agni, you are great.

##### English translation
Self-radiant, opulent in horses, they glorify you; the oblation poured out over (you) proceeds in a straight course, Agni, to you for your exhilaration ; you are mighty.

> धर्माणो यज्ञस्य धारयितार ऋत्विजो जुहूभिः संपूर्णाहुतिभिर्होमपात्रैस्वै त्वामेवासते । सेवंते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सिंचतीरिव वृष्टिलक्षणाः
> पृथिवीं सिंचंत्य आप अग्निं यथा स्वपितृत्वेन सेवंते तद्वत् । अग्नेरास इति श्रुतेस्तस्यापां पितृत्वं । यद्वा । जुहूभिः सिंचतीरिव सिच्यमाना आहुतय इव धर्माणस्त्वया धार्यमाणा रश्मयस्त्वै त्वय्यासते । निवसंति । हे अग्ने त्वं कृष्णा
> कृष्णवर्णान्यर्जुनार्जुनानि श्वेतवर्णानि ज्वालांतर्गतरूपाणि च विश्वाः सर्वाः
> श्रियः शोभा अधि धिषे । अधिकं यथा भवति तथा धारयसि । किमर्थं । वो
> युष्माकं सर्वॆषां देवानां विमदे विविधसोमपानजन्यमदार्थं । यत
> एवमतो विवक्षसे । त्वं महान्भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The धर्माणः (*dharmāṇaḥ*), the Ṛtviks who uphold the sacrifice, attend (आसते (*āsate*)) you alone with ladles (जुहूभिः (*juhūbhiḥ*)), the offering vessels filled with oblations. An illustration: सिंचतीरिव (*siṃcatīriva*), as the waters in the form of rain, sprinkling the earth, serve Agni as their father; that Agni is the father of the waters is known from the Śruti अग्नेरास (*agnerāsa*). Or else: like oblations being sprinkled with the ladles, the rays, upheld by you, dwell in you. O Agni, you hold more and more (अधि धिषे (*adhi dhiṣe*)) all splendours (श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*)): the black forms and the white (अर्जुना (*arjunā*)) forms, those seen within the flame. For what? For the manifold exhilaration of you, all the gods, arising from drinking Soma. Because this is so, you are विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*), great.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni,) सिंचतीरिव (*siṃcatīriva*)—as streams of rain sprinkle the earth
- धर्माणः (*dharmāṇaḥ*)—the Ṛtviks, upholders of the sacrifice
- जुहूभिः (*juhūbhiḥ*)—with their oblation vessels
- त्वै (*tvai*)—you alone
- आसते (*āsate*)—serve
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- वः (*vaḥ*)—of you and the other gods
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—for special satisfaction
- कृष्णा (*kṛṣṇā*)—black
- अर्जुना (*arjunā*)—white
- रूपाणि (*rūpāṇi*)—forms
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*)—splendours
- अधि धिषे (*adhi dhiṣe*)—you possess
- विनक्षसे (*vinakṣase*)—you are great **NOTE**

### Printed p. 650

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, as the streams of rain serve the earth, the sacrificial priests, holders of the sacrifice, serve you alone with their oblation-ladles. For the manifold satisfaction of you and of the other gods, you possess forms of black colour and of bright white colour, and all splendours. You are a great one.

##### English translation
The establishers (of the rite) worship you with their ladles (filled with the oblation), like (earth) sprinkling (showers); you sustain exceedingly black forms and white and all beauties for your exhilaration; you are mighty.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अमर्त्यामरणधर्मन् सहसावन्वलवन् एवंभूत हे अग्ने त्वं यं रयिं
> मन्यसे सर्वेषु धनेषु यद्धनं वरिष्ठमिति जानासि चित्रं चायनीयं तं रयिं
> नोऽस्माकं वाजसातयेऽन्नलाभाया भर । आहर । प्रयच्छ । किमर्थं । वो
> युष्माकं सर्वेषां देवानां यज्ञेषु विमदे विविधसोमादिहविर्जन्यमदनिमित्ते । यागेषु नानाप्रकारैर्हविभिर्युष्माकं तर्पणायेत्यर्थः । त्वमपि
> विवक्षसे । महान्भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, immortal and mighty: whatever wealth you consider the best among all riches, that wondrous, desirable wealth, bring to us, give us, for the gaining of food. For what purpose? In the sacrifices of all of you gods, on occasions of विमदे (*vimade*), the delight arising from the various oblations such as Soma; that is, to satisfy you with oblations of many kinds. You too are विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*): you are great.

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni

- मन्यसे (*manyase*)—you consider the best

- तं (*taṃ*)—that wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, free from mortality and exceedingly mighty, the wealth that you consider the best, that attractive wealth, fill into our sacrifices, for our gain of food and for your manifold satisfaction. You are a great one.

##### English translation
Powerful and immortal Agni, bring to us, for our sustenance, the precious wealth which you think best; (bring it) for your exhilaration at the sacrifices; you are mighty.

Agni, generated by Atharvan, is cognizant of all praises ; he is the messenger of Vivaswat, the beloved friend of Yama, for your exhilaration; you are mighty.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, when the rite proceeds well, when the offerings are near at hand in the sacrifices (यज्ञेषु (*yajñeṣu*), in the things to be worshipped), the priests and sacrificers praise you. Moreover, O Agni, you give all desirable riches to the sacrificer who has given an oblation, when there is satisfaction (विमदे (*vimade*)) arising from oblations such as Soma. For that reason विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*): you are great.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, in this well-proceeding sacrifice, when venerable oblations are offered, the priests and others praise you. When you and the other gods are satisfied, you give the sacrificer all the riches he desires. You are a great one.

##### English translation
The (worshipper) glorifies you, Agni, at sacrifices, when the solemnity is being celebrated; you grant in your exhilaration all desirable treasures to the donor (of the oblation); you are mighty.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priest named Hotṛ, graceful, with a face full of poured ghee, radiant, shining, and with his obtained splendours (अक्षभिः (*akṣabhiḥ*)) the most knowing. For what? For your manifold satisfaction arising from oblations such as Soma. Since it is so, विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*): you are great.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who are in the form of the Hotṛ, of attractive form, with a face full of ghee, radiant, endowed with intelligence together with venerable splendours: the sacrificers establish you in the sacrifices for the exceeding satisfaction of you and the other gods. You are a great one.

##### English translation
The men establish you, Agni, at sacrifices, the ministrant priest, graceful, whose face shines with butter, radiant, most intelligent with your eyes, for your exhilaration ; (hence) you are mighty.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने बृहन्महांस्त्वं शुक्रेण दीप्तेन शोचिषा तेजसोरु प्रथयसे ।
> विस्तीर्णं यथा भवति तथा प्रख्यातो भवसि : किंचाभिक्रदन्नाभिमुख्येन युद्धार्थं
> शत्रूनाह्वयन् वृषायसे । वृष इवाचरसि। युद्धकाले दर्पितवृष इव रोरुववद्भवसीत्यर्थः । त्वं माध्यमिकः सञ्जामिषु भगिनीभूतास्वोषधीषु गर्भं बीजलक्षणं दधासि । वृष्टिद्वारेण धारयसि । एकस्मात्प्रजापतेः सकाशादुद्भूतत्वादग्योषध्योर्जामित्वमुचर्यते । कस्मिन्सति । वि वो मदे तव विविधसोमादिहविर्जन्यमदे संजाते सति । यस्मादेवं कृतवानसि तस्मात्त्वं विवक्षसे । महान्भवसि ॥
> विवक्षस इति महन्नाम वक्तेर्वा वहतेर्वा सनंतस्य रूपमिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you who are great, by your bright, shining lustre you become renowned far and wide. Further, bellowing, calling the enemies forward to battle, you act like a bull; that is, in time of battle you roar like a proud bull. You, being the one of the middle region, place the germ, of the nature of seed, in the plants that are as sisters (जामिषु (*jāmiṣu*)); you bear it by way of rain. The kinship (जामित्व (*jāmitva*)) of Agni and the plants is spoken of because both arose from one Prajāpati. When? When your delight arising from the various oblations such as Soma has come about. Since you have done so, विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*): you are great. Nirukta-type remark: विवक्षस इति महन्नाम वक्तेर्वा वहतेर्वा सनंतस्य रूपमिति॥ (*vivakṣasa iti mahannāma vaktervā vahatervā sanaṃtasya rūpamiti‖*)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—you of great form
- शुक्रेण (*śukreṇa*)—with shining
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—lustre
- उरु (*uru*)—exceedingly
- प्रथयसे (*prathayase*)—you are renowned
- अभिक्रंदन् (*abhikraṃdan*)—making a sound
- वृषायसे (*vṛṣāyase*)—you rush forward like a bull
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—at the time of great joy
- जामिषु (*jāmiṣu*)—in the plants that are your kin
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the germ of the nature of seed
- दधासि (*dadhāsi*)—you place

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you of great form are exceedingly renowned by your shining lustre. You rush forward like a bull, making a sound. When great joy has arisen in you, you place the germ of the nature of seed in the plants that are your kin. You are a great one.

##### English translation
Agni, you, the mighty one, are known far and wide by your radiant lustre; bellowing, you rush like a bull, you impregnate the sister (plants) in your exhilaration; you are mighty.

## Sūkta 22 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कुहेति पंचदशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तमैंद्रं । पंचदशी त्रिष्टुप् पंचमीसप्तमानवम्यस्ति स्रोऽनुष्टुभः शिष्टाः पुरस्ताद्बृहत्यः । आद्यद्वादशकश्रष्टकवती
> पुरस्ताद्बृहती । पूर्ववदृषिः । तथा चानुक्रांतं। कुह पंचोना पुरस्ताद्बार्हतं
> त्रिष्टुबंतं त्वं त्या चिदा नस्त्वं नोऽनुष्टुभ इति॥ चतुर्थेऽहनि निष्केवल्य एतत्तूक्तं।
> सूत्रितं च । कुह श्रुत इंद्रो युध्मस्य त इति निष्केवल्यं । आ. ७-११ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the sixth sūkta, beginning कुह (*kuha*), is addressed to Indra and has fifteen Ṛks. The fifteenth is a Triṣṭubh; the fifth, seventh and ninth are Anuṣṭubhs; the rest are Purastād-bṛhatīs. The first quarter-verse (pāda) has twelve syllables, and the remaining ones have eight each. The seer is the same as before. He cites the Anukramaṇī: कुह पंचोना पुरस्ताद्बार्हतं त्रिष्टुबंतं त्वं त्या चिदा नस्त्वं नोऽनुष्टुभ इति॥ (*kuha paṃconā purastādbārhataṃ triṣṭubaṃtaṃ tvaṃ tyā cidā nastvaṃ no 'nuṣṭubha iti‖*) The sūkta is used in the Niṣkevalya Śastra on the fourth day, and the sūtra says: कुह श्रुत इंद्रो युध्मस्य त इति निष्केवल्यं (*kuha śruta iṃdro yudhmasya ta iti niṣkevalyaṃ*) (Ā. 7-11).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, कुह (*kuha*), is the sixth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has fifteen Ṛks. Its seer and deity are the same as those of the preceding sūkta. The fifteenth Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre; the fifth, seventh and ninth are in the Anuṣṭubh metre. The remaining Ṛks are in the Purastād-bṛhatī metre. If a Ṛk has four pādas, the first with twelve syllables and the other three with eight each, that Ṛk is said to be in the Purastād-bṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: कुह पंचोना पुरस्ताद्बार्हतं त्रिष्टुबंतं त्वं त्या चिदा नस्त्वं नोऽनुष्टुभः (*kuha paṃconā purastādbārhataṃ triṣṭubaṃtaṃ tvaṃ tyā cidā nastvaṃ no 'nuṣṭubhaḥ*). The sūkta is applied to the Niṣkevalya Śastra mantras on the fourth day of the sacrifice, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, कुह श्रुत इंद्रो युध्मस्य त इति निष्केवल्यं (*kuha śruta iṃdro yudhmasya ta iti niṣkevalyaṃ*) (Ā. 7-11).

Sūkta 22.
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 22.
Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 7; Vargas 6, 7, 8.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 15.
Ṛṣi: Pimada Aindra Prājāpatya, or Vasukṛt Vāsukra.
Devatā: Indra.
Chandas: 1, 4, 6, 8, 10-14: Purastād-bṛhatī. 5, 7, 9: Anuṣṭubh. 15: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कुह॑ श्रु॒त इंद्रः॒ कस्मि॑न्न॒द्य जने॑ मि॒त्रो न श्रू॑यते ।  
> ऋषी॑णां वा॒ यः क्षये॒ गुहा॑ वा॒ चर्कृ॑षे गि॒रा ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 657

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कुह । श्रुतः । इंद्रः । कस्मिन् । अद्य । जने । मित्रः । न । श्रूयते ।  
> ऋषीणां । वा । यः । क्षये । गुहा । वा । चर्कृषे । गिरा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अद्यास्मिन्निन इंद्रः कुह कुत्र स्थाने श्रुतो विश्रुतः प्रख्यातः । कस्मिञ्जने
> यजमान इज्यत्वेन स्तुत्यत्वेनावस्थितः श्रूयते । प्रख्यायते । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> मित्रो न सूर्य इव सखेव ना तद्वत् । य इंद्र ऋषीणां भृग्वादीनां क्षये निवास आश्रमे गुहा वा गुहायामरण्ये वा गिरा स्तुतिलक्षणया
> वाचा चर्कृषे अत्यर्थमाकृष्यते । अत्यर्थं स्तूयत इत्यर्थः । स इंद्रः कुह श्रुत
> इति पूर्वेण संबंधः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Where is Indra renowned today? Among what worshipper (yajamāna), as object of worship or of praise, is he heard of and famed? The example is मित्रो न (*mitro na*), "like Mitra": like the sun, or like a friend. Indra is greatly drawn (चर्कृषे (*carkṛṣe*)), that is, greatly praised, by the speech of praise at the dwelling (क्षये (*kṣaye*): abode, hermitage) of the sages Bhṛgu and others, or in a cave or forest. This is connected with the earlier question, "Where is that Indra renowned?"

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- ऋषीणां (*ṛṣīṇāṃ*)—of the sages
- क्षये वा (*kṣaye vā*)—either in the dwelling-places
- वा (*vā*)—or
- गुहा (*guhā*)—in secret places
- गिरा (*girā*)—by speech in the form of praise
- चर्कृषे (*carkṛṣe*)—is drawn
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अद्य (*adya*)—on this day of the sacrifice
- कुह (*kuha*)—in what place
- श्रुतः (*śrutaḥ*)—is he renowned?
- मित्रो न (*mitro na*)—like a dear friend
- कस्मिन् जने (*kasmin jane*)—among what people
- श्रूयते (*śrūyate*)—is he heard of as famed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who is drawn by speech in the form of praise whether in the dwelling-places of the sages or in secret places: in what place is he renowned on this day of the sacrifice? Like a dear friend, among what people is he heard of as famed?

##### English translation
In what place to-day is Indra renowned? In what nation is he famed like Mitra ? (Indra), who is worshipped with sacred praise at the dwelling of the rishis, or in secret.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒ह श्रु॒त इंद्रो॑ अ॒स्मे अ॒द्य स्तवे॑ व॒ज्र्य चे॑षमः ।  
> मि॒त्रो न यो जने॒ष्वा यश॑स्च॒क्रे असा॒म्या ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 658

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इह । श्रुतः । इंद्रः । अस्मे इति । अद्य । स्तवे । वज्री । ऋचीषमः ।  
> मिश्रः । न । यः । जनेषु । आ । यशः । चक्रे । असामि । आ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इहास्मिन्यज्ञ इंद्रः श्रुतः प्रख्यातः । अद्यास्मिन्दिवस अस्मे अस्माभिः स्तवे ।
> स्तूयते । कीदृशः । वज्री वज्रवान् ऋचीषमः । यद्दाव इंद्र ते शतं शतं
> भूमारुत स्युः न त्वा वज्रिन् । ऋ. सं. ८-७०-५ । इत्यादिकया स्तुत्या समानगुण
> इत्यर्थः । य इंद्रो मित्रो न सूर्य इव स्निग्ध इव वा जनेषु स्तोतृजनेषु
> यशोऽन्नं कीर्तिं वा चक्रे करोति । कीदृशं । असाम्यसाधारणं । स इंद्रोऽस्माभिः स्तूयत इति पूर्वेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, in this sacrifice, Indra is renowned; today, on this day, he is praised by us. What is he like? He is वज्री (*vajrī*), the wielder of the thunderbolt, and ऋचीषमः (*ṛcīṣamaḥ*): equal in qualities to the one praised by the hymn beginning यद्दाव इंद्र ते शतं शतं भूमारुत स्युः न त्वा वज्रिन् (*yaddāva iṃdra te śataṃ śataṃ bhūmāruta syuḥ na tvā vajrin*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-70-5) and so on. Indra, like Mitra (that is, like the sun, or like a friend), produces among the worshippers यशः (*yaśaḥ*), food or fame, which is असामि (*asāmi*), unequalled. This is connected with the earlier statement that this Indra is praised by us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रे (*vajre*)—the bearer of the thunderbolt
- यचीषमः (*yacīṣamaḥ*)—and deserving of praise
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- मित्रो न (*mitro na*)—like a friend
- जनेषु (*janeṣu*)—among the worshippers
- असामि (*asāmi*)—unequalled
- यशः (*yaśaḥ*)—food
- आ चक्रे (*ā cakre*)—provides
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- इह (*iha*)—here
- श्रुतः (*śrutaḥ*)—renowned
- अद्य (*adya*)—on this day of the sacrifice
- अस्मे (*asme*)—by us
- स्तवे (*stave*)—is praised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt and deserving of praise, who like a friend provides unequalled food among the worshippers, is renowned here and is praised by us on this day of the sacrifice.

##### English translation
Here is Indra renowned ; to-day he is praised by us, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the deserving of praise ; he who, like Mitra, bestows upon men unequalled abundance.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒हो यस्पतिः॒ शव॑सो॒ असा॒म्या म॒हो नृ॒णस्य॑ तूतु॒जिः ।  
> भ॒र्ता वज्र॑स्य धृ॒ष्टोः पि॒ता पु॒त्रमि॑व प्रि॒यं ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 659

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> महः । यः । पतिः । शवसः । असामि । आ । महः । नृम्मस्य । तूतुजिः ।  
> भर्ता । वज्रस्य । धृष्ण्णोः । पिता । पुत्रं इव । प्रियं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इंद्रो महो महतः शवसो बलस्य पतिरीश्वरोऽसाम्या । आङ्मर्यादायां । आ समाप्तेः । अनंतगुण इत्यर्तः । महो महतो नृणस्य धनस्य च
> तूतुजिः स्तोतृभ्यः प्रेरकः । किंच दृष्टोः शत्रूणां धर्षकस्य वज्रस्य स्वकीयस्यायुधस्य भर्ता य इंद्रो धारयिता । स इंद्रोऽस्मान्पात्विति शेषः । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> पिता पुत्रमिव प्रियं यथा पितेप्सितं सुतं पाति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who is lord of great strength, असाम्या (*asāmyā*) (आङ् (*āṅ*) in the sense of limit, "up to completion", so he has endless qualities), who is the impeller (तूतुजिः (*tūtujiḥ*)) of great wealth to the praisers, and who is the bearer (holder) of his own weapon, the thunderbolt, which overcomes enemies, may that Indra protect us (this is the word to be supplied). The example: as a father protects a dear son he longs for.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of great
- शवसः (*śavasaḥ*)—strength
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—being lord
- असामान्या (*asāmānyā*)—and possessed of unequalled qualities
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—to great
- नृम्मस्य (*nṛmmasya*)—wealth
- तूतुजिः (*tūtujiḥ*)—the impeller (so that it reaches the sacrificers)
- धृष्टोः (*dhṛṣṭoḥ*)—overcoming enemies
- वज्रस्य (*vajrasya*)—of the thunderbolt
- भर्ता (*bhartā*)—he who is the lord, that Indra
- पिता (*pitā*)—a father
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—a dear
- पुत्रं इव (*putraṃ iva*)—as he protects a son, so may he protect us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra who is lord of great strength, who provides abundant wealth to the sacrificer, and who is master of the enemy-overcoming thunderbolt: may he protect us as a father protects a dear son.

##### English translation
(May Indra protect us) who is the lord of great strength, of unequalled (power), the distributor of great wealth, the cherisher of the dreadful thunderbolt, as a father (cherishes) a dear son.

### Printed p. 660
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒जा॒नो अश्वा॒ वात॑स्य॒ धुनी॑ दे॒वो दे॒वस्य॑ वज्रिवः ।  
> स्यंता॑ प॒था वि॒रुक्म॑ता सृजा॒नः स्तो॒ष्यध्व॑नः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युजानः । अश्वा । वातस्य । धुनी इति । देवः । देवस्य । वज्रिवः ।  
> स्यंता । पथा । विरुक्मता । सृजानः । स्तोषि । अध्वनः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वज्रिवो वज्रवन्निंद्र ॥ एको मत्त्वर्थीयोनुवादकः ॥ देवो द्योतमानस्त्वं देवस्य द्योतमानस्य वातस्य वायोधुनी प्रेरका । वायोरपि शीघ्रगामिनावित्यर्थः । अश्वाश्वा त्वदीयौ हरिनामकौ युजानः स्वरथे संयोजयन् ।
> कीदृशौ । विरुक्कृता विरोचनवता पथा मार्गेण स्यंता स्यंता गच्छंतौ । अध्वनो
> युद्धे गमनमार्गान्सृजान उत्पादयन् स्तोषि । सततं स्तूयसे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*), Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt (the one व (*va*) is a possessive-suffix repetition). You, resplendent (देवः (*devaḥ*)), yoke to your chariot your two horses called Hari, अश्वा (*aśvā*), which are impellers (धुनी (*dhunī*)) of the resplendent wind, वातस्य (*vātasya*); that is, swifter even than the wind. They travel (स्यंता (*syaṃtā*)) along a shining road (*virukmatā pathā*). Creating (सृजानः (*sṛjānaḥ*)) the paths of going in battle, you are constantly praised (स्तोषि (*stoṣi*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*)—O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—you, the resplendent
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of the divine
- वातस्य (*vātasya*)—than the wind
- धुनी (*dhunī*)—swifter
- विरुक्मता (*virukmatā*)—resplendent
- पथा (*pathā*)—along the road
- स्यंता (*syaṃtā*)—which travel
- अश्वा (*aśvā*)—horses
- युजानः (*yujānaḥ*)—yoking to the chariot
- अध्वनः (*adhvanaḥ*)—the paths of battle
- सृजानः (*sṛjānaḥ*)—creating
- स्तोषि (*stoṣi*)—you are praised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, you, the resplendent, yoke to your chariot horses that are swifter than the divine wind and travel along a resplendent road, and, creating the paths of battle, you are praised.

##### English translation
Thunderer, you who are divine, yoking your horses which are swifter than the divine wind, and gliding along the resplendent road, you, opening out the way (t° battle), are glorified.

### Printed p. 661
#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं त्या चि॒द्वात॒स्याश्वागा॑ ऋ॒ज्रा त्मना॒ वह॑ध्यै ।  
> ययो॑र्दे॒वो न मर्त्यो॑ यं॒ता नकि॑र्वि॒दाय्यः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । त्या । चित् । वातस्य । अश्वा । आ । आगाः । ऋज्रा । त्मना । वहध्यै ।  
> ययोः । देवः । न । मर्त्यः । यंता । नकिः । विदाय्यः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यच्छब्द संबंधादुत्तरोर्धर्चः पूर्वं व्याख्यायते । ययोस्तदीययोर्यंता नियंता निवारयिता देवो न देवानां मध्यॆ कश्चिदपि देवो नास्ति
> मर्त्यो मनुष्याणां मध्यॆ कश्चिदपि नास्ति नकिर्न कश्चिदपि विदाय्यो वेत्ता । जवस्य
> बलस्येति वा शेषः । हे इंद्र त्वं वातस्य वार्योर्बलेन जवेन च युक्तावृज्रर्जुगामिनौ त्या चित्तावप्यश्वा त्वदीयावश्वा त्मनात्मनैव । सारथिनिरपेक्षेणेत्यर्थः ।
> वहध्यै वहनार्थं । अभिप्रेतदेशप्रापणायेत्यर्थः । आगाः । अभिमुख्येन गच्छसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Because of the connection with the relative word य (*ya*), the second half of the verse is explained first. Of those horses of his, the restrainer (यंता (*yaṃtā*)) is not a deity among the gods, मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*) is none among men, and no one (नकिः (*nakiḥ*)) is a knower (विदाय्यः (*vidāyyaḥ*)); "of their speed or strength" is to be supplied. O Indra, you come (आगाः (*āgāḥ*)) facing those two famed horses of yours, which are joined with the strength and speed of the wind and go straight (ऋज्रा (*ṛjrā*)), so that they may bear you (वहध्यै (*vahadhyai*)), that is, convey you to the intended place, त्मना (*tmanā*), of themselves, without need of a charioteer.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) ययोः (*yayoḥ*)—of which horses of yours
- यंता (*yaṃtā*)—the restrainer
- देवो न (*devo na*)—not among the gods
- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—among men
- नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—there is none; such horses
- वातस्य (*vātasya*)—endowed with the speed of the wind
- ऋज्रा (*ṛjrā*)—going straight
- त्या चित् (*tyā cit*)—and famed
- अश्वा (*aśvā*)—your horses
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—without a charioteer
- वहध्यै (*vahadhyai*)—to carry you
- विदाय्यः (*vidāyyaḥ*)—wise
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- आगाः (*āgāḥ*)—come facing them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you, the wise, come facing your horses, whose speed none among gods or men can restrain, which are joined with the strength of the wind, go straight and are famed, so that they may carry you of themselves, without a charioteer.

##### English translation
You have come to these two horses (which have the speed) of the wind, straight-going, for them to draw you of themselves, whom no deity, no mortal is able to restrain ; whose fleetness no one comprehends.
