#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध॒ ग्मंतो॒शना॑ पृच्छते वां॒ कद॑र्था न॒ आ गृ॒हं ।  
> आ ज॑ग्मथुः परा॒काद्दि॒ वश्च॒ ग्मश्च॒ मर्त्यं॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । ग्मंता । उशना । पृच्छते । वां । कत् अर्था । नः । आ । गृहं ।  
> आ । जग्मथुः । पराकात् । दिवः । च । ग्मः । च । मर्त्यं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अधाथ यज्ञसमाप्त्यनंतरमुशना भार्गव ऋषिर्हे इंद्राग्नी ग्मंता
> स्वस्थानं प्रति गच्छंत्वा नां युवां पृच्छते । पृच्छति स्म । यद्वा । उशनेति विभक्तिव्यत्ययः । उशनसमिंद्रस्य सखिभूतं भार्गवमिंद्रं च युवां सर्वो यजमानः
> पृच्छति । किं पृष्टवानिति उच्यते । युवां कदार्था कदर्थौ किंप्रयोजनवंतौ
> संतौ नोऽस्मदीयं । आकारः प्रतीत्यस्यार्थे ! गृहं प्रति पराकात् । दूरनामैतत् ।
> दूरादा जग्मथुः । आगतवंतौ स्थः। तदेवोक्तं । दिवश्च द्युलोकाच्च ग्मश्च भूलोकाच्च मर्त्यं मनुष्यं मां प्रत्यागतवंतौ । युवयोः कृतार्थत्पादत्रागमनमस्मदनुग्रहार्थमेव न स्वार्थमिति ब्रुवन्ननुव्रजतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

After the completion of the sacrifice, the seer Uśanas Bhārgava asks the two, Indra and Agni, who are going to their own place: "For what purpose have you come to our house?" Alternatively, उशना (*uśanā*) is a case-substitution: the sacrificer, every one of them, asks both Uśanas, the friend of Indra, a Bhārgava, and Indra. What does he ask? "You two, having what purpose, have come to our house from afar (पराकात् (*parākāt*) is a word for 'far'), from heaven and from earth, to me, a mortal?" The two have come for the sake of their own fulfilment, yet their coming is only to favour us, not for themselves; saying so, he follows after them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कदर्था (*kadarthā*)—having what purpose
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गृहं (*gṛhaṃ*)—to the house
- पराकात् (*parākāt*)—from a very distant region
- आ जग्मथुः (*ā jagmathuḥ*)—you have come
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the heaven
- ग्मः च (*gmaḥ ca*)—and from the earth
- मर्त्यं (*martyaṃ*)—to me, a human being
- आ (जग्मथुः) (*ā (jagmathuḥ)*)—with what aim have you come
- ग्मंता (*gmaṃtā*)—going to him
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you two
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- उशना (*uśanā*)—Uśanas, the son of Bhṛgu
- पृच्छते (*pṛcchate*)—asks

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, expecting what purpose have you both come to our house? From heaven, the farthest region, and from earth too, with what aim have you come to me, a human? So Uśanas, son of Bhṛgu, asks you as you go to him.

### Printed p. 663

##### English translation
Ushanas inquires of you two as you pass, " (Why) have you come to (our dwelling) from a distance ; from heaven and earth to a mortal ? "
#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ न॑ इंद्र पृक्षसे॒ऽस्माकं॒ ब्रह्मोद्य॑तं ।  
> तत्त्वा॑ याचाम॒हेवः॒ शुष्णं॒ यद्धन्नमा॑नुषं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । इंद्र । पृक्षसे । अस्माकं । ब्रह्म । उत्यतं ।  
> तत् । त्वा । याचामहे । अवः । शुष्णं । यत् । हन् । अमानुषं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं । न इति तृतीयार्थे षष्ठी । नोऽस्माभिरुद्यतमुत्किष्टं ।
> दत्तमित्यर्थः । अस्माकमस्मदीयं ब्रह्म हविर्लक्षणमन्नं । आङ्मयादायां । आ
> तृप्तेरित्यर्थः । पृक्षसे । आत्मना संपर्चय ॥ पृची संपर्क इति धातो रूपं ॥
> आभक्षयेत्यर्थः । किंच वयमपि त्वैवंभूतं त्वां तत् । यदुत्कृष्टमस्तीति शेषः ।
> तत्तादृशमन्नमवस्तद्रक्षणं च याचामहे । प्रार्थयामहे । तथा यच्छुष्णं
> बलं चामानुषं मनुष्यादन्यं राक्षसादिकं हन् हंति तदुत्कृष्टं बलं च याचामहे । यद्वा । हे इंद्र त्वं शुष्णमेतन्नामानममानुषं मनुष्यव्यतिरिक्तमसुरु
> हन् । हतवानसि । हत्वा च यद्येन रक्षणेन त्रैलोक्यं पालितवानसि तदवः पालनमस्माकमपि भवेदिति त्वां याचामह इति वाक्यार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, न (*na*) is a genitive in the sense of the instrumental: the food in the form of oblation, ब्रह्म (*brahma*), raised up, that is, offered, by us. आ (*ā*) marks the limit: until satisfied, partake (पृक्षसे (*pṛkṣase*), from the root पृची (*pṛcī*) meaning contact); that is, eat it. Moreover, we ask you, such as you are, for that excellent food and its protection (अवः (*avaḥ*)), and also for the strength (शुष्णं (*śuṣṇaṃ*)) by which you slay the non-human, the demons and the like, other than men. Alternatively: O Indra, you slew the non-human Śuṣṇa, an asura apart from men, and by the protection with which you guarded the three worlds, may that protection be ours too; so we ask you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—by us
- उद्यतं (*udyataṃ*)—offered
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—oblation
- आ पृक्षसे (*ā pṛkṣase*)—accept until satisfied
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- शुष्णं (*śuṣṇaṃ*)—your strength
- अमानुषं (*amānuṣaṃ*)—the demons and others who have no humanity
- हन् (*han*)—is able to kill
- तत् (*tat*)—such
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—powerful protection
- त्वा (*tvā*)—from you
- याचामहे (*yācāmahe*)—we ask

### Printed p. 664

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, accept this oblation offered by us until you are satisfied. We ask of you that powerful protection, your strength which can slay asuras who have no humanity.

##### English translation
Aaccpt, Indra, the oblation upraised by us ; we solicit of you that protection by which you did slay the non-human Shushna.
#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒क॒र्मा दस्यु॑र॒भि नो॑ अमं॒तुर॒न्यव्र॑तो॒ अमा॑नुषः ।  
> त्वं तस्या॑मित्रह॒न्वध॑र्दा॒स्य॑ दंभय ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अकर्मा । दस्युः । अभि । नः । अमंतुः । अन्यव्रतः । अमानुषः ।  
> त्वं । तस्य । अमित्रहन् । वधः । दासस्य । दंभय ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अकर्माविद्यमानयागादिकर्मा दस्युरुपक्षपयिताभ्याभिमुख्येन स्वरूपतो नोऽस्मानमंतुरज्ञाता । यद्वा । अत्रावेत्युपसर्गस्य वकारलोपो
> द्रष्टव्यः । अवमंतुरवमंताभिभविता । अन्यव्रतः श्रुतिस्मृतिव्यतिरिक्तकर्मामानुषो
> मनुष्यसंव्यवहाराद्बाह्यः । असुरप्रकृतिरित्यर्थः । य एवंभूतोऽस्ति हे आमित्रहञ्छत्रोणां हंतरिंद्र त्वं दासस्कोपक्षपयितव्यस्य वधर्हंता सन् दंभय । तं
> शत्रुं हिंधि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Dasyu, the destroyer, who has no sacrificial rites, is unknown to us, ignorant of us (अमंतुः (*amaṃtuḥ*)); or, with the loss of the letter v of the prefix ava, "one who despises, overpowers". He is अन्यव्रतः (*anyavrataḥ*), with rites other than those of śruti and smṛti, and अमानुषः (*amānuṣaḥ*), outside human intercourse, of asura nature. O Indra, slayer of foes, being the slayer, the weapon, of that slave (दासस्य (*dāsasya*)), who is to be destroyed, crush that enemy; kill him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अ मित्रहन् (*a mitrahan*)—O Indra, destroyer of enemies
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अकर्मा (*akarmā*)—being without rites
- दस्युः (*dasyuḥ*)—a destroyer
- अभि (*abhi*)—wholly
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अमंतुः (*amaṃtuḥ*)—one who does not know
- अन्यव्रतः (*anyavrataḥ*)—one whose rites are not those of worshippers of the gods
- अमानुषः (*amānuṣaḥ*)—one of demonic nature
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of whatever asura there is
- दासस्य (*dāsasya*)—of the destroying enemy
- वधः (*vadhaḥ*)—as destroyer
- दंभय (*daṃbhaya*)—kill him

### Printed p. 665

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, destroyer of enemies, whatever asura there is who is without rites, a destroyer, wholly ignorant of us, with rites that are not those of worshippers of the gods, and of demonic nature, be the slayer of that asura and kill him.

##### English translation
The Dasyu practising no religious rites, not knowing us thoroughly following other observances, obeying no human laws, baffle, destroyer of enemies, the wapon of that slave.
#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं न॑ इंद्र शूर॒ शूरै॑रु॒त त्वोता॑सो ब॒र्हणा॑ ।  
> पु॒रु॒त्रा ते॒ वि पू॒र्तयो॒ नवं॑त क्षो॒णयो॑ यथा ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । नः । इंद्र । शूर । शूरैः । उत । त्वाऊतासः । बर्हणा ।  
> पुरुत्रा । ते । वि । पूर्तयः । नवंत । क्षोणयः । यथा ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूर विक्रांतेंद्र त्वं शूरैर्भटैर्मरुद्भिः सहितः सन्नोऽस्मान् पाहीति
> शेषः । उतापि च त्वोतासस्त्वया रक्षिता वयं बर्हणा परिबर्हणायां शत्रूणां
> हिंसायां समर्था भवेम । किंच ते त्वदीयाः पूर्तयः कामानां पूरणानीप्सितार्थप्रदानानि पुरुत्रा बहून्सोत्थन्वि नवंत । विविधं व्याप्नुवंति । क्षोणयः ।
> मनुष्यनामैतत् । मनुष्याः स्वकीयं स्वामिनं सेवार्थं यथा व्याप्नुवंति
> तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O heroic Indra, together with the heroes, the Maruts, protect us (to be supplied). And protected by you, may we be able in the crushing of enemies. Moreover, your fulfilments of desires, the gifts granting what is wished, spread widely (नवंत (*navaṃta*)) among many, as men (क्षोणयः (*kṣoṇayaḥ*), a word for men) resort to their own lord for service.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- शूरैः (*śūraiḥ*)—with the heroic Maruts
- नः (*naḥ*)—protect us
- उते (*ute*)—and
- त्वोतासः (*tvotāsaḥ*)—we protected by you
- बर्हणा (*barhaṇā*)—may we withstand the enemy-destroying power
- क्षोणयः (*kṣoṇayaḥ*)—men
- यथा (*yathā*)—as

### Printed p. 666
- (continued) they go and join their lords for service
- ते (*te*)—given by you
- पूर्तयः (*pūrtayaḥ*)—gifts that fulfil wishes
- पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)—among many praisers
- वि नवंत (*vi navaṃta*)—go and join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, protect us together with the heroic Maruts. And protected by you, may we withstand the enemy-destroying power. As men go and join their lords for service, the gifts given by you, which fulfil wishes, go and join many praisers.

##### English translation
Hero, Indra, with the hero (Maruts defend) us; that protected by you (we may be able) to overcome (our enemies): your blessings are diffused among many (praisers), as men (repair to their lord)
#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं तान्वृ॑त्त॒हत्ये॑ चोदयो॒ न्यन्का॑र्पा॒णे शू॑र वज्रिवः ।  
> गुहा॒ युदी॑ कवी॒नां वि॒शां नक्ष॑त्रशवसां ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । तान् । वृत्रहत्ये । चोदयः । न्यन् । कार्पाणे । शूर । वज्रिवः ।  
> गुहा । यदि । कवीनां । विशां । नक्षत्रशवसां । १८

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वज्रिवो वज्रधर शूरेंद्र त्वं कार्पाणे । असिः कृपाणः । तेन साध्यं
> युद्धं कार्पाणं । तस्मिन्वृत्रहत्ये शत्रुहननार्थं नृन्नरांस्तान्प्रसिद्धान्मरुद्गणांश्चोदयः । चोदयसि । प्रेरयसि । यदि यदा त्वं कवीनां मेधाविनां
> नक्षत्रशवसां देवान्प्रतिगच्छत्सोतृबलानां विशां स्तोतृजनानां संबंधीनि गुहा
> गूढानि गुणैः संवृतानि स्तोत्राणि शृणोषीति शेषः । तदा प्रेरयसीति पूर्णेणान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O wielder of the thunderbolt, heroic Indra, in the battle कार्पाणे (*kārpāṇe*) (कृपाणः (*kṛpāṇaḥ*) is a sword; war accomplished with it is kārpāṇa), the slaying of Vṛtra, you urge on those well-known men, the Marut hosts, to kill enemies, when you hear the hidden praises, concealed by their qualities, of the wise praisers, whose strength goes towards the gods. The connection is with the final "then you urge".

### Printed p. 667

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*)—wielder of the thunderbolt
- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant Indra
- यदि (*yadi*)—when
- कवीनां (*kavīnāṃ*)—of the wise
- नक्षत्रशवसां (*nakṣatraśavasāṃ*)—who are fit to reach the gods
- विशां (*viśāṃ*)—of the praisers
- गुहा (*guhā*)—you hear the praises with hidden meaning, then
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- कार्पाणे (*kārpāṇe*)—in battle
- वृत्रहत्ये (*vṛtrahatye*)—for the destruction of Vṛtra
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—the leaders
- तान् (*tān*)—those Maruts
- चोदयः (*codayaḥ*)—you urge on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When you hear the hidden-meaning praises of the praisers, wielders of the thunderbolt, fit to reach the gods, then you urge the leading Maruts in battle to destroy Vṛtra.

##### English translation
Hero, Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you have animated those chiefs (the Maruts) to the slaughter of Vritra in battle, when (you hear) the mystical (praises), of the sages, the worshippers praising the might of the constellations.
#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒क्वू ता त॑ इंद्र दा॒नाप्य॑स अक्षा॒णे शू॑र वज्रिवः ।  
> यद्ध॒ शुष्क॑स्य दं॒भयो॑ जा॒तं विश्वं॑ स॒याव॑भिः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मक्षु । ता । ते । इंद्र । दानअप्नसः । आक्षाणे । शूर । वज्रिवः ।  
> यत् । ह । शुष्णस्य । दंभयः । जातं । विश्वं । सयावभिः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूर विक्रांत वज्रिवो वज्रोपेतेंद्र दानाप्नसो दानकर्मणः ।
> स्तोतृभ्यः सततमभीष्टफलप्रदस्येत्यर्थः । ते तव स्वभूतानि मक्षु क्षिप्राण्यविलंबितानि । क्षिप्रकारणयुक्ता नीत्यर्थः । आक्षणे योद्धृभिर्वाप्यमाने त्वय्यवस्थितानि
> ता तानि कर्माणि स्तोतारः स्तुवंतीति शेषः। सयावभिः सहयातृभिर्मरुद्धिः सहितस्त्वं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O heroic Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, of the giver, constantly granting the wished fruit to praisers, those deeds of yours are swift (मक्षु (*makṣu*)), without delay, that is, with swift causes. In the battle (आक्षणे (*ākṣaṇe*)), when you are pressed by warriors, the praisers praise those deeds that rest in you (to be supplied).

### Printed p. 668

> तुष्टस्यासुरस्य विश्वं जातं सर्वमपत्यजातं दंभयः । अदंभयः । हिंसितवानसि ।
> यद्वा ! एववादीनि यानि खलु कर्माणि संति तानि स्तुवंतीति पूर्वेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues the explanation of the preceding Ṛk. Indra injured (दंभयः (*daṃbhayaḥ*), "you harmed") the whole progeny of the asura Shushna, that is, all his offspring. Alternatively, the construction is with the preceding words: the singers praise the deeds of this kind that there are.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O mighty one
- वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*)—O bearer of the thunderbolt
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सयावभिः (*sayāvabhiḥ*)—together with the Maruts who accompany you
- शुष्णस्य (*śuṣṇasya*)—of the asura Shushna
- विश्वं चातं (*viśvaṃ cātaṃ*)—all the sons
- यत् ह (*yat ha*)—when
- दंभयः (*daṃbhayaḥ*)—you killed, then
- दानाप्यसः (*dānāpyasaḥ*)—of you who are engaged in acts of giving
- ते (*te*)—your
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—those that work quickly
- आक्षणे (*ākṣaṇe*)—those that are filled in you
- ता (*tā*)—they praise those well-known deeds

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O mighty Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, when you, together with the Maruts who accompany you, killed all the sons of the asura Shushna, the singers extol those well-known deeds of yours, which are bounteous, swift in action, and filled with you.

##### English translation
Hero, Indra, (your worshippers glorify) those prompt exploits performed by you in battle, (by you who are) ever bountiful, when with your associate (Maruts) you destroyed the whole race of Shushna.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> माकु॒ध्य॑गिंद्र शूर॒ वस्वी॑र॒स्यॆ भू॑वन्न॒भिष्ट॑यः ।  
> व॒यंव॑यं त आसां सु॒म्मे स्या॑म वज्रिवः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । अकुध्यक् । इंद्र । शूर । वस्वीः । अस्यॆ इति । भूवन् । अभिष्टयः ।  
> वयंवयं । ते । आसां । सुम्मे । स्याम । वज्रिवः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूर विक्रांतेंद्र अस्मे अस्माकं स्वभूता वस्वीर्महत्योऽभिष्टय
> अभिमुख्येष्टय इज्याः । यद्वा । अभिमुख्येच्छा अभीप्सितप्रार्थनाः । कुध्यक्

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O mighty, valiant Indra, our own great अभिष्टयः (*abhiṣṭayaḥ*) are the sacrifices (इज्याः (*ijyāḥ*)) directed towards us; or else they are our desired petitions, prayers for what we long for. May they not be कुध्यक् (*kudhyak*), that is, contemptible, which means fruitless.

### Printed p. 669

> कुत्सिताः । विफला इत्यर्थः । मा भूवन् । किंतर्हि हे वज्रिवो वज्रिन्निंद्र ते तव
> प्रसादाद्वयंवयमृत्विग्यजमानाः । द्विर्वचनमतित्वराप्रदर्शनार्थं । आसामिजानामिच्छानां वा संबंधिनि सुम्मे सुखेवस्थिताः स्याम । भवेम । वयमभिषिजन्येन दृष्टादृष्टसुखेन युक्ताः शीघ्रं भवेमेत्याशास्मह इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the contrary, O thunderbolt-bearing Indra, by your grace we, ṛtvijs and sacrificer alike (वयंवयं (*vayaṃvayaṃ*)), may be established in the comfort connected with these (आसां (*āsāṃ*)) sacrifices or desires. The doubling of the word shows great haste. "May we quickly be endowed with the visible and invisible happiness that arises from our aim": such is the wish expressed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O mighty one
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अस्मे (*asme*)—our
- वस्वीः (*vasvīḥ*)—those of great nature
- अभिष्टयः (*abhiṣṭayaḥ*)—prayers that ask for desired objects
- अकुध्रक् (*akudhrak*)—without purpose
- मा भूवन् (*mā bhūvan*)—let them not be
- वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*)—O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt
- ते (*te*)—by your favour
- वयंवयं (*vayaṃvayaṃ*)—all of us, who are priests and sacrificer
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—that has these desired objects as its goal
- सुम्मे (*summe*)—in happiness
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O mighty Indra, let our great prayers, which ask for what we desire, not be without purpose. O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, by your favour may all of us, priests and sacrificer, be in the happiness that has these desired objects as its target (its aim).

##### English translation
Hero, Indra, let not our manifold sacrifices be unavailing, but may we all, thunderer, (through) your (favour) continue in the fruition of these (our desires).

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स्मे ता त॑ इंद्र संतु स॒त्याहिं॑संतीरुप॒स्पृशः॑ ।  
> वि॒द्याम॒ यासां॒ भुजो॑ धेनू॒नां न व॑ज्रिवः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्मे इति । ता । ते । इंद्र । संतु । सत्या । अहिंसंतीः । उपस्पृशः ।  
> विद्याम । यासां । भुजः । धेनूनां । न । वज्रवः ॥ १३ ॥

### Printed p. 670

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अस्मे आस्माकं स्वभूताः ॥ ता सत्येत्युभयत्र प्रथमाबहुवचनस्य
> च्छांदस आकारः सति निर्देशस्याविशेषणत्वात् ॥ ता तास्त्रादृश्य उपस्पृशः । त्वामुपगम्य स्पृशंतीत्युपस्पृशः स्तुतयः । ते तव प्रसादात्सत्या सत्याः संतु । यथार्था
> भवंतु । तव सद्गुणग्राहिण्य इत्यर्थः । अपि चाहिंसंतीस्त्वामहिंसत्यश्च भवंतु ।
> सत्सुतित्वादनुद्वेजयंत्यश्चभवंतित्यर्थः । हे वज्रिव इंद्र यासां स्तुतीनां संबंधिनो भुजो दृष्टादृष्टान्भोगान्विद्याम वयं लभेमहि । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> धेनूनां न गवां क्षीरादिभोगान्यथा गोस्वामी लभते तद्वत् । ताः सत्या भवंत्विति
> पूर्वेणान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, "those" (ता (*tā*)) belong to us. In both ता (*tā*) and सत्या (*satyā*) the ending ā of the nominative plural is Vedic, since the word stands in the place of what is qualified. Those उपस्पृशः (*upaspṛśaḥ*) are the praises that approach you and touch you. By your grace may they be true, that is, conformable to fact, taking up your good qualities. Moreover may they be अहिंसंतीः (*ahiṃsaṃtīḥ*), non-injuring: being good praises, they do not vex you. O thunderbolt-bearing Indra, may we obtain the enjoyments, seen and unseen, connected with these praises. An illustration: as the owner of cows obtains the enjoyment of the milk and the like of the milch-cows. The construction is with the preceding: "may they be true".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*)—O bearer of the thunderbolt
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- धेनूनां न (*dhenūnāṃ na*)—as a cowherd also enjoys the milk of milch-cows
- यासां (*yāsāṃ*)—of whichever praises the fruit
- भुजः (*bhujaḥ*)—the enjoyments of happiness
- विद्याम (*vidyāma*)—we shall obtain such, and
- अस्मे (*asme*)—those offered by us
- अहिंसंतीः (*ahiṃsaṃtīḥ*)—those that give you no trouble
- ता (*tā*)—those well-known
- उपस्पृशः (*upaspṛśaḥ*)—those that reach you, the praises
- ते (*te*)—by your favour
- सत्या (*satyā*)—as being of the nature of truth
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—let them be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, as a cowherd enjoys the milk of milch-cows, so we obtain the enjoyments of happiness that are the fruit of certain praises. Let those praises, which are offered by us, give you no trouble, are well known and reach you, have by your favour a fruit of the nature of truth.

##### English translation
Mey these our (praises) reaching you, Indra, be successful, doing no detriment (to you), so that, thunderer, we may obtain the benefits derivable from them, as (a cowherd enjoys those) from the milk cows.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ह॒स्ता यद॒पदी॒ वर्ध॑त॒ क्पाः शची॑भिर्वे॒द्यानां॑ ।  
> शुष्णं॒ परि॑ प्रदक्षि॒णिद्वि॒श्वाय॑वे॒ नि शि॑श्नथः ॥ १४ ॥

### Printed p. 671

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहस्ता । यत् । अपदी । वर्धत । क्षाः । शचीभिः । वेद्यानां ।  
> शुष्णं । परि । प्रदक्षिणित् । विश्वआयवे । नि । शिश्नथः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यद्यदा क्षा भूमिरहस्ता पाणिरहितापदी चरणवर्जिता च। अमनुष्यकर्मकेत्यर्थः । वेद्यानां स्तोत्रयोग्यानां त्वत्प्रभृतीनां देवानां संबंधिभिः
> शचीभिः कर्मभिर्वर्धत अवर्धत। धनधान्यादिभिः समृद्धेत्यर्थः । तदा त्वं परि प्रदक्षिणिदेवंभूतां पृथिवीं परिवेष्ट्य प्रदक्षिणं यथा भवति तथा स्थितं शुष्णमसुरं
> विश्वायवे । तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी । सर्वत्राप्रतिहतगामिन एतदाख्यस्यौर्वशेयराज्ञोऽर्थायॆ नि शिश्नथः। नितरां ताडितवानसि । यद्वा । यदा शुष्ण स्याच्छादनार्थं
> हस्तपादवर्जिता काचित्पृथिवी वेदितव्यानामसुराणं मायारूपैः कर्मभिः शुष्णमसुरं परिवेष्ट्य प्रदक्षिणं यथा भवति तथावस्थितावर्धत तदानीं तां मायोत्पादितां पृथिवीं विश्वायवे सर्वव्यापकस्य मरुद्धणस्य प्रवेशनार्थं नि शिश्नथः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when the earth, अहस्ता (*ahastā*) without hands and अपदी (*apadī*) without feet, that is, not made by human action, flourished (वर्धत (*vardhata*)) through the acts (शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)) of the gods, yourself among them, who are worthy of praise (वेद्यानां (*vedyānāṃ*)), that is, was enriched with wealth, grain and the like, then you struck down the asura Shushna. He was encircling the earth, stationed so as to go round it with the right side towards it (प्रदक्षिणित् (*pradakṣiṇit*)). You did so विश्वायवे (*viśvāyave*), the dative being of purpose: for the sake of the king of Urvaśī's line so named, whose course is unobstructed everywhere.

Alternatively: when a certain earth without hands and feet, produced by the magical acts of the asuras, grew while encircling the asura Shushna in order to cover him, stationed so as to go round him with the right side, then you struck that magically produced earth so that the all-pervading host of the Maruts might enter (विश्वायवे (*viśvāyave*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) यत् (*yat*)—when
- क्षाः (*kṣāḥ*)—the earth
- अहस्ता (*ahastā*)—being without hands
- अपदी (*apadī*)—being without feet
- वेद्यानां (*vedyānāṃ*)—of the gods
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—by the acts
- वर्धत (*vardhata*)—it attained growth, then
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- परि प्रदक्षिणित् (*pari pradakṣiṇit*)—who had surrounded this earth on all sides
- शुष्णं (*śuṣṇaṃ*)—the asura Shushna
- विश्वायवे (*viśvāyave*)—for the king called Vishvayu
- नि शिश्नथः (*ni śiśnathaḥ*)—you destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when the earth, though without hands and feet, grew through the acts of the gods, then you destroyed the asura who had surrounded this earth on all sides, in order to do good to the king called Vishvayu.

##### English translation
When the earth which has neither hands nor feet flourished through the acts of (devotion paid to) the adorable (deities), then did you smite down Shushna, circumambulating it on the right, for the sake of Vishvayu.

### Printed p. 672
#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पिबा॑पि॒बेदिं॑द्र शूर॒ सोमं॒ मा रि॑षण्यो वसवानः॒ वसुः॒  
> सन् ।  
> उ॒त त्रा॑यस्व गृण॒तो म॒घोनो॑ म॒हश्च॑ रा॒यो रे॒वत॑स्कृधी नः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पिबपिब । इत् । इंद्र । शूर । सोमं । मा । रिषण्यः । वसवानः । वसुः । सन् ।  
> उत । त्रायस्व । गृणतः । मघोनः । महः । च । रायः । रेवतः । कृधि । नः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पिबपिबेति वीप्सातित्वराप्रदशनार्थं । हे शूर वीरेंद्र त्वमभिसुतं सोमं
> शीघ्रं पिब । यागकालातिपातो यावन्न भवति तावच्छिघ्रं सोमं पिबेत्यर्थः ।
> इदिति पूरणः । हे वसवान वसूनां धनानामानेतः त्वं वसुः प्रशस्तः सन्मा रिषण्यः ।
> यागकालातिक्रमजातेन दोषेणास्मान्मा हिंसीः । प्रशस्तस्य तव कर्मवैगुण्यकरणेन
> हिंसितुमयुक्तमित्यर्थः । उतापि च हे इंद्र त्वं गृणतस्त्वां स्तुवतः स्तोत्थन्मघोनो हविर्लक्षणधनवतो यजमानांश्च त्रायस्व । प्रमादजनितकर्मवैगुण्यदोषात्पालयस्व । किंच । महश्च राय इत्युभयत्र तृतीयार्थे षष्ठी । महो
> महता रायो धनेन च नोऽस्मान्रेवतः कृधि । धनवतः कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The repetition पिबपिब (*pibapiba*) shows great haste. O mighty, heroic Indra, drink quickly the Soma that has been pressed: drink it quickly, before the proper time of the sacrifice passes. इत् (*it*) is a filler. O वसवान (*vasavāna*), bringer of riches (वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*), of wealth), being वसुः (*vasuḥ*), excellent, do not harm us (मा रिषण्यः (*mā riṣaṇyaḥ*)), that is, do not injure us through any fault arising from the lapse of the sacrificial time. It is not fitting that you, being excellent, should harm us by making the rite defective. And, O Indra, protect those who praise you (गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)), the singers, and the sacrificers (मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*)) who possess wealth in the form of oblations; guard them from the fault of defect in the rite caused by negligence. Further, in महश्च राय (*mahaśca rāya*) the genitive stands in the sense of the instrumental in both words: make us (नः (*naḥ*)) rich (रेवतः (*revataḥ*)), that is, possessed of wealth, with great (महः (*mahaḥ*)) wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O mighty one
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- पिबपिब (*pibapiba*)—drink quickly
- वसवान (*vasavāna*)—you, the bringer of wealth
- वसुः सन् (*vasuḥ san*)—being highly praiseworthy
- मा रिषण्यः (*mā riṣaṇyaḥ*)—do not harm us
- उत (*uta*)—and
- गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)—your singers
- मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*)—the sacrificers who give oblations
- त्रायस्व (*trāyasva*)—protect
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—with great
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- रेवतः (*revataḥ*)—as possessed of wealth
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O mighty Indra, drink the Soma quickly. You, the bringer of wealth, being highly praiseworthy, do not harm us. Protect your singers and the sacrificers who give oblations. With great wealth make us possessed of wealth.

### Printed p. 673

##### English translation
Drink, hero Indra, drink the Soma; being excellent, harm (us) not, possessor of opulence; preserve those who praise you, and are offfluent (in offerings), and render us rich with great riches.

## Sūkta 23 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यजामह इति सप्तर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं । प्रथमासप्तम्या त्रिष्टुभौ : पंचम्यभिसारिणी । द्विर्दशकद्विद्वादशकवतीत्यभिसारिणीत्युच्यते । शिष्टाश्चतस्रो जगत्यः ।
> पूर्ववदृषिदेवते । तथा चानुक्रांतं । यजामहे सप्ताद्यांत्ये त्रिष्टुभौ पंचम्यभिसारिणीति ॥ चतुर्थेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने तृतीयापंचम्योरावर्तनेन श्रींस्तृचान् होत्रका एकैकं तृचमावपेरन् । सूत्रितं च । यजामह इंद्रं वज्र दक्षिणमिति द्वितीयानेवमेव । आ-७-११ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seven-Ṛk sūkta beginning यजामह (*yajāmaha*) is the seventh sūkta. The first and the seventh Ṛk are in triṣṭubh; the fifth is abhisāriṇī, which is the name for a verse having two twice-ten-syllable and two twice-twelve-syllable pādas. The remaining four are in jagatī. The seer and the deity are as before. So the Anukramaṇī says: यजामहे सप्ताद्यांत्ये त्रिष्टुभौ पंचम्यभिसारिणीति (*yajāmahe saptādyāṃtye triṣṭubhau paṃcamyabhisāriṇīti*). Use: on the fourth day, at the midday pressing, the Hotrakas should insert one trca each, by repeating the third and the fifth Ṛk, making three trcas. It is also taught in the Sūtra: यजामह इंद्रं वज्र दक्षिणमिति द्वितीयानेवमेव (*yajāmaha iṃdraṃ vajra dakṣiṇamiti dvitīyānevameva*) (Ā. Sū. 7-11).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning यजामहे (*yajāmahe*) is the seventh sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The seers and deity of this sūkta are the same as those of the preceding sūkta. The first and seventh Ṛks of this sūkta are in the triṣṭubh metre; the fifth Ṛk is in the metre called abhisāriṇī. If a Ṛk has four pādas, of which two have ten syllables each and the other two twelve syllables each, that Ṛk is said to be in the abhisāriṇī metre. The remaining Ṛks are in the jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated as यजामहे सप्ताद्यांते त्रिष्टुभौ पंचम्यभिसारिणी (*yajāmahe saptādyāṃte triṣṭubhau paṃcamyabhisāriṇī*). On the fourth day of the sacrifice, at the midday pressing, three Ṛks are to be put together by repeating the third and the fifth Ṛks of this sūkta, and the priests of the Hotṛ group should recite them for the purpose of āvāpa. This is explained by the sūtra यजामह इंद्रं वज्रदक्षिणमिति द्वितीयानेवमेव (*yajāmaha iṃdraṃ vajradakṣiṇamiti dvitīyānevameva*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 7-11).

Sūkta—23
- Maṇḍala—10; Anuvāka—2; Sūkta—23.
- Aṣṭaka—7; Adhyāya—7; Varga—9.
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—7.
- Ṛṣi: Vimada Aindra Prājāpatya, or Vasukṛt Vāsukra.
- Deity: Indra.
- Metre: 1, 7 triṣṭubh; 2-4, 6 jagatī; 5 abhisāriṇī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यजा॑मह॒ इंद्रं॒ वज्र॑दक्षिणं॒ हरी॑णां र॒थ्यं१॒॑ १ विव्र॑तानां ।  
> प्र श्मश्रु॒ दोधु॑वदू॒र्ध्वथा॑ भू॒द्वि सेना॑भि॒र्दय॑मानो॒ वि  ॑
> राधसा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यजामहे । इंद्रं । वज्रदक्षिणं । हरीणां । रथ्यं । विव्रतानां ।  
> प्र । श्मश्रु । दोधुवत् । ऊर्ध्वथा । भूत् । वि । सेनाभिः । दयमानः । वि ।  
> राधसा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वयमिंद्रं यजामहे । सोमलक्षणैर्हविर्भिः पूजयामः । कीदृशं ।
> वज्रदक्षिणं शत्रुवधाय सततं वज्रो दक्षिणे हस्ते यस्य तं विव्रतानां रथवहनादिविविधकर्मणां हरीणामेतत्संज्ञकानामश्वानां रथ्यमानेतारं । स इंद्रः सोमपानानंतरं स्मश्रु स्वकीयानि स्मश्रूणि दोधुवत् पुनःपुनर्धून्वानः सन्नूर्ध्वथोर्ध्व० प्र भूत् । प्रादुरभूत् । किंच सेनाभिर्मरुदादिस्वकीयैः सैन्यैर्वि
> दयमानो विविधं शत्रून्हिंसनाधसा । द्वितीयार्थे तृतीया । राधो धनं ।
> वीत्युपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । विविधं स्तोतृभ्यो ददाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We worship Indra with oblations in the form of Soma. He is described as वज्रदक्षिणं (*vajradakṣiṇaṃ*): the one who always holds the thunderbolt in his right hand in order to kill enemies. He is रथ्यं (*rathyaṃ*), the leader of the bay horses (Hari) called by this name, which are विव्रतानां (*vivratānāṃ*), that is, engaged in various works such as drawing the chariot. After drinking Soma, that Indra, repeatedly shaking his own beard, comes forth upward (प्र भूत् (*pra bhūt*) means "appeared"). Further, he destroys enemies in manifold ways with his own armies, the Maruts and the rest. राधसा (*rādhasā*) has the third case in the sense of the second; *rādhaḥ* is wealth. Because the preposition वि (*vi*) is heard, a suitable verb has to be supplied: he gives wealth variously to the praisers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रदक्षिणं (*vajradakṣiṇaṃ*)—one who holds the thunderbolt in his right hand
- विव्रतानां (*vivratānāṃ*)—capable of many works
- हरीणां (*harīṇāṃ*)—of the horses
- रथ्यं (*rathyaṃ*)—the leader
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- यजामहे (*yajāmahe*)—we worship
- श्मश्रु (*śmaśru*)—the hairs of his face
- दोधुवत् (*dodhuvat*)—shaking again and again
- ऊर्ध्वया (*ūrdhvayā*)—facing upward
- प्र भूत् (*pra bhūt*)—has mounted
- सेनाभिः (*senābhiḥ*)—with the armies of the Maruts and others
- वि दयमानः (*vi dayamānaḥ*)—destroying enemies in many ways
- राधसा (*rādhasā*)—with wealth he satisfies his worshippers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We worship Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his right hand and is the leader of the horses, which are capable of many works. That same Indra, shaking the hairs of his face again and again,
### Printed p. 675
has mounted upward. Destroying enemies in many ways with the armies of the Maruts and others, he satisfies his worshippers with wealth.

##### English translation
We worship Indra, bearing in his right hand the thunderbolt, the driver of the bay horses which have many functions: shaking his beard, he mounts on high, destroying (his enemies) by his armies he gives wealth (to his worshippers).
#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हरी॒ न्व॑स्य॒ या वने॑ वि॒दे वस्विंद्रो॑ म॒घैर्म॒घवा॑ वृत्र॒हा  ॑
> भुवत् ।  
> ऋ॒भुर्वाज॑ ऋभु॒क्षाः प॑त्यते॒ शवोऽव॑ क्षौमि॒ दास॑स्य॒ नाम॑  
> चित् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हरी इति । नु । अस्य । या । वने । विदे । वसु । इंद्रः । मघैः । मघवा ।  
> वृत्रहा । भुवत् ।  
> ऋभुः । वाजः । ऋभुक्षाः । पत्यते । शवः । अव । क्षौमि । दासस्य । नाम । चित् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्येंद्रस्य संबंधिनौ या यौ हरी अश्वा वने । वन्यंते संभज्यंतेऽस्मिन्देवा
> इति वनं यज्ञोऽरण्यं वा । तस्मिन्वस्वजीषलक्षणं धनं यवसलक्षणं वा नु क्षिप्रं
> विदे विंदेते लभेते । यद्वा । यौ हरी अस्येंद्रस्य वने संभजनार्थं वसु वसुनो
> लाभाय क्षिप्रं भवत इति शेषः । ताभ्यां हरिभ्यां मघैर्धनैर्मघवान्थनवानिंद्रो
> वृत्रहा वृत्राख्यस्यासुरस्य मेघस्य वा हंता भुवत् । भवति । अर्षिचर्भुर्दिप्तो
> वाजो बलवानृभुक्षा महानिंद्रः शवः शवसो बलस्य धनस्य वा पत्यते । ईष्टे ।
> यद्वा । शत्रूणां बलं प्रति पत्यते । प्रतिपद्यते । गच्छति । अहमपि तस्य प्रसादाद्दासस्योपक्षपयितव्यस्य शत्रोर्नाम चित् । नम्यतेऽनेनेति नाम शिरः । तदप्यव क्षामि ।
> अवहन्मि । किमुतान्यदंगं । अथवा । नामधेयमपि नाशयामि किमुत शत्रुं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two bay horses of this Indra find quickly, in the वने (*vane*), wealth (वसु (*vasu*)). वनं (*vanaṃ*) is the sacrifice (in which the gods are shared out, वन्यंते (*vanyaṃte*)) or else the forest. The wealth is of the kind of *ajīṣa* or of barley (यवस (*yavasa*)). विदे (*vide*) means "the two obtain". Or else: the two horses of Indra become quick in the वने (*vane*) in order to obtain wealth, with "become" to be supplied. By those two horses Indra, rich in मघैः (*maghaiḥ*) (riches), becomes the slayer of Vṛtra, the Asura of that name, or of the cloud. Ṛbhu is the shining one; Vāja is the strong one; Ṛbhukṣā is the great Indra; he is lord (पत्यते (*patyate*) = ईष्टे (*īṣṭe*)) of strength (शवः (*śavaḥ*)), or of wealth. Or else: पत्यते (*patyate*) means he goes against the strength of the enemies. By his grace I too cut off the head (नाम (*nāma*), so called because one bows by it) of the Dāsa who is to be destroyed; how much more any other limb. Or else: I destroy even the name; how much more the enemy.
**NOTE**

- वाजः (*vājaḥ*)—the powerful one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, accompanied by those horses which quickly provide wealth at the sacrifice, and wealthy through his riches, becomes the slayer of enemies. Indra, the radiant, powerful and great, is the lord of strength. With Indra's help I cut off the head of the enemy who is a harmer.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यदेंद्रो हिरण्यं हितरमणीयं वज्रं स्वकीयमायुधं शत्रुहननाय
> गृह्ञातीति शेषः । इदिति पूरणः । अथ तदानीमस्येंद्रस्य हरी अश्वा यं रथं वहतः
> गंतृप्रदेशं विशेषेण प्रापयतः मघवा धनवानिंद्रः सूरिभिः स्तोतृभिः कुत्सादिभिः

> विख्यात इत्यर्थः । दीर्घश्रवसो बहुकीर्तेर्वाजस्यान्नस्य पतिः स्वामी । एवंभूत
> इंद्रस्तं रथमारोहतीत्यर्थः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When Indra takes up his golden (हिरण्यं (*hiraṇyaṃ*) = beneficial and delightful) thunderbolt, his own weapon, to kill enemies (the verb "takes" is to be supplied; इत् (*it*) is a filler), then the two bay horses of Indra draw the chariot, bringing it specially to the place of going. Wealthy Indra mounts that chariot together with the सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*), the praisers such as Kutsa. He is सनश्रुतः (*sanaśrutaḥ*), long famed, that is, renowned in the world naturally. He is lord of वाजस्य (*vājasya*), food, of दीर्घश्रवसः (*dīrghaśravasaḥ*), of wide fame. Such an Indra mounts that chariot.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रं (*vajraṃ*)—the thunderbolt (Indra takes up)
- अथ (*atha*)—then immediately
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses
- यं रथं (*yaṃ rathaṃ*)—which chariot
- वहतः (*vahataḥ*)—draw, that very chariot
- मघवा (*maghavā*)—the wealthy
- सनश्रुतः (*sanaśrutaḥ*)—renowned from long ago
- दीर्घश्रवसः (*dīrghaśravasaḥ*)—of great fame
- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—of food
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—the lord
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*)—with his praisers
- आ तिष्ठति (*ā tiṣṭhati*)—mounts

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as Indra takes up the golden thunderbolt, his horses draw his chariot. Indra, renowned from long ago and lord of food of great fame, mounts that same chariot with his praisers.

##### English translation
When he grasps his golden thunderbolt, then the opulent Indra ascends with his praisers, the chariot which his two bay horses draw, (Indra) the lord of long celebrated and widely renowned food.

> अव । वेति । सुक्षयं । सुते । मधु । उत् । इत् । धूनोति । वातः । यथा ।  
> वनं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तच्छब्दश्रुतेर्यच्छब्दोऽध्याहर्तव्यः । या महती वृष्टिरस्ति सो सा वृष्टिर्नु
> क्षिप्रं । चिदित्युपमार्थे । यथा सर्वं सिंचति तथेंद्रः स्वा स्वानि यूथ्या यूथानि
> मरुदादिगणलक्षणानि सचा सह स्वानि श्मशूणि च हरिता हरिद्वर्णेन सोमेनाभि
> पुष्णुते ॥ पुष प्लुष स्नेहनसेचनपूरणेष्टिति धातुः ॥ अभिमुख्येन स्थित्वा क्षिप्रं
> सिंचति । सोमं पाययति पिबति चेत्यर्थः । अपि च सुक्षयं शोभनं यज्ञगृहमव
> वेति । अभिगच्छति । गत्वा च सुते सोमेऽभिषुते सति मधु मधुररसोपेतं सोमं
> पीत्वा । मत्तः सन्निति शेषः । उदिद्दूनोति । स्वशरीरमुत्कंपयति । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> पातो वायुर्यथा वनं वृक्षसमूहमुत्कंपयति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Because the word तत् (*tat*) is heard, the word *yat* must be supplied: the great rain that there is, that rain quickly; चित् (*cit*) is in the sense of comparison. As the rain wets everything, so Indra, together with his own troops (यूथ्या (*yūthyā*)), the hosts of Maruts and others, sprinkles his own beards with the green-coloured Soma (हरिता (*haritā*)). Of the root पुष (*puṣa*), प्लुष (*pluṣa*), in the sense of moistening, sprinkling, filling: standing facing, he quickly sprinkles; he makes Soma be drunk and drinks it. Further, he goes to the fair sacrificial house (सुक्षयं (*sukṣayaṃ*)). Having gone, when Soma is pressed, he drinks the sweet Soma and, intoxicated (to be supplied), shakes his body. The example: as the wind shakes the forest, the mass of trees.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सो (*so*)—the well-known
- वृष्टिः (*vṛṣṭiḥ*)—rain
- नु चित् (*nu cit*)—as it quickly wets all regions
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- स्वा (*svā*)—his own
- यूथ्या सचा (*yūthyā sacā*)—with the hosts of Maruts
- श्मशूणि (*śmaśūṇi*)—the hairs of his face
- हरिता (*haritā*)—with the green-coloured Soma
- अभि प्रुष्णुते (*abhi pruṣṇute*)—wets
- सु क्षयं (*su kṣayaṃ*)—the excellent sacrificial house
- अव वेति (*ava veti*)—enters
- वातः (*vātaḥ*)—the wind
- यथा (*yathā*)—as
- वनं (*vanaṃ*)—as it makes the forest tremble, so
- सुते (*sute*)—when Soma is pressed
- मधु (*madhu*)—having drunk the sweet Soma
- उदिद्दूनोति (*udiddūnoti*)—Indra trembles

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the well-known rain quickly wets all regions, Indra, with his hosts of Maruts, wets the hairs of his face with the green-coloured Soma. He enters the excellent sacrificial house. As the wind makes the forest tremble, so, when Soma is pressed, Indra drinks the sweet Soma and shows his satisfaction by shaking his head.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इंद्रो वाचा वाज्मात्रेणैन विवाचो विविधवाचः स्वशत्रुन् मृध्रवाचो हिंसितवाचः । कृत्वेति शेषः । पुरु पुरूणि बहून्यशिवाशिवान्यसुखकराणि ।
> दुःखकराणीत्यर्थः । सहस्रा शत्रुणां सहस्राणि जघान हंति । अपि च यश्चेंद्रः
> पितेव यथा पिता पुत्रस्य तविषीं बलमन्न प्रदानैर्ववृधे वर्धयति तथा वृष्टिद्वारेण सर्वस्य जगतः शवो बलं ववृधे वर्धयति अस्येंद्रस्य तत्तदित्तत्तदेव पौंस्यं
> बलं गृणीमसि । वयं स्तुमः । इंद्रो येन येन बलेन शत्रुन्हंति तस्य
> तत्तद्बलं वयं स्तुम इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, by speech alone, makes his enemies विवाचः (*vivācaḥ*), of various speech, and मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*), of harmed speech (*kṛtvā*, "having made", is to be supplied), and he kills many thousands of enemies, अशिवा (*aśivā*), that is, inauspicious and painful ones. Further, as a father increases the strength (तविषीं (*taviṣīṃ*)) of his son by gifts of food, so Indra, by means of rain, increases the strength (शवः (*śavaḥ*)) of the whole world. We praise (गृणीमसि (*gṛṇīmasi*)) each and every manly power (पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*)) of this Indra: by whatever strength Indra kills enemies, each such strength of his we praise.

- पुरु (*puru*)—of great number
- अशिवा (*aśivā*)—and inauspicious
- सहस्रा (*sahasrā*)—thousands of enemies
- जघान (*jaghāna*)—has killed

> पूर्वोत्तरयोरेकवाक्ययोः पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ कीदृशं । अपूर्वमपूर्वमन्यैः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, we who bear the name Vimada have produced for you, for the sake of your good giving, a special praise (स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*))." अजीजनन् (*ajījanan*) means "have produced, have made". Here, in the two sentences that form one statement, there is an interchange of person. What kind of praise? अपूर्वं (*apūrvaṃ*): not made before by others, that is, excellent.

### Printed p. 681

> पूर्वमकृतं । उत्कृष्टमित्यर्थः । पुरुतमं बहुतमं । नानाप्रकारोपेतमित्यर्थः ।
> हि यस्मात्कारणाद्दे इंद्र इनस्येश्वरस्यास्यॆदृशस्य तव यद्भोजनं धनमस्तीति विद्म
> वयं जानीमः तस्मात्कारणात्त्वदीयं तद्धनमा करामहे । वयमस्मदभिमुखं
> कुर्महे । तत्र दृष्टांतः । पशुं न गोपा यथा गोपालो धेनुमाह्वयन्
> स्वस्याभिमुखीं करोति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

पुरुतमं (*purutamaṃ*) means "most abundant", that is, endowed with many kinds. "Since, O Indra, we know the wealth (भोजनं (*bhojanaṃ*)) that belongs to you, the lord (इनस्य (*inasya*)), therefore we turn that wealth of yours toward us (आ करामहे (*ā karāmahe*))." The illustration: as a cowherd, calling his cow, makes her turn toward himself, so (we do).

- सुदानवे (*sudānave*)—for the sake of excellent giving
- अजीजनन् (*ajījanan*)—have produced
- हि (*hi*)—for what reason
- इनस्य (*inasya*)—of the lord
- अस्य (*asya*)—of you
- यत् भोजनं (*yat bhojanaṃ*)—which wealth
- विद्म (*vidma*)—we know; therefore
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—as cowherds
- पशुं न (*paśuṃ na*)—call a cow
- आ करामहे (*ā karāmahe*)—we pray to you and call you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we who bear the name Vimada have composed a new and most abundant praise addressed to you, for the sake of excellent giving. Since we know what wealth of yours, the lord, there is, therefore we pray to you and call you, as cowherds call a cow.

##### English translation

> जानीमः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । जामिवद्यथा भ्राता स्वभगिन्यां स्नेहयुक्तां मतिं
> जानाति तद्वत् । तस्मात्कारणादस्मे अस्माकं ते तव च सख्या सख्यानि शिवानि संतु ।
> मंगलानि भवंतु । अनपायानीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, may these friendships of ours, of you and of the seer Vimada, that is, of me, never be sundered." नः (*naḥ*) is a plural used for two (Pā. Sū. 1.2-59). The friendships (सख्या (*sakhyā*)), consisting in being the praised and the praiser, the sacrificed-to and the sacrificer, are the actions of friends; may they nowhere be loosened. "Since, O shining Indra, we know your gracious (*anugrāhikāṃ*) mind (प्रमतिं (*pramatiṃ*))", as a brother knows the affectionate mind of his own sister, "therefore may the friendships between us and you be auspicious", that is, free from loss.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- तव च (*tava ca*)—to you
- विमदस्य ऋषेः (*vimadasya ṛṣeḥ*)—and to me, the seer named Vimada
- नः (*naḥ*)—for the two of us
- एना (*enā*)—this famous
- सख्या (*sakhyā*)—friendship
- माकिः वियोषुः (*mākiḥ viyoṣuḥ*)—may it not be sundered
- हि (*hi*)—because
- देव (*deva*)—O shining Indra
- जामिवत् (*jāmivat*)—as one knows the mind of near ones
- ते (*te*)—your
- प्रमतिं (*pramatiṃ*)—excellent mind
- विद्म (*vidma*)—we know
- अस्मे (*asme*)—for us
- ते (*te*)—with you
- सख्या (*sakhyā*)—friendship
- शिवानि (*śivāni*)—auspicious
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—may it be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may no break come upon the famous friendship between you and me, the seer named Vimada. O shining Indra, we know your excellent mind, as one knows the mind of near ones. May the friendship we have with you be auspicious.

##### English translation
Never may these friendships of you, Indra, and of the Rishi Vimada be disunited: for we know your attachment, divine (Indra), to be like that of a sister (to a brother) so may the friendship between us and you prosper.

## Sūkta 24 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्र सोममिति षडृचमष्टमं सूक्तं । चतुर्थाद्यास्ति स्रोऽनुष्टुभोऽश्विदेवत्याः । आदितस्तिस्र ऐंद्र आस्तारपंक्तिच्छंदस्काः । आदितो द्वौ गायत्रौ ततो
> द्वौ जागतौ सास्तारपंक्तिः । ऋषिः पूर्ववत् । तथा चानुक्रांतं । इंद्र सोमं
> षळास्तारपांक्तं त्वाश्विन्योऽंत्यास्ति स्रोऽनुष्टुभ इति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta इंद्र सोमं (*iṃdra somaṃ*) has six Ṛks and is the eighth sūkta. The three Ṛks beginning with the fourth are Anuṣṭubh and addressed to the Aśvins. The first three are addressed to Indra and have the Āstārapaṅkti metre: the first two pādas are Gāyatra, the next two Jāgata, and so it is Āstārapaṅkti. The seer is as before. The Anukramaṇī says the same. The viniyoga has been given already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta "Indra somam" is the eighth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the same as that of the preceding sūkta. The three Ṛks from the fourth onward are in the Anuṣṭubh metre and have the Aśvins as deity. The first three Ṛks have Indra as deity and the Āstārapaṅkti metre: if a Ṛk has four pādas and two of them have the syllable count of the Gāyatrī metre and the remaining two that of the Jagatī metre, that Ṛk is called Āstārapaṅkti. The Anukramaṇī says the same. The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Sūkta—24
Maṇḍala—10; Anuvāka—2; Sūkta—24.
Aṣṭaka—7; Adhyāya—7; Varga—10.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—6.
Ṛṣi—विमद ऐंद्रः प्राजापत्यो वा वसुकृद्वा वासुक्रः (*vimada aiṃdraḥ prājāpatyo vā vasukṛdvā vāsukraḥ*).
Devatā—1-2. इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*); 4-6. अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*). **NOTE**
Chandas—1-3. आस्तारपंक्तिः (*āstārapaṃktiḥ*); 4-6. अनुस्टुप् (*anusṭup*).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॒ सोम॑मि॒मं पि॑ब॒ मधु॑मंतं च॒मू सु॒तं ।  
> अ॒स्मे र॒यिं नि धा॑रय॒ वि वो॒ मदे॑ सह॒स्रिणं॑ पुरूवसो॒  ॑
> विवक्षसे ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 684

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्र । सोमं । इमं । पिब । मधुमंतं । चमू इति सुतं ।  
> अस्मे इति । रयिं । नि । धारय । वि । वः । मदे ! सहस्रिणं पुरुवसो इति  
> पुरुवसो । विवक्षसे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वमिममीदृशं सोमं पिब ' कीदृशं । मधुमंतं मधुररसोपेतं चमू चमोरधिषवणफलकयोः सुतमभिषुतं। तदनंतरः पुरुवसो बहुधन
> हे इंद्र वस्तव विमदे विशेषेण सोमजन्ममवे सत्यस्य अस्मसु रयिं धनं निधारय । नितरां स्थापय । कीदृशं सहस्तिणं सहस्रसंख्यायुक्तं । प्रभूतमित्यर्थ!
> त्वया दत्तेन धनेन यस्माद्वयं पुनरपि त्ववर्षं यागं कुर्मः तस्मादस्मासु धनं
> निधेहीत्यर्थः । अतः कारणाद्विवक्षसे महन्नामैतत् । त्वं महानवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, drink this Soma", of what kind? मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*): endowed with sweet juice; चमू सुतं (*camū sutaṃ*): pressed in the two चमू (*camū*), namely the two pressing planks (*adhiṣavaṇaphalakayoḥ*). After that, "O Indra, rich in much wealth, at the exhilaration (मदे (*made*))", and the text then continues with a damaged passage **NOTE**, "place wealth firmly in us" (अस्मे रयिं नि धारय (*asme rayiṃ ni dhāraya*)); of what kind? सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*): endowed with a thousandfold number, that is, abundant. "Because with the wealth given by you we again perform a sacrifice त्ववर्षं यागं (*tvavarṣaṃ yāgaṃ*) **NOTE**, therefore place wealth in us." For this reason विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*), which is a name of "great": you are great.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this (satisfied?) **NOTE**
- मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)—possessed of sweet juice
- चमू (*camū*)—by the planks
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- पुरुवसो (*puruvaso*)—O Indra, possessed of very great wealth
- वि (*vi*)—to you
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—when very great joy has arisen
- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)—thousandfold
- रयं (*rayaṃ*)—wealth
- नि धारॆय (*ni dhārèya*)—place firmly
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are a great one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink the Soma offered by us, with sweet juice, pressed by the planks. O Indra, possessed of very great wealth, when very great joy has arisen in you, place wealth firmly in us. You are a great one.

##### English translation
Drink, Indra, this most sweet Soma, expressed by the planks (of the Soma-press), then bestow upon us riches in your exhilaration ; thousandfold (riches), lord of infinite wealth ; you are mighty.

> त्वां य॒ज्ञेभि॑रु॒क्थैरुस॑ ह॒व्येभि॑रीमहे ।  
> शची॑पते शचीनां॒ वि वो॒ मदे॒ श्रेष्ठं॑ नो धेहि॒ वार्यं॒  ॑
> विवक्षसे ॥ २ ॥

> शचीपते । शचीनां । वि । वः । मदे । श्रेष्ठं । नः । धेहि । वार्यं । विवक्षसे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वयं यज्ञेभिर्यज्ञैः सोमयागादिभिरुक्थैः शस्त्रलक्षणैः
> स्तोत्रैर्हव्येभिर्हव्यैः पुरोडाशादिभिश्च । उपेत्युपसर्गश्रुतेयोग्यपदाध्याहारः । त्वामुपेत्येमहे । अभिलषितं धनं याचामहे । अतो हे शचीपते
> कर्मणां पालयितः । त्वं केषांचित्कर्मणां पालको न भवसीति न किंतु शचीनां
> सर्वेषां कर्मणां पालको भवसीत्यर्थः । एवं याचितस्त्वं नोऽस्मभ्यं वार्यं
> वरणीयं श्रेष्ठं प्रशस्ततमं पश्वादिधनं धेहि । देहि । शिष्टं स्पष्टं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, we ask you for the wealth we desire, with sacrifices (यज्ञेभिः (*yajñebhiḥ*)), the Soma sacrifices and others; with *ukthaiḥ*, praises in the form of śastras; and with हव्येभिः (*havyebhiḥ*), oblations such as the purodāśa." Because the preverb उप (*upa*) is heard, a suitable word has to be supplied: "approaching you we ask (ईमहे (*īmahe*))", that is, we beg for the wealth we desire. Therefore, O शचीपते (*śacīpate*), protector of rites: you are not the protector of some rites only, but of all the शचीनां (*śacīnāṃ*), all rites. So entreated, give us choice (वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)), best, most excellent wealth such as cattle (धेहि (*dhehi*) means "give"). The rest is clear.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) यज्ञेभिः (*yajñebhiḥ*)—with sacrifices and the like
- उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*)—with śastra-mantras
- हव्येभिः (*havyebhiḥ*)—with oblations
- त्वां उप (*tvāṃ upa*)—worshipping you
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask for what we desire
- शचीपते (*śacīpate*)—O Indra, protector of rites
- शचीनां (*śacīnāṃ*)—you are the lord of all rites
- वः (*vaḥ*)—to you
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—when very great joy has arisen
- नः (*naḥ*)—in us
- श्रेष्ठं (*śreṣṭhaṃ*)—excellent
- वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)—and desired
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—place wealth
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are a great one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, worshipping you with sacrifices and the like, with śastra-mantras and with oblations, we ask for what we desire. O Indra, protector of rites, you are the lord of all rites. When very great joy has arisen in you, place in us wealth that is excellent and desired. You are a great one.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यस्त्वं वायाणां वरणीयानां धनानां पतिरसि स्वामी भवसि ।
> रध्रस्य राधकस्य स्तोतुश्च चोदिता धनदानेन कर्मसु नियोक्ता च भवसि । किं च
> हे इंद्र यस्त्वं स्तोत्कृणामविता रक्षकोऽसि । स त्वं वि वो मदे तव विविधे

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who are the lord of choice (वरणीयानां (*varaṇīyānāṃ*)) riches, and who are the impeller of the liberal worshipper (रध्रस्य (*radhrasya*)) and of the praiser, setting him to his tasks by the gift of wealth. Further, you who are the protector of the praisers: in your manifold Soma-born exhilaration, protect us from the hater, and protect us from sin. Why are you so addressed? Because you are mighty (विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*) = महान्भवसि (*mahānbhavasi*)).

- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are mighty

O Indra, you who are lord of all desired riches, impeller of the praiser and protector of them: in the time of your exceeding exhilaration protect us from enemies. Protect us also from sin. You are mighty.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विमदेन । यत् । ईळिता । नासत्या । निः अमंथतं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शक्रा शक्रौ शत्रुवधादिकर्मसु समर्थौ हे आश्विनौ मायाविना मायाविनौ प्रज्ञावंतौ शत्रुवंचनकुशलौ ना युवं युवां समीची परस्परं संगतौ
> निरमंथतं । अग्निं निरमथ्नीतं । अश्विनावध्वयू । ऐ. ब्रा. १-१८ । इति ब्राह्मणोक्तत्वादग्निमंथसमप्यश्विनोरुपपन्नमिति । कदाश्विनौ निर्मथितवंतौ उच्यते । यद्यदा
> नासत्या नासत्या युवां विमदेन मयेळितौ स्तुता निरमंथतं निरमथ्नीतं तदानीं
> युवां परस्परं संगतौ निर्मथितवंतौ स्थ इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śakras, the two Aśvins, able in deeds such as slaying enemies; O māyāvins, the wise, skilled in deceiving enemies: you two, joined together, churned (निरमंथतं (*niramaṃthataṃ*)) the fire. Since the Brāhmaṇa says अश्विनावध्वयू । ऐ. ब्रा. १-१८ । (*aśvināvadhvayū | ai. brā. 1-18 |*) (Ai. Brā. 1-18), the Aśvins' fire-churning is fitting. When did they churn? When, O Nāsatyas, you were praised by me, Vimada, then, joined together, you churned it forth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शक्रा (*śakrā*)—O able Aśvin deities
- मायाविना (*māyāvinā*)—O wise ones
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you
- समीची (*samīcī*)—being united
- निरमंथतं (*niramaṃthataṃ*)—churned the fire and made it blaze

- नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—O Aśvin deities, of true nature
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- विमदेन (*vimadena*)—by me, named Vimada
- ईळिता (*īḷitā*)—you were praised
- निरमंथतं (*niramaṃthataṃ*)—you churned the fire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O able Aśvin deities, wise as you are, you joined together and churned the fire. O Aśvin deities of true nature, when you were praised by me, named Vimada, you churned the fire and made it blaze.

##### English translation
Powerful and sagacious (Aswins) mutually associated, you have churned forth (the fire): when you, Nasatyas, glorified by Vimada, have churned it forth.

> नासत्यौ । अब्रुवन् । देवाः । पुनः । आ । वहतात् । इति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ युवाभ्यामग्निमंथनकाले प्रेर्यमाणयोः समीच्योः
> परस्परेण संयुक्तयोररण्योर्निष्पतंत्र्योर्विस्फुलिंगान्निर्गमयंत्योः सत्योर्विश्वे सर्व इंद्रादयो देवा अकृपंत । युवामस्तुवन् । किंच । देवा
> नासत्यावश्विनौ युवामब्रुवन् । अवोचन् । किमिति । पुनरा वहतादिति । पुनःपुनरीदृशानि जगत्स्थितिहेतुभूतानि कर्माणि युवामाभिमुख्येन स्थित्वावहतं ! यद्वा ।
> युवाभ्यामुत्पाद्यमानः पुनश्चायमग्निरस्मदीयानि हवींष्यावहत्वति देवा
> नासत्यावब्रुवन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, at the time of your fire-churning, while the two fire-sticks, joined with each other and driven by you, were sending out sparks, all the gods, Indra and the rest, were gracious (अकृपंत (*akṛpaṃta*); he glosses: they praised you). Further, the gods said to you, the Nāsatyas: पुनरा वहतादिति (*punarā vahatāditi*)—again and again stand facing us and carry out such acts as sustain the world. Or else: the gods said to the Nāsatyas that this fire, produced by you, should again bear our oblations.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, all the gods, Indra and the rest, have praised you, who are united and who send forth sparks and make the fire blaze. "Again carry out the sacrificial act that sustains the world," the gods have prayed to you of true nature.

##### English translation

> भवत्विति शेषः । पुनरायनं गृहं प्रत्यागमनं मधुमत् प्रीतियुक्तं भवतु । आपि
> xxvii 44

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, may my going away from the house be मधुमत् (*madhumat*). Here the word मधु (*madhu*), denoting a particular flavour, indicates the pleasure in it: by your grace may it be joyful. May my coming back to the house also be मधुमत् (*madhumat*), joyful. And
### Printed p. 690

> च हे देवा देवौ द्योतमानौ ता तौ युवं युवां नोऽस्मान्मधुमतः प्रीतियुक्तान्यतं । कुरुतं । केनेति उच्यते । देवतॆया देवत्वेन । अणिमादिदेवतैश्वर्ययोगेनेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining ones, you two, make us मधुमतः (*madhumataḥ*), endowed with pleasure. By what? By देवतॆया (*devatèyā*), divinity, that is, by possession of the divine powers beginning with aṇimā.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Aśvin deities) मे (*me*)—my
- परायणं (*parāyaṇaṃ*)—going out of the house
- मधुमत् (*madhumat*)—may it be beneficial
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- आयनं (*āyanaṃ*)—returning to the house
- मधुमत् (*madhumat*)—may it bring benefit
- देवा (*devā*)—O Aśvin deities, divine in nature
- ता (*tā*)—you two, the renowned
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you both
- देवतया (*devatayā*)—by your divine power
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मधुमतः (*madhumataḥ*)—as endowed with sweetness
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, may my going out of the house and my coming back home from outside give me a sweet experience. O Aśvin deities, divine in nature, you two, the renowned, by your divine power make us endowed with sweetness.

##### English translation
May my going forth be pleasant, may my coming back be pleasant, you two divine Aswins, render us, through your divine power possessed of pleasure.
## Sūkta 25 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भद्रमित्येकादशर्चं नवमं सूक्तं । तुह्यादिपरिभाषयेदमप्यास्तारपांक्तं।
> सोमदेवताकं । ऋषिश्चान्यस्मादिति परिभाषया प्राजापत्य ऐंद्रो ना विमदो
> वा वासुक्रो वसुकृद्वर्षिः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । भद्रमेकादश सौम्यमिति । गतो
> विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ninth sūkta, भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*), of eleven Ṛks. By the rule beginning तुह्यादि (*tuhyādi*) it is also in the Āstārapaṅkti metre; its deity is Soma. By the rule ऋषिश्चान्यस्मादिति (*ṛṣiścānyasmāditi*) the seer is Vimada, Aindra or Prājāpatya, or Vasukṛt, or Vāsukra. So the Anukramaṇī: भद्रमेकादश सौम्यमिति (*bhadramekādaśa saumyamiti*). The viniyoga has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*) is the ninth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. As for the preceding sūkta, its seer is the one called प्राजापत्य ऐंद्रो वा विमदो वा वासुक्रो वसुकृत् (*prājāpatya aiṃdro vā vimado vā vāsukro vasukṛt*). Soma is the deity; the metre is Āstārapaṅkti. The Anukramaṇī says भद्रमेकादश सौम्यं (*bhadramekādaśa saumyaṃ*). The viniyoga was stated earlier.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भ॒द्रं नो॒ अपि॑ वातय॒ मनो॒ दक्ष॑मु॒त क्रतुं॑ ॥  
> अधा॑ ते स॒ख्ये अंध॑सो॒ वि वो॒ मदे॒ रण॒न्गावो॒ न यव॑से॒  ॑
> विवक्षसे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भद्रं । नः । अपि । वातय । मनः । दक्षं । उत । क्रतुं ।  
> अध । ते । सख्ये । अंधसः । वि । वः । मदे । रणन् । गावः । न । यवसे । विवक्षसे ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं नोऽस्मदीयं मनो भद्रं कल्याणं वातय । गमय ।
> अस्माकं मनः शुभसंकल्पं कुर्वित्यर्थः । तथा दक्षमुत दक्षमपि ॥ दक्ष वृद्धौ ॥ वृद्धं
> सर्वव्यापिनमंतरात्मानमपि भद्रं शुभकारित्वलक्षणं प्रापय । अस्माकमंतरात्मानं
> शुभकारिणं कुर्वित्यर्थः । उतापि च क्रतुं प्रज्ञानं भद्रं शुभाध्यवसायलक्षणं
> प्रापय । शुभाध्यवसायिनं कुर्वित्यर्थः । आधाध स्तोतारस्ते तव सख्यॆ स्तुत्यस्तोतृत्वेज्ययष्टृत्वलक्षणे सखिकर्मणि रणन् । रमंतां । तत्र दृष्टांतः । गावो न
> यवसे यथा धेनवो घासे रमंते प्रीतिं कुर्वंति तद्वत् । कस्मिन्सति । अंधसः
> सोमाख्यस्यान्नस्य संबंधिनि वस्तव विमदे विविधसोमजन्यमदनिमित्ते सति । कस्मादेवं । यस्माद्विवक्षसे । महान्भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, make our mind भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*), auspicious (वातय (*vātaya*) = गमय (*gamaya*)): make our mind form good resolves. Likewise bring दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*) (root दक्ष (*dakṣa*) in the sense of growth), the grown, all-pervading inner self, to the state of doing good: make our inner self a doer of good. And bring our क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*), understanding, to the state of good resolve: make it resolve on good. Then your praisers, in your friendship, a friendly relation consisting of the praiser-and-praised and sacrificer-and-sacrificed, would delight (रणन् (*raṇan*) = रमंतां (*ramaṃtāṃ*)). The example: as cows delight in fodder (गावो न यवसे (*gāvo na yavase*)), as they take pleasure in grass. On what occasion? When there is exhilaration (विमदे (*vimade*)), arising in various ways from the food called Soma (अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)). Why so? Because you are mighty (विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*) = महान्भवसि (*mahānbhavasi*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma deva) नः (*naḥ*)—our
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind
- दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—strength
- उत (*uta*)—and
- क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)—act
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—as auspicious
- वातय (*vātaya*)—impel

- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—in your friendship
- रणन् (*raṇan*)—may they rejoice
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are exceedingly great

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, impel our mind, our strength and our rite so that they may be auspicious. As cows enjoy delight in the pasture, so when you are delighted by the oblation, may your praisers rejoice in your friendship. You are exceedingly great.

##### English translation
Sanctify (Soma) our mind, our heart, our intellect ; and may (your worshipper) delight in your friendship, like cattle in fresh pasture, in your exhilaration (produced) by tht (sacrificial) food; for you are mighty.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हृ॒दि॒स्पृश॑स्त आसते॒ विश्वे॑षु सोम॒ धाम॑सु ।  
> अधा॒ कामा॑ इ॒मे मम॒ वि वो॒ मदे॒ वि ति॑ष्ठंते वसू॒यवो॒  ॑
> विवक्षसे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हृदिस्पृशः । ते । आसते । विश्वेषु । सोम । धामसु ।  
> अध । कामाः । इमे । मम । वि । वः । मदे । वि । तिष्ठंते । वस्तुयवः । विवक्षसे ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम ते तव हृदिस्पृशः स्तुतिभिर्हृदयं स्पृशंत ऋत्विजो विश्वेषु
> धामसु सर्वॆषु स्थानेष्वासते । त्वां स्तुवंतस्तिष्ठंति । अधाधेदृग्भूताः कामा अभिलाषा वि वो मदे तव सोमपानजन्यविविधमदनिमित्ते सति । सोमयागार्थमित्यर्थः । वसूयवो वसुकामा धनमिच्छंतो मम। हृदयादिति शेषः । वि तिष्ठंते ।
> उत्तिष्ठंति । कस्मादेवं । यस्माद्विवक्षसे । महान्भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, those priests of yours who are हृदिस्पृशः (*hṛdispṛśaḥ*), "touching the heart" with their praises, remain in all the places (धामसु (*dhāmasu*)), that is, in all the sites of the rite, praising you. Then (अध (*adha*)), when your manifold exhilaration arises from the drinking of Soma, that is, for the sake of the Soma sacrifice, those desires of mine, wishing for wealth (वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*)), rise up (वि तिष्ठंते (*vi tiṣṭhaṃte*)) from my heart (the words "from the heart" are supplied). Why is it so? Because you are great.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, priests who give you satisfaction praise you in every sacrificial house. At that time, when you are delighted, all my desires, longing for wealth, rise up and show themselves. You are a great one.

##### English translation
They who seek to touch your heart, Soma, worship you in all places; and these desires for wealth rise from my heart at your exhilaration ; for you are mighty.

> सर्वार्थदर्शिना प्रज्ञया । यद्वा । पाक्येति व्रतविशेषणमेतत् । पाक्यानि परिपक्वानि ।

"Moreover, O Soma, I perform for you the व्रतानि (*vratāni*), that is, rites such as the sacrifice, with पाक्या (*pākyā*), a ripened intelligence that sees all ends." Or else: पाक्या (*pākyā*) is an epithet of the rites, meaning "ripened", that is, completed.

### Printed p. 694

> परिनिष्ठितानीत्यर्थः । प्र मिनामि । प्रहिनस्मि । प्रकर्षण करोमीत्यर्थः । अधाथ
> यागानंतरं वि वो मदे तव विविधे मदे सति नोऽस्मान्मृळ । सुखय । अभि
> चिद्वधादाभिमुख्येन स्थित्वा शत्र्वादिवधाच्चास्मान्पालयेति शेषः । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> पितेव सूनवे । यथा पिता पुत्रार्थं सुखयति सर्वस्मात्पुत्रमेव पालयति तद्वत् ।
> यस्मात्सुख्यमानः पाल्यमानश्चाहं युष्मदर्थं पुनःपुनः सोमयागं करोमि
> तस्मान्मां सुखय पालय चेत्यर्थः ! कस्मादेवमुच्यसे । यस्मात्त्वं विवक्षसे
> महान्भवसि । महांतश्च भक्तान्सुखयंति पालयंति चेति यावत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

प्र मिनामि (*pra mināmi*) means "I do", that is, I perform to perfection. Then (अध (*adha*)), after the sacrifice, when you are manifoldly exhilarated, make us happy (मृळ (*mṛḷa*)) and protect us from being killed by enemies and the like, facing them (the words "protect us" are supplied). The example: पितेव सूनवे (*piteva sūnave*), as a father makes his son happy and protects only him from everything. Since, being made happy and protected, I perform the Soma sacrifice again and again for you, therefore make me happy and protect me. Why are you addressed so? Because you are great; and the great make their devotees happy and protect them.

- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—when abundant delight arises
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मृळ (*mṛḷa*)—make happy
- अभि चिद्वधात् (*abhi cidvadhāt*)—protect us from violent enemies
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are a great one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, I prepare and offer to you rites such as the sacrifice with a ripened understanding. As a father makes his son happy, so after the sacrifice, when you are exceedingly delighted, make us happy. Protect us from violent enemies. You are a great one.

##### English translation
Verily, Soma, I practice all your observances with fullness; and as a father to his son, so do you in your exhilaration make us happy; protect us from being killed (by our enemies); for you are mighty.

> चमसानिन यथा वस्तव विमदे विविधसोmजन्यमदॆः कर्तव्यत्वेन निमित्तभूते
> सत्यध्वर्युर्हविर्धाने महता यत्नेन चमसान्नोmपात्राणि स्थापयति तद्वत् ।
> कस्मादेवमुच्यसे । यस्मात्त्वं विवक्षसे महान्भवसि । यद्वा । धीतयः । अंगुलिनामैतत् । धयंति पिबंत्याभिरिति धीतयोऽंगुलयः । हे सोम त्वां समु प्र यंति।
> सहैन प्रकर्षण त्वां प्राप्नुवंति । किमिन । अवतानिन । जलोद्धरणार्थं विसृज्यंत
> इति सर्गा रज्जवः । यथा कूपान्मति गच्छंति तद्वत् । ततस्त्वं नोऽस्माकं जीवसे
> चिरंजीवनाय क्रतुं कर्म धारय । यथा संपूर्णं भवति तथा पूरय । किमिन ।
> यथा चमसान्स्वयं पूरयसि तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, our धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*), our praises (so called because they take up, दधति (*dadhati*), the qualities of the deity), come together (समु प्र यंति (*samu pra yaṃti*)) and reach you with an excellent motion. The example: सर्गासोऽवतानिव (*sargāso 'vatāniva*). सर्गासः (*sargāsaḥ*) are herds of cattle let loose to drink water, or the sets of pots fixed on a machine for drawing it; as they go to the अवतान् (*avatān*) (a name for wells) to drink or to take up water, so do the praises go. Knowing this, support (धारय (*dhāraya*)) our rite, the sacrifice and the like, or our wisdom, with great regard for our long life (जीवसे (*jīvase*)). The example: चमसानिव (*camasāniva*), as when your exhilaration produced by Soma is to be brought about, the Adhvaryu sets up the cups (चमसान् (*camasān*)) in the oblation-vessel with great effort. Why are you addressed so? Because you are great.

Or else: धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*) is a name for the fingers; they drink with them (धयंति (*dhayaṃti*)), so the fingers are धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*). O Soma, they reach you together and with force. Like what? Like अवतानिव (*avatāniva*): सर्गासः (*sargāsaḥ*) are ropes, let down to draw up water; as they go to wells, so the fingers go to you. Therefore, for our long life, fulfil (धारय (*dhāraya*)) the rite so that it becomes complete. Like what? As you yourself fill the cups.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- सर्गासः (*sargāsaḥ*)—cows let loose for water
- अवतानिव (*avatāniva*)—as they go quickly to the pools
- धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*)—our praises
- समु प्रयंति (*samu prayaṃti*)—come quickly and reach you
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—for abundant satisfaction
- चमसानिव (*camasāniva*)—as one holds cup-vessels filled with the oblation
- नः क्रतुं (*naḥ kratuṃ*)—our sacrifice
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—for the increase of life
- धारय (*dhāraya*)—lift up and hold (raise it up)
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are a great one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, as cows let loose for water (or pots let down into a well for water) go straight to the well and reach it, so our praises come quickly and reach you.

### Printed p. 696
As we hold cup-vessels filled with the oblation for your abundant satisfaction, so establish our sacrifice for the increase of our life. You are a great one.

##### English translation
Our praises converge (Soma) towards you, as herds towards a well; establish our pious acts, Soma, for us to live (long), as (the priest sets up) the cups for your exhilaration . for you are mighty.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तव॒ तै सो॑म॒ शक्ति॑भि॒र्निका॑मासो॒ व्य॑ण्णिरे ॥  
> गृत्स॑स्य॒ धीरा॑स्त॒वसो॒ वि वो॒ मदे॑ व्र॒जं गोमं॑तम॒श्विनं॒  ॑
> विवक्षसे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शव । श्ये । सोम । शक्तिभिः । निकामासः । पि । यग्वरे ।  
> गृत्सस्य । धीराः । तवसः । वि । वः । मदे । व्रजं । गोऽमंतं । अश्विनं । विवक्षसे ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> निकामसो दृष्टादृष्टफले नियतकामास्त्ये ते प्रसिद्धा धीरा मेधाविन
> ऋत्विजः शक्तिभिर्यागादिकर्मभिः सह हे सोम गृत्सस्य मेधाविनस्तवसो महतस्तव
> वृण्वरे । विविधाः स्तुतीर्गमयंति । पा पयंति । कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः अत कारणाद्वि
> वो मदे तव सोमपानजन्यविविधमदनिमित्तभूते सत्यस्मभ्यं गोमंतं गोसहितमश्विनमत्वसहितं व्रजं गोष्ठं । सामर्थ्यान्मंदुरा लभ्यते । मंदुरां च देहीति
> शेषः । कस्मादेवमुच्यसे । यस्माद्विवक्षसे महान्भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

निकामासः (*nikāmāsaḥ*): those whose desires are fixed on a seen or unseen fruit, the well-known wise (धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)) priests, together with their powers (शक्तिभिः (*śaktibhiḥ*)), that is, rites such as the sacrifice, bring forth manifold praises of you, O Soma, who are wise and great (गृत्सस्य (*gṛtsasya*), तवसः (*tavasaḥ*)); the sense is that they perform them. Therefore, when your manifold exhilaration produced by the drinking of Soma arises, give us a stable (व्रजं (*vrajaṃ*)) with cattle (गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)) and with horses (अश्विनं (*aśvinaṃ*)); by implication "a stable" gives also the sense of a stable of horses, and "give" is supplied. Why are you addressed so? Because you are great.
**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- निकामासः (*nikāmāsaḥ*)—those who are attached to the fruit of rites
- श्यैः (*śyaiḥ*)—the well-known
- धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)—wise priests
- शक्तिभिः (*śaktibhiḥ*)—with their rites
- गृत्सस्य (*gṛtsasya*)—wise
- तवसः (*tavasaḥ*)—great
- तव (*tava*)—addressing you
- व्यण्णिरे (*vyaṇṇire*)—praise in many ways

### Printed p. 697
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—at the time of exceeding delight
- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—filled with cows
- अश्विनं (*aśvinaṃ*)—stocked with horses
- व्रजं (*vrajaṃ*)—provide a stable
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are a great one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, priests who are attached to the fruit of rites, well known and wise, praise you, the wise and great, in many ways with their rites. At the time of your exceeding delight provide a stable filled with cows and stocked with horses. You are a great one.

##### English translation
The intelligent (priests), whose desires are fixed (on the fruit of good works), with sacred rites show forth (the praises) of you, Soma, who are wise and powerful; you, in your exhilaration, (grant us) pastures, abounding with cattle, and with horses; for you are mighty.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प॒शुं नः॑ सोम रक्षसि पुरु॒त्रा विस्थि॑तं॒ जग॑त् ।  
> स॒माकृ॑णोषि जी॒वसे॒ वि वो॒ मदे॒ विश्वा॑ सं॒पश्य॒न्भव॑ना॒  ॑
> विवक्षसे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पशुं । नः । सोम । रक्षसि । पुरुत्रा । विस्थितं । जगत् ।  
> संआकृणोषि । जीवसे । वि । वः । मदे । विश्वा । संपश्यन् । भुवना । विवक्षसे ॥६॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं नोऽस्मदीयं पशुं देवयागार्थमुपाकृतं रक्षसि । पालयसि । न केवलं पशुं किंतु पुरुत्रा बहुधा विष्ठितं सुरनरतिर्यग्योन्यादिभावेनावस्थितं जगच्च रक्षसि । किंच । स त्वं समाकृणोषि । जगतो वृत्तिं सम्यगाकरोषीत्यर्थः । किमर्थं । जीवसे जीवनार्थं । किं कुर्वन् । विश्वा भुवना विश्वानि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you protect (रक्षसि (*rakṣasi*)) our animal (पशुं (*paśuṃ*)), the one brought near for the sacrifice to the gods. Not the animal only: you protect also the world (जगत् (*jagat*)) which stands divided (विष्ठितं (*viṣṭhitaṃ*)) in many ways (पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)), as the existence of gods, men, animals and other births. Further, you set in order (समाकृणोषि (*samākṛṇoṣi*)) the livelihood of the world, that is, you arrange it well. For what? For life (जीवसे (*jīvase*)). Doing what? विश्वा भुवना (*viśvā bhuvanā*), all beings, ….

### Printed p. 698

> भुवनानि भूतजातानि संपश्यन् । किमर्थमेतदादिकं सर्वं करोषि उच्यते । वि
> वो मदे युष्माकं सर्वेषां देवानां विविधहविर्जन्यतृप्त्यर्थं । उक्तं हि ।
> इतःप्रदानमुत देवा उप जीवंत्यमुतःप्रदानं मनुष्या उपजीवंति । तै. सं.
> ३-२-९-७ । इति । अत एव त्वं विवक्षसे । महान्भवसि । महतामेतत्सर्वमुचितमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the gloss of the preceding verse. Soma sees all beings (भुवनानि भूतजातानि (*bhuvanāni bhūtajātāni*)) and does all this for the sake of the delight (वि वो मदे (*vi vo made*)) of all of you gods, that is, for satisfaction produced by the various oblations. He cites *itaḥpradānamuta devā upa jīvaṃti* (Tai. Saṃ. 3-2-9-7): the gods live on what is given from here, and men live on what is given from yonder. Hence Soma is विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*), "you are great"; all this is fitting for the great.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- पशुं (*paśuṃ*)—cattle
- रक्षिसि (*rakṣisi*)—you protect
- पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)—in many ways
- विष्ठितं (*viṣṭhitaṃ*)—established
- जगत् (*jagat*)—the world; you protect it
- वः (*vaḥ*)—of you and of all the gods
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—for the exceeding joy
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—worlds
- संपश्यन् (*saṃpaśyan*)—beholding
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—for living
- समाकृणोषि (*samākṛṇoṣi*)—you prepare
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are great

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you protect our cattle. You also protect the world, which is established in many ways. For the exceeding joy of you and of all the gods, beholding all the worlds, you prepare everything for their living. You are great.

##### English translation
You protect our cattle, Soma, and the variously occupied world contemplating all existing beings ; you prepare (the world) for them to live in for your exhilaration ; for you are mighty.

### Printed p. 699

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम अदाभ्यः केनाप्यहिंस्यस्त्वं विश्वतः सर्वतो नोऽस्माकं गोपा
> रक्षिता भव । अपि च । हे राजन्राजमान सोम त्वं स्रिधोऽस्माकमुपक्षपयित्थनप सेध । अस्मत्तोऽपगमय । अपजहि वा । नोऽस्माकं दुःशंसो विद्यमानानामविद्यमानानां कर्मणां शंसिता प्रख्यापयिता मेशत । ईशिता मा भूत् । तव
> प्रसादादस्माकमपवक्ता कश्चिदपि मा भूदित्यर्थः । किमर्थमेतत्सर्वं प्रार्थ्यते । वि
> वो मदे तव विविधसोमादिहविर्जन्यतृप्त्यर्थं । अतो विनक्षसे । त्वं महान्भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, unassailable, being harmed by none, be our guardian on every side. O shining king, drive away our adversaries (स्रिधः (*sridhaḥ*)), who weaken us, or cast them off. Let no दुःशंसः (*duḥśaṃsaḥ*), one who proclaims actions, real or unreal, to our hurt, rule over us; that is, by your grace let no slanderer of ours exist. Why is all this asked? For your delight, produced by the various oblations such as Soma. Therefore you are great.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- अदाभ्यः (*adābhyaḥ*)—harmed by none
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—on all sides
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—as protector
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- वः (*vaḥ*)—of you and of the gods
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—for the winning of exceeding joy
- राजन् (*rājan*)—O shining Soma
- स्रिधः (*sridhaḥ*)—our injurers
- अप सेध (*apa sedha*)—drive far away
- नः (*naḥ*)—over us
- दुःशंसः (*duḥśaṃsaḥ*)—one who wishes evil
- मा ईशत (*mā īśata*)—let him not exercise lordship
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are great

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Soma, you who are harmed by none, be our protector on every side. For the exceeding joy of you and of the gods, drive our injurers far away. Let one who wishes us evil not rule over us. You are great.

##### English translation
Be on all sides our preserver, Soma, you, who are unassailable; drive away, monarch, our adversaries in your exhilaration, and let no columiator rule over us ; for you are mighty.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम सुक्रतुः शोभनप्रज्ञः क्षेत्रवित्तरः क्षेत्रस्यातिशयेन लंभकस्त्वं
> नोऽस्माकं वयोधेयायान्नदानाय जागृहि । किंच द्रुहो द्रोग्धुर्मनुषो
> मनुष्याच्छत्रोः सकाशान्नोऽस्मान्पाहि । रक्ष । अ०हसः पापाच्च नोऽस्मान्पाहि ।

> महान्भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, of good insight (सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)) and a great finder of fields (क्षेत्रवित्तरः (*kṣetravittaraḥ*)), be watchful for our food-giving (वयोधेयाय (*vayodheyāya*)). Protect us also from the injurer (द्रुहः (*druhaḥ*)), the enemy who is a man (मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)), and from sin (अ०हसः (*a0hasaḥ*)). Why? For your delight produced by Soma and the other oblations. You are great.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)—one of excellent insight
- क्षेत्रवित्तरः (*kṣetravittaraḥ*)—provider of excellent fields
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- वयोधेयाय (*vayodheyāya*)—for the giving of food
- जागृहि (*jāgṛhi*)—be watchful
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—in the time of exceeding joy
- द्रुहः (*druhaḥ*)—wishing us evil
- मनुष्यः (*manuṣyaḥ*)—from the human enemy
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect
- अ०हसः (*a0hasaḥ*)—from sins also protect
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are great

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you who are of excellent insight and provide excellent fields, be watchful for our food-giving. In the time of your exceeding joy protect us from the human enemy who wishes us evil. Protect us from sins also. You are great.

##### English translation
Soma, author of good works, liberal granter of fields, be vigilant in supplying us with food ; and in your exhilaration preserve us from oppres- sive men, (and) from sin ; for you are mighty.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं नो॑ वृत्रहंत॒मेंद्र॑स्येंदो शि॒वः सखा॑ ।

### Printed p. 701

> यत्सीं हवंते समिथे वि वो मदे युध्यमानास्तोकसात्  
> विवक्षसे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । नः । वृत्रहन्तम । इंद्रस्य । इंदो इति । शिवः । सखा ।  
> यत् । सीं । हवंते । संइथे । वि । वः । मदे । युध्यमानाः । तोकसातौ ।  
> विवक्षसे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहंतम शत्रुणामतिशयेन हंतर्हे इंदो हे सोम यस्त्वमिंद्रस्य शिवः सुखकरः सखा मित्रभूतोऽसि स त्वं नोऽस्मान्पाहीति शेषः । कदेति उच्यते ।
> तोकसात् । तोक इत्यपत्यनाम ॥ सातिः । षणु दान इत्यस्माद्धातो रूपं ॥ दीयतेऽस्मिन्न पत्यमिति तोकसातिः संग्रामविशेषणं । तस्मिन् । अतिमहतीत्यर्थः । समिथे
> संग्रामे युद्धमाना युद्धं कुर्वाणाः शत्रुजनाः सीं सर्वतो यद्यदा
> हवंते युद्धार्थमस्मानाह्वयंति । तदास्माकं रक्षिता भवेत्यर्थः । कस्मिन्निमित्ते ।
> वि वो मदे तव विविधहनिर्जन्यहर्षनिमित्ते । विवक्षसे । त्वं महान्भवसि । महतां
> हि पालनं युक्तमेवेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O supreme slayer of Vṛtra, that is, of enemies, O Indu, O Soma, you who are the auspicious friend of Indra: protect us (this is to be supplied). When? तोकसातौ (*tokasātau*): तोक (*toka*) is a name for offspring; साति (*sāti*) is a form from the root षणु दान (*ṣaṇu dāna*); where offspring is given, there is a तोकसाति (*tokasāti*), an epithet of battle, that is, a very great one. When enemies fighting in the battle (समिथे (*samithe*)) call us from all sides (सीं (*sīṃ*)) to fight, then be our protector. On what occasion? In your delight produced by the various oblations. You are great; the protection of the great is indeed fitting.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहंतम (*vṛtrahaṃtama*)—O destroyer of enemies
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—to Indra
- शिवः (*śivaḥ*)—auspicious
- सखा (*sakhā*)—you are a friend
- तोकसातौ (*tokasātau*)—in the offspring-bestowing
- समिथे (*samithe*)—battle
- युध्यमानाः (*yudhyamānāḥ*)—enemies who fight
- सीं (*sīṃ*)—everywhere
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- हवंते (*havaṃte*)—they call for battle, then
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- वि मदे (*vi made*)—in the time of exceeding joy
- नः (*naḥ*)—protect us
- विवक्षसे (*vivakṣase*)—you are great

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, destroyer of enemies, you are an auspicious friend to Indra. When enemies gather everywhere in the offspring-bestowing battle and call us to fight, then in the time of your exceeding joy protect us. You are great.

### Printed p. 702

##### English translation
Utter destroyer of enemies, Soma, who are the auspicious friend of Indra, (protect us), when hostile warriors everywhere call us to the combat that bestows offspring ; by your exhilaration preserve us) ; for you are mighty.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं घ॒ स तु॒रो मद॒ इंद्र॑स्य वर्धत प्रि॒यः ।  
> अ॒यं क॒क्षीव॑तो म॒हो वि वो॒ मदे॑ म॒तिं विप्र॑स्य वर्धय॒द्विव॑क्षसे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)
