> सिष॑क्त्य॒र्यः प्र यु॒गा जना॑नां स॒द्यः शि॒श्ना प्र॑मिना॒नो नवी॑यान् ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपश्यं । ग्रामं । वहमानं । आरात् । अचक्रया । स्वधया । वर्तमानं ।  
> सिसक्ति । अर्यः । प्र । युगा । जनानां । सद्यः । शिश्ना । प्रमिनानः । नवीयान् । १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपश्यं । वसुक्रोऽहं प्रजापतिरूपमिंद्रं सम्यग्ज्ञानेन दृष्टवानस्मि ।
> कीदृशं । ग्रामं ग्रामभूतं संघं वहमानं वाहयंतं । सृजंतमित्यर्थः ।
> कुतः । आराद्दूरात् । उपादानकारणात्पकृतित इत्यर्थः । अचक्रया चक्रवर्जितया
> रथहीनया स्वधया स्वयमात्मानं धारयंत्या सेनया वर्तमानवागच्छंतं ।
> एवंभूतमपश्यमित्यर्थः । किंचार्यः सर्वस्य स्वामींद्रो जनानां यजमानानां
> कार्यत्वेन संबंधिनो युगा युगानि यज्ञकालविशेषान् सिषक्ति । प्रकर्षण
> सेवते । कीदृशः । सद्यस्तदानीमेव शिश्ना शिश्नानि । शिश्नं श्नथतेरिति निर्वचनात् ।
> नि. ४-१९ । श्नथित्कृणि ताडयित्कृणि राक्षसादिवृंदानि प्रमिनानः प्रकर्षण हिंसन्नवीयाञ्यारीरेण च बलपौरुषनयनादिभिश्च नवतरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vasukra says: "I have seen Indra, who has the form of Prajāpati, with right knowledge." Of what kind is he? He is ग्रामं (*grāmaṃ*), the host (saṃgha) that is like a village, and he is वहमानं (*vahamānaṃ*), causing it to move, that is, creating it. From where? आरात् (*ārāt*) means from afar, that is, from the material cause, from Prakṛti. He is moving अचक्रया (*acakrayā*), with a wheelless, chariotless army that sustains itself by itself (स्वधया (*svadhayā*)). "I saw such a one" is the meaning. Further, अर्यः (*aryaḥ*), Indra, the lord of all, attaches to the people (जनानां (*janānāṃ*)), the sacrificers, the युगा (*yugā*), the yugas, that is, particular times for sacrifice, which relate to them as what is to be performed; he सिषक्ति (*siṣakti*), he serves them forth. सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*) means at that very moment. शिश्ना (*śiśnā*) means śiśnas; "शिश्ना (*śiśnā*)" is from the root śnath, according to the Nirukta (Ni. 4-19), so the hosts of Rākṣasas and the like that pierce and strike; प्रमिनानः (*praminānaḥ*) is destroying them greatly. नवीयान् (*navīyān*) means newer, by body and also by strength, valour, leading and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ग्रामं (*grāmaṃ*)—the whole host of beings
- वहमानं (*vahamānaṃ*)—the one who produces
- अचक्रया (*acakrayā*)—that which is without wheels
- स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—with an army that can carry all of them
- वर्तमानं (*vartamānaṃ*)—Indra, who is
- आरात् (*ārāt*)—from afar
- अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*)—I saw
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at once
- शिश्ना (*śiśnā*)—Rākṣasas and the like
- प्रमिनानः (*praminānaḥ*)—the one who greatly destroys
- नवीयान् (*navīyān*)—of new form
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—Indra, the lord
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—for the sacrificers
- युगा (*yugā*)—the sacrificial times such as the solstices
- प्र सिषक्ति (*pra siṣakti*)—he ordains

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I saw from afar Indra, who produces the whole host of beings and who is with an army that is wheelless and able to carry all of them. At once Indra, who greatly destroys Rākṣasas and the like, who is of new form and the lord, ordains for the sacrificers the sacrificial times such as the solstices.

### Printed p. 741

##### English translation
I beheld the crowd coming from afar, moving of themselves without wheels : the lord of all, (Indra), regulates the seasons (for the worship of men), younger in vigour, destroying at once the herds of evil beings.
#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒तौ मे॒ गावौ॑ प्रम॒रस्य॑ यु॒क्तौ मो षु प्र से॑धी॒र्मुहु॒रिन्मं॑धि ।  
> आप॑श्चिदस्य॒ वि न॑शं॒त्यर्थं॒ सूर॑श्च म॒र्क उप॑रो बभू॒वान् ॥२०॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एतौ । मे । गावौ । प्रमरस्य । युक्तौ । मो इति । सु । प्र । सेधीः । मुहुः ।  
> इत् । ममंधि ।  
> आपः । चित् । अस्य । वि । नशंति । अर्थं । सूरः । च । मर्कः । उपरः । बभूवान् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कार्यकारणयोरुपचारादात्मा वै पुत्रनामासीति वचनाच्चेंद्ररूपेणावस्थितस्य प्रमरस्य प्रकर्षण शत्रूणां मारयितुर्मे मम स्वभूतावेतावेतादृशौ
> युक्तौ सुष्टु पूजितौ गावौ शत्रून्यज्ञानंश्च प्रति गंतारौ हरी मो प्र सेधीः ।
> स्तुत्युपसंहारकरणेनास्मद्यज्ञानापगमय । किं तर्हि मुडुरिन्मुहुर्मुहुर्ममंधि । पुनःपुनः स्तुहि ममात्मन्नित्यर्थः । आपश्चिद्वृष्टिलक्षणान्युदकान्यप्यसेंद्रस्यार्थं गतिं वि नशंति । विनशतिर्वाप्तिकर्मा । व्याप्नुवंति । तथा सूरश्च सूर्यश्च
> व्याप्नोति । कीदृशः । मर्कॊ मर्जयिता सर्वस्य शोधयितोपरो मेघसदृतो
> बभूवान् भवन् । मेघवच्छिघ्रगतिः सन्नित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By the figurative transfer between cause and effect, and by the statement *ātmā vai putranāmāsīti*, the speaker is Pramara, who stands in the form of Indra and is the great slayer of enemies. "These two, my own, yoked and well worshipped, my गावौ (*gāvau*) (the two bay horses, which go towards enemies and towards the sacrifice): do not turn them back (मो प्र सेधीः (*mo pra sedhīḥ*)) by ending the praise or by driving them away from our sacrifice. What then? Praise again and again, my self." Even the waters, in the form of rain, reach the goal (अर्थं (*arthaṃ*), movement) of this Indra; विनशति (*vinaśati*) is a root of reaching, so वि नशंति (*vi naśaṃti*) means they pervade. So too the sun pervades. Of what kind is he? मर्कः (*markaḥ*) is the purifier of all; उपरः (*uparaḥ*) means like a cloud, "being" (बभूवान् (*babhūvān*)), that is, swift in motion like a cloud.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रमरस्य (*pramarasya*)—of the one who greatly destroys enemies
- मे (*me*)—belonging to me
- युक्ता (*yuktā*)—yoked to the chariot
- सु (*su*)—greatly worshipped
- गावौ (*gāvau*)—going towards the sacrifice
### Printed p. 742
- एतौ (*etau*)—these horses (of mine)
- मो प्र सेधीः (*mo pra sedhīḥ*)—do not make them turn back from the sacrifice
- मुहुरित् (*muhurit*)—many times
- ममंधि (*mamaṃdhi*)—praise
- आपश्चित् (*āpaścit*)—the waters
- अस्य (*asya*)—of Indra
- अर्थं (*arthaṃ*)—the purpose
- वि नशंति (*vi naśaṃti*)—they cause to be fulfilled
- मर्कः (*markaḥ*)—the purifier
- उपरः (*uparaḥ*)—like a cloud
- बभूवान् (*babhūvān*)—swift-going
- सूरः च (*sūraḥ ca*)—the sun also causes Indra's purpose to be fulfilled

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Do not make these horses of mine, who am the destroyer of enemies (Indra), yoked to the chariot, greatly worshipped and going towards the sacrifice, turn back from the sacrifice. And praise those horses again and again. The waters cause Indra's purpose to be fulfilled. The sun also, the purifier, swift-going like a cloud, causes Indra's purpose to be fulfilled.

##### English translation
Turn not back, but repeatedly praise these two yoked (steeds) of me the destroyer, which advance (to the foe and to the sacrifice); the waters fulfil Indra's purpose, and (so does) the all-cleansing sun, being (swift as) a cloud.
#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं यो वज्रः॑ पुरु॒धा विवृ॑त्तो॒ऽवः सूर्य॑स्य बृह॒तः  ॑
> पुरी॑षात् ।  
> श्रव॒ इदे॒ना प॒रो अ॒न्यद॑स्ति॒ तद॑व्य॒थी ज॑रि॒माण॑स्तरंति ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । यः । वज्रः । पुरुदा । विवृत्तः । अवः । सूर्यस्य । बृहतः । पुरीषात् ।  
> श्रवः । इत् । एना । परः । अन्यत् । अस्ति । तत् । अव्यथी । जरिमाणः । तरंति ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽयं वज्र इंद्रस्य स्वभूतः सूर्यस्यादित्यस्य बृहतो महतः पुरीषात्पूरकान्मंडलादवोऽवस्तादधोभागे स्थितेषु विवृत्तो वृष्ट्यर्थं प्रवृत्तः पतितः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This thunderbolt (वज्र (*vajra*)), Indra's own, has been turned about (विवृत्तः (*vivṛttaḥ*)) for the sake of rain: it has been sent forth and has fallen below (अवः (*avaḥ*)) the vast (बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)) filling orb (पुरीषात् (*purīṣāt*)) of the sun, Āditya, on those (clouds) that stand in the lower part.
### Printed p. 743

> इच्छब्दोऽप्यर्थे । तच्छब्दश्रुतेर्यच्चज्योऽध्याहार्यः । परः परस्तादंतरिक्षलोकस्कोपरि स्थिते सूर्यमंडले स्थितमेनैतत् । श्रव इत्यन्ननाम । तद्धेतुत्पादकं
> श्रव इत्युच्यते । यदप्युदकं मेघोदरगतादुवकादन्यदप्यस्ति अव्यथी वृथारहिता
> जरिमाणः स्तोतारो मरुदादयस्तत्तादृशमुदकं तरंति । अंतरिक्षलोकं
> प्रत्यवतारयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The word इत् (*it*) is in the sense of *api* ("also"). Because the word तत् (*tat*) is heard, यत् (*yat*) is to be supplied. परः (*paraḥ*) means beyond, above the world of the firmament, in the orb of the sun, there stands this (एना (*enā*)). श्रवः (*śravaḥ*) is a name for food; what produces that is called श्रवः (*śravaḥ*). This is the water that is also other than the water inside the cloud's belly. The जरिमाणः (*jarimāṇaḥ*), the praisers, the Maruts and others, who are अव्यथी (*avyathī*), free from distress, तरंति (*taraṃti*) bring such water down towards the world of the firmament.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—great
- पुरीषात् (*purīṣāt*)—than the filling orb
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—on the clouds in the lower part
- पुरुधा (*purudhā*)—many times
- विवृत्तः (*vivṛttaḥ*)—is employed
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this
- वज्रः (*vajraḥ*)—Indra's thunderbolt
- परः (*paraḥ*)—that which is in the orb of the sun
- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—that which is different from the water in the clouds
- एना श्रवः (*enā śravaḥ*)—this water which
- अस्ति (*asti*)—exists
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- अव्यथी (*avyathī*)—free from toil
- जरिमाणः (*jarimāṇaḥ*)—the Maruts and others
- तरंति (*taraṃti*)—they cause to fall towards the firmament

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This is the thunderbolt, the weapon of Indra, which is employed many times on the clouds in the part below the great orb of the sun. The Maruts and others, free from toil, cause to fall towards the firmament the water that is in the orb of the sun and is different from the water in the clouds.

##### English translation
This is the thunderbolt which repeatedly falls (on those who are) below the orb of the vast sun; the worshippers easily cause this water (in the sun's orb) above which is different from that (in the clouds) to pass through (the firmament).
#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृ॒क्षेवृ॑क्षे॒ निय॑ता मीमय॒द्गौस्ततो॒ वयः॒ प्र प॑तान्पूरु॒षादः॑ ।  
> अथे॒दं विश्वं॒ भुव॑नं भयात॒ इंद्रा॑य सु॒न्वदृष॑ये च॒  ॑
> शिक्षत् ॥ २२ ॥

### Printed p. 744

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृक्षेऽवृक्षे । नियता । मीमयत् । गौः । ततः । वयः । प्र । पतान् । पुरुषआदः ।  
> अथ । इदं । विश्वं । भुवनं । भयाते । इंद्राय । सुन्वत् । ऋषये । च । शिक्षत् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृक्षे वृक्षे सर्वस्मिन्वृक्षमये धनुषि नियता संबद्धा गौर्गोसंबंधिनी
> स्नायुमती मौर्वि मीमयत् । मीमयतिः शब्दकर्मा। अकृष्यमाणा सती शब्दं
> करोति । ततस्तस्माद्दनुषः पुरुषादः शत्रुजनानामत्तारः । मारयितार इत्यर्थः ।
> वयः पक्षिसदृशा गंतारो वाणाः प्र पतान् । शत्रूनृति प्रपतंति । अथ तदानीमिंद्रायेंद्रार्थं सुन्वत्सोमयागं कुर्वदृषये च शिक्षत्कर्मणां द्रष्ट
> ऋत्विजे च संपूर्णां दक्षिणां दददपीदमीदृशं विश्वं समस्तं भुवनं भूतजातं
> भयाते । इंद्राद्भिभेति । अन्यत्किमुतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वृक्षे वृक्षे (*vṛkṣe vṛkṣe*) means on every bow made of wood; the string (गौः (*gauḥ*)), connected with the cow, made of sinew and fixed (नियता (*niyatā*)) to it, मीमयत् (*mīmayat*); the root मीमयति (*mīmayati*) means sound, so when it is not drawn it makes a sound. Then from that bow the पुरुषादः (*puruṣādaḥ*), the devourers of enemy men, that is, the killers, the वयः (*vayaḥ*), the arrows, going like birds, प्र पतान् (*pra patān*), fall upon the enemies. Then at that moment the whole world, every being, even one that performs a Soma sacrifice (सुन्वत् (*sunvat*)) for Indra and gives the full dakṣiṇā to the ṛtvij (ऋषये (*ṛṣaye*), the seer of rites, शिक्षत् (*śikṣat*)), fears (भयाते (*bhayāte*)) Indra. What then of others? That is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृक्षेवृक्षे (*vṛkṣevṛkṣe*)—in all bows made of wood
- नियता (*niyatā*)—that which is fixed
- गौः (*gauḥ*)—that which is made of the sinew of a cow
- मौर्वी (*maurvī*)—the bowstring
- मीमयत् (*mīmayat*)—makes a sound
- ततः (*tataḥ*)—afterwards
- पुरुषादः (*puruṣādaḥ*)—those that devour enemies
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—the arrows, which are like birds
- प्र पतान् (*pra patān*)—fall on the enemies
- अथ (*atha*)—immediately after that
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—with Indra in view
- सुन्वत् (*sunvat*)—that which performs the Soma sacrifice
- ऋषये च (*ṛṣaye ca*)—to the ṛtvijs and others
- शिक्षत् (*śikṣat*)—that which gives the dakṣiṇā
- इदं विश्वं भुवनं (*idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ*)—this whole world
- भयाते (*bhayāte*)—is afraid of Indra

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The bowstring, fixed in all bows made of wood and made of the sinew of a cow, makes a sound. Afterwards the arrows, which devour enemies and are like birds, leave the strings and fall upon the enemies. Immediately after that, this whole world, which performs the Soma sacrifice with Indra in view and gives the dakṣiṇā to the ṛtvijs and others, sees Indra's power and is afraid.

### Printed p. 745

##### English translation
The bowstring fixed to each bow clangs loudly; then the man-destroying (shafts like) birds fall upon (the foes): and the whole of this world is alarmed, presenting libations to Indra, and donations to the Rishi.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the various meanings of the word गौः (*gauḥ*), Yāska has taken the present Ṛk as an example and has given for it the meaning of the sinew used for a bowstring. It is necessary to set out here the various meanings that Yāska gives for the word गौः (*gauḥ*).

1. (1) गौरिति वृथिव्या नामधेयं । यत् दूरंगता भवति । यच्चास्यां भूतानि गच्छंति । गौतेर्वकारो नामकरणः ॥ (*gauriti vṛthivyā nāmadheyaṃ | yat dūraṃgatā bhavati | yaccāsyāṃ bhūtāni gacchaṃti | gautervakāro nāmakaraṇaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 2-5)
The word गौः (*gauḥ*) denotes the earth, because it extends to a very great distance, or because living beings move about on it. Therefore गौः (*gauḥ*) means the earth; formed from the root गाज्-गतौ (*gāj-gatau*), having the sense "go", with the letter ओ (*o*) added as an affix, it has become the word गौः (*gauḥ*).

(2) अथापि पशुनामेह भवत्येतस्मादेव । (*athāpi paśunāmeha bhavatyetasmādeva |*)
Besides, the word गौः (*gauḥ*), formed from that same root गाज् गतौ (*gāj gatau*) mentioned above, is also a name for a beast (paśu).

(3) अथाप्यस्यां ताद्वितेन कृत्सवन्निगमा भवंति । गोभिः श्रीणीत मत्सरं इति पयसः । मत्सरः सोमो मंदतेस्तृप्तिकर्मणः । मत्सर इति लोभनामाभिमत्त एनेन धनं भवति । पयः पिबतेर्वा । क्षीरं क्षरतेः । घसेर्वेरो नामकरण उशीरमिति यथा ॥ (*athāpyasyāṃ tādvitena kṛtsavannigamā bhavaṃti | gobhiḥ śrīṇīta matsaraṃ iti payasaḥ | matsaraḥ somo maṃdatestṛptikarmaṇaḥ | matsara iti lobhanāmābhimatta enena dhanaṃ bhavati | payaḥ pibatervā | kṣīraṃ kṣarateḥ | ghaservero nāmakaraṇa uśīramiti yathā ‖*)
In the above sense of paśu, substances such as milk produced from the beast are denoted by the word गो (*go*). For instance, in the Vedic sentence गोभिः श्रीणीत मत्सरं (*gobhiḥ śrīṇīta matsaraṃ*) the meaning is "mix the Soma juice with milk, which is a product of the cow". गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*) means products of the cow, that is, substances produced from the cow such as milk and curds. मत्सरं (*matsaraṃ*) means Soma. From the root मंद् (*maṃd*), meaning "give satisfaction by drinking", the word मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*) is formed and denotes the Soma juice. For the word मत्सर (*matsara*), greed, desire

### Printed p. 746
(The sentence from the previous page continues.) The word matsara also means greed and desire. When it is taken in that sense, this word may also mean wealth. The word payaḥ, "milk," may be derived either from the root पा (*pā*) (pibati), meaning "to drink," or from the root प्र्यायति (*pryāyati*), meaning "to increase, to thrive." The word kṣīra also means milk. This word kṣīra is explained thus: for the root आद भक्षणे (*āda bhakṣaṇe*) the substitute घस (*ghasa*) is made, which yields the root kṣar, "to flow, to stream," and from that root kṣar the word kṣīra is formed. Because it is of a flowing nature, it means milk. The affix ईर (*īra*) is added to the root kṣar and the word kṣīra results. As the affix ईर (*īra*) is added to the root वश कांतौ (*vaśa kāṃtau*) and the word uśīra results, the example of the word uśīra is given.

1. (4) अंशुं दुहंतो अध्यासते गवि इत्यधिषवणचर्मणः । अंशुः शमष्टमात्रो भवति । अननाय शंभवतीति ना । चर्म चरतेवोच्चृतं भवतीति वा ॥ (*aṃśuṃ duhaṃto adhyāsate gavi ityadhiṣavaṇacarmaṇaḥ | aṃśuḥ śamaṣṭamātro bhavati | ananāya śaṃbhavatīti nā | carma caratevoccṛtaṃ bhavatīti vā ‖*) (Ni. 6-5)

The sentence "aṃśuṃ duhanto adhyāsate gavi" means: while pressing out the soma juice they sit upon the cowhide. The word gavi in this sentence means "on a cowhide." Aṃśu is soma, because as soon as the soma juice enters, that is, pervades, the body, it produces happiness or delight. Or, because it is the cause of the happy life of living beings, soma is called aṃśu. The word carma is derived from the root carati; it is like a covering for the bodies of living beings, or, because it is cut off, that is, taken off separated from the body, it is called carma.

(5) अथापि चर्म च श्लेष्मा च । गोभिः सन्नद्धो असि वीळयस्व इति रथस्तुत् ॥ (*athāpi carma ca śleṣmā ca | gobhiḥ sannaddho asi vīḷayasva iti rathastut ‖*)

The word gauḥ also means hide (covering) and phlegm (glue). The sentence praising a chariot, "गोभिः सन्नद्धो असि वीळयस्व (*gobhiḥ sannaddho asi vīḷayasva*)" means: O chariot, you are covered with cowhide and stuck together. The word gobhiḥ in this sentence means "by cowhides." When a chariot is built, cowhide is stretched over it as a covering and fastened with a kind of glue (śleṣma). This is what is described in this sentence in praise of the chariot.

(6) अथापि स्नाव च श्लेष्मा च । गोभिः सन्नद्धा पतति प्रसूत इतीषुस्तुत् ॥ (*athāpi snāva ca śleṣmā ca | gobhiḥ sannaddhā patati prasūta itīṣustut ‖*) (Ni. 6-5)

### Printed p. 747
The word go also means sinew and glue. The sentence "गोभिः सन्नद्धा पतति प्रसूत (*gobhiḥ sannaddhā patati prasūta*)" praises the arrow. When arrows are made, the feathers of birds are bound to them with sinews (thread-like nerves), stuck with glue, and so prepared. This is what the sentence describes.

(7) ज्यापि गौरुच्यते गव्याचेत्ताद्धितमथ चेन्न गव्यागमयतीपूनिति । (*jyāpi gaurucyate gavyācettāddhitamatha cenna gavyāgamayatīpūniti |*)

The bowstring (the cord that joins and ties the two ends of the bow) is also called gauḥ, because this string is made from cow sinew. The word gavyā is only a variant form of the word go. Because arrows go forth from it (the string), the string is called gauḥ. To explain this meaning, the Ṛk under discussion is taken as the example:

(8) वृक्षेवृक्षे नियतामिामयद्गौस्ततो वयः प्रपतान्पुरुषादः । वृक्षेवृक्षे धनुषि धनुषि । वृक्षो व्रश्चनात् । वृत्वा क्षां तिष्ठतीति वा । क्षा क्षियतेर्निवासकर्मणः । नियतामिामयद्गौ शब्दं करोति । मीमयतिः शब्दकर्मा । ततो वयः प्रपतंति पुरुषानदनाय । विरिति शकुनिनाम । वेतेर्गतिकर्मणः । अथापीषुनामेह भवत्येतस्मादेव ॥ ( (*vṛkṣevṛkṣe niyatāmiāmayadgaustato vayaḥ prapatānpuruṣādaḥ | vṛkṣevṛkṣe dhanuṣi dhanuṣi | vṛkṣo vraścanāt | vṛtvā kṣāṃ tiṣṭhatīti vā | kṣā kṣiyaternivāsakarmaṇaḥ | niyatāmiāmayadgau śabdaṃ karoti | mīmayatiḥ śabdakarmā | tato vayaḥ prapataṃti puruṣānadanāya | viriti śakunināma | vetergatikarmaṇaḥ | athāpīṣunāmeha bhavatyetasmādeva ‖ (*) (Ni. 2-6)

Because bows are made from vṛkṣas (trees), the word vṛkṣa is used in *vṛkṣe-vṛkṣe* to indicate the meaning "bow." When Indra fights his enemies he assumes many forms and holds many bows with many arms. Therefore it is said here: on each bow held in each of his many arms. The string on each bow makes a twanging sound. The arrows shot from that string devour (strike the bodies of) the lives of the enemy men and destroy them. Because the arrows are fitted with birds' feathers, the word vayaḥ, meaning "bird," is used here to indicate the arrow. Many arrows, fitted with birds' feathers and shot from the string of each bow, strike the enemies and destroy them. The word vṛkṣa is derived from the root व्रश्च (*vraśca*), meaning "to cut," because it is cut for firewood and for making other wooden things; hence it is called vṛkṣa. Or else, vṛ means "to pervade, to split"; kṣā means earth; this tree splits the earth and pervades it everywhere with its roots, so it is called vṛkṣa. The word kṣā, "earth," is derived from the root क्षि-निवासगत्योः (*kṣi-nivāsagatyoḥ*), meaning "to dwell"; because people dwell upon it (the earth), the earth is called kṣā. The sentence "niyatām īmayad gau"

### Printed p. 748
means: it makes a loud twanging sound. When the arrow is set on the string and drawn and released, it makes a twanging sound. The root मीम् (*mīm*) means "to make a sound." Thereafter, that is, after the string has sounded, birds, that is, arrows fitted with birds' feathers, go forth from it to devour (destroy) the enemies. The word vi, "bird," is derived from the root vi meaning "to go, to move about." In this very sense the word also means "arrow."

1. (9) आदित्योऽपि गौरुच्यते । उतादः परुषे गवि । पर्ववति भास्वतीत्यौपमन्यवः । ग (*ādityo 'pi gaurucyate | utādaḥ paruṣe gavi | parvavati bhāsvatītyaupamanyavaḥ | ga*)

The word gauḥ also means Āditya. In the Vedic sentence "उतादः परुषे गवि (*utādaḥ paruṣe gavi*)" the word gavi means "in Āditya." The opinion of the teacher Aupamanyava is that he shines in the midst of clustered rays, that is, in the halo.

(10) अथाप्यस्यको रश्मिश्चंद्रमसं प्रति दीप्यते तदेतेनोपेक्षितव्यं । आदित्यतोऽस्य दीप्तिर्भवतीति । सुषुम्ना: सूर्यरश्मिश्चंद्रमा गंधर्वः इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*athāpyasyako raśmiścaṃdramasaṃ prati dīpyate tadetenopekṣitavyaṃ | ādityato 'sya dīptirbhavatīti | suṣumnā: sūryaraśmiścaṃdramā gaṃdharvaḥ ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 2-7)

One ray of the sun makes the moon shine. That the moon shines by the sun's ray is established by the Vedic sentence "suṣumnaḥ sūryaraśmiś candramā gandharvaḥ." Suṣumna is a particular ray of the sun; the moon receives it and shines by it; such is the sense of the Vedic sentence.

(11) सोऽपि गौरुच्यते । अत्राह गोरमन्वत इति । तदुपरिष्टात् व्याख्यास्यामः । (*so 'pi gaurucyate | atrāha goramanvata iti | tadupariṣṭāt vyākhyāsyāmaḥ |*)

That ray called Suṣumna is also called gauḥ. On this point there is the Vedic sentence "अत्राह गोरमन्वत (*atrāha goramanvata*)" We shall explain this later.

(12) सर्वॆऽपि रश्मयो गाव उच्यंते । ता वां वास्तून्युश्यसि गमध्यै यत्र गावो भूरिशृंगा आयासः । अत्राह तदुरुगायस्य वृष्णः परमं पदमवभाति भूरि॥तानि वां वास्तूनि कामयामहे गमनाय यत्र गावो बहुशृंगाः । भूरीति बहुनो नामधेयं प्रभवतीति सतः । शृंगं श्रयतेर्वा शृणातेर्वा शरणायोद्धतमिति वा शिरसो निर्गतमिति वा । अयासोऽयनाः । तत्र तदुरुगायस्य विष्णोर्महागतेः परमं पदं परार्ध्यस्थमवभाति भूरि । पादः पद्यतेः । स्तन्निधानात्पदं । पशुपादप्रकृतिः प्रभागपादः । प्रभागपादसामान्यादितराणि पदानि ॥ ( (*sarvè 'pi raśmayo gāva ucyaṃte | tā vāṃ vāstūnyuśyasi gamadhyai yatra gāvo bhūriśṛṃgā āyāsaḥ | atrāha tadurugāyasya vṛṣṇaḥ paramaṃ padamavabhāti bhūri‖tāni vāṃ vāstūni kāmayāmahe gamanāya yatra gāvo bahuśṛṃgāḥ | bhūrīti bahuno nāmadheyaṃ prabhavatīti sataḥ | śṛṃgaṃ śrayatervā śṛṇātervā śaraṇāyoddhatamiti vā śiraso nirgatamiti vā | ayāso 'yanāḥ | tatra tadurugāyasya viṣṇormahāgateḥ paramaṃ padaṃ parārdhyasthamavabhāti bhūri | pādaḥ padyateḥ | stannidhānātpadaṃ | paśupādaprakṛtiḥ prabhāgapādaḥ | prabhāgapādasāmānyāditarāṇi padāni ‖ (*) (Ni. 9-7)

### Printed p. 749
Moreover, all other kinds of rays are also designated by the word gāvaḥ. As an example in this matter we shall also explain the following Ṛk: "We desire to reach that celestial abode, Viṣṇu's highest step, where many swiftly moving rays shine." Bhūri means "much." Because it produces much, the word bhūri means "many, abundant." The word śṛṅga may be derived from the root श्री (*śrī*), meaning "to resort to" (because it rests upon the head where it stands), or from the root शृ (*śṛ*), meaning "to kill," or from the root शम् (*śam*), meaning "to destroy." The meaning "horn" is established for the word śṛṅga either because with this horn the animal protects itself, or because it projects from the head. Ayāsaḥ means those whose nature is to move constantly, not resting for a moment in one place. This place called Viṣṇu's highest step is famed as a most splendid, supreme place of great motion. The word pāda is derived from the root पद् (*pad*), meaning "to go." From the same the word pada, "step, the placing of the foot," is also derived. Pāda means foot; pada means step, the placing of the foot. Since animals have four feet, we use the word pāda when we indicate one part of four. Hence it is customary, in ordinary usage, to use the word pāda also when indicating a fourth part or any part at all.

एवमन्येषापि सत्त्वानां संदेहा विद्यंते तानि चेत् समानकर्माणि समाननिर्वचनानि नानाकर्माणि चेन्नाना निर्वचनानि यथार्थं निर्वक्तव्यानीति ॥ (*evamanyeṣāpi sattvānāṃ saṃdehā vidyaṃte tāni cet samānakarmāṇi samānanirvacanāni nānākarmāṇi cennānā nirvacanāni yathārthaṃ nirvaktavyānīti ‖*) (Ni. 2-7)

In the same way, doubts may arise about the meaning of many other words. In such a case the general rule is: if words have one and the same meaning, their formation and explanation must be given in one and the same way; but if the words have various meanings, then the formation, explanation and exposition must be given according to the respective meanings.

> आदित्यो रश्मिभिराददान इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the making (creation) of all the gods, the clouds stood first: that is, at the time of creation. In the act of giving out the moisture that is the cause of the world's maintenance, they stood first as what was to be created. They stood earlier than Indra's command. Who are these? The clouds. How is this known? Because they are mentioned afterwards in a later place. For it is said (Ni. 2-22): "The clouds themselves are the gods of the middle region." Of these clouds, upon their cutting (kṛntatra), come the upara; upara is a name of cloud; here it denotes the waters standing in them. The waters in the clouds rose up, that is, were made to fall to earth as rain. When the waters have been made to fall, by Indra's command the three gods Parjanya, Vāyu and Āditya warm the earth, that is, the plants on it, with rain, cold and heat; that is, they ripen them. Of what kind are they? Anūpāḥ: sowers or producers in due order of the rains and the rest, that is, throwers (of seed). The two, Vāyu and Āditya, carry the water (bṛbūka) that stands in the ripened plants and gives delight to all, towards the sphere of the sun: Vāyu drying it up, Āditya drawing it in with his rays.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of all the gods
- माने (*māne*)—at the time of creation
- प्रथमा (*prathamā*)—first
- अतिष्ठन् (*atiṣṭhan*)—the clouds were created
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these clouds
- कृंतत्रात् (*kṛṃtatrāt*)—from the cutting
- उपराः (*uparāḥ*)—the rain-waters
- उदायॆन् (*udāyèn*)—came forth
- त्रयः (*trayaḥ*)—these three gods, Parjanya, Vāyu and Āditya

- अनूपाः (*anūpāḥ*)—sowing the seed in due order
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- तपंति (*tapaṃti*)—purify
- द्वा (*dvā*)—of them, Vāyu and Parjanya
- पुरीषं (*purīṣaṃ*)—satisfying
- बृबूकं (*bṛbūkaṃ*)—water
- वहतः (*vahataḥ*)—carry to the sphere of the sun

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the creation of the gods, the clouds stood first. From the splitting of these clouds the rain-waters came forth. The three gods Parjanya, Vāyu and Āditya, sowing the seed in due order, purify the earth. Of them, Vāyu and Parjanya carry the satisfying water to the sphere of the sun.

##### English translation
At the creation of the gods, the (clouds) stood first; from their division, the waters (of the rain) came forth : the three divinities (Parjanya Vayu and Aditya), sowing in succession, warm the earth: two of them (Vayu and Aditya) convey all-delighting water (to the sun's sphere).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given the explanation (nirvacana) of this Ṛk: देवानां निर्माणे प्रथमा अतिष्ठन्माध्यमिका देवगणाः । प्रथम इति मुख्यनाम प्रतमो भवति । कृंतत्रमंतरिक्षं विकर्तनं मेघानां विकर्तनेन मेघानामुदकं जायते- त्रयस्तपंति पृथिवीमनूपाः । पर्जन्यो वायुरादित्यः शीतोष्णवर्षैरोषधीः पाचयंति अनूपा अनुवपंति लोकान् स्वेन स्वेन कर्मणा ! अयमीतरोऽनूप एकस्मादेवानूप्यत उदकेन । अपि वान्वाबिति स्याद्यथा प्रागिति । तस्यानूप इति स्याद्यथा प्राचीनमिति । द्वा बृबूकं वहतः पुरीषं वाय्वादित्या उदकं । बृबूकमित्युदकनाम ब्रवीतेर्वा शब्दकर्मणो भ्रंशतेर्वा । पुरीषं पृणातेः पूरयतेर्वा ॥ (*devānāṃ nirmāṇe prathamā atiṣṭhanmādhyamikā devagaṇāḥ | prathama iti mukhyanāma pratamo bhavati | kṛṃtatramaṃtarikṣaṃ vikartanaṃ meghānāṃ vikartanena meghānāmudakaṃ jāyate- trayastapaṃti pṛthivīmanūpāḥ | parjanyo vāyurādityaḥ śītoṣṇavarṣairoṣadhīḥ pācayaṃti anūpā anuvapaṃti lokān svena svena karmaṇā ! ayamītaro 'nūpa ekasmādevānūpyata udakena | api vānvābiti syādyathā prāgiti | tasyānūpa iti syādyathā prācīnamiti | dvā bṛbūkaṃ vahataḥ purīṣaṃ vāyvādityā udakaṃ | bṛbūkamityudakanāma bravītervā śabdakarmaṇo bhraṃśatervā | purīṣaṃ pṛṇāteḥ pūrayatervā ‖*) (Ni. 2-22)

When the gods were created by Prajāpati, the gods of the middle region (the atmosphere), the clouds, obtained the chief place; that is, among all the gods they obtained pre-eminence. Here the word prathama means "chief." By the splitting of the clouds in the atmosphere the clouds pour rain in the form of water. The three gods Parjanya, Vāyu and Āditya together make the plants and herbs and the rest grow

### Printed p. 752
Then the sentence continues from the previous page: they cause the plants and the like to grow and flourish. That is, Parjanya pours down the rain, Vāyu blows as his helper, and Āditya, by his rays, aids the growth of plants and the like. With the cooperation of these, the herbs and trees grow and thrive. This work of theirs is called अनूप (*anūpa*). अनूप (*anūpa*) has another meaning also, "the bank of a river"; to this meaning the same derivation applies, because here too the predominance of water is seen. As the word प्राचीन (*prācīna*) is formed from the word प्राक् (*prāk*), so the word अनूप (*anūpa*) is formed from the word अन्वाप् (*anvāp*). Both of these, rain and the river bank, are filled with fertile drops of water. Wind and sun, bearing water-drops in the form of vapour, are the cause of the growth of plants and the like. बृबूकं (*bṛbūkaṃ*) means water (water in the form of dew or moisture). This word may be formed either from the root ब्रु (*bru*), meaning "to make a sound", or from the root भ्रःश् (*bhraḥś*), meaning "to fall down" (in the form of rain). पुरीषं (*purīṣaṃ*) means "that which is fertile". This word may be formed either from the root पृ (*pṛ*), meaning "to fill", or from the root प्प (*ppa*), meaning "to cause to fill". Such is the purport of the etymology.

#### Ṛk 24

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सा ते॑ जी॒वातु॑रु॒त तस्य॑ विद्धि॒ मा स्मै॑ता॒दृगप॑ गूहः  ॒
> समर्ये ।  
> आ॒विः स्वः॑ कृणु॒ते गूह॑ते बु॒सं स पा॒दुर॑स्य नि॒र्णिजो॒ न  ॑
> मुच्यते ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सा । ते । जीवातुः । उत । तस्य । विद्धि । मा । स्व । एतादृक् । अप । गूहः ।  
> सऽमर्ये ।  
> आविः । स्व १ रिति । स्वः । कृणुते । गूहते । बुसं । सः । पादुः । अस्य । निःनिजः । न ।  
> मुच्यते ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्रांतरात्मनेंद्रः स्तूयते । हे अंतरात्मन् ते तव सा तादृश्यादित्यात्मिका
> देवता जीवातुर्जीविका जीवनहेतुः । उतापि च तस्यादित्यस्यैतादृगीदृशं स्वरूपं
> समर्ये । संग्रामवाची समर्यशब्दोऽत्र यज्ञवाची । यज्ञे विद्दि । जानीहि ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here the inner self is praised as Indra. "O inner self, that solar divine form of yours is the cause of life. And know such a form of that Āditya at the sacrifice." The word समर्य (*samarya*) ordinarily denotes battle, but here it denotes the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 753

> स्तुत्यत्वेनेति शेषः । मा स्माप गूहः । मा खल्वपवृणोः । किंच निर्णिजः सर्वस्य
> शोधयितुरादित्यस्य स पादुस्तच्च पादनं गमनं रश्मिद्वारेण गत्वा स्वः सर्वं त्रैलोक्यमाविष्कुणुते । प्रकाशीकरोति । बुसमुदकं गूहते । संवृणोति । आदत्त
> इत्यर्थः । अस्मै प्रयोजनद्वयायादित्येन निर्वेदनाच्छ्रमेण वा गमनं न
> मुच्यते । न कदाचित्परित्यज्यत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Know it as worthy of praise—this is to be supplied. Do not conceal it." Further, the motion of the all-cleansing Āditya**NOTE**, going through his rays, makes the whole three worlds manifest and makes them shine; it takes up and covers the water (बुसं (*busaṃ*)). That is: this motion for the two purposes, by Āditya's decision or by effort, is never stopped, never abandoned.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—your (O inner self)
- सा (*sā*)—that form which is of Āditya's nature
- जीवातुः (*jīvātuḥ*)—is the cause of life
- उत (*uta*)—and
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that same Āditya
- एतादृक् (*etādṛk*)—such a form
- समर्य्यॆ (*samaryyè*)—at the time of sacrifice, as worthy of worship
- विद्धि (*viddhi*)—know
- मा स्म अप गूहः (*mā sma apa gūhaḥ*)—do not make anything forgotten
- निर्णिजः अस्य (*nirṇijaḥ asya*)—of this Āditya, the purifier
- स पादुः (*sa pāduḥ*)—that motion in the form of rays
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the three worlds
- आविः कृणुते (*āviḥ kṛṇute*)—makes manifest
- बुसं (*busaṃ*)—water
- गूहते (*gūhate*)—conceals
- न मुच्यते (*na mucyate*)—it never stops

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O inner self, that form of yours which is of Āditya's nature is the cause of life. And do not forget to know that such a form of the same Āditya is worthy of worship at the time of sacrifice. The motion, in the form of rays, of Āditya the purifier makes the three worlds manifest. It conceals the water; it never stops.

##### English translation
That your (divine) nature identified with the (sun) is the cause of life : and know such (solar form) of his (to be worthy of adoration) at the sacrtfice ; conceal nothing: that motion of him the all-cleansing (sun) makes manifest the universe; it absorbs the moisture; it is never discontinued.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पादुः (*pāduḥ*)—explaining the meaning of this word, Yāska says: पादुः। पादुः पद्यतेः । आविः स्वः कृणुते गूहते बुसं स पादुरस्य निर्णिजो न मुच्यते आविष्कुरुते भासमादित्यो गूहते बुसं । बुसमित्युदकनाम ब्रवीतेः शब्दकर्मणः । भ्रंशतीर्वा । यद्वर्षन्पातयत्युदकं रश्मिभिस्तत्पत्यादत्ते ॥ (*pāduḥ| pāduḥ padyateḥ | āviḥ svaḥ kṛṇute gūhate busaṃ sa pādurasya nirṇijo na mucyate āviṣkurute bhāsamādityo gūhate busaṃ | busamityudakanāma bravīteḥ śabdakarmaṇaḥ | bhraṃśatīrvā | yadvarṣanpātayatyudakaṃ raśmibhistatpatyādatte ‖*) (Ni. 5-19)

### Printed p. 754
The word पादुः (*pāduḥ*) is formed from the root पद् (*pad*), meaning "to walk, to go". It means the foot. In this matter the present Ṛk itself is the example. The word बुस (*busa*) here means water. The sun makes light manifest and hides water. The word बुस (*busa*) is formed either from the root ब्रु (*bru*), "to make a sound", or from the root भ्रंश् (*bhraṃś*), "to fall down". It means water. The purport is that water falls from the cloud in the form of rain, making a sound. The water thus falling on the earth through rain, the sun (Āditya) draws back by sucking it up through his rays. That is, the water of reservoirs heated by the rays of the sun is gathered, by way of vapour, in the sky facing the sun.

## Sūkta 28 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वो हीति द्वादशर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभं । इंद्रवसुक्रयोः पितापुत्रयोः संवादोऽत्र क्रियते । पुरा वसुक्रे यज्ञं कुर्वाणे सतींद्रः प्रच्छन्नरूप अजगाम । तं वसुक्रपत्नींद्रागमनाकांक्षिणी विप्रकृष्टमिवाद्ययास्तौत् । आतस्तस्याः सर्षिः इंद्रो देवता । अथ तस्याः प्रीत्यै वसुक्रेण सहेंद्रः संवादमकरोत् । द्वितीयादियुजश्चतुर्थीरहिताः पंचर्च इंद्रवाक्यानि । अतस्तासां स
> ऋषिः । यद्यप्यासु वसुक्रः संबोध्यत्वाद्देवता तथापि ता ऋच ऐंद्रे कर्मणि
> विनियोक्तव्या इंद्रलिंगसद्भावात् । चतुर्थीसहिताः शिष्टास्त्रीयाद्या वसुक्रवाक्यानि । अतः स ऋषिस्तासां इंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । विश्वो हि द्वादकेंद्रवसुक्रयोः संवाद ऐंद्रः सूक्तस्य प्रथमयेंद्रस्य स्नुषा परोक्षवदिंद्रमाहेंद्रस्य युजः शेषा ऋषेश्चतुर्थी चेति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning विश्वो हि (*viśvo hi*) has twelve Ṛks and is in the Triṣṭubh metre. A dialogue between Indra and Vasukra, father and son, is made here. Formerly, when Vasukra was performing a sacrifice, Indra came in disguise. Vasukra's wife, desiring Indra's arrival, praised him as though he were far away, with the first Ṛk. So she is the seer of that Ṛk and Indra its deity. Then, to please her, Indra held a dialogue with Vasukra. The even-numbered Ṛks other than the fourth, five in all, are Indra's words; therefore he is their seer. Although Vasukra is addressed in them, they are to be used in the Indra rite, since the Indra-marks are present, so Indra is their deity. The fourth Ṛk and the remaining odd Ṛks from the third onward are Vasukra's words; therefore he is their seer, Indra the deity. So the Anukramaṇī: विश्वो हि द्वादकेंद्रवसुक्रयोः संवाद ऐंद्रः सूक्तस्य प्रथमयेंद्रस्य स्नुषा परोक्षवदिंद्रमाहेंद्रस्य युजः शेषा ऋषेश्चतुर्थी चेति ॥ (*viśvo hi dvādakeṃdravasukrayoḥ saṃvāda aiṃdraḥ sūktasya prathamayeṃdrasya snuṣā parokṣavadiṃdramāheṃdrasya yujaḥ śeṣā ṛṣeścaturthī ceti ‖*) The use has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning विश्वो हि (*viśvo hi*) is the twelfth sūkta of the second anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks and is in the Triṣṭubh metre. In this sūkta is a conversation between Indra the father and the seer Vasukra the son. Formerly, while the seer Vasukra was performing a sacrifice, Indra came there with his disguise concealed. Then the wife of the seer Vasukra, desiring Indra's arrival and indicating his absence, praised him with the first Ṛk. Therefore for the first Ṛk Vasukra's wife is the seer and Indra the deity. Then, to please her, Indra held a conversation with Vasukra. Therefore, leaving aside the fourth Ṛk, the remaining five even-numbered Ṛks are Indra's words.

### Printed p. 755
Therefore Indra is the seer of those Ṛks. Even though the seer Vasukra is addressed in them, since the deeds praised in them relate to Indra, those Ṛks must be called Indra-deity Ṛks. The fourth Ṛk of this sūkta and the odd-numbered Ṛks from the third onward contain the words of the seer Vasukra. Therefore for those Ṛks Vasukra is the seer and Indra the deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: विश्वो हि द्वादशेंद्रवसुक्रयोः संवाद ऐंद्रः सूक्तस्य प्रथमयेंद्रस्य स्नुषा परोक्षवदिंद्रमाहेंद्रस्य युजः शेषा ऋषेश्चतुर्थी च (*viśvo hi dvādaśeṃdravasukrayoḥ saṃvāda aiṃdraḥ sūktasya prathamayeṃdrasya snuṣā parokṣavadiṃdramāheṃdrasya yujaḥ śeṣā ṛṣeścaturthī ca*). The use has been stated earlier.

Sūkta 28
Maṇḍala 10 | Anuvāka 2 | Sūkta 28.
Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 7 | Vargas 20, 21.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 12.
Ṛṣi: इंद्रवसुक्रयोः संवाद ऐंद्रः (*iṃdravasukrayoḥ saṃvāda aiṃdraḥ*). 1: इंद्रत्नाषा वसुक्रपत्नीऋषिका (*iṃdratnāṣā vasukrapatnīṛṣikā*). 2, 6, 8, 10, 12: इंद्र ऋषिः (*iṃdra ṛṣiḥ*). 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11: ऐंद्रो वसुक्रऋषिः (*aiṃdro vasukraṛṣiḥ*).
Devatā: 2, 6, 8, 10, 12: ऐंद्रो व'क्रो देवता (*aiṃdro va 'kro devatā*). 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11: इंद्रो देवता (*iṃdro devatā*).
Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वो॒ ह्य१॒ं॑न्यो अ॒रिरा॑ज॒गाम॒ ममेदह॒ श्वशु॑रो॒ ना ज॑गाम ।  
> ज॒क्षी॒याद्धा॒ना उ॒त सोमं॑ पपीया॒त्सा॑शितः॒ पुन॒रस्तं॑  
> जगायात् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वः । हि । अन्यः । अरिः । आजगाम । मम । इत् । अह । श्वशुरः । न । आ । जगाम ।  
> जक्षीयात् । धानाः । उत । सोमं । पपीयात् । सुआशितः । पुनः । आस्तं । जगायात् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया वसुक्रपत्निंद्रं स्तोति । अन्य इंद्रव्यतिरिक्तोऽरिरर्य ईश्वरो विश्वो
> हि सर्व एव देवगण आजगाम । अस्मद्यज्ञं प्रत्याययौ । इदित्यवधारणे । अहेत..

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk Vasukra's wife praises Indra. Every other lord, the whole company of gods other than Indra, has come; they have come to our sacrifice. इत् (*it*) is in the sense of emphasis.

### Printed p. 756

> द्भुते। सर्वदेवगण आगते सति ममैव श्वशुर इंद्रो ना जगाम! स इंद्रो यद्यागच्छेत् तर्हि धाना भृष्टयवाञ्ङक्षीयात् । भक्षयेत् । उतापि च सोममभिषुतं
> पपीयात् । पिबेत् । ततः स्वाशितः सुष्टु भुक्तस्तृप्तः सन् पुनर्भूयोऽस्तं स्वगृहं
> प्रति जगायात् । गच्छेत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the whole company of gods has come, my father-in-law Indra alone has not come. If that Indra were to come, let him eat the parched grain, and drink the pressed Soma; then, well fed and satisfied, let him go back again to his own home.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—other than Indra
- विश्वो हि अन्यः (*viśvo hi anyaḥ*)—all the other company of gods
- आजगाम (*ājagāma*)—have come to our sacrifice
- मम इत् (*mama it*)—my
- श्वशुरः (*śvaśuraḥ*)—father-in-law Indra alone
- नाजगाम (*nājagāma*)—has not come (let Indra come)
- धानाः (*dhānāḥ*)—barley grains
- जक्षीयात् (*jakṣīyāt*)—let him eat
- उत (*uta*)—and
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the pressed Soma
- पपीयात् (*papīyāt*)—let him drink
- स्वाशितः (*svāśitaḥ*)—having eaten until satisfied
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- अस्तं (*astaṃ*)—to his own home
- जगायात् (*jagāyāt*)—let him go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wife of the seer Vasukra says: All the other gods, apart from Indra, have come to the sacrifice. Only my father-in-law Indra has not come. Let Indra come and eat the barley grain. Let him drink the pressed Soma. Having eaten until satisfied, let him go back again to his own home.

##### English translation
(The wife of Vasukra speaks :) Every other (divine) lord has come, but my father-in-law has not come : may he eat the parched grain : and drink the Soma ; when he is well satisfied, may he return home.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स रोरु॑वद्वृष॒भस्ति॒ गृशृं॑गो॒ वर्ष॑न्तस्थौ॒ वरि॑म॒न्ना पृ॑थि॒व्याः ।  
> विश्वे॑ष्टेनं वृ॒जने॑षु पामि॒ यो मे॑ कु॒क्षि सु॒तसो॑मः  ॒॑
> पृणाति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । रोरुवत् । वृषभः । तिग्मृशृंगः । वर्षन् । तस्थौ । वरिमन् । आ । पृथिव्याः ।  
> विश्वेषु । एनं । वृजनेषु । पामि । यः । मे । कुक्षि इति । सुतसोमः । पृणाति ॥

### Printed p. 757

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषभः कामानां वर्षिता तिग्मशृंगस्तीक्ष्णरश्मि स इंद्रोऽहं पृथिव्या अंतरिक्षस्य वर्ष्मन् वर्ष्मणि । वर्ष्मण्यब्द उन्नतवचनः स्थिरवचनो वा । एवंभूते
> वरिमन् विस्तीर्णे प्रदेशे रोरुवद्भृशं शब्दायमानः सन्ना तस्थौ । आतिष्ठामि ।
> एवंभूतोऽहं विश्वेषु सर्वॆषु वृजनेषु संग्रामेष्टेनमीदृशं वसुक्रं यजमानं पामि । रक्षामि । यो यजमानः सुतसोमोऽभिषुतसोमो मे मम
> कुक्षि उभौ पार्श्व पृणाति सोमरसपुरोडाशादिहविर्भिः पूरयति । ईदृशं
> रक्षामीति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

*Gāyatrī-mantra* stands at the head of the block. वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*) is the showerer of desires; तिग्मशृंगः (*tigmaśṛṃgaḥ*) is one with sharp rays. That Indra, I, in the वर्ष्मन् (*varṣman*) of the earth—of the atmosphere—stand. The word वर्ष्मन् (*varṣman*) means "lofty" or "firm". In such a वरिमन् (*variman*), a wide region, roaring loudly, I take my stand. Being such, in all वृजनेषु (*vṛjaneṣu*), battles, I protect this Vasukra, the sacrificer, who, having pressed Soma, fills my two flanks (कुक्षि (*kukṣi*), both sides) with offerings such as Soma juice and the cake. The construction is "I protect such a one."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the showerer of desires
- तिग्मशृंगः (*tigmaśṛṃgaḥ*)—one with sharp rays
- सः (*saḥ*)—I (Indra), the famous
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- वर्ष्मन् (*varṣman*)—in the lofty
- वरिमन् (*variman*)—and wide region
- रोरुवत् (*roruvat*)—making a sound
- आ तस्थौ (*ā tasthau*)—I am established
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which sacrificer
- सुतसोमः (*sutasomaḥ*)—having pressed Soma
- मे (*me*)—my
- कुक्षि (*kukṣi*)—both flanks of the belly
- पृणाति (*pṛṇāti*)—fills
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—such a sacrificer
- विश्वेषु वृजनेषु (*viśveṣu vṛjaneṣu*)—in all battles
- पामि (*pāmi*)—I protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra: I, the showerer of desires, with sharp rays, the famous, am established, making a sound, in the lofty and wide region of the atmosphere. The sacrificer who, having pressed Soma, fills both flanks of my belly, such a sacrificer I protect in all battles.

##### English translation
(Indra speaks:) (Indra) the showerer (of blessings), having hot rays, abides roaring in the resounding expanse of the firmament : in all conflicts I defend him, (Vasukra), who, having effused the libation, fills my flanks.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अद्रि॑णा ते म॒ुंदिन॑ इंद्र॒ तूया॑न्तु॒न्वंति॒ सोमा॒न्पिब॑सि॒  ॑
> त्वमेषां ।

### Printed p. 758

> पचंति ते वृषभा अत्सि तेषां पृक्षेण यन्मघवन्नूयमानः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आद्रिणा । ते । मंदिनः । इंद्र । तूयान् । सुन्वंति । सोमान् । पिबसि । त्वं । एषां ।  
> पचंति । ते । वृषभान् । अत्सि । तेषां । प्रक्षेण । यत् । मघवन् । हूयमानः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते त्वदर्थं मुंदिनो मादयित्थंस्तूयानविलंबितान्सोमानद्रिणाभिषवग्रावा सुन्वंति। यजमाना अभिषुण्वंति।एषामस्मदादियजमानानां संबंधिनः सोमांस्तं पिबसि । किंच त्वदर्थं वृषभान्पशून्ये च यजमानाः पचंति
> तेषां संबंधिनो हविर्भूतान्नशूनस्ति । भक्षयसि । हे मघवनवन्निंद्र त्वं
> यदा प्रक्षेण हविर्भूतेनान्नेन निमित्तेन हूयमानः यजमानैर्हूयसे तदेति
> पूर्वेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, for you the worshippers press with the pressing-stone the exhilarating, swiftly flowing Soma-juices. You drink the Soma of these sacrificers (us and others). Moreover, the bulls, the animals that the sacrificers cook for you, you eat, as offerings belonging to them. O Maghavan Indra, when you are invoked by the sacrificers with the oblation-food (prakṣa), then (this connects with what precedes)."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—for you
- मंदिनः (*maṃdinaḥ*)—exhilarating
- तूयान् (*tūyān*)—swiftly flowing, Soma-juices
- अद्रिणा (*adriṇā*)—with the pressing-stones
- सुन्वंति (*sunvaṃti*)—the sacrificers press
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—given by these sacrificers
- सोमान् (*somān*)—Soma-juices
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- पिबसि (*pibasi*)—you drink
- वृषभान् (*vṛṣabhān*)—bulls
- ते पचंति (*te pacaṃti*)—the sacrificers cook for you
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- प्रक्षेण (*prakṣeṇa*)—by reason of the oblation
- यत् हूयमानः (*yat hūyamānaḥ*)—when you are invoked, then
- तेषां (*teṣāṃ*)—the oblations offered by the sacrificers
- अत्सि (*atsi*)—you eat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vasukra (Ṛks 3, 4, 5): O Indra, for you the sacrificers press with the pressing-stones the exhilarating, swiftly flowing Soma-juices. You drink the Soma-juices given by these sacrificers. The sacrificers cook bulls for you. O wealthy Indra, whenever you are invoked by reason of the oblation, you eat the oblations offered by the sacrificers.

### Printed p. 759

##### English translation
(Vasukra speaks :) Your worshippers express with the stone fast flowing exhilarating Soma-juices for you, you drink them ;they roast bulls for you, you eat them, when you are invoked, Maghavan, to the sacrificial food.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒दं सु मे॑ जरित॒रा चि॑किद्धि प्रती॒पं शापं॑ न॒द्यो॑ वहंति ।  
> लो॒पा॒शः सिं॒हं प्र॒त्यंच॑मत्साः क्रो॒ष्टा व॑रा॒हं निर॑तक्त॒  ॑
> कक्षात् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदं । सु । मे । जरितः । आ । चिकिद्दि । प्रतिईपं । शापं । नद्यः । वहंति ।  
> लोपाशः । सिंहं । प्रत्यंचं । अत्सारिति । क्रोष्टा । वराहं । निः । आतक्त । कक्षात् ॥४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जरितः शत्रूणां जरयितरिंद्र त्वं मे मम सु शोभनमपीदमादृशं
> रूपं सामर्थ्यमा चिकिद्दि । आ समंताज्ञानीहि । कीदृशं । नद्यो गंगाद्याः सरितः
> प्रतीपं प्रतिकूलं शापमुदकं वहंति । अपि च लोपाशः । लुष्यमानं तृणमश्नातीति लोपाशो मृगः । मया प्रेषितः सन् प्रत्यंचमात्मानं प्रति गच्छंतं सिंहमत्साः । अत्सारीत् । अभिमुख्येन गच्छति । तथा क्रोष्णा शृगालो वराहं बलवंतमपि सूकरं कक्षादतिगहनदेशान्निरतक्त । निर्गमयति । एतदपि सर्वं सामर्थ्यं
> त्वत्पुत्रे मयि त्वत्प्रसादाल्बद्धमपि जानीहीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Jaritṛ, destroyer of enemies, Indra, know well this kind of my power: the rivers such as the Gaṅgā bear their water against the current. Moreover the लोपाशः (*lopāśaḥ*), the animal that eats grass being cut, sent by me, drives off the lion coming against it (*atsāḥ* is read as 'goes facing'); and the jackal drives the boar, though strong, out of the deep thicket (निरतक्त (*niratakta*) means 'makes go out'). Know all this power, obtained by your grace in me, your son."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जरितः (*jaritaḥ*)—O Indra, destroyer of enemies (by which power of mine)
- नद्यः (*nadyaḥ*)—the rivers such as the Gaṅgā
- शापं (*śāpaṃ*)—water
- प्रतीपं (*pratīpaṃ*)—with the current turned back
- वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—flow
- लोपाशः (*lopāśaḥ*)—the animal that eats grass
- प्रत्यंचं (*pratyaṃcaṃ*)—falling upon itself
- सिंहं (*siṃhaṃ*)—the lion
- आत्साः (*ātsāḥ*)—is able to drive off (and)
- क्रोष्टा (*kroṣṭā*)—the jackal
- वराहं (*varāhaṃ*)—the powerful wild boar
- कक्षात् (*kakṣāt*)—from its thicket
- निरतक्त (*niratakta*)—is able to drive out
- मे (*me*)—my
- सु (*su*)—excellent
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this power
- आ चिकिद्दि (*ā cikiddi*)—know

### Printed p. 760

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vasukra: O Indra, destroyer of enemies, know this excellent power of mine, obtained by your grace, as a result of which the rivers such as the Gaṅgā make their current flow backwards, by which the grass-eating animal can drive off the lion that falls upon it, and the jackal can drive the powerful wild boar out of the dense thicket.

##### English translation
Overcomer of foes, (Indra) be cognizant of this my (power, where.
by) rivers bear their water backwards, and the eater of cut (grass) confronts
the lion, the jackal dries the wild boar from his lair.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सोमो अक्षाः (*somo akṣāḥ*)—Yāska has explained the etymology of the word अक्षाः (*akṣāḥ*) through two examples:
सोमो अक्षाः । न यस्य द्यावापृथिवी न धन्व नांतरिक्षं नाद्रयः सोमो अक्षाः । अश्नोतेरित्येवमेके । अनूपेगोमान्नोभिरक्षाः । सोमो दुग्धाभि रक्षाः । लोपाशः सिंहं प्रत्यंच मत्साः । क्षियतिनिगमः पूर्वः क्षरतिनिगम उत्तर इत्येके अनूपे गोमान्गोभिर्यदा क्षियंत्यथ सोमो दुग्धाभ्यः क्षरति सर्वे क्षियतिनिगमा इति शाकपूणिः ॥ (*somo akṣāḥ | na yasya dyāvāpṛthivī na dhanva nāṃtarikṣaṃ nādrayaḥ somo akṣāḥ | aśnoterityevameke | anūpegomānnobhirakṣāḥ | somo dugdhābhi rakṣāḥ | lopāśaḥ siṃhaṃ pratyaṃca matsāḥ | kṣiyatinigamaḥ pūrvaḥ kṣaratinigama uttara ityeke anūpe gomāngobhiryadā kṣiyaṃtyatha somo dugdhābhyaḥ kṣarati sarve kṣiyatinigamā iti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*) (Ni. 5.3)
The word अक्षाः (*akṣāḥ*) is derived from the root क्षि (*kṣi*) meaning "dwell". Some say it is derived from the root अश् (*aś*) meaning "go, pervade". Two Śruti sentences are given here as examples. In the first sentence the meaning "dwelling" is indicated for the word अक्षाः (*akṣāḥ*), and in the second example the meaning "flowing away". The view of the teacher Śākapūṇi is that in both examples the meaning "dwell" is indicated for the word अक्षाः (*akṣāḥ*).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क॒था त॑ ए॒तद॒हमा चि॑केतं॒ गृत्स॑स्य॒ पाक॑स्त॒वसो॑ मनी॒षां ।  
> त्वं नो॑ वि॒द्वा ऋ॑तु॒था वि वो॑चो॒ यमर्ध०॑ ते मघवन्क्षे॒म्या धूः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 761

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कथा । ते । एतत् । अहं । आ । चिकेतं । गृत्सस्य । पाकः । तवसः । मनीषां ।  
> त्वं । नः । विद्वान् । ऋतुथा । वि । वोचः । यं । अर्धं । ते । मघवन् ।  
> क्षेम्याः । धूः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र पाकः पक्तव्यप्रज्ञोऽहं गृत्सस्य मेधाविनस्तवसो वृक्षस्य ते तव
> मनीषां स्तुतिं । कर्तुमिति शेषः । एतदीदृशं त्वदीयं सामर्थ्यं कथा कथं केन
> प्रकारेणा चिकेतं । आ समंताज्ञानामि । त्वदुपदेशं विना न जानामीत्यर्थः ।
> तस्मात्कारणाद्विद्वान् सर्वज्ञस्वमेव नोऽस्मभ्यमृतुथा काले काले वि वोचः ।
> विशेषेण ब्रूहि । हे मघवनन्नवन्निंद्र ते तवार्धं यं स्तुत्यवयवं कुर्मः सा
> स्तुतिर्धूः क्षेम्या क्षेमे भवा क्लेशरहिता वोढुं शक्यास्ति । यस्मात्तव स्तुत्यवयवमेव वयमक्लेशेन कर्तुं न शक्कुमोऽस्माकं मंदबुद्धित्वात् तस्मात्त्वमेवास्सभ्यं स्वसमार्थ्यं स्तुतिप्रकारं च पुनरपि कथयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, I, with immature understanding, how can I know this power of yours, to compose praise (the infinitive is to be supplied) for you, the wise (गृत्सस्य (*gṛtsasya*)) and mighty (तवसः (*tavasaḥ*), here explained as 'tree' in the text)? I cannot know it without your instruction. Therefore you, the all-knowing, declare to us in due seasons. O Maghavan Indra, the portion of praise that we make for you: that praise is a burden easy to bear, free from trouble. Since we, dull of mind, cannot make even a part of your praise without trouble, tell us again your own power and the manner of praising."**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) पाकः (*pākaḥ*)—of immature understanding
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- गृत्सस्य (*gṛtsasya*)—wise
- तवसः (*tavasaḥ*)—and mature
- ते (*te*)—addressed to you
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—praise
- to offer: एतत् (*etat*)—this power of yours
- कथा (*kathā*)—in what manner
- आ चिकेतं (*ā ciketaṃ*)—can I know?
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—all-knowing
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*)—according to each time
- वि वोचः (*vi vocaḥ*)—teach discernment
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- यं अर्धं (*yaṃ ardhaṃ*)—which part of praise
- ते (*te*)—we offer to you
- धूः (*dhūḥ*)—its burden
- क्षेम्याः (*kṣemyāḥ*)—is without difficulty to bear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vasukra: O Indra, how can I, of immature understanding, know your power, so as to offer praise to you, the wise and the mature? You, the all-knowing, teach us discernment in due season. O wealthy Indra, the burden of whatever portion of praise we offer you will be easy for you to bear.

### Printed p. 762

##### English translation
How Indra, should I, yet immature (in understanding), be capable
of comprehending this (your power, so as to render fitting) praise to you
who are wise and powerful? Therefore you who are all-knowing instruct
us in fit season; the portion of your (praise), O Maghavan, which (we
offer) is a burden easy to be borne.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा हि मां त॒वसं॑ व॒र्धयं॑ति दि॒वश्चि॑न्ने बृह॒त उत्त॑रा॒ धूः ।  
> पु॒रू स॒हस्रा॒ नि शि॑शामि सा॒कम॑श॒त्रुं हि मा॒ जनि॑ता ज॒जान॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । हि । मां । तवसं । वर्धयंति । दिवः । चित् । मे । बृहतः । उत्तरा ।  
> धूः ।  
> पुरु । सहस्रा । नि । शिशामि । साकं । अशत्रुं । हि । मा । जनिता । जजान ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हि यस्मात्कारणादेवैवमुक्तप्रकारेण तवसं प्रवृद्धं मां स्तोतारः
> स्तुतिभिः स्तुवंतो वीर्येण वर्धयंति तस्मात्कारणाद्बृहतो महतो मे
> ममेंद्रस्य दिवश्चिद्दुलोकादपि धूः स्तुतिरुत्तरोद्धृततराधिकतरा । किंच पुरु
> पुरूणि बहूनि सहस्रा शत्रूणां सहस्राणि साकं युगपन्नि शिशामि । तनूकरोमि !
> हिनस्मीत्यर्थः । हि यस्मात्कारणाज्जनिता सर्वस्य जनयिता प्रजापतिर्मा मामिंद्रमुशत्रुमविद्यमानशत्रुं जजान जनितवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Because the praisers, praising with hymns, thus increase me, the mighty one, with strength, therefore the praise of me, great Indra, is higher and greater even than the heaven. Moreover I at once destroy (नि शिशामि (*ni śiśāmi*): make thin, kill) many thousands of enemies, because the generator of all, Prajāpati, has begotten me, Indra, without an enemy."**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हि (*hi*)—because
- एव (*eva*)—thus
- तवसं (*tavasaṃ*)—mighty
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- वर्धयंति (*vardhayaṃti*)—the praisers praise and strengthen; for that very reason
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—of great nature
- मे (*me*)—addressed to me
- धूः (*dhūḥ*)—praise
- दिवश्चित् (*divaścit*)—than heaven
- उत्तरा (*uttarā*)—is higher
- हि (*hi*)—by what power
- जनिता (*janitā*)—the generator, Prajāpati
- मा (*mā*)—

me
- अशत्रुं (*aśatruṃ*)—without an enemy
- जजान (*jajāna*)—has produced, therefore
- पुरु (*puru*)—many
- सहस्रा (*sahasrā*)—thousands of enemies
- साकं (*sākaṃ*)—together
- नि शिशामि (*ni śiśāmi*)—I destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra: Because the praisers praise and strengthen me, grown mighty for my greatness, therefore the praise addressed to me, of great nature, is higher than heaven. By the power through which Prajāpati, the generator of the world, has produced me without an enemy, I destroy together many thousands of enemies.

##### English translation
(Indra speaks :) Since (your laudations) thus increase my strength,
(let) the praise of me who am mighty, (rise) even higher than the heavens.
I destroy at once many thousands (of foes), for the generator (of all) has
engendered me without an enemy-

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> देवाः ।  
> वधीं॑ वृ॒त्रं वज्रे॑ण मंदसा॒नोऽप॑ व्र॒जं म॑हि॒ना दा॒शुषे॑  
> वं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । हि । मां । तवसं । जज्जुः । उग्रं । कर्मन्कर्मन् । वृषणं । इंद्र ।  
> देवाः ।  
> वधीं । वृत्रं । वज्रेण । मंदसानः । अप । व्रजं । महिना । दाशुषे । वं ॥ ७ ॥

> हि यस्मात्कारणादेवैवमनेनोक्तप्रकारेण हे इंद्र देवा मरुदादय
> ऋत्विग्यजमाना वा तवसं महांतं त्वत्पुत्रंत्वद्रूपेणावस्थितं संतं वसुक्रं मां

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Because, O Indra, the gods, the Maruts and others, or the priests and sacrificers, in the manner thus stated, (increase) me, mighty, great, your son, existing in your form, Vasukra…".

### Printed p. 764

> कर्मन्कर्मन् वृत्रवधाग्निहोत्रादौ सर्वस्मिन्कर्मण्युग्रं शूरमसह्यं वा वृषणं
> वर्षितारं हविषां दातारं जज्जुः जानंति अतो मंदसानो मोदमानोऽहं
> वज्रेणायुधेन वृत्रं मेघासुरं वधीं । अवधिषं । किंच दाशुषे दविर्दत्तवते
> यजमानाय वृष्टिप्रदानार्थं महिना महत्वेन व्रजं मेघसमूहमप वं ।
> अपावं । अपवृणोमि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vasukra (as Indra) continues: in every rite, such as the slaying of Vṛtra or the agnihotra, they know him as fierce, mighty or irresistible, a showerer and giver of oblations. Therefore, exulting, he has slain the cloud-demon Vṛtra with the thunderbolt. For the sacrificer who has given an oblation he has opened the mass of clouds by his greatness, in order to grant rain. वधीं (*vadhīṃ*) is explained as "I slew" and वं (*vaṃ*) (with अप (*apa*)) as "I opened".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- हि (*hi*)—for what reason
- एव (*eva*)—thus
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- तवसं (*tavasaṃ*)—powerful
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- कर्मन् कर्मन् (*karman karman*)—in every rite
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—mighty
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—as the giver of oblations
- जज्जुः (*jajjuḥ*)—have known; for that very reason
- मंदसानः (*maṃdasānaḥ*)—I, filled with joy
- वज्रेण (*vajreṇa*)—with the thunderbolt
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra the Asura
- वधीं (*vadhīṃ*)—I have destroyed
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—for the sacrificer
- महिना (*mahinā*)—by greatness
- व्रजं (*vrajaṃ*)—the mass of clouds
- अप वं (*apa vaṃ*)—I have split open

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vasukra: O Indra, because the gods thus know me, the powerful one, in every rite as the mighty giver of oblations, therefore I, filled with joy, have destroyed the Asura Vṛtra with the thunderbolt. For the sacrificer, by my greatness, I have split open the mass of clouds.

##### English translation
Since, Indra, the gods have known me to be powerful, fierce in every act, the showerer (of oblations): exulting I have slain Vritra with your thunderbolt, and by my might have opened the clouds for the donor (of oblations).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वास॑ आयन्पर॒शूर॑भिभ्र॒न्नना॑ वृ॒श्चंतो॑ अ॒भि वि॒ड्भिरा॑यन् ।  
> नि सु॒द्वं१॒॑गदध॑तो व॒क्षणा॑सु॒ यत्रा॒ कृपी॑ट॒मनु॒ तद्द॑हंति ॥८॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवासः । आयन् । परशून् । अभिभ्रन् । वना । वृश्चंतः । अभि । विट्ऽभिः । आयन् ।  
> नि । सुद्वं । दधतः । वक्षणासु । यत्र । कृपीटं । अनु । तत् । दहंति ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 765

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवासो देवा इंद्रेण चोदिताः संत आयन् । गच्छंति । मेघवधार्थं
> परशून्वज्रानबिभ्रन् । धारयंति च । तदनंतरं विद्धिर्मरुदादिप्रजाभिः सहिता
> वृश्चंतो मेघांश्मिंदंतो वना वनानि वृष्टिलक्षणान्युदकान्यभ्यायन् । अभिमुख्येन गच्छंति । ततः सुद्र्व्वं शोभनद्रवणं वृष्टु दकं वक्षणासु नदीषु नि दधतो
> नियमेन स्थापयंतो यत्र यस्मिन्मेघजाते कृपीटं । उदकनामैतत् । निगूढमुदकं तिष्ठति त इमे देवास्तन्मेघजातमनु लक्षीकृत्य दहंति । उदकनिर्गमनार्थं
> शोषयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, urged by Indra, come; to slay the cloud they bear axes (thunderbolts). Then, together with the Maruts and the other folk, cleaving the clouds, they approach the "woods" (वना (*vanā*)), that is, the waters in the form of rain. Then, firmly depositing the fair-flowing rain-water in the rivers (वक्षणासु (*vakṣaṇāsu*)), they burn (dry up) that mass of cloud in which कृपीटं (*kṛpīṭaṃ*) stands, कृपीटं (*kṛpīṭaṃ*) being a name for water, the hidden water that remains; they do so for the water to come out.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods
- आयन् (*āyan*)—have come
- परशून् (*paraśūn*)—their weapons
- अभिभ्रन् (*abhibhran*)—bear
- विड्भिः (*viḍbhiḥ*)—together with the Maruts and other folk
- वृश्चंतः (*vṛścaṃtaḥ*)—cleaving the clouds
- वना (*vanā*)—the waters
- अभ्यायन् (*abhyāyan*)—they meet (they pour down)
- सुद्वं (*sudvaṃ*)—excellent water
- वक्षणासु (*vakṣaṇāsu*)—in the rivers
- नि दधतः (*ni dadhataḥ*)—have established
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which group of clouds
- कृपीटं (*kṛpīṭaṃ*)—there is water
- तत् अनु (*tat anu*)—aiming at that
- दहंति (*dahaṃti*)—they dry it up for the sake of the water

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra: By my impulse the gods have come. They bear their weapons. Together with the Maruts and other folk they cleave the clouds and meet the waters. They have established the excellent waters in the rivers. In whichever group of clouds there is water, aiming at that they dry it up for the sake of the water.

##### English translation
The gods came, they bare their axes ; clearing the woods, they came with men in front of the waters : depositing (the tree) of good wood in the belly (of the river), where the underwood (is), they burnt it up.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बृ॒हंतं॑ चिदृह॒ते रं॑धयानि॒ वय॑द्व॒त्सो वृ॑ष॒भं शूशु॑वानः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शशः । क्षुरं । प्रत्यंचं । जगार । अद्रिं । लोगेन । वि । अभेदं । आरात् ।  
> बृहंतं । चित् । ऋहते । रंधयानि । वयत् । वत्सः । वृषभं । शूशुवानः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वसुक्र इंद्रं प्रतिब्रूते । शश एतत्संज्ञितो मया प्रेरितो मृगविशेषः
> प्रत्यंचं वधायात्मानं प्रति गच्छंतं क्षुरं क्षुरवंतं दृढदीर्घतीक्ष्णनखं सिंहव्याघ्रादिकं । बलवत्यूरमृगमित्यर्थः । जगार । गिरति गृह्णाति वा । किंच लोगेन
> लोष्टेनाद्रिं हिमवदादिकं पर्वतमाराद्दूरे स्थितमपि व्यभेदं । अहं भिनद्मि ।
> बृहंतं चिन्महांतमपि हस्त्यादिकमृते ह्रस्वकायाल्पाय शशकादिकाय रंधयानि ।
> वशं गमयानि । शूशुवानो वीर्येण वर्धमानो वत्सो वृषभं महोक्षं
> वयत् । युद्धाय गच्छति । हे इंद्र एतदपि सर्वं त्वत्पसादादहं करोमीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vasukra answers Indra. The hare (शश (*śaśa*)), a creature urged on by him, seizes the assailing क्षुरं (*kṣuraṃ*), that is, one with firm, long, sharp claws, a lion, tiger and the like, a powerful wild beast, coming against it to kill. Further, with a clod (लोगेन (*logena*)) he splits a mountain such as the Himālaya, even though far off. He can bring even a huge creature such as an elephant under the power of a small-bodied one such as a hare. The calf, growing in vigour, goes to fight the great bull. O Indra, all this he does by Indra's favour.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शशः (*śaśaḥ*)—the hare
- प्रत्यंचं (*pratyaṃcaṃ*)—that which falls upon it
- क्षुरं (*kṣuraṃ*)—lions and the like with sharp claws
- जगार (*jagāra*)—seizes
- आरात् (*ārāt*)—though far off
- अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)—a mountain
- लोगेन (*logena*)—with a clod (a lump of earth)
- व्यभेदं (*vyabhedaṃ*)—I can split
- बृहंतं चित् (*bṛhaṃtaṃ cit*)—a large-bodied creature
- ऋहते (*ṛhate*)—to a small-bodied creature
- रंधयानि (*raṃdhayāni*)—I can make subject
- शूशुवानः (*śūśuvānaḥ*)—grown strong with vigour
- वत्सः (*vatsaḥ*)—a small calf
- वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*)—a big bull
- वयत् (*vayat*)—can face and fight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vasukra: (If Indra's favour is present) the hare can seize lions and the like with sharp claws that fall upon it. Though far away, I can split a mountain with a small clod of earth. I can make a large creature subject to a small one. A small calf grown strong with vigour can face and strike a big bull (can fight).

##### English translation
(Vasukra speaks:) The hare grasps the assailing beast of prey : with a clod of clay I cleave the distant (mountain): I can compel the great to submit to the small : swelling (with courage) the calf attacks the bull.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि॒रु॒द्धश्चि॑न्महि॒षस्त॒र्ष्यावा॑न्नो॒गाधा तस्मा॑ अ॒यथं॑ कर्षदे॒तत् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुपर्णः । इत्था । नखं । आ । सिसाय । अवरुद्धः । परिपदं । न । सिंहः ।  
> निरुद्धः । चित् । महिषः । तर्ष्यावान् । गोधा । तस्मै । अयथं । कर्षत् ।  
> एतत् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुपर्णः पक्षिरूपा गायत्रीत्थामुत्र द्युलोके नखमात्मीयमा सिषाय ।
> सोमाहरणकाल इंद्रार्थमाबबंध । इंद्रस्य प्रसादाद्दिवि पदं न्यस्तवतीत्यर्थः ।
> तत्र दृष्टांतः । अवरुद्धः पंजरेणावृतः परिवेष्टितः सिंहः परिपदं न । यथा करस्कोपरि सर्वतः पादमवबध्नाति । किंच । चिदित्युपमार्थे । यथा केनापि बद्धपादो
> निरुद्धो महिषस्तर्ष्यावानुदकाभावे तृषावान्भवति एवमिंद्रः सोमाहरणातूर्वं सोमाभावे तृषितवानभूदिति शेषः । तस्मै । तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी । तादृशस्य
> तृषितस्येंद्रस्यार्थं गोधा । गमयति वर्णानिति गौर्वाक् तत्र निधीयमानत्वाद्यायत्रि गोधा । यद्वा । गुधिर्निष्कर्षणार्थः । निष्कृष्यसोमाहरणाद्गोधा गायत्री ।
> आयथमयत्नेन । लीलयेत्यर्थः । एतत्सोमजातं कर्षत् । आकृष्टवती । दिवः
> सकाशादाहृतवतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The bird-formed Gāyatrī, yonder in heaven (इत्था (*itthā*)), fastened (सिषाय (*siṣāya*)) her claw for Indra at the time of fetching Soma; by Indra's favour she set her foot in heaven. Illustration: like a lion confined in a cage (परिपदं न (*paripadaṃ na*)), which fastens its foot all round over its paw. Further, चित् (*cit*) is in the sense of comparison: as a buffalo whose foot is bound by someone becomes thirsty when there is no water, so Indra, after the fetching of Soma, grew thirsty when Soma was lacking (this is to be supplied). तस्मै (*tasmai*) is dative of purpose: for such a thirsty Indra. गोधा (*godhā*) is Gāyatrī: "gau" is speech, which conveys the letters, and being placed in it she is गोधा (*godhā*); or else the root गुधि (*gudhi*) has the sense of drawing out, and Gāyatrī, having drawn out and fetched Soma, is गोधा (*godhā*). आयथं (*āyathaṃ*) is "without effort", i.e. playfully. कर्षत् (*karṣat*): she drew this Soma, brought it from heaven.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अवरुद्धः (*avaruddhaḥ*)—confined in a cage
- सिंहः न परिपदं (*siṃhaḥ na paripadaṃ*)—as a lion places one foot over another
- सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*)—the bird (Gāyatrī)
- इत्था (*itthā*)—in heaven
- नखं (*nakhaṃ*)—her claw
- आ सिसाय (*ā sisāya*)—fixed
- निरुद्धः (*niruddhaḥ*)—tied up
- महिषः (*mahiṣaḥ*)—the buffalo
- तर्षान्वान् (*tarṣānvān*)—suffers from thirst (Indra suffered from lack of Soma)
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—for that Indra
- गोधा (*godhā*)—Gāyatrī
- अयथं (*ayathaṃ*)—without effort
- एतत् (*etat*)—this Soma
- कर्षत् (*karṣat*)—carried off and brought

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra: As a lion confined in a cage places one foot over another, so Gāyatrī in bird form fixed her claw in heaven. As a tied-up buffalo suffers from thirst, so Indra suffered from lack of Soma.

### Printed p. 768
For that Indra, Gāyatrī carried off this Soma and brought it without effort.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तेभ्यो॑ गो॒धा आ॒यथं॑ कर्षदे॒तद्ये ब्र॒ह्मणः॑ प्रति॒पीयं॒त्यन्नैः॑ ।  
> सि॒म उ॒क्ष्णो॑ऽवसृ॒ष्टा अ॑दंति स्व॒यं बला॑नि त॒न्वः॑ शृणा॒नाः ॥११॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तेभ्यः । गोधा । अयथं । कर्षत् । एतत् । ये । ब्रह्मणः । प्रतिपीयंति । अन्नैः ।  
> सिमः । उष्णः । अवसृष्टान् । अदंति । स्वयं । बलानि । तन्वः । शृणानाः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये मरुदादिदेवगणा ब्रह्मणः परिवृढस्येंद्रस्य स्वभूतैरन्नैः सोमाख्यैः ।
> तृप्ताः संत इति शेषः । प्रतिपीयंति । पीयतिर्हिंसाकर्मा । इंद्रादेशाद्दिंसकांत्रतिहिंसंति तेभ्यस्तेषां देवगणानामर्थाय गोधाः पूर्वोक्ता गायत्र्ययथमनायासेन्नैतत्सोमजातं कर्षत् । आकृष्टवती । किंच सिमः सिमाइष्ठान् ।
> यद्वा । सिमशब्दः सर्वशब्द पर्यायः । सर्वान् । उक्ष्णः सिंचतोऽवसृष्टानिंद्रेण
> निसृष्टाननुज्ञातान्विर्भूतान्नोमान्यज्ञॆष्टदंति । भक्षयंति । किं कुर्वंतः । स्वयमात्मनैव बलानि शत्रूणां सैन्यानि तन्नः शरीराणि च शृणाना हिंसंतः । गायत्रींद्रादेशाद्देवेभ्यः सोममाहृतवतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hosts of gods, Maruts and others, who, satisfied with the Soma-foods that are the property of ब्रह्मणः (*brahmaṇaḥ*) (the great Indra), प्रतिपीयंति (*pratipīyaṃti*): the root पीय (*pīya*) means to injure; at Indra's command they injure in return those who injure them. For those hosts of gods the aforesaid Gāyatrī, गोधा (*godhā*), drew this Soma without effort. Further, सिमः (*simaḥ*) means "all", सिम (*sima*) being a synonym of सर्व (*sarva*). They eat (अदंति (*adaṃti*)) all the sprinkling (उक्ष्णः (*ukṣṇaḥ*)) Somas that Indra has released (अवसृष्टान् (*avasṛṣṭān*)), allowed, made manifest, at the sacrifice. What are they doing? Themselves, by their own strength, destroying (शृणानाः (*śṛṇānāḥ*)) the armies of enemies and their bodies. The meaning: at Indra's command Gāyatrī brought Soma for the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts and other gods
- ब्रह्मणः (*brahmaṇaḥ*)—of the strong Indra
- अन्नैः (*annaiḥ*)—with the foods in the form of Soma, satisfied
- प्रतिपीयंति (*pratipīyaṃti*)—are able to injure enemies
- तेभ्यः (*tebhyaḥ*)—for them

### Printed p. 769
- गोधाः (*godhāḥ*)—Gāyatrī
- अयथं (*ayathaṃ*)—without effort
- एतत् (*etat*)—this Soma
- कर्षत् (*karṣat*)—carried off and brought
- स्वयं (*svayaṃ*)—by their own power
- बलानि (*balāni*)—the armies of enemies
- तन्नः (*tannaḥ*)—the bodies of enemy people
- शृणानाः (*śṛṇānāḥ*)—destroying
- अवसृष्टान् (*avasṛṣṭān*)—those that remain after Indra has drunk
- उक्ष्णः (*ukṣṇaḥ*)—and that flow
- सिमः (*simaḥ*)—all the Soma juices
- अदंति (*adaṃti*)—they eat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vasukra: The Maruts and other gods who, satisfied with the Soma-foods of the strong Indra, are able to injure enemies: for them Gāyatrī carried off this Soma and brought it without effort. Destroying by their own power the armies of enemies and the bodies of enemy people, they drink all the Soma juices that remain (after Indra has drunk) and that flow.

##### English translation
Gayatri drew it away without difficulty, for the good of those (gods) who, (satisfied) with the viands of Indra, retaliate the injuries (of the enemies of the gods): they devour all the sprinkling (Soma libations) left (by Indra), spontaneously destroying the armies and bodies (of the enemy).

> ये देवर्ष्यादयस्तन्वः शरीराणि सोमे सोमयाग उक्षैः शस्त्रैर्हिन्विरे
> वर्धयंति एते देवादय इंद्रादेशात्सोम आह्ृते सति शमीभिः सोमयाग-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The divine seers and others who strengthen (हिन्विरे (*hinvire*)) their bodies at the Soma sacrifice with उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*), that is, with praises (*śastraiḥ*): these gods and the rest, when Soma has been fetched at Indra's command, with शमीभिः (*śamībhiḥ*) (the rites of the Soma sacrifice)…

### Printed p. 770

> कर्मभिः सुशमी सुकर्माणोऽभूवन् । नृवन्मनुष्यवद्वदन् इदं युष्मभ्यं मया
> दत्तमिति व्यक्तां वाचमुच्चारयन् नोऽस्मभ्यमुप माहि । उपगम्य वाजानन्नानि
> बलानि ना हे इंद्र त्वं देहीति शेषः । अतः कारणाद्वीरो दानशूरस्त्वं दिवि
> द्युलोके श्रवो दानपतिरिति कीर्तितं नाम नामधेयं दधिषे । धारयसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his gloss of the previous Ṛk. Through the Soma-sacrifice rites those sacrificers became "of good rites" (सुशमी (*suśamī*) is read as *sukarmāṇaḥ*, those whose rites are good). Speaking like a man (नृवत् (*nṛvat*) means "like a human being"), uttering plain words such as "This has been given to you by me", come to us (उप माहि (*upa māhi*)). Having come, give us वाजान् (*vājān*), that is, foods and strengths; "O Indra, you give" is the word to be supplied. For this reason you, the hero, the one heroic in giving, bear in heaven (the world of Dyu) a famed name, "lord of givers". दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*) means "you hold".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—who
- तन्नः (*tannaḥ*)—their bodies
- सोमे (*some*)—in the Soma-sacrifice
- उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*)—with śastra-mantras
- हिन्विरे (*hinvire*)—(those who) strengthen
- एते (*ete*)—all of them
- शमीभिः (*śamībhiḥ*)—by the rites of the Soma-sacrifice
- सुशर्मा (*suśarmā*)—possessing excellent rites
- अभूवन् (*abhūvan*)—became (O Indra)
- नृवत् (*nṛvat*)—like men
- वदन् (*vadan*)—speaking
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- उप माहि (*upa māhi*)—approach
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—give foods
- वीरः (*vīraḥ*)—you, the hero
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the world of heaven
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—famed
- नाम (*nāma*)—name
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you have taken on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, those sacrificers who strengthen their bodies in the Soma-sacrifice with śastra-mantras have all become possessors of excellent rites through the rites of the Soma-sacrifice. O Indra, speaking like a man, approach us and give us foods. You, the hero, have taken on a famed name in the world of heaven.

##### English translation
They have been sanctified by holy rites, who have fostered their bodies with prayers, at the Soma (sacrifice): speaking like a man, grant us food, you possess in heaven name and fame as a hero.

## Sūkta 29 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वने न वेत्यष्टर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं वसुक्रस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं ।
> अनुक्रांतं च । वने नाष्टाविति ॥ चतुर्थेऽहनि स्तोमवृद्धौ ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन एतत्सूक्तमावापार्थं । सूत्रितं च । स्तोमे वर्धमाने को अद्य नर्यो वने न
> वा यः । आ. ७-१२ । इति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्य एतत्सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । प्र वो

### Printed p. 771

> महे मंदमानायांधस इति निविद्धानं वने न वा यो न्यधायि चाकन् । ऐ. आ.
> ५-३-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta वने न वा (*vane na vā*) has eight Ṛks, and is the thirteenth sūkta (of the anuvāka). Its seer is Vasukra, its deity Indra, its metre Triṣṭubh. Sāyaṇa notes the Anukramaṇī, which reads वने नाष्टौ (*vane nāṣṭau*). On the fourth day, when the Stoma is being increased, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin uses this sūkta for the purpose of āvāpa (insertion); this is stated in the sūtra with the reference Ā. 7-12. In the Mahāvrata it is used in the niṣkevalya (śastra), as the sūtra says, and then the Brāhmaṇa quotes the line containing वने न वा यो न्यधायि चाकन् (*vane na vā yo nyadhāyi cākan*) (Ai. Ā. 5-3-1).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, "वने न वा (*vane na vā*)", is the thirteenth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer is Vasukra; its deity is Indra; its metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says "वने नाष्टौ (*vane nāṣṭau*)". On the fourth day of the sacrifice, for the increase of the Stoma, the ṛtvij called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite this sūkta for the purpose of āvāpa, as explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra "Stome vardhamāne ko adya naryo vane na nāyaḥ" (Ā. 7-12). It is also stated that in the Mahāvratestyi this sūkta is used for the niṣkevalya-śastra mantras, by the sentence of the Aitareya-Āraṇyaka, "Pra vo mahe mandamānāyāndhasa iti nividdhānaṃ vane na vā yo nyadhāyi cākan" (Ai. Ā. 5-3-1).

- Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 29.
- Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 7; Vargas 22, 23.
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8.
- Seer: Vasukra.
- Deity: Indra.
- Metre: Triṣṭubh.

> यस्येदिंद्र इति नृणां नृतमो नर्यश्च क्षपावांश्च समानमेत्पूर्वेणार्थेन ।
> यमेवमिंद्रः प्रार्थयते स एष स्तोमस्तं प्रत्यजीगः । गच्छतीत्यर्थः । अथवा
> स एष स्तोमोऽस्माभिरुदीर्यमाणस्तस्येंद्रस्य गुणान्गृह्णातीति स्यात् । जिगर्तिर्गृह्णातिकर्मेति ह्युक्तं ! नि. ६-८ । एवमत्र चाकन्नित्यस्य चायन्निति वा कामयमान
> इति वेत्येतौ विपरिणामावुपपद्येते शब्दसारूप्यादर्थाविरोधाच्च । एतस्मिन्निगमे
> पदविभागगतः कश्चिद्विचारोऽस्ति । तमाह भाष्यकारः । वेति च य इति च
> चकार शाकल्य इति । वेति य इति च पदे चकार शाकल्यः पदकारः । तदेतद्विचार्यमाणं न साधु भवति । किं कारणं । उदात्तं त्वेवमाख्यातमभविष्यत् । एवमेतस्मिन्नदद्वये सति यदेतदाख्यातं न्यधायीति तदुदात्तमभविष्यत् । यद्वृत्तात्परस्य
> नित्यमाख्यातस्य निघातो न भवतीति लक्षणविदो मन्यंते । न चेदमुदात्तं तस्माद्य
> इति नेदं यद्वृत्तं किं तर्हि वाय इत्येकमेव पदं । किंच । असुसमाप्तश्चार्थः ।
> अपुष्कलः । एवमेव तस्मिन्नदद्वये सति मंत्रस्यार्थोऽसुसमाप्नो भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains the first line. As a bird in a tree places in its own nest its own young one, not yet fledged, and that young one, so placed, looks about in fear, or else is eager, longing (चाकन् (*cākan*) is "looking" or "desiring"); in the same way this pure stoma, free of every fault, belonging to you, O Bhuraṇau (the two bearers, the Aśvins, or "swift"; he adds that *bhuraṇyuḥ* is a name for "quick"), lodged in us as in a nest, being like the bird's son, goes to you. Of which stoma Indra, on many days, is the invoker: Indra too calls, thinking "may this stoma be mine". What is Indra like? He is the manliest of men, the most heroic even among heroes; नर्यः (*naryaḥ*) is "beneficial to men"; क्षपावान् (*kṣapāvān*) is the one having a Soma-share in the night-rounds. The stoma that even Indra desires, and that is present among us, goes to you (अजीगः (*ajīgaḥ*): it goes constantly).

Some expositors take this Ṛk as addressed to the Aśvins. Sāyaṇa says that is wrong: in an Indra-sūkta this Ṛk is the first, and it is used on the sixth day of the Pṛṣṭhya, at the midday pressing, in the śastra of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, when the stoma is being increased.

Second explanation: "O bearers, lords of the gods, this pure, fault-free stoma lodged in us abides toward Indra, like the bird's young in the tree, longing. Of whose stoma Indra on many days was the invoker, thinking, 'may they praise me with this stoma'." The words "manliest of men", "beneficial to men" and क्षपावान् (*kṣapāvān*) have the same sense as before; Indra desires this stoma and it goes to him. Or else this stoma, recited by us, grasps the qualities of Indra, for it is said "जिगर्तिर्गृह्णातिकर्म (*jigartirgṛhṇātikarma*)" (Ni. 6-8). In this way both changes of reading are possible for चाकन् (*cākan*), as चायन् (*cāyan*) or as "desiring", through similarity of sound and absence of conflict in sense.

Then he turns to a point of word-division and cites the Bhāṣyakāra (Yāska): Śākalya, the Padakāra, made "वा (*vā*)" and "ya" two separate words. Sāyaṇa says this, on examination, is not sound: the verb न्यधायि (*nyadhāyi*) would then have had to be udātta, which the accent-knowers do not allow after a yad-word; and it is not so. So वायः (*vāyaḥ*) is one word, not "yad"-relative. Moreover the sense of the mantra would be incomplete.
