##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भुरणौ (*bhuraṇau*)—O Aśvin deities, bearers of the world
- नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)—among all men
- नृतमः (*nṛtamaḥ*)—the most excellent
- नर्यः (*naryaḥ*)—beneficial to men
- क्षपावान् (*kṣapāvān*)—who has Soma offered at night
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- पुरुदिनेषु (*purudineṣu*)—on many days
- यस्य (*yasya*)—to obtain which stoma
- होता (*hotā*)—he is the one who prays
- शुचिः (*śuciḥ*)—pure
- यः स्तोमः (*yaḥ stomaḥ*)—which stoma
- न्यधायि (*nyadhāyi*)—is lodged in us
- वने (*vane*)—as a bird laying its egg in a tree
- चाकन् न (*cākan na*)—looks after it carefully
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- अजीगः (*ajīgaḥ*)—(it) looks after carefully

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, bearers of the world: the pure stoma that is lodged in us, for obtaining which Indra, the foremost of all men, beneficial to men, he who has Soma offered at night, has been the one who prays for many days, looks after you carefully, as a bird that has laid its egg (its young) in a tree looks after it carefully.

##### English translation
As (the bird) who deposits its young (in its nest) in the tree (is) eagerly looking around, so you bearers (Aswins) your pure praise (ever) keeps you awake: (that praise) of which Indra has for many days been the invoker, (Indra) the friend of man, the manliest of men, (to whom the soma is offered) at night.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the word चाकन् (*cākan*), Yāska has given the Nirukta on this Ṛk thus:
वनेन वायो न्यधायि चाकन् । वन इव वायो वेः पुत्रश्चायन्निति वा कामयमान इति वा । वेति च य इति च चकार शाकल्य उदात्तं त्वेवमाख्यातमभविष्यदसुसमाप्तश्चार्थः ॥ (*vanena vāyo nyadhāyi cākan | vana iva vāyo veḥ putraścāyanniti vā kāmayamāna iti vā | veti ca ya iti ca cakāra śākalya udāttaṃ tvevamākhyātamabhaviṣyadasusamāptaścārthaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 6-28).
Here the word वन (*vana*) means a tree. The sense of the sentence is: a bird sitting in a tree places its tender young one, that is, a small chick whose wings have not yet grown, in the tree, and, since it cannot yet fly, looks about with anxiety about whether it will fall down somewhere —

### Printed p. 774

it may fall: with such eager anxiety it looks around. The sage Śākalya has divided the word वायः (*vāyaḥ*) in this sentence into two words, "वा (*vā*)" and "यः (*yaḥ*)". If that is done, the verb of the sentence would have had to have the udātta, and the sense of the sentence would be incomplete; so the author of the Nirukta has indicated his opinion.

If वायः (*vāyaḥ*) is taken as a single word, "vi" means a bird, and वायः (*vāyaḥ*) means "belonging to a bird", that is, the bird's young, born of the bird. This sense alone is fitting. But Śākalya, the author of the Pada-pāṭha, has separated the words as "वा यः (*vā yaḥ*)". If the words are so divided, the main verb न्यधायि (*nyadhāyi*) would have had to be ādyudātta, and the sense of the sentence would not be complete. Therefore, the Bhāṣyakāra has supported the view of the author of the Nirukta, that taking वायः (*vāyaḥ*) as a single word is the acceptable course.

> अनु॑ त्रि॒शोकः॑ श॒तमाव॑ह॒न्नन्नुत्से॑न॒ रथो॒ यो अस॑त्सस॒वान् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । ते । अस्याः । उषसः । प्र । अपरस्याः । नृतौ । स्याम । नृतमस्य । नृणां ।  
> अनु । त्रिशोकः । शतं । आ । अवहत् । न्यन् । कुत्सेन । रथः । यः । असत् । ससवान् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्या वर्तमानाया ईदृश्या उषसो नृतौ ॥ नृ नये ॥ नयने प्रापणे ।
> उदयकाल इत्यर्थः । नृणां नेतृणां मध्यॆ नृतमस्यातिशयेन नेतुस्ते तवेंद्रस्य
> स्तुत्या यागेन च प्र स्याम । वयं प्रकृष्टा भवेम । तथा हे इंद्र अपरस्या
> आगामिन्याश्चोषसो नृतौ प्रापणे तव स्तुत्या यागेन च वयं प्रकृष्टा भवेमेत्याशास्महे । किंच त्रिशोको नामर्षिर्हॆ इंद्र त्वामाराध्य त्वत्पसादाच्छतं
> बहूनन्वनुचरभूतान्ननुष्यानावहत् । प्रापितवान् । लब्धवानित्यर्थः । तथा
> तव कुत्सस्य च ससवान् सनिता युगपदेव संभक्ता यो रथोऽसत् अस्ति स रथः
> कुत्सेन । कुत्सो लब्धवानिति शेषः । तथा च मंत्रंतरे श्रूयते । यासि कुत्सेन
> सरथमवस्युः । ऋ ४-१६-११ । इति । यस्मादेवं तस्मात्त्वत्पसादाद्वयं प्रकृष्टा
> भवेमेत्यर्थः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the leading (नृतौ (*nṛtau*), from the root nṛ, "to lead", "to bring") of this present dawn, that is, at the time of its rising, we would be advanced (प्र स्याम (*pra syāma*)) through praise and sacrifice to you, Indra, the most leading of leaders (नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)). Likewise, O Indra, at the leading in (that is, the coming of) the future dawn too we hope to be advanced through praise and sacrifice to you. Further, the seer Triśoka, having propitiated you, through your favour brought (आवहत् (*āvahat*): obtained) a hundred, that is many, men as followers. And the chariot which is ससवान् (*sasavān*) (सनिता (*sanitā*), one who shares at once) between you and Kutsa was obtained by Kutsa (this last is supplied). That this is so is heard in another mantra: "यासि कुत्सेन सरथमवस्युः (*yāsi kutsena sarathamavasyuḥ*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16-11). Since it is so, by your favour may we be advanced.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, at the rising of the present dawn we shall be prosperous through the worship of you, the most excellent of all men. May we be so also in the coming dawn-times! The seer named Triśoka has obtained, through your favour, a numerous following. Kutsa has obtained, through your favour, a chariot endowed with wealth.

##### English translation
May we be prosperous at the coming of the present or of any future dawn, (through the adoration) of you, the chief leader of men : through your favour Trishoka obtained a hundred followers; the chariot which was common to him and you was acquired by Kutsa.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तवेषन्मध्यमोत्तमानां सोमजन्यानां मदानां मध्यॆ को
> मदो रंत्यो रमयिता प्रीतिकरो भूत् । भवति । त्वत्प्रीतिकरमदयोग्यसोमदानाभिप्रायेणायं प्रश्नॆः । उग्र ओजस्वी त्वं दुरो यज्ञगृहद्वाराणि गिरः
> स्तुतिलक्षणा वाचश्चाभि वि धाव । अभ्यागच्छ ! किंच कत् कदा वाहः । इंद्रं प्रत्युह्यत
> इति नाहः सोम उच्यते । एवंभूतोर्वाक् त्वत्पसादात्सलदानायास्मदभिमुखो भविष्यतीति शेषः । अपि च कदा मनीषा सर्वार्थदर्शना प्रज्ञा सर्वगुणग्राहिणी स्तुतिर्वा मा मां त्वत्पसादादुपगमिष्यतीति शेषः । कदा हे इंद्र त्वा त्वां ।
> आ इत्युपसर्गश्रुतेयोग्यपदाध्याहारः । आराध्य वयमन्नॆः सह राधो
> धनमुपमं मत्समीपं शक्यां। शकिरत्र गत्यर्थोऽंतर्भावितण्यर्थः । संगमयेयं॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, among your exhilarations born of Soma (**NOTE**), which exhilaration has become रंत्यः (*raṃtyaḥ*), delighting, pleasing? The question is meant for the gift of Soma fit for the exhilaration that pleases you. You, the mighty one, hasten (*abhi vi dhāva*: come) to the doors of the sacrificial house and to the voices of praise. Further, when will वाहः (*vāhaḥ*) (Soma is called "वाहः (*vāhaḥ*)" because it is carried to Indra) turn to us, by your favour, for giving the fruit (**NOTE**)? And when will मनीषा (*manīṣā*), insight that sees all things, or praise that grasps all qualities, come to me by your favour? And when, O Indra, having propitiated you (आ (*ā*) is a preposition that is heard, so a suitable word is supplied) shall we, together with foods, शक्यां (*śakyāṃ*), bring wealth (राधः (*rādhaḥ*)) near to me (उपमं (*upamaṃ*))? Here the root शक (*śaka*) is in the sense of motion, with a causative implied; the sense is संगमयेयं (*saṃgamayeyaṃ*), "may I bring together".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—for you
- कः मदः (*kaḥ madaḥ*)—what sort of exhilaration
- रंत्यः (*raṃtyaḥ*)—satisfying
- भूत् (*bhūt*)—is
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—you who are of great power
- दुरः (*duraḥ*)—to the doors of the sacrificial house
- गिरः अभि (*giraḥ abhi*)—and to the praises
- विधाव (*vidhāva*)—run and come
- कत् (*kat*)—when
- वाहः (*vāhaḥ*)—the Soma
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—is turned toward us
- मनीषा (*manīṣā*)—the intelligence that praises you
- मा (*mā*)—me
- उप (*upa*)—when will it come and join
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आ (*ā*)—having propitiated
- अन्नैः (*annaiḥ*)—together with foods
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—wealth (when)
- उपमं (*upamaṃ*)—near to us
- शक्यां (*śakyāṃ*)—we shall be able to obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, what sort of exhilaration is satisfying to you? You, who are of great power, run to the door of the sacrificial house and to the praises. When will the Soma be turned toward us? When will the intelligence that praises you come and join me? When shall we be able to obtain to our side, having propitiated you, wealth together with foods?

##### English translation
What sort of exhilaration, Indra, is agreeable to you? You who are powerful hasten to the doors (of the sacrificial chamber) to our praises : when will the Soma be present ? (when will) intelligence (come) to me ? when, having propitiated you, may I acquire wealth and food ?

> शेषः । कया धिया केन कर्मणा नन्नेत्यनस्मांस्तावतत्त्वदृशान्यरसे । करिष्यसि ।
> कत् कदा नोऽस्मान्त्यागन् । आगमिष्यसि । सत्यः । अनवद्य इत्यर्थः । मित्रो न सखेव
> तथा । हे उरुगाय बहुकीर्त इंद्र त्वं भृत्यै भरणाय पोषणाय भवसीति
> शेषः । यद्यदा समस्यास्मदादिकस्य सर्वस्य जगतोऽन्ने जगत्स्थितिनिमित्त आहारे
> मनीषा अन्नाभिलक्षणा बुद्धयोऽसन् भवेयुः । तदा सर्वस्य पोषणाय त्वं
> भवसीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when will you eat our oblation-food (the word द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*) is explained as the oblation, our food; "having eaten" is supplied)? By what rite will you make us, the worshippers, like yourself (त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*))? When will you come to us? You are true (सत्यः (*satyaḥ*)), faultless, like a friend. O widely renowned Indra, you are there for the nourishment and support of all. When the minds (मनीषाः (*manīṣāḥ*)) of the whole world, ours and others, are directed towards food, the means of the world's continuance, then you exist for the nourishment of all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- कदु (*kadu*)—when
- द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*)—having eaten the oblation
- कया धिया (*kayā dhiyā*)—by what kind of rite
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—us, the sacrificers
- त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*)—equal to you
- करसे (*karase*)—will you make
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- कत् (*kat*)—when
- आगन् (*āgan*)—will you come
- उरुगाय (*urugāya*)—O Indra, praised in many ways
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- समस्यॆ (*samasyè*)—of the entire world
- अन्ने (*anne*)—for the sake of food
- मनीषाः (*manīṣāḥ*)—our praises
- आसन् (*āsan*)—approach you, then
- सत्यः (*satyaḥ*)—pure
- मित्रो न (*mitro na*)—like a friend
- भृत्यै (*bhṛtyai*)—you are ready for the nourishment of all

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when, having eaten the oblation, and by what kind of rite will you make us, the sacrificers, equal to yourself? When will you come to us? O Indra, praised in many ways, when our praises approach you for the sake of the food of the whole world, then, like a pure friend, you are ready for the nourishment of all.

### Printed p. 778

##### English translation
When, Indra, (having partaken of) our oblation, and by what sacred rite, will you render men resembling you? when will you bring them to us? you, who are widely renowned, are to us like a true friend, (attentive) for our support, when the minds of all were (anxious) for food.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रेर॑य॒ सूरो॒ अर्थं॒ न पा॒रं ये अ॑स्य॒ कामं॑ जनि॒धा इ॑व॒  
> ग्मन् ।  
> गिर॑श्च॒ ये ते॑ तुविजात पू॒र्विर्नर॑ इंद्र प्रति॒शिक्षं॒त्यन्नैः॑ ॥५॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । ईरय । सूरः । अर्थं । न । पारं । ये । अस्य । कामं । जनिधाः इव । ग्मन् ।  
> गिरः । च । ये । ते । तुविजात । पूर्वि । नरः । इंद्र । प्रतिशिक्षंति । आन्नैः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूरः सूर्योऽर्थं न यथार्तारं गंतारं योगिनमनुगृह्णन् पारं
> संसारस्यांतमपवर्गं गमयति तथा हे इंद्र त्वं यजमानान्संसारस्यांतं
> प्रेरय । गमय। येऽस्मदादयो यजमाना अस्य तवेंद्रस्य कामं सोमपाने
> च्छां ग्मन । गमिरत्र विपूर्वोऽंतर्भावितण्यर्थश्च द्रष्टव्यः । विगमयंति महता
> सोमपानेनापनयंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । जनिधा इव जनीनां जायानां संभोगकाले शय्यासु धारयितारः पतयो यथा प्रभूतसंभोगप्रदानेन मैथुनेच्छामपनयंति तद्वत् । किंच नरो नेतारोऽस्मदादयो ये यजमाना हे तुविजात
> बहुरूप । रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव । ऋ. सं. ६-४७-१८ । इति वचनात् ।
> सर्वात्मन्निंद्र ते तुभ्यं पूर्वीरनादिकालप्रवृत्ता गिरश्च स्तुतिलक्षणा वाचश्चान्नॆ
> पुरोडाशादिहविभिः सह प्रतिशिक्षंति प्रतिकालं प्रयच्छंति तानस्मदीयान्यजमानान्सारं
> गमयेति पूर्वेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As the sun (सूरः (*sūraḥ*)), favouring the traveller, the yogin, takes him across to the far shore (पारं (*pāraṃ*)), the end of saṃsāra, liberation, so, O Indra, send the sacrificers to the end of saṃsāra. Those sacrificers, we and others, who fulfil (ग्मन् (*gman*)) this Indra's desire for Soma-drinking — the verb गमि (*gami*) is to be understood here with the prefix vi and a causative sense: they remove it by great Soma-drinking. The example: like जनिधा इव (*janidhā iva*), husbands who hold their wives on the bed at the time of union and remove their desire for intercourse by giving abundant enjoyment. Further, the leaders (नरः (*naraḥ*)), we and others, the sacrificers, O तुविजात (*tuvijāta*), multiform one — by the statement रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव । ऋ. सं. ६-४७-१८ । (*rūpaṃrūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva | ṛ. saṃ. 6-47-18 |*) — O Indra, soul of all, offer to you in every season the ancient (beginningless) praises, speeches of eulogy, together with food-oblations such as the cake: bring those our sacrificers across; this connects with the first part.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जनिधा इव (*janidhā iva*)—as husbands fulfil their wives' wishes
- ये (*ye*)—which sacrificers
- अस्य (*asya*)—your
- कामं (*kāmaṃ*)—desire for Soma-drinking
- ग्मन् (*gman*)—fulfil; those sacrificers
- सूरः अर्थं न (*sūraḥ arthaṃ na*)—as the sun takes yogins across saṃsāra
- पारं (*pāraṃ*)—to the far shore of saṃsāra
- प्रेरय (*preraya*)—bring
- तुविजात (*tuvijāta*)—born in many kinds of form
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—addressing you
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the leaders
- ये (*ye*)—which sacrificers
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—handed down from of old
- गिरः च (*giraḥ ca*)—praises
- अन्नॆ: (*annè:*)—with oblations
- प्रतिशिक्षंति (*pratiśikṣaṃti*)—offer; carry those across saṃsāra

### Printed p. 779

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, those sacrificers who fulfil your desire for Soma-drinking as husbands fulfil their wives' wishes — as the sun takes yogins across saṃsāra, so you also bring them to the farther shore of saṃsāra. O Indra, born in many forms, those sacrificers, leaders, who offer to you the praises handed down from of old with oblations — carry them across saṃsāra.

##### English translation
As the sun (brings) the ascetic, you bring to the end (of existence) (your worshippers), who satisfy your desire (for the Soma), as husbands (the desire of their wives); and who (being) leaders of rites, multiform Indra, offer to you ancient praises with (sacrificial) viands.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मात्रे॒ नु ते॒ सुमि॑ते इंद्र पू॒र्वी द्यौर्म॒ज्मना॑ पृथि॒वी  ॑
> काव्येन ।  
> वरा॑य ते घृ॒तवं॑तः सु॒तासः॒ स्वाद्म॑न्भवंतु पी॒तये॒  ॑
> मधूनि ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 780

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मात्रेऽइति । नु । ते । सुमिते इति सुमिते । इंद्र । पूर्वि इति । द्यौः । मज्मना ।  
> पृथिवी । काव्येन ।  
> वराय । ते । धृतवंतः ! सुतासः । स्वाद्मन् । भवंतु । पीतये । मधूनि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव स्वभूतेन मज्जना शत्रोणां मज्जकेन काव्येन कर्मणा
> द्याः पृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्या नु क्षिप्रं सुमिते । निर्मिते । कीदृश्या मात्रे निर्मात्र्यौ
> पूर्वी पूर्व्य महत्यौ । यस्मादीदृशेन महत्वेन युक्तः तस्माद्कृतवंतोऽग्निमुखत्वात् त्वां क्षरंतो दीप्तिमंतो वा सुसंस्कृतत्वात् यद्वाज्यासंयुक्ताः
> सुतासोऽभिषुताः सोमा वराय श्रेष्ठाय तुभ्यमिंद्राय स्वादन् भवंतु ।
> आस्वादिताः संतु । किमर्थं । पीतये पानाय । मधूनि मधुररसात्मकानि पुरोडाशादीन्न्यन्नानि हवींषि भक्षणार्थं दत्तानि भवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, by your own crushing action (मज्मना (*majmanā*), that which crushes enemies), your poetic deed (काव्येन (*kāvyena*)), heaven and earth, the two measurers, great and ancient (पूर्वी (*pūrvī*)), have quickly been fashioned (सुमिते (*sumite*)). Since you possess such greatness, the Soma-pressings (सुतासः (*sutāsaḥ*)), either ghee-bearing because they are well prepared with the fire as their mouth, or mixed with ghee, shining, be sweet (स्वाद्मन् भवंतु (*svādman bhavaṃtu*)) to you, the most excellent, for drinking. And may sweet (मधूनि (*madhūni*)) oblations, cakes and other foods of sweet flavour, be given to be eaten.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- मज्मना (*majmanā*)—endowed with power
- काव्येन (*kāvyena*)—by the deed
- मात्रे (*mātre*)—the makers of the world
- पूर्वी (*pūrvī*)—possessing great form
- द्यौः पृथिवी (*dyauḥ pṛthivī*)—heaven and earth, both
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- सुमिते (*sumite*)—have been fashioned
- घृतवंतः (*ghṛtavaṃtaḥ*)—mixed with ghee
- सुतासः (*sutāsaḥ*)—pressed Soma juices
- वराय ते (*varāya te*)—to you, the most excellent
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—for drinking
- स्वाद्मन् भवंतु (*svādman bhavaṃtu*)—let them be offered, tasty
- मधूनि (*madhūni*)—let sweet oblations also be offered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, by your powerful deed heaven and earth, the makers of the world and of great form, have quickly been fashioned. May the Soma juices, mixed with ghee and pressed, be offered tasty to you, the most excellent, for drinking. May sweet oblations also be offered.

##### English translation
By your overwhelming energy, Indra, the vast heaven and earth, the measurers (of all), have been quickly constructed: may the Soma-

### Printed p. 781
libations mixed wiht ghee be acceptable to (you) who are most excellent : (may the oblations be) sweet for your drinking.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ मध्यो॑ अस्मा असिच॒न्नम॑त्र॒मिंद्रा॑य पू॒र्णं स हि स॒त्यरा॑धाः ।  
> स वा॑वृधे॒ वरि॑म॒न्ना पृ॑थि॒व्या अ॒भि क्रत्वा॒ नर्यः॒ पौंस्यै॑श्च ॥७॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । मध्यः । अस्मै । असिचन् । अमत्रं । इंद्राय ! पूर्णं । सः । हि । सत्यराधाः ।  
> सः । ववृधे । वरिमन् । आ । पृथिव्याः । अभि । क्रत्वा । नर्यः । पौंस्यैः । च ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आस्मा इंद्रायेंद्रार्थं मध्वो मधुररसस्य सोमस्य पूर्णममत्रं
> ग्रहचमसादिकं पात्रमासिचन् । अभिमुख्येन स्थित्वा परया भक्त्यास्मदीया ऋत्विजः
> सिक्तवंतः । अग्नौ प्रक्षिप्तवंतः । हि यस्मात्कारणात्स इंद्रः सत्यराधाः सत्यधनः । यजमानेभ्यो दातव्यत्वेनाविसंवादिधन इत्यर्थः। तस्मादसिचन्निति संबंधः। अग्नावासिकेन
> तेन पात्रेण तृप्तः स इंद्रः पृथिव्या अंतरिक्षस्य वरिमन्नतिशयेन विस्तीर्णे स्थान
> आगत्याभि ववृधे। अभिवर्धते। कीदृश इंद्रः। नर्यो नृभ्यो हितः । क्रत्वा वृत्रवधादिकर्मणा प्रज्ञानेन वा पौंस्यैश्च युक्त इति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Our priests, standing before him with supreme devotion, have poured (*āsican*), that is, cast into the fire, for this Indra a vessel (अमत्रं (*amatraṃ*): a cup such as the graha or camasa) full of sweet Soma. Because that Indra is सत्यराधाः (*satyarādhāḥ*), of true wealth — wealth that, as something to be given to the sacrificers, does not fail — therefore they poured; this is the connection. Satisfied by that vessel poured into the fire, Indra comes to the exceedingly wide space of the earth, that is, the atmosphere (पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)), and grows (ववृधे (*vavṛdhe*)). What kind of Indra? नर्यः (*naryaḥ*), beneficial to men, endowed with his act (क्रत्वा (*kratvā*): Vṛtra-slaying and other deeds, or wisdom) and with manly powers (पौंस्यैः (*pauṃsyaiḥ*)); "endowed" is supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हि (*hi*)—by what power
- सः (*saḥ*)—Indra
- सत्यराधाः (*satyarādhāḥ*)—because he possesses true wealth
- अस्मै इंद्राय (*asmai iṃdrāya*)—for this Indra
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—with sweet Soma juice
- पूर्णं (*pūrṇaṃ*)—filled
- अमत्रं (*amatraṃ*)—the vessel
- असिचन् (*asican*)—they offer
- नरैः (*naraiḥ*)—beneficial to men
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—and by excellent action
- पौंसैश्च (*pauṃsaiśca*)—and by valour
- सः (*saḥ*)—Indra, so endowed
- आ पृथिव्याः (*ā pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- वरिमन् (*variman*)—in the wide region
- अभि ववृधे (*abhi vavṛdhe*)—grows

### Printed p. 782

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

By the power through which Indra is possessor of true wealth, therefore they offer to this Indra a vessel full of sweet Soma juice. Indra, beneficial to men and endowed with excellent action and valour, grows in the wide region of the atmosphere.

##### English translation
(The worshipper) have poured out the vessel full of the sweet (Soma) (into the fire) for that Indra, for he is true (to his promises) of wealth : Indra, the friend of man, (distinguished) by his actions, and his prowess, is magnified throughout the expanse of the firmament.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व्या॑न॒ळिंद्रः॒ पृत॑नाः॒ स्तोजा॒ आस्मै॑ यतंते स॒ख्याय॑ पू॒र्वीः।  
> आ स्मा॒ रथं॒ न पृत॑नासु तिष्ठ॒यं भ॒द्रया॑ सुम॒त्या चो॒दया॑से ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । आनट् । इंद्रः । पृतनाः ! सुओजाः । आ । अस्मै । यतंते । सख्याय । पूर्वीः ।  
> आ । स्म । रथं । न । पृतनासु । तिष्ठ । यं । भद्रया । सुमत्या । चोदयासे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्टोजा शोभनबल इंद्रः पृतनाः शत्रुसेना व्यानट् । व्याप्तोति । स इंद्रः
> संग्रामेषु केनाप्यप्रतिहन्यमानः सङ्ज्यत्रूञ्चयतीत्यर्थः । किंच पूर्वीः । अत्र
> पूर्वशब्द उत्कृष्टवाची । उत्कृष्टाः शत्रुसेना अप्रभवंत्यः सत्योऽस्मा अस्येंद्रस्य
> सख्याय संधित्वलक्षणाय सखित्वाया यतंते । संधिं कर्तुमिच्छंतीत्यर्थः ।
> अपरोऽर्धर्चः प्रत्यक्षकृतत्वाद्दिन्नं वाक्यं । हे इंद्र त्वं यं स्वीयं रथं भद्रया
> कल्याण्या सुमत्या शोभनया परानुग्रहया बुद्ध्या चोदयासे यज्ञानृति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, of fine strength, pervades (व्यानट् (*vyānaṭ*)) the enemy armies (पृतनाः (*pṛtanāḥ*)): unopposed by anyone in battles he conquers the enemies. Further पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*): here the word पूर्व (*pūrva*) means excellent; the excellent enemy armies, though powerless, strive (यतंते (*yataṃte*)) for friendship with this Indra, that is, for alliance; they wish to make peace. The latter half of the verse is a separate sentence, being addressed directly: O Indra, the chariot of your own which you drive with auspicious, fine, others-favouring thought, in the sacrifices ….

### Printed p. 783

> प्रेरयसि तं रथमस्मद्यज्ञं प्रत्यागंतं महतादरेणा तिष्ठ । आरोह । तत्रदृष्टांतः ।
> पृतनासु संग्रामेषु रथं न यथा स्वरथं महतादरेणातिष्ठसि तद्वत् । स्मेति
> पदपूरणः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the gloss of the second half-verse. Indra is told to mount, with great respect, the chariot that he drives to come back to our sacrifice. The example is that in battles he mounts his own chariot with great respect, and he is asked to do the same here. The word स्मेति (*smeti*) is only a filler of the line.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वोजाः (*svojāḥ*)—one of excellent valour
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- पृतनाः (*pṛtanāḥ*)—the enemy armies
- व्यानट् (*vyānaṭ*)—pervades
- पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*)—the excellent enemy armies
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—with this Indra
- सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)—for a treaty
- आ यतंते (*ā yataṃte*)—strive
- (O Indra) पृतनासु (*pṛtanāsu*)—in battles
- रथं न (*rathaṃ na*)—as you mount your excellent chariot
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which chariot
- भद्रया (*bhadrayā*)—with that which is auspicious
- सुमत्या (*sumatyā*)—with a mind that is gracious
- चोदयासे (*codayāse*)—you drive
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—that same chariot
- आ तिष्ठ (*ā tiṣṭha*)—mount, to come to our sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, of excellent valour, pervades the enemy armies. The excellent enemy armies strive with this Indra for a treaty. O Indra, mount, to come to our sacrifice, that same chariot which you drive with an auspicious and gracious mind, just as you mount your excellent chariot in battles.

##### English translation
The powerful Indra reaches the hosts (of the enemy), the mightiest (hosts) exert themselves to obtain his friendship: ascend, Indra, that chariot which you direct with favourable intent (to our sacrifice), as a chariot (which you mount) against the armies (of the foe).

## Sūkta 30 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Pīṭhike**

Introduction. For this sūkta and the next five sūktas the seer is Kavaṣa, son of Ilūṣa. Because he was born of a Śūdra serving-woman, he was a Śūdra and the son of a serving-woman, and the Brāhmaṇas, the ṛṣis and others, did not keep social dealings with him. He had no entry into the sacrificial hall. There is an old story about this in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and in the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa. We set it out here.

### Printed p. 784
Account in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa

यषयो वै सरस्वत्यां सत्रमासत ते कवषमैलूषं सोमादनयन्दास्याः पुत्रः कितवोऽब्राह्मणः कथं नो मध्येऽदीक्षिष्टेति तं बहिर्धन्वोदवहन्नतैनं पिपासा हंतु सरस्वत्या उदकं मा पादिति स बहिर्धन्वोदूह्रळः पिपासया वित्त एतदपोनप्रीयमपश्यत्प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे गातुरेत्विति तॆनापां प्रियं धामोपागच्छत्तमापोऽनूदायंस्तं सरस्वती समंतं पर्यधावत् ॥ (*yaṣayo vai sarasvatyāṃ satramāsata te kavaṣamailūṣaṃ somādanayandāsyāḥ putraḥ kitavo 'brāhmaṇaḥ kathaṃ no madhye 'dīkṣiṣṭeti taṃ bahirdhanvodavahannatainaṃ pipāsā haṃtu sarasvatyā udakaṃ mā pāditi sa bahirdhanvodūhraḷaḥ pipāsayā vitta etadaponaprīyamapaśyatpra devatrā brahmaṇe gāturetviti tènāpāṃ priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchattamāpo 'nūdāyaṃstaṃ sarasvatī samaṃtaṃ paryadhāvat ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 8-19) **NOTE**

In former times some ṛṣis, the Bhṛgus, Aṅgirases and others, were performing a sattra sacrifice on the bank of the river Sarasvatī. A sattra is a special sacrifice lasting not fewer than twelve days, thirteen, fourteen or more. In a sacrifice of this kind there are many sacrificers; that is, many join together to perform it. Many ṛṣis, the Bhṛgus, Aṅgirases and others, had gathered at that sacrificial altar. In their midst sat one Kavaṣa, son of Ilūṣa. He was a Śūdra by birth and the son of a serving-woman. When the ṛṣis saw him sitting down among them, they said: "What is this? That this Kavaṣa, son of a serving-woman and a gambler, should come here and sit in our midst! He is not a Brāhmaṇa. Does one who is not a Brāhmaṇa come and sit among ṛṣis rich in good conduct and learn the secrets of sacrifices and of their rules and ordinances? This is against the world." So saying, they drove Kavaṣa by force out of the sacrificial hall. Thinking also that this sinful man was not fit to drink the water of the holy river Sarasvatī, they forcibly took him to a sandy desert, without water or shade, a long way from the Sarasvatī, and left him there, saying: "Let him die there of thirst." In that sandy land without water or shade Kavaṣa, worn out and limp with thirst, was suffering, when the sūkta प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे (*pra devatrā brahmaṇe*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-30) appeared to him. He then recited that mantra silently, and by the grace of the deities presiding over the waters a region abounding in water appeared to him. As soon as he went there, the deities of the waters and the river Sarasvatī welcomed him with a gracious look and surrounded him on all sides with the flowing water.

तस्माद्दाप्येतर्हि परिसरकमित्याचक्षते यदेनं सरस्वती समंतं परिससार (*tasmāddāpyetarhi parisarakamityācakṣate yadenaṃ sarasvatī samaṃtaṃ parisasāra*)

Those learned in the Purāṇas say that the region which the river Sarasvatī encircled with her flood around Kavaṣa is an excellent special holy place called Parisaraka. The meaning is that, because Sarasvatī flowed round him (एनं परिससार (*enaṃ parisasāra*)), the name Parisaraka became a name fitting the place.

### Printed p. 785
ते ना ऋषयोऽब्रुवन्विदुर्वा इमं देवा उपेमं ह्वयामहा इति तथेति तमुपाह्वयंत तमुहूय्यतदपोनप्रीयमकुर्वत प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे गातुरेत्त्विति तेनापां प्रियं धामोपागच्छन्नुपदेवानां । स (*te nā ṛṣayo 'bruvanvidurvā imaṃ devā upemaṃ hvayāmahā iti tatheti tamupāhvayaṃta tamuhūyyatadaponaprīyamakurvata pra devatrā brahmaṇe gāturettviti tenāpāṃ priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchannupadevānāṃ | sa*)

The ṛṣis saw that the river Sarasvatī had encircled Kavaṣa with her flood and favoured him, and said to one another: "This Kavaṣa has become worthy of the grace of the deities of the waters, Sarasvatī and the rest. None of a gambler's faults seem to be in him. Let us call him back to come to us." Having decided so, they called Kavaṣa back. They then completed, with all its parts, the sūkta प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे (*pra devatrā brahmaṇe*) seen by him and the rite called Aponaprīya, and won the dear abode, that is, the grace, of the deities of the waters and of the other deities.

उपापां प्रियं धाम गच्छत्युप देवानां जयति परमं लोकं य एवं वेद यश्चैवं विद्वानेतदपोनस्त्रीयं कुरुते । (*upāpāṃ priyaṃ dhāma gacchatyupa devānāṃ jayati paramaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda yaścaivaṃ vidvānetadaponastrīyaṃ kurute |*) (Ai. Brā. 8-19) **NOTE**

The man who knows the matters stated above and completes with all its parts the rite called Aponaprīya becomes worthy of the grace of the deities and obtains the highest world.

The account of Kavaṣa given in the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa we set out here in brief.

(Account in the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa)

माध्यमाः सरस्वत्यां सत्रमासत तद्धापि कवषो मध्यॆ निषसाद । तं हेम उपोदुद्वास्या वै त्वं पुत्रोऽसि न वयं त्वया सह भक्षयिष्याम इति सह क्रुद्धः प्रद्रवन्त्सरस्वतीमेतेन सूक्तेन तुष्वाव । तं हेयमन्वेयाय त उ हेमे निरागा इव मेनिरे तं हान्यावृत्योचुर्यषे नमस्ते अस्तु मा नो हिंसीत्वं वै नः श्रेष्ठोऽसि यं त्वेयमन्वेतीति। तं ह यज्ञपयां चक्रुस्तस्य ह क्रोधं विनिन्युः । स एष कवषस्यैष महिमा सूक्तस्य चानुवेदिता ॥ (*mādhyamāḥ sarasvatyāṃ satramāsata taddhāpi kavaṣo madhyè niṣasāda | taṃ hema upodudvāsyā vai tvaṃ putro 'si na vayaṃ tvayā saha bhakṣayiṣyāma iti saha kruddhaḥ pradravantsarasvatīmetena sūktena tuṣvāva | taṃ heyamanveyāya ta u heme nirāgā iva menire taṃ hānyāvṛtyocuryaṣe namaste astu mā no hiṃsītvaṃ vai naḥ śreṣṭho 'si yaṃ tveyamanvetīti| taṃ ha yajñapayāṃ cakrustasya ha krodhaṃ vininyuḥ | sa eṣa kavaṣasyaiṣa mahimā sūktasya cānuveditā ‖*) (Kau. Brā. 12-3) **NOTE**

In former times ṛṣis called Mādhyamas were performing a sattra sacrifice on the bank of the river Sarasvatī. Here *Mādhyamas* means the seers of the sūktas in the seven middle maṇḍalas of the Ṛgveda (excluding the first maṇḍala and the last, 9th and 10th, of the ten), namely the ṛṣis Gṛtsamada, Viśvāmitra, Vāmadeva, Atri, Bharadvāja, Vasiṣṭha, and the ṛṣis of their lines. While these ṛṣis were performing the sacrifice on the bank of the Sarasvatī, one Kavaṣa came and sat among them

### Printed p. 786
. Seeing him, the ṛṣis rebuked him in anger: "O Kavaṣa, you are the son of a serving-woman, not a Brāhmaṇa. We shall neither eat nor drink sitting with you. Therefore leave this place and go." Hearing this, Kavaṣa left the place in anger, ran to the river Sarasvatī, praised that deity with this sūkta प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे (*pra devatrā brahmaṇe*) and gained her grace. Sarasvatī, pleased with his praise, followed him wherever he went. Seeing this, the ṛṣis thought: "He is not faulty; let us call him back." They went to him and said: "O Kavaṣa, here is our homage to you. You are the best among us ṛṣis. Forgive the wrong we have done; do not harm us. The river Sarasvatī too is following you. There is no fault in you." Entreating him in many ways, they made him the leader in their sacrifice and appeased his anger. This is the greatness of the ṛṣi Kavaṣa, and it is by this ṛṣi that this sūkta प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे (*pra devatrā brahmaṇe*) was seen and became well known.

As to how this sūkta appeared to the ṛṣi Kavaṣa, the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa itself says:

तद्ध स्म पुरा यज्ञमुहो रक्षांसि तीर्थेष्टपो गोपायंति । तदेकेऽपोऽच्छ जग्मुस्तत एव तान् सर्वान् जघ्नुस्त एव तत् कवषः सूक्तमपश्यत्पंचदशर्चं प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे गातुरेश्विति तदन्वब्रवीत्तेन यज्ञमुहो रक्षांसि तीर्थेभ्योपाहन् ॥ (*taddha sma purā yajñamuho rakṣāṃsi tīrtheṣṭapo gopāyaṃti | tadeke 'po 'ccha jagmustata eva tān sarvān jaghnusta eva tat kavaṣaḥ sūktamapaśyatpaṃcadaśarcaṃ pra devatrā brahmaṇe gātureśviti tadanvabravīttena yajñamuho rakṣāṃsi tīrthebhyopāhan ‖*)

In former times the rākṣasas, creating obstacles to sacrifices and the like, killed the people who went to the rivers to bathe. Kavaṣa, a seer of mantras, saw this sūkta with his eye of knowledge and recited it. By reciting that mantra he drove away the rākṣasas who were near the river and destroyed them. So it is said.

The rite called Aponaprīya
With the ṛks of this sūkta the sacrificial rite called Aponaprīya is performed. Aponaprīya means uniting, according to rule and with mantras, the water in the vessel called Vasatīvarī with the water in another vessel called Ekadhanā.

After the Hotṛ has recited the Prātaranuvāka mantras, the Adhvaryu directs the Hotṛ with the Praiṣa mantra परिहितेऽप इष्य होतः (*parihite 'pa iṣya hotaḥ*). In reply the Hotṛ says अपोनप्रीया अन्वाह (*aponaprīyā anvāha*). Then the Adhvaryu, by Praiṣa mantras,

### Printed p. 787
tells the Camasādhvaryu, the Maitrāvaruṇa and those who hold the Ekadhanā vessel to come. He directs the Neṣṭṛ to bring the sacrificer's wife. He says: "O Āgnīdhra, place the Hotṛ's camasa and the Vasatīvarī jar facing each other in the Cātvāla." Then the Camasādhvaryu brings the camasa. Those who hold the Ekadhanā vessel bring three vessels. The Adhvaryu then puts one blade of darbha in each of the three vessels and purifies them. The Neṣṭṛ brings the sacrificer's wife. She holds a vessel in her hand. Then the Adhvaryu puts one blade of kuśa in each of the vessels, recites the mantra देवीरापः (*devīrāpaḥ*), pours ghee to fill four sruvas and offers the oblation. Then the Adhvaryu brings the camasas of the Hotṛ and the Maitrāvaruṇa, together with the water of the Ekadhanā vessel, to the Vasatīvarī jar, and pours its water into the Hotṛ's camasa vessel, from that into the Maitrāvaruṇa's vessel, and again from the Maitrāvaruṇa's vessel into the Hotṛ's camasa. As the water is poured into the Hotṛ's camasa, the Hotṛ addresses the Adhvaryu and asks three times अवेरापोऽध्वर्या ३ उ (*averāpo 'dhvaryā 3 u*). The Adhvaryu replies उतेमनन्नमुः (*utemanannamuḥ*) (उतेमाः पश्य (*utemāḥ paśya*)). Then the Hotṛ performs the rising-up (pratyutthāpana) toward those waters.

The procedure of this rite called Aponaprīya is stated separately in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā the order to be followed by the Adhvaryu is stated, and in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa the mantras to be recited by the Hotṛ. Since the mantras to be recited by the Hotṛ belong to the Ṛgveda, we explain here only the order given in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.

Explanation of the rite called Aponaprīya
(as in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa)
After the recitation of the Prātaranuvāka, as soon as the Adhvaryu directs the Hotṛ with the Praiṣa mantra, the Hotṛ recites the mantras belonging to the Aponaprīya. In this recitation an order is to be followed. It is stated here:

तत्संततमनुब्रूयात् । संततवर्षीह प्रजाभ्यः पर्जन्या भवति यत्रैवं विद्वानेतत्संततमन्वाह यदवग्राहमनुब्रूयाज्जिमूतवर्षीह प्रजाभ्यः पर्जन्यः स्यात्तस्मात्संततमेवानूच्यं । तस्य त्रिः प्रथमां संततमन्वाह तेनैव तत्सर्वं संततमनूक्तं भवति ॥ (*tatsaṃtatamanubrūyāt | saṃtatavarṣīha prajābhyaḥ parjanyā bhavati yatraivaṃ vidvānetatsaṃtatamanvāha yadavagrāhamanubrūyājjimūtavarṣīha prajābhyaḥ parjanyaḥ syāttasmātsaṃtatamevānūcyaṃ | tasya triḥ prathamāṃ saṃtatamanvāha tenaiva tatsarvaṃ saṃtatamanūktaṃ bhavati ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 8 19)

When the mantras of the sūkta प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे (*pra devatrā brahmaṇe*) that are to be recited in this rite called Aponaprīya are recited, they must be recited in one continuous stream, without stopping anywhere in the middle. If recited so,

### Printed p. 788
the god Parjanya will rain continuously for the benefit of the people. If instead the ṛks are recited with a stop at the pādas, or at half-ṛks, or at the ends of the ṛks, Parjanya will rain on mountains and the like, of use to no one, and will not rain on plants and the like. Therefore this sūkta must be recited in one stream to the end, without stopping anywhere in the middle. But is it not impossible to recite all the ṛks of this sūkta without stopping in the middle? In place of that, if the first ṛk of this sūkta is recited three times without the least stop, it is as if the sūkta itself had been recited without a stop.

ता एता नवानंतरायमन्वाह । हिनोता नो अध्वरं देवयज्येति दशमीं । आवर्वृततीरध नु द्विधारा इत्यावृत्तास्वेकधनासु । (*tā etā navānaṃtarāyamanvāha | hinotā no adhvaraṃ devayajyeti daśamīṃ | āvarvṛtatīradha nu dvidhārā ityāvṛttāsvekadhanāsu |*) (Ai. Brā. 8-20)

There is a special order in reciting the mantras of the sūkta प्रदेवत्रा (*pradevatrā*). Beginning with the first ṛk, प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे (*pra devatrā brahmaṇe*), one recites to the end of the ninth ṛk, and then recites the 11th ṛk, हिनोता नो अध्वरं (*hinotā no adhvaraṃ*) (10-30-11). Then one must recite the 10th ṛk, आवर्वृततीरध (*āvarvṛtatīradha*). **NOTE**

Here it is necessary to explain the order of performance in detail. On the Sutyā-day-before, that is, the day before the pressing of the Soma, after the Agnīṣomīya ceremony the waters called Vasatīvarī must be established on the sacrificial altar for use at the time of the Soma pressing. After midnight has passed, one gives up sleep and rises, touches the Āgnīdhra, Dhiṣṇya fires and the rest with the proper mantras, sets out the vessels needed for the Soma pressing, and directs the Hotṛ with the Praiṣa mantra to recite the Prātaranuvāka mantras. After the recitation of the Prātaranuvāka, one offers an oblation with the mantra शृणोत्वग्निः (*śṛṇotvagniḥ*), and, as the men go to fetch water in the Ekadhanā vessels, one directs the Hotṛ, for the recitation of the Aponaprīya sūkta, with the Praiṣa mantra एकधना अप आनय (*ekadhanā apa ānaya*). All these steps are described in the Adhvaryu's procedure. In this matter the great ṛṣi Āpastamba has laid down the course of action in sūtra sentences such as यित्राभिजानात्यभूदुषा (*yitrābhijānātyabhūduṣā*) and so on. The great ṛṣi Āśvalāyana too, regarding the recitation of the mantras and the rest belonging to the Hotṛ, has laid down the order in sentences such as परिहितेऽप इष्ट होतः (*parihite 'pa iṣṭa hotaḥ*). After the recitation of the ten ṛks of the sūkta (9-11), when the men who went to fetch water in the Ekadhanā vessels fill their vessels and return from the river, the Hotṛ recites the tenth ṛk of the sūkta, आवर्वृतशरीरध (*āvarvṛtaśarīradha*) (10-30-10).

### Printed p. 789
The first lines complete the Āśvalāyana rule quoted before: प्रति यदापो अदृश्रमायतीरिति प्रतिदृश्यमानासु । आ धेनवः पयसा तूर्णर्था इत्युपायतीषु । समन्या यंत्युप यंत्यन्या इति समायतीषु । (*prati yadāpo adṛśramāyatīriti pratidṛśyamānāsu | ā dhenavaḥ payasā tūrṇarthā ityupāyatīṣu | samanyā yaṃtyupa yaṃtyanyā iti samāyatīṣu |*)

When the men have filled the ekadhanā vessels with water and are coming back from the river bank, the Hotṛ sees them carrying the water-filled ekadhanā vessels and recites the mantra Prati yadāpaḥ (10-30-13). He recites the mantra Ā dhenavaḥ payasā (5.43-3) when the waters in those ekadhanā vessels reach the Cātvāla (a pit or hollow in the sacrificial ground). **NOTE**

An explanation is necessary here. As soon as the Adhvaryu has directed, by the Praiṣa mantra उन्नेतर्होतृचमसेन वसतीवरीभिश्व चात्वालं प्रत्यास्व (*unnetarhotṛcamasena vasatīvarībhiśva cātvālaṃ pratyāsva*), the priest called Unnetṛ carries to the neighbourhood of the Cātvāla the water that was placed the day before in the vessel called vasatīvarī, in the Hotṛ's cup (camasa). Then, according to the Praiṣa mantra मैत्रावरुणस्य चमसाध्वर्यवाद्रव (*maitrāvaruṇasya camasādhvaryavādrava*), the Camasādhvaryu, the attendant of the priest Maitrāvaruṇa, brings the Maitrāvaruṇa cup also to the Cātvāla. Here "the Hotṛ's cup" is to be understood as the water in the vasatīvarī vessel, and "the Maitrāvaruṇa cup" as the water in the ekadhanā vessels. Then the Adhvaryu pours the waters of the ekadhanā vessels in the Maitrāvaruṇa cups into the Hotṛ's cup that holds the vasatīvarī water, mixing one with the other. While he mixes, the Hotṛ recites the Ṛk Samanyā yantyupa (2.35-3). The sage Āpastamba has explained this clearly in the sūtra beginning होतृ चमसेन वसतीवरीभ्यो (*hotṛ camasena vasatīvarībhyo*).

There is an ancient story about these Ṛks, which is given here.

आपो वा अस्पर्धंत वयं पूर्वं यज्ञं वक्ष्यामो वयमिति याश्चेमाः पूर्वेद्युर्वसतीवर्योगृह्यंते याश्च प्रातरेकधनास्ता भृगुरपश्यदापो वै स्पर्धंत इति ता एतयर्चा समज्ञपयत्समन्या यंत्युप यंत्यन्या इति ताः समजानत संजानाना हास्यापो यज्ञं वहंति य एवं वेद ॥ (*āpo vā aspardhaṃta vayaṃ pūrvaṃ yajñaṃ vakṣyāmo vayamiti yāścemāḥ pūrvedyurvasatīvaryogṛhyaṃte yāśca prātarekadhanāstā bhṛgurapaśyadāpo vai spardhaṃta iti tā etayarcā samajñapayatsamanyā yaṃtyupa yaṃtyanyā iti tāḥ samajānata saṃjānānā hāsyāpo yajñaṃ vahaṃti ya evaṃ veda ‖*)

The water brought the day before the Soma-pressing is stored in the vessel called vasatīvarī. On the very day of the pressing, that is, in the morning of that day, freshly drawn water from the river is brought and placed in the vessels called ekadhanā. The waters in these two kinds of vessels once competed with one another, with jealousy, over the carrying out of the sacrifice. That is, the vasatīvarī waters (or the deities presiding over water) said "we are able to carry out the sacrifice", and the waters in the ekadhanā vessels said "we have greater power", and they struggled in rivalry. The sage Bhṛgu saw this

### Printed p. 790
and recited the Ṛk Samanyā yanti (2-35-3). He removed the mutual discord of the two kinds of waters, pacified them with conciliatory words and brought them to agreement. By the power of that mantra both kinds of water put their quarrels aside and began to act in harmony in carrying out the sacrifice. The sacrificer who knows this becomes able to complete his sacrificial acts without quarrel, in mutual agreement and without obstacle.

आपो न देवीरुपयंति होत्रियमिति होतृचमसे समवनीयमानास्वन्वाह वसतीवरीष्टेकधनासु च । (*āpo na devīrupayaṃti hotriyamiti hotṛcamase samavanīyamānāsvanvāha vasatīvarīṣṭekadhanāsu ca |*)

After the two kinds of water from the vasatīvarī and ekadhanā vessels have been poured into the Hotṛ's cup, the Hotṛ recites the mantra Āpo na devīrupayanti (1-83-2).

अवेरपोऽध्वर्या ३ उ इति होताध्वर्युं पृच्छति । आपो वै यज्ञोऽ विदो यज्ञा ३ मित्येव तदाह । उतेमनन्नमुरित्यध्वर्युः प्रत्याह । उतेमाः पश्येत्येव तदाह । (*averapo 'dhvaryā 3 u iti hotādhvaryuṃ pṛcchati | āpo vai yajño ' vido yajñā 3 mityeva tadāha | utemanannamurityadhvaryuḥ pratyāha | utemāḥ paśyetyeva tadāha |*)

Then the Hotṛ recites a Yajus mantra and asks the Adhvaryu: "O Adhvaryu, you have now obtained the two kinds of water, have you not?" The two kinds of water are, as said before, the waters in the vasatīvarī and ekadhanā vessels. These waters are used at the time of the Soma-pressing for carrying out the sacrifice; therefore the sacrifice is said to be of the nature of water. To that question the Adhvaryu replies: "O Hotṛ, I have obtained for the carrying out of the sacrifice the two kinds of water you asked about. Look."

तास्वध्वयो इंद्राय सोमं सोता मधुमंतं वृष्टिवनिं तीव्रांतं बहुरमध्यं वसुमते रुद्रवत आदित्यवत ऋभुमते विभुमते वाजवते बृहस्पतिवते विश्वदेव्यावते । यस्येंद्रः पीत्वा वृत्राणि जंघनत्प स जन्यानि तारिषो ३ मिति प्रत्युत्तिष्ठति ॥ (*tāsvadhvayo iṃdrāya somaṃ sotā madhumaṃtaṃ vṛṣṭivaniṃ tīvrāṃtaṃ bahuramadhyaṃ vasumate rudravata ādityavata ṛbhumate vibhumate vājavate bṛhaspativate viśvadevyāvate | yasyeṃdraḥ pītvā vṛtrāṇi jaṃghanatpa sa janyāni tāriṣo 3 miti pratyuttiṣṭhati ‖*)

Having recited this mantra, the Hotṛ must perform the rising (pratyutthāna) addressed to the deities presiding over the waters, that is, he must stand up and pray: "O Adhvaryu, with the help of the two kinds of water you have obtained, the vasatīvarī and the ekadhanā, perform the Soma-pressing, that is, crush the Soma plants, take out the juice, press it and prepare it for Indra to drink." What the Soma juice must be like: sweet, endowed with sweet juice, causing rain (vṛṣṭi), giving its fruit quickly, and accompanied by many kinds of ritual subsidiary acts. Here for the word madhumantaṃ

### Printed p. 791
the sense is that the Soma juice must be sweet like honey, or pleasant to the taste. Vṛṣṭivanim means "giving rain": Indra, satisfied by drinking this Soma, in his joy splits the clouds and makes the rain fall. Tīvrāntaṃ: the sacrifice is completed without obstacle and its fruit is obtained quickly. Bahura(la)madhyaṃ: there are many kinds of subsidiary acts in the sacrifice; from the choosing of the priests up to the completion there are many kinds of ritual acts. Therefore the intention is: prepare for Indra, by pressing it, a Soma juice with these qualities, which is the means of carrying out these many acts. This Soma juice is not for Indra alone; it is for the drinking of Indra and of the other deities who are with Indra. Who those deities are: वसुमते रुद्रवते आदित्यवते विश्वदेव्यावते । (*vasumate rudravate ādityavate viśvadevyāvate |*) That is, the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the twelve Ādityas, the three Ṛbhus called Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja, Bṛhaspati, the Viśvedevas and others. The intention is: press and prepare the Soma juice for the drinking of Indra together with these deities. Having drunk such Soma juice, Indra becomes able to destroy the enemies and the sins of the sacrificing sacrificer. The meaning of the mantra is: "O Adhvaryu, prepare such Soma juice." Having recited this mantra, and at its end the praṇava mantra Om, the Hotṛ stands up and prays.

प्रत्युत्थेया वा आपः प्रति वै श्रेयांसमायंतमुत्तिष्ठंति तस्मात्पृत्युत्थेयाः । अनु पर्यावृत्याः अनु वै श्रेयांसं पर्यावर्तंते तस्मादनु.. पर्यावृत्या अनुब्रुवतैवानुप्रपत्तव्यं । (*pratyuttheyā vā āpaḥ prati vai śreyāṃsamāyaṃtamuttiṣṭhaṃti tasmātpṛtyuttheyāḥ | anu paryāvṛtyāḥ anu vai śreyāṃsaṃ paryāvartaṃte tasmādanu.. paryāvṛtyā anubruvataivānuprapattavyaṃ |*)

One must stand up to show respect to these two kinds of water. In worldly custom, when some great person comes, that is, a teacher, an elder, a father and the like, it is the practice for pupils, sons and others to stand up to show respect. In the same way here, the priests and others must stand up to show respect to these two kinds of water, which are indispensable for the sacrificial acts worthy of worship. Not only that: when those worthy of respect move about, it is natural to follow them and honour them humbly from behind. The intention is that the same is to be done here.

ईश्वरो ह यद्यप्यन्नो यजेताथ;होतारं यशोर्तोस्तस्मादनुब्रुवतैवानुप्रपत्तव्यं । (*īśvaro ha yadyapyanno yajetātha;hotāraṃ yaśortostasmādanubruvataivānuprapattavyaṃ |*)

Even if the Hotṛ is not one who takes part in the sacrifice, if the Hotṛ who recites the mantras shows respect to these waters and follows them, fame and eminence come to him.

### Printed p. 792
Therefore those who recite the mantras must necessarily follow those waters. While following them thus, one must recite the mantra not yet recited in this rite,

अंबयो यंत्यध्वभिरित्येतामनुब्रुवन्ननु प्रपद्येत । (*aṃbayo yaṃtyadhvabhirityetāmanubruvannanu prapadyeta |*)

namely Ambayo yanti (1-23-16).

जामयो अध्वरीयतां । पृंचतीर्मधुना पयॆ इति योऽमधव्यो यशोऽर्तोर्बुभूषेत् । (*jāmayo adhvarīyatāṃ | pṛṃcatīrmadhunā payè iti yo 'madhavyo yaśo 'rtorbubhūṣet |*)

The meaning of this Ṛk is explained: the word amba is a word for "mother" that shows respect. Ambayaḥ means these waters, who are to be honoured like mothers. These two kinds of water, equal to mothers, go by various paths. For the sacrificer who wishes to carry out the sacrifice they are bhaginī, that is, like sisters, wishing his good; and they satisfy everyone with their own sweet water. The man who has not so far known the taste of Soma juice and who wishes to gain fame by performing the Soma sacrifice, if he recites the mantra, shows respect to these waters and follows them, obtains his desired aim.

अमूर्या उप सूर्ये याभिर्वा सूर्यः सहेति तेजस्कामो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामः । (*amūryā upa sūrye yābhirvā sūryaḥ saheti tejaskāmo brahmavarcasakāmaḥ |*)

In the next Ṛk other fruits are stated: if one recites the Ṛk Amūryā upa sūrye (1-23-17), one becomes radiant and full of brahmic splendour through the wealth of learning.

अपो देवीरुपह्वये यत्र गावः पिबंति न इति पशुकामः ॥ (*apo devīrupahvaye yatra gāvaḥ pibaṃti na iti paśukāmaḥ ‖*)

The man who desires wealth of cattle should recite the Ṛk Apo devīrupa hvaye (11-23-18). **NOTE**

ता एताः सर्वा एवानुब्रुवन्ननुप्रपद्येतैतेषां कामानामवरुध्यॆ । एतान्यामानवरुंधे य एवं वेद ॥ (*tā etāḥ sarvā evānubruvannanuprapadyetaiteṣāṃ kāmānāmavarudhyè | etānyāmānavaruṃdhe ya evaṃ veda ‖*)

One who wishes to obtain all his desired aims should recite all three Ṛks mentioned above. The man who knows this obtains all his desired aims and is happy.

एमा अग्नस्रेवतीर्जीवधन्या इति साद्यमानास्वन्वाह वसतीवरीष्वेकधनासु च । आग्मन्नाप उशतीर्बर्हिरेदमिति सन्नासु स एतया परिदधाति ॥ (*emā agnasrevatīrjīvadhanyā iti sādyamānāsvanvāha vasatīvarīṣvekadhanāsu ca | āgmannāpa uśatīrbarhiredamiti sannāsu sa etayā paridadhāti ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 8-20)

### Printed p. 793
When the two kinds of water mentioned above, that is, the waters of the vasatīvarī and ekadhanā vessels, are being carried to the neighbourhood of the Uttaravedi, the Hotṛ must recite the Ṛk Emā agmanrevatīḥ (10-30-14). After those two kinds of water have been placed on the vedi, the Hotṛ must recite the Ṛk Agmannāpa (10-30-15) as the last Ṛk of this Apo-naptrīya rite and bring the rite to completion.

Here the description of the rite called Aponaptrīya is complete.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तृतीयेऽनुवाके त्रयोदश सूक्तानि । तत्र प्र देवत्रेति पंचदशर्चं
> प्रथमं सूक्तं । इलूषपुत्रस्य कवषस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमद्देवत्यमपांनपाद्देवताकं
> वा । तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्र देवत्रा पंचोना कवष ऐलूष अपमपोनप्रीयं
> वेति॥ अपयिष्य होतरित्युक्तः सन् होता प्र देवत्रेत्याद्या नवर्चोऽनुब्रूयात्।
> सूत्रितं च । प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे गातुरेत्विति नव हिनोता नो अध्वरं देवयज्येति
> दशमीं । आ. ५-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the third anuvāka there are thirteen sūktas. Of these the first is the fifteen-Ṛk sūkta Pra devatrā. Its seer is Kavaṣa, son of Ilūṣa. Its deity is the Waters, or else Apāṃnapāt; its metre is Triṣṭubh. Sāyaṇa cites the Anukramaṇī: प्र देवत्रा पंचोना कवष ऐलूष अपमपोनप्रीयं वेति॥ (*pra devatrā paṃconā kavaṣa ailūṣa apamaponaprīyaṃ veti‖*) Use: when the Adhvaryu has said "Hotṛ, [offer] the waters" (*apayiṣya hotaḥ*), the Hotṛ should recite the first nine Ṛks beginning Pra devatrā. He states this is laid down in the sūtra: प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे गातुरेत्विति नव हिनोता नो अध्वरं देवयज्येति दशमीं । आ. ५-१ । (*pra devatrā brahmaṇe gāturetviti nava hinotā no adhvaraṃ devayajyeti daśamīṃ | ā. 5-1 |*) i.e. Ā. 5-1. **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

In the third anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala there are thirteen sūktas. Of these this sūkta, Pra devatrā, is the first; it has fifteen Ṛks. Its seer is Kavaṣa, son of Ilūṣa; its deity is the Waters or Apāṃnapāt; its metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: Pra devatrā paṃcona Kavaṣa Ailūṣa Āpamaponastrīyaṃ vā. As soon as the Adhvaryu, addressing the Hotṛ, has recited the Praiṣa mantra "अप इष्ट्य होतः (*apa iṣṭya hotaḥ*)", the Hotṛ must recite the first nine Ṛks of this sūkta beginning Pra devatrā; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 5-1): "Pra devatrā brahmaṇe gāturetvi, nine; Hinotā no adhvaraṃ devayajyā, the tenth."

Sūkta 30. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 30. Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 7; Vargas 24, 25, 26. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Kavaṣa Ailūṣa. Deity: Āpaḥ or Apāṃnapāt. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

### Printed p. 794
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र दे॑व॒त्रा ब्रह्म॑णे गा॒तुरे॑त्व॒पो अच्छा॒ मन॑सो॒ न प्रयु॑क्ति ।  
> म॒हीं मि॒त्रस्य॒ वरु॑णस्य धा॒सिं पृ॑थु॒ज्रय॑से रीरधा सुवृ॒क्तिं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । देवत्रा । ब्रह्मणे । गातुः । एतु । अपः । अच्छ । मनसः । न । प्रयुक्ति ।  
> महीं । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । धासिं । पृथुज्रयसे । रीरध । सुवृक्तिं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ब्रह्मणे । तृतीयार्थे चतुर्थी । ब्रह्मणा स्तोत्रेण । स्सूयमान इति शेषः।
> गातुर्देवानपो वा प्रतिगमनशीलः सोमो देवत्रा देवीर्दोतमाना अपो
> वसतीवर्येकधनालक्षणान्वयुदकान्यच्छाभि प्रैतु । प्रकर्षेण गच्छतु । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> मनसो न प्रयुक्ति यथा मनसः प्रयुक्तिः प्रयोग उद्योगः शीघ्रं गच्छति
> तद्वत् । एवं सोमेऽपः प्रतिगते सति हे मदीयात्मन् अध्वर्यो ना महीं
> धासिं महत्सोमलक्षणमन्नं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चार्थाय पृथुज्रयसे विस्तीर्णजवाय । महागतेरिंद्रस्य चार्थायेत्यर्थः । रीरध । संसाधय । संस्कुरु । दानयोग्यं कुरु । सुवृक्तिं सुष्टु दोषैर्वर्जितां स्तुतिं च कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*): the fourth case is used in the sense of the third; "by brahman", that is, by a stotra, "being praised" is to be supplied. गातुः (*gātuḥ*) is Soma, whose nature is to go to the gods or to the waters. Let him go forth towards (*acchābhi praitu*) the shining (देवत्रा (*devatrā*)) waters, namely the waters of the vasatīvarī and ekadhanā kind; let him advance. An example: मनसो न प्रयुक्ति (*manaso na prayukti*), as the prayoga, the impulse, of the mind goes swiftly, so. When Soma has thus gone to the waters, "O Adhvaryu, my own self" (हे मदीयात्मन् अध्वर्यो ना (*he madīyātman adhvaryo nā*)), bring to completion (रीरध (*rīradha*): perfect, prepare, make fit for giving) the great food (महीं धासिं (*mahīṃ dhāsiṃ*)), whose nature is Soma, for Mitra and Varuṇa, and for पृथुज्रयसे (*pṛthujrayase*), one of wide speed, that is, for Indra of great motion. And make (सुवृक्तिं (*suvṛktiṃ*)) a praise well free from faults.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनसः (*manasaḥ*)—of the mind
- प्रयुक्ति न (*prayukti na*)—swiftly, like the activity
- ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*)—praised with praise
- गातुः (*gātuḥ*)—going, Soma that has the nature of going
- देवत्रा (*devatrā*)—shining
- अपः अच्छ (*apaḥ accha*)—towards the waters of the vasatīvarī and other vessels
- प्र एतु (*pra etu*)—let it flow
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—for Mitra
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—for Varuṇa
- पृथुज्रयसे (*pṛthujrayase*)—for Indra, who has great speed
- महीं (*mahīṃ*)—great
- धासिं (*dhāsiṃ*)—the food in the form of Soma
- रीरध (*rīradha*)—prepare and offer
- सुवृक्तिं (*suvṛktiṃ*)—offer also a praise free from faults

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let Soma, praised with praise and given to going, flow swiftly, like the activity of the mind, towards the shining waters of the vasatīvarī and other vessels. Prepare and offer the great food in the form of Soma to Mitra and Varuṇa and to Indra of great speed. Offer a praise free from faults.

### Printed p. 795

##### English translation
(Honoured) by adoration, let the advancing Soma approach the celestial waters like the celerity of the mind : offer abundant (sacrificial) food, and perfect praise for the sake of Mitra and Varuna, and for (Indra) the rapid mover.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध्व॑र्यवो ह॒विष्मं॑तो॒ हि भू॒ताच्छा॒प इ॑तोष॒तीरु॑शंतः ।  
> अव॒ याश्चष्टे॑ अरु॒णः सु॑प॒र्णस्तमास्य॑ध्वमू॒र्मिम॒द्वा  ॑
> सुहस्ताः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध्वर्यवः । हविष्मंतः । हि । भूत । अच्छ । अपः । इत । उशतीः । उशंतः ।  
> अव । याः । चष्टे । अरुणः । सुपर्णः । तं । आ । अस्यध्वं । ऊर्मि० । अद्य ।  
> सुहस्ताः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यवः यूयं हविष्मंतो ह्यभिषोतव्येन सोमलक्षणेन हविषा
> युक्ताः खलु भूत । भवत । किं च हे उशंतः सोमाभिषवं कर्तुं कामयमाना अध्वर्यवः यूयमुशतीः सोमाभिषवांगभावमभिलषंतीरेकधनालक्षणा
> अपोऽच्छाभिमुख्येनेत । गच्छत । अरुणो रक्तवर्णः सुपर्णः सुपतनः सोमोऽनाधस्तादंतरिक्षे या मेघोदरगता अपश्चष्टे पश्यति हे सुहस्ताः सोमाभिषवादिशोभनकर्मकारित्वात् सुमर्णमयपवित्राद्यलंकृताः । यद्वा । शोभनहस्ताः ।
> एतेऽध्वर्यवः यूयमद्येदानीं तं तादृशमूर्मिं सोमसंघातं ताभिरद्धिः
> सहास्यध्वं । अभिमुख्येन स्थित्वा महतादरेण दशापवित्रॆ शोधनार्थं प्रक्षिपत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the adhvaryu priests. "You are indeed endowed with oblations", that is, joined with the oblation in the form of Soma that is to be pressed; "be so". Further, O adhvaryus who desire to perform the pressing of Soma, you who long for the waters that are the means of the Soma-pressing, the waters of the kind called ekadhanā, go towards those waters, facing them. The red-coloured Soma, of good flight, sees below in the atmosphere those waters that lie in the belly of the cloud. O you of good hands: either because you perform good acts such as the pressing of Soma and are adorned with golden filters and the like, or else, "of beautiful hands". Now, to-day, mingle that wave, that mass of Soma, with those waters. Standing facing them, with great regard, cast it into the ten-fibred filter for the purpose of purifying it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*)—O priests
- हविष्मंतः हि (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ hi*)—you, endowed with oblations
- भूत (*bhūta*)—are
- उशंतः (*uśaṃtaḥ*)—you who desire to press the Soma
- उशतीः (*uśatīḥ*)—desiring that very thing, and
- अरुणः (*aruṇaḥ*)—the red-coloured one
- सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*)—the one of good flight

### Printed p. 796

- अव (*ava*)—in the lower region of the atmosphere
- याः (*yāḥ*)—which waters, lying in the cloud
- चष्टे (*caṣṭe*)—he beholds; such waters
- अपः अच्छ (*apaḥ accha*)—towards the waters
- इत (*ita*)—move
- सुहस्ताः (*suhastāḥ*)—O priests of good hands
- आद्य (*ādya*)—now
- तं ऊर्मिं (*taṃ ūrmiṃ*)—that mass of Soma, like waves
- अस्यध्वं (*asyadhvaṃ*)—mingle with the waters

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O adhvaryus, you are provided with oblations. You who desire to press Soma, move towards the waters that you long for, and which the red-coloured Soma of good flight beholds in the lower region of the atmosphere, lying in the cloud. O adhvaryus of good hands, now mingle that mass of Soma, like waves, with the waters of the vasatīvarī and others.

##### English translation
Priests, since you are charged with the libation, desiring (to present it), proceed to the waters desiring (to receive it); to those (waters) which the red hawk beholds descending from the clouds: you, dextrous-handed (priests), cast to-day that flood (of Soma) into (the consecrated water).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध्व॑र्यवो॒ऽप इ॑ता समु॒द्रम॒पां नपा॑तं ह॒विषा॑ यजध्वं।  
> स वो॑ दददू॒र्मिम॒द्या सुपू॑तं॒ तस्मै॒ सोमं॒ मधु॑मंतं  
> सुनोत ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध्वर्यवः । अपः । इत । समुद्रं । अपां । नपातं । हविषा । यजध्वं ।  
> सः । वः । ददत् । ऊर्मिं । अद्य । सुपूतं । तस्मै । सोमं । मधुमंतं ।  
> सुनोत ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यवः यूयमप एकधनालक्षणान्युदकानि । आहर्तुमिति शेषः !
> समुद्रमुदधिस्थानीयं जलाशयमित । गच्छत । इदानीमुत्तरोर्धर्चो

### Printed p. 797

> व्याखायते पश्चाद्वितीयः पादः । स्वार्थिकोऽयं क्रमः । अद्येऽदानीं सोऽपां
> नपाद्वो जलाशयं प्रतिगतेभ्यो युष्मभ्यं सुपूतं सुशुद्ध मूर्मिं जलसमूहं ददत् । ददातु । यूयमपि तेन समूहेन तस्मा अपां नपाते मधुमंतं
> मधुरस्वादूपेतं सोमं सुनोत । अभिषुणुत । अभिषुतेन सोमाख्येन हविषापां नपातं वृष्टिकर्मण्यधिकृतं देवं यजध्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O adhvaryus, go to the sea, that is, the reservoir that stands in the place of the ocean, in order to fetch the waters, the waters of the ekadhanā kind (the words "in order to fetch" are to be supplied). The latter half of the verse is now explained first; the second pāda comes afterwards, this order being intended for the sense. To-day, now, may that grandson of the waters give to you, who have gone to the reservoir, the well-purified flood, the mass of water. And you also, with that mass of water, press for that grandson of the waters the Soma that is joined with sweet flavour. With the pressed Soma-oblation worship the god Apāṃnapāt, who presides over the work of rain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*)—O adhvaryus
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—to fetch the ekadhanā waters
- समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*)—to the sea
- इत (*ita*)—go
- अपां नपातं (*apāṃ napātaṃ*)—the god called Apāṃnapāt
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblation
- यजध्वं (*yajadhvaṃ*)—worship
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- सः (*saḥ*)—that god called Apāṃnapāt
- वः (*vaḥ*)—to you
- सुप्रोतं (*suprotaṃ*)—well-purified
- ऊर्मिं (*ūrmiṃ*)—the mass of water
- ददत् (*dadat*)—may he provide
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—addressing him
- मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)—possessing a sweet flavour
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- सुनोत (*sunota*)—press and offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O adhvaryus, go to the sea to fetch the ekadhanā waters. Worship the god called Apāṃnapāt with oblation. May that god provide you with a well-purified mass of water. Addressing him, press and offer Soma possessing a sweet flavour.

##### English translation
Go, priests, to the reservoir ; worship the grandson of the waters with oblations : may he to-day give you the consecrated water, and you pour forth to him the sweet-flavoured Soma.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो अ॑नि॒ध्मो दीद॑यद॒प्स्व१॒ं॑ तर्यं विप्रा॑स॒ ईळ॑ते अध्व॒रेषु॑ ।  
> अपां॑ नपा॒न्नधु॑मतीठ॒पो दा॒ याभि॒रिंद्रो॑ वावृ॒धे  ॒॑
> वीर्याय ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 798

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । अनिध्मः । दीदयत् । अप्सु । अंतः । यं । विप्रासः । ईळते । अध्वरेषु ।  
> अपां । नपात् । मधुमतीः । अपः । दाः । याभिः । इंद्रः । ववृधे । वीर्याय॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत्तरार्धस्य प्रत्यक्षकृतत्वादेकवाक्यताय्कॆ युष्मच्छब्देन समानार्थो भवच्छब्दः प्रथमार्धेऽध्याहार्यः । यो भवानपां नपादस्वंतरपां मध्यॆ मेघस्थानेऽनिध्मः काष्ठवर्जितः सन् दीदयत् दीव्यते विप्रासो मेधाविन ऋत्विग्यजमाना अध्वरेषु यागेषु यं भवंतमीळते स्तुवंति हे अपां नपात् स त्वं
> मधुमतिर्मधुररसयुक्ता अपो वृष्टिलक्षणा दाः । अस्मभ्यं देहि । याभिर्वसतीवर्येकधनारूपाभिः सोमेन मिश्रिताभिरद्भरिंद्रो वीर्याय वृत्रवधादिशूरकर्मणे ववृधे वर्धते ता अपो देहीति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Since the latter half of the verse has been made a direct address, a word for "you" that is equal in meaning to the pronoun of the second person is to be supplied in the first half so that the sentence is one. You who, O Apāṃnapāt, in the midst of the waters, in the place of the cloud, shine without fuel, free of wood; you whom the wise priests and sacrificers praise at the sacrifices: O Apāṃnapāt, you give us the sweet waters, that is, waters joined with sweet flavour and having the form of rain. Those waters, mixed with Soma, namely the vasatīvarī and ekadhanā waters, by which Indra grows for heroic deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra: give those waters. This is the connection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*)—O god called Apāṃnapāt
- यः (*yaḥ*)—you who
- अप्पु अंतः (*appu aṃtaḥ*)—in the midst of the waters (in the cloud)
- अनिध्मः (*anidhmaḥ*)—without any wood
- दीदयत् (*dīdayat*)—shine, and
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whom, you
- विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)—the wise priests
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—at sacrifices
- ईळते (*īḷate*)—praise; such as you are
- याभिः (*yābhiḥ*)—by which waters (mixed with Soma)
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वीर्याय (*vīryāya*)—for performing heroic deeds
- ववृधे (*vavṛdhe*)—grows strong; such
- मधुमतीः (*madhumatīḥ*)—sweet
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—waters
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god called Apāṃnapāt, you who shine in the midst of the waters (in the region of the cloud) without any wood, and whom the wise priests praise at sacrifices: give us the waters that are sweet, that are fit to be joined with the Soma, and that give strength to Indra for performing heroic deeds.

##### English translation
(He) who shines without fuel, in the midst of the waters, he whom the pious worship at sacrifices; grandson of the waters, give us those sweet waters by which (mixed with the Soma-juice), Indra is elevated to herosim.

### Printed p. 799

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the derivation of the word Apāṃnapāt, the Nirukta has given the explanation of this Ṛk as an example: योऽनिध्मो दीदयद्दीप्यसेऽभ्यंतरमप्पु यं मेधाविनः स्तुवंति यज्ञेषु सोऽपान्नपान्मधुमतीरपो देह्यभिषवाय याभिरिंद्रो वर्धते वीर्याय वीरकर्मणे ॥ (*yo 'nidhmo dīdayaddīpyase 'bhyaṃtaramappu yaṃ medhāvinaḥ stuvaṃti yajñeṣu so 'pānnapānmadhumatīrapo dehyabhiṣavāya yābhiriṃdro vardhate vīryāya vīrakarmaṇe ‖*) (Ni. 10-19). Apāṃnapāt means the fire that is in the middle of the water or arises there, or a transformed form of fire. This god called Apāṃnapāt shines in the middle of the water without the help of fuel and the like (wood or timber). Such a god, distinguished by these qualities, is praised at sacrifices and the like by wise people such as the priests. O deity Apāṃnapāt, for the increase of Indra's power we are pressers of the Soma-juice. For that, graciously grant us sweet waters, tasty like honey. This is the purport of the explanation.

> भवति हर्षते च । पुनरुक्तिरादरार्था । अत्यर्थं हृष्यतीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः ॥

### Printed p. 800

> कल्याणीभिः कमनीयाभिर्युवतिभिस्तरुणीभिः स्त्रीभिः सह मर्यो न यथा मनुष्यो
> मोदते तद्वत् । हे अध्वर्यो त्वं तास्तादृशीरपोऽच्छाभिप्राप्तं परेहि । जलाशयं प्रतिगच्छ । किंच यद्यदाहृताभिस्ताभिरद्धिरासिंचाः आ समंतात्सोमानासिंचसि
> तदौषधीभिः सोमैः सहापश्च पुनीतात् । दशापवित्रेण पुनीहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The pressed Soma rejoices, becomes glad, with those waters, namely the vasatīvarī and ekadhanā waters, and delights; the repetition is for emphasis: he is exceedingly delighted. An illustration follows. As a man rejoices with lovely young women, with maidens, so Soma rejoices with those waters. O adhvaryu, you go towards those waters, to the reservoir. Further, when you sprinkle the Soma with those fetched waters, then purify the waters along with the plants, that is, the Soma-stalks, with the ten-fibred filter.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वर्यो (*adhvaryo*)—O adhvaryu
- मर्यः (*maryaḥ*)—a man
- कल्याणीभिः (*kalyāṇībhiḥ*)—with attractive in form
- युवतिभिः न (*yuvatibhiḥ na*)—as he is glad and delighted when in the company of young women
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the god Soma
- याभिः (*yābhiḥ*)—with which waters
- मोदते (*modate*)—he rejoices
- हर्षते च (*harṣate ca*)—and is glad and delighted
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—such
- अपः अच्छ (*apaḥ accha*)—towards the waters (to fetch them)
- परेहि (*parehi*)—go to the sea
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- आसिंचाः (*āsiṃcāḥ*)—you mix them with the Soma, then
- ओषधीभिः (*oṣadhībhiḥ*)—with the Soma-plants
- पुनीतात् (*punītāt*)—purify them also

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O adhvaryu, as a man is glad and delighted when in the company of young women of attractive form, so the god Soma is delighted with the waters that he joins. Go to the sea to fetch such waters, facing them. When you mix them with the Soma, then purify them along with the Soma-plants.

##### English translation
Those waters with which Soma sports and delights as a man (sports) with elegant young damsels : you, priest, approach to obtain them : when you sprinkle them (in libation), purify (them with the filter) along with the plants (the Soma).

> एवैवं वसतीवर्येकधनाख्या आपः सोमाय प्रह्वीभवंति । यद्वा । युवतयः
> सोमेन सह मिश्रयित्र्य आपो यूनेऽभिषवादिकर्मणामात्मना सह मिश्रयित्रॆ
> कर्त्रेऽध्वर्यवे नमंत । प्रह्वीभवंत्येव । इदिति पूरणः । कदा । यद्यदोशन्नभिषवार्थं वसतीवरीः कामयमानः सोमः सोमाभिषवं कर्तुं कामयमानोऽध्वर्युर्वोशतीः सोमेन सह मिश्रिभावमभिषवादिकर्मांगभावं च
> कामयमाना ईमेना अपोऽच्छ प्राप्तुमेति गच्छति तदोपनमंते । अध्वर्यवो
> धिषणा तदीयास्तुतिलक्षणा वाक्च देवीर्देव्य आपश्च मनसा विशिष्टया बुद्ध्या सं
> जानते । सम्यग्ज्ञानंति । सं चिकित्से । स्वं स्वमधिकारं परस्परोपकारं च चक्षुषा
> सम्यक् पश्यंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Young women", that is, maidens, bow to a youth, that is, become submissive to him; in the same way the waters called vasatīvarī and ekadhanā become submissive to Soma. Or else: the young waters, which mix with Soma, bow to the youth, namely the adhvaryu, the doer, who mingles with himself the rites of pressing and the rest; they become submissive indeed, the particle "id" being a filler. When? When Soma, desiring the vasatīvarī waters for the pressing, or the adhvaryu desiring to perform the pressing of Soma, goes to reach these waters, which desire to be mixed with Soma and to be parts of the rites of pressing and the rest, then they bow. The adhvaryus, and the speech in the form of their praise, and the divine waters, know well with mind, that is, with distinguished understanding; and they see well with the eye their own respective office and their mutual service.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- युवतयः (*yuvatayaḥ*)—young women
- यूने (*yūne*)—towards the youths they desire
- नमंत (*namaṃta*)—as they are submissive
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- उशन् (*uśan*)—Soma, desiring the vasatīvarī waters
- ईं उशतीः (*īṃ uśatīḥ*)—**NOTE**
- अच्छ (*accha*)—to the vasatīvarī and other waters that long for him
- एति (*eti*)—approaches; then they are submissive to him
- अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*)—the adhvaryus
- धिषणा (*dhiṣaṇā*)—and speech in the form of praise
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—shining
- अपश्च (*apaśca*)—and the waters
- मनसा (*manasā*)—joined with good understanding
- सं जानते (*saṃ jānate*)—together know their duty
- सं चिकित्से (*saṃ cikitse*)—and understand also their mutual helpfulness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As young women are submissive to the youths they desire, so when Soma, desiring the vasatīvarī waters, approaches the vasatīvarī and other waters that long for him, they are submissive to him. The adhvaryus, the speech in the form of praise and the shining waters, joined with good understanding, together know their duty. They understand also their mutual helpfulness.

##### English translation
Verily as young damsels welcome a youth, when desiring (them), he comes to them desiring (him), so the priests and their praise and divine waters agree in mind and contemplate (their mutual assistance).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who made for you, the waters, enveloped and surrounded by the clouds, an opening, that is, a way of exit from the belly of the cloud (the particle "u" being a filler); and further, who released you from the great harm of being encircled by the clouds. O waters, send forth to that Indra the wave, that is, the mass of water, which is sweet, endowed with sweet flavour, and which gladdens the gods: mingled with Soma, it satisfies Indra and the other gods. Cause it to go to the sacrifice; send it forth for the purpose of serving the rite of the pressing of Soma.

- अकृणोत् (*akṛṇot*)—made
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- मह्याः (*mahyāḥ*)—from the very great

- प्र हिणोतन (*pra hiṇotana*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O waters, to that Indra who made for you, enveloped by the clouds, a way of coming out from the belly of the clouds, and who released you from very great harm: provide the mass of water that is sweet and satisfying to the gods.

##### English translation
Present, waters, the sweet-flavoured god-exhilarating mixture to that Indra who has made an issue for you when enveloped (by the clouds); who has liberated you from a great calamity.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, because of the relation with the relative word, the second pāda is to be explained first. O sindhus, flowing waters, that embryo of yours, which is the spring, the outflow, of sweet juice, that is, of honey-flavoured juice: the word "that" is to be supplied because of the relative. That sweet wave, the mass of water endowed with a honey-flavoured juice, that is, the essence, send forth for him, for the sake of this Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—O waters in the form of streams
- यः (*yaḥ*)—he who
- वः (*vaḥ*)—to you
- गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)—is in the form of an embryo, and
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—for the sweet juice
- उत्सः (*utsaḥ*)—is like a spring
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to such an Indra
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—at sacrifices
- घृतपृष्ठं (*ghṛtapṛṣṭhaṃ*)—having its back anointed with ghee
- ईड्यं (*īḍyaṃ*)—praiseworthy
- मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)—and possessing sweet juice
- ऊर्मिं (*ūrmiṃ*)—the mass of water
- प्र हिनोत (*pra hinota*)—offer
- रेवतीः (*revatīḥ*)—wealthy
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—O waters
- मे (*me*)—my
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—invocation
- शृणुत (*śṛṇuta*)—hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O waters in the form of streams, to that Indra who is in the form of an embryo to you and is like a spring for the sweet juice, offer at the sacrifices the mass of water that has its back anointed with ghee, is praiseworthy and possesses sweet juice. O wealthy waters, hear my invocation.

##### English translation
Send forth, rivers, the sweet-flavoured beverage to him who is your germ, a well of the sweet (Soma-juice), the beverage which is mixed with butter adorable at sacrifices : hear, opulent waters my invocation.

> पानीयं तं तादृशमूर्मिमुदकसमूहं प्र हेत । प्रगमयत । अस्मद्यज्ञं प्रति
> प्रेरयत । कीदृशं । मदच्युतं मदस्य च्यावकमौशानं सोमेन सह मिश्रीभावं
> कामयमानं नभोजां नभस्यंतरिक्षे वृष्टिरूपेण जातं परि सर्वतस्त्रितंतुं
> त्रयाणां लोकानां तनितारं विस्तारयितारं विचरंतं यज्ञपात्रॆषु गच्छंतमुत्समुत्स्यंदनं । तर्पितारं देवान्मत्तौर्धं गंतारमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O sindhus, flowing waters, that essential mass of yours which, being the giver to us of both fruits, the seen and the unseen, comes into service as a part of the rite: send forth that wave, that mass of water, which is gladdening, satisfying Indra and the other gods; to be drunk by Indra, the chief of the gods. Cause it to go forth, send it to our sacrifice. Of what kind is it? It makes the exhilaration flow; it desires to be mixed with Soma; it is born in the firmament, in the form of rain; it stretches out the three worlds on every side; it goes about, moving in the sacrificial vessels; it is a spring, that is, an outflow. The meaning is that it satisfies the gods and goes upward. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—O flowing waters
- यः (*yaḥ*)—that mass of water of yours which
- उभे (*ubhe*)—two fruits, seen and unseen
- इयर्ति (*iyarti*)—provides; such
- मत्सरं (*matsaraṃ*)—gladdening
- इंद्रपानं (*iṃdrapānaṃ*)—fit to be drunk by Indra
- मदच्युतं (*madacyutaṃ*)—exhilarating
- औशानं (*auśānaṃ*)—desiring a connection with Soma
- नभोजां (*nabhojāṃ*)—born in the firmament
- परि (*pari*)—everywhere
- त्रितंतुं (*tritaṃtuṃ*)—making the three worlds extend
- विचरंतं (*vicaraṃtaṃ*)—entering the sacrificial vessels
- उत्सं (*utsaṃ*)—and being like a spring
- तं ऊर्मिं (*taṃ ūrmiṃ*)—that mass of water
- प्र हेत (*pra heta*)—send forth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O flowing waters, that mass of water of yours which provides both fruits, the seen and the unseen, being gladdening, fit to be drunk by Indra, exhilarating, desiring a connection with Soma, born in the firmament, making the three worlds extend everywhere, entering the sacrificial vessels and being like a spring: send forth that mass of water.

##### English translation
Send, rivers, (to our sacrifice), that exilarating wave, the beverage of Indra, which sends us both (kinds of fruit), exciting exhilaration, desirous, (of mixing with the Soma), generated in the firmament ; spreading through the three (worlds), flowing (amidst the vessels of sacrifice), a well (of satisfaction to the gods).

> ऋषे । जनित्रीः । भुवनस्य । पत्निः । अपः । वंदस्व । सवृधः । सयोनीः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपोनप्रीय एकधनास्वावृत्तास्वावर्वृततीरित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । आवर्वृततीरध नु द्विधारा इत्यावृत्तास्वेकधनासु । आ. ५.१ । इति । तत्रैव हिनोता न इत्येषा।
> सूत्रं पूर्वमुदाहृतं ॥
> अधाथानंतरं गोषुयुधो न । गोष्टप्पु निमित्तभूतासु मेघैः सह
> युध्यत इति गोषुयुदिंद्रः ; तस्य यथा वृष्टिलक्षणा अपो द्विधाराः । द्विशब्दोऽत्रानेकत्रवाची । अनेकधाराः । अपर्यंतधारा इत्यर्थः । अस्माकमप्येवंस्थिता
> आवर्वृततीरावृत्ता नियवं सोमं प्रति निश्चयेन मिश्रीभावं चरंतीर्गच्छंतीभुवनस्य लोकस्य जनत्रीर्जनयित्रिः पत्नीः पालयित्रिश्च सवृधः सह सोमस्य वर्धयित्रिः सयोनीः सोमेन सह समानस्थाना हे ऋषे मदीयांतरात्मन्
> अध्वयो वा त्वमेवंभूता अपो नु क्षिप्रं वंदस्व । स्तुहीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This verse belongs to the ritual of the grandson of the waters, in the repeated ekadhanā waters. **NOTE** It is also laid down in the sūtra: the verse आवर्वृततीरध नु द्विधारा (*āvarvṛtatīradha nu dvidhārā*) is for the repeated ekadhanā waters (Ā. Sū. 5.1). There too the verse हिनोता न (*hinotā na*) is named; the sūtra has been quoted before. Next, गोषुयुधो न (*goṣuyudho na*): Indra, who fights with the clouds when the waters are the occasion, is "he who fights in the cows"; as to him the waters in the form of rain have two streams, the word "two" here meaning many, that is, they have countless streams; so also for us, waters standing thus, recurring, going to Soma for certain mixture; the creators of the world, and also its protectors; the increasers of Soma together with him; sharing a common place with Soma. O sage, my inner self, or O adhvaryu, quickly praise such waters; that is, extol them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋषे (*ṛṣe*)—O sage
- द्विधाराः (*dvidhārāḥ*)—having many streams
- आ वर्वृततीः (*ā varvṛtatīḥ*)—returning again
- नियवं (*niyavaṃ*)—certainly
- मिश्रीभावं (*miśrībhāvaṃ*)—union with Soma
- चरंतीः (*caraṃtīḥ*)—attaining
- भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)—for the world
- जनित्रीः (*janitrīḥ*)—the producers
- पत्नीः (*patnīḥ*)—the protectors
- सवृधः (*savṛdhaḥ*)—those who make Soma thrive
- सयोनीः (*sayonīḥ*)—and are born together with Soma
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- गोषुयुधो न (*goṣuyudho na*)—like Indra, who fights for the cows
- वंदस्व (*vaṃdasva*)—salute

### Printed p. 807

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sage, quickly salute the waters, like Indra who fights for the cows: the waters that have many streams, that return again, that certainly unite with Soma, that create and protect the world, that make Soma thrive, and that are born together with Soma.

##### English translation
Praise, Rishi, the waters like (those) of the cloud-warring Indra, falling in many showers returning, flowing to mix (with the Soma), the mothers of the world and its protectresses, augmenting and combining (with the Soma).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the ancillary rite of the sacrifice that is named after the grandson of the waters, when the waters are brought from the reservoir in the vessels called ekadhanā, this Ṛk beginning आवर्वृततीः (*āvarvṛtatīḥ*) has its application, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra आवर्वृततीरध द्विधारा इत्यावृत्तास्वेकधनासु (*āvarvṛtatīradha dvidhārā ityāvṛttāsvekadhanāsu*) (Ā. Sū. 5-1). And in that same context the next Ṛk, beginning हिनोता नः (*hinotā naḥ*), is also to be recited. The sūtra has been quoted before.
